issues.title: [Win] UR Error when OOM and break the tensor context
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

We found that when running models and the model is OOM, we get the UR Error, and this UR Error will break tensor context. 

```Python
# On a 16.5 GB host memory of LNL

# 1. First fill all the GPU memory
(8GB)>>> x1 = torch.ones(1024*1024*1024, dtype=torch.float64, device='xpu')
(8GB)>>> x2 = torch.ones(1024*1024*1024, dtype=torch.float64, device='xpu')
(0.5GB)>>> x3 = torch.ones(128*1024*1024, dtype=torch.float32, device='xpu')

# 1.1 You can see this access is ok
>>> x1[100]
tensor(1., device='xpu:0', dtype=torch.float64)

# 1.2 Fill another tensor, this is OOM, expected. This x4 should not be created.
>>> x4 = torch.ones(128*1024*1024, dtype=torch.float32, device='xpu')
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
torch.OutOfMemoryError: XPU out of memory. Tried to allocate 512.00 MiB. GPU 0 has a total capacity of 16.50 GiB. Of the allocated memory 16.50 GiB is allocated by PyTorch, and 0 bytes is reserved by PyTorch but unallocated. Please use `empty_cache` to release all unoccupied cached memory.
 
# 2. Re-access the tensor, it gets UR Error with OUT_OF_RESOURCES. This is unexpected, the tensor context of x1 should be normal.
 
>>> x1[100]
File "C:\Users\sdp\miniforge3\envs\tongsu_onednn_37_no_fix\lib\site-packages\torch\_tensor_str.py", line 146, in __init__
    tensor_view, torch.isfinite(tensor_view) & tensor_view.ne(0)
RuntimeError: UR backend failed. UR backend returns:40 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES)
 
# 3. Re-access, it gets UR Error without any useful information
>>> x1[100]
File "C:\Users\sdp\miniforge3\envs\tongsu_onednn_37_no_fix\lib\site-packages\torch\_tensor.py", line 568, in __repr__
    return torch._tensor_str._str(self, tensor_contents=tensor_contents)
  File "C:\Users\sdp\miniforge3\envs\tongsu_onednn_37_no_fix\lib\site-packages\torch\_tensor_str.py", line 704, in _str
    return _str_intern(self, tensor_contents=tensor_contents)
  File "C:\Users\sdp\miniforge3\envs\tongsu_onednn_37_no_fix\lib\site-packages\torch\_tensor_str.py", line 621, in _str_intern
    tensor_str = _tensor_str(self, indent)
  File "C:\Users\sdp\miniforge3\envs\tongsu_onednn_37_no_fix\lib\site-packages\torch\_tensor_str.py", line 353, in _tensor_str
    formatter = _Formatter(get_summarized_data(self) if summarize else self)
  File "C:\Users\sdp\miniforge3\envs\tongsu_onednn_37_no_fix\lib\site-packages\torch\_tensor_str.py", line 146, in __init__
    tensor_view, torch.isfinite(tensor_view) & tensor_view.ne(0)
RuntimeError: UR error
```

As a comparison, CUDA could handle all of the above. It has the following logic:

1. If the dedicated memory is not enough, it will try allocate from the host memory. This behavior could be disabled by [地址已移除]
2. If disabled CUDA's unified memory oversubscription, it will throw OOM, and the re-access `x1` in the example could also work, its tensor context won't be affected.


### Versions

-

issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

When the prebuilt wheels is built with oneapi 2025.0 and I use oneapi 2025.1 for cpp extension, the following error shows up

![Image]([地址已移除])

Could we provide a clear error message like "Error: Inconsistent OneAPI versions detected. Please check the version"  for better UX 


Steps to reproduce this issue

```
# Create conda env and install ninja by  
conda install ninja

# Install nightly wheels  , packages from oneapi 2025.0 included in this wheel  
pip3 install --pre torch==2.8.0.dev20250427+xpu  --index-url [地址已移除]


# Install oneapi 2025.1 by offline packages
wget [地址已移除] 
sudo sh ./intel-deep-learning-essentials-2025.1.2.13_offline.sh -a --silent --eula accept

# build & run cpp extension example
git clone [地址已移除]
cd pytorch_examples/pytorch/extension-cpp-sycl

source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh
pip install --no-build-isolation -e .

```

This will cause the above libur_loader error 

![Image]([地址已移除])


And if we uninstall pip installed oneapi and rebuild 
```
pip uninstall intel-cmplr-lib-rt  intel-cmplr-lib-ur intel-cmplr-lic-rt intel-pti intel-sycl-rt
pip install --no-build-isolation -e .
```

Error related to pti package will appear.

![Image]([地址已移除])


### Motivation for this issue

When users install PyTorch wheels (which bundle several packages in specific oneapi version), they are often unaware of the implicit oneAPI dependency. 

When build with sycl extension, users also need install the entire oneAPI packages (e.g., from Intel’s official sources) into their environment and source activate the env. 

However, there is a time gap between Intel’s oneAPI release and PyTorch’s support for the new version. 

When a oneAPI version mismatch occurs, the error messages shown is inconsistent with different scenario and do not explicitly indicate the root cause (oneAPI incompatibility). These cryptic error messages reference internal dependency packages (e.g., pti / libur_loader etc), which are unfamiliar to users. Consequently, users cannot determine how to resolve the version mismatch because they are unaware of the purpose of these dependencies.

Improve the error handling logic to detect oneAPI version mismatches explicitly. When detected, surface a clear, actionable error message that:

Clearly states the root cause: "oneAPI component version mismatch detected."
Lists the conflicting packages and their detected versions
Provides direct steps to resolve the issue, such as:

To fix this,  
1. let user know which oneapi packages is installed with current pytorch wheel 
2. where can user install oneapi which match the current pytorch wheel

nodes.body:
I think that the issue which user will face mixing different torch builds with different oneapi environments is highly dependent on the usage scenarios. For example, consider the very basic pytorch developer usage scenario when user builds pytorch itself with oneapi 2025.0. I.e.:
```
. /opt/intel/oneapi/compiler/2025.0/env/vars.sh
. /opt/intel/oneapi/umf/0.9/env/vars.sh
. /opt/intel/oneapi/pti/0.10/env/vars.sh
. /opt/intel/oneapi/ccl/2021.14//env/vars.sh
cd pytorch && python3 setup.py develop
```
Then if user activates 2025.1 environment, he will get this just importing torch:
```
. /opt/intel/oneapi/compiler/2025.0/env/vars.sh
. /opt/intel/oneapi/umf/0.9/env/vars.sh
. /opt/intel/oneapi/pti/0.10/env/vars.sh
. /opt/intel/oneapi/ccl/2021.14//env/vars.sh
python3 -c "import torch"
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/home/dvrogozh/git/pytorch/pytorch/torch/__init__.py", line 419, in <module>
    from torch._C import *  # noqa: F403
    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
ImportError: libpti_view.so.0.10: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```
And the error signature will change depending on which libraries will be found in the path and which exact step user has taken to activate oneapi environment.

So, one thing we need to do before digging into this issue is to itemize key usage scenarios we can face around this story.

nodes.body:
I think there are the following cases we need to consider at the moment:

* User installs pytorch xpu from wheels and activates oneAPI environment. Eventually, there are 3 cases depending on which oneAPI environment he activates (version B) in relevance to what oneAPI environment was used to build installed pytorch version (version A):
  * Versions match - everything's good
  * B > A - that's backward compatibility case. **This should work to import torch, but currently fails.** Basically that's the case @ZhaoqiongZ described in the issue. At the moment the failure here is actually not CPP extension issue - that's `import torch` issue and an be reproduced with:
```
$ python3 -c "import torch"
  File "/home/dvrogozh/pytorch.xpu2/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/__init__.py", line 418, in <module>
    from torch._C import *  # noqa: F403
    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
ImportError: /opt/intel/oneapi/2025.1/lib/libur_loader.so.0: version `LIBUR_LOADER_0.10' not found (required by /home/dvrogozh/pytorch.xpu2/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/lib/../../../../libsycl.so.8)
```
  * A < B - that's forward compatibility case. It should not work unless compatibility package exists and is installed.

* User builds extension with wrong pytorch version. Basically that's what will happen if user does not specify XPU index in extension pip install command. Extension will get built, but it will be unclear with which pytorch version it is compatible as it was built using pytorch where XPU support was not included at all. **We can add a check to SYCL CPP extension to avoid such use case entirely.**
```
$ git clone [地址已移除]
$ cd pytorch_examples/pytorch/extension-cpp-sycl

$ source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh
$ pip install -e .  # mind no --no-build-isolation

... here default CUDA torch version will be installed
... instead user should have used --index-url [地址已移除]
```


Further, if oneAPI backward compatibility will get fixed to `import torch`, then additional question for B >A case is whether extensions built with B should work with A. Here we step into forward compatibility and this might not work without compatibility packages.

I think there are the following cases we need to consider at the moment:

User installs pytorch xpu from wheels and activates oneAPI environment. Eventually, there are 3 cases depending on which oneAPI environment he activates (version B) in relevance to what oneAPI environment was used to build installed pytorch version (version A):

Versions match - everything's good
B > A - that's backward compatibility case. This should work to import torch, but currently fails. Basically that's the case @ZhaoqiongZ described in the issue. At the moment the failure here is actually not CPP extension issue - that's import torch issue and an be reproduced with:



$ python3 -c "import torch"
  File "/home/dvrogozh/pytorch.xpu2/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/__init__.py", line 418, in <module>
    from torch._C import *  # noqa: F403
    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
ImportError: /opt/intel/oneapi/2025.1/lib/libur_loader.so.0: version `LIBUR_LOADER_0.10' not found (required by /home/dvrogozh/pytorch.xpu2/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/lib/../../../../libsycl.so.8)



A < B - that's forward compatibility case. It should not work unless compatibility package exists and is installed.


User builds extension with wrong pytorch version. Basically that's what will happen if user does not specify XPU index in extension pip install command. Extension will get built, but it will be unclear with which pytorch version it is compatible as it was built using pytorch where XPU support was not included at all. We can add a check to SYCL CPP extension to avoid such use case entirely.


$ git clone [地址已移除]
$ cd pytorch_examples/pytorch/extension-cpp-sycl

$ source /opt/intel/oneapi/setvars.sh
$ pip install -e .  # mind no --no-build-isolation

... here default CUDA torch version will be installed
... instead user should have used --index-url [地址已移除]

Further, if oneAPI backward compatibility will get fixed to import torch, then additional question for B >A case is whether extensions built with B should work with A. Here we step into forward compatibility and this might not work without compatibility packages.

```
  File "/home/gta/kdrozd/kdrozd/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/multiprocessing/reductions.py", line 619, in reduce_storage
    fd, size = storage._share_fd_cpu_()
```

This is due to the fact that we are trying to pickle xpu tensor storage during model transfer to processes. I believe that for xpu we must do something similar.

issues.title: Validation Check List
issues.body:
We have set up an automatic mechanism to validate PyTorch XPU for PyTorch releases. The validation scope includes but not limited to all applicable unit test cases for both eager mode and compile mode, dynamo benchmarks, Windows and Linux, different Intel GPU platforms including iGPU and dGPU. 

However, we still found some corner cases that are not of the validation scope or cannot be automated easily. Therefore, we create a checklist here to record all the corner cases to guarantee the test scope.

- [ ] Check AOT binary for different platforms without jitting SYCL kernels
- [ ] Scan build logs including both torch-xpu-ops and Triton to ensure there are not newly warning and error message

cc @chuanqi129 , pls. feel free to add items to the check list.

### Versions

nodes.body:
I've checked issue also on CUDA with pytorch 2.8 and it is also visible there. After limiting model "box_detections_per_img" to 4 in inference mode:
[地址已移除]

test is passing on CUDA (test is comparing results from compile and eager mode). On XPU test is not passing even with "box_detections_per_img" set to 4 in inference.


Per my understanding issue is caused by discrepancies between compile and eager results (even on cuda - it is already mentioned in pytorch code:
[地址已移除])

There are for outputs from vision_maskrcnn model:
- boxes - object coordinates
- labels - object class
- score -  model confidence about the object
- masks - mask containing pixels which belong to specific object.

The point now is that all outputs are sorted by scores. That is, in boxes, values ​​start with the coordinates for the box with the highest score, and the same applies to labels.

And the problem is that scores can differ slightly (for compile/eager), and this can affect how the values ​​are sorted in the output. It's possible that for one implementation (eager), box label x has the highest score, while for compile, it's box label y. In our i.e. XPU case (box_detections_per_img=4):
- eager: 
```
DEBUG: correct_result=[{'boxes': tensor([[195.5549, 226.1746, 265.6295, 256.3354],
        [493.1869, 197.0160, 599.9907, 396.5140],
        [404.7639, 203.6848, 466.3620, 298.0402],
        [495.8043,  84.8642, 640.0000, 427.0000]], device='xpu:0'), 'labels': tensor([16, 31,  1,  1], device='xpu:0'), 'scores': tensor([0.9973, 0.9973, 0.9973, 0.9911], device='xpu:0'),
```
- compile:
```
DEBUG: new_result=[{'boxes': tensor([[492.3416, 197.1078, 601.0658, 397.2148],
        [194.3636, 225.8905, 265.8414, 257.4185],
        [404.4320, 203.6618, 466.1400, 298.0813],
        [496.3506,  84.7872, 639.8771, 427.0000]], device='xpu:0'), 'labels': tensor([31, 16,  1,  1], device='xpu:0'), 'scores': tensor([0.9976, 0.9975, 0.9975, 0.9911], device='xpu:0'),
```
As we can see above, the values ​​in score are quite similar, but they cause the outputs to be sorted differently.

I think the best way could be to compare vision model output using IoU method. Here is the draft:
[地址已移除]

issues.title: Functionality issues in TestCommon.test_out.
issues.body:
<!-- agent:status:NEEDS_HUMAN -->

## Summary
Multiple test cases in TestCommon.test_out are failing on XPU for float32 inputs. The active (non-struck-through) failures include test_out_triangular_solve, test_out_cholesky_inverse, test_out_geqrf, test_out_narrow_copy, and test_out_ormqr. One representative failure is test_out__native_batch_norm_legit_xpu_float32, which hits an INTERNAL ASSERT in the XPU BatchNorm kernel at BatchNormKernels.cpp:585 due to out_invstd not satisfying contiguity/shape constraints when a non-standard output tensor is passed via the `out=` argument.

## Test Info
- **Test Type:** ut
- **Category:** op correctness / out-variant contract
- **Dependency:** upstream
- **Platform:** xpu

## Failed Tests

## Root Cause Analysis
In BatchNormKernels.cpp, after resize_output(out_mean/out_invstd, {n_input}), the kernel asserts that the output tensors are contiguous. When test_out passes a non-standard (e.g., non-contiguous or strided) output tensor via the out= argument, resize_output resizes it but does not guarantee contiguity, causing the TORCH_INTERNAL_ASSERT at lines 596-603 and 900-903 to fire.

## Proposed Fix Strategy
In batch_norm_stats_xpu_template (around line 585) and the corresponding template at line 897, after resize_output calls, add contiguity enforcement: either call out_mean = out_mean.contiguous() / out_invstd = out_invstd.contiguous() and copy results back, or allocate fresh contiguous temporaries for the kernel and copy into the user-provided out tensors afterward. The same pattern should be applied at both call sites (lines 588-603 and 897-903) in /home/stonepia/torch-xpu-ops/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BatchNormKernels.cpp.

Root Cause Analysis
In BatchNormKernels.cpp, after resize_output(out_mean/out_invstd, {n_input}), the kernel asserts that the output tensors are contiguous. When test_out passes a non-standard (e.g., non-contiguous or strided) output tensor via the out= argument, resize_output resizes it but does not guarantee contiguity, causing the TORCH_INTERNAL_ASSERT at lines 596-603 and 900-903 to fire.
Proposed Fix Strategy
In batch_norm_stats_xpu_template (around line 585) and the corresponding template at line 897, after resize_output calls, add contiguity enforcement: either call out_mean = out_mean.contiguous() / out_invstd = out_invstd.contiguous() and copy results back, or allocate fresh contiguous temporaries for the kernel and copy into the user-provided out tensors afterward. The same pattern should be applied at both call sites (lines 588-603 and 897-903) in /home/stonepia/torch-xpu-ops/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BatchNormKernels.cpp.

test_matmul_mv_xpu_float32:
- XPU issue, not test wiring: matmul / addmv / mm go through the same oneDNN GPU matmul path.
- Repro is stable: all 3 APIs are numerically identical and show the same float32 large-reduction error (~7.6e-4).
- CPU is better on the same pattern (~2.7e-4), indicating backend-specific accumulation behavior.
- mkldnn.matmul.fp32_precision toggles do not change this outcome (not a TF32 switch issue).
- There is a possible fix via FP64/chunked accumulation in XPU addmv, but the trade-off is noticeable performance regression on this hot path.

Based on current evidence, this is expected numerics, not a confirmed oneDNN bug.

issues.title: [TorchAO]  Memory Efficient Optimizers
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch
## Motivation

As you know, memory consumption is a challenge for LLM task, especially for finetune task. Optimizers like ADAM can consume substantial GPU memory - 2x as much as the model parameters themselves. TorchAO provides two approaches to reduce this overhead. We need to enable it on the XPU device.

### What was done

**Tooling**
Piotr extended `benchmark_low_bit_adam.py` with a `--memory_profile` flag and wrote two companion scripts:
- `summarize_memory.py` — builds a peak-memory comparison table from snapshot `.pkl` files
- `extract_allocations.py` — classifies allocations by model module (Attention, MLP, etc.) and training phase (forward, backward, optimizer step), with a `--compare` mode for cross-device diffs and a `--module` drill-down

(Code available in [ao fork]([地址已移除]).)


**Experiments**
Model: `timm/vit_huge_patch14_224.orig_in21k` (630M params), batch size 8, BF16 AMP, 5 training steps with memory profiling.
Devices: Intel Arc B580 (XPU, 16.2 GB) vs. NVIDIA A100 (CUDA).
Modes: eager and compile.

Metrics measured:
- **Peak memory (GB)** per optimizer per device per mode
- **Memory ratio** vs. baseline (AdamW)
- **Module-level peak active memory** (MB) per phase
- **Op-level breakdown** inside Attention and MLP modules
- **XPU–CUDA delta** by configuration

Key findings:
| Configuration        | CUDA (GB) | XPU (GB) | Delta |
| -------------------- | --------- | -------- | ----- |
| Eager, AdamW         | 12.27     | 12.80    | +0.53 |
| Eager, AdamW8bitAo   | 8.36      | 8.90     | +0.54 |
| Compile, AdamW       | 12.22     | 12.81    | +0.59 |
| Compile, AdamW8bitAo | 8.29      | 8.87     | +0.58 |

The 8-bit optimizer reduces memory by ~32% on both devices (ratio 0.68–0.70). The ~0.5–0.6 GB XPU overhead is **stable across all optimizer and compilation combinations**, pointing to a fixed per-operation issue — not optimizer states, MLP, or autograd gradients (all identical across devices).

The Attention module is the sole culprit: `scaled_dot_product_attention` (SDPA) forward workspace is **+910 MB on XPU** vs. CUDA. All other components (MLP, optimizer, backward) are essentially equal.

---

### Final Diagnosis 

The root cause is **head dimension alignment** in PyTorch's attention dispatch ([source]([地址已移除])):

> Before calling the flash attention kernel, PyTorch pads Q, K, V's head dimension to a backend-specific alignment: **64 for XPU, 8 for CUDA**.

ViT-Huge uses `head_dim = 80` (1280 hidden / 16 heads):
- **XPU**: padded to **128** (next multiple of 64) — a **60% increase**
- **CUDA**: padded to **88** (next multiple of 8), then internally rounded to 96

XPU dispatches the 128-dim variant (it only supports fixed sizes {64, 96, 128, 192}), making every Q/K/V and workspace tensor across all **32 layers × 16 heads** approximately **33% larger** than on CUDA (128 vs. 96).

This single alignment difference accounts for essentially **the entire ~0.5–0.6 GB memory gap** between the XPU and CUDA backends. The TorchAO low-bit optimizers themselves are working correctly on XPU.

### Triage: #2127 — Path Coverage enhancement

**Level**: L3

**Case Summary**: This is a feature enhancement request (0 failing cases / 0 total).

**Analysis**:

This issue is a meta-level infrastructure investigation. The context is clear: PR #2073 exposed a latent bug in error handling (`src/ATen/native/xpu/mkl/BatchLinearAlgebra.cpp:57`) that lived in a code path never executed by tests. The original loop iterated over an empty `ids` vector, so the error-rethrow body never ran and the out-of-bounds issue remained undetected. The fix changed iteration to `errs` directly, enabling the error path to be exercised safely. Line coverage alone cannot surface such unreachable/untried branches; path/branch coverage is needed.

**Next Steps**:

- Confirm practical options and data formats: Many coverage tools emit branch/path information (e.g., gcc/clang’s `--coverage` `.gcda` reports include branch details; some static analyzers can flag unexecuted code). Identify whether branch/path coverage targets can be generated in this build system and whether they already exist or need new steps added.
- Assess integration trade-offs and platform constraints: Evaluate tooling availability on supported platforms, cost (build time, runtime overhead, storage), and whether integration aligns with existing CI stages.
- Provide actionable guidance: If immediate integration is infeasible, document quick wins (e.g., code patterns to write testable error paths, optional local/use-time branch coverage) and outline a roadmap for CI integration.

<!-- agent:status:IN_REVIEW -->

## Summary
The issue requests an enhancement to avoid unnecessary `copy_` calls in three FFT kernel output functions: `_fft_c2c_mkl_out`, `_fft_r2c_mkl_out`, and `_fft_c2r_mkl_out`. The goal is to improve performance by eliminating intermediate copy operations in these MKL-based FFT kernels.

## Type
- **Category:** performance
- **Platform:** xpu
- **Related Components:** _fft_c2c_mkl_out, _fft_r2c_mkl_out, _fft_c2r_mkl_out, FFT kernels, MKL backend

## Objective
Refactor the FFT kernel output functions to avoid the use of `copy_` and instead write results directly to the output tensor.

## Current Status


## Context



## Root Cause Analysis
The three `_out` variants (`_fft_c2c_mkl_out`, `_fft_r2c_mkl_out`, `_fft_c2r_mkl_out`) each call their non-`_out` counterpart (which allocates a fresh intermediate tensor), then call `resize_output` + `copy_` to move results into the caller-provided `out` tensor. This double-allocation and copy is avoidable because `_exec_fft` already accepts the output tensor directly.


## Proposed Fix Strategy
Refactor `_fft_c2c_mkl_out`, `_fft_r2c_mkl_out`, and `_fft_c2r_mkl_out` in `src/ATen/native/xpu/mkl/SpectralOps.cpp` to write directly into `out` (passing it through the existing `_exec_fft` / `_fft_with_size` call chain) instead of creating an intermediate result tensor and copying. This mirrors the pattern already used inside `_fft_c2c_mkl` for multi-pass transforms where `out` is passed directly to `_exec_fft`.

```
Let me also check: in `_fft_c2c_mkl_out`, when not doing type promotion, `final_out` is a reference to `out`. We call `resize_output(out, out_sizes)` before. Then `_exec_fft` calls `out.resize_(...)` to the batched shape, then `as_strided_` back. This should work correctly.

The code looks logically sound. Let me stage the changes:The changes look correct. Let me provide the summary:

- **What I changed:**
```

### Triage: #2140 — Consider how to avoid copy in FFT kernels

**Level**: L3

**Analysis**: This is a performance optimization request. The three FFT out-variant functions (`_fft_c2c_mkl_out`, `_fft_c2r_mkl_out`, `_fft_r2c_mkl_out`) all follow the same pattern: call the non-out variant (which allocates a new tensor), then `out.copy_(result)`. - Update the three out-variant wrappers to use the new in-path logic
- Add/update tests to verify behavior is unchanged and performance is improved via benchmarks
- Review for potential memory aliasing edge cases, especially with type promotions like `promote_fft_input`

## Triage Summary

**Owner Guess**: oneMKL / math backend

**Category**: performance

**Priority**: P3

**Confidence**: High

---

## Why

- The issue is specifically about avoiding `copy_` in oneMKL-based FFT kernel implementations in `torch-xpu-ops`
- The request targets three functions: `_fft_c2c_mkl_out`, `_fft_c2r_mkl_out`, and `_fft_r2c_mkl_out`
- Current implementation pattern creates intermediate result tensors then copies to output via `out.copy_(result)` at `src/ATen/native/xpu/mkl/SpectralOps.cpp` (approximately lines 267-272, 312-317, and 355-360)
- This is clearly a performance optimization request for MKL FFT operations rather than a correctness bug or environment issue

---

## Missing Info

- Performance benchmarks quantifying current `copy_` overhead
- Whether oneMKL DFT API supports writing directly to caller-provided buffers
- Expected output tensor characteristics (sizes, strides, memory format) from typical invocation contexts
- Compatibility with `ComplexHalf` type handling in optimization path

---

## Suspected Cause

- Current implementation design separates computation from output: underlying FFT functions create intermediate results, then `_fft_*_mkl_out` wrappers copy to provided output
- The `_fft_c2c_mkl`, `_fft_c2r_mkl`, and `_fft_r2c_mkl` implementations don't support writing directly to pre-allocated output tensors
- oneMKL DFT descriptor setup may require contiguous input/output buffers incompatible with arbitrary output tensor layouts

---

## Recommended Labels

- `owner: onemkl`
- `category: performance`
- `path: src/ATen/native/xpu/mkl/SpectralOps.cpp`

---

## Next Action

- Examine oneMKL DFT descriptor API to determine if `compute_forward`/`compute_backward` can write directly to caller-provided output buffers
- Investigate modifying `_fft_with_size`, `_exec_fft`, and `_mkl_dft` to accept and write directly to output tensors
- Prototype removing `copy_` by threading output tensor through the MKL DFT call chain
- Establish benchmarks to quantify improvement from eliminating the copies

Replying to [this mention]([地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#2140]).

## Triage Summary

- **Owner Guess:** torch-xpu-ops
- **Category:** performance (optimization)
- **Priority:** P3 (suggestion/optimization)
- **Confidence:** High

---

## Why

- After calling `at::empty()`/`at::clone()` inside `_fft_c2c_mkl`, `_fft_c2r_mkl`, and `_fft_r2c_mkl` to allocate buffers, the `*_out` wrappers perform an additional `out.copy_(result)`.
- This allocation + copy is safe and correct, but introduces an extra device memory copy that could be eliminated if outputs and workspaces were reused smarter.

---

## Missing Info

- Concrete performance impact or benchmark showing regression from the extra copies
- Specific tensor shapes/dtypes where the copy overhead is most noticeable

---

## Suspected Cause

- Current implementation returns a fresh tensor from the non-`_out` function, then resizes+copies into the `out` argument
- oneMKL DFT’s `compute_forward`/`compute_backward` require pre-allocated in/out buffers; if we could make the result allocation use the `out` buffer directly (with proper resizing and stride/order constraints), the copy might be avoided

---

## Suggested Directions (not a fix request)

1. Try refactoring so the `*_out` variant pre-allocates and owns the buffers passed to oneMKL, then reuses that as the final result where the caller’s `out` can be aliased or resized in place
2. Ensure any change preserves all current correctness guarantees (contiguity constraints, stride/alignment, hermitian symmetry, conjugate symmetry)
3. Validate large MS/ND and multi-dim transforms (sorted dims, workspace) under the new pattern

---

## Recommended Labels

- `owner: torch-xpu-ops`
- `category: performance`
- `path: src/ATen/native/xpu/mkl/SpectralOps.cpp`

---

## Next Action

If you’re driving this, prototype an in-buffer version of one FFT type (e.g., `_fft_c2c_mkl_out`) that allocates into `out` up front and passes it as the output buffer to oneMKL/`_exec_fft`, then validate correctness and compare measured memory traffic. Once one pattern is vetted, apply to `_fft_c2r_mkl_out` and `_fft_r2c_mkl_out`.

Root-caused and fixed in pytorch fork: [`c0f60b19`]([地址已移除]) on `daisyden/missing_test` (will land via pytorch/pytorch#181822).

### Root cause
`torch/nn/modules/activation.py:_check_arg_device` gated the MultiheadAttention NestedTensor fast path with an allowlist of `cpu`, `cuda`, and the privateuse1 backend name only. XPU is a real upstream backend (not privateuse1), so XPU tensors failed the device check, fell off the fast path, and tripped the assertion in `MultiheadAttention.forward`:

```
AssertionError: MultiheadAttention does not support NestedTensor outside of its fast path.
The fast path was not hit because some Tensor argument's device is neither one of cpu, cuda or privateuseone.
```

The companion module `torch/nn/modules/transformer.py` already includes `"xpu"` in its parallel `_supported_device_type` lists at lines 509–514 and 892–897, so this was simply an asymmetry between `activation.py` and `transformer.py`.

### Fix
Add `"xpu"` to the `_check_arg_device` allowlist (and update the matching diagnostic message). Two-line change.

Covers all three cases listed in this issue:
- `test_nn_xpu::TestNNDeviceTypeXPU::test_transformerencoderlayer_xpu_float16`
- `test_nn_xpu::TestNNDeviceTypeXPU::test_transformerencoderlayer_xpu_float32`
- `test_transformers_xpu::TestTransformersXPU::test_with_nested_tensor_input_xpu`

issues.body:
<!-- agent:status:NEEDS_HUMAN -->

## Summary
This is a tracking issue to enable FP8 and MXFP8 operations on XPU, covering memory ops (fill, flip, index_put, gather, cat, eq, ne, where, empty/zeros/ones, to, copy, clone, add/sub/mul/div, compare, normal) and GEMM ops (_scaled_mm and _scaled_grouped_mm) across multiple FP8 variants (e4m3fn, e4m3fnuz, e5m2, e5m2fnuz, e8m0fnu). The issue tracks support status with green/yellow/red indicators and links to related PRs, targeting PyTorch releases from 2.10 through 2.16.

## Type
- **Category:** feature-gap
- **Platform:** xpu
- **Related Components:** FP8/MXFP8 kernels, memory ops (fill, flip, index_put, index_select, gather, cat, eq, ne, where, empty/zeros/ones, to, copy, clone, add/sub/mul/div, compare, normal), GEMM ops (_scaled_mm, _scaled_grouped_mm)

## Objective
Enable FP8/MXFP8 support for a set of memory and GEMM operations across all FP8 dtype variants (e4m3fn, e4m3fnuz, e5m2, e5m2fnuz, e8m0fnu), with CUDA alignment for scaled matrix multiply ops.

|                     | MxFP8(E4M3/E5M2)    | 32-element 1D block scaling                   | UE8M0           | Tiled Tensor  |    🟡    |        | 2.16    |

## Context
Labels: dtype: float8. Related PRs: #2190, #2152, #2145, #2154, #2258, pytorch/pytorch#165978, pytorch/pytorch#173630. PyTorch release targets range from 2.10 to 2.16.


## Root Cause Analysis
This is a tracking issue (not a bug report) for incrementally enabling FP8 and MXFP8 operations on XPU. Several memory ops (add/sub/mul/div, compare, normal) and GEMM ops (_scaled_mm with block scaling and MXFP8, _scaled_grouped_mm) are partially implemented (🟡) or missing. The gaps are in kernel implementations within torch-xpu-ops for arithmetic/comparison ops on FP8 dtypes, and GEMM ops for advanced scaling modes.


## Proposed Fix Strategy
This is a multi-PR tracking issue. Individual sub-tasks are tracked via linked PRs (e.g., #2145 for add/sub/mul/div, #2154 for compare). Each unfinished item requires separate kernel implementations in torch-xpu-ops. No single agent action closes this issue — it is an umbrella tracker that must be resolved incrementally as sub-PRs land.

    """????????????????"""
    if torch.cuda.is_available():
        device = torch.device("cuda")
        device_type = "cuda"
    elif hasattr(torch, 'xpu') and torch.xpu.is_available():
        device = torch.device("xpu")
        device_type = "xpu"
    else:
        device = torch.device("cpu")
        device_type = "cpu"
    
    print(f"Using device: {device_type.upper()}")
    return device, device_type


def get_memory_info(device_type: str) -> Dict[str, float]:
    """????????????????"""
    memory_info = {}
    
    if device_type == "cuda":
        memory_info["allocated"] = torch.cuda.memory_allocated() / 1024**3  # GB
        memory_info["reserved"] = torch.cuda.memory_reserved() / 1024**3   # GB
        memory_info["max_allocated"] = torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / 1024**3  # GB
        memory_info["max_reserved"] = torch.cuda.max_memory_reserved() / 1024**3    # GB
        
        device_props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(0)
        memory_info["total"] = device_props.total_memory / 1024**3  # GB
        
    elif device_type == "xpu":
        memory_info["allocated"] = torch.xpu.memory_allocated() / 1024**3  # GB
        memory_info["reserved"] = torch.xpu.memory_reserved() / 1024**3   # GB
        memory_info["max_allocated"] = torch.xpu.max_memory_allocated() / 1024**3  # GB

    return memory_info


def print_memory_info(device_type: str, prefix: str = ""):
    """????????????"""
    if device_type == "cpu":
        return
    
    memory_info = get_memory_info(device_type)
    print(f"\n{prefix}Memory Info ({device_type.upper()}):")
    print("-" * 50)
    for key, value in memory_info.items():
        print(f"{key:15}: {value:.3f} GB")

    batch_size: int = 1,

Hi @LuFinch, I agree that Dropout should be set to 0; however, memory usage remains high when performing quantization using AutoRound.

After investigating further, I made a new discovery.

When `attn_mask` is not `None`, the MATH backend is triggered, because the FLASH implementation on XPU does not yet support this feature.

Is it correct? Do we have the plan to support attn_mask?

issues.title: the supported dtypes are not align with cuda
issues.body:
<!-- agent:status:NEEDS_HUMAN -->

## Summary
XPU operator dtype support does not align with CUDA. Multiple ops (addmm, addmv, baddbmm, histogram, mv, conv variants, einsum, mm, embedding_bag, linear, matmul, tensordot, bmm, bilinear, linalg_multi_dot, addbmm) fail test_dtypes, test_noncontiguous_samples, test_numpy_ref, and test_multiple_devices checks because XPU does not support the same set of dtypes (e.g. int64, complex32) as CUDA.

## Type
- **Category:** feature-gap
- **Platform:** xpu
- **Related Components:** addmm, addmv, baddbmm, histogram, histogramdd, mv, nn.functional.conv1d, nn.functional.conv2d, nn.functional.conv3d, nn.functional.conv_transpose1d, einsum, mm, nn.functional.embedding_bag, nn.functional.linear, matmul, tensordot, bmm, addbmm, nn.functional.bilinear, linalg.multi_dot, true_divide

## Objective
Align XPU supported dtypes with CUDA for all listed operators so that test_dtypes, test_noncontiguous_samples, test_numpy_ref, and test_multiple_devices tests pass on XPU.

## Current Status


## Context
Tests are in third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/test_ops_xpu.py (TestCommonXPU). Some cases are struck through in the issue body indicating they may already be resolved. Labels include duplicate, skipped, ut_upstream, agent:active.


## Root Cause Analysis
XPU kernels for multiple operators (addmm, addmv, baddbmm, histogram, mv, conv variants, einsum, mm, embedding_bag, linear, matmul, tensordot, bmm, addbmm, bilinear, linalg.multi_dot) do not dispatch on the same set of dtypes as their CUDA counterparts. This causes test_dtypes and related tests to fail because XPU is missing support for types like int64 and complex32.


## Proposed Fix Strategy
Each operator's XPU kernel (in src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/) needs its AT_DISPATCH macro updated to include the missing dtypes, and the underlying SYCL kernels need to handle those types. This is operator-by-operator work across 20+ ops.


## Target Repository
torch-xpu-ops


## Agent Assessment
**Verdict:** NEEDS_HUMAN

**Why this needs human intervention:**
Feature-gap / umbrella enablement issue requiring dtype support additions across 20+ operators — not a single fixable bug.

**Root Cause:** XPU kernels for multiple operators (addmm, addmv, baddbmm, histogram, mv, conv variants, einsum, mm, embedding_bag, linear, matmul, tensordot, bmm, addbmm, bilinear, linalg.multi_dot) do not dispatch on the same set of dtypes as their CUDA counterparts. This causes test_dtypes and related tests to fail because XPU is missing support for types like int64 and complex32.

**Proposed Fix Strategy:** Each operator's XPU kernel (in src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/) needs its AT_DISPATCH macro updated to include the missing dtypes, and the underlying SYCL kernels need to handle those types. This is operator-by-operator work across 20+ ops.

Related Components: addmm, addmv, baddbmm, histogram, histogramdd, mv, nn.functional.conv1d, nn.functional.conv2d, nn.functional.conv3d, nn.functional.conv_transpose1d, einsum, mm, nn.functional.embedding_bag, nn.functional.linear, matmul, tensordot, bmm, addbmm, nn.functional.bilinear, linalg.multi_dot, true_divide

Objective
Align XPU supported dtypes with CUDA for all listed operators so that test_dtypes, test_noncontiguous_samples, test_numpy_ref, and test_multiple_devices tests pass on XPU.
Current Status
Context
Tests are in third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/test_ops_xpu.py (TestCommonXPU). Some cases are struck through in the issue body indicating they may already be resolved. Labels include duplicate, skipped, ut_upstream, agent:active.
Root Cause Analysis
XPU kernels for multiple operators (addmm, addmv, baddbmm, histogram, mv, conv variants, einsum, mm, embedding_bag, linear, matmul, tensordot, bmm, addbmm, bilinear, linalg.multi_dot) do not dispatch on the same set of dtypes as their CUDA counterparts. This causes test_dtypes and related tests to fail because XPU is missing support for types like int64 and complex32.
Proposed Fix Strategy
Each operator's XPU kernel (in src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/) needs its AT_DISPATCH macro updated to include the missing dtypes, and the underlying SYCL kernels need to handle those types. This is operator-by-operator work across 20+ ops.

**Details:**
1) `test_reference_numerics_extremal__refs_acos_xpu_complex64`

| Problematic input | XPU output | Expected output |
|-------------------|------------|-----------------|
| `inf+infj` | `0.7853981256484985-infj` | `0.7853981852531433-infj` |
| `inf-infj` | `0.7853981256484985+infj` | `0.7853981852531433+infj` |

**Explanation:** Although, the real part satisfies the `rtol` and `atol` tolerances, the `torch.isclose` call still returns `False` for these cases. Looking at the actual implementation of `torch.isclose` we see that:

a) the first check fails (because the numbers are not exactly equal):

```cpp
Tensor close = self == other;
```

b) the allowed and actual errors turn out not to be finite:

```cpp
  Tensor allowed_error = atol + (rtol * cast_other).abs();
  Tensor actual_error = (cast_self - cast_other).abs();

  // Computes finite closeness
  close.__ior__(
      at::isfinite(actual_error).__iand__(actual_error <= allowed_error));
```

For this particular input, `allowed_error = inf` and `actual_error = nan`.

**Possible solution:** Separately compare the real and imaginary parts of the complex numbers.


2) `test_reference_numerics_extremal__refs_acosh_xpu_complex64`

| Problematic input | XPU output | Expected output |
|-------------------|------------|-----------------|
| `inf+infj` | `inf+0.7853981256484985j` | `inf+0.7853981852531433j` |
| `inf-infj` | `inf-0.7853981256484985j` | `inf-0.7853981852531433j` |

**Explanation:** Fails for the same reason as in 1), but here the imaginary part differs.
**Possible solution:** Separately compare the real and imaginary parts of the complex numbers.

nodes.body:
@EikanWang This is not related to `reciprocal_math`.

There are two separate issues here:

### 1️⃣ Sign mismatch for complex special values
For certain inputs involving `inf`/`nan`, the imaginary part sign differs between backends.  
For example, for `acos`:

- CPU (NumPy reference): `nan + infj`  
- XPU: `nan - infj`  

So the discrepancy is in the **sign of the infinite imaginary component**, not a general precision issue.

### 2️⃣ Comparison artifact with infinities
Even when results look identical, `assert_close` / `assert_equal` may fail because internally it computes differences, for acosh:

```python
inf - inf = nan
```
This can lead to reported nan differences during comparison, even if both tensors contain inf at the same positions.

I made a small test for acos
```python
import torch

z = torch.tensor(
    [complex(float('inf'), float('nan'))],
    dtype=torch.complex64
)

print("Input (CPU):", z)
print("acos (CPU):", torch.acos(z))

if torch.xpu.is_available():
    z_xpu = z.to("xpu")
    print("Input (XPU):", z_xpu)
    print("acos (XPU):", torch.acos(z_xpu))
```

@chunhuanMeng This aligns with my initial analysis. Let me provide a bit more information:

> ### 1️⃣ Sign mismatch for complex special values
> For certain inputs involving `inf`/`nan`, the imaginary part sign differs between backends. For example, for `acos`:
> 
> * CPU (NumPy reference): `nan + infj`
> * XPU: `nan - infj`
> 
> So the discrepancy is in the **sign of the infinite imaginary component**, not a general precision issue.

This problem is masked in the `torch.isclose` function, because of the argument `equal_nan=True` - in case either the real or imaginary part is NaN, the whole number is treated as NaN and if both of them are "considered" as NaNs, the function returns True. E.g., `torch.isclose(actual=nan - inf*j, expected=nan + inf*j, equal_nan=True) == True`. I tried to implement a comparison function for comparing the real part separately of the imaginary part, but this revealed the mentioned problem.

> ### 2️⃣ Comparison artifact with infinities
> Even when results look identical, `assert_close` / `assert_equal` may fail because internally it computes differences, for acosh:
> 
> inf - inf = nan
> This can lead to reported nan differences during comparison, even if both tensors contain inf at the same positions.
> 
> I made a small test for acos
> 
> import torch
> 
> z = torch.tensor(
>     [complex(float('inf'), float('nan'))],
>     dtype=torch.complex64
> )
> 
> print("Input (CPU):", z)
> print("acos (CPU):", torch.acos(z))
> 
> if torch.xpu.is_available():
>     z_xpu = z.to("xpu")
>     print("Input (XPU):", z_xpu)
>     print("acos (XPU):", torch.acos(z_xpu))

This is the problem, I described in comment [地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#2257] 

For instance, when computing `acos` for `inf+infj`, we should get `pi/4 - inf * j`. Both the XPU output and the Numpy references are more or less equal to this number, but between XPU and Numpy there is a precision discrepancy on approx. the 8th digit (see example below). The `torch.isclose` function first compares if the numbers are **exactly** equal, otherwise it computes the `actual_error` and `allowed_error`, which for non-finite complex numbers yields NaN/Inf for the error computations.

```
XPU:   0.7853981||256484985 - inf * j 
Numpy: 0.7853981||852531433 - inf * j
```

nodes.body:
I investigated the `acos` behavior with input `inf + NaN*j` and observed the following results:

|  Compiler / Platform  | Result (real, imag) |
|--------------------|-------------------|
| icpx host           | NaN, +Inf         |
| icpx XPU            | NaN, +Inf         |
| GCC host            | NaN, -Inf         |
| NVCC host           | NaN, -Inf         |
| NVCC CUDA device    | NaN, -Inf         |

From this, we can see that the difference in output is due to **different implementations of `std::acos` in the compiler's standard library / math backend**, rather than a bug in PyTorch or device computation.
cc @EikanWang

### Automated fix: intel/torch-xpu-ops#2270 **Status:** `DONE` - fix verified on BMG, patch exported for human review. | Stage | Status | |---|---| | Triage | done - single bug, reproducer present | | Reproduce | REPRODUCED (skip marker was hiding it) | | Root cause | done - missing XPU dispatch for `aten::_flash_attention_forward` | | Implement | done - 7 files in `pytorch` | | Verify | PASSED - lint clean |
Triage | Field | Value | |---|---| | issue_type | single-bug | | scope | `test/xpu/test_decomp_xpu.py::TestDecompXPU::test_comprehensive_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16` | | reproduction_missing | no | | runtime_dependencies | SYCL-TLA (FlashAttention kernels in torch-xpu-ops) | | handling | agent-fixable | *Automated by issue-triage.*

As collected today the case is **skipped**, not failed: upstream's OpInfo for `torch.ops.aten._flash_attention_forward` carries a blanket `skipXPU` decorator, so the case reports `SKIPPED test doesn't work on XPU backend`. Per the reproduce contract an XPU skip marker is treated as potentially hiding the failure, so it was removed in place for one run and then reverted. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_comprehensive_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16` | REPRODUCED | `NotImplementedError: The operator 'aten::_flash_attention_forward' is not currently implemented for the XPU device.` | The original report showed a `'CPU' backend` variant of the same error; that was the XPU-fallback path (`PYTORCH_ENABLE_XPU_FALLBACK=1`) re-dispatching the unimplemented op to CPU, which has no kernel for it either. Root cause `aten::_flash_attention_forward` / `aten::_flash_attention_backward` are dispatched to CUDA only in `aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml`; there is no `XPU:` entry. torch-xpu-ops already ships the kernels (`sycltla::_flash_attention_forward` / `_flash_attention_backward` in `src/ATen/native/transformers/xpu/flash_attn/flash_api.cpp`, landed in intel/torch-xpu-ops#3404), and the older entry points there are already marked `// Deprecated: Use _flash_attention_forward instead.` - but nothing in PyTorch binds them to the XPU dispatch key, so the op is unimplemented on XPU. The blanket `skipXPU` on the OpInfo masks this in CI, which is why the case currently reports SKIPPED rather than FAILED. - **target_repo:** `pytorch` - **domain:** transformers / SDPA - **Known upstream work:** `pytorch/pytorch#181559` adds the two dispatch entries and the `_flash_attention_forward_xpu` / `_flash_attention_backward_xpu` wrappers. It is approved but has been unmerged and stale since September 2026, and it does **not** remove the OpInfo `skipXPU`, so landing it alone would leave this case skipped. *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement All seven files are in `pytorch`. Review in this order: 1. **Carried verbatim from `pytorch/pytorch#181559`** - the `XPU:` dispatch entries, the `_flash_attention_forward_xpu` / `_flash_attention_backward_xpu` wrappers forwarding to the existing torch-xpu-ops `sycltla::` kernels, the meta-kernel `device_hint` fix, and the `c_shim_xpu.h` entry. Taken as-is rather than re-derived so this does not become a third variant of a change that has already been reviewed upstream. 2. **The delta that actually unskips this issue's case** - the OpInfo's blanket `skipXPU` is replaced with `skipXPUIf(not PLATFORM_SUPPORTS_FLASH_ATTENTION_XPU, ...)`, mirroring the gate the same OpInfo already uses for CUDA. The OpInfo's `skips=` list already carries `device_type=('cuda', 'xpu')` entries that are dead while the blanket skip is in place. 3. **A gap that unskipping exposed** - the OpInfo's XPU dtypes are inherited from `dtypesIfCUDA`, which resolves to float16 only on a machine with no CUDA device, while the XPU kernels accept fp16 and bf16 (`mha_fwd` asserts exactly that pair). `dtypesIfXPU` / `backward_dtypesIfXPU` now state both, which is what `test_dtypes` checks. 4. `torch/csrc/stable/c/shim_function_versions.txt` was added by `lintrunner` as the required companion manifest for the versioned c_shim symbol introduced in (1). One hunk of `pytorch/pytorch#181559` is **deliberately not carried over**: its removal of the `test/inductor/test_torchinductor_opinfo.py` expected-failure entry for this op. That removal was a no-op there (the blanket `skipXPU` meant the case never ran), but once the case does run, `test_torchinductor_opinfo` fails with `None mismatch: None is not tensor(...)` on BMG - so the entry still describes a real gap and is kept. *Automated by fix-implement.*

Regression checks on the fixed build: | Suite | Result | |---|---| | `test_decomp_xpu.py -k flash_attention_forward` | 2 passed | | `test_ops_xpu.py -k flash_attention_forward` | 6 passed | | `test_meta_xpu.py -k flash_attention_forward` | 6 passed, 6 skipped | | `test/inductor/test_torchinductor_opinfo.py -k "flash_attention_forward and xpu"` | 1 xfailed | | `test_transformers_xpu.py` (full) | 147 failed, 48553 passed, 37460 skipped | The transformers suite was run in full because this patch reroutes `_scaled_dot_product_flash_attention_xpu` through `at::_flash_attention_forward`. All 147 failures match entries already in `test/xpu/skip_list_common.py` for that file - every one is pre-existing, none are new. - **Verdict:** PASSED - **Lint:** clean (`lintrunner` over the changed files) - **Caveat:** verified on BMG only; PVC was not exercised. Per the verify contract the "before" was a nightly wheel and the "after" a source build with the fix, so this does not by itself prove the change is what made the test pass - though the op being unregistered before and registered after is directly observable. *Automated by fix-verify.*
Summary The failing case is not a decomposition bug: `aten::_flash_attention_forward` simply has no XPU dispatch entry in PyTorch, even though torch-xpu-ops has shipped the SYCL-TLA kernels for months, and the op's OpInfo carries a blanket `skipXPU` that turns the resulting failure into a skip. The fix registers both the forward and backward ops for XPU - reusing the approved-but-stale upstream change `pytorch/pytorch#181559` verbatim for that part - and then replaces the blanket skip with the same hardware-capability gate the OpInfo already uses for CUDA, correcting the XPU dtype declarations that unskipping exposes. nodes.body:
Progres update.

After initial problems with fitting the models in memory (OOM), quantization benchmark enablement is progressing (see: [Enable benchmarks/quantization for XPU]([地址已移除])]. Encountering new problems, for example:
- int4_groupwise_weight_float8_rowwise_activation: `ImportError: Requires mslk >= 1.0.0` — failed on all attention (q/k/v/o) and MLP (gate/up/down) weight conversions, followed by RuntimeError: We encountered some issues during automatic conversion of the weights.
- int4_groupwise_hqq_weight_only: `AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled` — HQQ int4 path requires CUDA, incompatible with XPU-only build.
- nvfp4: `AssertionError: NVFP4 DYNAMIC mode is only supported on sm100+ machines` — targets Blackwell hardware, not applicable to Intel XPU.
- mxfp8: quantized and saved successfully (1.546 GB) but lm-eval crashed 

Regarding float8/int8/int4/nf4 benchmarks enablement, there was a problem with XPU always reporting self device time = 0.
Related issue has been closed ([地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#3985]) and the fix is confirmed to work. The work can be continued.

Work for [\[TorchAO\] Adapt LLAMA3 benchmark to XPU]([地址已移除]) has not yet started.

# AI Triage 

 Even with dropout off, XPU's peak memory before checkpointing is 4.50 GiB,
  compared with about 2.41 GiB on CUDA, so case1 still has no feasible plan. Here is which attention kernel XPU picks for each input type:

 # XPU SDPA backend selection

Backend chosen by `torch._fused_sdp_choice` on XPU for `q/k/v` of shape `(8, 16, 1024, 64)`, `is_causal=True`.

| dtype | requires_grad | dropout_p | XPU backend |
|---|---|---|---|
| float32  | False | 0.0 | OVERRIDEABLE (oneDNN) |
| float32  | False | 0.1 | **MATH** |
| float32  | True  | 0.0 | **MATH** |
| float32  | True  | 0.1 | **MATH** |
| bfloat16 | False | 0.0 | OVERRIDEABLE (oneDNN) |
| bfloat16 | False | 0.1 | **MATH** |
| bfloat16 | True  | 0.0 | FLASH_ATTENTION |
| bfloat16 | True  | 0.1 | **MATH** |
| float16  | False | 0.0 | OVERRIDEABLE (oneDNN) |
| float16  | False | 0.1 | **MATH** |
| float16  | True  | 0.0 | FLASH_ATTENTION |
| float16  | True  | 0.1 | **MATH** |

## Why

| Backend | Constraint on XPU | Source |
|---|---|---|
| OVERRIDEABLE (oneDNN) | no grad, no dropout | `aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/Attention.cpp:63,74` |
| FLASH_ATTENTION | fp16/bf16 only, no dropout | `aten/src/ATen/native/transformers/xpu/sdp_utils.cpp:178` |
| EFFICIENT_ATTENTION | not implemented, falls back to MATH | `aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/Attention.cpp:236` |

## Impact on `test_sac_ilp.py`

The test trains an fp32 model with `dropout_p=0.1`, so XPU always uses MATH, which stores the full attention matrix per layer. CUDA uses memory-efficient attention, which supports fp32 + grad + dropout.

| | Baseline peak memory (no AC) | `case1` (1.6 GiB budget) | `case2` (2.4 GiB budget) |
|---|---|---|---|
| CUDA | ~2.41 GiB | feasible | no AC needed |
| XPU, dropout=0.1 | 6.08 GiB | infeasible | AC on 4 layers |
| XPU, dropout=0.0 | 4.50 GiB | infeasible | AC on 4 layers |

Parity gap: XPU needs a memory-efficient attention kernel supporting fp32, training (grad) and dropout.



  The test trains an fp32 model, so XPU always falls back to MATH, which stores the full 1024×1024 attention matrix in every layer. On CUDA the
  memory-efficient kernel handles fp32, training and dropout together.

  On XPU no fused kernel covers that case:
  - oneDNN fused: only works when nothing needs gradients (mkldnn/xpu/Attention.cpp:74) and doesn't support dropout.
  - Flash: fp16/bf16 only, no dropout (transformers/xpu/sdp_utils.cpp:178).
  - Memory-efficient: not implemented; it silently falls back to MATH (mkldnn/xpu/Attention.cpp:236).

issues.title: [oneAPI][backward compatibility] libur_loader.so.0: version `LIBUR_LOADER_0.11' not found
issues.body:
On:
 * Ubuntu 24.04
 * Intel Data Center GPU Max

Usage scenario:
 * User installs pytorch of some version
 * User installs oneAPI of some version
 * User intends to use pytorch and oneAPI for separate sub-tasks (i.e. there is no user intent to use installed oneAPI in pytorch workflow and vice versa). However, pytorch and oneAPI sub-tasks might be ingredients of bigger common workflow.
 * User activates oneAPI environment within existing pytorch environment

Issue:
 * If activated oneAPI version does not match the version of oneAPI used in the selected version of pytorch user will see the following failure:

```
$ pip install torch==2.8 --index-url [地址已移除]
$ pip install numpy
$ python -c "import torch; print(torch.xpu.is_available())"
True

$ . /opt/intel/oneapi/2025.2/oneapi-vars.sh
$ python -c "import torch; print(torch.xpu.is_available())"
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/home/dvrogozh/pt2.8/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/__init__.py", line 416, in <module>
    from torch._C import *  # noqa: F403
    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
ImportError: /opt/intel/oneapi/2025.2/lib/libur_loader.so.0: version `LIBUR_LOADER_0.11' not found (required by /home/dvrogozh/pt2.8/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/lib/../../../../libsycl.so.8)
```

**Expectation:**
* Pytorch is using RPATH pointing to pinned versions of oneAPI runtime distributed with pytorch itself. Expectation is that pytorch will continue to run regardless whether user installed and sourced environment of some other version of oneAPI.

CC: @riverliuintel @chuanqi129

finetune command: run in [peft folder]([地址已移除])

python olora_finetuning.py \
        --base_model hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-BNB-NF4 \
        --init_lora_weights gaussian \
      --seed 42 \
      --torch_dtype bfloat16 \
      --device_map xpu:0 \
      --output_dir ./output

```
NF4                   | cuda  | triton|  ipex | sycl
--------------------- | ----- | ----- | ----- | -----
time per step (s/it)  | 0.95  | 1.16  | 1.16  | 1.16
```

nodes.body:
```python
"""
Standalone SDPA memory benchmark (OP level) extracted from the QLoRA SFT training
of hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-BNB-NF4.

Captured from the real training run (single process, no DDP):
    q/k/v shape : [1, 32, S, 128]   (batch=1, num_heads=32, head_dim=128)
    seq length  : packed, variable, up to 2048  (default max_length)
    dtype       : float32           (as seen entering F.scaled_dot_product_attention)
    attn_mask   : explicit bool mask [1, 1, S, S]  (block-diagonal / packing)
    is_causal   : False
    scale       : 1/sqrt(128) = 0.08838834764831845

The key point for the XPU memory regression: training passes an *explicit* bool
attn_mask (because of sequence packing) with is_causal=False. This prevents the
flash / SYCLTLA path and falls back to the math backend, which materializes the
full [B, H, S, S] score matrix -> the extra memory.

This script measures peak device memory of a forward+backward over SDPA for the
different backends and for the two relevant call patterns:
  A) explicit bool mask, is_causal=False  (what training actually does)
  B) is_causal=True, no explicit mask     (flash-friendly reference)

Run on XPU:   python sdpa_mem_benchmark.py --device xpu
Run on CUDA:  python sdpa_mem_benchmark.py --device cuda
"""
import argparse
import math

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def get_device(name):
    if name == "auto":
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            return "cuda"
        if hasattr(torch, "xpu") and torch.xpu.is_available():
            return "xpu"
        return "cpu"
    return name


def mem_reset(device):
    if device == "cuda":
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    elif device == "xpu":
        torch.xpu.empty_cache()
        torch.xpu.reset_peak_memory_stats()


def mem_peak(device):
    if device == "cuda":
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        return torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / 1024**3
    if device == "xpu":
        torch.xpu.synchronize()
        return torch.xpu.max_memory_allocated() / 1024**3
    return 0.0


def build_inputs(b, h, s, d, dtype, device, requires_grad=True):
    q = torch.randn(b, h, s, d, dtype=dtype, device=device, requires_grad=requires_grad)
    k = torch.randn(b, h, s, d, dtype=dtype, device=device, requires_grad=requires_grad)
    v = torch.randn(b, h, s, d, dtype=dtype, device=device, requires_grad=requires_grad)
    return q, k, v


def causal_bool_mask(b, s, device):
    # lower-triangular True (keep) -> mimic the explicit packing mask shape [b,1,s,s]
    m = torch.tril(torch.ones(s, s, dtype=torch.bool, device=device))
    return m.view(1, 1, s, s).expand(b, 1, s, s)


def run_once(q, k, v, attn_mask, is_causal, scale, backend, device):
    mem_reset(device)
    ctx = None
    if backend is not None:
        from torch.nn.attention import sdpa_kernel, SDPBackend
        name = {
            "math": SDPBackend.MATH,
            "efficient": SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION,
            "flash": SDPBackend.FLASH_ATTENTION,
        }[backend]
        ctx = sdpa_kernel(name)
    try:
        if ctx is not None:
            ctx.__enter__()
        out = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
            q, k, v, attn_mask=attn_mask, is_causal=is_causal, scale=scale
        )
        loss = out.float().pow(2).mean()
        loss.backward()
        peak = mem_peak(device)
        ok = True
        err = ""
    except Exception as e:  # backend not supported for this config
        peak = float("nan")
        ok = False
        err = type(e).__name__ + ": " + str(e).splitlines()[0][:80]
    finally:
        if ctx is not None:
            ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
    for t in (q, k, v):
        t.grad = None
    return ok, peak, err


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--device", default="auto")
    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--heads", type=int, default=32)
    ap.add_argument("--head_dim", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--seq", type=int, default=2048)
    ap.add_argument("--dtype", default="bfloat16",
                    choices=["bfloat16", "float32", "float16"])
    args = ap.parse_args()

    device = get_device(args.device)
    dtype = getattr(torch, args.dtype)
    b, h, s, d = args.batch, args.heads, args.seq, args.head_dim
    scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(d)

    print(f"device={device} dtype={args.dtype} shape=[{b},{h},{s},{d}] scale={scale:.6f}")
    score_gb = b * h * s * s * torch.empty((), dtype=dtype).element_size() / 1024**3
    print(f"full [B,H,S,S] score tensor = {score_gb:.3f} GB (per materialization)\n")

    patterns = [
        ("A: explicit bool mask, is_causal=False (training)", causal_bool_mask(b, s, device), False),
        ("B: is_causal=True, no mask (flash-friendly ref)", None, True),
    ]
    backends = [None, "math", "efficient", "flash"]

    for title, mask, is_causal in patterns:
        print(f"== {title}")
        for be in backends:
            q, k, v = build_inputs(b, h, s, d, dtype, device)
            ok, peak, err = run_once(q, k, v, mask, is_causal, scale, be, device)
            label = be if be else "auto"
            if ok:
                print(f"   {label:10s} peak={peak:6.3f} GB")
            else:
                print(f"   {label:10s} UNSUPPORTED  ({err})")
            del q, k, v
        print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

  falls back to **math**, which materializes the full `[B,H,S,S]` score matrix.

"""
Standalone SDPA memory benchmark (OP level) extracted from the QLoRA SFT training
of hugging-quants/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct-BNB-NF4.

Captured from the real training run (single process, no DDP):
    q/k/v shape : [1, 32, S, 128]   (batch=1, num_heads=32, head_dim=128)
    seq length  : packed, variable, up to 2048  (default max_length)
    dtype       : float32           (as seen entering F.scaled_dot_product_attention)
    attn_mask   : explicit bool mask [1, 1, S, S]  (block-diagonal / packing)
    is_causal   : False
    scale       : 1/sqrt(128) = 0.08838834764831845

The key point for the XPU memory regression: training passes an *explicit* bool
attn_mask (because of sequence packing) with is_causal=False. This prevents the
flash / SYCLTLA path and falls back to the math backend, which materializes the
full [B, H, S, S] score matrix -> the extra memory.

This script measures peak device memory of a forward+backward over SDPA for the
different backends and for the two relevant call patterns:
  A) explicit bool mask, is_causal=False  (what training actually does)
  B) is_causal=True, no explicit mask     (flash-friendly reference)

Run on XPU:   python sdpa_mem_benchmark.py --device xpu
Run on CUDA:  python sdpa_mem_benchmark.py --device cuda
"""
import argparse
import math

import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def get_device(name):
    if name == "auto":
        if torch.cuda.is_available():
            return "cuda"
        if hasattr(torch, "xpu") and torch.xpu.is_available():
            return "xpu"
        return "cpu"
    return name


def mem_reset(device):
    if device == "cuda":
        torch.cuda.empty_cache()
        torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
    elif device == "xpu":
        torch.xpu.empty_cache()
        torch.xpu.reset_peak_memory_stats()


def mem_peak(device):
    if device == "cuda":
        torch.cuda.synchronize()
        return torch.cuda.max_memory_allocated() / 1024**3
    if device == "xpu":
        torch.xpu.synchronize()
        return torch.xpu.max_memory_allocated() / 1024**3
    return 0.0


def build_inputs(b, h, s, d, dtype, device, requires_grad=True):
    q = torch.randn(b, h, s, d, dtype=dtype, device=device, requires_grad=requires_grad)
    k = torch.randn(b, h, s, d, dtype=dtype, device=device, requires_grad=requires_grad)
    v = torch.randn(b, h, s, d, dtype=dtype, device=device, requires_grad=requires_grad)
    return q, k, v


def causal_bool_mask(b, s, device):
    # lower-triangular True (keep) -> mimic the explicit packing mask shape [b,1,s,s]
    m = torch.tril(torch.ones(s, s, dtype=torch.bool, device=device))
    return m.view(1, 1, s, s).expand(b, 1, s, s)


def run_once(q, k, v, attn_mask, is_causal, scale, backend, device):
    mem_reset(device)
    ctx = None
    if backend is not None:
        from torch.nn.attention import sdpa_kernel, SDPBackend
        name = {
            "math": SDPBackend.MATH,
            "efficient": SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION,
            "flash": SDPBackend.FLASH_ATTENTION,
        }[backend]
        ctx = sdpa_kernel(name)
    try:
        if ctx is not None:
            ctx.__enter__()
        out = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
            q, k, v, attn_mask=attn_mask, is_causal=is_causal, scale=scale
        )
        loss = out.float().pow(2).mean()
        loss.backward()
        peak = mem_peak(device)
        ok = True
        err = ""
    except Exception as e:  # backend not supported for this config
        peak = float("nan")
        ok = False
        err = type(e).__name__ + ": " + str(e).splitlines()[0][:80]
    finally:
        if ctx is not None:
            ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
    for t in (q, k, v):
        t.grad = None
    return ok, peak, err


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    ap.add_argument("--device", default="auto")
    ap.add_argument("--batch", type=int, default=1)
    ap.add_argument("--heads", type=int, default=32)
    ap.add_argument("--head_dim", type=int, default=128)
    ap.add_argument("--seq", type=int, default=2048)
    ap.add_argument("--dtype", default="bfloat16",
                    choices=["bfloat16", "float32", "float16"])
    args = ap.parse_args()

    device = get_device(args.device)
    dtype = getattr(torch, args.dtype)
    b, h, s, d = args.batch, args.heads, args.seq, args.head_dim
    scale = 1.0 / math.sqrt(d)

    print(f"device={device} dtype={args.dtype} shape=[{b},{h},{s},{d}] scale={scale:.6f}")
    score_gb = b * h * s * s * torch.empty((), dtype=dtype).element_size() / 1024**3
    print(f"full [B,H,S,S] score tensor = {score_gb:.3f} GB (per materialization)\n")

    patterns = [
        ("A: explicit bool mask, is_causal=False (training)", causal_bool_mask(b, s, device), False),
        ("B: is_causal=True, no mask (flash-friendly ref)", None, True),
    ]
    backends = [None, "math", "efficient", "flash"]

    for title, mask, is_causal in patterns:
        print(f"== {title}")
        for be in backends:
            q, k, v = build_inputs(b, h, s, d, dtype, device)
            ok, peak, err = run_once(q, k, v, mask, is_causal, scale, be, device)
            label = be if be else "auto"
            if ok:
                print(f"   {label:10s} peak={peak:6.3f} GB")
            else:
                print(f"   {label:10s} UNSUPPORTED  ({err})")
            del q, k, v
        print()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

nodes.body:
## Process Summary

**Problem**
When tf32_on_and_off() enables TF32 on XPU,  `test_Conv2d_size_1_kernel_xpu` and `test_ConvTranspose2d_size_1_kernel_xpu` failed the accuracy check on XPU when TF32 was enabled.
```text
Greatest absolute difference: 0.008617401123046875 (up to 0.005 allowed)
```

The failure was concentrated in `weight.grad`; the errors in `forward` and `bias.grad` were very small.

**Investigation**

1. **PyTorch-side reproduction**: Created `repro_xpu_tf32_conv.py` using the same `Conv2d(3, 3, kernel_size=1)` configuration and compared it against a CPU reference. This confirmed that the `weight_grad` error was approximately `8.8e-3` with TF32 enabled and approximately `9.5e-7` with TF32 disabled. This verified that the error came specifically from the TF32 `convolution_backward_weights` path.

2. **Attempted an independent reproduction with oneDNN BenchDNN**:
   - Built BenchDNN from the same oneDNN commit used by PyTorch, oneDNN v3.12.0.
   - Used the corresponding convolution descriptor, `mb2_ic3ih5oc3oh5kh1ph0`, with `--dir=BWD_W`.
   - Ran both strict mode and `--attr-fpmath=tf32`.
   - Result: both cases passed. BenchDNN did **not** reproduce the ACC failure.

3. **Root cause identified**: After reading the BenchDNN source in `dnnl_common.cpp`, we found that BenchDNN intentionally reduces the reference precision according to `fpmath_mode`:

```cpp
switch (attr.fpmath_mode.mode) {
    case dnnl_fpmath_mode_strict: break;
    case dnnl_fpmath_mode_tf32: dt_ = dnnl_bf16; break;  // The reference also uses bf16 precision
    ...
}
```

In other words, the official oneDNN test framework considers TF32 to be expected to produce precision loss comparable to bf16. Therefore, it lowers the precision of its reference computation and adjusts its comparison behavior accordingly, rather than treating this precision loss as a bug.

This explains why BenchDNN could not reproduce the ACC issue: from oneDNN’s perspective, this is expected behavior by design, not a bug.

**Final Conclusion and Solution**

Since oneDNN itself treats this level of TF32 precision loss as expected, the PyTorch tests should not continue to require XPU TF32 to meet a tolerance close to strict FP32 precision, such as `0.005`.

Therefore, the final solution was to widen the tolerance on the PyTorch test side instead of filing this as a oneDNN defect.

In test/nn/test_convolution.py:

```python
from torch.testing._internal.common_utils import (
    ...
    TEST_WITH_ROCM,
    TEST_XPU,
    ...
)
```

```python
@onlyAccelerator
@tf32_on_and_off(0.01 if TEST_WITH_ROCM or TEST_XPU else 0.005)
def test_Conv2d_size_1_kernel(self, device): ...

@onlyAccelerator
@tf32_on_and_off(0.01 if TEST_WITH_ROCM or TEST_XPU else 0.005)
def test_ConvTranspose2d_size_1_kernel(self, device): ...
```

This reuses the existing `0.01` tolerance already used for ROCm instead of introducing a new XPU-specific value. Both XPU tests passed local validation.

The CUDA branch is unaffected and continues to use the stricter `0.005` tolerance.

Ran both strict mode and --attr-fpmath=tf32.
Result: both cases passed. BenchDNN did not reproduce the ACC failure.



Root cause identified: After reading the BenchDNN source in dnnl_common.cpp, we found that BenchDNN intentionally reduces the reference precision according to fpmath_mode:


switch (attr.fpmath_mode.mode) {
    case dnnl_fpmath_mode_strict: break;
    case dnnl_fpmath_mode_tf32: dt_ = dnnl_bf16; break;  // The reference also uses bf16 precision
    ...
}
In other words, the official oneDNN test framework considers TF32 to be expected to produce precision loss comparable to bf16. Therefore, it lowers the precision of its reference computation and adjusts its comparison behavior accordingly, rather than treating this precision loss as a bug.
This explains why BenchDNN could not reproduce the ACC issue: from oneDNN’s perspective, this is expected behavior by design, not a bug.
Final Conclusion and Solution
Since oneDNN itself treats this level of TF32 precision loss as expected, the PyTorch tests should not continue to require XPU TF32 to meet a tolerance close to strict FP32 precision, such as 0.005.
Therefore, the final solution was to widen the tolerance on the PyTorch test side instead of filing this as a oneDNN defect.
In test/nn/test_convolution.py:
from torch.testing._internal.common_utils import (
    ...
    TEST_WITH_ROCM,
    TEST_XPU,
    ...
)
@onlyAccelerator
@tf32_on_and_off(0.01 if TEST_WITH_ROCM or TEST_XPU else 0.005)
def test_Conv2d_size_1_kernel(self, device): ...

@onlyAccelerator
@tf32_on_and_off(0.01 if TEST_WITH_ROCM or TEST_XPU else 0.005)
def test_ConvTranspose2d_size_1_kernel(self, device): ...
This reuses the existing 0.01 tolerance already used for ROCm instead of introducing a new XPU-specific value. Both XPU tests passed local validation.
The CUDA branch is unaffected and continues to use the stricter 0.005 tolerance.

In Python it is `torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32` (`torch/backends/mkldnn/__init__.py:118`). `torch.xpu.is_tf32_supported()` already exists (`torch/xpu/__init__.py:329`), so the gate has everything it needs. Wall time grows where the TF32 pass now genuinely runs (`test_efficient_conv_bn_eval.py` 7:40 -> 11:26, `test_aot_inductor.py` 1:45 -> 3:33) -- that is the extra pass doing real work. - **Verdict:** PASSED -- the helpers drive oneDNN on XPU, and no suite gained a failure. - **Lint:** clean. `lintrunner` / `spin` are not installed in this container, so flake8, `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` were run directly against the repo config; the two `FURB110` hits `ruff` reports in `test_torch.py` are pre-existing on `origin/main` (confirmed against the base file) and were left alone. Two limits on this verdict, for the reviewer: there is no CUDA device on this runner, so "CUDA behaviour is unchanged" rests on reading the gate (the `TEST_XPU` guard and the per-device `is_tf32_supported()` branch) rather than on a CUDA run; and the regression sweep covers the call sites reachable here, not the whole XPU CI suite. *Automated by fix-verify.*
Summary **Outcome:** IMPLEMENTING(fix_verified). `tf32_on_and_off()` and its four sibling helpers in `torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py` only ever drove the cuBLAS/cuDNN flags, so on an XPU device the decorated body ran once with TF32 never enabled; XPU takes TF32 from oneDNN's fpmath mode instead, which the helpers now toggle through `torch.backends.mkldnn.flags` while the gate asks each device type for its own `is_tf32_supported()`. Running that pass on XPU for the first time exposed three tests written to NVIDIA's TF32 budget -- the two `size_1_kernel` conv tests at `0.0086` and `test_cdist_large` at `0.0067` against `0.005` -- which now take the `0.01` ROCm already uses for exactly these paths. Verification ran every `tf32_on_and_off` call site reachable on this host twice, once with the patched helpers and once with the stock ones: the three tests above went FAIL to PASS and no other suite changed its failure set. The fix is in pytorch, not in this repo, so the patch lands as a pytorch PR; note that the feature was also attempted upstream in `pytorch/pytorch#201528` and `pytorch/pytorch#190958` (both open drafts, neither landed), so a human should reconcile with those before opening another. - **Branch:** `agent/fix-issue-2400` (in the pytorch checkout) - **Base:** `06413cc8b6c62042fb8b85a410e40ea04048d112` - **Changed files:** `torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py`, `test/nn/test_convolution.py`, `test/test_torch.py` - **Follow-up, deliberately not in this patch:** `test/xpu/test_gemm.py:36-131` carries a private XPU-only copy of these five helpers, written the same way; it can now be deleted in favour of the shared ones, which is a separate ~95-line cleanup over 28 tests. - **Nothing was pushed.** The patch is exported as a workflow artifact for a human to review and apply.

Automated by fix-reproduce.



Root Cause
Analyzed at pytorch origin/main@06413cc8b6c.
The five TF32 test helpers in torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py only know about CUDA. tf32_off() (line 487) and tf32_on() (line 514) drive torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 plus a torch.backends.cudnn.flags(allow_tf32=...) context; tf32_enabled() (line 531) does the same; and tf32_on_and_off() gates the double run on cond = torch.cuda.is_tf32_supported() and only_if, narrowed further by torch.device(kwargs['device']).type == 'cuda' (lines 588-590). On an XPU device cond is therefore always false: the decorated body runs once, with TF32 neither enabled nor deliberately disabled, so every XPU test behind the decorator silently loses its TF32 pass -- including the 28 decorated tests in test/xpu/test_gemm.py.
XPU's TF32 switch is a different flag. oneDNN's fpmath mode is set from at::Context::allowTF32OneDNN() for both matmul (aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/detail/Matmul.cpp:202-206) and convolution (aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/detail/Utils.cpp:585-587), and nothing else in ATen reads that flag, so toggling it is inert for CUDA and CPU. In Python it is torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32 (torch/backends/mkldnn/__init__.py:118). torch.xpu.is_tf32_supported() already exists (torch/xpu/__init__.py:329), so the gate has everything it needs. One constraint shapes the implementation: common_utils calls disable_global_flags(), so a test process may not assign torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32 directly -- only the flags() context manager is permitted, and its signature defaults (enabled=False, allow_tf32=True, fp32_precision="none" at torch/backends/mkldnn/__init__.py:102) mean "set to this", not "leave alone", so every unrelated argument has to be passed as None.
Turning the TF32 pass on for XPU then exposes a tolerance gap of its own: test_Conv2d_size_1_kernel and test_ConvTranspose2d_size_1_kernel (test/nn/test_convolution.py:3379 and :3411) allow 0.01 for ROCm but 0.005 otherwise, and oneDNN's TF32 conv backward-weights loss on XPU exceeds 0.005. That is expected precision for oneDNN rather than a kernel bug -- benchdnn lowers its own reference to bf16 when fpmath_mode=tf32, which is why the issue thread could not reproduce it as a oneDNN defect -- so those two decorators need the existing ROCm-grade tolerance on XPU as well.

Verdict: IMPLEMENTING -- extend the existing helpers in place; no new module, no backend change.
Target repo: pytorch
Domain: upstream-pytorch

Prior art that touches the same function, for collision awareness: pytorch/pytorch#201528 (open draft, same in-place approach) and pytorch/pytorch#190958 (open draft, moves the helpers into a new torch/testing/_internal/common.py). Neither has landed; both stalled on rebase conflicts in common_cuda.py, which is one reason this fix stays as small as possible.
Automated by fix-root-cause.
