nodes.body:
Two subtests fail (pin_memory=True, share_memory=False and pin_memory=True, share_memory=True). Both fail because StateDictStager gates pinning on torch.cuda.is_available(), which is False on XPU-only systems.

Even bypassing that check, the CUDA-specific cudaHostRegister path would crash on XPU. The XPU equivalent (prepare_for_device_copy from sycl_ext_oneapi_copy_optimize) page-locks memory for DMA but does not register the pointer in SYCL's USM allocation table — so sycl::get_pointer_type() returns unknown and is_pinned() remains False.

**Case breakdown:**

- pin=True, share=False — solvable: allocate upfront from XPUCachingHostAllocator instead of in-place registration
- pin=True, share=True — blocked: requires in-place registration of shared memory as USM host type, which needs a SYCL API that doesn't exist yet
- 
The missing SYCL API was previously requested in CMPLRLLVM-70326 (closed as "implement when needed"). This issue represents the concrete use case. Synchronization with the SYCL/DPC++ team is in progress to either reopen or file a follow-up ticket requesting full USM host registration for externally-allocated pointers.

**Current Status**
I've contacted @guangyey who led the effort to add prepare_for_device_copy. Currently we're waiting for a SYCL runtime API that can register an externally-allocated pointer (e.g. from shared memory) into SYCL's USM allocation table as usm::alloc::host, so that sycl::get_pointer_type() returns host and consequently is_pinned() returns True.

Starting automated fix on this issue. Follow progress in the [workflow run]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659236033]). ### Stage 1 - Triage `single-bug`, reproducer present. Target repo is upstream `pytorch/pytorch` (`torch/distributed/checkpoint/_state_dict_stager.py` plus the XPU pinned-memory plumbing in ATen), not this repo. ### Stage 2 - Reproduce: REPRODUCED Reproduced on the nightly XPU wheel `2.16.0.dev20261027+xpu` using the upstream test file (no third-party fork needed), on BMG (`Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics`), oneAPI 2026.1.1: ``` python -m pytest -v test/distributed/checkpoint/test_state_dict_stager.py::TestStateDictStager::test_tensor_pinned_and_shared ``` ``` SUBFAILED (pin_memory=True, share_memory=False) - Booleans mismatch: False is not True SUBFAILED (pin_memory=True, share_memory=True) - Booleans mismatch: False is not True UserWarning: Ignoring pin_memory flag for checkpoint staging as pinning memory requires CUDA, but CUDA is not available. ``` ### Stage 3 - Root cause Two layers, matching the analysis already in this thread: 1. `StateDictStager.__init__` gates pinning on `torch.cuda.is_available()` and pins through `torch.cuda._pin_memory_utils`, which calls `cudaHostRegister`. On an XPU-only box the gate silently drops `pin_memory`, so `is_pinned()` is `False` for both failing sub-tests. 2. There is no XPU equivalent of `cudaHostRegister` in PyTorch. XPU's `isPinnedPtr()` only answers `sycl::get_pointer_type(...) == usm::alloc::host`, which holds only for memory SYCL itself allocated, so in-place pinning of an already-allocated (and, for `share_memory=True`, shm-backed) buffer cannot be observed. I measured the SYCL side directly rather than assuming (standalone DPC++ program, oneAPI 2026.1.1, BMG): | probe | result | |---|---| | `prepare_for_device_copy` on a `MAP_SHARED` mapping | succeeds | | ... on an unaligned `malloc` pointer | succeeds | | `get_pointer_type` after registering | still `unknown` | | device-to-host `queue.memcpy` into the registered range | correct data | | `release_from_device_copy` after the host buffer is freed | succeeds | | two disjoint ranges registered inside one page | succeeds | So the page-locking primitive already exists and already works on shared memory; the only missing piece is that SYCL's USM table cannot be told about it. ### Stage 4 - Fix Have PyTorch keep its own record of host-registered ranges rather than wait for SYCL to expose one - which is in effect what CUDA does too, since the table behind `cudaPointerGetAttributes` belongs to the CUDA runtime, not to any allocator: - `at::xpu::hostRegister/hostUnregister/isHostRegistered` wrap `prepare_for_device_copy`/`release_from_device_copy` and keep an ordered map of the registered ranges (ordered, so an interior address answers too, as it does on CUDA - XPU's copy fast path in this repo queries `isPinnedPtr()` with offset pointers). `XPUHooks::isPinnedPtr()` consults it after the USM-type query. - exposed as `torch._C._xpu_hostRegister/_xpu_hostUnregister`, with `torch/xpu/_pin_memory_utils.py` mirroring the CUDA module of the same name. - the stager resolves `_pin_memory_utils` from `torch.accelerator` instead of hardcoding CUDA, which is what `staging.py` next to it already does. A backend shipping no such module keeps the old warn-and-disable behaviour. **This needs no compiler update**, so `pin=True, share=True` is fixed now rather than waiting on CMPLRLLVM-70326. 7 files, ~115 lines, all in `pytorch/pytorch`; nothing in this repo, so there is no second patch to land. ### Stage 5 - Verify: PASSED Source build `torch 2.16.0a0+gitc5c9a00`, `TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc`, oneAPI 2026.1.1, BMG: ``` python -m pytest -v test/distributed/checkpoint/test_state_dict_stager.py ``` | | whole file | `test_tensor_pinned_and_shared` | |---|---|---| | before | `2 failed, 16 passed` | 2 of 4 sub-tests fail | | after | `16 passed, 16 subtests passed` | all 4 sub-tests pass | Both runs are on the same build - the "before" column was produced by reverting only the two Python files, so collection and binaries are identical and the comparison is apples to apples. `lintrunner -a` reports no lint issues on the changed files.
Summary Both failing sub-tests come from one bug with two layers: checkpoint staging only pinned memory when CUDA was available, and PyTorch had no XPU counterpart of `cudaHostRegister` underneath it. The fix makes the stager resolve its pinning helpers from `torch.accelerator`, and adds `at::xpu::hostRegister` on top of `sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::prepare_for_device_copy` with PyTorch keeping its own ordered map of registered ranges, which `isPinnedPtr()` consults - the one piece SYCL cannot provide, and the reason this thread was waiting on a new SYCL API. Taking that route fixes the `share_memory=True` case too, on the shipping 2026.1 compiler rather than a future one, so the fix no longer depends on CMPLRLLVM-70326. Verified on a source build: the whole file goes from `2 failed, 16 passed` to `16 passed, 16 subtests passed`, with the before run taken on the same binaries so nothing else moved. One related spot was deliberately left alone as out of scope and is worth a human's eye: `torch/distributed/_state_dict_utils.py::_create_cpu_state_dict` still imports `torch.cuda._pin_memory_utils` directly for its share-plus-pin path, which the same accelerator-generic treatment would fix. - **Branch:** `agent/fix-issue-2404` (in a `pytorch/pytorch` checkout) - **Base:** `c5c9a00715c54fdf9e3498c529cd8e7fe714d636` - **Changed files:** `aten/src/ATen/xpu/CachingHostAllocator.cpp`, `aten/src/ATen/xpu/CachingHostAllocator.h`, `aten/src/ATen/xpu/detail/XPUHooks.cpp`, `torch/_C/__init__.pyi.in`, `torch/csrc/xpu/Module.cpp`, `torch/distributed/checkpoint/_state_dict_stager.py`, `torch/xpu/_pin_memory_utils.py` - **Nothing was pushed.** The patch is exported as a workflow artifact for a human to review and apply.
_Generated by [fix job]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659236033])._

One comment per sub-item, since a bare verdict on a batch does not say which test it means and is dropped. `run=` only when judging a run other than the newest, in both places too. The expanded weights backward pass on XPU fails to propagate gradients to the input tensor, leaving input.grad as None. When the test then calls input.grad.clone(), it raises AttributeError. Check if the XPU backward implementations in third_party/torch-xpu-ops/src/ATen/native/xpu/ properly support the per-sample-grad path.

nodes.body:
**Status**: Managed to reproduce issue in `functorch/test_ops_xpu.py`. Looks like memory issue at the SYCL kernel side.

---

## What's Happening

The test `test_vmapjvpvjp_max_pool2d_with_indices_backward_xpu_float32` hangs for 60+ seconds, then crashes with a Windows access violation (`c0000005`) inside the SYCL runtime.

**Root Cause**: Heap corruption within SYCL's kernel JIT compilation path, triggered by nested `vmap/jvp/vjp` transforms calling `max_pool2d_with_indices_backward` on XPU.

---

## Reproduction (Minimal Test)

```bash
pytest -xvs functorch/test_ops_xpu.py -k "vmapjvpvjp and max_pool2d_with_indices_backward and float32"
```

**Expected behavior**: Hangs ~60-120 seconds, then crashes with Windows access violation (`c0000005`).

---

## Native Stack Evidence (Windows CDB Debugger)

The crash occurs in this exact execution sequence:

```
torch_cpu::at::_ops::max_pool2d_with_indices::call
  ↓ (functorch vmap/jvp/vjp dispatch)
torch_xpu::at::native::xpu::max_pool2d_with_indices_backward_kernel
  ↓
sycl8::sycl::_V1::detail::get_kernel_bundle_impl
  ↓
sycl8::sycl::_V1::ext::oneapi::experimental::detail::build_from_source
  ↓
sycl8::sycl::_V1::ext::intel::experimental::pipe_base::wait_non_blocking  [×4 nested calls]
  ↓
ntdll::RtlFreeHeap  ← heap corruption occurs here
  ↓
python312::Py_DumpTracebackThreads+0x47c  ← access violation crash point (c0000005)
```

The `wait_non_blocking` function is called **4 times in nested sequence** before a heap free operation, indicating recursive allocation/deallocation issues within SYCL's kernel JIT build pipeline.

---

## Evidence Artifacts

All captured via Windows CDB debugger with comprehensive dump:

- **CDB Log**: `cdb.log` (full stack trace + all threads)
- **Stderr**: `stderr.log` (timeout markers, AV exception details)
- **Stdout**: `stdout.log` (test progress at hang point)

---

## Root Cause Assessment

**Affected Component**: SYCL Runtime (`sycl8::ext::oneapi::experimental::detail::build_from_source`)

**Issue Type**: Heap corruption / use-after-free in kernel JIT build pipeline

**Specific Problem**: 
- Nested `wait_non_blocking` calls suggest recursive GPU task queue management
- Heap free (`RtlFreeHeap`) within nested wait loops indicates memory lifecycle mismanagement


- Crash occurs specifically when XPU dispatches functorch transforms with complex autodiff paths

**Trigger Conditions**:
- Requires: nested `vmap/jvp/vjp` transforms
- Requires: `max_pool2d_with_indices_backward` operation on XPU
- Requires: float32 data type
---



## Next Steps
1. Investigate cited `test_decomp.py` to confirm if there is similar issue.
2. Confirm stability of the reproduction environment (especially used flags, methodology)
3. After confirmation that SYCL memory managament issue is the root and not coincidence

issues.title: Host may stuck when submit too many kernels when event recording
issues.body: ### 🐛 Describe the bug run this reproducer as an example. If remove event record, it will be fine. Note l0 event pool size is 256 by default ```python import torch import time import os a = torch.randn(1024,1024,1024, device="xpu") b = torch.randn(1, device="xpu") @torch.compile def my_kernel(a, b): return a + b a = my_kernel(a, b) torch.xpu.synchronize() repeat = 20000 s = [torch.xpu.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(repeat)] e = [torch.xpu.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(repeat)] t = [0 for _ in range(repeat)] os.environ["PTI_ENABLE_COLLECTION"] = "1" for i in range(repeat): t1 = time.time() s[i].record() a = my_kernel(a, b) e[i].record() t2 = time.time() t[i] = t2 - t1 torch.xpu.synchronize() for i in range(repeat): print(s[i].elapsed_time(e[i]), t[i]) ``` ### Versions PVC, main branch, oneapi 2025.2
issues.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
run this reproducer as an example. If remove event record, it will be fine. Note l0 event pool size is 256 by default

import torch
import time
import os
a = torch.randn(1024,1024,1024, device="xpu")
b = torch.randn(1, device="xpu")

@torch.compile
def my_kernel(a, b):
    return a + b
a = my_kernel(a, b)
torch.xpu.synchronize()

repeat = 20000
s = [torch.xpu.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(repeat)]
e = [torch.xpu.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(repeat)]
t = [0 for _ in range(repeat)]
os.environ["PTI_ENABLE_COLLECTION"] = "1"
for i in range(repeat):
    t1 = time.time()
    s[i].record()
    a = my_kernel(a, b)
    e[i].record()
    t2 = time.time()
    t[i] = t2 - t1
torch.xpu.synchronize()
for i in range(repeat):
    print(s[i].elapsed_time(e[i]), t[i])


Versions
PVC, main branch, oneapi 2025.2

issues.title: test_cuda.py gaps
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

[ ] TestCuda cannot run all the test because the counterpart of torch.cuda.host_memory_stats, torch.cuda.cudart(), torch.cuda.memory._set_allocator_settings,  torch.backends.cuda.preferred_blas_library, torch.cuda.DoubleTensor, torch.cuda.FloatStorage, torch.IntStorage no supported.

[ ] TestCudaMallocAsync cannot run because the conterpart of  torch.cuda.memory_snapshot is not supported.

compile = False

    @parametrize("device", _DEVICES)

    def test_bf16_stochastic_round(self, device, compile):
        x = torch.rand(32, device=device) * 100

        x_rep_bf16 = func(x_rep)

issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

When we use autocast decorator in diffusers: [L168]([地址已移除]) on Intel XPU device, it throws warning: `UserWarning: In XPU autocast, but the target dtype is not supported. Disabling autocast.
  XPU Autocast only supports dtypes of torch.bfloat16, torch.float16 currently.` And the autocast does not take effect. Can you add fp32 datatype support like CUDA? I suppose just a `to` operation is OK.

@kaixuanliu Thanks for raising the issue. CUDA has a special path in autocast: [地址已移除] For the other devices, `device_supported_dtypes` is `[torch.bfloat16, torch.float16]` so that autocast is not enabled for float32.
Your goal is to promote dtype to float32 in the scenario you mentioned, right?

nodes.body: Yes.
nodes.bodyText: Yes.

nodes.body:
Two actions are required to support `torch.float32` in XPU autocast:

- Ensure that all existed ATen Ops supports float32 dtype and `to` supports conversions from all dtypes to float32.
- Allow XPU float32 autocast in `autocast_mode.py`.
nodes.bodyText:
Two actions are required to support torch.float32 in XPU autocast:

Ensure that all existed ATen Ops supports float32 dtype and to supports conversions from all dtypes to float32.
Allow XPU float32 autocast in autocast_mode.py.

nodes.body:
@kaixuanliu I think this behavior is expected. Currently, XPU autocast only supports half and bfloat16. On CUDA, autocast may accept fp32 as an input dtype, but it effectively becomes a no-op. Please refer to [地址已移除]
In PyTorch, autocast is designed to convert fp32 to lower-precision types (fp16/bf16) only.

issues.title: [upstream_ut]  RuntimeError: Cannot swap t2 because it has weakref associated with it ; RuntimeError: _apply(): Co
issues.body:
<!-- agent:status:NEEDS_HUMAN -->

## Summary
The test_module_to test in FakeTensorOperatorInvariants fails with a RuntimeError when calling module.to(device_type). The error occurs because torch.utils.swap_tensors cannot swap a tensor (t2) that has a weakref associated with it, causing _apply() to fail when trying to swap Linear.weight.

## Test Info
- **Test Type:** ut
- **Category:** fake_tensor
- **Dependency:** upstream
- **Platform:** xpu

## Failed Tests
- `test/test_fake_tensor.py::FakeTensorOperatorInvariants::test_module_to`

## Error Log
```
Command: cd <pytorch> && PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 pytest -v test/test_fake_tensor.py -k test_module_to
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/daisyden/miniforge3/envs/freeze/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 986, in _apply
    torch.utils.swap_tensors(param, param_applied)
  File "/home/daisyden/miniforge3/envs/freeze/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/utils/__init__.py", line 47, in swap_tensors
    raise RuntimeError("Cannot swap t2 because it has weakref associated with it")
RuntimeError: Cannot swap t2 because it has weakref associated with it

The above exception was the direct cause of the following exception:

Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/home/daisyden/upstream/test_nestedtensor/test/test_fake_tensor.py", line 1731, in test_module_to
    m.to(device_type)
  File "/home/daisyden/miniforge3/envs/freeze/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 1383, in to
    return self._apply(convert)
  File "/home/daisyden/miniforge3/envs/freeze/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/nn/modules/module.py", line 990, in _apply
    raise RuntimeError(
RuntimeError: _apply(): Couldn't swap Linear.weight

To execute this test, run the following from the base repo dir:
    python test/test_fake_tensor.py FakeTensorOperatorInvariants.test_module_to

This message can be suppressed by setting PYTORCH_PRINT_REPRO_ON_FAILURE=0
```

## Reproducer
```bash
cd <pytorch> && PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 pytest -v test/test_fake_tensor.py -k test_module_to
```

## Commit Scope


## Root Cause Analysis
The test_module_to test fails because swap_tensors raises RuntimeError when t2 (the newly created param_applied tensor) has a weakref. In the normal FakeTensorMode (non-PropagateRealTensors), FakeTensor internals or the XPU backend are creating weakrefs on fake tensors during the .to() operation. The upstream test hardcodes 'cuda' and passes on CUDA because CUDA's FakeTensor path doesn't create these weakrefs, but the XPU device_type path does. This is likely caused by XPU-specific FakeTensor handling or caching that holds weakrefs to intermediate tensors.

## Proposed Fix Strategy
Investigate whether FakeTensorMode or XPU-specific dispatch is creating weakrefs on tensors during .to() conversion. The fix likely belongs in torch/_subclasses/fake_tensor.py or the XPU backend's tensor creation path. Alternatively, swap_tensors in torch/utils/__init__.py could be updated to clear weakrefs on t2 before swapping (since t2 is the newly created tensor and its weakrefs are transient). Another option: check if nn/modules/module.py _apply() should handle this case more gracefully.

pytorch

issues.title: [upstream_ut] torch.ops.aten._flash_attention_forward lack of support for XPU.
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_schema_check.TestSchemaCheckModeOpInfoXPU,test_schema_correctness_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16

There is lack of support for `_flash_attention_forward` operation on XPU.
Currently PyTorch tries to dispatch to CPU, but there is no CPU implementation (only CUDA).

There is a need to implement the `_flash_attention_forward` operation for XPU.

Reproduce command:
```
cd pytorch; pip install -r .ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt; cd third_party/torch-xpu-ops/xpu; PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 pytest -v test_meta_xpu.py::TestMetaXPU -k test_meta_outplace_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16
```

🐛 Describe the bug
Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_schema_check.TestSchemaCheckModeOpInfoXPU,test_schema_correctness_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16
There is lack of support for _flash_attention_forward operation on XPU.
Currently PyTorch tries to dispatch to CPU, but there is no CPU implementation (only CUDA).
There is a need to implement the _flash_attention_forward operation for XPU.
Reproduce command:
cd pytorch; pip install -r .ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt; cd third_party/torch-xpu-ops/xpu; PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 pytest -v test_meta_xpu.py::TestMetaXPU -k test_meta_outplace_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16

issues.title: SYCL compilation flag -fsycl-id-queries-fit-in-int does not work as expected for TriuTril kernel.
issues.body:
This issue is created to track unexpected behavior observed when launching sycl kernels on XPU.

## Problem description

During SYCL code build the flag `-fsycl-id-queries-fit-in-int` is the default one: [DOCUMENTATION]([地址已移除])
In the main PyTorch build system there is no such flag, so the default one is used.
It assumes that the ranges passed when launching sycl kernel fit into `uint32` limits. That supposedly allows some optimizations by not using double precision for indexing.

I created simple cpp sycl kernel to test it.
The attempt to launch sycl kernel with range exceeding max `uint32` ends up in thrown Exception.
```cpp
size_t large_range = 5000000000UL;  // > uint32 max
q.submit([&](sycl::handler& h) {
    h.parallel_for(sycl::range<1>(large_range), [=](sycl::id<1> idx) {
        auto global_id = idx[0];  // Throws exception with default flag
        // kernel work...
    });
});
```

Exception:
```text
Provided range and/or offset does not fit in int. Pass '-fno-sycl-id-queries-fit-in-int' to remove this limit.
```
On the other hand, when launching the TriuTril kernel in PyTorch ([MENTIONED KERNEL]([地址已移除])), there is no Exception, but the results are wrong.

So in normal, simple case, there is Exception thrown when range exceeds the max `uint32`. We need to disable the default flag to make it work by adding `-fno-sycl-id-queries-fit-in-int` to build.

In PyTorch Triangular kernels for XPU, there is no Exception thrown. Kernel executes, but results are wrong. The experiments showed that the wrong results are caused by `get_global_id()` function that returns the ids truncated to `uint32`.
```cpp
IndexType linear_idx = item.get_global_id(0) * elements_per_thread;
// The linear_idx is effectively:
// linear_idx = real_id % MAX_UINT32
```

## Considerations

I believe it would be good to investigate this mismatch in behavior and find the root cause. It is much better to have the Exception rather than silently truncating `uint64` values to `uint32`.
On the other hand, maybe the flag `-fno-sycl-id-queries-fit-in-int` may be added to build system to avoid the truncation in the kernel and allow ranges bigger than max `uint32`. But due to  [DOCUMENTATION]([地址已移除]) it may introduce performance issues.

The main goal of this issue is to first find why the TriangularOpsKernels doesn't throw Exceptions when range is bigger than max `uint32` value.

## Additional links

There is the discussion about it in one of the PRs: #2864

### Verification

- Standalone: `python test/distributed/tensor/test_dtensor_compile.py TestDTensorCompile.test_dtensor_basic_export` → **PASS** on XPU.
- Companion test `test_dtensor_basic_compile` (also covered by this issue's title) already had no skip and **passes** on XPU.

### Caveat

When `test_dtensor_basic_export` runs after `test_dtensor_basic_compile` in the same process (e.g. `pytest -k`, or `python test_dtensor_compile.py TestDTensorCompile.test_dtensor_basic_compile TestDTensorCompile.test_dtensor_basic_export`), it fails an `assertExpectedInline` mismatch:

```
- L_self_buffers_buffer_ , L_self_buffers_buffer_device_mesh , L_x_ , = self._dynamo_bytecode_flatten(*_fn_args)
+ L_self_buffers_buffer_ , L_x_ , L_mesh_ , = self._dynamo_bytecode_flatten(*_fn_args)
- from_local = ... from_local(l_x_, l_self_buffers_buffer_device_mesh, [...])
+ from_local = ... from_local(l_x_, l_mesh_, [...])
```

This is a test-ordering/dynamo-cache pollution that is **not XPU-specific** — it appears to be a regression from pytorch/pytorch#178115 (`[coor] fully flatten DTensorSpec in __tensor_flatten__`, 2026-03-27). Should be filed as a separate upstream issue.

### Branch

- Repo: [地址已移除]
- Branch: `daisyden/missing_test`
- Base: `pytorch/pytorch:viable/strict` @ `fc69434ab0a`
- Commit: `728a822917d` — `[xpu][test] Re-enable test_dtensor_basic_export on XPU (#2958)`

issues.title: [distributed] all_to_all_single Compatibility Issue on B60/XCCL
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Problem Description

On Intel Arc Pro B60 with XCCL backend, `torch.distributed.all_to_all_single` produces
data corruption, while `torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single`
(ft_c version) works correctly.

## Symptoms

- sglang-diffusion in Ulysses attention mode produces completely wrong attention outputs
- Ulysses attention redistributes data between sequence and head dimensions via all_to_all
- `dist.all_to_all_single` corrupts the redistributed data, causing incorrect attention output
- End result: severely degraded or completely black generated images/videos

## Root Cause

`torch.distributed.all_to_all_single` has a bug on the XCCL backend causing incorrect
data exchange. Using `torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single`
(PyTorch functional collectives API) bypasses this issue.

## Current walk around

Override `all_to_all_4D` in `XpuCommunicator` to use ft_c instead of dist:

```python
import torch.distributed._functional_collectives as ft_c

# Original code (broken on XPU)
output = torch.empty_like(input_)
dist.all_to_all_single(output, input_, group=group)

# Fixed (ft_c workaround)
output = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
    input_.flatten(),
    output_split_sizes=None,
    input_split_sizes=None,
    group=group,
)
output = output.reshape(input_shape)
```

## Affected Locations in Codebase

| File | Function | Purpose | Status |
|------|----------|---------|--------|
| `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/device_communicators/base_device_communicator.py` | `AllToAll4D.forward()` | Default all_to_all_4D implementation | Uses `dist.all_to_all_single` |
| `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/device_communicators/xpu_communicator.py` | `all_to_all_4D()` | XPU-specific override | **Fixed** (uses ft_c) |

## Reproduction Test

```bash
# Run on XPU (4 GPUs)
export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1,2,3
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py

# Test different dtypes
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py --dtype bfloat16
```

Expected results (PyTorch 2.9.0+xpu, 4 GPUs):
- Test 1 (dist.all_to_all_single simple): **FAIL** (small tensor corrupted on 4 GPUs)
- Test 2 (ft_c.all_to_all_single simple): PASS
- Test 3 (dist.all_to_all_single large): PASS (large tensor works)
- Test 4 (ft_c.all_to_all_single large): PASS
- Test 5 (4D Ulysses pattern dist vs ft_c): PASS (large tensor)
- Test 6 (Sequential ft_c stability): PASS

## Reproduction Script

```python
"""
Minimal reproduction script for all_to_all_single issue on XPU/XCCL.

On Intel XPU with XCCL backend, `torch.distributed.all_to_all_single` produces
corrupted data, while `torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single`
works correctly.

This bug affects Ulysses attention in sglang-diffusion, where all_to_all_4D is used
to redistribute attention heads and sequence dimensions across devices.

Usage:
    export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1,2,3
    torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py
    # or
    torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py --dtype bfloat16
"""

import argparse
import os
import sys

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.distributed._functional_collectives as ft_c


def init_distributed():
    if "RANK" in os.environ:
        rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
        local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
    elif "PMI_RANK" in os.environ:
        rank = int(os.environ["PMI_RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["PMI_SIZE"])
        local_rank = rank % torch.xpu.device_count()
    else:
        raise RuntimeError("No distributed launch detected. Use torchrun or mpirun.")

    backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
    device = f"xpu:{local_rank}" if torch.xpu.is_available() else f"cuda:{local_rank}"

    if torch.xpu.is_available():
        torch.xpu.set_device(local_rank)
    else:
        torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)

    dist.init_process_group(
        backend=backend, rank=rank, world_size=world_size,
        device_id=torch.device(device),
    )
    return rank, world_size, device


def test_dist_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 1: Basic dist.all_to_all_single with small verifiable data.
    Each rank sends rank*10+i to rank i.
    """
    input_tensor = torch.arange(world_size, device=device, dtype=dtype) + rank * 10
    output_tensor = torch.zeros(world_size, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    dist.all_to_all_single(output_tensor, input_tensor)

    # Verify: output[i] should be i*10 + rank
    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        expected = float(i * 10 + rank)
        actual = output_tensor[i].float().item()
        if abs(actual - expected) > 1e-3:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"idx[{i}]: expected={expected}, actual={actual}")

    return passed, input_tensor.tolist(), output_tensor.tolist(), errors


def test_ftc_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 2: Same test using ft_c.all_to_all_single (workaround).
    """
    input_tensor = torch.arange(world_size, device=device, dtype=dtype) + rank * 10

    output_tensor = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
        input_tensor,
        output_split_sizes=None,
        input_split_sizes=None,
        group=dist.group.WORLD,
    )

    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        expected = float(i * 10 + rank)
        actual = output_tensor[i].float().item()
        if abs(actual - expected) > 1e-3:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"idx[{i}]: expected={expected}, actual={actual}")

    return passed, input_tensor.tolist(), output_tensor.tolist(), errors


def test_dist_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 3: dist.all_to_all_single with large tensor (attention-sized).
    Each rank fills its chunk with rank+1 values, then verifies after exchange.
    """
    chunk_size = 128 * 64  # seq_chunk * head_dim
    total = world_size * chunk_size

    # Each rank creates [world_size] chunks, chunk[i] filled with rank+1
    input_tensor = torch.full((total,), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
    output_tensor = torch.zeros(total, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    dist.all_to_all_single(output_tensor, input_tensor)

    # After all_to_all, chunk[i] in output should come from rank i, so value = i+1
    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        chunk = output_tensor[i * chunk_size : (i + 1) * chunk_size]
        expected = float(i + 1)
        actual_mean = chunk.float().mean().item()
        if abs(actual_mean - expected) > 1e-2:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"chunk[{i}]: expected_mean={expected}, actual_mean={actual_mean}")

    return passed, errors


def test_ftc_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 4: ft_c.all_to_all_single with large tensor (workaround).
    """
    chunk_size = 128 * 64
    total = world_size * chunk_size

    input_tensor = torch.full((total,), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)

    output_tensor = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
        input_tensor,
        output_split_sizes=None,
        input_split_sizes=None,
        group=dist.group.WORLD,
    )

    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        chunk = output_tensor[i * chunk_size : (i + 1) * chunk_size]
        expected = float(i + 1)
        actual_mean = chunk.float().mean().item()
        if abs(actual_mean - expected) > 1e-2:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"chunk[{i}]: expected_mean={expected}, actual_mean={actual_mean}")

    return passed, errors


def test_alltoall_4d_pattern(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 5: Simulate the all_to_all_4D pattern from Ulysses attention.
    scatter_dim=2 (heads), gather_dim=1 (sequence).
    [B, shard_S, H, D] -> all_to_all -> [B, S, shard_H, D]

    Tests both dist.all_to_all_single and ft_c.all_to_all_single, then compares.
    """
    batch = 1
    shard_seqlen = 64
    num_heads = 8  # must be divisible by world_size
    head_dim = 64

    assert num_heads % world_size == 0, f"num_heads={num_heads} must be divisible by world_size={world_size}"
    shard_hn = num_heads // world_size

    # Create deterministic input (same seed on all ranks, but use rank-specific data)
    torch.manual_seed(42 + rank)
    input_4d = torch.randn(batch, shard_seqlen, num_heads, head_dim, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    # ---- dist.all_to_all_single path ----
    input_t = input_4d.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()  # [H, shard_S, B, D]
    output_dist = torch.empty_like(input_t)
    dist.all_to_all_single(output_dist, input_t)
    output_dist = torch.cat(output_dist.split(shard_hn), dim=1)  # [shard_H, S, B, D]
    output_dist = output_dist.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()  # [B, S, shard_H, D]

    # ---- ft_c.all_to_all_single path (workaround) ----
    input_t2 = input_4d.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()
    input_shape = input_t2.shape
    output_ftc = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
        input_t2.flatten(),
        output_split_sizes=None,
        input_split_sizes=None,
        group=dist.group.WORLD,
    )
    output_ftc = output_ftc.reshape(input_shape)
    output_ftc = torch.cat(output_ftc.split(shard_hn), dim=1)
    output_ftc = output_ftc.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()

    # Compare
    has_nan_dist = torch.isnan(output_dist).any().item()
    has_nan_ftc = torch.isnan(output_ftc).any().item()
    max_diff = (output_dist.float() - output_ftc.float()).abs().max().item()
    match = max_diff < 1e-3

    expected_shape = (batch, shard_seqlen * world_size, shard_hn, head_dim)
    shape_ok = output_dist.shape == expected_shape and output_ftc.shape == expected_shape

    return match and shape_ok and not has_nan_dist and not has_nan_ftc, {
        "output_shape": output_dist.shape,
        "expected_shape": expected_shape,
        "max_diff": max_diff,
        "has_nan_dist": has_nan_dist,
        "has_nan_ftc": has_nan_ftc,
        "match": match,
    }


def test_sequential_calls(rank, world_size, device, dtype, rounds=5):
    """
    Test 6: Multiple sequential all_to_all calls to check for intermittent failures.
    """
    chunk_size = 256 * 64
    total = world_size * chunk_size
    all_passed = True

    for i in range(rounds):
        input_tensor = torch.full((total,), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)

        output = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
            input_tensor,
            output_split_sizes=None,
            input_split_sizes=None,
            group=dist.group.WORLD,
        )

        for j in range(world_size):
            chunk = output[j * chunk_size : (j + 1) * chunk_size]
            expected = float(j + 1)
            if abs(chunk.float().mean().item() - expected) > 1e-2:
                all_passed = False

    return all_passed


def _gather_pass_count(passed, world_size):
    """Gather pass/fail from all ranks via all_gather_object (CPU-side)."""
    result_list = [None] * world_size
    dist.all_gather_object(result_list, 1 if passed else 0)
    return sum(result_list)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Test all_to_all_single on XPU/XCCL")
    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=["float32", "float16", "bfloat16"], default="float32")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    dtype_map = {"float32": torch.float32, "float16": torch.float16, "bfloat16": torch.bfloat16}
    dtype = dtype_map[args.dtype]

    rank, world_size, device = init_distributed()

    if rank == 0:
        backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
        print(f"=== all_to_all_single compatibility test ===")
        print(f"Backend: {backend}, World size: {world_size}, Dtype: {args.dtype}")
        print(f"Device: {device}")
        print()

    dist.barrier()

    results = {}

    # --- Test 1: Basic dist.all_to_all_single ---
    p1, inp1, out1, err1 = test_dist_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc1 = _gather_pass_count(p1, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc1 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 1] dist.all_to_all_single (simple):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc1}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p1:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] input={inp1}, output={out1}, errors={err1}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["dist_simple"] = pc1 == world_size

    # --- Test 2: ft_c.all_to_all_single (workaround) ---
    p2, inp2, out2, err2 = test_ftc_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc2 = _gather_pass_count(p2, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc2 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 2] ft_c.all_to_all_single (simple, workaround):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc2}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p2:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] input={inp2}, output={out2}, errors={err2}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["ftc_simple"] = pc2 == world_size

    # --- Test 3: dist.all_to_all_single large ---
    p3, err3 = test_dist_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc3 = _gather_pass_count(p3, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc3 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 3] dist.all_to_all_single (large tensor):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc3}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p3:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] errors={err3}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["dist_large"] = pc3 == world_size

    # --- Test 4: ft_c.all_to_all_single large (workaround) ---
    p4, err4 = test_ftc_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc4 = _gather_pass_count(p4, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc4 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 4] ft_c.all_to_all_single (large tensor, workaround):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc4}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p4:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] errors={err4}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["ftc_large"] = pc4 == world_size

    # --- Test 5: 4D attention pattern (dist vs ft_c) ---
    p5, info5 = test_alltoall_4d_pattern(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc5 = _gather_pass_count(p5, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc5 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 5] all_to_all_4D Ulysses pattern (dist vs ft_c):")
        print(f"  Output shape: {info5['output_shape']}, expected: {info5['expected_shape']}")
        print(f"  Max diff: {info5['max_diff']}, NaN(dist)={info5['has_nan_dist']}, NaN(ftc)={info5['has_nan_ftc']}")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc5}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
        print()
    results["4d_pattern"] = pc5 == world_size

    # --- Test 6: Sequential stability ---
    p6 = test_sequential_calls(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc6 = _gather_pass_count(p6, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc6 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 6] Sequential ft_c.all_to_all_single (5 rounds):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc6}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
        print()
    results["sequential"] = pc6 == world_size

    # --- Summary ---
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print("=== Summary ===")
        labels = [
            ("dist.all_to_all_single (simple)", "dist_simple"),
            ("ft_c.all_to_all_single (simple, WA)", "ftc_simple"),
            ("dist.all_to_all_single (large)", "dist_large"),
            ("ft_c.all_to_all_single (large, WA)", "ftc_large"),
            ("all_to_all_4D Ulysses (dist vs ft_c)", "4d_pattern"),
            ("Sequential ft_c stability", "sequential"),
        ]
        for name, key in labels:
            ok = results[key]
            print(f"  {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}")

        dist_broken = not results["dist_simple"] or not results["dist_large"]
        ftc_ok = results["ftc_simple"] and results["ftc_large"] and results["sequential"]

        if dist_broken and ftc_ok:
            print("\n** dist.all_to_all_single is BROKEN on current XCCL backend. **")
            print("** Use torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single as workaround. **")
        elif not dist_broken:
            print("\nAll tests passed. dist.all_to_all_single works on this backend.")
        else:
            print("\nBoth paths have issues. Check environment.")

    dist.destroy_process_group()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

```

🐛 Describe the bug
Problem Description
On Intel Arc Pro B60 with XCCL backend, torch.distributed.all_to_all_single produces
data corruption, while torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single
(ft_c version) works correctly.
Symptoms

sglang-diffusion in Ulysses attention mode produces completely wrong attention outputs
Ulysses attention redistributes data between sequence and head dimensions via all_to_all
dist.all_to_all_single corrupts the redistributed data, causing incorrect attention output
End result: severely degraded or completely black generated images/videos

Root Cause
torch.distributed.all_to_all_single has a bug on the XCCL backend causing incorrect
data exchange. Using torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single
(PyTorch functional collectives API) bypasses this issue.
Current walk around
Override all_to_all_4D in XpuCommunicator to use ft_c instead of dist:
import torch.distributed._functional_collectives as ft_c

# Original code (broken on XPU)
output = torch.empty_like(input_)
dist.all_to_all_single(output, input_, group=group)

# Fixed (ft_c workaround)
output = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
    input_.flatten(),
    output_split_sizes=None,
    input_split_sizes=None,
    group=group,
)
output = output.reshape(input_shape)
Affected Locations in Codebase

Function
Purpose

Default all_to_all_4D implementation

torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py

# Test different dtypes
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py --dtype bfloat16
Expected results (PyTorch 2.9.0+xpu, 4 GPUs):

Test 2 (ft_c.all_to_all_single simple): PASS

Reproduction Script
"""
Minimal reproduction script for all_to_all_single issue on XPU/XCCL.

On Intel XPU with XCCL backend, `torch.distributed.all_to_all_single` produces
corrupted data, while `torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single`
works correctly.

This bug affects Ulysses attention in sglang-diffusion, where all_to_all_4D is used
to redistribute attention heads and sequence dimensions across devices.

Usage:
    export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1,2,3
    torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py
    # or
    torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_alltoall_single.py --dtype bfloat16
"""

import argparse
import os
import sys

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist
import torch.distributed._functional_collectives as ft_c


def init_distributed():
    if "RANK" in os.environ:
        rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
        local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
    elif "PMI_RANK" in os.environ:
        rank = int(os.environ["PMI_RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["PMI_SIZE"])
        local_rank = rank % torch.xpu.device_count()
    else:
        raise RuntimeError("No distributed launch detected. Use torchrun or mpirun.")

    backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
    device = f"xpu:{local_rank}" if torch.xpu.is_available() else f"cuda:{local_rank}"

    if torch.xpu.is_available():
        torch.xpu.set_device(local_rank)
    else:
        torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)

    dist.init_process_group(
        backend=backend, rank=rank, world_size=world_size,
        device_id=torch.device(device),
    )
    return rank, world_size, device


def test_dist_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 1: Basic dist.all_to_all_single with small verifiable data.
    Each rank sends rank*10+i to rank i.
    """
    input_tensor = torch.arange(world_size, device=device, dtype=dtype) + rank * 10
    output_tensor = torch.zeros(world_size, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    dist.all_to_all_single(output_tensor, input_tensor)

    # Verify: output[i] should be i*10 + rank
    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        expected = float(i * 10 + rank)
        actual = output_tensor[i].float().item()
        if abs(actual - expected) > 1e-3:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"idx[{i}]: expected={expected}, actual={actual}")

    return passed, input_tensor.tolist(), output_tensor.tolist(), errors


def test_ftc_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 2: Same test using ft_c.all_to_all_single (workaround).
    """
    input_tensor = torch.arange(world_size, device=device, dtype=dtype) + rank * 10

    output_tensor = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
        input_tensor,
        output_split_sizes=None,
        input_split_sizes=None,
        group=dist.group.WORLD,
    )

    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        expected = float(i * 10 + rank)
        actual = output_tensor[i].float().item()
        if abs(actual - expected) > 1e-3:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"idx[{i}]: expected={expected}, actual={actual}")

    return passed, input_tensor.tolist(), output_tensor.tolist(), errors


def test_dist_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 3: dist.all_to_all_single with large tensor (attention-sized).
    Each rank fills its chunk with rank+1 values, then verifies after exchange.
    """
    chunk_size = 128 * 64  # seq_chunk * head_dim
    total = world_size * chunk_size

    # Each rank creates [world_size] chunks, chunk[i] filled with rank+1
    input_tensor = torch.full((total,), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
    output_tensor = torch.zeros(total, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    dist.all_to_all_single(output_tensor, input_tensor)

    # After all_to_all, chunk[i] in output should come from rank i, so value = i+1
    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        chunk = output_tensor[i * chunk_size : (i + 1) * chunk_size]
        expected = float(i + 1)
        actual_mean = chunk.float().mean().item()
        if abs(actual_mean - expected) > 1e-2:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"chunk[{i}]: expected_mean={expected}, actual_mean={actual_mean}")

    return passed, errors


def test_ftc_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 4: ft_c.all_to_all_single with large tensor (workaround).
    """
    chunk_size = 128 * 64
    total = world_size * chunk_size

    input_tensor = torch.full((total,), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)

    output_tensor = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
        input_tensor,
        output_split_sizes=None,
        input_split_sizes=None,
        group=dist.group.WORLD,
    )

    passed = True
    errors = []
    for i in range(world_size):
        chunk = output_tensor[i * chunk_size : (i + 1) * chunk_size]
        expected = float(i + 1)
        actual_mean = chunk.float().mean().item()
        if abs(actual_mean - expected) > 1e-2:
            passed = False
            errors.append(f"chunk[{i}]: expected_mean={expected}, actual_mean={actual_mean}")

    return passed, errors


def test_alltoall_4d_pattern(rank, world_size, device, dtype):
    """
    Test 5: Simulate the all_to_all_4D pattern from Ulysses attention.
    scatter_dim=2 (heads), gather_dim=1 (sequence).
    [B, shard_S, H, D] -> all_to_all -> [B, S, shard_H, D]

    Tests both dist.all_to_all_single and ft_c.all_to_all_single, then compares.
    """
    batch = 1
    shard_seqlen = 64
    num_heads = 8  # must be divisible by world_size
    head_dim = 64

    assert num_heads % world_size == 0, f"num_heads={num_heads} must be divisible by world_size={world_size}"
    shard_hn = num_heads // world_size

    # Create deterministic input (same seed on all ranks, but use rank-specific data)
    torch.manual_seed(42 + rank)
    input_4d = torch.randn(batch, shard_seqlen, num_heads, head_dim, device=device, dtype=dtype)

    # ---- dist.all_to_all_single path ----
    input_t = input_4d.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()  # [H, shard_S, B, D]
    output_dist = torch.empty_like(input_t)
    dist.all_to_all_single(output_dist, input_t)
    output_dist = torch.cat(output_dist.split(shard_hn), dim=1)  # [shard_H, S, B, D]
    output_dist = output_dist.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()  # [B, S, shard_H, D]

    # ---- ft_c.all_to_all_single path (workaround) ----
    input_t2 = input_4d.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()
    input_shape = input_t2.shape
    output_ftc = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
        input_t2.flatten(),
        output_split_sizes=None,
        input_split_sizes=None,
        group=dist.group.WORLD,
    )
    output_ftc = output_ftc.reshape(input_shape)
    output_ftc = torch.cat(output_ftc.split(shard_hn), dim=1)
    output_ftc = output_ftc.transpose(0, 2).contiguous()

    # Compare
    has_nan_dist = torch.isnan(output_dist).any().item()
    has_nan_ftc = torch.isnan(output_ftc).any().item()
    max_diff = (output_dist.float() - output_ftc.float()).abs().max().item()
    match = max_diff < 1e-3

    expected_shape = (batch, shard_seqlen * world_size, shard_hn, head_dim)
    shape_ok = output_dist.shape == expected_shape and output_ftc.shape == expected_shape

    return match and shape_ok and not has_nan_dist and not has_nan_ftc, {
        "output_shape": output_dist.shape,
        "expected_shape": expected_shape,
        "max_diff": max_diff,
        "has_nan_dist": has_nan_dist,
        "has_nan_ftc": has_nan_ftc,
        "match": match,
    }


def test_sequential_calls(rank, world_size, device, dtype, rounds=5):
    """
    Test 6: Multiple sequential all_to_all calls to check for intermittent failures.
    """
    chunk_size = 256 * 64
    total = world_size * chunk_size
    all_passed = True

    for i in range(rounds):
        input_tensor = torch.full((total,), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)

        output = ft_c.all_to_all_single(
            input_tensor,
            output_split_sizes=None,
            input_split_sizes=None,
            group=dist.group.WORLD,
        )

        for j in range(world_size):
            chunk = output[j * chunk_size : (j + 1) * chunk_size]
            expected = float(j + 1)
            if abs(chunk.float().mean().item() - expected) > 1e-2:
                all_passed = False

    return all_passed


def _gather_pass_count(passed, world_size):
    """Gather pass/fail from all ranks via all_gather_object (CPU-side)."""
    result_list = [None] * world_size
    dist.all_gather_object(result_list, 1 if passed else 0)
    return sum(result_list)


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Test all_to_all_single on XPU/XCCL")
    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=["float32", "float16", "bfloat16"], default="float32")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    dtype_map = {"float32": torch.float32, "float16": torch.float16, "bfloat16": torch.bfloat16}
    dtype = dtype_map[args.dtype]

    rank, world_size, device = init_distributed()

    if rank == 0:
        backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
        print(f"=== all_to_all_single compatibility test ===")
        print(f"Backend: {backend}, World size: {world_size}, Dtype: {args.dtype}")
        print(f"Device: {device}")
        print()

    dist.barrier()

    results = {}

    # --- Test 1: Basic dist.all_to_all_single ---
    p1, inp1, out1, err1 = test_dist_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc1 = _gather_pass_count(p1, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc1 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 1] dist.all_to_all_single (simple):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc1}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p1:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] input={inp1}, output={out1}, errors={err1}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["dist_simple"] = pc1 == world_size

    # --- Test 2: ft_c.all_to_all_single (workaround) ---
    p2, inp2, out2, err2 = test_ftc_alltoall_simple(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc2 = _gather_pass_count(p2, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc2 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 2] ft_c.all_to_all_single (simple, workaround):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc2}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p2:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] input={inp2}, output={out2}, errors={err2}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["ftc_simple"] = pc2 == world_size

    # --- Test 3: dist.all_to_all_single large ---
    p3, err3 = test_dist_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc3 = _gather_pass_count(p3, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc3 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 3] dist.all_to_all_single (large tensor):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc3}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p3:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] errors={err3}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["dist_large"] = pc3 == world_size

    # --- Test 4: ft_c.all_to_all_single large (workaround) ---
    p4, err4 = test_ftc_alltoall_large(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc4 = _gather_pass_count(p4, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc4 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 4] ft_c.all_to_all_single (large tensor, workaround):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc4}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not p4:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] errors={err4}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()
    results["ftc_large"] = pc4 == world_size

    # --- Test 5: 4D attention pattern (dist vs ft_c) ---
    p5, info5 = test_alltoall_4d_pattern(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc5 = _gather_pass_count(p5, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc5 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 5] all_to_all_4D Ulysses pattern (dist vs ft_c):")
        print(f"  Output shape: {info5['output_shape']}, expected: {info5['expected_shape']}")
        print(f"  Max diff: {info5['max_diff']}, NaN(dist)={info5['has_nan_dist']}, NaN(ftc)={info5['has_nan_ftc']}")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc5}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
        print()
    results["4d_pattern"] = pc5 == world_size

    # --- Test 6: Sequential stability ---
    p6 = test_sequential_calls(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    pc6 = _gather_pass_count(p6, world_size)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if pc6 == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"[Test 6] Sequential ft_c.all_to_all_single (5 rounds):")
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({pc6}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
        print()
    results["sequential"] = pc6 == world_size

    # --- Summary ---
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print("=== Summary ===")
        labels = [
            ("dist.all_to_all_single (simple)", "dist_simple"),
            ("ft_c.all_to_all_single (simple, WA)", "ftc_simple"),
            ("dist.all_to_all_single (large)", "dist_large"),
            ("ft_c.all_to_all_single (large, WA)", "ftc_large"),
            ("all_to_all_4D Ulysses (dist vs ft_c)", "4d_pattern"),
            ("Sequential ft_c stability", "sequential"),
        ]
        for name, key in labels:
            ok = results[key]
            print(f"  {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}")

        dist_broken = not results["dist_simple"] or not results["dist_large"]
        ftc_ok = results["ftc_simple"] and results["ftc_large"] and results["sequential"]

        if dist_broken and ftc_ok:
            print("\n** dist.all_to_all_single is BROKEN on current XCCL backend. **")
            print("** Use torch.distributed._functional_collectives.all_to_all_single as workaround. **")
        elif not dist_broken:
            print("\nAll tests passed. dist.all_to_all_single works on this backend.")
        else:
            print("\nBoth paths have issues. Check environment.")

    dist.destroy_process_group()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()

issues.title: [distributed] batch_isend_irecv Compatibility Issue on B60/XCCL
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Problem Description

On Intel Arc Pro B60 with XCCL backend, `torch.distributed.batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))`
causes silent data corruption on the receive side (all-zeros or garbage data), while
individual `dist.irecv` / `dist.isend` calls work correctly.

## Symptoms

- sglang-diffusion in USP mode (tp=1, ulysses=4) generates completely black videos
- TP mode (tp=4, ulysses=1) works normally
- Denoising stage latent data is correct; the issue appears in VAE parallel decoding
- VAE parallel decoding uses height-dimension sharding + halo exchange; halo exchange is called in every convolution layer
- `batch_isend_irecv` causes halo data transfer failure, convolution output errors, and ultimately all-black VAE output

## Root Cause

The `halo_exchange` function was changed from individual `irecv/isend` to
`batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))` after commit `574aa8c1f`. This API does not work
correctly on the XCCL backend.

## Current walk around

In `wan_dist_utils.py`'s `halo_exchange`, check the platform via `current_platform.is_xpu()`:
use individual `irecv/isend` on XPU, and `batch_isend_irecv` on other platforms.

## Affected Locations in Codebase

| File | Function | Purpose | Status |
|------|----------|---------|--------|
| `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/vaes/parallel/wan_dist_utils.py` | `halo_exchange()` | Wan VAE parallel decoding halo exchange | **Fixed** |
| `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/distributed/group_coordinator.py` | `PipelineGroupCoordinator._communicate_shapes()` | Pipeline Parallel inter-stage shape communication | To be fixed (triggered when pp>1) |
| `python/sglang/srt/eplb/expert_location_updater.py` | expert rebalance P2P | LLM-side MoE expert load balancing | Non-diffusion path |

## Reproduction Test

```bash
# Run on XPU (4 GPUs)
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_batch_isend_irecv.py

# Or use mpirun
mpirun -np 4 python test_batch_isend_irecv.py

# Test different dtypes
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_batch_isend_irecv.py --dtype bfloat16
```

Expected results:
- Test 1 (individual basic): PASS
- Test 2 (batch basic): FAIL (on XPU/XCCL)
- Test 3 (halo individual): PASS
- Test 4 (halo batch): FAIL (on XPU/XCCL)

## Environment

- Container image: intel/llm-scaler-omni:0.1.0-b6
- PyTorch: 2.9.0+xpu
- oneAPI: 2025.1
- oneCCL: 2021.15.6
- Platform: Intel Arc Pro B60 × 4
- Distributed backend: XCCL (PyTorch XPU distributed)
- CCL environment variables:
  - `CCL_SYCL_ALLTOALL_ARC_LL=1`
  - `CCL_SYCL_CCL_BARRIER=1`
- Model: Wan2.1-T2V-1.3B-Diffusers (reproduced in USP mode)
- sglang-diffusion branch: xpu_0122

## Reproduce Script
```python
"""
Minimal reproduction script for batch_isend_irecv compatibility issue on XPU/XCCL.

On Intel XPU with XCCL backend, `dist.batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))` silently
produces corrupted data (zeros or garbage), while individual `dist.irecv/dist.isend`
calls work correctly.

Usage:
    mpirun -np 4 python test_batch_isend_irecv.py
    # or
    torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_batch_isend_irecv.py
"""

import os
import argparse

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist


def init_distributed():
    if "RANK" in os.environ:
        # torchrun launch
        rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
        local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
    elif "PMI_RANK" in os.environ:
        # mpirun launch
        rank = int(os.environ["PMI_RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["PMI_SIZE"])
        local_rank = rank % torch.xpu.device_count()
    else:
        raise RuntimeError("No distributed launch detected. Use torchrun or mpirun.")

    backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
    device = f"xpu:{local_rank}" if torch.xpu.is_available() else f"cuda:{local_rank}"

    dist.init_process_group(backend=backend, rank=rank, world_size=world_size)
    torch.xpu.set_device(local_rank) if torch.xpu.is_available() else torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)

    return rank, world_size, device


def test_individual_isend_irecv(rank, world_size, device, dtype=torch.float32):
    """Test P2P communication using individual dist.irecv / dist.isend calls."""
    send_tensor = torch.full((4, 8), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
    recv_tensor = torch.zeros((4, 8), device=device, dtype=dtype)

    reqs = []
    if rank > 0:
        prev_rank = rank - 1
        reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_tensor, src=prev_rank))
        reqs.append(dist.isend(send_tensor, dst=prev_rank))
    if rank < world_size - 1:
        next_rank = rank + 1
        reqs.append(dist.isend(send_tensor, dst=next_rank))
        reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_tensor, src=next_rank))

    for req in reqs:
        req.wait()

    dist.barrier()

    # Verify: rank 0 should receive from rank 1, middle ranks from both neighbors, last rank from prev
    if rank < world_size - 1:
        expected_val = float(rank + 2)  # value from next rank
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    elif rank > 0:
        expected_val = float(rank)  # value from prev rank
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    else:
        passed = True
        expected_val = actual_val = 0.0

    return passed, expected_val, actual_val, recv_tensor


def test_batch_isend_irecv(rank, world_size, device, dtype=torch.float32):
    """Test P2P communication using dist.batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))."""
    send_tensor = torch.full((4, 8), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
    recv_tensor = torch.zeros((4, 8), device=device, dtype=dtype)

    p2p_ops = []
    if rank > 0:
        prev_rank = rank - 1
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_tensor, prev_rank))
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, send_tensor, prev_rank))
    if rank < world_size - 1:
        next_rank = rank + 1
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, send_tensor, next_rank))
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_tensor, next_rank))

    if p2p_ops:
        reqs = dist.batch_isend_irecv(p2p_ops)
        for req in reqs:
            req.wait()

    dist.barrier()

    if rank < world_size - 1:
        expected_val = float(rank + 2)
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    elif rank > 0:
        expected_val = float(rank)
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    else:
        passed = True
        expected_val = actual_val = 0.0

    return passed, expected_val, actual_val, recv_tensor


def test_halo_exchange_pattern(rank, world_size, device, use_batch, dtype=torch.float32):
    """
    Simulate the halo exchange pattern used in WanVAE parallel decode.
    Each rank owns a local slice of a height-sharded tensor and exchanges
    top/bottom halo rows with neighbors.
    """
    local_h, w = 8, 16
    # Fill with rank-specific values so correctness is verifiable
    x = torch.full((1, 4, local_h, w), float(rank + 1) * 10, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    # Make top/bottom rows distinctive
    x[..., 0, :] = float(rank + 1) * 100  # top row
    x[..., -1, :] = float(rank + 1) * 200  # bottom row

    halo_size = 1
    top_row = x[..., :halo_size, :].contiguous()
    bottom_row = x[..., -halo_size:, :].contiguous()
    recv_top = torch.zeros_like(top_row)
    recv_bottom = torch.zeros_like(bottom_row)

    if use_batch:
        p2p_ops = []
        if rank > 0:
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_top, rank - 1))
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, top_row, rank - 1))
        if rank < world_size - 1:
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, bottom_row, rank + 1))
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_bottom, rank + 1))
        if rank == 0:
            recv_top.zero_()
        if rank == world_size - 1:
            recv_bottom.zero_()
        if p2p_ops:
            reqs = dist.batch_isend_irecv(p2p_ops)
            for req in reqs:
                req.wait()
    else:
        reqs = []
        if rank > 0:
            reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_top, src=rank - 1))
            reqs.append(dist.isend(top_row, dst=rank - 1))
        if rank < world_size - 1:
            reqs.append(dist.isend(bottom_row, dst=rank + 1))
            reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_bottom, src=rank + 1))
        if rank == 0:
            recv_top.zero_()
        if rank == world_size - 1:
            recv_bottom.zero_()
        for req in reqs:
            req.wait()

    dist.barrier()

    # Verify recv_top: should be bottom_row of (rank-1), i.e. rank * 200
    # Verify recv_bottom: should be top_row of (rank+1), i.e. (rank+2) * 100
    passed = True
    details = []

    if rank > 0:
        expected_top = float(rank) * 200  # bottom_row value of prev rank
        actual_top = recv_top.mean().item()
        ok = abs(actual_top - expected_top) < 1e-3
        passed = passed and ok
        details.append(f"recv_top: expected={expected_top}, actual={actual_top}, {'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    else:
        details.append("recv_top: zeroed (rank 0)")

    if rank < world_size - 1:
        expected_bottom = float(rank + 2) * 100  # top_row value of next rank
        actual_bottom = recv_bottom.mean().item()
        ok = abs(actual_bottom - expected_bottom) < 1e-3
        passed = passed and ok
        details.append(f"recv_bottom: expected={expected_bottom}, actual={actual_bottom}, {'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    else:
        details.append("recv_bottom: zeroed (last rank)")

    return passed, details


def main():

    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=["float32", "float16", "bfloat16"], default="float32")

🐛 Describe the bug
Problem Description
On Intel Arc Pro B60 with XCCL backend, torch.distributed.batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))
causes silent data corruption on the receive side (all-zeros or garbage data), while
individual dist.irecv / dist.isend calls work correctly.
Symptoms

sglang-diffusion in USP mode (tp=1, ulysses=4) generates completely black videos
TP mode (tp=4, ulysses=1) works normally
Denoising stage latent data is correct; the issue appears in VAE parallel decoding
VAE parallel decoding uses height-dimension sharding + halo exchange; halo exchange is called in every convolution layer
batch_isend_irecv causes halo data transfer failure, convolution output errors, and ultimately all-black VAE output

Root Cause
The halo_exchange function was changed from individual irecv/isend to
batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...)) after commit 574aa8c1f. This API does not work
correctly on the XCCL backend.
Current walk around
In wan_dist_utils.py's halo_exchange, check the platform via current_platform.is_xpu():
use individual irecv/isend on XPU, and batch_isend_irecv on other platforms.

Reproduce Script
"""
Minimal reproduction script for batch_isend_irecv compatibility issue on XPU/XCCL.

On Intel XPU with XCCL backend, `dist.batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))` silently
produces corrupted data (zeros or garbage), while individual `dist.irecv/dist.isend`
calls work correctly.

Usage:
    mpirun -np 4 python test_batch_isend_irecv.py
    # or
    torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 test_batch_isend_irecv.py
"""

import os
import argparse

import torch
import torch.distributed as dist


def init_distributed():
    if "RANK" in os.environ:
        # torchrun launch
        rank = int(os.environ["RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["WORLD_SIZE"])
        local_rank = int(os.environ["LOCAL_RANK"])
    elif "PMI_RANK" in os.environ:
        # mpirun launch
        rank = int(os.environ["PMI_RANK"])
        world_size = int(os.environ["PMI_SIZE"])
        local_rank = rank % torch.xpu.device_count()
    else:
        raise RuntimeError("No distributed launch detected. Use torchrun or mpirun.")

    backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
    device = f"xpu:{local_rank}" if torch.xpu.is_available() else f"cuda:{local_rank}"

    dist.init_process_group(backend=backend, rank=rank, world_size=world_size)
    torch.xpu.set_device(local_rank) if torch.xpu.is_available() else torch.cuda.set_device(local_rank)

    return rank, world_size, device


def test_individual_isend_irecv(rank, world_size, device, dtype=torch.float32):
    """Test P2P communication using individual dist.irecv / dist.isend calls."""
    send_tensor = torch.full((4, 8), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
    recv_tensor = torch.zeros((4, 8), device=device, dtype=dtype)

    reqs = []
    if rank > 0:
        prev_rank = rank - 1
        reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_tensor, src=prev_rank))
        reqs.append(dist.isend(send_tensor, dst=prev_rank))
    if rank < world_size - 1:
        next_rank = rank + 1
        reqs.append(dist.isend(send_tensor, dst=next_rank))
        reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_tensor, src=next_rank))

    for req in reqs:
        req.wait()

    dist.barrier()

    # Verify: rank 0 should receive from rank 1, middle ranks from both neighbors, last rank from prev
    if rank < world_size - 1:
        expected_val = float(rank + 2)  # value from next rank
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    elif rank > 0:
        expected_val = float(rank)  # value from prev rank
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    else:
        passed = True
        expected_val = actual_val = 0.0

    return passed, expected_val, actual_val, recv_tensor


def test_batch_isend_irecv(rank, world_size, device, dtype=torch.float32):
    """Test P2P communication using dist.batch_isend_irecv(P2POp(...))."""
    send_tensor = torch.full((4, 8), float(rank + 1), device=device, dtype=dtype)
    recv_tensor = torch.zeros((4, 8), device=device, dtype=dtype)

    p2p_ops = []
    if rank > 0:
        prev_rank = rank - 1
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_tensor, prev_rank))
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, send_tensor, prev_rank))
    if rank < world_size - 1:
        next_rank = rank + 1
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, send_tensor, next_rank))
        p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_tensor, next_rank))

    if p2p_ops:
        reqs = dist.batch_isend_irecv(p2p_ops)
        for req in reqs:
            req.wait()

    dist.barrier()

    if rank < world_size - 1:
        expected_val = float(rank + 2)
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    elif rank > 0:
        expected_val = float(rank)
        actual_val = recv_tensor.mean().item()
        passed = abs(actual_val - expected_val) < 1e-5
    else:
        passed = True
        expected_val = actual_val = 0.0

    return passed, expected_val, actual_val, recv_tensor


def test_halo_exchange_pattern(rank, world_size, device, use_batch, dtype=torch.float32):
    """
    Simulate the halo exchange pattern used in WanVAE parallel decode.
    Each rank owns a local slice of a height-sharded tensor and exchanges
    top/bottom halo rows with neighbors.
    """
    local_h, w = 8, 16
    # Fill with rank-specific values so correctness is verifiable
    x = torch.full((1, 4, local_h, w), float(rank + 1) * 10, device=device, dtype=dtype)
    # Make top/bottom rows distinctive
    x[..., 0, :] = float(rank + 1) * 100  # top row
    x[..., -1, :] = float(rank + 1) * 200  # bottom row

    halo_size = 1
    top_row = x[..., :halo_size, :].contiguous()
    bottom_row = x[..., -halo_size:, :].contiguous()
    recv_top = torch.zeros_like(top_row)
    recv_bottom = torch.zeros_like(bottom_row)

    if use_batch:
        p2p_ops = []
        if rank > 0:
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_top, rank - 1))
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, top_row, rank - 1))
        if rank < world_size - 1:
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.isend, bottom_row, rank + 1))
            p2p_ops.append(dist.P2POp(dist.irecv, recv_bottom, rank + 1))
        if rank == 0:
            recv_top.zero_()
        if rank == world_size - 1:
            recv_bottom.zero_()
        if p2p_ops:
            reqs = dist.batch_isend_irecv(p2p_ops)
            for req in reqs:
                req.wait()
    else:
        reqs = []
        if rank > 0:
            reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_top, src=rank - 1))
            reqs.append(dist.isend(top_row, dst=rank - 1))
        if rank < world_size - 1:
            reqs.append(dist.isend(bottom_row, dst=rank + 1))
            reqs.append(dist.irecv(recv_bottom, src=rank + 1))
        if rank == 0:
            recv_top.zero_()
        if rank == world_size - 1:
            recv_bottom.zero_()
        for req in reqs:
            req.wait()

    dist.barrier()

    # Verify recv_top: should be bottom_row of (rank-1), i.e. rank * 200
    # Verify recv_bottom: should be top_row of (rank+1), i.e. (rank+2) * 100
    passed = True
    details = []

    if rank > 0:
        expected_top = float(rank) * 200  # bottom_row value of prev rank
        actual_top = recv_top.mean().item()
        ok = abs(actual_top - expected_top) < 1e-3
        passed = passed and ok
        details.append(f"recv_top: expected={expected_top}, actual={actual_top}, {'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    else:
        details.append("recv_top: zeroed (rank 0)")

    if rank < world_size - 1:
        expected_bottom = float(rank + 2) * 100  # top_row value of next rank
        actual_bottom = recv_bottom.mean().item()
        ok = abs(actual_bottom - expected_bottom) < 1e-3
        passed = passed and ok
        details.append(f"recv_bottom: expected={expected_bottom}, actual={actual_bottom}, {'OK' if ok else 'FAIL'}")
    else:
        details.append("recv_bottom: zeroed (last rank)")

    return passed, details


def main():
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Test batch_isend_irecv on XPU/XCCL")
    parser.add_argument("--dtype", choices=["float32", "float16", "bfloat16"], default="float32")
    args = parser.parse_args()

    dtype_map = {"float32": torch.float32, "float16": torch.float16, "bfloat16": torch.bfloat16}
    dtype = dtype_map[args.dtype]

    rank, world_size, device = init_distributed()

    if rank == 0:
        backend = "xccl" if torch.xpu.is_available() else "nccl"
        print(f"=== batch_isend_irecv compatibility test ===")
        print(f"Backend: {backend}, World size: {world_size}, Dtype: {args.dtype}")
        print(f"Device: {device}")
        print()

    dist.barrier()

    # --- Test 1: Basic individual irecv/isend ---
    passed1, exp1, act1, _ = test_individual_isend_irecv(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print("[Test 1] Individual irecv/isend (basic):")
    all_passed = torch.tensor([1 if passed1 else 0], device=device)
    dist.all_reduce(all_passed)
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if all_passed.item() == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({all_passed.item()}/{world_size} ranks passed)\n")

    # --- Test 2: Basic batch_isend_irecv ---
    passed2, exp2, act2, recv2 = test_batch_isend_irecv(rank, world_size, device, dtype)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print("[Test 2] batch_isend_irecv (basic):")
    all_passed2 = torch.tensor([1 if passed2 else 0], device=device)
    dist.all_reduce(all_passed2)
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if all_passed2.item() == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({all_passed2.item()}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not passed2:
        print(f"  [Rank {rank}] expected={exp2}, actual={act2}, recv_tensor={recv2.flatten()[:4].tolist()}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()

    # --- Test 3: Halo exchange pattern (individual) ---
    passed3, details3 = test_halo_exchange_pattern(rank, world_size, device, use_batch=False, dtype=dtype)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print("[Test 3] Halo exchange pattern (individual irecv/isend):")
    all_passed3 = torch.tensor([1 if passed3 else 0], device=device)
    dist.all_reduce(all_passed3)
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if all_passed3.item() == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({all_passed3.item()}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not passed3:
        for d in details3:
            print(f"  [Rank {rank}] {d}")
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print()

    # --- Test 4: Halo exchange pattern (batch_isend_irecv) ---
    passed4, details4 = test_halo_exchange_pattern(rank, world_size, device, use_batch=True, dtype=dtype)
    dist.barrier()
    if rank == 0:
        print("[Test 4] Halo exchange pattern (batch_isend_irecv):")
    all_passed4 = torch.tensor([1 if passed4 else 0], device=device)
    dist.all_reduce(all_passed4)
    if rank == 0:
        status = "PASS" if all_passed4.item() == world_size else "FAIL"
        print(f"  Result: {status} ({all_passed4.item()}/{world_size} ranks passed)")
    if not passed4:
        for d in details4:
            print(f"  [Rank {rank}] {d}")
    dist.barrier()

    # --- Summary ---
    if rank == 0:
        print("\n=== Summary ===")
        tests = [
            ("Individual irecv/isend (basic)", all_passed.item() == world_size),
            ("batch_isend_irecv (basic)", all_passed2.item() == world_size),
            ("Halo exchange (individual)", all_passed3.item() == world_size),
            ("Halo exchange (batch)", all_passed4.item() == world_size),
        ]
        for name, ok in tests:
            print(f"  {'PASS' if ok else 'FAIL'}  {name}")

        if not all(ok for _, ok in tests):
            print("\n** batch_isend_irecv is NOT compatible with current backend. **")
            print("** Use individual irecv/isend as workaround. **")
        else:
            print("\nAll tests passed.")

    dist.destroy_process_group()

No response

nodes.body:
This is not a functionality issue of distributed because the failure is cause by different default behavior of xpu test suite. The TestCase class will initialize cuda context with a default device 0 before test runs. However, in xpu's case, device is not set until later in the test being initialized based on rank, so for these ForwardInputs tests the expected device is different.

I noticed in the TestCase class there are lots of cuda specifc code which might cause such tiny differences. Are there any ongoing efforts checking or adapting this class?
