issues.title: [XPU] Enable functionalize_rng_ops on XPU (philox_rand prim + RNG decompositions)
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

test_cases:
  - test/dynamo/test_higher_order_ops.py::ActivationCheckpointingTests::test_dropout
  - test/dynamo/test_higher_order_ops.py::ActivationCheckpointingTests::test_dropout_inductor
---

## Parent Issue

Follow-up to intel/torch-xpu-ops#1970 — *RuntimeError: CUDA not available from CUDARngStateHelper*.

The PyTorch in-tree fix for #1970 makes `CUDARngStateHelper` device-agnostic via
`torch.accelerator.current_accelerator()` (alias preserved). With that change, the
two reporting tests get past `CUDARngStateHelper.get_torch_state_as_tuple` but now
hit a **second, deeper layer of CUDA-only gates** in the AOTAutograd
`functionalize_rng_ops=True` path. Enabling those tests on XPU requires generalizing
that path. This issue tracks that work.

## Affected Test Cases

After the helper fix and `device=GPU_TYPE` retargeting:

- `test/dynamo/test_higher_order_ops.py::ActivationCheckpointingTests::test_dropout`
- `test/dynamo/test_higher_order_ops.py::ActivationCheckpointingTests::test_dropout_inductor`

Same root cause is expected to surface in any other test that toggles
`torch._functorch.config.functionalize_rng_ops=True` and runs on a non-CUDA accelerator.

## Root Cause

The functionalized-RNG lowering for `aten.rand` / `aten.rand_like` / dropout is
currently CUDA-only at three places:

1. **`torch/_decomp/decompositions_for_rng.py`** — `rand` (line 33) and `rand_like`
   (line 56) explicitly call `throw_on_non_cuda(device)` for any non-CUDA device.
2. **`torch/_prims/rng_prims.py`** — `_philox_rand` impl (line 116) raises
   `throw_on_non_cuda` when `device.type != "cuda"`.
3. **`torch/_prims/rng_prims.py:philox_rand_offset`** (line 71) — hardcodes
   `torch.cuda.get_device_properties(torch.cuda.current_device())` and reads
   `multi_processor_count` / `max_threads_per_multi_processor`. These fields do not
   exist on `torch.xpu.get_device_properties()` (XPU exposes `gpu_eu_count`,
   `max_compute_units`, `gpu_subslice_count`, `max_num_sub_groups`,
   `max_work_group_size` instead).

Functionally, XPU already uses Philox/counter-based RNG (`torch.xpu.initial_seed`,
`_get_rng_state_offset`, `_set_rng_state_offset`, `set_rng_state` exist and have
the same semantics as the CUDA equivalents), so generalization is feasible — only
the device-properties query and the hard gates are CUDA-shaped.

## Reproducer

After applying intel/torch-xpu-ops#1970's fix
(`CUDARngStateHelper` → `RngStateHelper`) and switching the two tests to
`device=GPU_TYPE` + `@requires_gpu_and_triton`:

```bash
cd <pytorch>
python test/dynamo/test_higher_order_ops.py \
    ActivationCheckpointingTests.test_dropout \
    ActivationCheckpointingTests.test_dropout_inductor
```

Fails with:

```
RuntimeError: You are trying to functionalize a xpu RNG operator but xpu does not
use Philox/counter-based RNG. Therefore, functionalizing a xpu RNG operator is not
supported. ...
```

raised from `torch/_decomp/decompositions_for_rng.py:23`.

## Scope of Changes

### Files to update (PyTorch in-tree)

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `torch/_decomp/decompositions_for_rng.py` | Replace `throw_on_non_cuda` gate in `rand` / `rand_like` with an "accelerator supports Philox" check (allow `cuda`, `xpu`, future Philox-capable backends). Update message accordingly. |
| `torch/_prims/rng_prims.py` (`_philox_rand` impl) | Drop the `device.type != "cuda"` raise; route `set_torch_state_tensor` through the device-agnostic `RngStateHelper` (already done by #1970 follow-up); call `torch.rand(shape, device=device, ...)` which already works on XPU. |
| `torch/_prims/rng_prims.py` (`philox_rand_offset`) | Generalize the device-properties query. Introduce a small helper `_philox_offset_grid_params(device)` that returns `(block_size, blocks_per_sm, sm_count)`-equivalent values per backend. For XPU, derive from `max_compute_units`, `max_work_group_size`, `gpu_subslice_count`, `max_num_sub_groups`. A safe alternative is a conservative upper-bound offset jump that does not depend on hardware geometry — acceptable because over-advancing the Philox counter only wastes counter space, not correctness. |
| `torch/_prims_common/__init__.py` | Already done by #1970 follow-up (`RngStateHelper` device-agnostic). No further change. |

### Out of scope (do separately)

- Numerical equivalence of the XPU Philox stream vs. eager XPU RNG output.
  `philox_rand` is a *new* RNG stream tracked by AOTAutograd; it is not required
  to match the existing eager `torch.rand` numerics on XPU. The two existing
  tests use `skip_check=True` for this exact reason.
- Inductor lowering of `philox_rand` for the XPU backend. `aot_eager` should
  work after the in-tree fix; `inductor` may need a separate Triton/SYCL lowering
  if a kernel-level emit is missing. Verify before scoping.
- Other accelerators (`hpu`, `mps`). Pattern should be extensible but not part
  of this issue.

### Suggested approach

1. Introduce a backend predicate (`_supports_philox_functionalization(device)`)
   and use it in both `decompositions_for_rng.py` and `rng_prims.py`. Initial
   set: `{"cuda", "xpu"}`.
2. Generalize `philox_rand_offset` to accept `device` (already in the signature
   via callers — currently ignored) and dispatch device-properties lookup off
   `device.type`. For XPU, use:
   - `block_size`: `max_work_group_size` (typically 1024).
   - `sm_count`-equivalent: `gpu_subslice_count` or `max_compute_units / threads_per_eu`.
   - Or take the conservative path and compute a safe upper-bound offset jump
     independent of geometry.
3. Route `_philox_rand`'s `set_torch_state_tensor` call through the
   device-agnostic `RngStateHelper` (no API change — it already resolves the
   active accelerator after #1970 fix).
4. Extend the `test_dropout` / `test_dropout_inductor` enablement to verify
   both `aot_eager` and `inductor` paths on XPU.

### Test plan

- Re-run the two `ActivationCheckpointingTests` on XPU; both must pass.
- Add a smoke test in `test/test_prims.py` that exercises
  `torch.ops.rngprims.philox_rand` directly on the active accelerator.
- Sanity-check CUDA path is unaffected by re-running
  `test/test_prims.py` and one CUDA-pinned `test_dropout*` variant if available.

## Representative Error

```
File "/home/tszulist/src/pytorch/torch/_decomp/decompositions_for_rng.py", line 56, in rand_like
    throw_on_non_cuda(device)
File "/home/tszulist/src/pytorch/torch/_decomp/decompositions_for_rng.py", line 23, in throw_on_non_cuda
    raise RuntimeError(
torch._dynamo.exc.BackendCompilerFailed: backend='compiler_fn' raised:
RuntimeError: You are trying to functionalize a xpu RNG operator but xpu does
not use Philox/counter-based RNG. Therefore, functionalizing a xpu RNG operator
is not supported. We are discussing the possibility of a Philox-based RNG
implementation for CPU.
```

## Shared Context

- HW: Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100 (and BMG); reproduces on any XPU host.
- Software: PyTorch `main` after #1970's `CUDARngStateHelper` fix.
- Dependency on #1970: this issue is only meaningful **after** #1970's helper
  generalization is merged. Without it, the failure surfaces earlier (in
  `_prims_common`) and masks the deeper gates this issue addresses.
- Where the PR belongs: PyTorch in-tree (`pytorch/pytorch`), not `torch-xpu-ops`.
- Labels suggested: `module: xpu`, `module: functorch`, `module: dynamo`.

Same root cause is expected to surface in any other test that toggles
torch._functorch.config.functionalize_rng_ops=True and runs on a non-CUDA accelerator.
Root Cause
The functionalized-RNG lowering for aten.rand / aten.rand_like / dropout is
currently CUDA-only at three places:

torch/_decomp/decompositions_for_rng.py — rand (line 33) and rand_like
(line 56) explicitly call throw_on_non_cuda(device) for any non-CUDA device.
torch/_prims/rng_prims.py — _philox_rand impl (line 116) raises
throw_on_non_cuda when device.type != "cuda".
torch/_prims/rng_prims.py:philox_rand_offset (line 71) — hardcodes
torch.cuda.get_device_properties(torch.cuda.current_device()) and reads
multi_processor_count / max_threads_per_multi_processor. These fields do not
exist on torch.xpu.get_device_properties() (XPU exposes gpu_eu_count,
max_compute_units, gpu_subslice_count, max_num_sub_groups,
max_work_group_size instead).

Functionally, XPU already uses Philox/counter-based RNG (torch.xpu.initial_seed,
_get_rng_state_offset, _set_rng_state_offset, set_rng_state exist and have
the same semantics as the CUDA equivalents), so generalization is feasible — only
the device-properties query and the hard gates are CUDA-shaped.
Reproducer
After applying #1970's fix
(CUDARngStateHelper → RngStateHelper) and switching the two tests to
device=GPU_TYPE + @requires_gpu_and_triton:
cd <pytorch>
python test/dynamo/test_higher_order_ops.py \
    ActivationCheckpointingTests.test_dropout \
    ActivationCheckpointingTests.test_dropout_inductor
Fails with:
RuntimeError: You are trying to functionalize a xpu RNG operator but xpu does not
use Philox/counter-based RNG. Therefore, functionalizing a xpu RNG operator is not
supported. ...

raised from torch/_decomp/decompositions_for_rng.py:23.
Scope of Changes
Files to update (PyTorch in-tree)



File
Change




torch/_decomp/decompositions_for_rng.py
Replace throw_on_non_cuda gate in rand / rand_like with an "accelerator supports Philox" check (allow cuda, xpu, future Philox-capable backends). Update message accordingly.


torch/_prims/rng_prims.py (_philox_rand impl)
Drop the device.type != "cuda" raise; route set_torch_state_tensor through the device-agnostic RngStateHelper (already done by #1970 follow-up); call torch.rand(shape, device=device, ...) which already works on XPU.


torch/_prims/rng_prims.py (philox_rand_offset)
Generalize the device-properties query. Introduce a small helper _philox_offset_grid_params(device) that returns (block_size, blocks_per_sm, sm_count)-equivalent values per backend. For XPU, derive from max_compute_units, max_work_group_size, gpu_subslice_count, max_num_sub_groups. A safe alternative is a conservative upper-bound offset jump that does not depend on hardware geometry — acceptable because over-advancing the Philox counter only wastes counter space, not correctness.


torch/_prims_common/__init__.py
Already done by #1970 follow-up (RngStateHelper device-agnostic). No further change.



Out of scope (do separately)

Numerical equivalence of the XPU Philox stream vs. eager XPU RNG output.
philox_rand is a new RNG stream tracked by AOTAutograd; it is not required
to match the existing eager torch.rand numerics on XPU. The two existing
tests use skip_check=True for this exact reason.
Inductor lowering of philox_rand for the XPU backend. aot_eager should
work after the in-tree fix; inductor may need a separate Triton/SYCL lowering
if a kernel-level emit is missing. Verify before scoping.
Other accelerators (hpu, mps). Pattern should be extensible but not part
of this issue.

Suggested approach

Introduce a backend predicate (_supports_philox_functionalization(device))
and use it in both decompositions_for_rng.py and rng_prims.py. Initial
set: {"cuda", "xpu"}.
Generalize philox_rand_offset to accept device (already in the signature
via callers — currently ignored) and dispatch device-properties lookup off
device.type. For XPU, use:

block_size: max_work_group_size (typically 1024).
sm_count-equivalent: gpu_subslice_count or max_compute_units / threads_per_eu.
Or take the conservative path and compute a safe upper-bound offset jump
independent of geometry.


Route _philox_rand's set_torch_state_tensor call through the
device-agnostic RngStateHelper (no API change — it already resolves the
active accelerator after #1970 fix).
Extend the test_dropout / test_dropout_inductor enablement to verify
both aot_eager and inductor paths on XPU.

Test plan

Re-run the two ActivationCheckpointingTests on XPU; both must pass.
Add a smoke test in test/test_prims.py that exercises
torch.ops.rngprims.philox_rand directly on the active accelerator.
Sanity-check CUDA path is unaffected by re-running
test/test_prims.py and one CUDA-pinned test_dropout* variant if available.

not use Philox/counter-based RNG. Therefore, functionalizing a xpu RNG operator
is not supported. We are discussing the possibility of a Philox-based RNG
implementation for CPU.

Shared Context

HW: Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100 (and BMG); reproduces on any XPU host.
Software: PyTorch main after #1970's CUDARngStateHelper fix.
Dependency on #1970: this issue is only meaningful after #1970's helper
generalization is merged. Without it, the failure surfaces earlier (in
_prims_common) and masks the deeper gates this issue addresses.
Where the PR belongs: PyTorch in-tree (pytorch/pytorch), not torch-xpu-ops.

issues.title: [release/2.15] New failing test case test_vjpvmap_nn_functional_conv3d_xpu_float32
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

New failing test cases appeared in the latest Nightly / Build-from-source and in some pull workflows:
[运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:25439279276]

Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_ops_xpu.TestOperatorsXPU,test_vjpvmap_nn_functional_conv3d_xpu_float32

### Likely root cause

Many similar test cases related to convolution operations that call oneDNN kernels under the hood are failing due to default non deterministic behavior of the oneDNN kernels. That causes slightly different results between consecutive kernel launches with exactly the same inputs, which makes the tests fail as they expect more exact results.
Quick test if that is the root cause is to launch the same tests with `DeterministicGuard(True)` context manager that changes oneDNN kernels into deterministic mode.

issues.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
New failing test cases appeared in the latest Nightly / Build-from-source and in some pull workflows:
[运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:25439279276]
Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_ops_xpu.TestOperatorsXPU,test_vjpvmap_nn_functional_conv3d_xpu_float32
Likely root cause
Many similar test cases related to convolution operations that call oneDNN kernels under the hood are failing due to default non deterministic behavior of the oneDNN kernels. That causes slightly different results between consecutive kernel launches with exactly the same inputs, which makes the tests fail as they expect more exact results.
Quick test if that is the root cause is to launch the same tests with DeterministicGuard(True) context manager that changes oneDNN kernels into deterministic mode.

Prepared tolerance override commit: [地址已移除]

This commit overrides the tolerance for the conv3d operator in the test_vjpvmap test for the xpu device.
The tolerance override is necessary, because the conv3d operator on xpu is non deterministic by default, so launching the same perator with exactly the same inputs can yield slightly different outputs. In case of calculating the gradients with vjpvmap, the non deterministic results can be amplified, which can cause the test to fail with the default tolerance.

To confirm this, I launched the overrided test case with context manager `DeterministicGuard(True)` and with it, test case passed every time.

It is similar change to previous ones in the following PR:
[地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#177069]

Many test cases in functorch module needed tolerance override for conv3d especially.

Adding `wait_upstream` label to create batched PR to PyTorch when several similar changes are needed.

**Outcome:** IMPLEMENTING(fix_verified) -- fix verified in `pytorch`, patch exported for a human to apply. Automated fix session for intel/torch-xpu-ops#3595. Each stage below is appended as it completes.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | pytorch | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Checked against the nightly XPU wheel `2.16.0.dev20261027+xpu` on this BMG runner (`xpu` device). The test node named in the issue no longer exists: the local copy of `dynamo/test_functions.py` was deleted in intel/torch-xpu-ops#4122, and upstream now keeps `test_get_device_properties_tensor_device` in a `FunctionTestsCudaOnly` class instantiated with `only_for="cuda"`, so it never runs on XPU (`pytest --collect-only -k get_device_properties` collects 0 items). The underlying defect the issue describes is still live, and reproduces directly. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_functions.py -k get_device_properties` (original node id) | NO LONGER COLLECTED | `no tests collected (772 deselected)` -- test is CUDA-only upstream | | dynamo tracing of `torch.xpu.get_device_properties()` | REPRODUCED | `torch._dynamo.exc.Unsupported: SourcelessBuilder.create does not know how to wrap ` | Dynamo registers `torch.cuda._CudaDeviceProperties` in `common_constant_types` but has no XPU counterpart, so any traced function that reads XPU device properties hard-errors under `fullgraph`. The missing `max_threads_per_multi_processor` attribute from the original report is a second, separate point: it is a CUDA-only concept, so the fix is to make the test ask for the XPU equivalent rather than to add the attribute. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@36d79410c72`, torch-xpu-ops `main@73a6552c`. Dynamo decides whether a Python value can be folded into a constant via `ConstantVariable.is_base_literal`, which is just `type(obj) in common_constant_types` (`torch/_dynamo/variables/constant.py:206-208`). That set, at `torch/_dynamo/utils.py:3011-3035`, lists `torch.cuda._CudaDeviceProperties` but has no XPU counterpart. `torch.xpu.get_device_properties` is registered as an in-graph function (`torch/_dynamo/trace_rules.py:3063`), so Dynamo evaluates it during tracing and hands the resulting `torch._C._XpuDeviceProperties` to `SourcelessBuilder.create`; the `ConstantVariable.is_literal` branch at `torch/_dynamo/variables/builder.py:5612` therefore misses and execution falls through to the `unimplemented()` at `torch/_dynamo/variables/builder.py:5791-5796`, which is the observed `Unexpected type in sourceless builder` error. The CUDA equivalent is covered and passing (`test/dynamo/test_user_defined_object.py:1911-1921`), which is what makes this an XPU-only gap. The `AttributeError` in the original report was a second, downstream symptom. The test `test_get_device_properties_tensor_device` reads `prop.major`, `prop.multi_processor_count` and `prop.max_threads_per_multi_processor`, all CUDA-specific fields; the torch-xpu-ops copy of the file mechanically rewrote `torch.cuda` to `torch.xpu` without translating the field names. That copy has since been deleted (intel/torch-xpu-ops#4122) and upstream moved the test into a `FunctionTestsCudaOnly` class instantiated `only_for="cuda"` (`test/dynamo/test_functions.py:7314-7350`), so XPU no longer runs it at all -- the symptom was silenced while the underlying Dynamo gap stayed. `max_threads_per_multi_processor` is a CUDA SM concept with no XPU meaning, so the fix is to give XPU its own test over the XPU property names, not to add that attribute to `_XpuDeviceProperties`. Fix strategy: add `torch.xpu._XpuDeviceProperties` to `common_constant_types` next to the CUDA entry -- safe to reference unconditionally because `torch/xpu/__init__.py:78-83` falls back to `_dummy_type("_XpuDeviceProperties")` on builds without XPU -- and restore XPU coverage by mirroring `FunctionTestsCudaOnly` with an XPU-only class over the XPU property names, following the `HardwareClassification.XPU` + `only_for="xpu", allow_xpu=True` pattern already used by `test/test_transformers.py:7096`. A prior upstream PR (`pytorch/pytorch#190323`, open) proposed the same one-line `common_constant_types` addition but branched the then-shared CUDA test on device; upstream has since split that test into a CUDA-only class, so its test half no longer applies. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- one-line Dynamo constant-type registration plus the XPU test that covers it - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** inductor *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Analyzed at:** pytorch@36d79410c72 - **What I changed:** `torch/_dynamo/utils.py` (+1) registers the XPU device-properties type as a Dynamo constant type; `test/dynamo/test_functions.py` (+26/-1) adds an XPU-only test class covering it and registers it for device-type instantiation. - **Why:** `ConstantVariable.is_base_literal` is a membership test against `common_constant_types` (`torch/_dynamo/variables/constant.py:206-208`), so the missing entry is the whole defect; `torch/xpu/__init__.py:78-83` makes the symbol safe to reference on non-XPU builds via its `_dummy_type` fallback. the same one-line common_constant_types addition but branched the then-shared CUDA test on
device; upstream has since split that test into a CUDA-only class, so its test half no longer
applies.

issues.title: [kernel][perf]index_select / embedding kernel 5-22x slower on XPU vs CUDA
issues.body:
`torch.index_select` (used internally by `torch.nn.functional.embedding`) is 5-22x slower on XPU compared to CUDA for identical workloads. Non-contiguous index tensors exacerbate the gap (~2.7x additional penalty on XPU vs ~1.2x on CUDA).

This was discovered during roofline projection analysis of 154 OOB models. `aten::embedding` has R_op ≈ 0.01 in models like LayoutLMForMaskedLM, making it the second-largest projection deficit across the fleet.

reproducer:
 python repro_embedding.py --device xpu
```
import argparse, time, torch

def benchmark(weight_shape, indices_shape, stride_mode, device, warmup=20, repeat=50):
    vocab_size, embed_dim = weight_shape
    weight = torch.randn(vocab_size, embed_dim, dtype=torch.float16, device=device)

    if stride_mode == "contiguous":
        indices = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, indices_shape, dtype=torch.long, device=device)
    else:
        flat = torch.randint(0, vocab_size, (indices_shape[0] * 2048,), dtype=torch.long, device=device)
        indices = torch.as_strided(flat, indices_shape, (2048, 4))

    sync = torch.cuda.synchronize if device == "cuda" else torch.xpu.synchronize

    for _ in range(warmup):
        torch.index_select(weight, 0, indices.reshape(-1))
    sync()

    times = []
    for _ in range(repeat):
        sync()
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        torch.index_select(weight, 0, indices.reshape(-1))
        sync()
        times.append((time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000)

    return sorted(times)[len(times) // 2]
if __name__ == "__main__":
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument("--device", default="cuda", choices=["cuda", "xpu"])
    args = parser.parse_args()
    d = args.device

    cases = [
        ("Large vocab, contiguous",    (30522, 768), (128, 512), "contiguous"),
        ("Small vocab, non-contiguous", (1024, 768),  (128, 512), "non-contiguous"),
        ("Small vocab, contiguous",     (1024, 768),  (128, 512), "contiguous"),
        ("Tiny vocab, contiguous",      (2, 768),     (128, 512), "contiguous"),
    ]

    print(f"Device: {d} ({torch.xpu.get_device_name(0) if d == 'xpu' else torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)})")
    print(f"PyTorch: {torch.__version__}\n")
    for name, ws, ids, stride in cases:
        ms = benchmark(ws, ids, stride, d)
        print(f"  {name:>35} | {ms:.3f} ms")
```

CUDA dispatches to `vectorized_gather_kernel` (contiguous) or `_scatter_gather_elementwise_kernel` (non-contiguous). XPU uses `at::native::xpu::IndexKernel` for all cases.

Model Impact:
In full-model profiling (LayoutLMForMaskedLM_bs128), embedding calls account for 239ms of GPU time on B580 vs 1.3ms on 4080S.

issues.title: Improve errors logging when run_test_with_skip.py is executed
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

When tests are executed stderr is redirected to a file *_test_error.log. But it is not shown in console so GitHub will not saved them. Also because two separate files are created *_test_error.log and *_test.log without any timestamps there is no possibility to see what test cause what error or what happened during each test execution. This is not a problem when the same error is captured by python and show in test summary but that's no the case for some tests. Also if test is random sometime is hard to reproduce a problem but if occur on CI, it will be a great addition to debugging if there is a log error with additional information.

```
python run_test_with_skip.py \
          2> ${{ github.workspace }}/ut_log/op_ut/op_ut_with_skip_test_error.log | \
          tee ${{ github.workspace }}/ut_log/op_ut/op_ut_with_skip_test.log
```

### Alternatives

1) First fix is to just save all the data in one file. So redirect 2>&1. Main log file for Linux op_ut is ~83MB so adding an error log ~180KB is not a big problem in terms of log size.
2) Second idea is to leave two separate logs but use for both of them tee and redirect stderr to console to have all needed data in one GitHub log.

```
python run_test_with_skip.py \
          > >(tee ${{ github.workspace }}/ut_log/op_ut/op_ut_with_skip_test.log) \
          2> >(tee ${{ github.workspace }}/ut_log/op_ut/op_ut_with_skip_test_error.log >&2)
```

### Additional context

_No response_

issues.title: Register spill in XeFMHAFwdKernel on PVC (SIMD16, 256 GRF)
issues.body:
# Summary
Register spill warnings observed when compiling FMHA forward kernels on PVC. All three kernel variants use SIMD16 + 256 GRF configuration and spill 2–6 registers. While the spill count is small, it may cause measurable performance degradation in latency-sensitive attention kernels.

# Compiler Warnings
```
warning: kernel XeFMHAFwdKernel<FMHAProblemShape<false>, FMHAFwdMainloop<XeDefault<2>, causal=true,  TiledMMA QK(64x32), PV(32x64), VTiles=2, EpilogueTile(128x64)>>
  compiled SIMD16 allocated 256 regs and spilled around 6

warning: kernel XeFMHAFwdKernel<FMHAProblemShape<false>, FMHAFwdMainloop<XeDefault<2>, causal=false, TiledMMA QK(64x32), PV(32x64), VTiles=3, EpilogueTile(128x96)>>
  compiled SIMD16 allocated 256 regs and spilled around 2

  compiled SIMD16 allocated 256 regs and spilled around 2
```

issues.title: [BMG] PyTorch 2.12 performance cases where inductor is slower than eager (speedup < 1)
issues.body:
## Summary

BMG PyTorch 2.12 release performance results contain multiple cases where inductor is slower than eager (`speedup < 1`).

nodes.body: In PyTorch 2.12, models with 4D broadcasted attention masks (e.g. HuggingFace BERT/BART/Electra with shape [B, 1, 1, S]) fail to dispatch to the oneDNN SDPA backend (overrideable_attention) on XPU, falling back to the un-fused math backend. Profiling traces show that this fallback introduces extra general GEMMs and unfused softmax kernels per attention block, causing substantial performance regressions (speedup < 1.0). after the sdpa path fix ([地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#197505]): we could see that model 05_plbart_bf16_inf and 06_bert_amp_inf did not show regression again: - 05_plbart_bf16_inf: 121 gemm + 12 triton safe_softmax_add + 6 micro_sdpa -> 97 gemm + 18 micro_sdpa - 06_bert_amp_inf: 97 gemm + 12 triton safe_softmax_add -> 73 gemm + 12 micro_sdpa - and all other models that have attention blocks improved (models that don't have attention: 09_lennard_bf16_inf, 10_maml_bf16_inf, 11_sac_bf16_inf)
nodes.bodyText:
In PyTorch 2.12, models with 4D broadcasted attention masks (e.g. HuggingFace BERT/BART/Electra with shape [B, 1, 1, S]) fail to dispatch to the oneDNN SDPA backend (overrideable_attention) on XPU, falling back to the un-fused math backend.
Profiling traces show that this fallback introduces extra general GEMMs and unfused softmax kernels per attention block, causing substantial performance regressions (speedup < 1.0).
after the sdpa path fix (pytorch/pytorch#197505):

we could see that model 05_plbart_bf16_inf and 06_bert_amp_inf did not show regression again:

05_plbart_bf16_inf:  121 gemm + 12 triton safe_softmax_add + 6 micro_sdpa -> 97 gemm + 18 micro_sdpa
06_bert_amp_inf: 97 gemm + 12 triton safe_softmax_add -> 73 gemm + 12 micro_sdpa
and all other models that have attention blocks improved (models that don't have attention: 09_lennard_bf16_inf, 10_maml_bf16_inf, 11_sac_bf16_inf)

nodes.body:
MAML inference performs task-specific finetuning and calls `torch.autograd.grad()`. With PyTorch 2.14's default Dynamo settings, autograd operations are not traced, which causes graph breaks.

This change:
- enables `trace_autograd_ops` for MAML;
- passes parameters and BatchNorm state explicitly;
- removes `deepcopy()` and `Tensor.item()` from the compiled path.

MAML inference now compiles without the observed graph breaks or recompilations. Validated on Intel XPU with numerical correctness checks and approximately 2.7x Inductor speedup over eager.

issues.title: [OOB][Perf] aten::cat performance gap on XPU vs CUDA (54 models affected)
issues.body:
## Summary

`aten::cat` is the top 1 op priority for XPU performance improvement in OOB 300 eager inference (fp16). Improving cat to match CUDA roofline efficiency would give the largest fleet geomean R improvement.

## Data (from roofline profiling, 154 models, fp16 inference)

| Platform | Geomean R Delta | Models Affected | Total Saving (ms) |
|----------|------:|------:|------:|
| B580 | +0.0147 | 54 | 8,717 |
| G31 (B70) | +0.0082 | 46 | 1,033 |

Current fleet geomean R: B580=0.644, G31=0.675, 4080S=0.683.

## Worst affected models

| Model | BS | Suite | B580 R | 4080S R | G31 R | B580/4080S T2 | G31/4080S T2 | Top Gap Op |
|-------|---:|-------|------:|------:|------:|------:|------:|------|
| hf_Reformer | 128 | torchbench | 0.167 | 0.735 | 0.555 | 7.60x | 1.75x | aten::cat |
| dpn107 | 512 | timm | 0.646 | 0.746 | 0.615 | 1.87x | 1.45x | aten::cat |
| res2net50_14w_8s | 1024 | timm | 0.569 | 0.673 | 0.589 | 2.06x | 1.49x | aten::cat |
| yolov3 | 128 | torchbench | 0.865 | 0.790 | 0.697 | 1.39x | 1.22x | aten::cat |
| moondream | 1 | torchbench | 0.585 | 0.687 | 0.503 | 1.35x | 1.01x | aten::cat |
| selecsls42b | 1024 | timm | 0.682 | 0.752 | 0.674 | 1.71x | 1.25x | aten::cat |
| BartForCausalLM | 32 | huggingface | 0.778 | 0.835 | 0.725 | 1.27x | 0.89x | aten::cat |
| MBartForCausalLM | 32 | huggingface | 0.779 | 0.831 | 0.725 | 0.83x | 0.58x | aten::cat |

## Methodology

T1/T2/R roofline projection framework. R_op = projected_time / actual_time per op. If R_op on XPU < R_op on CUDA for the same model, the XPU kernel is underperforming relative to hardware capability. "Total Saving" = sum across all affected models of (actual_xpu - target_xpu) where target = proj / R_cuda.

## Hardware

- B580: 93 TFLOPS fp16, 410 GB/s
- G31 (B70): 154 TFLOPS fp16, 532 GB/s
- 4080S: 100.96 TFLOPS fp16, 716.8 GB/s

## Summary

| densenet121 | 2048 | torchbench | 0.066 | 0.711 | 0.567 | 18.67x | 1.67x | aten::convolution |
| poolformer_m36 | 1024 | timm | 0.418 | 0.557 | 0.483 | 2.26x | 1.48x | aten::clone |
| res2net50_14w_8s | 1024 | timm | 0.569 | 0.673 | 0.589 | 2.06x | 1.49x | aten::cat |

issues.title: [OOB][Perf] aten::addmm (GEMM) performance gap on XPU vs CUDA (62 models affected)
issues.body:
## Summary

`aten::addmm` (GEMM) is the top 1 op priority on G31 (B70) for XPU performance improvement in OOB 300 eager inference (fp16). It affects the most models (62) of any op. The gap indicates oneMKL GEMM is not reaching peak efficiency at the shapes used by these models.

## Data (from roofline profiling, 154 models, fp16 inference)

| Platform | Geomean R Delta | Models Affected | Total Saving (ms) |
|----------|------:|------:|------:|
| G31 (B70) | +0.0091 | 62 | 1,165 |
| B580 | +0.0039 | 11 | 5,193 |

Current fleet geomean R: B580=0.644, G31=0.675, 4080S=0.683.

## Worst affected models

| Model | BS | Suite | B580 R | 4080S R | G31 R | B580/4080S T2 | G31/4080S T2 | Top Gap Op |

| hf_Roberta_base | 32 | torchbench | 0.732 | 0.778 | 0.625 | 1.01x | 0.73x | aten::addmm |
| hf_Bert | 256 | torchbench | 0.853 | 0.866 | 0.744 | 1.23x | 0.91x | aten::addmm |
| BertForMaskedLM | 128 | huggingface | 0.862 | 0.876 | 0.769 | 1.28x | 0.95x | aten::addmm |
| CamemBert | 128 | huggingface | 0.823 | 0.818 | 0.729 | 0.82x | 0.61x | aten::addmm |

| timm_vision_transformer_large | 512 | torchbench | 0.731 | 0.898 | 0.653 | 1.49x | 1.08x | aten::sdpa_forward |

## Note

GEMM (addmm) affects 62 models on G31 — the widest impact of any single op. These are primarily transformer/NLP models where matrix multiplication dominates. ## Hardware

- B580: 93 TFLOPS fp16, 410 GB/s
- G31 (B70): 154 TFLOPS fp16, 532 GB/s
- 4080S: 100.96 TFLOPS fp16, 716.8 GB/s

issues.title: [OOB][Perf] aten::clone unnecessary memory copies on XPU (18 models affected)
issues.body:
## Summary

`aten::clone` is the top 3 op priority on B580 and top 5 on G31 for XPU performance improvement in OOB 300 eager inference (fp16). Clone creates unnecessary memory copies that inflate T2 relative to CUDA. This could indicate missing in-place optimizations or suboptimal memory format handling on XPU.

## Data (from roofline profiling, 154 models, fp16 inference)

| Platform | Geomean R Delta | Models Affected | Total Saving (ms) |
|----------|------:|------:|------:|
| B580 | +0.0097 | 18 | 5,579 |
| G31 (B70) | +0.0042 | 9 | 2,824 |

Current fleet geomean R: B580=0.644, G31=0.675, 4080S=0.683.

## Worst affected models

| Model | BS | Suite | B580 R | 4080S R | G31 R | B580/4080S T2 | G31/4080S T2 | Top Gap Op |
|-------|---:|-------|------:|------:|------:|------:|------:|------|
| cait_m36_384 | 128 | timm | 0.404 | 0.709 | 0.395 | 2.88x | 2.20x | aten::clone |
| detectron2_maskrcnn | 16 | torchbench | 0.477 | 0.620 | 0.511 | 2.03x | 1.37x | aten::clone |
| detectron2_maskrcnn_r_50_fpn | 16 | torchbench | 0.481 | 0.616 | 0.513 | 2.00x | 1.36x | aten::clone |
| detectron2_fasterrcnn_r_50_fpn | 16 | torchbench | 0.594 | 0.641 | 0.551 | 1.67x | 1.30x | aten::clone |
| poolformer_m36 | 1024 | timm | 0.418 | 0.557 | 0.483 | 2.26x | 1.48x | aten::clone |
| detectron2_maskrcnn_r_101_fpn | 16 | torchbench | 0.550 | 0.657 | 0.579 | 1.86x | 1.28x | aten::clone |
| detectron2_fasterrcnn_r_50_dc5 | 16 | torchbench | 0.690 | 0.629 | 0.548 | 1.28x | 1.13x | aten::clone |

## Analysis

Clone being the top gap op in multiple detectron2 and vision models suggests XPU's memory format conversion (e.g., channels-last to contiguous) or tensor copy paths are slower than CUDA. If these clones are introduced by format conversion, optimizing the strided copy kernel or avoiding unnecessary format transitions would help.

## Hardware

- B580: 93 TFLOPS fp16, 410 GB/s
- G31 (B70): 154 TFLOPS fp16, 532 GB/s
- 4080S: 100.96 TFLOPS fp16, 716.8 GB/s

issues.title: [OOB][Perf] aten::native_batch_norm performance gap on B580 (13 models affected)
issues.body:
## Summary

`aten::native_batch_norm` is the top 4 op priority on B580 for XPU performance improvement in OOB 300 eager inference (fp16). The gap is significantly larger on B580 than G31, suggesting a platform-specific kernel issue.

## Data (from roofline profiling, 154 models, fp16 inference)

| Platform | Geomean R Delta | Models Affected | Total Saving (ms) |
|----------|------:|------:|------:|
| B580 | +0.0049 | 13 | 6,168 |
| G31 (B70) | +0.0012 | 10 | 145 |

Current fleet geomean R: B580=0.644, G31=0.675, 4080S=0.683.
## Note

The B580 total saving (6,168 ms) is 42x larger than G31 (145 ms) despite fewer affected models. This strongly suggests a B580-specific performance issue with the batch_norm kernel — likely related to occupancy, vectorization, or memory access patterns on BMG architecture.

Batch norm is a memory-bound op (vector engine). The roofline projects it at bytes/BW, so a gap means the kernel is not achieving peak bandwidth on B580.

## Hardware

- B580: 93 TFLOPS fp16, 410 GB/s
- G31 (B70): 154 TFLOPS fp16, 532 GB/s
- 4080S: 100.96 TFLOPS fp16, 716.8 GB/s

XPU's backend priority is overrideable (oneDNN) before flash (`aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/Attention.cpp:179-184`), and `can_use_overrideable_attention` carries a `check_no_grad` gate (`:45-53`, listed at `:74`) that rejects the oneDNN backend whenever an input requires grad with GradMode enabled, so selection falls through to flash (`:220-224`). issues.title: _flash_attention_forward not implemented for XPU — meta test failures
issues.body:
Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_meta_xpu.TestMetaXPU,test_dispatch_symbolic_meta_outplace_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_meta_xpu.TestMetaXPU,test_dispatch_meta_outplace_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16

## Root Cause

The `aten::_flash_attention_forward` operator is not registered for the XPU device. When the meta dispatch tests try to execute this op on an XPU tensor, it fails with a "not implemented" error, which gets wrapped as `Exception: Original OpInfo is broken`.

The underlying error is:
```
The operator 'aten::_flash_attention_forward' is not currently implemented for the XPU device.
```

This is separate from the flex_attention export tests (Group 1), which fail due to graph structure mismatch. Here, the op itself cannot run on XPU.

**Fix:** Either:
1. Implement `_flash_attention_forward` for XPU (substantial effort).
2. Add these test patterns to the skip list in `skip_list_common.py` (the `_flash_attention_` pattern already skips flash attention in `test_ops_xpu.py` but not in `test_meta_xpu.py`).

## Reproducer

```bash
source ~/.bashrc && cd third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu && python -m pytest -sxv test_meta_xpu.py -k "test_dispatch_symbolic_meta_outplace_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16"
```

```bash
source ~/.bashrc && cd third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu && python -m pytest -sxv test_meta_xpu.py -k "test_dispatch_meta_outplace_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16"
```

## Representative Error

```
Exception: Original OpInfo is broken

Caused by sample input at index 0: SampleInput(input=Tensor[size=(4, 11, 4, 8),
device="xpu:0", dtype=torch.float16, contiguous=False], ...)

The operator 'aten::_flash_attention_forward' is not currently implemented for
the XPU device. Please open a feature on [地址已移除]
You can set the environment variable `PYTORCH_ENABLE_XPU_FALLBACK=1` to use the
CPU implementation as a fallback for XPU unimplemented operators.
```

Automated fix run for this issue. Follow progress in the [workflow run]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659326117]). ### Stage 1 - Triage - **Type:** single-bug (two test ids, one root cause) - **Scope:** `test/xpu/test_meta_xpu.py`, op-info driven meta dispatch tests - **Reproducer:** present in the issue body - **Runtime dependency:** upstream `aten::_flash_attention_forward` XPU registration ### Stage 2 - Reproduce: NOT_REPRODUCED Environment: nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261027+xpu`, `torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c` (main), matching `pytorch` checkout at `087ceb5bbaf` on BMG (Arc Pro B60). Both reproducer commands from the issue body now report the test as skipped, not failed: | Test | Before (issue, 2026-06-03) | Now | |---|---|---| | `test_dispatch_symbolic_meta_outplace_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16` | FAILED (`Original OpInfo is broken`) | SKIPPED | | `test_dispatch_meta_outplace_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16` | FAILED (`Original OpInfo is broken`) | SKIPPED | The other four instantiations of that OpInfo (`test_meta_outplace`, `test_meta_inplace`, and the two `_inplace` dispatch variants) skip as well, so the whole OpInfo is quiet on XPU. ### Why it stopped failing The original symptom was real and its cause is unchanged - `aten::_flash_attention_forward` still has no XPU registration. Probing it directly on this nightly: ``` NotImplementedError: The operator 'aten::_flash_attention_forward' is not currently implemented for the XPU device. ``` What changed is the OpInfo, not the op. The `torch.ops.aten._flash_attention_forward` OpInfo in `torch/testing/_internal/common_methods_invocations.py` now carries a `skipXPU` decorator, added upstream by `pytorch/pytorch#176688` ("Enable eager tests for inductor-unittest - enable test_dtypes and align XPU op dtypes with OpInfo", in nightlies since 2026-07-22). `skipXPU` is an unconditional `skipXPUIf(True, ...)` in the OpInfo's `decorators` list, so every `@ops`-generated test for that OpInfo skips on XPU - including the meta dispatch tests this issue tracks. That is also why intel/torch-xpu-ops#4278, which replaced the hand-maintained test with the `XPUImportCtx` wrapper, did not need a skip-list entry: `_flash_attention_forward` is deliberately absent from the `test_meta_xpu.py` tuple in `test/xpu/skip_list_common.py` (unlike `_efficient_attention_forward`, kept there for intel/torch-xpu-ops#2285). ### No patch produced Nothing was changed and no fix branch exists, for two reasons: 1. The reported failures do not reproduce, so there is nothing to fix in this repository. Adding the skip-list entry option 2 of the issue body proposes would be dead weight on top of the upstream `skipXPU`. 2. Option 1, implementing `_flash_attention_forward` / `_flash_attention_backward` for XPU, is feature work already in flight (`pytorch/pytorch#181559` plus intel/torch-xpu-ops#3404) and well outside what this job may land autonomously. `pytorch/pytorch#181559` is still open, which is the condition the 2026-08-10 comment left this issue waiting on. **Suggested human action:** this issue is now only a tracker for the unmerged `pytorch/pytorch#181559`. Either close it in favour of that PR and intel/torch-xpu-ops#3404, or retitle it as the feature request, since the meta-test symptom in the title no longer occurs. Worth noting for whoever picks up `pytorch/pytorch#181559`: the upstream `skipXPU` on this OpInfo will have to be removed in the same change, or the XPU implementation lands with these meta and op tests still skipped.
Summary The two `test_meta_xpu.py` failures reported here no longer reproduce: upstream `pytorch/pytorch#176688` added a `skipXPU` decorator to the `torch.ops.aten._flash_attention_forward` OpInfo, so all six of its XPU test instantiations now skip instead of erroring out on the missing operator. The underlying cause is untouched - `aten::_flash_attention_forward` is still unregistered for XPU - but registering it is feature work already in flight as `pytorch/pytorch#181559` and intel/torch-xpu-ops#3404, not something this job should land. Verified on nightly `2.16.0.dev20261027+xpu` against `torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c` on BMG; both reproducer commands report SKIPPED. - **Verdict:** `SKIPPED(no_longer_reproduces)` - **Branch:** none - **Changed files:** none - **Nothing was pushed and no patch artifact was produced** - there is no diff to review.
_Generated by [fix job]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659326117])._
Review Copy into a new comment, keep ONE verdict, add a note. Two verdicts in one comment are dropped as ambiguous. ``` **strong-accepted** **weak-accepted** **weak-rejected** **strong-rejected** **issue-drop** notes: ``` On a batch run add `item=` to say which sub-item the verdict is about, **in the bold text and in the marker** -- the marker is invisible, so the bold line is all a reader sees. One comment per sub-item, since a bare verdict on a batch does not say which test it means and is dropped. `run=` only when judging a run other than the newest, in both places too. A CI DISABLED sub-item, `item=` from the fan-out table: ``` **strong-accepted item=197334** notes: same TensorAssign overload as upstream CUDA, fp8 dispatch list matches ``` Another sub-item of the same batch, judged on an earlier run: ``` **weak-rejected run=35171979678 item=197335** notes: green only because the test is skipped, the kernel still lacks fp8 ``` An `[xpu-alignment]` issue that should not have been filed -- one issue per difference, so no `item=`: ``` **issue-drop** notes: accepted XPU/CUDA numerics difference, nothing to repair ```

test_dispatch_symbolic_meta_outplace_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16
FAILED (Original OpInfo is broken)
SKIPPED


test_dispatch_meta_outplace_torch_ops_aten__flash_attention_forward_xpu_float16
FAILED (Original OpInfo is broken)
SKIPPED



The other four instantiations of that OpInfo (test_meta_outplace,
test_meta_inplace, and the two _inplace dispatch variants) skip as well, so
the whole OpInfo is quiet on XPU.
Why it stopped failing
The original symptom was real and its cause is unchanged - aten::_flash_attention_forward
still has no XPU registration. Probing it directly on this nightly:
NotImplementedError: The operator 'aten::_flash_attention_forward' is not
currently implemented for the XPU device.

What changed is the OpInfo, not the op. The torch.ops.aten._flash_attention_forward
OpInfo in torch/testing/_internal/common_methods_invocations.py now carries a
skipXPU decorator, added upstream by pytorch/pytorch#176688 ("Enable eager
tests for inductor-unittest - enable test_dtypes and align XPU op dtypes with
OpInfo", in nightlies since 2026-07-22). skipXPU is an unconditional
skipXPUIf(True, ...) in the OpInfo's decorators list, so every
@ops-generated test for that OpInfo skips on XPU - including the meta dispatch
tests this issue tracks. That is also why #4278, which
replaced the hand-maintained test with the XPUImportCtx wrapper, did not need a
skip-list entry: _flash_attention_forward is deliberately absent from the
test_meta_xpu.py tuple in test/xpu/skip_list_common.py (unlike
_efficient_attention_forward, kept there for #2285).
No patch produced
Nothing was changed and no fix branch exists, for two reasons:

The reported failures do not reproduce, so there is nothing to fix in this
repository. Adding the skip-list entry option 2 of the issue body proposes
would be dead weight on top of the upstream skipXPU.
Option 1, implementing _flash_attention_forward / _flash_attention_backward
for XPU, is feature work already in flight (pytorch/pytorch#181559 plus
#3404) and well outside what this job may land
autonomously. pytorch/pytorch#181559 is still open, which is the condition
the 2026-08-10 comment left this issue waiting on.

Suggested human action: this issue is now only a tracker for the unmerged
pytorch/pytorch#181559. Either close it in favour of that PR and
#3404, or retitle it as the feature request, since the
meta-test symptom in the title no longer occurs. Worth noting for whoever picks
up pytorch/pytorch#181559: the upstream skipXPU on this OpInfo will have to
be removed in the same change, or the XPU implementation lands with these meta
and op tests still skipped.


Summary
The two test_meta_xpu.py failures reported here no longer reproduce: upstream
pytorch/pytorch#176688 added a skipXPU decorator to the
torch.ops.aten._flash_attention_forward OpInfo, so all six of its XPU test
instantiations now skip instead of erroring out on the missing operator. The
underlying cause is untouched - aten::_flash_attention_forward is still
unregistered for XPU - but registering it is feature work already in flight as
pytorch/pytorch#181559 and #3404, not something this job
should land. Verified on nightly 2.16.0.dev20261027+xpu against
torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c on BMG; both reproducer commands report SKIPPED.

review.

nodes.body:
Automated fix session for this issue. Stage reports are appended below as the pipeline advances.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | pytorch | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Failing test: `test/dynamo/test_repros.py::ReproTestsDeviceXPU::test_partitioner_activation_memory_budget_with_unbacked_symints_xpu` (numerical mismatch, currently carries a `skipIfXpu` referencing this issue upstream). *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Ran against the latest XPU nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261027+xpu` with the pytorch tree at `origin/main` (`dd50eb629ec`), on this job's BMG runner (Intel Arc Pro B60, driver `1.17.39395+16`). The test is currently skipped upstream by `@skipIfXpu(msg=".../issues/3860")`, so the decorator was removed in place for the run and the file reverted afterwards. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_partitioner_activation_memory_budget_with_unbacked_symints_xpu` | NOT_REPRODUCED on this runner | `1 passed` -- `out_ref` and `out_test` come out **bitwise identical** (`torch.equal` is `True`, 0/262144 elements differ) | The reported failure came from the June 2026 nightly UT job, which ran on **PVC** (`nightly_ondemand.yml` used `runner: pvc` then; it uses `bmg-test` today). This job runs on BMG, so the as-reported failure is not reachable from here, which also matches the two earlier manual attempts recorded on this issue. That is not evidence the bug is gone: the defect is in the test's tolerance, not in a kernel, and it is still present in `origin/main`. Measured on this runner, the assertion only passes while the two matmuls agree bit-for-bit -- see Root Cause. The pipeline therefore continued instead of closing this out as stale. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@dd50eb629ec`. The test is numerically ill-conditioned: it demands that eager and compiled `matmul` agree **bit for bit**. `test/dynamo/test_repros.py:9681` returns `torch.matmul(x, param).sin() * z2.sum()` for `x`, `param` of shape `(512, 512)` drawn from `randn`, and `z2.sum()` is exactly `513`. `test/dynamo/test_repros.py:9687` then compares with a bare `self.assertEqual(out_ref, out_test)`, i.e. the default float32 tolerances `rtol=1.3e-6, atol=1e-5` (`torch/testing/_comparison.py:99`). Measured on this runner, the matmul result reaches `|.| = 115.7`, where one float32 ULP is `1.4e-5`; multiplying by `513` turns that single ULP into `~4e-3` of absolute error in the compared tensor -- about 400x the `1e-5` atol. The tolerance therefore admits a matmul difference of only `~1.3e-6`, which is *below* half a ULP at that magnitude, so the assertion passes only while the two matmuls are bitwise equal. That is exactly the reported magnitude. The issue log shows `Greatest absolute difference: 0.0038909912109375`, which is `513 x 7.6e-6` -- one float32 ULP at `|matmul| ~ 64`. The same log also shows two runs of the same test mismatching different element counts (4367 and 2108 of 262144), so on that machine the two matmuls were not even reproducible run to run. To put a number on how little slack the assertion has: recomputing this matmul in fp32 with a split-K reduction order instead (a legitimate alternative ordering) moves the result by up to `1.3e-4`, which through `.sin() * 513` becomes up to `4.3e-2` and mismatches 180974/262144 elements at the default tolerance. Nothing about this is XPU-specific; CUDA passes only because its two matmuls happen to come out identical. The `@skipIfXpu` added at `test/dynamo/test_repros.py:9631` by `pytorch/pytorch#174370` (landed as `1c94cbdb620`, 2026-06-08) silenced the test rather than fixing it, so the fragility is still in `origin/main`. Removing the skip on its own is not enough either: pytorch's own `xpu.yml` runs the `default` config, which includes `test/dynamo/`, on `linux.idc.xpu` (PVC) -- the same hardware class that reported the failure. The fix is to give the assertion a tolerance sized to the `513x` amplification, and drop the skip. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- the test's own tolerance is the defect and it is a two-line change in pytorch. - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch (test infra; secondary: inductor) Side note for a human, out of scope here: if `aten::mm` for fp32 really is not run-to-run reproducible on PVC, that is worth its own look. This test is not the place it should be caught, since PyTorch does not promise eager and compiled runs share a reduction order. *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Analyzed at:** pytorch@dd50eb629ec - **What I changed:** `test/dynamo/test_repros.py` (+7/-2) -- dropped the `@skipIfXpu` on `test_partitioner_activation_memory_budget_with_unbacked_symints` and gave its `assertEqual` an explicit `atol=1e-1, rtol=1e-5`, with the derivation of the number in a comment. - **Why:** the compared tensor is `matmul(x, param).sin() * 513`, so it scales any matmul disagreement by 513x; the default float32 `atol=1e-5` (`torch/testing/_comparison.py:99`) leaves less than half a float32 ULP of slack at the matmul's magnitude, which is why only a bitwise-identical matmul passes. issues.title: index_select / advanced indexing / nn.Embedding hang indefinitely on Intel UHD Graphics (Raptor Lake iGPU), XPU backend
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

On an Intel **UHD Graphics** integrated GPU (Raptor Lake-P), integer-tensor indexing operations **hang indefinitely** on the XPU device — no error, no progress, the call never returns (only killable via SIGKILL). The identical operations are instant on CPU and CUDA.

**Hangs:** `tensor[index_tensor]` (advanced indexing), `torch.index_select`, `nn.Embedding`, and `matmul` whose operand is a `one_hot(...).float()` tensor.

**Works (for contrast):** scalar/slice indexing (`A[3]`), `torch.gather`, conv1d/conv2d, matmul of normal tensors, LSTM, `argmax`, `one_hot`.

| Operation | XPU result |
|-----------|-----------|
| `A[3]` (scalar/slice) | ✅ OK |
| `torch.gather(A, dim, idx)` | ✅ OK |
| conv / matmul(normal) / LSTM / argmax / one_hot | ✅ OK |
| `A[idx_tensor]` (advanced indexing) | ❌ HANG |
| `torch.index_select(A, 0, idx)` | ❌ HANG |
| `nn.Embedding(...)(idx)` | ❌ HANG |
| `matmul(one_hot(...).float(), B)` | ❌ HANG |

### Minimal reproducer

```python
import torch
dev = torch.device("xpu")
A = torch.randn(7, 3, device=dev)
idx = torch.tensor([3, 1, 4, 1], device=dev)
y = A[idx]            # hangs forever on Intel UHD Graphics XPU
torch.xpu.synchronize()
print(y.shape)        # never reached
```

`torch.gather`, `A[3]`, conv, matmul, and LSTM all complete instantly on the same device; only integer-tensor indexing / `index_select` / `nn.Embedding` hang.

### Impact

Any model using embedding lookups (all transformer/LLM token embeddings) or advanced indexing hangs on this iGPU under the XPU backend. It surfaced for me in pyannote.audio speaker diarization: the Powerset→multilabel conversion (`one_hot(argmax) @ mapping`, equivalently `mapping[argmax]`) hangs, deadlocking the segmentation step on XPU while a pure-conv embedding model runs fine.

### Workaround

Run the affected op on CPU (`x.cpu()` around the indexing), or restructure to use `torch.gather` (which works) instead of `index_select` / advanced indexing.

### Versions

- GPU: Intel Core i7-1355U integrated **Raptor Lake-P "UHD Graphics"** (PCI `8086:a721`)
- torch: `2.6.0+xpu`
- OS: Fedora 42; Level Zero `oneapi-level-zero` 1.24.2, `intel-compute-runtime` 25.31
- `torch.xpu.is_available()` → True; basic compute (matmul/conv/LSTM) works.

### Related

- intel/intel-extension-for-pytorch#802 — same UHD Graphics class, "Native API failed … during tensor indexing operations", XPU-only, unresolved (repo archived).
- intel/intel-extension-for-pytorch#513 — `xpu.synchronize` hangs (related synchronization class).

## PR opened: #4883 (ConvTranspose1d parity sub-issue)

Following the [dashboard batch]([地址已移除：CuiYifeng/torch-xpu-ops-sandbox#120]) for this issue: review verdict was approval, target repo is torch-xpu-ops, so the verified patch is submitted here.

- PR: #4883 — [地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#4883]
- Branch: `agent/issue-18-conv-transpose1d-parity`

### Fix

Add `("nn.ConvTranspose1d", "test_cpu_gpu_parity")` to `_cuda_xfail_xpu_pass` in `test/xpu/xpu_test_utils.py`.

### Root cause

The XPU test harness `align_db_decorators` remaps every CUDA `expectedFailure` decorator onto XPU unless the `(op, test)` pair is whitelisted in `_cuda_xfail_xpu_pass`. `test_cpu_gpu_parity_nn_ConvTranspose1d_xpu_complex32` inherits a CUDA `expectedFailure` even though the XPU kernel actually computes correctly, so pytest reports "Unexpected success". `ConvTranspose2d` / `LazyConvTranspose2d` are already whitelisted for their memory-format parity tests; the 1D sibling was simply missing.

### Verification

Verified PASS on `torch==2.14.0.dev20260725+xpu` (PVC single tile):

```
pytest -v test/xpu/test_modules_xpu.py::TestModuleXPU::test_cpu_gpu_parity_nn_ConvTranspose1d_xpu_complex32
```

### Other sub-issues on this parent

Following the dashboard batch for this issue: review verdict was approval, target repo is torch-xpu-ops, so the verified patch is submitted here.

PR: #4883 — #4883
Branch: agent/issue-18-conv-transpose1d-parity

Fix
Add ("nn.ConvTranspose1d", "test_cpu_gpu_parity") to _cuda_xfail_xpu_pass in test/xpu/xpu_test_utils.py.
Root cause
The XPU test harness align_db_decorators remaps every CUDA expectedFailure decorator onto XPU unless the (op, test) pair is whitelisted in _cuda_xfail_xpu_pass. test_cpu_gpu_parity_nn_ConvTranspose1d_xpu_complex32 inherits a CUDA expectedFailure even though the XPU kernel actually computes correctly, so pytest reports "Unexpected success". ConvTranspose2d / LazyConvTranspose2d are already whitelisted for their memory-format parity tests; the 1D sibling was simply missing.

issues.body:

Goal of this task is to add support for lu_factor without pivoting. oneMKL `getrfnp`/`getrfnp_batch` should be used

### Alternatives

_No response_

### Additional context

Gap was found in unit tests, not model

issues.title: Remove upcasting workaround for FFT operations once oneMKL introduce native support for Half dtype.
issues.body:
## Problem description

There was a problem that MKL FFT doesn't support dtype Half. It was originally tracked in the issue #2617.
There was a workaround added that simply upcasts the Half dtype to single precision 32 bit type and then performs calculations. This workaround was introduced in Pull Request [地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#2637] That is mathematically valid and correct, but for the performance reasons it would be better to use directly the native MKL Half dtype computations for FFT.

## Task

The Half dtype support for MKL FFT kernels is on the MKL roadmap.
This task issue is to track the MKL releases and remove the workaround introduced by #2637 once MKL oficially supports the Half dtype for FFT operations.

issues.title: Add XPU GPU IPC support for tensor multiprocessing
issues.body:
## Problem

PyTorch's tensor multiprocessing (Queue-based sharing) relies on GPU IPC for cross-process mutation visibility. CUDA provides this via `cudaIpcMemHandle` — both processes map the same GPU memory allocation, so mutations in one process are immediately visible in the other.

XPU currently has no GPU IPC mechanism, which blocks proper tensor multiprocessing support.

## Impact

In pytorch/pytorch PR #186793, XPU tensor multiprocessing was implemented using CPU copy fallback. This correctly preserves values but cannot support cross-process mutation visibility — 3 device-generic tests must be skipped:

- `test_simple_sharing`: child's `fill_(4)` not visible to parent
- `test_variable_sharing`: parent's post-send mutation not visible to child
- `test_parameter_sharing`: same pattern

## What's needed

1. XPU-level IPC mechanism (equivalent to `cudaIpcMemHandle` + `cudaIpcGetMemHandle`/`cudaIpcOpenMemHandle`)
2. `XPUCachingAllocator::shareIpcHandle()` method
3. C++ IPC types for XPU (ref-counting, event sync) — see `CUDACachingAllocator.cpp` and `CudaIPCTypes.h` for reference
4. `_share_xpu_()` Python binding exposing the IPC handle

## References

- CUDA IPC path: `torch/multiprocessing/reductions.py:341-375` (`reduce_tensor` CUDA branch)
- CUDA IPC rebuild: `torch/multiprocessing/reductions.py:153-218` (`rebuild_cuda_tensor`)
- PyTorch PR #186793: [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#186793]
- PyTorch issue #186585: [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#186585]

issues.body:

op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_distributions_xpu.TestDistributionsXPU,test_wishart_moments_xpu

## Root Cause

Distribution sampling and moment-verification tests fail with `AssertionError` on XPU. The failures fall into two patterns:

1. **"Tensor-likes are not close"** — gradient or icdf/quantile comparisons show large absolute/relative differences (e.g., `scale.grad` mismatch of 64.5 in `test_cauchy_xpu`, moment mismatches in `test_wishart_moments_xpu`). All 25/25 elements mismatched in several tests, indicating a systematic numerical divergence rather than occasional precision loss.

2. **"sample() is biased"** — statistical hypothesis tests (Kolmogorov-Smirnov style) reject the null hypothesis that samples come from the expected distribution. Bias values narrowly exceed thresholds (e.g., `0.062 > 0.060` for GeneralizedPareto, `-0.059 > -0.061` for LogisticNormal), suggesting XPU's RNG or floating-point arithmetic produces sample statistics that deviate slightly from CPU/CUDA expectations.

Both patterns point to XPU numerical precision differences in distribution sampling operations and their gradients.

## Reproducer

For each affected test case, run individually:

```bash
source ~/.bashrc && cd third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu && python -m pytest -sxv test_distributions_xpu.py -k "<test_name>"
```

## Representative Error

```
=================================== FAILURES ===================================
_____________________ TestDistributionsXPU.test_cauchy_xpu _____________________
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/lib/python3.12/unittest/case.py", line 58, in testPartExecutor
    yield
  File "/usr/lib/python3.12/unittest/case.py", line 634, in run
    self._callTestMethod(testMethod)
  File "/usr/lib/python3.12/unittest/case.py", line 589, in _callTestMethod
    if method() is not None:
  File "/home/gta/Projects/pytorch/torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py", line 3591, in wrapper
    method(*args, **kwargs)
  File "/home/gta/Projects/pytorch/torch/testing/_internal/common_device_type.py", line 551, in instantiated_test
    result = test(self, **param_kwargs)
  File "/home/gta/Projects/pytorch/torch/testing/_internal/common_device_type.py", line 1637, in efail_fn
    return fn(slf, *args, **kwargs)
  File "/home/gta/Projects/pytorch/torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py", line 2753, in wrapper
    return fn(test_self, *args, **kwargs)
  File "test/distributions/test_distributions.py", line 2363, in test_cauchy
    self.assertEqual(scale.grad, eps)
  File "/home/gta/Projects/pytorch/torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py", line 4609, in assertEqual
    raise error_metas.pop()[0].to_error(
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!

Mismatched elements: 25 / 25 (100.0%)
Greatest absolute difference: 64.50811796602322 at index (3, 4) (up to 1e-07 allowed)
Greatest relative difference: 33.2504545757245 at index (3, 4) (up to 1e-07 allowed)
```

<!-- agent:routing-decision -->
## Routing: patch-proposal only (target = pytorch upstream)

Following the [dashboard batch]([地址已移除：CuiYifeng/torch-xpu-ops-sandbox#120]) for this issue: review verdict was approval, but the target repo is `pytorch` upstream. Per the routing rules, no PR is opened here for pytorch upstream fixes; the verified diff stays as a patch-proposal for a human to shepherd upstream.

### Fix target

`test/distributions/test_distributions.py` — device-aware RNG-replay: introduce `_default_device_rng_module` / `_get_rng_state` / `_set_rng_state` helpers so `rsample()` gradcheck tests correctly save/restore the accelerator generator when the suite runs under `set_default_device(xpu)`. `torch.{get,set}_rng_state` only touch the CPU generator, so the reference `eps` and the actual sample diverge and gradients look wrong.

### Verified

`torch==2.14.0.dev20260725+xpu` (PVC) — 3 tests PASS: `test_cauchy_xpu`, `test_exponential_xpu`, `test_halfcauchy_xpu`.

The remaining 6 distribution numerics tests on this issue (chi2/studentT/generalized_pareto/wishart/multivariate_normal/logisticnormal) are `NEEDS_HUMAN` — genuine XPU RNG/statistics gap, not fixable via seed/tolerance workarounds.

Full patch diff and reproducer command: CuiYifeng/torch-xpu-ops-sandbox#42 (`<!-- agent:state -->` comment).

Mirror sandbox tracking: CuiYifeng/torch-xpu-ops-sandbox#42.

*Automated by issue-handler.*

I was able to reproduce with Conda and got Claude to do an analysis to distill the results and cover different cases. Thanks @bjarzemb !

<details>
<summary>Click here to expand AI analysis</summary>

# Claude Analysis

## Symptom

`TestProfiler::test_kineto_profiler_with_environment_variable` fails with
`AssertionError: Kineto is not working properly with the Dynolog environment variable`.

The test only runs a child Python process and checks its exit code. The real problem
is that **after profiling with `ProfilerActivity.XPU`, Python sometimes crashes during
process exit** (`0xC0000005`, access violation). The script itself has already finished.

## Tested on

| | |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 11 Pro 10.0.28000 |
| GPU | Intel Arc 130V (Lunar Lake), driver 32.0.101.9150 |
| Python | 3.14.8, conda-forge (miniforge) |
| torch | 2.16.0.dev20261021+xpu (nightly) |
| intel-pti | 1.1.0 and 1.2.0 (both crash) |
| oneAPI runtime | intel-sycl-rt 2026.1.2 |

## Steps

**1. Environment**

```powershell
conda create -n repro4063 python=3.14 -y
conda activate repro4063
python -m pip install --pre torch --index-url [地址已移除]
python -m pip install intel-pti==1.2.0   # optional: latest PTI (nightly pins 1.1.0)
```

**2. Save as `repro_4063.py`**

```python
import torch
from torch.profiler import profile, ProfilerActivity

x = torch.ones(1, device="xpu")
with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.XPU]):
    x + x
    torch.xpu.synchronize()
print("SCRIPT_DONE", flush=True)
```

**3. Run it in a loop (the crash is intermittent)**


```powershell
foreach ($i in 1..20) { python repro_4063.py 2>&1 | Out-Null; "run ${i}: 0x{0:X8}" -f $LASTEXITCODE }
```

**Expected:** every run prints `SCRIPT_DONE`, but some runs end with
`0xC0000005` instead of `0x00000000`. That was 3-5 out of 20 runs here.

## Repro through the actual unit test

From a torch-xpu-ops checkout:

```powershell
python -m pip install pytest pytest-timeout expecttest hypothesis psutil pyyaml
cd test\xpu
$env:PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW = "1"
foreach ($i in 1..10) { pytest -q profiler/test_profiler_xpu.py -k test_kineto_profiler_with_environment_variable }
```

## Results

| torch | intel-pti | UT failed | `repro_4063.py` crashed | UT child script crashed |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2.14.1+xpu (oneAPI rt 2026.1.0) | 1.0.1 | 0/2 | not run | 0/10 |
| nightly 2.16.0.dev20261021 | 1.0.1 | 0/1 | not run | 8/10 |
| nightly | 1.1.0 (nightly's pin) | 7/10 | 5/20 | 5/10 |
| nightly | 1.2.0 (latest) | 7/10 | 3/20 | 6/10 |

The "child script" is the test's inline script, run directly with
`KINETO_USE_DAEMON=1` and `KINETO_DAEMON_INIT_DELAY_S=1`.

## Notes

- The crash needs XPU activities. Over 10 runs each, CPU-only profiling and no
  profiler at all never crashed.
- The `KINETO_*` env vars are **not** needed; `repro_4063.py` crashes without them.
  The test needs `KINETO_USE_DAEMON` only for its step-count check.
- Changing the PTI version (1.0.1 / 1.1.0 / 1.2.0) makes no difference on nightly.
- torch 2.14.1 did not crash, but going to nightly also moved the oneAPI runtime
  from 2026.1.0 to 2026.1.2. It is not yet known which of the two causes it.
- The original report (B580, Python 3.12) shows exit code `0xC0000409`
  (`3221226505`) instead of `0xC0000005`. The test and the symptom are the same.
</details>

nodes.body:
I think I found a workaround

Setting PTI_COLLECTION_MODE=2 

```powershell
$env:PTI_COLLECTION_MODE = "2"
```

@bjarzemb . My suspicion - Triton import is automatically bringing in PTI_COLLECTION_MODE=0, when this is set, tracing is never disabled and a callback comes in after the tracing layer is unloaded.

`PTI_COLLECTION_MODE=0` is automatically a bug and we're already in talks with Triton team to remove this. Whether this should crash the program - I am not sure. The tracing layer or the runtime probably shouldn't be called during dll unload time. 

Here is the PR it was introduced: [地址已移除：intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton#7670] . I fixed an issue today actually which caused this to be merged (the env set), so hopefully this can be fixed soon.

nodes.body:
One more thing, given a callback from L0 is being done on dll unload - this means the PyTorch XPU runtime is likely calling L0 on dll unload through SYCL. 

@bjarzemb @tsocha @kdrozd-dev we might want to submit an issue for PyTorch XPU to prevent doing real work on dll unload time.

nodes.body:
There is a difference in execution path between Linux and Windows. On Linux get_sharing_strategy()='file_descriptor' but on Windows this is get_sharing_strategy()='file_system' and execution goes through condition that fails on xpu.
`torch/multiprocessing/__init__.py:`
```python
if sys.platform == "darwin" or sys.platform == "win32":
    _sharing_strategy = "file_system"
else:
    _sharing_strategy = "file_descriptor"
```

Also I observe that cuda runs through different path so maybe xpu also should execute differently.

issues.title: [upstream_ut] test_max_reads_limits_fusion (OverFusionTest) precision failure on PVC due to sdpa flash attention sycltla
issues.body:
## Summary

`OverFusionTest.test_max_reads_limits_fusion` in `test/inductor/test_mix_order_reduction.py` fails on Intel PVC (Data Center GPU Max 1100) due to a precision issue in the SYCL Flash Attention backward path with wheels building upon LTS driver.

**The root cause is that SYCLTLA on PVC with LTS driver does not currently guarantee precision/numerical determinism.** This means the gradient accumulation in the XPU Flash Attention backward kernel can produce results that vary beyond the test tolerance (`tol=5e-2`).

When oneDNN adds training (backward) support for this attention pattern on PVC, the dispatch will go through oneDNN instead of the current SYCL TLA path, which is expected to resolve the precision issue.

## Root Cause Confirmed via Ablation

The SDPA backward path is confirmed as the root cause by ablation: **replacing `F.scaled_dot_product_attention` with `sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.MATH)` makes the test pass**, even in the CI Docker environment (Ubuntu 24.04 Noble) with CI build wheels (MKL 2024.2). All other kernels in the backward pass (RMSNorm backward, MLP backward, mix_order_reduction triton kernels) remain unchanged in the ablation.

| Test | Backend | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `OverFusionTest.test_max_reads_limits_fusion` | OVERRIDEABLE (XPU Flash / SYCL TLA) | **FAIL** |
| `OverFusionSdpaAblationTest.test_max_reads_limits_fusion_sdpa_math` | MATH (no SYCL TLA) | **PASS** |

This isolates the precision failure exclusively to `_scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable_xpu` backward (SYCL TLA on PVC build upon LTS driver).

The ablation test code (not in upstream pytorch, for local reproduction only):

```python
class OverFusionSdpaAblationTest(TestBase):
    @inductor_config.patch(
        {
            "triton.mix_order_reduction": True,
            "triton.mix_order_reduction_max_reads": 10,
            "force_disable_caches": True,
        }
    )
    def test_max_reads_limits_fusion_sdpa_math(self):
        if not HAS_GPU:
            self.skipTest("requires GPU")

        from torch.nn.attention import sdpa_kernel, SDPBackend

        num_heads = 8
        num_kv_heads = 4
        dim = 512
        head_dim = dim // num_heads

        class Attention(nn.Module):
            def __init__(self):
                super().__init__()
                self.c_q = nn.Linear(dim, dim, bias=False)
                self.c_k = nn.Linear(dim, num_kv_heads * head_dim, bias=False)
                self.c_v = nn.Linear(dim, num_kv_heads * head_dim, bias=False)
                self.proj = nn.Linear(dim, dim, bias=False)

            def forward(self, x):
                B, T, D = x.shape
                q = self.c_q(x).reshape(B, T, num_heads, head_dim)
                k = self.c_k(x).reshape(B, T, num_kv_heads, head_dim)
                v = self.c_v(x).reshape(B, T, num_kv_heads, head_dim)
                q = F.rms_norm(q, (q.size(-1),))
                k = F.rms_norm(k, (k.size(-1),))
                q = q.transpose(1, 2)
                k = k.transpose(1, 2).repeat_interleave(num_heads // num_kv_heads, dim=1)
                v = v.transpose(1, 2).repeat_interleave(num_heads // num_kv_heads, dim=1)
                # Force MATH backend to bypass XPU Flash Attention (OVERRIDEABLE / SYCL TLA)
                with sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.MATH):
                    y = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True)
                return self.proj(y.transpose(1, 2).reshape(B, T, D))

        class Block(nn.Module):
            def __init__(self):
                super().__init__()
                self.attn_norm = nn.RMSNorm(dim)
                self.mlp_norm = nn.RMSNorm(dim)
                self.attn = Attention()
                self.fc1 = nn.Linear(dim, dim * 4, bias=False)
                self.fc2 = nn.Linear(dim * 4, dim, bias=False)

            def forward(self, x):
                x = x + self.attn(self.attn_norm(x))
                h = self.mlp_norm(x)
                x = x + self.fc2(F.leaky_relu(self.fc1(h), negative_slope=0.5).square())
                return x

        model = nn.Sequential(*[Block() for _ in range(3)]).to(GPU_TYPE).bfloat16()
        x = torch.randn(8, 2048, dim, device=GPU_TYPE, dtype=torch.bfloat16, requires_grad=True)
        dy = torch.randn_like(x)

        out_ref = model(x)
        out_ref.backward(dy)
        grad_ref = x.grad.clone()
        x.grad = None

        compiled = torch.compile(model, dynamic=False, fullgraph=True)
        out_act = compiled(x)
        out_act.backward(dy)
        grad_act = x.grad.clone()

        self.assertTrue(same(grad_ref, grad_act, tol=5e-2))
```

## Reproducibility: CD rolling driver vs LTS2 driver (CI)

The failure is **build-environment-dependent**:

| Build environment | Result |
|---|---|
| Ubuntu 22.04 LTS (local pt_nightly wheel, `manylinux_2_28`, MKL 2026.0) | **PASS** |
| Ubuntu 24.04 LTS2 (CI wheel `linux-noble`, MKL 2024.2, Python 3.10) | **FAIL** |

The CI wheel is built on Ubuntu 24.04 Noble (`linux-noble-xpu-n-py3.10`, tag `linux_x86_64`, not manylinux). The locally-verified passing build uses `manylinux_2_28_x86_64` with a newer MKL runtime (2026.0 vs 2024.2). The oneDNN version and git hash are identical (`v3.12.0 / 80afa710`) between both builds.

The difference in MKL runtime version likely affects the SYCL TLA kernel code path on PVC, resulting in different gradient accumulation precision between the two builds.

## Background

The test exercises a **training** workload (forward + backward + grad check) using:
- GQA attention (num_heads=8, num_kv_heads=4) with QK-norm
- `F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True)` in bfloat16
- `torch.compile` with `mix_order_reduction=True`, `mix_order_reduction_max_reads=10`
- Assertion: compiled grad matches eager grad within `tol=5e-2`

On XPU (PVC), `F.scaled_dot_product_attention` dispatches via the `OVERRIDEABLE` backend (SDPBackend=4) through the following chain:

```
F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True)   # Python entry
  -> _fused_sdp_choice() = 4 (OVERRIDEABLE)               # backend selection
  -> aten._scaled_dot_product_flash_attention.default      # AOT post_grad graph
  -> Inductor extern kernel (pass-through, no triton)
  -> aten._scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable # XPU dispatch
  -> _scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable_xpu  # mkldnn/xpu/Attention.cpp
```

The precision gap appears in the backward pass where TLA-based gradient accumulation is used. Since **SYCL TLA on PVC does not currently guarantee reproducible precision**, the grad values computed by the compiled path can exceed the `tol=5e-2` threshold when compared to the eager reference.

## oneDNN training support (expected fix path)

Currently the XPU Flash Attention backward on PVC goes through a SYCL TLA kernel path that does not guarantee precision. Once **oneDNN adds training (backward) support** for this attention pattern on PVC, the dispatch will route through oneDNN instead of the SYCL TLA path. This is the expected resolution path — at that point the precision should meet the `tol=5e-2` requirement and this test can be re-enabled on XPU.

## Build environments compared

| Item | LTS (PASS) | LTS2 / CI (FAIL) |
|---|---|---|
| PyTorch version | `2.14.0.dev20260620+xpu` | `2.14.0a0+git02fc2d3` |
| PyTorch commit | `7f2583984d` | `02fc2d3511` |
| Wheel platform tag | `manylinux_2_28_x86_64` | `linux_x86_64` (noble) |
| Build OS | Ubuntu 22.04 LTS | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS2 (Noble) |
| MKL version | 2026.0 (Build 20260401) | 2024.2 (Build 20240605) |
| oneDNN version | v3.12.0 / `80afa710` | v3.12.0 / `80afa710` |
| SYCL compiler | 20260000 | 20260000 |
| GCC | 13.3 | 13.3 |
| Python | 3.12 | 3.10 |

## Upstream tracking

This test was disabled in upstream PyTorch CI via:
- Disable issue: [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#181699]

A follow-up PyTorch PR adds an explicit `@skipIfXpu` annotation referencing this issue (intel/torch-xpu-ops#4094), and will close the disable issue once the XPU-side precision is resolved:
- PR: [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#187822]

## Expected resolution

Once oneDNN supports the training (backward) path for this Flash Attention pattern on PVC, the dispatch will bypass the SYCL TLA kernel and the precision issue will be resolved. At that point:
1. Remove the `@skipIfXpu` annotation from the test in upstream PyTorch
2. Close this issue and pytorch/pytorch#181699
