issues.title: [PyTorch CI] TestSDPAGpuOnlyXPU.test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy_type_dense_fused_kernel0_xpu fails: Tensor-likes are not close
issues.body:
## Description

`test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy_type_dense_fused_kernel0_xpu` (`TestSDPAGpuOnlyXPU`, `test/test_transformers.py`) fails on XPU with a large accuracy mismatch when running the FLASH_ATTENTION fused kernel (`fused_kernel0` == `SDPBackend.FLASH_ATTENTION`) against the MATH reference backend, for the `dense` (non-nested) input case.

```
AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!

Mismatched elements: 32655 / 32768 (99.7%)
Greatest absolute difference: 2.993957042694092 at index (12, 1, 0, 15) (up to 0.007 allowed)
Greatest relative difference: 1.0007356405258179 at index (5, 1, 1, 4) (up to 0.007 allowed)
```

## Root cause / context

This test cell is running on XPU **for the first time** as of pytorch/pytorch#185115 ("[Test] Enable `TestSDPAGpuOnly` on XPU and skip cases unsupported by torch-xpu-ops"), which renamed `TestSDPACudaOnly` -> `TestSDPAGpuOnly` and instantiated it on XPU via `instantiate_device_type_tests`.

That PR already narrowed the `type` parametrize to `["dense"]` only on XPU (skipping `nested`, tracked at #3132), but it did **not** add a skip for the `dense` + `FLASH_ATTENTION` combination, so this cell now runs unguarded and fails with a near-100% element mismatch — i.e. XPU's flash attention fused kernel is producing numerically incorrect output for this dense packed-QKV case, not just failing tolerance by a small margin.

PR #185115's own DrCI AI verdict on the XPU CI failure confirms this analysis:

> "This causes `test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy` with `type="dense"` and `fused_kernel=FLASH_ATTENTION` to run on XPU for the first time. The test fails because XPU's flash attention kernel produces inaccurate results for this case, which was not skipped by the PR."

No existing tracking issue was found in `intel/torch-xpu-ops` for this specific dense+FLASH_ATTENTION accuracy cell (related but distinct issues: #3132 nested-type skip, #3133 nested-contiguity RuntimeError).

## Failing test

```
Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_transformers_xpu.TestSDPAGpuOnlyXPU,test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy_type_dense_fused_kernel0_xpu
```

## Reproduction

```
python test/test_transformers.py TestSDPAGpuOnlyXPU.test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy_type_dense_fused_kernel0_xpu
```

## CI reference

- PR: [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#185115]
- Failing job: [运行记录：pytorch/pytorch@run:29566643723]
- Related: #3132, #3133

## Action items

- [ ] Confirm root cause (XPU flash attention kernel numerical bug vs. missing skip)
- [ ] Add `@skipIfXpu` / in-body skip for `type="dense"` + `fused_kernel=FLASH_ATTENTION` in `test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy` in `pytorch/pytorch` `test/test_transformers.py`, referencing this issue
- [ ] Mirror the skip in `third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/skip_list_common.py`
- [ ] Investigate/fix the underlying XPU flash attention kernel accuracy issue for dense packed QKV inputs

<!-- agent:session -->

Automated fix session for #4401 — [workflow run]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:34078830505]).

<!-- agent:triage -->

## Issue Triage

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Issue type | single-bug |
| Reproduction missing | no |
| Scope | torch-xpu-ops |
| Dependencies | (none named in body) |
| Handling | agent-fixable |

**Carried context:** a maintainer comment on this issue attributes the failure to
the CI machine's PVC LTS2 driver shipping an older IGC with a known accuracy
issue. That is a hypothesis about the *environment*, not the body-declared
scope, so this run does not stop on it — instead Stage 2 reproduces the case on
the current nightly wheel + this runner's driver, which is the empirical test of
that claim.

*Automated by issue-triage.*

<!-- agent:reproduce -->

## Reproduce (stage: nightly)

**Verdict: CANNOT_VERIFY** — blocker: the reported failure is PVC-specific and
this fix runner has no PVC device.

| | |
|---|---|
| Wheel | `torch 2.15.0.dev20260905+xpu` (nightly XPU index) |
| Fix runner GPU | 8x `Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics` (BMG, `0xE211`), driver `26.22.38646.7` |
| Failing CI runner | `dut7900_pvc_card_3`, labels `linux.idc.xpu` (**PVC**) |
| Command run | `pytest -sv --timeout 600 test_transformers_xpu.py::TestSDPACudaOnlyXPU::test_scaled_dot_product_attention_fused_kernels_packed_accuracy_type_dense_fused_kernel0_xpu` |
| Result | **PASSED** in 10.7s |

The exact node id in the issue (`TestSDPAGpuOnlyXPU`) exists only on the
unmerged pytorch PR, so the equivalent cell was run from torch-xpu-ops' own
vendored copy of the file, which carries the identical test body and is not
covered by `skip_list_common.py` for `type=dense` (only the two `nested` cells
are skipped there).

Checks run beyond the single cell, all on BMG:

- The FLASH_ATTENTION backend is genuinely selected (`_fused_sdp_choice` returns
  `1` under `sdpa_kernel([FLASH_ATTENTION])`), so the pass is not a silent
  fallback to MATH.
- 40 random seeds of the exact test shape (`B=16, S=8, H=4, D=64`, fp16, packed
  QKV, strides `(6144, 64, 768, 1)`): **0 failures**, worst absolute deviation
  `0.0074` — i.e. fp16 rounding scale, nothing like the reported `2.99` /
  99.7% mismatch.
- A 144-config sweep over head dims 32/64/96/128/192/256, packed vs unpacked,
  contiguous vs strided, causal vs not: **0 failures in all 72 fp16 configs**.
  (The bf16 half of the sweep exceeds a 7e-3 tolerance, which is expected for
  bf16 against an fp32 MATH reference and is not what this test measures --
  the test only uses fp16.)

<!-- agent:root-cause -->

## Root cause analysis

Not a torch-xpu-ops source-level defect that this run can locate or fix, on
three independent pieces of evidence:

1. **No functional change since the failure.** `git log` over
   `src/ATen/native/transformers/xpu/flash_attn/` shows the last change after
   2026-07-21 to be clang-tidy / modernization work (#4372, #4373, #4827).
   Nothing landed that could have fixed a genuine numerical bug, so the pass on
   BMG today is not "already fixed upstream" -- it is the same kernel source
   behaving correctly.
2. **No PVC-specific code path exists.** The SYCL-TLA FMHA forward kernel is
   architecture-agnostic in source: `kSubgroupSize` is a fixed `16`, the QK/PV
   tile shapes are compile-time constants selected per head dim, and the device
   architecture is consulted only for an allowlist check in
   `sycltla/mha_fwd.cpp` (`intel_gpu_pvc`, `intel_gpu_pvc_vg`,
   `intel_gpu_bmg_g21`, `intel_gpu_bmg_g31`). There is no device-property-driven
   tiling or accumulation-order choice that could diverge between PVC and BMG.

   attributing the failure to the PVC LTS2 driver's older IGC. A near-total

Automated fix session for this issue. Progress in the [workflow run]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659405307]); each stage is appended below as it completes.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | both | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Single affected case: `test/xpu/test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py::TestCudaMultiGPU::test_cuda_memory_leak_detection`. The issue body points the root cause at `torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py` (CUDA-only memory-leak check) while the failing test lives in this repo, so scope is `both` pending source analysis. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Ran against the installed XPU nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261027+xpu` on the BMG runner (8 XPU devices visible). The test is not currently guarded by any skip decorator in this repo, so it runs and fails outright. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_cuda_memory_leak_detection` | REPRODUCED | `AssertionError: CUDA must be available when calling initialize_cuda_context_rng` | Refined command: `cd test/xpu && python -m pytest -sv --timeout 600 test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py::TestCudaMultiGPU::test_cuda_memory_leak_detection` *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at `pytorch@dd50eb629ec`, torch-xpu-ops `main@73a6552c3`. `TestCase.wrap_with_cuda_memory_check` (`torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py:4050`) wraps the test body in `assertLeaksNoCudaTensors` (`:3934`), which constructs `CudaMemoryLeakCheck` (`:3277`). That constructor calls `initialize_cuda_context_rng` (`torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py:448`), which raises `AssertionError('CUDA must be available when calling initialize_cuda_context_rng')` at `:451` whenever `TEST_CUDA` is false. The rest of the class is hardcoded to `torch.cuda` as well -- `device_count` / `memory_allocated` / `mem_get_info` / `empty_cache` at `:3297-3313` and `:3321-3333`, plus `torch._C._cuda_clearCublasWorkspaces()` -- and the leak messages hardcode the string "CUDA" (`:3387`, `:3397`). There is no code path for a non-CUDA accelerator, so the leak check is unusable on XPU. The XPU port `test/xpu/test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py:1133` (added by intel/torch-xpu-ops#4294) substitutes `GPU_TYPE` for the device but keeps upstream's `self.wrap_with_cuda_memory_check`, so on an XPU runner it trips the assert before allocating anything. Upstream's own copy of this test now lives in `test/test_multigpu.py:1390`, inside `TestMultiGPUCudaOnly` which is `@unittest.skipUnless(TEST_CUDA, "CUDA only tests!")` (`:1308-1309`) -- upstream kept it CUDA-only *because* the leak check is CUDA-only, so there is no upstream fix to pick up. Every primitive the check needs already exists for XPU: `torch.get_device_module` (`torch/__init__.py:3468`), `torch.xpu.memory_allocated` (`torch/xpu/memory.py:136`), `torch.xpu.mem_get_info` (`torch/xpu/memory.py:197`), `torch.xpu.empty_cache` (`torch/xpu/memory.py:26`). Measured on this BMG runner, holding a 32 MB tensor moves `torch.xpu.memory_allocated(0)` from 0 to 33554432 and driver in-use bytes from 294707200 to 328261632, and both return to baseline once the tensor is dropped -- so the caching-allocator arm *and* the driver-API arm the class relies on are both observable on XPU. Strategy: resolve the accelerator's device module once in `CudaMemoryLeakCheck.__init__`, route every memory query through it, initialize context/RNG generically (making `common_cuda.initialize_cuda_context_rng` dead, so it goes away with it), keep `torch._C._cuda_clearCublasWorkspaces()` behind a CUDA check since only `torch/csrc/cuda/Module.cpp:2530` binds it and XPU has no equivalent, and label the messages with the accelerator name so CUDA text is unchanged while XPU reports "XPU driver API confirmed ...". The XPU test then needs its expected-message regex made device-aware. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- device-generic test-infra change with every primitive already available - **Target repo:** pytorch (lands first) + torch-xpu-ops (companion) - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch (lands first) + torch-xpu-ops (companion) - **Analyzed at:** `pytorch@dd50eb629ec`, `torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c3` - **What I changed:** `torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py` (+46/-25): `CudaMemoryLeakCheck` resolves the current accelerator's device module once in `__init__` and routes `device_count` / `memory_allocated` / `mem_get_info` / `empty_cache` through it; the one-time context+RNG warm-up is inlined with a class-level guard; `torch._C._cuda_clearCublasWorkspaces()` moves behind a `device_type == "cuda"` check; the two leak messages take the accelerator label. `torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py` (-17): `initialize_cuda_context_rng` and its module flag removed -- the change above left them with no callers. `test/xpu/test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py` (+2/-2): the expected-message regex takes its device label from `GPU_TYPE`. - **Why:** the `AssertionError` came from `common_cuda.py:450-451`, which refuses to run without CUDA, so the leak check had to stop depending on it; every `torch.cuda.*` call in the class body was the second half of the same problem. `torch._C._cuda_clearCublasWorkspaces` stays CUDA-gated because `torch/csrc/cuda/Module.cpp:2530` is the only binding of it and XPU has no equivalent. The message label is derived rather than hardcoded so CUDA output is byte-identical (`cuda`.upper() == `CUDA`) while XPU reports `XPU driver API confirmed ...`; the test's regex is derived from `GPU_TYPE` for the same reason. - **Names kept:** `CudaMemoryLeakCheck`, `assertLeaksNoCudaTensors` and `wrap_with_cuda_memory_check` keep their CUDA-era names. Renaming would touch six unrelated test files and break out-of-tree callers for no functional gain; a comment on the class records that the names are historical. - **Deliberately out of scope:** `wrap_with_cuda_policy` (`common_utils.py:4018`) still gates the `PYTORCH_TEST_CUDA_MEM_LEAK_CHECK` env-var path on `TEST_CUDA`. That flag is only set for CUDA slow-gradcheck builds (`.ci/pytorch/test.sh:258`), so generalizing it would be an unrequested behaviour change for XPU CI. - **Skip added:** no (and none removed -- the test was not skipped in this repo) - **Ready for verify:** yes ```diff @@ class CudaMemoryLeakCheck: +# Checks the current accelerator (CUDA, XPU, ...) for leaks. The "Cuda" in +# this name, in `TestCase.assertLeaksNoCudaTensors` and in +# `TestCase.wrap_with_cuda_memory_check` predates accelerator-agnostic testing +# and is kept for the existing call sites. class CudaMemoryLeakCheck: + # Guards the one-time context & RNG initialization below. + _ctx_rng_initialized = False + def __init__(self, testcase, name=None): self.name = testcase.id() if name is None else name self.testcase = testcase + acc = torch.accelerator.current_accelerator(check_available=True) + if acc is None: + raise AssertionError('an accelerator must be available when checking for memory leaks') + self.device_type = acc.type + self.device_label = self.device_type.upper() + self.device_module = torch.get_device_module(acc) # initialize context & RNG to prevent false positive detections # when the test is the first to initialize those - from torch.testing._internal.common_cuda import initialize_cuda_context_rng - initialize_cuda_context_rng() + if not CudaMemoryLeakCheck._ctx_rng_initialized: + for i in range(self.device_module.device_count()): + torch.randn(1, device=torch.device(self.device_type, i)) + CudaMemoryLeakCheck._ctx_rng_initialized = True + + # cuBLAS workspaces are a CUDA-only allocation that must not be counted as + # a leak; no other accelerator has an equivalent. + def _clear_cublas_workspaces(self): + if self.device_type == "cuda": + torch._C._cuda_clearCublasWorkspaces() @@ __enter__ / __exit__ (every query re-pointed at the resolved module) - num_devices = torch.cuda.device_count() - caching_allocator_mem_allocated = torch.cuda.memory_allocated(i) - torch._C._cuda_clearCublasWorkspaces() - torch.cuda.empty_cache() - bytes_free, bytes_total = torch.cuda.mem_get_info(i) + num_devices = self.device_module.device_count() + caching_allocator_mem_allocated = self.device_module.memory_allocated(i) + self._clear_cublas_workspaces() + self.device_module.empty_cache() + bytes_free, bytes_total = self.device_module.mem_get_info(i) @@ leak messages - msg = ("CUDA caching allocator reports a memory leak not " - f"CUDA driver allocated memory was {self.driver_befores[i]} and is now {driver_mem_allocated}.") - msg = (f"CUDA driver API confirmed a leak in {self.name}! " + msg = (f"{self.device_label} caching allocator reports a memory leak not " + f"{self.device_label} driver allocated memory was {self.driver_befores[i]} and is now {driver_mem_allocated}.") + msg = (f"{self.device_label} driver API confirmed a leak in {self.name}! " --- a/torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py -# Used below in `initialize_cuda_context_rng` to ensure that CUDA context and -# RNG have been initialized. -__cuda_ctx_rng_initialized = False -# after this call, CUDA context and RNG must have been initialized on each GPU -def initialize_cuda_context_rng(): - global __cuda_ctx_rng_initialized - if not TEST_CUDA: - raise AssertionError('CUDA must be available when calling initialize_cuda_context_rng') - if not __cuda_ctx_rng_initialized: - # initialize cuda context and rng for memory tests - for i in range(torch.cuda.device_count()): - torch.randn(1, device=f"cuda:{i}") - __cuda_ctx_rng_initialized = True --- a/test/xpu/test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py - regex = r"CUDA driver API confirmed .+ on device 0.+" + regex = rf"{GPU_TYPE.upper()} driver API confirmed .+ on device 0.+" - RuntimeError, r"CUDA driver API confirmed .+ on device 1.+" + RuntimeError, rf"{GPU_TYPE.upper()} driver API confirmed .+ on device 1.+" ``` A separate-context skip-guard reviewer checked the staged diff and returned APPROVE: no skip-shaped construct is added, and the regex change only parameterizes the device label -- the `driver API confirmed a leak` phrase is still emitted on exactly one path, the `RuntimeError` raised when both the caching-allocator and the driver-API discrepancy are confirmed. *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verify Built PyTorch from source at base `dd50eb629ec` with the fix applied (`torch 2.16.0a0+git6e39481`, `USE_XPU=1`, `TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc`, oneAPI 2026.1.1), with the companion torch-xpu-ops branch pinned via `third_party/xpu.txt`. `torch` resolves to the source tree, not site-packages, so the patched test infrastructure is what runs. | Test case | Before | After | |-----------|--------|-------| | `TestCudaMultiGPU::test_cuda_memory_leak_detection` | FAIL | PASS | `Before` was `AssertionError: CUDA must be available when calling initialize_cuda_context_rng`, recorded against nightly `2.16.0.dev20261027+xpu`. Regression checks on the fixed build: | Suite | Result | |---|---| | `test/xpu/test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py` (whole file) | 3 failed, 3 passed, 55 skipped (was 4 failed, 2 passed, 55 skipped) | | upstream `test/test_multigpu.py` on XPU | 29 passed, 33 skipped | | `test_cuda.py` / `test_linalg.py` / `test_jit.py` / `jit/test_models.py` / `test_torch.py` / `test_multigpu.py` collection | all collect clean (removing `initialize_cuda_context_rng` broke no importer) | | `test_cuda.py -k memory_leak` (CUDA-gated) | 1 skipped, no error | The three remaining failures in the file are pre-existing and unrelated: `test_external_streams` (`torch.xpu` has no `cudart`), `test_mem_get_info`, `test_memory_stats`. They fail identically before and after. On attribution: the usual "before was a wheel, after was a source build" caveat is narrowed here. The unfixed base `dd50eb629ec` still carries the `TEST_CUDA` assert at `torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py:450-451`, and applying *only* this patch to the nightly wheel's own copies of the two files -- changing nothing else -- flipped the test from FAIL to PASS. So the fix, not an intervening upstream change, is what makes it pass. No CUDA device exists on this runner, so the CUDA side was not exercised. It is unchanged by construction: `"cuda".upper()` is `"CUDA"`, so every message is byte-identical, and `_clear_cublas_workspaces()` calls the same binding on CUDA. - **Verdict:** PASSED -- target test green, no new failures in the surrounding suites - **Lint:** clean (`lintrunner -a` on the changed files in both repos; one ruff-format reflow in the XPU test was amended into its commit) *Automated by fix-verify.*
Summary > [!IMPORTANT] > **Two PRs, in this order.** > 1. `pytorch` -- patch dir `fix-issue-4405-pytorch`. Makes the test memory-leak check accelerator-generic. > 2. `torch-xpu-ops` -- patch dir `fix-issue-4405-torch-xpu-ops`, after a nightly carries step 1 (the test asserts on the message step 1 produces). > > **No closing keyword in either PR** (`Fixes` / `Closes` / `Resolves`): merging one would close this issue with the other half still out. Reference the issue plainly; a human closes it once both have landed. **Outcome:** IMPLEMENTING(fix_verified). `TestCase.wrap_with_cuda_memory_check` could not run anywhere but CUDA -- `CudaMemoryLeakCheck.__init__` went through a helper that asserts `TEST_CUDA`, and every memory query in the class called `torch.cuda` directly -- so the XPU port of `test_cuda_memory_leak_detection` died on `AssertionError: CUDA must be available ...` before allocating anything. Root Cause
Analyzed at pytorch@dd50eb629ec, torch-xpu-ops main@73a6552c3.
TestCase.wrap_with_cuda_memory_check (torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py:4050) wraps the test body in assertLeaksNoCudaTensors (:3934), which constructs CudaMemoryLeakCheck (:3277). That constructor calls initialize_cuda_context_rng (torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py:448), which raises AssertionError('CUDA must be available when calling initialize_cuda_context_rng') at :451 whenever TEST_CUDA is false. The rest of the class is hardcoded to torch.cuda as well -- device_count / memory_allocated / mem_get_info / empty_cache at :3297-3313 and :3321-3333, plus torch._C._cuda_clearCublasWorkspaces() -- and the leak messages hardcode the string "CUDA" (:3387, :3397). There is no code path for a non-CUDA accelerator, so the leak check is unusable on XPU.
The XPU port test/xpu/test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py:1133 (added by #4294) substitutes GPU_TYPE for the device but keeps upstream's self.wrap_with_cuda_memory_check, so on an XPU runner it trips the assert before allocating anything. Upstream's own copy of this test now lives in test/test_multigpu.py:1390, inside TestMultiGPUCudaOnly which is @unittest.skipUnless(TEST_CUDA, "CUDA only tests!") (:1308-1309) -- upstream kept it CUDA-only because the leak check is CUDA-only, so there is no upstream fix to pick up.
Every primitive the check needs already exists for XPU: torch.get_device_module (torch/__init__.py:3468), torch.xpu.memory_allocated (torch/xpu/memory.py:136), torch.xpu.mem_get_info (torch/xpu/memory.py:197), torch.xpu.empty_cache (torch/xpu/memory.py:26). Measured on this BMG runner, holding a 32 MB tensor moves torch.xpu.memory_allocated(0) from 0 to 33554432 and driver in-use bytes from 294707200 to 328261632, and both return to baseline once the tensor is dropped -- so the caching-allocator arm and the driver-API arm the class relies on are both observable on XPU. the skill's two branches for that outcome fits. The skip is not a stale XPU

The failure was a bad port, not an XPU defect. #4294 snapshot-copied
upstream's pre-refactor test/test_cuda_multigpu.py into test/xpu/ and applied a
blanket torch.cuda.<x> -> torch.get_device_module(GPU_TYPE).<x> rewrite, which also
hit _get_external_stream -- a helper whose entire job is to allocate a raw
cudaStream_t outside PyTorch via torch.cuda.cudart(), an API that has no torch.xpu
counterpart, and whose tests assert on ExternalStream.cuda_stream, which XPU streams do
not have. The fix moves that helper and both external-stream tests out of the
XPU-executed class into a TestMultiGPUCudaOnly class gated by
@unittest.skipUnless(TEST_CUDA, "CUDA only tests!"), with their bodies reverted to
literal torch.cuda.* -- exactly the classification upstream itself chose in
pytorch/pytorch#197241, the PR that makes this same file device-generic and enables it
on XPU, so a future resync against the renamed upstream test/test_multigpu.py stays
clean. Running the whole file on one nightly wheel against trees differing only by this
file takes it from 4 failures to 3: precisely the reported failure disappears, with no new
failure and no previously-passing case newly skipped.

matches an existing idiom in the file, but it leaves GPU_TYPE-generic bodies in an XPU
class that can never run them and suppresses the bad rewrite instead of undoing it; the
mandatory independent skip-guard review rejected it on those grounds and proposed the
restructure that was adopted. Rewriting the tests around
torch.xpu.get_stream_from_external(torch.xpu.Stream().sycl_queue) would pass on XPU, but
it feeds back a PyTorch-owned queue and so no longer tests the externally-allocated-stream
contract the tests are named for.
Found while verifying, not fixed here: test_cuda_memory_leak_detection in the same
file is also in upstream's CUDA-only class and also fails on XPU from the same mis-rewrite
(AssertionError: CUDA must be available when calling initialize_cuda_context_rng).
test_default_stream and test_tensor_device are in that upstream class too but
currently pass or skip here. Those are outside this issue's scope and want their own
issue; the cleanest long-term move is to resync this snapshot against upstream's renamed
test/test_multigpu.py.

issues.title: [Inductor] Optimize scaled_mm Triton Template
issues.body:
### 🚀 The feature, motivation and pitch

## Summary

This issue tracks ongoing optimizations to the Triton template implementation of `scaled_mm` in PyTorch Inductor.

The current Triton template leaves room for performance improvements on XPU. This tracking issue serves as a central place to organize optimization efforts and link the corresponding PRs.

## Goals
- [x]  Validate Triton kernel correctness
- [ ]  Improve `scaled_mm` kernel performance
    - [x]  Use 2D block prefetch and load for matrix B
    - [x]  Enable SIMD32 code generation. Triton currently generates SIMD16 instructions by default, which limits performance on some workload.
    - [ ] Investigate unexpected MOV instructions between 2D Block Load and DPAS
    - [ ] Investigate unexpected initialization instructions before 2D Block Load

## Planned Optimizations
### Use 2D block prefetch and load for matrix B
1. Created a Triton issue([地址已移除：intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton#7441]) to track the performance issue.
2. Optimized the FP8 tensor-wise scaled_mm Triton template by leveraging tl.make_tensor_descriptor for matrix loading, enabling 2D Block Load and prefetch. The optimization improved the kernel performance for (M=512, N=512, K=256, no bias), reducing execution latency from 70 μs to 30 μs (~57% reduction).

### Enable SIMD32 code generation. Triton currently generates SIMD16 instructions by default, which limits performance on some workload.
Triton currently generates SIMD16 instructions by default. Performance analysis shows that, for the `(M=512, N=512, K=256, no bias)` workload, using TRITON_INTEL_ENABLE_DPAS_FOR_WARP_SIZE_32=1 to generate SIMD32 instructions can improve kernel performance by approximately 20%.

### Investigate unexpected MOV instructions between 2D Block Load and DPAS
1. Created a Triton issue([地址已移除：intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton#7561]) to track the performance issue.

### Investigate unexpected initialization instructions before 2D Block Load
1. Created a Triton issue([地址已移除：intel/intel-xpu-backend-for-triton#7626]) to track the performance issue.

issues.title: [DLE 2026.1 / XPU] `expandable_segments:True` regresses on BMG — `DEVICE_LOST` in xccl collectives (and a matching FSDP2 hang); clean on DLE 2025.3
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Hi,

We hit a reproducible regression on Intel Arc Pro B70 (BMG, 2-GPU, PCIe) that
appears when the PyTorch XPU caching allocator runs in **`expandable_segments`**
mode. It is **new in the DLE 2026.1 runtime** — the identical repro passes on
DLE 2025.3. There are two surface symptoms that we've traced to the same trigger.


Setting `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` (the shared alloc-conf; the
CUDA-named `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF` alias also reaches the XPU allocator) makes
the allocator hand out virtual-memory (VMM/USM) blocks. On DLE 2026.1, downstream
use of those blocks fails:

1. **Collective path → crash.** A 256 MiB `all_reduce` (the log prints `268MB`
   decimal) on such a buffer dies at the next `torch.xpu.synchronize()` with
   `RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 20 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST)`.
   Minimal (~40-line repro, no model/FSDP).
2. **Local FSDP2 path → hang.** A real 2-GPU FSDP2 step-1 forward hangs (no
   collective involved) at a single-scalar device→host copy
   (`_can_skip_causal_mask_xpu` → `.item()` → `appendUSMMemcpy`, L0-v2 adapter).
   Both ranks ~97% CPU, no error.

Same trigger, same fix (don't set `expandable_segments` on XPU). Flipping only that
one env var flips each case between pass and fail.

Same box, same GPU kernel driver (26.22.38646) throughout; only the DLE runtime set
differs. Full `collect_env` for both stacks is in the repo.

| torch | oneCCL | DLE | `expandable_segments:True` + 256 MiB `all_reduce` |
|---|---|---|---|
| 2.13.0+xpu (stable) | 2022.0 | 2026.1 | ❌ DEVICE_LOST |
| 2.14 nightly | 2022.0 | 2026.1 | ❌ DEVICE_LOST |
| **2.13 nightly** | **2021.17** | **2025.3** | ✅ SURVIVED  ← torch held at 2.13, only runtime changed |
| 2.12.0+xpu | 2021.17 | 2025.3 | ✅ SURVIVED |

## Ask

On DLE 2026.1, could you look at how the oneCCL / L0-v2 collective path handles
buffers from the `expandable_segments` (VMM/USM) allocator? Specifically:
- the collective that crashes at `torch.xpu.synchronize()` with `DEVICE_LOST`, and
- the immediate-in-order-queue `appendUSMMemcpy` that hangs when FSDP2 work is
  pending (details + gdb/py-spy stacks in the scalar-copy-hang folder).

[repro.py]([地址已移除])

### log
for the detail log, can pm me. Because put in internal repository. But sent to panas for the log

## extra information on non docker image or proper setup steps.
--
the current native machine.

Both installed as plain pip wheels into isolated venvs. Both pull the same runtime on their own: oneCCL 2022.0 + intel-sycl-rt 2026 (libsycl.so.9), xpu_build=20260000. No DLE image anywhere.

Stack (native pip, no DLE)	EXPANDABLE=1	EXPANDABLE=0

torch 2.13.0+xpu (stable)	❌ DEVICE_LOST at synchronize() (catchable RuntimeError)	✅ SURVIVED (val=2.0)

torch 2.14.0.dev20260722+xpu (nightly)	❌ SIGABRT — oneCCL send_entry.hpp:109 SEND failed / OFI Bad address(14)	✅ SURVIVED (val=2.0)

Both flip deterministically on the one env var. So yes — the bug reproduces natively, with the public wheel, on both torch versions. No DLE required.

--

Adding fresh repro data from PyTorch 2.14 XPU nightly. These tests passed with PyTorch 2.13, but crash during collection with 2.14 before any test body runs.

## Environment

- Container: `intelgpu/ubuntu-26.04-rolling:26.18`
- Python: 3.10.20
- PyTorch target: `torch==2.14.0.dev20260805+xpu`
- torchvision target: `torchvision==0.29.0.dev20260806+xpu`
- torchaudio target: `torchaudio==2.11.0.dev20260806+xpu`
- Triton XPU target: `triton-xpu==3.8.0+git1e2d42a0`
- Baseline: PyTorch 2.13 XPU, same tests passed

## Additional affected tests observed

```text
pytest -v test/xpu/export/test_export_training_ir_to_run_decomp_xpu.py
pytest test/xpu/quantization/core/test_workflow_module_xpu.py
pytest test/xpu/quantization/core/test_quantized_op_xpu.py
pytest test/xpu/quantization/core/test_quantized_tensor_xpu.py
```

All four fail during collection with:

```text
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'functorch.experimental'
```

Representative stacks:

```text
test/xpu/export/test_export_training_ir_to_run_decomp_xpu.py:30: in <module>
    from export import test_export, testing
../../test/export/test_export.py:31: in <module>
    from functorch.experimental.control_flow import cond, map
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'functorch.experimental'
```

```text
test/xpu/quantization/core/test_workflow_module_xpu.py:28: in <module>
    from test_workflow_module import (
../../test/quantization/core/test_workflow_module.py:48: in <module>
    from torch.testing._internal.common_quantization import (
.../site-packages/torch/testing/_internal/common_quantization.py:14: in <module>
    from functorch.experimental import control_flow
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'functorch.experimental'
```

```text
test/xpu/quantization/core/test_quantized_op_xpu.py:28: in <module>
    from test_quantized_op import TestQuantizedOps
../../test/quantization/core/test_quantized_op.py:39: in <module>
    from torch.testing._internal.common_quantization import (
.../site-packages/torch/testing/_internal/common_quantization.py:14: in <module>
    from functorch.experimental import control_flow
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'functorch.experimental'
```

```text
test/xpu/quantization/core/test_quantized_tensor_xpu.py:33: in <module>
    from test_quantized_tensor import TestQuantizedTensor
../../test/quantization/core/test_quantized_tensor.py:17: in <module>
    from torch.testing._internal.common_quantization import get_supported_device_types
.../site-packages/torch/testing/_internal/common_quantization.py:14: in <module>
    from functorch.experimental import control_flow
E   ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'functorch.experimental'
```

## Light analysis

This looks like an API/package compatibility regression between the 2.14 wheel and tests/helpers being imported:

1. The XPU wrapper tests import upstream PyTorch test modules, for example `test/export/test_export.py` and `test/quantization/core/test_*.py`.
2. Those upstream modules or packaged internal helpers still import `functorch.experimental`, especially `functorch.experimental.control_flow`.
3. In the observed PyTorch 2.14 XPU environment, the `functorch.experimental` namespace is not available, so pytest fails during collection.
4. The quantization failures route through `torch.testing._internal.common_quantization` from the installed PyTorch package, so this is not only a torch-xpu-ops wrapper issue. The installed 2.14 package itself still contains an internal helper that imports the missing namespace.
5. A nearby unrelated XPU op test still passes, which points to an import/API compatibility issue rather than a general XPU runtime failure.

Possible fix direction: restore/ship the `functorch.experimental` compatibility namespace in the 2.14 XPU package, or update the affected upstream test/helper imports to the current replacement API and sync the XPU wrapper tests.

Automated fix session for this issue. Stage reports are appended below as the pipeline advances.

<!-- agent:triage -->

## Issue Triage

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Reproduction missing | no |
| Scope | torch-xpu-ops |
| Dependencies | (none) |
| Handling | agent-fixable |

*Automated by issue-triage.*

<!-- agent:root-cause -->

## Root-cause Analysis

- **Issue type:** core framework bug (pytorch test infra)
- **Fix repo:** pytorch
- **Analyzed at:** pytorch@ded21956
- **Root cause:** `TestFX.setUp` in pytorch's `test/test_fx.py` flips the
  process-global `torch.fx.proxy.TracerBase.check_mutable_operations` to `True`
  (`test/test_fx.py:271-276`) and restores it only in `tearDown`
  (`test/test_fx.py:282-286`); it then calls
  `torch.ops.load_library(find_library_location("libtorchbind_test.so"))`
  (`test/test_fx.py:278-280`), which raises `OSError` in XPU CI because the
  installed wheel does not ship that test-only library
  (`find_library_location` falls back to a non-existent
  `torch/build/lib/libtorchbind_test.so`). unittest does not run `tearDown`
  when `setUp` raised, so the flag stays `True` for the remainder of that
  xdist worker process. The next `TestCommonPass` mutation case in the same
  module (`test/xpu/test_fx_xpu.py:164` tracing
  `test/fx/test_common_passes.py:51-54`, `y.add_(1)`) then hits the guard at
  `torch/fx/proxy.py:232` and fails with
  `RuntimeError: Tried to trace mutable operation aten::add_.Tensor`.
  Nothing device-specific is involved: in the referenced nightly run all 422
  `TestFX` cases fail with the `libtorchbind_test.so` `OSError`, and all ten
  `TestCommonPass` mutation cases fail — **including the `_cpu` variants**
  (`test_correctness_CSEPass_Mutation_cpu`,
  `test_correctness_factory_CSEPass_MutationFactory_cpu`, ...), which rules out
  any XPU kernel or functionalization gap.
- **Fix strategy:** In pytorch `test/test_fx.py`, move the
  `libtorchbind_test.so` load in `TestFX.setUp` ahead of the
  `check_mutable_operations` save/flip so no statement that can raise executes
  while the global flag is flipped. This matches the ordering the sibling
  classes in the same file already use (`TestOperatorSignatures:5188`,
  `TestFXAPIBackwardCompatibility:5231`, `TestFunctionalTracing:5593`,
  `TestVisionTracing:5872` all set the flag as the last statement of `setUp`).
- **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING — non-exception-safe global-state flip in a
  device-agnostic pytorch test file; one-file, test-only fix.

*Automated by fix-root-cause.*

<!-- agent:implement -->

## Implementation

- **Target repo:** pytorch (`test/test_fx.py`)
- **Changed files:** `test/test_fx.py` (1 file, +8 / -5)
- **Skip-guard review:** APPROVE (no skip / xfail / tolerance-loosening / assertion-deletion constructs added)

```diff

--- a/test/test_fx.py
+++ b/test/test_fx.py
@@ -268,17 +268,20 @@ def _parse_profiler_trace_lines(traces: str) -> list[tuple[str, str, str]]:
 class TestFX(JitTestCase):
     def setUp(self):
         super().setUp()
+        if not (IS_FBCODE or IS_WINDOWS or IS_MACOS):
+            lib_file_path = find_library_location("libtorchbind_test.so")
+            torch.ops.load_library(str(lib_file_path))
+
         # Checking for mutable operations while tracing is feature flagged
-        # Enable it in testing but not by default
+        # Enable it in testing but not by default. check_mutable_operations is
+        # process-global and is only restored in tearDown, which unittest skips
+        # when setUp raises -- so this must stay the last statement of setUp, or
+        # a failure above would leak it into every later test in the process.
         self.orig_tracer_mutable_flag = (
             torch.fx.proxy.TracerBase.check_mutable_operations
         )
         torch.fx.proxy.TracerBase.check_mutable_operations = True
 
-        if not (IS_FBCODE or IS_WINDOWS or IS_MACOS):
-            lib_file_path = find_library_location("libtorchbind_test.so")
-            torch.ops.load_library(str(lib_file_path))
-
     def tearDown(self):
         super().tearDown()
         torch.fx.proxy.TracerBase.check_mutable_operations = (
```

The `load_library` call is the only statement in `setUp` that can raise, so
moving it above the flag flip means a missing `libtorchbind_test.so` can no
longer leave `check_mutable_operations = True` behind for the rest of the
worker process. No behavioural change for the `TestFX` cases themselves.

*Automated by fix-implement.*

<!-- agent:verify -->

## Verify Result

- **Target repo:** pytorch
- **Refined command:** `pytest -q -rf test_fx_xpu.py::TestFX::test_all_input_nodes test_fx_xpu.py::TestCommonPass::test_correctness_factory_CSEPass_MutationFactory_xpu` (run from `test/xpu`)
- **Verdict:** PASSED — all ten `TestCommonPass` mutation cases pass with the poisoning `TestFX` case running first in the same process
- **Lint:** clean (FLAKE8, RUFF, CODESPELL, NEWLINE, SPACES, TABS; PYFMT does not apply — `test/test_fx.py` is in its `exclude_patterns`)
- **Rebuild:** not needed (python-only test-file change; nightly wheel `2.15.0.dev20260905+xpu`)

### Before / after

Same wheel, same checkout, same command — the only difference is the patch, so
this is a true A/B rather than a nightly-vs-source comparison.

| Test case | Before | After |
|-----------|--------|-------|
| `TestCommonPass::test_correctness_factory_CSEPass_MutationFactory_xpu` | FAILED (`RuntimeError: Tried to trace mutable operation aten::add_.Tensor`) | PASSED |
| the other 9 `TestCommonPass` `Mutation*` cases (`_cpu` + `_xpu`) | FAILED (same error) | PASSED |
| `TestFX::test_all_input_nodes` (the poisoning case) | FAILED (`OSError: Could not load this library: .../libtorchbind_test.so`) | FAILED, unchanged — pre-existing and out of scope |

Final run: `1 failed, 10 passed`. The one failure is the untouched
`libtorchbind_test.so` problem in `TestFX` itself.

*Automated by fix-verify.*

<!-- agent:summary -->

## Summary

**Fixed — patch ready for a human to apply.** The fix is one file in **pytorch**,
not torch-xpu-ops.

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| Verdict | PASSED |
| Fix repo | pytorch |
| Branch | `agent/fix-issue-4455` |
| Base | `ded2195678819b22d7855d9b883967176686d5e7` |
| Changed files | `test/test_fx.py` (+8 / -5) |

`TestFX.setUp` flipped the process-global
`torch.fx.proxy.TracerBase.check_mutable_operations` to `True` before doing the
one thing in `setUp` that can fail (loading the test-only
`libtorchbind_test.so`, which the XPU wheel does not ship). Because unittest
skips `tearDown` when `setUp` raises, the flag stayed `True` for the rest of the
xdist worker, and the next `TestCommonPass` mutation test to trace an in-place
op failed. Moving the library load above the flag flip means the flip is the
last statement in `setUp`, so nothing can leak it. The reported failure was
never device-specific; the `_cpu` variants failed the same way.

**Follow-up, not fixed here:** the ~422 `TestFX` `setUp` errors from the wheel
not shipping `libtorchbind_test.so` remain. This change only stops them from
taking the 10 mutation tests down with them. Making `TestFX` itself pass on a
wheel install needs a separate decision (ship the library, or skip those cases
when it is absent) and belongs in its own issue.

*Automated by issue-handler.*

<!-- review: strong-accepted -->
why: root-cause

**Strongly accept.**

Root cause dates back to #64467 (2021): that PR added the mutable-op tracing flag to `TestFX`, but inserted the process-global flag flip *before* the only statement in `setUp` that can throw (loading `libtorchbind_test.so`), with the restore left in `tearDown`. unittest does not run `tearDown` when `setUp` raises, so the flag stays flipped for the rest of the process.

What exposed it: our wheel is built with the upstream release config (`INSTALL_TEST=0`), so it does not ship that `.so` and `setUp` always throws; and `test_fx_xpu.py` puts `TestFX` and `TestCommonPass` in the same module. Those two together surface a hazard that has been there since 2021, showing up as `TestCommonPass`'s `add_` being rejected. Nothing XPU-specific — the `_cpu` variants fail the same way.

Patch looks good. Two follow-ups:

- [ ] **Land the fix upstream.** Opened as pytorch/pytorch#196569. Next: add it to the `apply_torch_pr.py` pr-list so CI picks it up without waiting for the pin to move. Keep this issue open until the fix actually reaches the pytorch used by CI — the case is currently exempted via this issue's `skipped` label feeding `Known_issue.log`, and closing the issue removes that exemption.
- [ ] **Make `TestFX` skip instead of error when the library is missing.** The missing `.so` still takes down all 422 `TestFX` cases at `setUp`, including the three SYCL profiler tests we added in `test_fx_xpu.py`, which have therefore never run. Upstream already landed pytorch/pytorch#193122, which makes `load_torchbind_test_lib()` raise `SkipTest` rather than `OSError`, but `test_fx.py` still calls `find_library_location` + `load_library` directly. Switching it over would turn those 422 errors into honest skips. Two things to settle first: it changes Windows behaviour (`TestFX` currently skips the load entirely on Windows, the helper loads `torchbind_test.dll`), and it would leave our three profiler tests permanently skipped unless we also make the library available in the test job. Worth a separate issue.

issues.title: [xpu-aglinment] Fix NLLLoss2d backward 32-bit offset overflow
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

<!-- agent:status:IN_REVIEW -->

`F.nll_loss(...).backward()` produces a silently wrong gradient on XPU when the
flattened offset reaches 2^31. The XPU SYCL backward kernel still uses 32-bit
`sample`, `toffset`, and `ioffset` values, so the offset wraps around instead of
addressing the full tensor.

This was found during XPU alignment for upstream PyTorch issue
[地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#190139] The upstream CUDA path was
already fixed by selecting a 64-bit index type when 32-bit indexing is unsafe;
the analogous XPU kernel was never updated, so XPU still exhibits the original
overflow.

### Reproducer

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

print("torch", torch.__version__)
print("xpu available", torch.xpu.is_available())

x = torch.zeros((2**16 + 1, 2**15, 1, 1), device="xpu", dtype=torch.float16, requires_grad=True)
target = torch.zeros((2**16 + 1, 1, 1), device="xpu", dtype=torch.long)

F.nll_loss(x, target, reduction="sum").backward()

assert x.grad[0, 0, 0, 0].item() == -1.0
assert x.grad[-1, 0, 0, 0].item() == -1.0
```

### Actual behavior

The first gradient is correct while the final sample gradient is zero, matching
32-bit offset wraparound at `sample * map_nelem * n_classes == 2**31`:

```text
x.grad[0,0,0,0]  = -1.0
x.grad[-1,0,0,0] = 0.0
RESULT: confirmed
```

### Expected behavior

Every valid target position receives its gradient regardless of tensor size,
matching CPU/CUDA eager semantics:

```text
x.grad[0,0,0,0]  = -1.0
x.grad[-1,0,0,0] = -1.0
```

### Alignment metadata

- Upstream source: [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#190139]
- Source type: upstream issue (CUDA fixed; XPU unaligned)
- Local XPU result: confirmed
- Routed area: `intel/torch-xpu-ops`, XPU NLLLoss2d backward kernel offset typing
- Target repository: `intel-sandbox/torch-xpu-ops-exp`

### Notes

The upstream CUDA issue was closed after its kernel selected a 64-bit index type
when 32-bit indexing is unsafe. The XPU fix should independently align the SYCL
implementation with that guard (widen `sample`/`toffset`/`ioffset` to 64-bit when
the flattened extent exceeds `INT_MAX`) rather than modifying shared PyTorch code.

A regression test should be added under `test/repro/` and run with `pytest`.

### Versions

```text
PyTorch version: 2.14.0.dev20260713+xpu
OS: Ubuntu 22.04.5 LTS (x86_64)
Is XPU available: True
Intel GPU: Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100
Relevant path: src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/*Loss*.cpp (NLLLoss2d backward)
```

<!-- agent:fix-log -->
<!-- agent:discovery-log -->
<!-- agent:env-log -->
<!-- agent:upstream-log -->
<!-- agent:verification-log -->

nodes.body:
Automated fix run on this issue. Follow progress in the [workflow run]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659448467]). ### Stage 1 - Triage - **Issue type:** single-bug (one UT case, `MemoryBudgetTest::test_attention_vs_linear`) - The local XPU copy `test/xpu/functorch/test_ac_xpu.py` named in this issue no longer exists on `main`. It was deleted by intel/torch-xpu-ops#5423, which points `skip_list_common.py` at the upstream `functorch/test_ac.py` instead (no per-case skips). - Upstream already guards the case: `test/functorch/test_ac.py` carries `@skipXPUIf(True, ...)` on `test_attention_vs_linear`, referencing this issue. So XPU CI is **green today** - this is a live capability gap behind an existing skip, not an active CI break. ### Stage 2 - Reproduce: REPRODUCED Against the installed nightly wheel (`2.16.0.dev20261027+xpu`) on BMG, with the upstream skip removed: ``` python test/functorch/test_ac.py MemoryBudgetTestDeviceXPU.test_attention_vs_linear_xpu -> AssertionError: Scalars are not close! Expected 2 but got 5.0 ``` Matches the reported failure exactly. ### Stage 3 - Root cause `scaled_dot_product_attention` cannot select any fused backend for this test's inputs (fp32, `head_dim` 512..4608, `requires_grad=True`), so it falls back to the device-agnostic **math composite**: | XPU backend | Why it is rejected | |---|---| | FlashAttentionXPU (SYCL-TLA) | fp32 unsupported (bf16/fp16 only), and `head_dim > 256` | | Overrideable (oneDNN) | accepts fp32 but is forward-only - no `_scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable_backward` XPU dispatch - and caps `head_dim` at 576 | | Mem-efficient | not implemented; `select_sdp_backend_xpu` maps it straight to math | CUDA passes because its mem-efficient kernel supports `kFloat` with no absolute `head_dim` cap, and saves only the q/k/v views, the output and `logsumexp`. Walking the autograd graph at `S=D=1` accounts for all 5.0 MiB. The math path materializes and saves three tensors a fused kernel would not: | Saved tensor | Size | |---|---| | `query * scale` | `S*D` | | `key_expanded.transpose(-2,-1) * scale` | `S*D` | | `softmax(attn)` | `S^2` | | SDPA output (expected) | `S*D` | | `mm` output (expected) | `S*D` | So eager activation memory is `4*S*D + S^2`, not the `2*S*D` the test asserts. That model matched the measured value for **all 7** `(S, D)` pairs in the test (5/13/20/12/44/128/160 MiB). ### Stage 4/5 - Outcome: NEEDS_HUMAN (feature-sized work) No agent-sized fix exists, in either repo: - **Nothing to change in torch-xpu-ops.** Backend selection and the test both live upstream; `skip_list_common.py` already defers to the upstream file and the case is already skipped there. - **Product fix is kernel work.** Making this pass needs a fused XPU attention kernel with fp32 + large `head_dim` + backward (SYCL-TLA FMHA or oneDNN SDPA backward). Feature-sized, not a patch. - **Adjusting the test's expectations does not work either.** I tried the obvious backend-agnostic reformulation - deriving the budget from measured eager memory (`1.2*S*D/eager_mem`, which is identically `0.6` on CUDA, so CUDA behaviour is unchanged). The second assertion (`mem == S*D`) then passes on XPU for all 7 cases, but the third still fails for 4 of 7: under the math decomposition the attention chain carries that extra `S^2` MiB softmax activation, so "recompute attention" is the *only* choice that fits the budget, and the mm-vs-attn arithmetic-intensity comparison that is the whole point of the test becomes unreachable. Any further change would be an upstream redesign owned by `oncall: pt2`. **Recommendation:** keep the existing upstream skip, and keep this issue open as the tracking item for XPU fp32 fused SDPA with backward. The `wontfix` label already on this issue is consistent with that. No patch artifact was produced.
Summary `MemoryBudgetTest::test_attention_vs_linear` fails on XPU because no XPU fused SDPA backend accepts this test's inputs (fp32, head_dim 512..4608, requires_grad), so `scaled_dot_product_attention` falls back to the math composite, which saves three activation tensors a fused kernel would not - making eager activation memory `4*S*D + S^2` MiB instead of the `2*S*D` the test asserts. I confirmed that model against the autograd graph's saved tensors and against all seven `(S, D)` pairs, and confirmed the case is already skipped upstream with a reference to this issue, so XPU CI is green. The verdict is NEEDS_HUMAN: closing the gap needs a fused XPU attention kernel supporting fp32 with backward at large head dims, and the alternative of reworking the test's expectations provably cannot preserve what it checks, since under the math decomposition recomputing attention is the only way to meet any budget. - **Branch:** none - no fix was committed - **Base:** `087ceb5bbaf110c670d587fbfcc37dfd8d9400b5` (pytorch, the nightly wheel's commit) - **Changed files:** none - **Nothing was pushed.** `fix_result.json` records the NEEDS_HUMAN verdict and the analysis; there is no patch to apply.
_Generated by [fix job]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659448467])._
Review Copy into a new comment, keep ONE verdict, add a note. Two verdicts in one comment are dropped as ambiguous. ``` **strong-accepted** **weak-accepted** **weak-rejected** **strong-rejected** **issue-drop** notes: ``` On a batch run add `item=` to say which sub-item the verdict is about, **in the bold text and in the marker** -- the marker is invisible, so the bold line is all a reader sees. One comment per sub-item, since a bare verdict on a batch does not say which test it means and is dropped. `run=` only when judging a run other than the newest, in both places too. A CI DISABLED sub-item, `item=` from the fan-out table: ``` **strong-accepted item=197334** notes: same TensorAssign overload as upstream CUDA, fp8 dispatch list matches ``` Another sub-item of the same batch, judged on an earlier run: ``` **weak-rejected run=35171979678 item=197335** notes: green only because the test is skipped, the kernel still lacks fp8 ``` An `[xpu-alignment]` issue that should not have been filed -- one issue per difference, so no `item=`: ``` **issue-drop** notes: accepted XPU/CUDA numerics difference, nothing to repair ```

issues.title: [XPU] torchrun --numa-binding fails on XPU: _XpuDeviceProperties missing pci_domain_id/pci_bus_id/pci_device_id
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`torch/numa/binding.py` was made device-generic in #185266 (`torch.cuda` ->
`torch.accelerator`), but XPU doesn't satisfy the implicit backend contract, so
`--numa-binding` is unusable on Intel GPUs.

`_get_numa_node_index_for_device_index` (`torch/numa/binding.py:595-604`) reads
three PCI attributes to find the device's NUMA node via sysfs:

```python
domain = device_properties.pci_domain_id
bus    = device_properties.pci_bus_id
device = device_properties.pci_device_id
pci_addr = f"{domain:04x}:{bus:02x}:{device:02x}.0"
with open(f"/sys/bus/pci/devices/{pci_addr}/numa_node") as f: ...
```

CUDA binds them at `torch/csrc/cuda/Module.cpp:1201-1203`. XPU exposes no `pci_*`
attribute at all (full list: `torch/csrc/xpu/Module.cpp:326-360`), and
`grep -rn "pci" torch/csrc/xpu/ torch/xpu/ c10/xpu/` returns zero hits. The data is
missing one layer down too — `AT_FORALL_XPU_EXT_DEVICE_PROPERTIES`
(`c10/xpu/XPUDeviceProp.h:116-139`) never queries a PCI address — so *
need a change**, not just the pybind11 binding.

### Impact

`torchrun --numa-binding=<mode>` **fails to launch** with `AttributeError`:
`torch/distributed/run.py:957-960` doesn't set
`should_fall_back_if_binding_fails`, which defaults to `False`
(`binding.py:95`), so `_handle_exception` re-raises (`binding.py:266`)
fallback enabled it instead runs unbound and loses the locality win. The upstream
default (`numa_options=None`) is unaffected.

### Secondary issue: no test enforces the contract

`test/test_numa_binding.py` passes on XPU but gives no real XPU covera
`torch.get_device_module` to a `MagicMock` returning a hand-rolled
`MockDeviceProperties` that declares the three `pci_*` fields (lines 2
It would pass with no accelerator present. That mocking is right for its purpose
(fabricating 4-socket / 8-NUMA-node topologies no CI runner has), so t
missing test at a different layer. The contract exists only in #185266's
description:

> backends ... must expose `get_device_properties()` returning an obje
> `pci_domain_id`, `pci_bus_id`, and `pci_device_id`

`test/test_xpu.py:131` runs on real hardware but only checks self-consistency and a
few `> 0` assertions, so it misses this too.

### Suggested direction

1. Expose the PCI address on XPU. SYCL appears to offer it as one stri
   (`"0000:4d:00.0"`) not three ints — confirm against the installed
   `sycl/ext/intel/info/device.hpp`, including drivers lacking the ext
   Parsing to ints in the XPU layer keeps `binding.py` single-shaped.
2. Add a real-hardware contract test asserting those attributes exist
   `torch.accelerator.current_accelerator()`'s properties.
   `test/test_accelerator.py:277` is a good template.

HPU and PrivateUse1/OpenReg are likely affected the same way.

### Versions

`main` at f594cadbd10e.

Automated fix session for this issue. Stages are appended below as they complete.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | pytorch | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261027+xpu` on a BMG runner (8 XPU devices visible). Reproducer is a one-liner, not a pytest node id: the issue is a missing attribute, so the failure is in `torch/numa/binding.py`'s device-properties lookup rather than in any test that currently runs on XPU. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `torch.numa.binding._get_numa_node_index_for_device_index(0)` | REPRODUCED | `AttributeError: 'torch._C._XpuDeviceProperties' object has no attribute 'pci_domain_id'` | | `torch.xpu.get_device_properties(0).pci_domain_id` | REPRODUCED | same `AttributeError` | `dir()` on `_XpuDeviceProperties` confirms none of `pci_domain_id` / `pci_bus_id` / `pci_device_id` is present, so every NUMA-binding mode that needs device locality raises before it can read `/sys/bus/pci//numa_node`. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@eb428e0f31a`. `torch/numa/binding.py:602-610` resolves a device's NUMA node by reading three integer PCI fields off the accelerator's device-properties object (`pci_domain_id`, `pci_bus_id`, `pci_device_id`) and formatting them into the sysfs path `"{domain:04x}:{bus:02x}:{device:02x}.0"`. CUDA satisfies that contract at `torch/csrc/cuda/Module.cpp:1239-1241`, which `def_readonly`s the three `cudaDeviceProp` fields. The XPU side never exposes them: `registerXpuDeviceProperties` (`torch/csrc/xpu/Module.cpp:366-400`) binds 27 members and none is PCI-related, and the data is missing one layer down too -- `AT_FORALL_XPU_EXT_DEVICE_PROPERTIES` (`c10/xpu/XPUDeviceProp.h:141-168`) never queries a PCI address, so `c10::xpu::DeviceProp` has no field to bind. The attribute lookup raises `AttributeError` before any sysfs read. This surfaced when `binding.py` was made device-generic in `pytorch/pytorch#185266` (`b6e17f1b31e`), which replaced the `torch.cuda` calls with `torch.accelerator` / `torch.get_device_module` and thereby applied CUDA's implicit device-properties contract to every accelerator. `torch/distributed/run.py` leaves `should_fall_back_if_binding_fails` at its `False` default (`binding.py:95`), so `_handle_exception` re-raises and `torchrun --numa-binding=` fails to launch rather than degrading to unbound. SYCL does provide the data, in a different shape: `sycl::ext::intel::info::device::pci_address` returns a single `std::string` (`sycl/info/ext_intel_device_traits.def:19`), gated by `sycl::aspect::ext_intel_pci_address` (`sycl/info/aspects.def:15`). Verified on this runner -- all 8 devices advertise the aspect and report e.g. `'0000:17:00.0'`, and `/sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:17:00.0/numa_node` reads `0`. The fix parses that string into three integer members on `c10::xpu::DeviceProp` inside the XPU layer and binds them under CUDA's names, so `binding.py` stays single-shaped. The existing `ASSIGN_EXT_DEVICE_PROP` pattern in `c10/xpu/XPUFunctions.cpp:162-165` already establishes aspect-guarded queries with a fallback default, which covers drivers lacking the extension. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- the missing data is reachable through an existing SYCL extension query; the change is confined to the XPU property layer in pytorch. - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Analyzed at:** pytorch@eb428e0f31a - **What I changed:** - `c10/xpu/XPUDeviceProp.h` (+4): one entry in `AT_FORALL_XPU_EXT_DEVICE_PROPERTIES` for `pci_address`, so `DeviceProp` gains a `std::string pci_address` populated by the existing aspect-guarded `ASSIGN_EXT_DEVICE_PROP` machinery (empty when the driver lacks the extension). `c10/xpu/XPUFunctions.cpp` therefore needed no change. - `torch/csrc/xpu/Module.cpp` (+19): a `get_pci_id` helper that splits that string, plus three `def_property_readonly` bindings exposing `pci_domain_id` / `pci_bus_id` / `pci_device_id`, returning `-1` when no address is reported. - `torch/_C/__init__.pyi.in` (+3), `torch/xpu/__init__.py` (+3): the three fields in the `_XpuDeviceProperties` stub and the `get_device_properties` docstring. - `test/test_xpu.py` (+17): `test_device_properties_pci_address`, a real-hardware contract test. - **Why:** `torch/numa/binding.py:602-610` reads these three integer fields through `torch.get_device_module(...).get_device_properties(...)`; CUDA satisfies that at `torch/csrc/cuda/Module.cpp:1239-1241` while XPU bound no PCI field, so the lookup raised `AttributeError`. Parsing SYCL's single `pci_address` string on the XPU side, rather than teaching `binding.py` a second shape, keeps the device-agnostic code single-shaped. - **Skip added:** no - **Ready for verify:** yes Two designs were weighed. Parsing into three `int32_t` members of `c10::xpu::DeviceProp` populated in `XPUFunctions.cpp` reads better semantically, but adding plain member declarations to that macro-only struct body lets clang-format parse the struct and reflow its whole body -- 25 lines of unrelated churn in a file that is clang-format-clean at HEAD. Deriving at the pybind layer touches one C++ file fewer, adds no single-use macro, and matches the existing `gpu_subslice_count` / `architecture` derived properties in the same function. ```diff + /* the PCI address of the device as "domain:bus:slot.function", empty when \ + * the device does not report one. */ \ + _(pci_address, pci_address, std::string()) \ ``` ```diff + auto get_pci_id = [](const DeviceProp& prop, size_t field) { + std::array ids{}; + if (std::sscanf( + prop.pci_address.c_str(), "%x:%x:%x", &ids[0], &ids[1], &ids[2]) != + 3) { + return int64_t{-1}; + } + return static_cast(ids[field]); + }; ... + .def_property_readonly( + "pci_domain_id", + [get_pci_id](const DeviceProp& prop) { return get_pci_id(prop, 0); }) + .def_property_readonly( + "pci_bus_id", + [get_pci_id](const DeviceProp& prop) { return get_pci_id(prop, 1); }) + .def_property_readonly( + "pci_device_id", + [get_pci_id](const DeviceProp& prop) { return get_pci_id(prop, 2); }) ``` ```diff + def test_device_properties_pci_address(self): + # torch/numa/binding.py reaches the properties through + # torch.get_device_module() and formats these three fields into a sysfs + # path, so exercise the contract through the same indirection. + device_module = torch.get_device_module(torch.accelerator.current_accelerator()) + props = device_module.get_device_properties(0) + self.assertGreaterEqual(props.pci_domain_id, 0) + self.assertGreaterEqual(props.pci_bus_id, 0) + self.assertGreaterEqual(props.pci_device_id, 0) + if IS_LINUX: + pci_addr = f"{props.pci_domain_id:04x}:{props.pci_bus_id:02x}:{props.pci_device_id:02x}.0" + self.assertTrue(os.path.isdir(f"/sys/bus/pci/devices/{pci_addr}")) + self.assertGreaterEqual( + _get_numa_node_index_for_device_index(device_index=0), 0 + ) ``` *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verify Source build `06b5a40e5e7` (base `eb428e0f31a` plus the fix), `USE_XPU=1`, `TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc`, editable install; `torch` resolves to the source tree, not site-packages. | Test case | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `torch.numa.binding._get_numa_node_index_for_device_index(0)` | FAIL | PASS (returns `0`) | | `TestXpu::test_device_properties_pci_address` | n/a (new test) | PASS | | `torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 --numa-binding=node` | FAIL | PASS | `Before` was `AttributeError: 'torch._C._XpuDeviceProperties' object has no attribute 'pci_domain_id'`. **The fix is what makes it pass, not an unrelated upstream change.** `git grep -i pci` at the base commit returns zero hits across `torch/csrc/xpu/`, `torch/xpu/` and `c10/xpu/`, so the attributes cannot exist without this commit. That closes the usual nightly-before / source-after ambiguity with a measurement. **End-to-end, the reported impact is gone.** `torchrun --numa-binding=node` with 8 ranks now launches, and the affinity is correct rather than merely non-crashing: the measured PCI-to-NUMA map puts devices 0-3 on node 0 and 4-7 on node 1, and ranks 0-3 land on node 0's CPUs (`first_cpu=0`) with ranks 4-7 on node 1's (`first_cpu=128`), agreeing with `numactl --hardware`. (`numactl` had to be installed in this container first -- without it binding stops one step later on `RuntimeError: numactl CLI is required for NUMA binding`, which is environmental.) Regression checks on the fixed build: | Suite | Result | |---|---| | `test_xpu.py -k "pci_address or get_device_properties or get_device_capability"` | 3 passed | | `test_numa_binding.py` (device-generic, mocked) | 21 passed | | `test_xpu.py` (full) | 196 passed, 6 skipped, 3 xfailed, 3 failed | The three failures are pre-existing, each established by measurement rather than assumption: `test_sleep` and `test_cached_zes_device_infos` fail with identical messages on the unmodified nightly wheel in an isolated venv, and `test_xpu_header_installed` checks `torch/include/ATen/`, which an editable install never populates (the headers are present and correct under `build/install/`). None references `pci`. - **Verdict:** PASSED -- the reproducer, the new contract test, and the end-to-end `torchrun` path all pass, with correct NUMA locality. - **Lint:** clean. `lintrunner --revision HEAD~1 --skip CLANGTIDY` reports `ok No lint issues`. CLANGTIDY flags 5 errors in `torch/csrc/xpu/Module.cpp`, all pre-existing -- reproduced identically against the base version of the same file, and none on an added line. *Automated by fix-verify.*
Summary **Outcome:** IMPLEMENTING(fix_verified) One bug: `torch/numa/binding.py` became device-generic in `pytorch/pytorch#185266` and thereby applied CUDA's device-properties contract -- `pci_domain_id`, `pci_bus_id`, `pci_device_id` -- to every accelerator, but the XPU property layer exposed no PCI data at any level, so the lookup raised `AttributeError` and `torchrun --numa-binding` failed to launch on Intel GPUs. The fix queries SYCL's `pci_address` string into `c10::xpu::DeviceProp` through the existing aspect-guarded macro and splits it into the three integers at the pybind layer, so the device-agnostic code stays single-shaped and a driver without the extension yields `-1` rather than throwing. Verification was end to end: the reproducer returns a node index, a new real-hardware contract test passes, and 8-rank `torchrun --numa-binding=node` binds ranks 0-3 to NUMA node 0 and 4-7 to node 1 -- correct locality, matching `numactl --hardware`, not just the absence of a crash. - **Branch:** `agent/fix-issue-4732` (in the **pytorch** checkout) - **Base:** `eb428e0f31a0dafc2cce417af9dcc09aa15fd16b` - **Changed files:** `c10/xpu/XPUDeviceProp.h`, `torch/csrc/xpu/Module.cpp`, `torch/_C/__init__.pyi.in`, `torch/xpu/__init__.py`, `test/test_xpu.py` - **Nothing was pushed.** The patch is exported as a workflow artifact for a human to review and apply. Two things for whoever picks this up: 1. **The PR goes to `pytorch/pytorch`, not this repo.** The bug is filed here but the root cause is entirely in pytorch's XPU property layer, so no torch-xpu-ops change is needed. Use no closing keyword (`Fixes` / `Closes`): the PR cannot close an issue in this repo, so a human should close intel/torch-xpu-ops#4732 once it lands. 2. **The issue's own suggestion was followed but narrowed.** It proposed asserting the contract in `test/test_accelerator.py`; the test went into `test/test_xpu.py` instead, because `test_accelerator.py` is device-generic and would impose the same PCI contract on every other backend -- including the HPU and PrivateUse1/OpenReg backends the issue itself flags as likely affected.
**The fix targets `pytorch/pytorch`, not this repo -- see Summary.** _Generated by [fix job]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659455906])._

Two verdicts in one comment are dropped as ambiguous. ``` **strong-accepted** **weak-accepted** **weak-rejected** **strong-rejected** **issue-drop** notes: ``` On a batch run add `item=` to say which sub-item the verdict is about, **in the bold text and in the marker** -- the marker is invisible, so the bold line is all a reader sees. One comment per sub-item, since a bare verdict on a batch does not say which test it means and is dropped. `run=` only when judging a run other than the newest, in both places too. A CI DISABLED sub-item, `item=` from the fan-out table: ``` **strong-accepted item=197334** notes: same TensorAssign overload as upstream CUDA, fp8 dispatch list matches ``` Another sub-item of the same batch, judged on an earlier run: ``` **weak-rejected run=35171979678 item=197335** notes: green only because the test is skipped, the kernel still lacks fp8 ``` An `[xpu-alignment]` issue that should not have been filed -- one issue per difference, so no `item=`: ``` **issue-drop** notes: accepted XPU/CUDA numerics difference, nothing to repair ```

torch/distributed/run.py leaves should_fall_back_if_binding_fails at its
False default (binding.py:95), so _handle_exception re-raises and
torchrun --numa-binding=<mode> fails to launch rather than degrading to
unbound.
SYCL does provide the data, in a different shape:
sycl::ext::intel::info::device::pci_address returns a single std::string
(sycl/info/ext_intel_device_traits.def:19), gated by
sycl::aspect::ext_intel_pci_address (sycl/info/aspects.def:15). Verified on
this runner -- all 8 devices advertise the aspect and report e.g.
'0000:17:00.0', and /sys/bus/pci/devices/0000:17:00.0/numa_node reads 0.
The fix parses that string into three integer members on c10::xpu::DeviceProp
inside the XPU layer and binds them under CUDA's names, so binding.py stays
single-shaped. The existing ASSIGN_EXT_DEVICE_PROP pattern in
c10/xpu/XPUFunctions.cpp:162-165 already establishes aspect-guarded queries
with a fallback default, which covers drivers lacking the extension.

Verdict: IMPLEMENTING -- the missing data is reachable through an existing SYCL extension query; the change is confined to the XPU property layer in pytorch.
Target repo: pytorch
Domain: upstream-pytorch

Automated by fix-root-cause.



Implement Result

Target repo: pytorch
Analyzed at: pytorch@eb428e0f31a
What I changed:

c10/xpu/XPUDeviceProp.h (+4): one entry in AT_FORALL_XPU_EXT_DEVICE_PROPERTIES for pci_address, so DeviceProp gains a std::string pci_address populated by the existing aspect-guarded ASSIGN_EXT_DEVICE_PROP machinery (empty when the driver lacks the extension). c10/xpu/XPUFunctions.cpp therefore needed no change.
torch/csrc/xpu/Module.cpp (+19): a get_pci_id helper that splits that string, plus three def_property_readonly bindings exposing pci_domain_id / pci_bus_id / pci_device_id, returning -1 when no address is reported.
torch/_C/__init__.pyi.in (+3), torch/xpu/__init__.py (+3): the three fields in the _XpuDeviceProperties stub and the get_device_properties docstring.
test/test_xpu.py (+17): test_device_properties_pci_address, a real-hardware contract test.


Why: torch/numa/binding.py:602-610 reads these three integer fields through torch.get_device_module(...).get_device_properties(...); CUDA satisfies that at torch/csrc/cuda/Module.cpp:1239-1241 while XPU bound no PCI field, so the lookup raised AttributeError. Parsing SYCL's single pci_address string on the XPU side, rather than teaching binding.py a second shape, keeps the device-agnostic code single-shaped.
Skip added: no
Ready for verify: yes

Two designs were weighed. Parsing into three int32_t members of
c10::xpu::DeviceProp populated in XPUFunctions.cpp reads better
semantically, but adding plain member declarations to that macro-only struct
body lets clang-format parse the struct and reflow its whole body -- 25 lines of
unrelated churn in a file that is clang-format-clean at HEAD. Deriving at the
pybind layer touches one C++ file fewer, adds no single-use macro, and matches
the existing gpu_subslice_count / architecture derived properties in the
same function.
+  /* the PCI address of the device as "domain:bus:slot.function", empty when  \
+   * the device does not report one. */                                       \
+  _(pci_address, pci_address, std::string())                                  \
+  auto get_pci_id = [](const DeviceProp& prop, size_t field) {
+    std::array<unsigned int, 3> ids{};
+    if (std::sscanf(
+            prop.pci_address.c_str(), "%x:%x:%x", &ids[0], &ids[1], &ids[2]) !=
+        3) {
+      return int64_t{-1};
+    }
+    return static_cast<int64_t>(ids[field]);
+  };
...
+      .def_property_readonly(
+          "pci_domain_id",
+          [get_pci_id](const DeviceProp& prop) { return get_pci_id(prop, 0); })
+      .def_property_readonly(
+          "pci_bus_id",
+          [get_pci_id](const DeviceProp& prop) { return get_pci_id(prop, 1); })
+      .def_property_readonly(
+          "pci_device_id",
+          [get_pci_id](const DeviceProp& prop) { return get_pci_id(prop, 2); })
+    def test_device_properties_pci_address(self):
+        # torch/numa/binding.py reaches the properties through
+        # torch.get_device_module() and formats these three fields into a sysfs
+        # path, so exercise the contract through the same indirection.
+        device_module = torch.get_device_module(torch.accelerator.current_accelerator())
+        props = device_module.get_device_properties(0)
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(props.pci_domain_id, 0)
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(props.pci_bus_id, 0)
+        self.assertGreaterEqual(props.pci_device_id, 0)
+        if IS_LINUX:
+            pci_addr = f"{props.pci_domain_id:04x}:{props.pci_bus_id:02x}:{props.pci_device_id:02x}.0"
+            self.assertTrue(os.path.isdir(f"/sys/bus/pci/devices/{pci_addr}"))
+            self.assertGreaterEqual(
+                _get_numa_node_index_for_device_index(device_index=0), 0
+            )
Automated by fix-implement.



Verify
Source build 06b5a40e5e7 (base eb428e0f31a plus the fix), USE_XPU=1,
TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc, editable install; torch resolves to the source
tree, not site-packages.



Test case
Before
After




torch.numa.binding._get_numa_node_index_for_device_index(0)
FAIL
PASS (returns 0)


TestXpu::test_device_properties_pci_address
n/a (new test)
PASS


torchrun --nproc_per_node=8 --numa-binding=node
FAIL
PASS



Before was AttributeError: 'torch._C._XpuDeviceProperties' object has no attribute 'pci_domain_id'.
The fix is what makes it pass, not an unrelated upstream change. git grep -i pci
at the base commit returns zero hits across torch/csrc/xpu/, torch/xpu/ and
c10/xpu/, so the attributes cannot exist without this commit. That closes the
usual nightly-before / source-after ambiguity with a measurement.
End-to-end, the reported impact is gone. torchrun --numa-binding=node with 8
ranks now launches, and the affinity is correct rather than merely non-crashing:
the measured PCI-to-NUMA map puts devices 0-3 on node 0 and 4-7 on node 1, and
ranks 0-3 land on node 0's CPUs (first_cpu=0) with ranks 4-7 on node 1's
(first_cpu=128), agreeing with numactl --hardware. (numactl had to be
installed in this container first -- without it binding stops one step later on
RuntimeError: numactl CLI is required for NUMA binding, which is environmental.)
Regression checks on the fixed build:



Suite
Result




test_xpu.py -k "pci_address or get_device_properties or get_device_capability"
3 passed


test_numa_binding.py (device-generic, mocked)
21 passed


test_xpu.py (full)
196 passed, 6 skipped, 3 xfailed, 3 failed



The three failures are pre-existing, each established by measurement rather than
assumption: test_sleep and test_cached_zes_device_infos fail with identical
messages on the unmodified nightly wheel in an isolated venv, and
test_xpu_header_installed checks torch/include/ATen/, which an editable
install never populates (the headers are present and correct under
build/install/). None references pci.

Verdict: PASSED -- the reproducer, the new contract test, and the end-to-end torchrun path all pass, with correct NUMA locality.
Lint: clean. lintrunner --revision HEAD~1 --skip CLANGTIDY reports ok No lint issues. CLANGTIDY flags 5 errors in torch/csrc/xpu/Module.cpp, all pre-existing -- reproduced identically against the base version of the same file, and none on an added line.

Automated by fix-verify.



Summary
Outcome: IMPLEMENTING(fix_verified)
One bug: torch/numa/binding.py became device-generic in pytorch/pytorch#185266
and thereby applied CUDA's device-properties contract -- pci_domain_id,
pci_bus_id, pci_device_id -- to every accelerator, but the XPU property layer
exposed no PCI data at any level, so the lookup raised AttributeError and
torchrun --numa-binding failed to launch on Intel GPUs. The fix queries SYCL's
pci_address string into c10::xpu::DeviceProp through the existing
aspect-guarded macro and splits it into the three integers at the pybind layer,
so the device-agnostic code stays single-shaped and a driver without the
extension yields -1 rather than throwing. Verification was end to end: the
reproducer returns a node index, a new real-hardware contract test passes, and
8-rank torchrun --numa-binding=node binds ranks 0-3 to NUMA node 0 and 4-7 to
node 1 -- correct locality, matching numactl --hardware, not just the absence
of a crash.

Branch: agent/fix-issue-4732 (in the pytorch checkout)
Base: eb428e0f31a0dafc2cce417af9dcc09aa15fd16b
Changed files: c10/xpu/XPUDeviceProp.h, torch/csrc/xpu/Module.cpp, torch/_C/__init__.pyi.in, torch/xpu/__init__.py, test/test_xpu.py
Nothing was pushed. The patch is exported as a workflow artifact for a human to review and apply.

Two things for whoever picks this up:

The PR goes to pytorch/pytorch, not this repo. The bug is filed here but
the root cause is entirely in pytorch's XPU property layer, so no
torch-xpu-ops change is needed. Use no closing keyword (Fixes / Closes):
the PR cannot close an issue in this repo, so a human should close
#4732 once it lands.
The issue's own suggestion was followed but narrowed. It proposed asserting
the contract in test/test_accelerator.py; the test went into
test/test_xpu.py instead, because test_accelerator.py is device-generic and
would impose the same PCI contract on every other backend -- including the HPU
and PrivateUse1/OpenReg backends the issue itself flags as likely affected.


The fix targets pytorch/pytorch, not this repo -- see Summary.

issues.title: [xpu-aglinment] Fix GELU erf-tail catastrophic cancellation
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

<!-- agent:status:OPEN -->

Exact GELU on XPU loses the negative tail to catastrophic cancellation. The XPU
SYCL kernel computes the normal CDF term as `0.5 * (1 + erf(x * sqrt(1/2)))`.
For large negative values `erf` approaches `-1`, so `1 + erf(...)` cancels and
the remaining precision is lost.

This was found during XPU alignment for upstream PyTorch PR
[地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#189234] CPU/CUDA/MPS were covered by the
upstream fix, while XPU was explicitly excluded as an out-of-tree backend, so
XPU still exhibits the cancellation.

### Reproducer

```python
import math
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

x = torch.arange(-12.0, 12.0, 2**-6, device="xpu", dtype=torch.float32)
xref = x.cpu().double()
tail = xref.abs() >= 4.0
alpha = math.sqrt(0.5)

expected_fwd = 0.5 * xref * torch.erfc(-xref * alpha)
actual_fwd = F.gelu(x).cpu().double()
fwd_error = ((actual_fwd - expected_fwd)[tail] /
             expected_fwd[tail].abs().clamp(min=1e-30)).abs().max().item()

grad = torch.ones_like(x)
expected_bwd = (0.5 * torch.erfc(-xref * alpha) +
                xref * math.sqrt(2.0 / math.pi) * 0.5 *
                torch.exp(-0.5 * xref * xref))
actual_bwd = torch.ops.aten.gelu_backward(grad, x).cpu().double()
bwd_error = ((actual_bwd - expected_bwd)[tail] /
             expected_bwd[tail].abs().clamp(min=1e-30)).abs().max().item()

print(f"forward tail relative error: {fwd_error:.3e}")
print(f"backward tail relative error: {bwd_error:.3e}")
assert fwd_error < 1e-3
```
