Automated fix session for the DISABLED-test queue entries named in the trigger comment. Progress follows in the collapsed stage blocks below; the [workflow run]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:36371714111]) has the live log.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | batch-bug (skip-list) | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | unclear | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Sub-items handled this run (both are `TestFlexDecodingXPU` in `test/inductor/test_flex_decoding.py`, mirrored DISABLED tests): 1. `test_pointwise_query_producer_head_dims1_xpu` -- `pytorch/pytorch#198713` 2. `test_pointwise_query_producer_head_dims2_xpu` -- `pytorch/pytorch#198714` They are two parametrizations of the same test body, so sub-item 1 takes the fix and sub-item 2 is re-checked against it. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Ran against the nightly XPU wheel (`2.15.0.dev20260921+xpu`) on this runner's Battlemage (Arc Pro B60) GPU, from `/tmp` with an absolute test path so `import torch` resolves to the wheel rather than the checkout. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | 1. `test_pointwise_query_producer_head_dims1_xpu` | CANNOT_VERIFY | passes on BMG; CI signature is `Mismatched elements: 968 / 1024 (94.5%)`, `Greatest absolute difference: 1.14e-3`, `Greatest relative difference: 0.198` on PVC | | 2. `test_pointwise_query_producer_head_dims2_xpu` | CANNOT_VERIFY | same, PVC-only | The first run on the stale wheel failed with `Greatest absolute difference: 2.147` -- a different, already-fixed bug (the flex-decoding query layout was read before being frozen, fixed upstream in `17b697f26c`, which postdates the installed nightly). After applying those two lines locally so the wheel matches current `main`, all three `head_dims` parametrizations pass here, which is what isolated the remaining CI failure as a precision difference rather than a stride bug. The blocker is hardware: this runner is Battlemage, and oneDNN TF32 is a no-op there. A `512x512` fp32 matmul produces bit-identical results with the oneDNN TF32 flag off and on, and the Triton flex-decoding kernel produces `max_abs=2.38419e-07` against eager under both `FLOAT32_PRECISION='ieee'` and `'tf32'`. The failing configuration only exists on PVC, whose XMX units implement TF32. See the Root Cause block for the simulation that reproduces the CI numbers device-independently. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@2e9b4aff8d`. `test/inductor/test_flex_decoding.py` turns on oneDNN TF32 process-wide at import time (`torch._C._set_onednn_allow_tf32(True)`, `test/inductor/test_flex_decoding.py:111`), and `test_pointwise_query_producer` is decorated `@with_tf32_off`. But `tf32_off()` in `torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py:449` only clears the CUDA and cuDNN knobs: it sets `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False` and enters `torch.backends.cudnn.flags(allow_tf32=False)`, and its `_save_matmul_precision`/`_restore_matmul_precision` pair carries only the legacy `Float32MatmulPrecision` enum plus the two `fp32_precision` values. The oneDNN flag is a separate `Context` member, `allow_tf32_onednn` (`aten/src/ATen/Context.h:538`), which `Context::setFloat32MatmulPrecision` (`aten/src/ATen/Context.cpp:485`) never writes, so nothing in `tf32_off` reaches it. The consequence is a split precision inside one assertion. The eager reference `f(x, k, v)` runs its matmuls through oneDNN, which selects `dnnl::fpmath_mode::tf32` whenever `allowTF32OneDNN()` is true (`aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/detail/Matmul.cpp:201`), while the compiled branch goes through Inductor's flex lowering, where `set_float32_precision` (`torch/_inductor/kernel/flex/flex_attention.py:131`) reads `torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision` -- which `tf32_off` *did* clear -- and emits `FLOAT32_PRECISION='ieee'` into the Triton template. So `assertEqual` compares a TF32 eager result against an IEEE compiled result at default fp32 tolerances (`atol=1e-5`, `rtol=1.3e-6`). On PVC that gap is ~1e-3; on BMG both paths are IEEE regardless of the flag, which is why the test is green here. Emulating PVC by truncating the eager inputs' mantissas to 10 bits reproduces the CI regime exactly: IEEE-vs-IEEE gives `0/1024` mismatched at `max_abs=2.4e-7`, while TF32-eager-vs-IEEE-compiled gives `1009/1024` at `max_abs=2.7e-3` and `max_rel=0.215` -- the same shape as the reported `968/1024`, `1.14e-3`, `0.198`. The fix is in `tf32_off()`: it must also disable the oneDNN flag on XPU, the way `test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py:147-171` already maps a `"highest"` request to `torch._C._set_onednn_allow_tf32(False)`. `torch.backends.mkldnn` is a bracketed-mutation `PropModule`, so the flag has to be driven through `torch.backends.mkldnn.flags(...)` as a context manager rather than by assignment -- the same shape as the existing `cudnn.flags` handling two lines above. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- test-infrastructure gap in `tf32_off`, fixable from source - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch, inductor *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Analyzed at:** pytorch@2e9b4aff8d - **What I changed:** `torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py` (+12/-1) -- `tf32_off()` now also disables oneDNN's fpmath mode, held in a new `_tf32_off_mkldnn_ctx` alongside the existing cuDNN context so the depth-counted last-out restore covers it. `test/test_xpu.py` (+14) -- regression test asserting the flag is off inside `tf32_off()` and restored on exit. - **Why:** `tf32_off` cleared only the CUDA/cuDNN knobs and the `fp32_precision` values, none of which reach `allow_tf32_onednn` (`aten/src/ATen/Context.h:538`); that is the flag `Matmul.cpp:201` reads to pick `dnnl::fpmath_mode::tf32` for the eager reference, while the compiled branch was already forced to `'ieee'` by `flex_attention.py:131`. The flag is driven through `torch.backends.mkldnn.flags(...)` rather than by assignment because `torch.backends.mkldnn` is a bracketed-mutation `PropModule` -- a direct write raises `not allowed to set torch.backends.mkldnn flags after disable_global_flags` under the test runner, which is why the adjacent cuDNN handling uses `flags(...)` too. The `TEST_XPU` guard avoids the `TORCH_WARN` that `Context::setAllowTF32OneDNN` emits on builds without XPU support (`aten/src/ATen/Context.cpp:295-301`). - **Skip added:** no - **Ready for verify:** yes ```diff --- a/torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py +++ b/torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py @@ -423,6 +423,7 @@ _tf32_off_lock = threading.Lock() _tf32_off_depth = 0 _tf32_off_saved_precision = None _tf32_off_cudnn_ctx = None +_tf32_off_mkldnn_ctx = None @@ -453,13 +454,20 @@ def tf32_off(): - global _tf32_off_depth, _tf32_off_saved_precision, _tf32_off_cudnn_ctx + global _tf32_off_depth, _tf32_off_saved_precision, _tf32_off_cudnn_ctx, _tf32_off_mkldnn_ctx with _tf32_off_lock: if _tf32_off_depth == 0: _tf32_off_saved_precision = _save_matmul_precision() torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False _tf32_off_cudnn_ctx = torch.backends.cudnn.flags(enabled=None, benchmark=None, deterministic=None, allow_tf32=False) _tf32_off_cudnn_ctx.__enter__() + if TEST_XPU: + # oneDNN's fpmath mode is the knob XPU matmuls read. It is a + # Context field of its own that _save_matmul_precision's + # fp32_precision values do not cover, so leaving it enabled here + # runs the eager reference of a with_tf32_off test at TF32. + _tf32_off_mkldnn_ctx = torch.backends.mkldnn.flags(enabled=None, deterministic=None, allow_tf32=False, fp32_precision=None) + _tf32_off_mkldnn_ctx.__enter__() _tf32_off_depth += 1 try: yield @@ -467,6 +475,9 @@ def tf32_off(): with _tf32_off_lock: _tf32_off_depth -= 1 if _tf32_off_depth == 0: + if _tf32_off_mkldnn_ctx is not None: + _tf32_off_mkldnn_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None) + _tf32_off_mkldnn_ctx = None _tf32_off_cudnn_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None) _tf32_off_cudnn_ctx = None _restore_matmul_precision(_tf32_off_saved_precision) --- a/test/test_xpu.py +++ b/test/test_xpu.py @@ -26,6 +26,7 @@ import torch.multiprocessing as mp from torch.testing._internal.autocast_test_lists import AutocastTestLists, TestAutocast +from torch.testing._internal.common_cuda import tf32_off @@ -1710,6 +1711,19 @@ class TestXpu(TestCase): + def test_tf32_off_disables_onednn_tf32(self): + # oneDNN's fpmath flag is the knob XPU matmuls read, and it is separate + # from the fp32_precision values set_float32_matmul_precision writes. A + # test that enables it globally (test/inductor/test_flex_decoding.py + # does) would leak TF32 into the eager reference of a with_tf32_off test + # if tf32_off did not cover it. + with torch.backends.mkldnn.flags( + enabled=None, deterministic=None, allow_tf32=True, fp32_precision=None + ): + with tf32_off(): + self.assertFalse(torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32) + self.assertTrue(torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32) ``` *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verify Python-only fix, so no rebuild: the two changed files were applied into the nightly XPU wheel's `site-packages` (`2.15.0.dev20260921+xpu`) and run on this runner's Arc Pro B60 (Battlemage), `TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc`. Root Cause
Analyzed at pytorch origin/main@2e9b4aff8d.
test/inductor/test_flex_decoding.py turns on oneDNN TF32 process-wide at import time (torch._C._set_onednn_allow_tf32(True), test/inductor/test_flex_decoding.py:111), and test_pointwise_query_producer is decorated @with_tf32_off. But tf32_off() in torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py:449 only clears the CUDA and cuDNN knobs: it sets torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False and enters torch.backends.cudnn.flags(allow_tf32=False), and its _save_matmul_precision/_restore_matmul_precision pair carries only the legacy Float32MatmulPrecision enum plus the two fp32_precision values. The oneDNN flag is a separate Context member, allow_tf32_onednn (aten/src/ATen/Context.h:538), which Context::setFloat32MatmulPrecision (aten/src/ATen/Context.cpp:485) never writes, so nothing in tf32_off reaches it.
The consequence is a split precision inside one assertion. The eager reference f(x, k, v) runs its matmuls through oneDNN, which selects dnnl::fpmath_mode::tf32 whenever allowTF32OneDNN() is true (aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/detail/Matmul.cpp:201), while the compiled branch goes through Inductor's flex lowering, where set_float32_precision (torch/_inductor/kernel/flex/flex_attention.py:131) reads torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision -- which tf32_off did clear -- and emits FLOAT32_PRECISION='ieee' into the Triton template. On PVC that gap is ~1e-3; on BMG both paths are IEEE regardless of the flag, which is why the test is green here.

Greatest relative difference: 1.389e-05 at index (15,) (up to 1.3e-06 allowed)` | | 2. `ComboKernelTestsPerSubkernelBlocks::test_combo_kernel_per_config_subkernel_r0_r1` | REPRODUCED | same signature, identical magnitudes | The signature matches the [failing CI job]([运行记录：pytorch/pytorch@run:35674831489]) byte for byte (`1 / 16` mismatched elements, greatest absolute difference `1.1444091796875e-05`), so no source build or CI-environment alignment was needed. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@958e9824`. `test_combo_kernel_per_config_subkernel_r0_r1` (`test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py:825-839`) compares an eager `a.sum(dim=(1, 2))` against the `torch.compile` result with a bare `self.assertEqual(out_eager, out_compiled)` at `test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py:837`, i.e. with `torch.testing`'s default float32 tolerances (`atol=1e-5`, `rtol=1.3e-6`). The inputs are `torch.randn(32, 16, 64).permute(1, 0, 2)`, so each of the 16 outputs is a float32 sum of 2048 standard normals. Under the test's `triton.prefer_nd_tiling` + `triton.tile_reductions` config the Triton kernel accumulates that sum as a tiled 2D (`r0_`, `r1_`) reduction, which is a different summation order from the eager reduction, so the two results differ by float32 rounding noise. That is exactly what CI sees: element 15 has value ~0.82 while the sum of the absolute values feeding it is ~1.6e3, i.e. near-total cancellation, so the `rtol=1.3e-6` bound is meaningless there and the `atol=1e-5` bound is just barely exceeded (observed `1.1444e-05`). Neither side is wrong. Measured against a float64 reference of the same reduction, the eager result is off by up to `8.9e-06` and the compiled result by up to `1.1e-05`; relative to the `~1.6e3` sum of absolute values both are `~6e-09`, i.e. ordinary float32 accumulation error for a 2048-element reduction. The test is simply the only reduction test in this file that forgot to pass tolerances: the two sibling tests added by the same PR, `test_combo_kernel_per_config_subkernel_per` (`test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py:783`) and `test_combo_kernel_per_config_subkernel_red` (`test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py:806`), compare their eager/compiled sums with `torch.testing.assert_close(..., atol=1e-4, rtol=1e-4)`. The test was introduced by `pytorch/pytorch#171671` ("[inductor] Add per-sub-kernel block dimensions for combo kernels"), which is also what makes it run twice: `ComboKernelTestsPerSubkernelBlocks` (`test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py:1954`) subclasses `ComboKernelTests`, so both `pytorch/pytorch#198180` and `pytorch/pytorch#198181` are the same assertion. The fix is to give that one comparison the same explicit tolerances the sibling reduction tests already use. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- too-tight default float32 tolerance on a tiled-reduction eager/compiled comparison. - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** inductor *Automated by fix-root-cause.*

The accelerator's `device_lazy_init` reaches `PyImport_ImportModule("torch.xpu")`, and CPython's `PyImport_Import` reads `__builtins__` off the *calling* frame's globals with `PyObject_GetItem`, which raises `KeyError` on a dict that lacks it. What the bug was. pytorch/pytorch#198709 disables test_load_then_compile_survives_baked_in_global_collision on xpu; it fails with AssertionError: Subprocess failure (KeyError: '__builtins__'). GraphRuntimeEnv.forward_callable builds the Dynamo-generated function's __globals__ as a plain dict with no __builtins__ key. On a machine with an accelerator the generated pre-graph bytecode opens with store_user_object_weakrefs(get_current_stream(torch.device('xpu', 0))), and torch._dynamo.utils.get_current_stream is now a pybind function instead of a Python one — so there is no intermediate Python frame. The accelerator's device_lazy_init reaches PyImport_ImportModule("torch.xpu"), and CPython's PyImport_Import reads __builtins__ off the calling frame's globals with PyObject_GetItem, which raises KeyError on a dict that lacks it. Only the load path trips (an in-process compile has already initialized the device), and it is xpu-only because that is the CI configuration which runs test/dynamo/ on a box with an accelerator.
Fix. Seed __builtins__ into that globals dict before the function object is created, first in the literal so a recorded or caller-supplied binding still wins. I chose this over hardening device_lazy_init because PyImport_ImportModule is reached from many places in torch's C++, so making Dynamo's synthesized namespace look like a real module namespace fixes the whole class. Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | batch-bug (heterogeneous) | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | torch-xpu-ops | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Sub-items handled by this run (both are the same test body, parametrized by test class): 1. `test_weight_norm_1d_and_reduced_dtypes_xpu` (`GPUTests`, `test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py`) -- `pytorch/pytorch#199140` 2. `test_weight_norm_1d_and_reduced_dtypes_dynamic_shapes` (`DynamicShapes`, `test/inductor/test_torchinductor_dynamic_shapes.py`) -- `pytorch/pytorch#199141` Sub-item 1 takes the fix; sub-item 2 is re-checked against it, since both run the same test body and both failed inside the eager reference call. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Reproduced on the latest resolvable XPU nightly wheel (`2.15.0.dev20260921+xpu`, pytorch `afa73d98`) on an Intel Arc Pro B60 (BMG). The failing call is the eager reference inside the test body, `torch._weight_norm(v, g, 0)` with a 1-D `v` -- the same line the CI traceback stops on. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | 1. `test_weight_norm_1d_and_reduced_dtypes_xpu` | REPRODUCED | eager `_weight_norm_interface` with 1-D `v` returns garbage norms, e.g. fp32 `[3.963, 0, 0, 0, ...]` vs CPU `[1.541, 0.293, 2.179, 0.568, ...]`; fp16/bf16 give `nan`/`inf` | | 2. `test_weight_norm_1d_and_reduced_dtypes_dynamic_shapes` | REPRODUCED | same eager call, same test body | The CI log for `pytorch/pytorch#199140` shows the same defect manifesting as `torch.OutOfMemoryError: XPU out of memory. Tried to allocate 130290.75 GiB` ([job log]([运行记录：pytorch/pytorch@run:36653643191])). Both symptoms come from one uninitialized read: the kernel derives its reduction extent from an out-of-bounds `TensorInfo` slot, so the value is whatever happened to be on the stack -- a huge number on the PVC CI runner (OOM), a small one here (silently wrong results). The 2-D shapes in the same test match CPU exactly, which isolates the defect to the 1-D case. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at `torch-xpu-ops@51acfc9f`, pytorch `origin/main@18a1d563`. The fused XPU `weight_norm` kernels derive their launch geometry from a collapsed `TensorInfo` and assume the input always collapses to two dimensions -- the kept dim and the reduction dim. `weight_norm_kernel` collapses `v` around `dim`, then flips to the surviving reduction dim with `dim_after_collapse = 1 - dim_after_collapse` and reads `vinfo.sizes[dim_after_collapse]` as the reduction extent (`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/WeightNormKernels.cpp:379-401`). For a 1-D `v` with `dim=0` the collapse leaves `dims == 1`, so that index is `1` -- one past the end of the populated part of the info. `TensorInfo`'s constructor only writes `sizes[0..dims)` (`src/comm/TensorInfo.h:90-91`, `:106-116`), so the kernel picks up whatever was on the stack: on the PVC CI runner a huge value, which made the carrier allocation ask for 130290.75 GiB and throw `torch.OutOfMemoryError`; on the BMG box used here a small value, which silently produced garbage norms. `weight_norm_backward_kernel` had the same read. Upstream CUDA never hits this because it computes the reduction extent arithmetically -- `rowSize = prod(v.size(i) for i in ndims-1..1)`, an empty product of `1` for a 1-D `v` (`aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/WeightNorm.cu:361-363`). The test appeared on 2026-09-29 with the upstream fix for `pytorch/pytorch#198676` (an Inductor decomposition bug for 1-D `weight_norm`). It was the first test to call eager `_weight_norm_interface` with a 1-D `v` on XPU, which is why the latent out-of-bounds read only surfaced now, and why both disable issues point at the same eager line rather than at anything Inductor does. **This is already fixed on torch-xpu-ops `main`.** intel/torch-xpu-ops#5598 (merged 2026-10-05) appends a trivial size-1 reduction dim when `dim_after_collapse >= vinfo.dims`, in both the forward and the backward path, and adds `test/regressions/test_weight_norm.py`. That commit is not in pytorch's `third_party/xpu.txt` pin yet -- the pin is still `5934d4f5` (2026-09-25) -- so pytorch CI and the nightly wheels keep hitting the old code. There is no new patch to author here; the remaining work is the pin bump. - **Verdict:** ALREADY_FIXED -- fixed at `main` by intel/torch-xpu-ops#5598, nothing left to implement - **Target repo:** torch-xpu-ops - **Domain:** xpu-kernel *Automated by fix-root-cause.*

Tried to allocate 121797.90 GiB` at `ref = fn(v, g)`, against `130290.75 GiB` in the `pytorch/pytorch#199140` job log -- a different garbage value from the same uninitialized slot. Reproduce
Reproduced on the latest resolvable XPU nightly wheel (2.15.0.dev20260921+xpu, pytorch afa73d98) on an Intel Arc Pro B60 (BMG). The failing call is the eager reference inside the test body, torch._weight_norm(v, g, 0) with a 1-D v -- the same line the CI traceback stops on.

The CI log for pytorch/pytorch#199140 shows the same defect manifesting as torch.OutOfMemoryError: XPU out of memory. Tried to allocate 130290.75 GiB (job log). Both symptoms come from one uninitialized read: the kernel derives its reduction extent from an out-of-bounds TensorInfo slot, so the value is whatever happened to be on the stack -- a huge number on the PVC CI runner (OOM), a small one here (silently wrong results). The 2-D shapes in the same test match CPU exactly, which isolates the defect to the 1-D case.
Automated by fix-reproduce.



Root Cause
Analyzed at torch-xpu-ops@51acfc9f, pytorch origin/main@18a1d563.
The fused XPU weight_norm kernels derive their launch geometry from a collapsed TensorInfo and assume the input always collapses to two dimensions -- the kept dim and the reduction dim. weight_norm_kernel collapses v around dim, then flips to the surviving reduction dim with dim_after_collapse = 1 - dim_after_collapse and reads vinfo.sizes[dim_after_collapse] as the reduction extent (src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/WeightNormKernels.cpp:379-401). For a 1-D v with dim=0 the collapse leaves dims == 1, so that index is 1 -- one past the end of the populated part of the info. TensorInfo's constructor only writes sizes[0..dims) (src/comm/TensorInfo.h:90-91, :106-116), so the kernel picks up whatever was on the stack: on the PVC CI runner a huge value, which made the carrier allocation ask for 130290.75 GiB and throw torch.OutOfMemoryError; on the BMG box used here a small value, which silently produced garbage norms. weight_norm_backward_kernel had the same read. Upstream CUDA never hits this because it computes the reduction extent arithmetically -- rowSize = prod(v.size(i) for i in ndims-1..1), an empty product of 1 for a 1-D v (aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/WeightNorm.cu:361-363).
The test appeared on 2026-09-29 with the upstream fix for pytorch/pytorch#198676 (an Inductor decomposition bug for 1-D weight_norm). It was the first test to call eager _weight_norm_interface with a 1-D v on XPU, which is why the latent out-of-bounds read only surfaced now, and why both disable issues point at the same eager line rather than at anything Inductor does.
This is already fixed on torch-xpu-ops main. #5598 (merged 2026-10-05) appends a trivial size-1 reduction dim when dim_after_collapse >= vinfo.dims, in both the forward and the backward path, and adds test/regressions/test_weight_norm.py. That commit is not in pytorch's third_party/xpu.txt pin yet -- the pin is still 5934d4f5 (2026-09-25) -- so pytorch CI and the nightly wheels keep hitting the old code. There is no new patch to author here; the remaining work is the pin bump.

Nothing pushed; `agent_space_xpu/fix_result.json` records `verdict: PASSED`, `target_repo: torch-xpu-ops`, and `upstream_disabled_issue: 199213`. **Root cause.** The triggering comment pointed at upstream disable issue `pytorch/pytorch#199213`, i.e. `TestInductorNextafterXPU::test_nextafter_noncontiguous_False_xpu_float32`. The test asserts the Inductor result is bit-exactly equal to the eager result on the same device, and eager XPU is the wrong side: the SYCL device `std::nextafter` returns `+0.0` for the `float`/`double` step that lands on zero from the smallest-magnitude *negative* subnormal, where IEEE 754 requires `-0.0`. I chose the targeted correction over reimplementing `nextafter` from scratch because an exhaustive sweep of every fp16/bf16 bit pattern plus ~3M random/boundary fp32/fp64 pairs found the signed zero to be the only disagreement with CPU. **Verification** on a source build of pytorch `8ab9c868` with this branch as `third_party/torch-xpu-ops` (`TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc`, Arc Pro B60): `TestInductorNextafterXPU -k nextafter` went from `4 failed, 14 passed` to `18 passed`; the eager sweep went from 6 mismatches per dtype to 0. `TestInductorOpInfoXPU -k "nextafter or heaviside"`, `test_binary_ufuncs.py -k "(nextafter or heaviside) and xpu"`, and `test/regressions/test_binary.py` all clean. `lintrunner -a` clean — note `spin` exposes no lint command in this repo, so I used `lintrunner` directly. +// converts to an integer here, so a position past INT_MAX keeps its voxel.
+template <typename scalar_t>
+static inline scalar_t compute_coordinates_sized(
+    scalar_t coord,
+    int64_t size,
+    GridSamplerPadding padding_mode,
+    bool align_corners) {
+  if (padding_mode == GridSamplerPadding::Border) {
+    coord = clip_coordinates(coord, size);
+  } else if (padding_mode == GridSamplerPadding::Reflection) {
+    // the bounds reflect_coordinates halves, formed without doubling the extent
+    const scalar_t low =
+        align_corners ? static_cast<scalar_t>(0) : static_cast<scalar_t>(-0.5);
+    const scalar_t span =
+        static_cast<scalar_t>(align_corners ? size - 1 : size);
+    if (span == 0) {
+      coord = 0;
+    } else {
+      const scalar_t in = sycl::fabs(coord - low);
+      const scalar_t extra = sycl::fmod(in, span);
+      const bool odd =
+          sycl::fmod(sycl::floor(in / span), static_cast<scalar_t>(2)) != 0;
+      coord = odd ? span - extra + low : extra + low;
+    }
+    coord = clip_coordinates(coord, size);
+  }
+  return coord;
+}
+
+// The four cubic taps one axis contributes at `coord`: the Keys coefficients
+// of its fractional part, the index each tap reads, and, when `coeffs_grad` is
+// given, the coefficient derivatives. The taps sit around the unclipped index.
+// A tap the padding drops takes a negative index, contributes a zero value and
+// keeps its coefficient, as get_value_bounded does in 4-D.
+template <typename scalar_t, typename index_t>
+static inline void resolve_cubic_taps(
+    scalar_t coord,
+    index_t size,
+    GridSamplerPadding padding_mode,
+    bool align_corners,
+    scalar_t coeffs[4],
+    scalar_t* coeffs_grad,
+    index_t indices[4]) {
+  const scalar_t base = sycl::floor(coord);
+  get_cubic_upsample_coefficients<scalar_t>(coeffs, coord - base);
+  if (coeffs_grad != nullptr) {
+    get_cubic_coefficients_grad<scalar_t>(coeffs_grad, coord - base);
+  }
+  const scalar_t index_limit =
+      static_cast<scalar_t>(std::numeric_limits<index_t>::max());
+  for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
+    const scalar_t tap = at::native::xpu::compute_coordinates_sized(
+        base - 1 + i, size, padding_mode, align_corners);
+    // a tap that is not finite, or past the index type, fails before the cast
+    const index_t index = (tap >= 0 && tap < index_limit)
+        ? static_cast<index_t>(tap)
+        : static_cast<index_t>(-1);
+    indices[i] = index < size ? index : static_cast<index_t>(-1);
+  }
+}

CI job logs from the run that triggered the upstream disable have already aged out of GitHub retention, so the signature above comes from the local reproduction rather than from the original job log. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@a49d6be19d`. `linalg.tensorinv`'s OpInfo carries an `unittest.expectedFailure` for `TestCommon` / `test_numpy_ref` on `device_type="xpu"` / `torch.float64` (`torch/testing/_internal/opinfo/definitions/linalg.py:2650-2657`, commented `torch-xpu-ops/issues/4313`). `test_numpy_ref` (`test/test_ops.py:458-473`) now compares `torch.linalg.tensorinv` against `np.linalg.tensorinv` successfully on XPU, and `unittest` converts a pass under `expectedFailure` into a hard `Unexpected success` failure. The op itself is not broken: over both of the OpInfo's reference inputs -- `(2, 2, 3, 12, 1)` with `ind=3` (the exact sample quoted in intel/torch-xpu-ops#4313) and `(4, 3, 6, 1, 2)` with `ind=2` -- the largest relative deviation from NumPy is `1.8e-14`, versus the `107.5` reported when the decoration was added. `torch.linalg.inv` runs natively on XPU here (no `XPUFallback` warning with `PYTORCH_DEBUG_XPU_FALLBACK=1`), so the correct result comes from the XPU oneMKL LAPACK path, not from a CPU fallback. Why it surfaced now: the decoration landed 2026-08-20 (`02dbce8ad5`, `pytorch/pytorch#178849`), and the upstream disable was filed 2026-10-08. In between, `.ci/docker/common/install_xpu.sh` moved the CI toolchain from Intel oneAPI Deep Learning Essentials `2026.1.2.25` to `2026.1.3.17` on 2026-09-18 (`43f512a1c4`, `pytorch/pytorch#195128`), which carries a new oneMKL. That bump is consistent with the LAPACK inverse numerics being corrected underneath the still-present xfail; no torch-xpu-ops commit in that window touches the `linalg.inv` path (`src/ATen/native/xpu/mkl/BatchLinearAlgebra.cpp` last changed 2026-08-12). Fix strategy: delete the stale `DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, ...)` entry so `test_numpy_ref` runs as an ordinary passing test again. The fix is entirely in pytorch test infrastructure; torch-xpu-ops has no skip or decoration for this test. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- remove a stale `expectedFailure` decoration whose underlying numerical bug is fixed. - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Analyzed at:** pytorch@a49d6be19d - **What I changed:** `torch/testing/_internal/opinfo/definitions/linalg.py` -- removed the 8-line `DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, "TestCommon", "test_numpy_ref", device_type="xpu", dtypes=(torch.float64,))` entry from `linalg.tensorinv`'s `skips`. - **Why:** the decoration was the only thing failing the test -- `linalg.tensorinv` matches `np.linalg.tensorinv` to 1.8e-14 relative on both OpInfo reference inputs, and `test_numpy_ref` (`test/test_ops.py:458`) therefore passes, which `unittest` reports as `Unexpected success`. - **Skip added:** no (a stale one was removed) - **Ready for verify:** yes ```diff --- a/torch/testing/_internal/opinfo/definitions/linalg.py +++ b/torch/testing/_internal/opinfo/definitions/linalg.py @@ -2647,14 +2647,6 @@ op_db: list[OpInfo] = [ device_type="mps", dtypes=(torch.complex64,), ), - # torch-xpu-ops/issues/4313 - DecorateInfo( - unittest.expectedFailure, - "TestCommon", - "test_numpy_ref", - device_type="xpu", - dtypes=(torch.float64,), - ), # The test is flaky on AMX with Inductor DecorateInfo( unittest.skip, ``` *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verify Run on the nightly XPU wheel `2.15.0.dev20260923+xpu` (Intel Arc Pro B60), pytorch test tree at `origin/main` `a49d6be19d`. Before and after are the **same** build, differing only by the removed `DecorateInfo` -- so the comparison isolates the fix. | Test case | Before | After | |-----------|--------|-------| | `test_numpy_ref_linalg_tensorinv_xpu_float64` | FAIL | PASS | `Before` was `Failed: Unexpected success`. Regression checks on the fixed build: | Suite | Result | |---|---| | `test_ops.py -k "tensorinv and xpu"` (with fix) | 23 passed, 3 skipped | | `test_ops.py -k "tensorinv and xpu"` (without fix) | 1 failed, 22 passed, 3 skipped | **How the fix was exercised.** The changed file lives inside the installed `torch` package, so a wheel cannot pick up an edit in the checkout. Rather than pay a cold source build for an 8-line deletion of test metadata, the identical removal was applied in memory by a pytest plugin (`agent_space_xpu/verify/apply_fix_plugin.py`) at `pytest_configure`, before `test_ops.py` is imported and `instantiate_device_type_tests` reads the decorators; the plugin asserts it removed exactly one entry. The decoration is byte-identical in the wheel and in the checkout, no compiled code is involved, and the committed file passes `py_compile` / `ast.parse`. - **Verdict:** PASSED -- the test passes once the stale decoration is gone, and the other 22 `tensorinv` XPU cases are unaffected. - **Lint:** clean (`ruff check` and `ruff format --diff` on the changed file; `spin` / `lintrunner` are not installed in this container, so the full lint suite was not run) *Automated by fix-verify.*

The mutation semantics the test exists to check are not involved. The generated wrapper issues the two extern mms into `buf0` / `buf1` and then one pointwise kernel which, per index, does `tmp2 = buf0 + buf1; tmp3 = buf1 + tmp2` and stores them back -- exactly the order the test's `add_in_order` reference applies, with no cross-index dependency and so no race. Everything after the matmul is therefore bit-exact, which was confirmed here: when both matmuls agree, the compiled and eager outputs are bitwise equal. So the test's only inexact ingredient is the matmul, and it asks two independent GEMM invocations to agree to within a float32 atol over a million elements. **Stage: reproduce — stopped.** No code change proposed; nothing to patch in either repo. Upstream bug: `pytorch/pytorch#179891` — `torch.xpu.get_device_properties()` SIGSEGV (`ip=0x0`) on Intel Arc Pro B70 (Battlemage, device `0xe223`). ### Reproduce result: NOT_REPRODUCED | | Reporter | This runner | |---|---|---| | GPU | 2x Arc Pro B70 (BMG-G31, `0xe223`) | 8x Arc Pro B60 (BMG, `0xE211`) | | torch | 2.10.0+xpu / 2.13.0a0 source | 2.15.0.dev20260923+xpu | | compute-runtime | 26.09.37435 | 26.22.38646.7 | | Level Zero loader | 1.21.9 | 1.28.6 | | `get_device_properties(i)` | segfault | OK, all 8 devices | | `get_device_name(i)` | segfault | OK, all 8 devices | | `mem_get_info(i)` | OK | OK, all 8 devices | | `tensor.to("xpu:i")` | segfault (source build) | OK, all 8 devices | ### Why there is nothing to fix here The upstream maintainers root-caused this on the driver side, not in PyTorch: `zeDeviceGetComputeProperties` added a new entry to the Level Zero Driver Direct Interface Table, and the reporter's `libze-intel-gpu1` was older than the `libze1` loader it was paired with, so the loader dispatched through a null function pointer — hence `ip=0x0`. The matching report on an Arc Pro B50 in that thread was likewise attributed to the known driver bug `pytorch/pytorch#157989`. That also means the reporter's fallback request ("at minimum raise a Python exception rather than segfaulting") is not implementable from either repo: the null jump happens inside the Level Zero loader's dispatch table, before any PyTorch frame, so there is no C++ or Python boundary at which it could be converted into an exception. The only fix is the driver-version pairing, which this runner's stack (newer than the versions upstream identified as fixed) already satisfies. An upstream maintainer proposed closing `pytorch/pytorch#179891` on 2026-10-12, noting it should already be fixed outside WSL. This run's evidence agrees.
Summary `pytorch/pytorch#179891` reports that `torch.xpu.get_device_properties()` dies with a null-instruction-pointer segfault on an Intel Arc Pro B70, and the upstream thread already traces that to a Level Zero ABI mismatch between an old `libze-intel-gpu1` driver and a newer `libze1` loader, where a new Driver Direct Interface Table entry for `zeDeviceGetComputeProperties` is dispatched as a null pointer. Reproducing the full symptom list on this runner's Battlemage hardware (8x Arc Pro B60, compute-runtime 26.22.38646.7, Level Zero 1.28.6) against the latest nightly showed every reported call succeeding on every device, including the `tensor.to("xpu:0")` crash raised in the follow-up comment. Because the faulting jump occurs inside the loader's dispatch table before any PyTorch frame, neither a fix nor a graceful-error guard is possible from pytorch or torch-xpu-ops, so the pipeline stopped at reproduce without staging a change. - **Outcome:** `SKIPPED(no_longer_reproduces)` — driver/environment issue, already fixed by the current driver stack - **Branch:** none created - **Changed files:** none - **Nothing was pushed, and there is no patch artifact for this run.** The recommended action is to close the tracking entry and point reporters at upgrading `libze-intel-gpu1` and `libze1` to matching versions.

Automated fix run for `pytorch/pytorch#164966` — *XPU OOM when allocating a tensor sized from its reported available memory*. **Outcome: `SKIPPED` (does not reproduce).** No code change, no branch, no patch artifact. ### Progress - [x] Triage — single bug, filed upstream in `pytorch/pytorch` - [x] Reproduce on latest nightly — **NOT_REPRODUCED** - [ ] ~~Root cause~~ / ~~Implement~~ / ~~Verify~~ — not reached
Reproduce Environment: latest XPU nightly `torch 2.15.0.dev20260923+xpu` (confirmed newest on the index), 8x Intel Arc Pro B60 (BMG), 23.906 GiB each, driver `1.15.38646+7`, Level-Zero V2 adapter. The reproducer from the issue **passes 6/6 runs across 2 devices**: | | reported free | requested | result | |---|---|---|---| | `xpu:0` / `xpu:1`, 3 runs each | 23.694 GiB | 23.554 GiB | PASS | The request is larger than this device's `max_mem_alloc_size` (22.711 GiB) and still succeeds, so the Level-Zero single-allocation restriction that produced `ZE_RESULT_ERROR_UNSUPPORTED_SIZE` on the reporter's 64 GiB PVC is not enforced on this stack. **Caveat:** the report is against PVC and only BMG is attached to this runner, so this is "does not reproduce on available hardware", not proof the PVC path changed. Residual driver-side inaccuracy measured here, for the record: - allocating *exactly* the reported free memory fails, while 99% of it succeeds (~240 MiB over-report); - after a 22.5 GiB block is freed and `empty_cache()` returns, the driver takes about 1s to return it to its free-memory accounting; an immediate re-allocation of the same size OOMs, then succeeds once the accounting catches up.

Large single allocations needing `UR_L0_USE_RELAXED_ALLOCATION_LIMITS=1`, stated by the driver team to be by design — internal URLZA-666. Test lives in pytorch `test/inductor/test_flex_decoding.py`. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Reproduced on the nightly XPU wheel `2.16.0.dev20261013+xpu` (PVC, Data Center GPU Max 1100), with the pytorch test tree at `origin/main` (`6c3e5b90e4`). All three `head_dims` parametrizations fail, not only the disabled `head_dims0`. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_pointwise_query_producer_head_dims0_xpu` | REPRODUCED | `AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close!` -- greatest abs diff `1.29e-03` (atol `1e-05`) | | `test_pointwise_query_producer_head_dims1_xpu` | REPRODUCED | greatest abs diff `1.14e-03` | | `test_pointwise_query_producer_head_dims2_xpu` | REPRODUCED | greatest abs diff `1.35e-03` | Command (from the pytorch checkout's `test/` directory, nightly wheel on `sys.path`): ``` python -m pytest inductor/test_flex_decoding.py -k test_pointwise_query_producer --timeout 600 ``` Measuring both sides against an fp64 CPU reference shows the **eager** side is the inaccurate one (`1.3e-03`), while the compiled flex-decoding kernel is exact (`3.0e-07`) -- so this is not a flex-decoding codegen bug. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause | Field | Value | |---|---| | Domains | `upstream-pytorch` | | Target repo | `pytorch` | | Analyzed sha | `6c3e5b90e4` (`origin/main`) | | Verdict | IMPLEMENTING | **Not a flex-decoding bug.** Measured against an fp64 CPU reference, the compiled flex-decoding kernel is exact (`3e-07`) and the *eager* reference the test compares against is the inaccurate side (`1.3e-03`). The compiled kernel is generated with `FLOAT32_PRECISION='ieee'`, so the 1e-3 gap is TF32 in the eager XPU matmuls. XPU eager matmul precision is gated by one switch that nothing else writes: `at::globalContext().allowTF32OneDNN()` (exposed as `torch.backends.mkldnn.allow_tf32`, read in `aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/detail/Matmul.cpp`). It is **not** touched by `torch.set_float32_matmul_precision()` or by the `fp32_precision` / `allow_tf32` setters for the `cuda` and `mkldnn` backends. `test/inductor/test_flex_decoding.py` turns that switch on at import time (`torch._C._set_onednn_allow_tf32(True)` when running on XPU), mirroring the module's `set_float32_matmul_precision("high")` so the loose-tolerance tests exercise the same reduced-precision paths CUDA does. `test_pointwise_query_producer` (added by `pytorch/pytorch#198543`, compares with `assertEqual`'s default fp32 tolerances `rtol=1.3e-6, atol=1e-5`) is decorated `@with_tf32_off`. On CUDA that decorator delivers full fp32 on both sides. On XPU it sets the cuda/mkldnn `fp32_precision` values to `ieee` but leaves the oneDNN TF32 switch on, so the eager reference keeps running in TF32 and the comparison fails by ~1.3e-3. Confirmed in-test: `cuda.matmul=ieee`, `mkldnn.matmul=tf32`, `onednn_allow_tf32=True`, and a bare `q @ k.transpose(-2, -1)` in that same context is off by `1.0e-02`. So the gap is in test infrastructure: `tf32_off()` in `torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py` does not cover the XPU oneDNN TF32 flag, even though `with_tf32_off`'s contract is "enforce torch.float tensors to be always computed at full precision". `test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py` already works around this by hand in its local `temp_float32_matmul_precision` helper. **Fix strategy:** make `tf32_off()` also clear the oneDNN TF32 switch on XPU builds, and save/restore it alongside the other matmul-precision state so the context manager stays leak-free. The alternative -- having `torch.set_float32_matmul_precision()` / `setAllowTF32CuBLAS` drive `allow_tf32_onednn` in `aten/src/ATen/Context.cpp` -- would change user-visible eager precision across all of XPU and is far beyond what this disabled test needs. *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result ```diff diff --git a/torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py b/torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py --- a/torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py +++ b/torch/testing/_internal/common_cuda.py @@ -469,11 +469,12 @@ _tf32_off_cudnn_ctx = None def _save_matmul_precision(): return (_get_legacy_float32_matmul_precision(), torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision, - torch.backends.mkldnn.matmul.fp32_precision) + torch.backends.mkldnn.matmul.fp32_precision, + torch._C._get_onednn_allow_tf32() if torch.xpu.is_available() else None) def _restore_matmul_precision(saved): - legacy, cuda_precision, mkldnn_precision = saved + legacy, cuda_precision, mkldnn_precision, onednn_allow_tf32 = saved # set_float32_matmul_precision overwrites both backend-specific values, so # it goes first. Restoring those as fp32_precision strings rather than as # allow_tf32 booleans also preserves the "none" default, which allow_tf32 @@ -481,6 +482,8 @@ def _restore_matmul_precision(saved): _set_legacy_float32_matmul_precision(legacy) torch.backends.cuda.matmul.fp32_precision = cuda_precision torch.backends.mkldnn.matmul.fp32_precision = mkldnn_precision + if onednn_allow_tf32 is not None: + torch._C._set_onednn_allow_tf32(onednn_allow_tf32) @contextlib.contextmanager @@ -495,6 +498,10 @@ def tf32_off(): if _tf32_off_depth == 0: _tf32_off_saved_precision = _save_matmul_precision() torch.backends.cuda.matmul.allow_tf32 = False + # XPU eager matmul reads a separate oneDNN TF32 switch that none of + # the fp32_precision / allow_tf32 setters above write. + if torch.xpu.is_available(): + torch._C._set_onednn_allow_tf32(False) _tf32_off_cudnn_ctx = torch.backends.cudnn.flags(enabled=None, benchmark=None, deterministic=None, allow_tf32=False) _tf32_off_cudnn_ctx.__enter__() _tf32_off_depth += 1 ``` The `torch._C._set_onednn_allow_tf32` setter warns on builds without XPU support, so both the save and the clear are guarded by `torch.xpu.is_available()`; non-XPU platforms are byte-for-byte unaffected. `tf32_on()` is deliberately left alone -- making it *enable* the switch would change what `tf32_on_and_off` tests measure on XPU. *Automated by fix-implement.*

### :robot: Agent fix run — `pytorch/pytorch#200422` **Stages 1-6 complete — fix verified.** Scope: the triggering comment pointed this run at the single upstream DISABLED test `pytorch/pytorch#200422`, so the fix belongs upstream and the branch is named after that issue. | Stage | Result | |---|---| | triage | single-bug, CI break (upstream-disabled test), `allow_skip=true` | | reproduce | **REPRODUCED** — 6 failures in 10 consecutive runs on `xpu-agent-pvc` | | root cause | test-side tolerance, not an operator bug (below) | | implement | 1 file, 8 insertions in `pytorch/pytorch` | | verify | **PASSED** — 20/20 runs, whole parametrized family green on cpu and xpu | **Environment.** Runner `xpu-agent-pvc` (Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100), nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261013+xpu`, pytorch tree at `origin/main` (`fb9187d4a6`). Test-only change, so no source build was needed. **Reproduction.** Test `test/inductor/test_torchinductor_dynamic_shapes.py::DynamicShapesGPUTests::test_mutate_realized_buffer_in_make_fx_graph_case_foreach_reads_sibling_target_dynamic_shapes_xpu` fails with `Tensor-likes are not close!`, 1 mismatched element out of 1048576, greatest absolute difference `1.5e-05` against `atol=1e-05`. The failure is flaky run to run, not seed dependent, which is why it only shows up on some shards. **Root cause.** The case computes `a = x @ w1` and `b = x @ w2` on 1024x1024 float32 and compares the inductor result against an independently computed eager result at the default float32 tolerance. Both runs add the two mms together, which cancels and leaves elements near zero, so the comparison rests entirely on `atol=1e-05` — `rtol` buys nothing at those magnitudes. The XPU float32 GEMM is not run-to-run bit-exact at this size: two back-to-back eager `x @ w` calls already differ by up to `1.5e-05`, which is the whole atol budget. Both results are equally accurate against a float64 reference (`1.46e-04` each), so neither side is wrong, and the mutation ordering the test actually checks is never involved. `x @ w` becomes bit-stable again under `torch.use_deterministic_algorithms(True)`, consistent with a GEMM that splits the reduction dimension by default. **Fix.** Draw that one case's inputs from small integers instead of `randn`, so the 1024-term dot products are exactly representable in float32 and any GEMM reproduces them bit-for-bit whatever order it accumulates in. The assertion keeps its tight tolerance. This is the idiom `test_index_put_as_masked_fill_mask_reads_target_by_extern_kernel` and `test_mutable_op_layout_copy_written_back_in_place` already use in the same file. Loosening the tolerance instead would also have worked, but exactness costs nothing here: a wrong mutation order changes elements by order of their own magnitude, not by `1e-05`. The other mm-bearing case, `foreach_reads_target_elsewhere`, is left alone: its single `x @ x.t()` keeps elements large enough for `rtol` to cover the same GEMM spread, and it passed 8 of 8 runs unmodified. **Verification.** 20/20 passes of the previously failing test, plus the full parametrized family green on cpu and xpu across all three generated suites (16 + 16 + 24 tests). `ruff 0.14.4` format and check are clean on the changed file.

### :robot: Agent fix run — `pytorch/pytorch#198709` **Outcome:** fix implemented and verified. Target repo: `pytorch`. Branch: `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-198709` (patch exported as a workflow artifact; nothing pushed). Target test: `test/dynamo/test_aot_compile.py::TestAOTCompile::test_load_then_compile_survives_baked_in_global_collision`, disabled for `xpu` by `pytorch/pytorch#198709`.
Reproduce Reproduced on this runner (BMG, `intel/omix:latest-devel-ubuntu26.04`) by pinning the torch build; the test is device-independent in its own right (CPU tensors, `backend="eager"`), so only the build changed between these rows. | torch build | python | `test_load_then_compile_...` | |---|---|---| | `2.15.0.dev20260926+xpu` (the build the disable was filed against) | 3.11 | FAIL - `AssertionError: Subprocess failure (KeyError: '__builtins__')`, traceback identical to the CI job | | `2.15.0.dev20260923+xpu` | 3.10 | PASS | | `2.16.0.dev20261015+xpu` | 3.11 | FAIL | | `2.16.0.dev20261016+xpu` and `2.16.0.dev20261017+xpu` | 3.11, 3.12 | PASS | The flip to green is `pytorch/pytorch#199169` ("Lazily load current stream argument", in main since the 2026-10-16 nightly), which stopped emitting the pregraph current-stream read when the graph does not use it. That masks the defect rather than fixing it - see below.
Root cause `GraphRuntimeEnv.forward_callable` (`torch/_dynamo/convert_frame.py`) builds an AOT artifact's generated `fn.__globals__` as a fresh dict from `import_sources`, `used_globals` and `extra_globals`. The capture path inherits a `__builtins__` binding from the traced frame through `extra_globals`; a **load** of a saved artifact has none, so the served function runs in a frame whose globals lack that key. CPython's `PyImport_Import` - which every C-level module import goes through, `PyImport_ImportModule` included - reads `__builtins__` out of the *calling* frame's globals with `PyObject_GetItem`, so a missing key is a `KeyError`, not a fallback to the interpreter builtins. On an accelerator host the artifact's pregraph bytecode calls `get_current_stream(torch.device('xpu', 0))`, whose `maybe_initialize_device` lazily imports `torch.xpu` from C - and that import raised out of the generated frame instead of the graph running. That is why only XPU CI saw it: `test/dynamo` otherwise runs on hosts with no accelerator, where no current-stream read is emitted. Disassembling the served artifact on the failing build put the raise at the `CALL` for `get_current_stream`, and the mechanism was then confirmed in isolation - calling that helper from a function built over a builtins-less globals dict raises `KeyError: '__builtins__'` on **today's** nightly too, so the defect is still live on main.
Fix and verification Seed the live builtins dict under `__builtins__` in `forward_callable`, before `types.FunctionType` caches the bytecode's builtins at creation. `setdefault`, not an unconditional write, so a binding the traced globals already supplied still wins. Plus a regression test that pins the binding on both the capture and the load path - asserted as the binding rather than as the original serve failure, because after `pytorch/pytorch#199169` nothing in the generated bytecode imports from C on its own. The change is Python-only, so it was verified by applying it to the installed nightly wheel (the patched hunk's context is identical to the committed tree); no C++ is involved and no source build was needed. | Check | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `test_load_then_compile_survives_baked_in_global_collision` on `2.16.0.dev20261015+xpu` | FAIL (`KeyError: '__builtins__'`) | PASS | | new `test_generated_function_globals_carry_the_live_builtins` on `2.16.0.dev20261017+xpu` | FAIL (`KeyError: '__builtins__'`) | PASS | | `test/dynamo/test_aot_compile.py` (whole file) | - | 342 passed, 5 skipped | | `test_package.py`, `test_precompile_package.py`, `test_precompile_context.py`, `test_streams.py` | - | each green run on its own; the four in one pytest process give the same 11 pre-existing failures with and without the fix |
Follow-ups for a human - Merging the PR for this patch with `Fixes #198709` (already in the commit message) closes the upstream issue and re-enables the test on XPU. - Worth a separate upstream change: `device_lazy_init` in `torch/csrc/utils/device_lazy_init.cpp` imports via `PyImport_ImportModule`. Switching it to `PyImport_ImportModuleLevelObject`, which ignores the caller's globals, would harden that caller on its own. Not folded in here - it needs a source build to verify and does not help the other C-level imports reachable from generated bytecode. - Nothing in intel/torch-xpu-ops needed changing; no skip-list entry here referenced this test.

🤖 Agent fix run — pytorch/pytorch#198709
Outcome: fix implemented and verified. Target repo: pytorch. Branch: agent/fix-pytorch-issue-198709 (patch exported as a workflow artifact; nothing pushed).
Target test: test/dynamo/test_aot_compile.py::TestAOTCompile::test_load_then_compile_survives_baked_in_global_collision, disabled for xpu by pytorch/pytorch#198709.

Reproduce
Reproduced on this runner (BMG, intel/omix:latest-devel-ubuntu26.04) by pinning the torch build; the test is device-independent in its own right (CPU tensors, backend="eager"), so only the build changed between these rows.



torch build
python
test_load_then_compile_...




2.15.0.dev20260926+xpu (the build the disable was filed against)
3.11
FAIL - AssertionError: Subprocess failure (KeyError: '__builtins__'), traceback identical to the CI job


2.15.0.dev20260923+xpu
3.10
PASS


2.16.0.dev20261015+xpu
3.11
FAIL


2.16.0.dev20261016+xpu and 2.16.0.dev20261017+xpu
3.11, 3.12
PASS



The flip to green is pytorch/pytorch#199169 ("Lazily load current stream argument", in main since the 2026-10-16 nightly), which stopped emitting the pregraph current-stream read when the graph does not use it. That masks the defect rather than fixing it - see below.


Root cause
GraphRuntimeEnv.forward_callable (torch/_dynamo/convert_frame.py) builds an AOT artifact's generated fn.__globals__ as a fresh dict from import_sources, used_globals and extra_globals. The capture path inherits a __builtins__ binding from the traced frame through extra_globals; a load of a saved artifact has none, so the served function runs in a frame whose globals lack that key.
CPython's PyImport_Import - which every C-level module import goes through, PyImport_ImportModule included - reads __builtins__ out of the calling frame's globals with PyObject_GetItem, so a missing key is a KeyError, not a fallback to the interpreter builtins. On an accelerator host the artifact's pregraph bytecode calls get_current_stream(torch.device('xpu', 0)), whose maybe_initialize_device lazily imports torch.xpu from C - and that import raised out of the generated frame instead of the graph running.
That is why only XPU CI saw it: test/dynamo otherwise runs on hosts with no accelerator, where no current-stream read is emitted. Disassembling the served artifact on the failing build put the raise at the CALL for get_current_stream, and the mechanism was then confirmed in isolation - calling that helper from a function built over a builtins-less globals dict raises KeyError: '__builtins__' on today's nightly too, so the defect is still live on main.


Fix and verification
Seed the live builtins dict under __builtins__ in forward_callable, before types.FunctionType caches the bytecode's builtins at creation. setdefault, not an unconditional write, so a binding the traced globals already supplied still wins. Plus a regression test that pins the binding on both the capture and the load path - asserted as the binding rather than as the original serve failure, because after pytorch/pytorch#199169 nothing in the generated bytecode imports from C on its own.
The change is Python-only, so it was verified by applying it to the installed nightly wheel (the patched hunk's context is identical to the committed tree); no C++ is involved and no source build was needed.

Before
After




test_load_then_compile_survives_baked_in_global_collision on 2.16.0.dev20261015+xpu
FAIL (KeyError: '__builtins__')
PASS


new test_generated_function_globals_carry_the_live_builtins on 2.16.0.dev20261017+xpu
FAIL (KeyError: '__builtins__')
PASS


test/dynamo/test_aot_compile.py (whole file)

342 passed, 5 skipped


test_package.py, test_precompile_package.py, test_precompile_context.py, test_streams.py
-
each green run on its own; the four in one pytest process give the same 11 pre-existing failures with and without the fix

Switching it to PyImport_ImportModuleLevelObject, which ignores the caller's globals, would harden that caller on its own. MultiTensorApplyCallableWrapper, ...>>(...)), 1, 1, ...> ``` The multi_tensor_apply kernels were ported to the SYCL free function kernel extension (intel/torch-xpu-ops#5203, landed 2026-10-15), which matches the last-good/first-bad window. The mechanism is the extension's host API, not anything torch-xpu-ops wrote. In `enqueue_functions.hpp`, `nd_launch(q, range, kernel_function, args...)` does **not** enqueue `Func` directly -- it submits a `parallel_for` over a lambda that calls `Func`, named by the wrapper type `detail::NdRangeFreeFunctionKernelWrapper<&Func, Dims, tag, Args...>`. That type, not the kernel, is what lands in the device image, so it is what PTI reports. Confirmed with a standalone DPC++ program reproducing the same submit shape: | Launch path | Kernel name in the device image | |---|---| | `nd_launch(q, range, kernel_function, ...)` (used when `SYCL_COMPILER_VERSION >= 20260100`) | `_ZTSN4sycl3_V13ext...NdRangeFreeFunctionKernelWrapperIXadL_Z...` | | `ext_oneapi_get_kernel()` then `nd_launch(q, range, kernel_obj, ...)` | `_ZN16__sycl_kernel_at6native3xpu25multi_tensor_apply_kernel...` | **Fix strategy.** Normalize the wrapper name back to the kernel it calls, and update the golden node. The file's own documented policy is to coerce platform-dependent kernel names into a stable form rather than record them verbatim, and it already collapses the template arguments of XPU functor kernels -- this follows that precedent and keeps the tree stable as the remaining kernels are ported. **Path not taken.** Fixing it in torch-xpu-ops by launching through a `sycl::kernel` from `ext_oneapi_get_kernel` (a real free function kernel launch, which keeps the kernel's own name) was rejected: it adds a kernel bundle lookup to every launch on a hot path shared by every ported kernel, and it still does not restore the old functor name. The multi_tensor_apply kernels were ported to the SYCL free function kernel
extension (#5203, landed 2026-10-15), which matches the
last-good/first-bad window.
The mechanism is the extension's host API, not anything torch-xpu-ops wrote.
In enqueue_functions.hpp, nd_launch(q, range, kernel_function<Func>, args...)
does not enqueue Func directly -- it submits a parallel_for over a lambda
that calls Func, named by the wrapper type
detail::NdRangeFreeFunctionKernelWrapper<&Func, Dims, tag, Args...>. That type,
not the kernel, is what lands in the device image, so it is what PTI reports.
Confirmed with a standalone DPC++ program reproducing the same submit shape:



Launch path
Kernel name in the device image




nd_launch(q, range, kernel_function<kptr>, ...) (used when SYCL_COMPILER_VERSION >= 20260100)
_ZTSN4sycl3_V13ext...NdRangeFreeFunctionKernelWrapperIXadL_Z...


ext_oneapi_get_kernel<kptr>() then nd_launch(q, range, kernel_obj, ...)
_ZN16__sycl_kernel_at6native3xpu25multi_tensor_apply_kernel...



Fix strategy. Normalize the wrapper name back to the kernel it calls, and
update the golden node. The file's own documented policy is to coerce
platform-dependent kernel names into a stable form rather than record them
verbatim, and it already collapses the template arguments of XPU functor
kernels -- this follows that precedent and keeps the tree stable as the
remaining kernels are ported.
Path not taken. Fixing it in torch-xpu-ops by launching through a
sycl::kernel from ext_oneapi_get_kernel (a real free function kernel launch,
which keeps the kernel's own name) was rejected: it adds a kernel bundle lookup
to every launch on a hot path shared by every ported kernel, and it still does
not restore the old functor name. See the follow-up note in the summary.



Implement Result
--- a/test/profiler/test_profiler_tree.py
+++ b/test/profiler/test_profiler_tree.py
@@ -240,6 +240,17 @@ class ProfilerTree:
         # whole operand type list rather than ending in an argument list.
         name = re.sub(r"^(at::native::xpu::\w+)<.+>$", r"\1<...>", name)
 
+        # An XPU kernel ported to the SYCL free function kernel extension is
+        # enqueued through a wrapper type that takes the kernel as a template
+        # argument, so the profiled name is the wrapper rather than the kernel.
+        # Name the kernel, so that porting a kernel does not rewrite the tree.
+        name = re.sub(
+            r"^sycl::\w+::ext::oneapi::experimental::detail::"
+            r"NdRangeFreeFunctionKernelWrapper<&\(\w+ (at::native::xpu::\w+)<.+>$",
+            r"\1<...>",
+            name,
+        )
+
         # HACK: this patches around the fact that PyBind11 improperly sets the
         # __qualname__ attribute on functions and methods; see
@@ -1222,7 +1233,7 @@ class TestProfilerTreeDevice(_TestProfilerTreeBase):
                     urEnqueueKernelLaunchWithArgsExp
-                      at::native::xpu::MultiTensorApplyKernelFunctor<...>
+                      at::native::xpu::multi_tensor_apply_kernel<...>
                     aten::empty



Verify
Source build, TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc, BMG runner, pytorch@783802cc +
torch-xpu-ops@eb0b9898.



Check
Before fix
After fix

FAIL (failures=1)
PASS


whole file test/profiler/test_profiler_tree.py
1 failed
17 passed, 8 skipped


lintrunner --take RUFF,PYFMT,FLAKE8 on the changed file

ok, no lint issues

python test/profiler/test_profiler_tree.py
lintrunner --take RUFF,PYFMT,FLAKE8 test/profiler/test_profiler_tree.py



Summary
One bug, one node. torch-xpu-ops ported the multi_tensor_apply kernels to the
SYCL free function kernel extension, and that extension's nd_launch enqueues
the kernel through a NdRangeFreeFunctionKernelWrapper lambda rather than
directly, so PTI reports the wrapper type instead of the kernel and the
expecttest golden tree in test/profiler/test_profiler_tree.py stopped
matching. The fix normalizes that wrapper name back to the kernel it calls and
updates the golden node, which also keeps the tree stable as the rest of the
port lands. Verified on a source build: the case fails before and passes after,
the whole file is green, and lint is clean.

Root cause `.to(torch.float16)` on an int64 XPU tensor reaches `copy_kernel`, which needs dynamic casting because the source dtype differs from the common dtype. The load goes through `c10::fetch_and_cast` and the store through `c10::cast_and_store`; both switch over *every* `ScalarType`, so their `Double` and `ComplexDouble` arms put FP64 instructions into the kernel even though neither tensor is FP64. GPUs without FP64 (TGL/ADL-class Iris Xe) are not AOT targets, so the kernel is JIT compiled from the SPIR-V image on first launch. The backend compiler rejects it and the failed program build surfaces as `UR error`. Compiling the copy kernel ahead-of-time for `tgllp` (Tiger Lake, the reporter's iGPU) reproduces it exactly, and 51 of its cast kernels are rejected this way — for every dtype, not just the FP64 ones: ``` [tgllp] error: in kernel '...CopyScalarFunc...LoadWithCast<1>...': Double type is not supported on this platform. ```
Fix FP64-free variants of the two cast helpers that keep the switch shape but compile the FP64 arms out, plus a `gpu_kernel_no_fp64_cast` entry point that selects them when no operand dtype is `Double`/`ComplexDouble`; `copy_kernel` uses it. SYCL splits device code per kernel by default (verified), so the FP64-free copy kernel forms its own device image and JIT compiles on a device without FP64. A genuine FP64 copy keeps the generic cast and still cannot run there, which is unavoidable. `-fsycl-fp64-conv-emu`, which the build already enables for dg2/ats-m, was checked first: the backend compiler does not accept it for gen12lp. **Two things a reviewer should weigh.** The specialization is opt-in per call site because it adds a second instantiation of the cast kernel — measured at +30% on the copy kernel's device object (21.8 MB to 28.4 MB for `bmg,pvc` plus SPIR-V), about 1% of `libtorch_xpu.so` for this one TU. So this is a **partial fix by design**: every reproducer on the upstream issue is a `.to()` / `.type()` call, but mixed-dtype elementwise ops still carry FP64 in their dynamic cast and still fail on such a device. Enabling it everywhere is a maintainer call on binary size. No test is added: the failure needs a GPU without FP64, and there is no compile-only test harness here to assert the absence of FP64 instructions.
Verification Source build of `pytorch` main (`14a29ad`) plus this branch, `TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc`, on BMG (`Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60`). **The bug** — kernel images the backend compiler accepts for `-device tgllp`: | | before | after | |---|---|---| | accepted | 378 | **418** | | rejected | 51 | 51 | The 40 new images are the FP64-free cast kernels, two per non-FP64 dtype; a `Long -> Half` copy now dispatches to one of them. The rejected set is unchanged because those are the generic instantiations, which only run when an operand really is FP64. **Non-regression** on BMG, since the new path now serves every non-FP64 copy: | Check | Result | |---|---| | 512 dtype/layout `.to()` combinations vs CPU | byte-identical to nightly `2.16.0.dev20261019+xpu`, including its 42 pre-existing floating-to-barebones-unsigned divergences | | `test_torch_xpu.py` | 867 passed, 103 skipped, 1 failed | | `test_tensor_creation_ops_xpu.py` | 682 passed, 59 skipped | | `test_binary_ufuncs_xpu.py` | 12794 passed, 638 skipped, 37 xfailed | | `test_complex_xpu.py` | 17 passed | | `test_ops_xpu.py -k "_to_copy or to_sparse or clone"` | 98 passed, 3 xfailed | The one failure, `test_cpp_warnings_have_python_context_xpu`, fails identically on the unmodified nightly wheel and asserts on a CPU warning message. No new failures.
Summary The XPU copy kernel's dynamic cast pulls `Double` and `ComplexDouble` arms into every mixed-dtype copy, so a `Long -> Half` `.to()` produces a kernel that Intel GPUs without FP64 cannot compile, which they report as `UR error`. The fix adds FP64-free variants of the two cast helpers and points `copy_kernel` at them whenever no operand dtype is FP64. Compiling the copy kernel for the reporter's Tiger Lake iGPU goes from 378 to 418 accepted kernel images, and on BMG a 512-combination dtype matrix plus five test suites are byte-identical to the nightly wheel. It is a partial fix by design — mixed-dtype elementwise ops other than copy still carry FP64, and extending the specialization to them costs device object size, so that call is left to a maintainer. - **Branch:** `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-149953` - **Base:** `36aa23949e41c7909f86bd5ce45829f9f3fe0132` - **Changed files:** `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.cpp`, `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/DynamicCastNoFP64.h`, `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ElementwiseInvoke.h`, `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/Loops.h`, `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/MemoryAccessUtils.h` - **Nothing was pushed.** The patch is exported as a workflow artifact for a human to review and apply.
_Generated by [fix job]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:39396469216])._
Review Copy into a new comment, keep ONE verdict, add a note. Two verdicts in one comment are dropped as ambiguous. ``` **strong-accepted** **weak-accepted** **weak-rejected** **strong-rejected** **issue-drop** notes: ``` On a batch run add `item=` to say which sub-item the verdict is about, **in the bold text and in the marker** -- the marker is invisible, so the bold line is all a reader sees. One comment per sub-item, since a bare verdict on a batch does not say which test it means and is dropped. `run=` only when judging a run other than the newest, in both places too. A CI DISABLED sub-item, `item=` from the fan-out table: ``` **strong-accepted item=197334** notes: same TensorAssign overload as upstream CUDA, fp8 dispatch list matches ``` Another sub-item of the same batch, judged on an earlier run: ``` **weak-rejected run=35171979678 item=197335** notes: green only because the test is skipped, the kernel still lacks fp8 ``` An `[xpu-alignment]` issue that should not have been filed -- one issue per difference, so no `item=`: ``` **issue-drop** notes: accepted XPU/CUDA numerics difference, nothing to repair ```

Automated fix session for the DISABLED test tracked by `pytorch/pytorch#201542` (`ComboKernelDynamicShapesTests::test_dynamic_shapes_activations_no_autotune`, platform `xpu`), triggered from this tracking issue.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | pytorch | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Upstream disable issue: `pytorch/pytorch#201542` — DISABLED `test_dynamic_shapes_activations_no_autotune (__main__.ComboKernelDynamicShapesTests)`, first seen on commit `b8449a4af2a7e16496e5f724b0789bc061d0f558` ([xpu.yml run]([运行记录：pytorch/pytorch@run:39310665366])). This tracking issue is only the queue, so the fix branch is named after the upstream issue. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Runner is BMG (`Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics`); the failing CI shard ran on a PVC card (`dut7363_pvc_card_4`, `Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100`, `linux.idc.xpu`). Checked against nightly `2.16.0.dev20261019+xpu` with the test file from pytorch `origin/main@bf90d4e1`. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_dynamic_shapes_activations_no_autotune` | NOT_REPRODUCED on BMG | passes standalone, with its class, and with the whole file (179 passed / 25 skipped) | | same, PVC CI job log | FAILED CONSISTENTLY | `AssertionError: Scalars are not equal! Expected 1 but got 3` at the `async_compile.triton(` count | The CI job log for `pytorch/pytorch` run 39310665366 is still available and shows the test failing deterministically (3 reruns, plus 3 more in the isolated retry step), so it is a hard PVC-only divergence rather than flakiness in that run. The failure signature itself was reproduced locally -- see the Root Cause block. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause **Target repository:** `pytorch` (`test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py`), analyzed at `bf90d4e14dcdd39a4319a90eab8ddaecf29ebee6`. `ComboKernelDynamicShapesTests.setUp` enables `benchmark_combo_kernel`, so whether the three activations are horizontally fused is decided at compile time by `Scheduler.speedup_by_combo_kernel`, which benchmarks each sub-kernel and the combo kernel on the actual device. The test then asserts the generated wrapper contains exactly one `async_compile.triton(` call -- i.e. that the benchmark accepted the fusion. Everything else feeding that decision is device-independent (the partitioning heuristics in `triton_combo_kernel._default_custom_combo_kernel_horizontal_partition` and `_base_horizontal_partition`, the grouping callback, and the `combo_kernel_*` thresholds, all pinned by `setUp`). The benchmark is the only hardware-dependent input, and it declines fusion whenever a sub-kernel scores `inf` (`n_spills > 8`, or an in-process compile failure) or the measured combo time loses to the sum of the stand-alone kernels. A declined fusion emits the three sub-kernels as ordinary Triton kernels, which is exactly `got 3`. The verdict is memoised in a `.kernel_perf` file under the inductor cache dir, which is why the CI retries kept failing identically. Confirmed locally on BMG: with the real benchmark the decision is `True` by a wide margin (`ms1 = 0.0138`, `ms2 - ms2_clone = -0.051`) and the count is 1; forcing the sub-kernel benchmark to score `inf` -- the hardware-dependent branch -- flips the decision to `False` and the count to 3, reproducing the CI assertion exactly. **Fix strategy:** pin the fusion decision for this test instead of letting a runtime benchmark gate a codegen-shape assertion, the same way `pytorch/pytorch#196217` already did for `test_benchmark_combo_kernel_emits_real_num_gb` in this file after `pytorch/pytorch#195976`. The test's subject is `combo_kernels_autotune = 0` codegen, not fusion profitability. *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result ```diff --- a/test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py +++ b/test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py @@ -2130,10 +2130,16 @@ class ComboKernelDynamicShapesTests(TestCase): ] out_eager = test_activations(*inps) - out_compiled, code = run_and_get_code(torch.compile(test_activations), *inps) + # setUp enables benchmark_combo_kernel, so the fusion is gated on a + # device benchmark; pin it so the kernel count below cannot be decided + # by benchmark noise or a cached inf from a spilling sub-kernel. + with patch.object(Scheduler, "speedup_by_combo_kernel", return_value=True): + out_compiled, code = run_and_get_code( + torch.compile(test_activations), *inps + ) self.assertEqual(out_eager, out_compiled) self.assertEqual(sum(s.count("async_compile.triton(") for s in code), 1) ``` `patch` and `Scheduler` are already imported at module scope, so no new imports. The subclass `ComboKernelDynamicShapesTestsPerSubkernelBlocks` inherits the method and is covered by the same change. *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verify The CI failure is PVC-only and this runner is BMG, so the hardware-dependent input was emulated: `Scheduler.benchmark_codegened_module` forced to score `inf`, which is the branch that makes `speedup_by_combo_kernel` decline the fusion. | Case | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `test_dynamic_shapes_activations_no_autotune`, emulated PVC verdict | FAIL -- `AssertionError: Scalars are not equal! Expected 1 but got 3.` | PASS | | same, real benchmark on BMG | PASS | PASS | | whole `test_combo_kernels.py` | 179 passed, 25 skipped | 179 passed, 25 skipped | `ruff format --diff` and `ruff check` (pinned `ruff==0.14.4`) are clean on the changed file. The "before" column reproduces the CI assertion verbatim, so the fix removes the exact mechanism that failed. Confirmation on PVC hardware is still outstanding -- it is not available on this runner. *Automated by fix-verify.*
Summary **Outcome:** IMPLEMENTING(fix_verified) `ComboKernelDynamicShapesTests::test_dynamic_shapes_activations_no_autotune` asserts that the three activations are emitted as a single combo kernel, but `setUp` leaves `benchmark_combo_kernel` on, so that outcome is decided by a device benchmark in `Scheduler.speedup_by_combo_kernel`; on the PVC CI card the benchmark declines the fusion, three standalone Triton kernels are emitted, and the verdict is cached in a `.kernel_perf` file so every retry fails the same way. The fix pins the fusion decision for this test, the same way `pytorch/pytorch#196217` did for `test_benchmark_combo_kernel_emits_real_num_gb` in this file, leaving the `combo_kernels_autotune = 0` codegen path the test actually covers untouched. Verification forced the hardware-dependent branch on BMG: before the change the test fails with the CI assertion verbatim, after it passes, and the whole file is unchanged at 179 passed / 25 skipped. - **Branch:** `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201542` (in a `pytorch/pytorch` checkout) - **Base:** `bf90d4e14dcdd39a4319a90eab8ddaecf29ebee6` - **Changed files:** `test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py` - **Caveat:** final confirmation needs a run on PVC (`linux.idc.xpu`); this runner is BMG. - **Nothing was pushed.** The patch is exported as a workflow artifact for a human to review and apply.

One comment per sub-item, since a bare verdict on a batch does not say which test it means and is dropped. `run=` only when judging a run other than the newest, in both places too.
