Automated fix session for the DISABLED upstream test reported in [this comment]([地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#5272]). Upstream disable issue: `pytorch/pytorch#201710`. **Outcome:** IMPLEMENTING(fix_verified) -- fix committed on `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201710`.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | pytorch | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Sub-item handled by this session: 1. `test_tma_with_customer_kernel_options_selection_backend_TRITON_xpu` (`TestFlexAttentionXPU`, `test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py`) -- `pytorch/pytorch#201710` *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce The latest XPU nightly (`2.16.0.dev20261021+xpu`, built from `ea870f7f`) **passes** all six subtests, so the fast path reported no failure. A source build of `origin/main` (`e149fba40596a8181f44e1f318da5fa10d609118`) on this BMG runner reproduces the CI failure exactly -- same four subtests, same assertion. The nightly simply predates the inductor change that causes it (see Root Cause), so this is a recency gap, not a PVC-vs-BMG difference. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_tma_with_customer_kernel_options_selection_backend_TRITON_xpu` | REPRODUCED | `AssertionError: Regex didn't match: '\\bload_checked_2d\\(\\s*Q\\s*,'` | The four failing subtests are exactly the pointer-path cases -- `{'USE_TMA': False}`, `{'USE_TMA': 0}`, `{'USE_TMA': None}` and `{'USE_TMA': True, 'fwd_USE_TMA': False}` -- matching the [failing job]([运行记录：pytorch/pytorch@run:39702803134]) one for one. The two descriptor-path subtests pass in both places. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@e149fba405`. The test matches generated Triton source for the pointer-load fallback with `_pointer_load_pattern` (`test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py:882-885`), which hardcodes the helper name: `rf"\bload_checked_2d\(\s*{operand.upper()}\s*,"`. The pointer arm of the forward template emits exactly that call -- `q = load_checked_2d(Q, offs_m, ...)` at `torch/_inductor/kernel/flex/templates/flex_attention.py.jinja:135` -- but the python wrapper no longer splices the kernel source verbatim. `emit_triton_kernel_definition` runs it through `_rename_kernel_module_globals` (`torch/_inductor/codegen/wrapper.py:4510`, defined at `:829-873`), which suffixes every top-level `def` in a kernel with that kernel's name so two kernels defining the same `@triton.jit` helper cannot shadow each other at module scope. The generated call is therefore `load_checked_2d_triton_tem_fused__to_copy_flex_attention_ones_sum_zeros_4(Q, ...)` and the regex no longer matches. The descriptor pattern is unaffected because `tl.load_tensor_descriptor(desc_q, ...)` is a Triton builtin applied to a kernel-local variable, which is why exactly the four pointer-path subtests fail while the two descriptor-path ones pass. The failure is new because `PythonWrapperCodegen.defines_triton_kernels_as_code()` was flipped to `return True` (`torch/_inductor/codegen/wrapper.py:4523-4524`) by `pytorch/pytorch#200502`, which landed, was reverted, and re-landed as `3d3485473d` on 2026-10-21. Before the flip the wrapper bound kernels through `async_compile.triton('''''')` and the helper kept its plain name. The latest XPU nightly is built from `ea870f7f`, which predates the flip, which is why the nightly passes and `88fe47d13a` in CI does not. The pointer-path assertions are gated `@skipIfRocm` and `@skipCUDAIf(not has_triton_tma_device())` (`test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py:8219-8227`), and the CUDA arm of `has_triton_tma_device()` requires compute capability 9.0 or newer (`torch/utils/_triton.py:150-160`), so the XPU lane is where this fires in CI. Re-running with `TORCHINDUCTOR_FORCE_DISABLE_CACHES=1` reproduces identically, so it is not stale-cache pollution. The fix is a test-side expectation update: the per-kernel suffix is deliberate (see `test/inductor/test_module_level_kernels.py:320-324`, `test_same_named_helpers_do_not_shadow`, which asserts the generated module has no duplicate top-level defs), so the pattern must tolerate it rather than the renaming being reverted. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- test expectation is stale against a deliberate inductor codegen change - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** inductor *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Analyzed at:** pytorch@e149fba405 - **What I changed:** `test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py` -- `_pointer_load_pattern` now accepts the per-kernel name suffix (1 regex line, plus 3 comment lines explaining why). - **Why:** the helper call the pattern looks for is renamed to `load_checked_2d_` by `_rename_kernel_module_globals` (`torch/_inductor/codegen/wrapper.py:829-873`), so `\w*` after the base name matches both the module-level form and the plain name the string-form wrappers (C++, FX) still emit. - **Skip added:** no - **Ready for verify:** yes ```diff --- a/test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py +++ b/test/inductor/test_flex_attention.py @@ -881,8 +881,10 @@ def _descriptor_load_pattern(operand): def _pointer_load_pattern(operand): # load_checked_2d is defined unconditionally in every generated kernel, so - # only an operand-qualified call establishes the fallback. - return rf"\bload_checked_2d\(\s*{operand.upper()}\s*," + # only an operand-qualified call establishes the fallback. A module-level + # kernel suffixes every top-level def with the kernel name to keep it unique + # in the wrapper's namespace, so the call carries that suffix too. + return rf"\bload_checked_2d\w*\(\s*{operand.upper()}\s*," def _check_int64_decode_narrows_coordinates( ``` *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verify Both columns come from the same source build of pytorch `origin/main@e149fba405` (`TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc`) on this Arc Pro B60 (Battlemage) host; the only difference is the one-line test change, so the A/B is attributable to the fix. The change is python-only, so no rebuild was needed between the two runs. Inductor caches were disabled (`TORCHINDUCTOR_FORCE_DISABLE_CACHES=1`) for both. | Test case | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `TestFlexAttentionXPU::test_tma_with_customer_kernel_options_selection_backend_TRITON_xpu` | FAIL | PASS | `Before` was `AssertionError: Regex didn't match: '\bload_checked_2d\(\s*Q\s*,'` on the four pointer-path subtests (`4 failed, 1 passed, 2 subtests passed`); after, `1 passed, 6 subtests passed`. Regression checks on the fixed build: | Suite | Result | |---|---| | `test_flex_attention.py -k "tma_with_customer_kernel_options or tdm_flex"` | 4 passed, 35 skipped, 12 subtests passed | The 35 skips are the `TestFlexAttentionTDMEndToEnd` cases behind the gfx1250 hardware gate; they do not run on XPU. - **Verdict:** PASSED -- the pointer-path assertions match the module-level kernel's generated call - **Lint:** clean (`lintrunner` on the changed file, no autofixes needed) *Automated by fix-verify.*
Summary The disabled test asserts on generated Triton source to distinguish flex attention's TMA descriptor path from its pointer fallback, and its pointer pattern hardcoded the helper name `load_checked_2d(`. Since `pytorch/pytorch#200502` made the python wrapper define Triton kernels at module level, every top-level `def` in a kernel is suffixed with that kernel's name so same-named helpers in different kernels cannot shadow each other, so the generated call is `load_checked_2d_(Q, ...)` and the four subtests that expect the pointer path stopped matching. no longer splices the kernel source verbatim. emit_triton_kernel_definition runs it through

generated call is therefore

What the CI failure actually is From the referenced `xpu.yml` run (commit `30f2f72b`, job `linux-noble-xpu-n-py3.11 / test (default, 4, 12)`), the assertion that fails is the gradient check at the end of `MapTests._run_test`: ``` File "test/inductor/test_control_flow.py", line 2553, in _run_test self.assertEqual(param.grad, model_compiled_params[name].grad) AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close! Mismatched elements: 1 / 5 (20.0%) Greatest absolute difference: 0.13075685501098633 at index (4,) (up to 1e-05 allowed) ``` Five elements means `linear.bias`, so the compiled backward produces a wrong bias gradient. The magnitude is not a tolerance problem, and it is not stable: the two reruns in the same job reported `0.1089...e1` (`1.0899319648742676`) while the recorded failure reported `0.1307...`, i.e. the wrong value changes run to run. Within the same CI run, 7 of the 8 variants of this test pass -- only `cpp_wrapper=True` **and** `dynamic=True` **and** `autograd=True` fails. The plain `MapTests` (python wrapper) version of the identical parametrisation passes, and there is no equivalent disable issue for the CUDA device.
Why it could not be reproduced here CI runs this shard on `dut7900_pvc_card_0`, an **Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100** (PVC). This fix job runs on `xpu-agent`, an **Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60** (BMG). On BMG against the nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261022+xpu` the test passes every time: - the upstream test itself, standalone: `ok (30.468s)` - all 8 `MapTestsCppWrapper::test_map_pytree_in_out` variants, 3 consecutive runs: `8 passed` each time - a standalone reproducer of the same model/loss over 9 random seeds and 6 input shapes (including shapes large enough to change the reduction tiling): no gradient mismatch beyond float accumulation noise - the same reproducer with `max_autotune_pointwise` and with `coordinate_descent_tuning` forced on: clean A source build was not attempted because it cannot change the answer here: the `torch/_inductor` delta between the nightly's source (`b40a4f2c`) and the CI commit (`30f2f72b`) is limited to `UserDefinedTritonKernel`'s `restore_value`/`reset_to_zero` plumbing and memory-pool size-expression flattening, and this test uses neither. The remaining variable is the GPU (and its driver/IGC stack), which a rebuild does not move.
Where a human should look Inspecting the generated cpp-wrapper backward on BMG: the mapped region is lowered to a `while_loop`, and the bias gradient is produced inside the loop body by `triton_red_fused_add_copy__cos_mul_reshape_select_sum_5`. That kernel is a read-modify-write on `in_out_ptr0` (it reloads the `mm` result to recompute `cos(bias + linear(x))`) and it writes the loop-carried accumulator `out_ptr1` at offset `5*u2`; both buffers are in `mutated_arg_names`, and the kernel is marked `optimize_mem`. So the first loop iteration is the one that both autotunes and executes it, through `runTritonKernelWithAutotune`. As emitted on BMG that code is correct -- the indices are right and the first invocation returns early rather than launching the kernel a second time -- which is why a plain re-read of the codegen does not explain the failure. The suspicious remainder is how a mutating, in-loop reduction is protected while it is being benchmarked (`copy_args_to_cpu_if_needed` takes the CPU-restore path rather than cloning once the allocator budget is exhausted), since the configuration set being benchmarked is exactly what differs between PVC and BMG. Confirming that needs the failure in hand. **Suggested next step:** re-run this job on `xpu-agent-pvc`. The single-test command is ``` PYTHONPATH=/test python3 /test/inductor/test_control_flow.py -v \ MapTestsCppWrapper.test_map_pytree_in_out_device_xpu_dynamic_True_autograd_True ```

A rebuild would not have helped either, since the inductor delta between the nightly wheel and the CI commit does not touch any path this test uses. Automated fix session for the bug tracked by this issue, filed upstream as `pytorch/pytorch#200666`. Follow progress in the [workflow run]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:39910414134]).
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | pytorch | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Upstream bug: `pytorch/pytorch#200666` -- several `test/test_xpu.py` tests fail only when run after `TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices`, and only on Python 3.15. Reproducer given in the upstream issue: ``` pytest -q test/test_xpu.py::TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices test/test_xpu.py::TestXpu::test_mem_get_info ``` The `level_zero backend failed with error: 54` string in the upstream log is a symptom of lost process environment, not a driver-side dependency, so no runtime dependency is recorded. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261022+xpu` (cp315) under CPython 3.15.1 installed via `uv`, pytorch test file from `origin/main@fed346df`, on this BMG runner (Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics, 8 devices). | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices` destroys the process environment | REPRODUCED | `ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN` goes from `'1'` to unset across the test on CPython 3.15.1, and is preserved on 3.12.15 | | `TestXpu::test_mem_get_info` run after `TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices` | NOT REPRODUCIBLE HERE | both tests pass on BMG; the reported `RuntimeError ... doesn't support querying the available free memory` needs PVC | The symptom in the upstream report is hardware-gated, so it was reproduced one level down, at the defect itself. `c10/xpu/XPUCachingAllocator.h:23` gates `mem_get_info()` on `sycl::aspect::ext_intel_free_memory`; on PVC the Level Zero adapter only reports that aspect while `ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN` is set in the process environment, so losing the variable makes every later call raise. On this BMG runner the aspect is reported independently of `ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN` -- verified directly: wiping the environment and then calling `mem_get_info()` still returns `(25446047744, 25669140480)`. The reproducer therefore plants `ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN` natively via `setenv()` (the way the Level Zero adapter does, invisibly to `os.environ`), runs `test_parse_visible_devices`, and asserts the variable survived. That is the exact state loss the PVC failures are caused by, and it is device-independent. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@fed346df`. `test/test_xpu.py:274` wraps the call under test in `patch.dict(os.environ, {"ZE_AFFINITY_MASK": val}, clear=True)`. `unittest.mock._patch_dict._unpatch_dict` restores the mapping by calling `_clear_dict(in_dict)` -- i.e. `os.environ.clear()` -- and then `in_dict.update(original)`. CPython 3.15 added an `os._Environ.clear` override whose body is `_clearenv(); self._data.clear()`; before 3.15 there was no override, so `MutableMapping.clear` removed only the keys Python itself knew about, one `unsetenv` at a time. Under 3.15 the `clearenv()` call wipes the real process environment wholesale, and `in_dict.update(original)` can only put back the keys recorded in `os.environ`. Any variable set natively through `setenv()` after interpreter start-up is gone for good -- including `ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN`, which the Level Zero adapter plants during XPU runtime initialization and which `sycl::aspect::ext_intel_free_memory` is re-derived from on every free-memory query. That is why the failures are order-dependent, why they are all memory queries, and why they only appear on 3.15. `clear=True` is not the deciding factor: `_unpatch_dict` calls `.clear()` on the restore path whatever `clear` was set to, so `patch.dict` on `os.environ` is unsafe on 3.15 in general. The fix is to stop patching the whole mapping and set/restore just `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK`, which is the only variable `torch.xpu._parse_visible_devices` reads (`torch/xpu/__init__.py:105`). Same conclusion, and essentially the same patch, as the already-open upstream draft `pytorch/pytorch#200669` -- see the Summary. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- test-side environment handling, fixable in place. - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Analyzed at:** pytorch@fed346df - **What I changed:** `test/test_xpu.py` -- `test_parse_visible_devices` now sets and restores `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` itself (+13/-2) instead of wrapping the call in `patch.dict(os.environ, ..., clear=True)`; the module-level `from unittest.mock import patch` import became unused and was dropped (the other `mock` uses in the file are fully qualified, and the `patch` import at line 541 lives inside an embedded subprocess script string). - **Why:** `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` is the only variable `torch.xpu._parse_visible_devices` reads (`torch/xpu/__init__.py:105`), so patching the entire mapping was never needed, and under CPython 3.15 the restore path's `os.environ.clear()` is what destroys `ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN`. - **Skip added:** no - **Ready for verify:** yes ```diff @@ -19,7 +19,6 @@ import unittest import warnings from copy import deepcopy from itertools import product -from unittest.mock import patch import torch import torch.multiprocessing as mp @@ -271,8 +270,20 @@ class TestXpu(TestCase): def test_parse_visible_devices(self): def _parse_visible_devices(val, strict=False): - with patch.dict(os.environ, {"ZE_AFFINITY_MASK": val}, clear=True): + # Set and restore ZE_AFFINITY_MASK by hand. mock.patch.dict(os.environ) + # is unusable here: it restores via os.environ.clear(), which on + # Python 3.15 calls clearenv() and so drops variables the XPU runtime + # set natively (ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN), breaking every later + # mem_get_info(). See pytorch/pytorch#200666. + prev = os.environ.get("ZE_AFFINITY_MASK") + os.environ["ZE_AFFINITY_MASK"] = val + try: return torch.xpu._parse_visible_devices(strict=strict) + finally: + if prev is None: + del os.environ["ZE_AFFINITY_MASK"] + else: + os.environ["ZE_AFFINITY_MASK"] = prev # Tokens with trailing non-numeric characters are invalid; entire list is rejected self.assertEqual(_parse_visible_devices("1a, 2b"), []) ``` *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verify No build needed -- the change is test-only. Verified against nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261022+xpu` (cp315) under CPython 3.15.1 on this BMG runner, with the test file taken straight from the fix branch; baseline and fixed runs differ only by `test/test_xpu.py`. | Test case | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices` leaves the process environment intact (CPython 3.15.1) | FAIL | PASS | | `TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices` then `TestXpu::test_mem_get_info` (CPython 3.15.1, BMG) | PASS | PASS | | `TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices` leaves the process environment intact (CPython 3.12.15) | PASS | PASS | `Before` was `ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN` going from `'1'` to unset across the test on CPython 3.15.1 -- the state loss that makes later `mem_get_info()` calls raise `RuntimeError: ... doesn't support querying the available free memory` on PVC. The two rows that already passed are controls: they confirm the change is a no-op on hardware where the aspect does not depend on sysman, and on pre-3.15 Python. Regression checks on the fixed build: | Suite | Result | |---|---| | `test_xpu.py`, CPython 3.15.1, baseline | 9 failed, 188 passed, 6 skipped, 3 xfailed | | `test_xpu.py`, CPython 3.15.1, with fix | 9 failed, 188 passed, 6 skipped, 3 xfailed | The two failure sets are identical name-for-name. All 9 are pre-existing on this runner and unrelated: missing `ninja` for C++ extension tests, CPython 3.15 `forkserver` behaviour in `test_lazy_init` / `test_wrong_xpu_fork`, a `_xpu_sleep` signature skew between the nightly wheel and the `main` test file, and the sysman device-info tests. - **Verdict:** PASSED -- the reproducer flips FAIL to PASS and the suite is unchanged otherwise. - **Lint:** clean (`pyfmt_linter.py` and `ruff_linter.py` adapters on `test/test_xpu.py`) *Automated by fix-verify.*
Summary > [!IMPORTANT] > **An equivalent fix is already open upstream as a draft PR by the issue > reporter.** Please review and land that PR rather than opening a duplicate from > this patch; the patch artifact here is a fallback if that PR stalls. Search > `pytorch/pytorch` for the open draft titled "[xpu] Do not use > patch.dict(os.environ) in test_parse_visible_devices of test/test_xpu.py" > (`pytorch/pytorch#200669`). One bug, one line: `TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices` set `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK` through `patch.dict(os.environ, ..., clear=True)`, and `unittest.mock` restores such a patch by calling `os.environ.clear()` and re-adding the keys it saved. CPython 3.15 added an `os._Environ.clear` override that calls `clearenv()`, so that restore now wipes the entire process environment and cannot put back `ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN`, which the Level Zero adapter sets natively during XPU initialization and which `sycl::aspect::ext_intel_free_memory` is re-derived from on every free-memory query -- hence the order-dependent `mem_get_info()` failures across `test/test_xpu.py`, only on Python 3.15, only on devices that need sysman for that aspect. Upstream bug: pytorch/pytorch#200666 -- several test/test_xpu.py tests fail only
when run after TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices, and only on Python 3.15.
Reproducer given in the upstream issue:
pytest -q test/test_xpu.py::TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices test/test_xpu.py::TestXpu::test_mem_get_info

The level_zero backend failed with error: 54 string in the upstream log is a
symptom of lost process environment, not a driver-side dependency, so no runtime
dependency is recorded.
Automated by issue-triage.



Reproduce
Nightly wheel 2.16.0.dev20261022+xpu (cp315) under CPython 3.15.1 installed via
uv, pytorch test file from origin/main@fed346df, on this BMG runner
(Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics, 8 devices).



Test case
Verdict
Observed




TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices destroys the process environment
REPRODUCED
ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN goes from '1' to unset across the test on CPython 3.15.1, and is preserved on 3.12.15


TestXpu::test_mem_get_info run after TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices
NOT REPRODUCIBLE HERE
both tests pass on BMG; the reported RuntimeError ... doesn't support querying the available free memory needs PVC



The symptom in the upstream report is hardware-gated, so it was reproduced one
level down, at the defect itself. c10/xpu/XPUCachingAllocator.h:23 gates
mem_get_info() on sycl::aspect::ext_intel_free_memory; on PVC the Level Zero
adapter only reports that aspect while ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN is set in the process
environment, so losing the variable makes every later call raise. On this BMG
runner the aspect is reported independently of ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN -- verified
directly: wiping the environment and then calling mem_get_info() still
returns (25446047744, 25669140480). The reproducer therefore plants
ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN natively via setenv() (the way the Level Zero adapter does,
invisibly to os.environ), runs test_parse_visible_devices, and asserts the
variable survived. That is the exact state loss the PVC failures are caused by,
and it is device-independent.
Automated by fix-reproduce.



Root Cause
Analyzed at pytorch origin/main@fed346df.
test/test_xpu.py:274 wraps the call under test in
patch.dict(os.environ, {"ZE_AFFINITY_MASK": val}, clear=True).
unittest.mock._patch_dict._unpatch_dict restores the mapping by calling
_clear_dict(in_dict) -- i.e. os.environ.clear() -- and then
in_dict.update(original). CPython 3.15 added an os._Environ.clear override
whose body is _clearenv(); self._data.clear(); before 3.15 there was no
override, so MutableMapping.clear removed only the keys Python itself knew
about, one unsetenv at a time. Under 3.15 the clearenv() call wipes the real
process environment wholesale, and in_dict.update(original) can only put back
the keys recorded in os.environ. Any variable set natively through setenv()
after interpreter start-up is gone for good -- including ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN,
which the Level Zero adapter plants during XPU runtime initialization and which
sycl::aspect::ext_intel_free_memory is re-derived from on every free-memory
query. That is why the failures are order-dependent, why they are all memory
queries, and why they only appear on 3.15.
clear=True is not the deciding factor: _unpatch_dict calls .clear() on the
restore path whatever clear was set to, so patch.dict on os.environ is
unsafe on 3.15 in general. The fix is to stop patching the whole mapping and
set/restore just ZE_AFFINITY_MASK, which is the only variable
torch.xpu._parse_visible_devices reads (torch/xpu/__init__.py:105).
Same conclusion, and essentially the same patch, as the already-open upstream
draft pytorch/pytorch#200669 -- see the Summary.

Verdict: IMPLEMENTING -- test-side environment handling, fixable in place.
Target repo: pytorch
Domain: upstream-pytorch

Automated by fix-root-cause.



Implement Result

Target repo: pytorch
Analyzed at: pytorch@fed346df
What I changed: test/test_xpu.py -- test_parse_visible_devices now sets and restores ZE_AFFINITY_MASK itself (+13/-2) instead of wrapping the call in patch.dict(os.environ, ..., clear=True); the module-level from unittest.mock import patch import became unused and was dropped (the other mock uses in the file are fully qualified, and the patch import at line 541 lives inside an embedded subprocess script string).
Why: ZE_AFFINITY_MASK is the only variable torch.xpu._parse_visible_devices reads (torch/xpu/__init__.py:105), so patching the entire mapping was never needed, and under CPython 3.15 the restore path's os.environ.clear() is what destroys ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN.
Skip added: no
Ready for verify: yes

@@ -19,7 +19,6 @@ import unittest
 import warnings
 from copy import deepcopy
 from itertools import product
-from unittest.mock import patch
 
 import torch
 import torch.multiprocessing as mp
@@ -271,8 +270,20 @@ class TestXpu(TestCase):
 
     def test_parse_visible_devices(self):
         def _parse_visible_devices(val, strict=False):
-            with patch.dict(os.environ, {"ZE_AFFINITY_MASK": val}, clear=True):
+            # Set and restore ZE_AFFINITY_MASK by hand. mock.patch.dict(os.environ)
+            # is unusable here: it restores via os.environ.clear(), which on
+            # Python 3.15 calls clearenv() and so drops variables the XPU runtime
+            # set natively (ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN), breaking every later
+            # mem_get_info(). See pytorch/pytorch#200666.
+            prev = os.environ.get("ZE_AFFINITY_MASK")
+            os.environ["ZE_AFFINITY_MASK"] = val
+            try:
                 return torch.xpu._parse_visible_devices(strict=strict)
+            finally:
+                if prev is None:
+                    del os.environ["ZE_AFFINITY_MASK"]
+                else:
+                    os.environ["ZE_AFFINITY_MASK"] = prev
 
         # Tokens with trailing non-numeric characters are invalid; entire list is rejected
         self.assertEqual(_parse_visible_devices("1a, 2b"), [])

Automated by fix-verify.



Summary

[!IMPORTANT]
An equivalent fix is already open upstream as a draft PR by the issue
reporter. Please review and land that PR rather than opening a duplicate from
this patch; the patch artifact here is a fallback if that PR stalls. Search
pytorch/pytorch for the open draft titled "[xpu] Do not use
patch.dict(os.environ) in test_parse_visible_devices of test/test_xpu.py"
(pytorch/pytorch#200669).

One bug, one line: TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices set ZE_AFFINITY_MASK
through patch.dict(os.environ, ..., clear=True), and unittest.mock restores
such a patch by calling os.environ.clear() and re-adding the keys it saved.
CPython 3.15 added an os._Environ.clear override that calls clearenv(), so
that restore now wipes the entire process environment and cannot put back
ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN, which the Level Zero adapter sets natively during XPU
initialization and which sycl::aspect::ext_intel_free_memory is re-derived from
on every free-memory query -- hence the order-dependent mem_get_info() failures
across test/test_xpu.py, only on Python 3.15, only on devices that need sysman
for that aspect. The fix sets and restores just ZE_AFFINITY_MASK, the only
variable torch.xpu._parse_visible_devices reads. Verification flips the

failures); the upstream report's PVC symptom is not reproducible on this BMG
runner, so the defect was reproduced one level down, at the environment loss
itself, which is hardware-independent.

The failure is Python-version dependent, so reproduction needed a Python 3.15 environment built specifically for this run: - Python 3.15.1 (uv-managed) + nightly wheel `torch 2.16.0.dev20261022+xpu` (cp315 manylinux) - pytorch test tree at `fed346df557d144bc8a48f2a018ca2403fcdb7e7` Refined command: ``` pytest -q test/test_xpu.py::TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices \ test/test_xpu.py::TestXpu::test_mem_get_info ``` Result before any change: ``` FAILED test_xpu.py::TestXpu::test_mem_get_info - RuntimeError: The device (Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100) doesn't support querying the available free memory. 1 failed, 1 passed ``` The same command on the repo's default Python 3.12 environment passes, matching the reporter's observation that the failure is specific to Python 3.15.
Root Cause | Field | Value | |---|---| | Target repository | `pytorch` (`test/test_xpu.py`) | | Domain | test infrastructure / XPU runtime environment | | Analyzed sha | `fed346df557d144bc8a48f2a018ca2403fcdb7e7` | | Verdict | IMPLEMENTING | `test_parse_visible_devices` wrapped its parser calls in `patch.dict(os.environ, {"ZE_AFFINITY_MASK": val}, clear=True)`. `unittest.mock` restores a patched dict by calling `os.environ.clear()` and then re-adding the saved keys. The XPU runtime sets `ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN=1` natively during initialization and re-reads it from the process environment on every free-memory query. That variable never appears in `os.environ`, which is only a startup snapshot plus Python-side writes, so the restore step cannot put it back. Direct confirmation on this runner (CPython 3.15.1): ``` os._clearenv present: True before: os.environ ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN = None <- invisible to Python before: real env ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN = b'1' <- set natively by the runtime after : os.environ ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN = None after : real env ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN = None <- wiped, not restored ``` Dropping `clear=True` is not sufficient: `_unpatch_dict` calls `os.environ.clear()` either way. **Fix strategy:** stop patching `os.environ` as a whole; save and restore the one variable the test actually needs.
Implement Result ```diff diff --git a/test/test_xpu.py b/test/test_xpu.py --- a/test/test_xpu.py +++ b/test/test_xpu.py @@ -19,7 +19,6 @@ import unittest import warnings from copy import deepcopy from itertools import product -from unittest.mock import patch import torch import torch.multiprocessing as mp @@ -271,8 +270,20 @@ if __name__ == "__main__": def test_parse_visible_devices(self): def _parse_visible_devices(val, strict=False): - with patch.dict(os.environ, {"ZE_AFFINITY_MASK": val}, clear=True): + # Set and restore ZE_AFFINITY_MASK by hand rather than with + # patch.dict(os.environ): patch.dict restores by calling + # os.environ.clear(), which since Python 3.15 maps to clearenv() + # and so also drops variables the XPU runtime set natively (notably + # ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN, which mem_get_info() needs). + orig = os.environ.get("ZE_AFFINITY_MASK") + os.environ["ZE_AFFINITY_MASK"] = val + try: return torch.xpu._parse_visible_devices(strict=strict) + finally: + if orig is None: + del os.environ["ZE_AFFINITY_MASK"] + else: + os.environ["ZE_AFFINITY_MASK"] = orig # Tokens with trailing non-numeric characters are invalid; entire list is rejected self.assertEqual(_parse_visible_devices("1a, 2b"), []) ``` The module-level `from unittest.mock import patch` became unused and was removed (the other `patch` uses in the file are `unittest.mock.patch...` or live inside subprocess script strings that import it themselves). Alternative considered: `patch.object(os, "environ", {"ZE_AFFINITY_MASK": val})`, which never touches the process environment at all and is a one-liner. It was rejected because it depends on `torch.xpu._parse_visible_devices` reading the variable only through `os.getenv`; the explicit save/restore keeps the test's intent legible and survives that helper later growing a subprocess or native lookup.
Verify **Verdict: PASSED.** No build needed - the change is confined to a pytorch test file, so verification ran against the nightly wheel. Environment: CPython 3.15.1 (uv-managed) + `torch 2.16.0.dev20261022+xpu` (cp315 manylinux), Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100, runner `xpu-agent-pvc`. Targeted command from the issue: ``` pytest -q test/test_xpu.py::TestXpu::test_parse_visible_devices \ test/test_xpu.py::TestXpu::test_mem_get_info ``` | | Result | |---|---| | Before | `1 failed, 1 passed` (`test_mem_get_info`: device "doesn't support querying the available free memory") | | After | `2 passed` | Whole file, same Python 3.15 environment (`pytest -q -rf test/test_xpu.py`): | | Result | |---|---| | Before | 35 failed, 162 passed, 8 skipped, 3 xfailed | | After | 8 failed, 187 passed, 8 skipped, 3 xfailed | 27 tests go FAIL -> PASS and nothing newly fails. The fixed set is exactly the list named in `pytorch/pytorch#200666`: `test_raises_oom`, `test_repeat_graph_capture_oneDNN_memory`, `test_set_per_process_memory_fraction`, `TestMemPool::test_mempool_oom_recovery_releases_cached_blocks` (both subtests), `TestMemPool::test_oom_mempool_with_limited_memory`, and the 21 `TestXpuOptimsCPU::test_graph_*` cases. The 8 remaining failures are a subset of the pre-fix failures and are environmental for this throwaway checkout (missing `ninja` for the C++-extension test, `multiprocessing` forkserver re-import under `pytest`), unrelated to this bug. Regression check on the Python version CI uses today (3.12.15, repo `.venv`): | | Result | |---|---| | Before | 6 failed, 189 passed, 8 skipped, 3 xfailed | | After | 6 failed, 189 passed, 8 skipped, 3 xfailed | Identical, i.e. no behavior change off Python 3.15. `ruff check` is clean on the changed file. Mismatched elements: 1 / 5 (20.0%) Greatest absolute difference: 0.13075685501098633 at index (4,) (up to 1e-05 allowed) Greatest relative difference: 0.02018318511545658 at index (4,) (up to 1.3e-06 allowed) FAILED CONSISTENTLY ``` So it is not a one-off: it has failed in at least two xpu runs. Four facts narrow it: 1. It is `linear.bias.grad` (the only 5-element parameter in `MapModels.PytreeInOut`), and only *part* of it is wrong - `1/5` elements on one attempt, `3/5` on two others. 2. The wrong values are byte-identical across runs a day apart (`0.13075685501098633`, `1.0899319648742676`), so this is a stable miscomputation, not a race. 3. `MapTests::test_map_pytree_in_out_device_xpu_dynamic_True_autograd_True` - the same test without `cpp_wrapper` - **passes in the same process**, so it is specific to `torch._inductor.config.cpp_wrapper=True`. 4. It needs a long process history: in CI it sits at 96% of a 917-item file run.
Reproduction attempts (nightly 2.16.0.dev20261022+xpu, Data Center GPU Max 1100, driver 1.17.39395+16) | Attempt | Result | |---|---| | target test alone | PASS | | whole `MapTestsCppWrapper` class, one process (32) | PASS | | `CondTestsCppWrapper`+`AssociativeScanTestsCppWrapper`+`MapTestsCppWrapper` (112) | PASS | | whole file, one process, alphabetical (unittest) order (917) | target PASSED | | whole file, one process, **exact CI pytest collection order** (917, 44 min) | target PASSED | | same again, first ~40% under GPU contention from a second test process | target PASSED, `813 passed, 100 skipped, 4 xfailed` | | standalone repro that dirties the XPU caching allocator with `1e9` before the compiled fwd/bwd | PASS | **No source build was attempted, and it would not have helped.** The nightly wheel is built from main `b40a4f2c`; the two failing CI runs are `e149fba4` and `30f2f72b`. Across `torch/_inductor`, `torch/_higher_order_ops`, `torch/_dynamo` and the test file, those commits differ only in `torch/_inductor/ir.py`, by the user-defined-Triton-kernel `restore_value`/`reset_to_zero` refactor - code this test never reaches. A rebuild would compile byte-identical logic. The one CI failure this runner *did* reproduce, once, is the sibling `ScanTests::test_scan_conv_device_xpu_dynamic_False_reverse_True_dim_0_scan_length_5_autograd_False`, with exactly the wrong value CI reports for it (`0.1627837219376429`); it passed in the second full-file run, so it is flaky here too.
Where the wrong value comes from (from the generated wrapper) `map` is lowered to a `while_loop` (`decompose_map_to_while_loop`) whose outputs are pre-allocated with `torch.empty_strided` and filled one slice per iteration. In the backward graph, `linear.bias.grad` is produced by `triton_red_fused_add_copy__cos_mul_reshape_select_sum_5`, which writes one 5-element row per iteration (`tl.store(out_ptr1 + (x0 + 5*ks1), tmp13, xmask)`) into that uninitialised buffer; the rows are summed after the loop. A row that is only partially written would leave the rest of that 5-element slot holding whatever the allocator handed back - which matches all four facts above: a subset of the 5 bias elements wrong, by `O(1)`, stable within a process, varying with process history, and `cpp_wrapper`-only. Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | batch-bug (skip-list) | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | unclear | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Sub-items this run handles (all mirrored from `pytorch/pytorch` DISABLED issues, CI commit `97a3cf652accf801225a2a05b5b3ab19b4d65473`): 1. `test_python_ref__refs_arange_xpu_complex128` (`TestCommonXPU`) -- `pytorch/pytorch#201987` 2. `test_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` (`TestOperatorsDeviceXPU`) -- `pytorch/pytorch#201988` 3. `test_vmap_autograd_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float64` (`TestOperatorsDeviceXPU`) -- `pytorch/pytorch#201989` 4. `test_operator_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` (`TestCompositeComplianceXPU`) -- `pytorch/pytorch#201990` 5. `test_profiler_experimental_tree_xpu` (`TestProfilerTreeDeviceXPU`) -- `pytorch/pytorch#201991` 6. `test_noncontiguous_samples_arange_xpu_complex64` (`TestCommonXPU`) -- `pytorch/pytorch#201992` 7. `test_redispatch_arange_xpu_complex128` (`TestTorchFunctionRedispatchOpsDeviceXPU`) -- `pytorch/pytorch#201993` 8. `test_histc_out_dtype_xpu_float32` (`TestReductionsDeviceXPU`) -- `pytorch/pytorch#201994` 9. `test_jvp_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` (`TestOperatorsDeviceXPU`) -- `pytorch/pytorch#201995` 10. `test_fn_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float64` (`TestBwdGradientsXPU`) -- `pytorch/pytorch#201996` Expected grouping: sub-items 2, 3, 4, 9, 10 all exercise `nn.functional.grid_sample` and likely share one root cause; sub-items 1, 6, 7 all exercise `arange` with complex dtypes and likely share another. Sub-items 5 and 8 are investigated on their own. One sub-item per group takes the fix; the rest are re-checked against it. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce All 10 reproduce on the nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261025+xpu` (built from pytorch main `c9b5004c45`) on an Intel Arc Pro B60 (BMG), with pytorch test files from `origin/main@d0b9d245f4`. The CI that disabled them ran on PVC (`linux-noble-xpu-n-py3.11 / test (default, *, 12, linux.idc.xpu)`); the per-test failure signatures in those job logs match what reproduces here exactly, so the verdicts are not BMG-specific. | Sub-item | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `test_python_ref__refs_arange_xpu_complex128` | REPRODUCED | `Failed: Unexpected success` | | 2 | `test_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` | REPRODUCED | `Failed: Unexpected success` | | 3 | `test_vmap_autograd_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float64` | REPRODUCED | `Failed: Unexpected success` | | 4 | `test_operator_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` | REPRODUCED | `Failed: Unexpected success` | | 5 | `test_profiler_experimental_tree_xpu` | REPRODUCED | `AssertionError: ... at::native::xpu::MultiTensorApplyKernelFu[...] != ... sycl::_V1::ext::oneapi::experimental::det[...]` | | 6 | `test_noncontiguous_samples_arange_xpu_complex64` | REPRODUCED | `Failed: Unexpected success` | | 7 | `test_redispatch_arange_xpu_complex128` | REPRODUCED | `Failed: Unexpected success` | | 8 | `test_histc_out_dtype_xpu_float32` | REPRODUCED | `AssertionError: expected test to fail, but it passed` | | 9 | `test_jvp_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` | REPRODUCED | `Failed: Unexpected success` | | 10 | `test_fn_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float64` | REPRODUCED | `Failed: Unexpected success` | Nine of the ten are *unexpected successes*: the XPU test expectation says the op should fail and it no longer does. Sub-item 5 is the only genuine output mismatch -- a profiler tree golden string naming a SYCL kernel that has since been renamed. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@d0b9d245f4`, torch-xpu-ops pin `4260c030d7` (the same pin the CI commit and the nightly wheel carry). Nine of the ten sub-items are *stale test expectations*, not broken code: a feature XPU could not do was marked `unittest.expectedFailure` / `xfail` upstream, torch-xpu-ops then implemented it, and `expectedFailure` turns the resulting pass into a failure. Three distinct features, hence three groups: **Group 1 -- complex `arange` (sub-items 1, 6, 7).** `torch.arange` gained complex dtypes in `pytorch/pytorch#194890`; XPU did not support them, so `pytorch/pytorch#200510` added four `DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, ..., device_type='xpu', dtypes=(torch.complex64, torch.complex128))` entries to `arange`'s `OpInfo` (`torch/testing/_internal/common_methods_invocations.py:12334-12342`) and two more to its `PythonRefInfo` (`:23715-23719`). intel/torch-xpu-ops#5684 implements complex arange, so `torch.arange(0, 5, 1, dtype=torch.complex128, device='xpu')` returns correctly on the current pin and all six decorators are stale. **Group 2 -- 5-D bicubic `grid_sample` (sub-items 2, 3, 4, 9, 10).** `reference_inputs_grid_sample` includes a 5-D bicubic sample. XPU used to raise on it, so the `OpInfo` carried eight XPU `expectedFailure` entries (`common_methods_invocations.py:22172-22197`) and `test/functorch/test_ops.py:368` carried an op-wide `xpu_unsupported = {xfail("nn.functional.grid_sample", device_type="xpu")}` unioned into eleven skip lists. intel/torch-xpu-ops#5511 implements bicubic `grid_sampler_3d`, so `F.grid_sample` on a 5-D input with `mode='bicubic'` now succeeds on XPU and those expectations are stale. **Group 3 -- `histc(out=)` dtype check (sub-item 8).** `test/test_reductions.py:3406` carried `@expectedFailureXPU` on `test_histc_out_dtype` because XPU's `_histc_out_xpu` silently cast a mismatched `out`. intel/torch-xpu-ops#5380 added the check, so both instantiations now pass. **Sub-item 5 -- profiler tree golden string.** The only genuine output mismatch. `ProfilerTree.fmt_name` collapses an XPU kernel's template arguments with `^(at::native::xpu::\w+)<.+>$` (`test/profiler/test_profiler_tree.py:241`), which only matches a SYCL functor name. intel/torch-xpu-ops#5203 rewrote `multi_tensor_apply` as a SYCL free function, so the profiler now reports a 762-character `sycl::_V1::ext::oneapi::experimental::detail::NdRangeFreeFunctionKernelWrapper<&(void at::native::xpu::multi_tensor_apply_kernel<...>(...)), ...>` that the pattern does not match. The unmunged name reaches `assertExpectedInline`, so the `aten::_foreach_add_` subtree no longer matches the golden string, which still says `at::native::xpu::MultiTensorApplyKernelFunctor<...>`. Every one of the four fixes is therefore in pytorch: the XPU side already works, only pytorch's statements about it are out of date. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- four independent, source-local fixes, one per group - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch (all four patches) - **Analyzed at:** pytorch@d0b9d245f4 - **Skip added:** no -- all four patches only *remove* stale expectations, except sub-item 5 which widens a name-munging regex - **Ready for verify:** yes **1. `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201987-test_python_ref__refs_arange`** -- `torch/testing/_internal/common_methods_invocations.py`, 14 deletions. Reverts the `common_methods_invocations.py` half of `pytorch/pytorch#200510` (its unrelated legacy-kineto skip in `test/profiler/test_profiler.py` is left alone). ```diff - # XPU complex arange is unsupported. Tracked in intel/torch-xpu-ops#5668. - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, 'TestCommon', 'test_noncontiguous_samples', - device_type='xpu', dtypes=(torch.complex64, torch.complex128)), - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, 'TestCommon', 'test_out_requires_grad_error', - device_type='xpu', dtypes=(torch.complex64, torch.complex128)), - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, 'TestFakeTensor', 'test_strided_layout', - device_type='xpu', dtypes=(torch.complex64, torch.complex128)), - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, 'TestTorchFunctionRedispatchOpsDevice', 'test_redispatch', - device_type='xpu', dtypes=(torch.complex64, torch.complex128)), ``` ```diff skips=( - # XPU complex arange is unsupported. Tracked in intel/torch-xpu-ops#5668. - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, 'TestCommon', 'test_python_ref', device_type='xpu', - dtypes=(torch.complex64, torch.complex128)), - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, 'TestCommon', 'test_python_ref_torch_fallback', device_type='xpu', - dtypes=(torch.complex64, torch.complex128)), # Tests that assume input is a tensor or sequence of tensors ``` **2. `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201988-test_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample`** -- `torch/testing/_internal/common_methods_invocations.py` + `test/functorch/test_ops.py`, 15 insertions / 38 deletions. Key hunks (the functorch side is eleven mechanical `.union(xpu_unsupported)` removals, elided): ```diff - # mps and xpu refuse 5-D bicubic in eager. Not listed: test_dtypes, where a + # mps refuses 5-D bicubic in eager. Not listed: test_dtypes, where a # raising sample only marks a dtype partially supported, and test_out_warning, # which returns on the first sample, a 4-D bilinear one. - # TODO: drop these when mps / xpu implement 5-D bicubic. + # TODO: drop these when mps implements 5-D bicubic. # MPS TestConsistency has its own entry in common_mps.py. DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, "TestCommon", "test_noncontiguous_samples", device_type="mps"), - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, "TestCommon", - "test_noncontiguous_samples", device_type="xpu"), DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, "TestCommon", "test_variant_consistency_eager", device_type="mps"), - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, "TestCommon", - "test_variant_consistency_eager", device_type="xpu"), - # not instantiated on mps - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, "TestCompositeCompliance", - "test_operator", device_type="xpu"), - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, "TestCompositeCompliance", - "test_backward", device_type="xpu"), - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, "TestCompositeCompliance", - "test_view_replay", device_type="xpu"), - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, "TestMathBits", - "test_neg_view", device_type="xpu"), + # xpu eager samples 5-D bicubic, but the meta kernel still refuses it, + # so the crossref backward suites disagree with eager. DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, "TestFakeTensor", "test_fake_crossref_backward_no_amp", device_type="xpu"), DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, "TestFakeTensor", "test_fake_crossref_backward_amp", device_type="xpu"), - # the gradient suites run on xpu, which claims float64 - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, "TestBwdGradients", - "test_fn_grad", device_type="xpu"), - DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, "TestBwdGradients", - "test_fn_gradgrad", device_type="xpu"), )), ``` ```diff -# torch-xpu-ops does not implement 5-D bicubic grid_sample yet; only those samples -# fail. The xfail is op-wide, so it also hides XPU regressions in the 2-D, bilinear -# and nearest paths. A per-sample xfailIf won't work: it needs the test to call -# sample_inputs(..., use_subtests=True), and these tests don't. -# [地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#5542] -xpu_unsupported = {xfail("nn.functional.grid_sample", device_type="xpu")} - ``` **3. `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201991-test_profiler_experimental_tree`** -- `test/profiler/test_profiler_tree.py`, 11 insertions / 1 deletion. ```diff + # An XPU kernel written as a SYCL free function is reported through a + # wrapper whose template arguments repeat the whole kernel signature; + # name the wrapped kernel instead. + name = re.sub( + r"^sycl::_V1::ext::oneapi::experimental::detail::\w*FreeFunctionKernelWrapper<" + r"&\((?:[\w:]+ )?(at::native::xpu::\w+)<.+>$", + r"\1<...>", + name, + ) + # XPU kernels are SYCL functors, so the template arguments spell out the # whole operand type list rather than ending in an argument list. name = re.sub(r"^(at::native::xpu::\w+)<.+>$", r"\1<...>", name) ``` ```diff urEnqueueKernelLaunchWithArgsExp - at::native::xpu::MultiTensorApplyKernelFunctor<...> + at::native::xpu::multi_tensor_apply_kernel<...> ``` **4. `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201994-test_histc_out_dtype`** -- `test/test_reductions.py`, 1 insertion / 2 deletions. ```diff @dtypes(torch.float32, torch.float64) - @expectedFailureXPU # XPU _histc_out_xpu (out-of-tree) does not enforce dtype check yet def test_histc_out_dtype(self, device, dtype): ``` `expectedFailureXPU` was the file's only use of that import, so it is dropped from the `common_device_type` import list as well. *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verify All four patches are Python-only, so no rebuild was needed; `TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc` was set but never used. Everything ran against the same nightly wheel the reproduce stage used, `2.16.0.dev20261025+xpu`, on an Intel Arc Pro B60 (BMG), with the pytorch checkout detached at `origin/main@d0b9d245f4`. The `test/` files are read straight from that checkout. The two patches that touch `torch/testing/_internal/common_methods_invocations.py` live inside the installed package, so for those runs the edited file was copied over the wheel's copy; `diff -q` confirmed the wheel's copy was byte-identical to the checkout's before the edit, and the wheel was restored to pristine afterwards. Each branch was verified in isolation, off the same base. | Sub-item | Test case | Before | After | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | `test_python_ref__refs_arange_xpu_complex128` | FAIL | PASS | | 2 | `test_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` | FAIL | PASS | | 3 | `test_vmap_autograd_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float64` | FAIL | PASS | | 4 | `test_operator_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` | FAIL | PASS | | 5 | `test_profiler_experimental_tree_xpu` | FAIL | PASS | | 6 | `test_noncontiguous_samples_arange_xpu_complex64` | FAIL | PASS | | 7 | `test_redispatch_arange_xpu_complex128` | FAIL | PASS | | 8 | `test_histc_out_dtype_xpu_float32` | FAIL | PASS | | 9 | `test_jvp_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` | FAIL | PASS | | 10 | `test_fn_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float64` | FAIL | PASS | `Before` was `Failed: Unexpected success` for sub-items 1-4, 6, 7, 9, 10; `AssertionError: expected test to fail, but it passed` for 8; and an `assertExpectedInline` tree mismatch on the `at::native::xpu::MultiTensorApplyKernelFunctor<...>` line for 5. Regression checks on the fixed trees -- each suite is the full surface the patch's expectations covered, so it also bounds what the removed op-wide xfails were hiding: | Suite | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `test_ops.py -k "arange and xpu"` | 8 failed, 63 passed, 19 skipped, 9 xfailed | 71 passed, 19 skipped, 9 xfailed | | `test_overrides.py -k arange` | 21 passed, 1 skipped | 21 passed, 1 skipped | | `test_ops.py -k "grid_sample and xpu"` | 8 failed, 22 passed, 22 skipped, 2 xfailed | 2 failed, 28 passed, 22 skipped, 2 xfailed | | `test_ops_gradients.py -k "grid_sample and xpu"` | 2 failed, 2 passed, 11 skipped | 4 passed, 11 skipped | | `functorch/test_ops.py -k "grid_sample and xpu"` | 3 failed, 21 passed, 14 skipped, 4 xfailed | 24 passed, 14 skipped, 4 xfailed | | `test_profiler_tree.py` (whole file) | 1 failed, 8 passed, 8 skipped | 9 passed, 8 skipped | | `test_reductions.py -k histc` (all devices) | 2 failed, 27 passed, 6 skipped | 29 passed, 6 skipped | The 2 remaining `grid_sample` failures are `test_fake_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` and `test_fake_autocast_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32`. They fail identically before and after -- `torch/_meta_registrations.py` `check_grid_sampler_3d` still allows 5-D bicubic only on `cpu`/`cuda`, so the meta kernel disagrees with XPU eager. Neither is in this issue's ten and neither carries an expectation that sub-item 2's patch touches; they are called out as a follow-up rather than folded in, because widening that allow-list is a meta-kernel change with its own blast radius (it would also decide the fate of the two `test_fake_crossref_backward_*` xfails the patch deliberately keeps). - **Verdict:** PASSED -- all ten sub-items pass, no suite regressed - **Lint:** clean (`ruff check` on each changed file reports no new findings vs. the same file at the base commit; `ruff format` reports no diff on the files pytorch formats). `lintrunner` / `spin` are not installed in this container, so `spin fixlint` could not be run. Two caveats a reviewer should weigh: verification ran on BMG while the CI that disabled these tests runs on PVC (`linux-noble-xpu-n-py3.11 / test (default, *, 12, linux.idc.xpu)`) -- the per-test failure signatures match that job's logs exactly, but the post-fix passes are BMG-only observations. And because "before" is the nightly wheel and "after" is the same wheel plus the patch, a PASSED verdict shows the tests pass with the patch applied; for these four patches that is also causal, since each one only deletes or widens the expectation that produced the failure. *Automated by fix-verify.*
Batch fan-out results Base: pytorch `origin/main@d0b9d245f4`, torch-xpu-ops pin `4260c030d7` (reproduce base: nightly `2.16.0.dev20261025+xpu`, BMG) | Sub-item | Outcome | Branch / Reason | |---|---|---| | 1. `test_python_ref__refs_arange_xpu_complex128` | FIXED | `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201987-test_python_ref__refs_arange` | | 2. `test_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` | FIXED | `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201988-test_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample` | | 3. `test_vmap_autograd_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float64` | COVERED | by sub-item 2's fix, same branch | | 4. `test_operator_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` | COVERED | by sub-item 2's fix, same branch | | 5. `test_profiler_experimental_tree_xpu` | FIXED | `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201991-test_profiler_experimental_tree` | | 6. `test_noncontiguous_samples_arange_xpu_complex64` | COVERED | by sub-item 1's fix, same branch | | 7. `test_redispatch_arange_xpu_complex128` | COVERED | by sub-item 1's fix, same branch | | 8. `test_histc_out_dtype_xpu_float32` | FIXED | `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201994-test_histc_out_dtype` | | 9. `test_jvp_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` | COVERED | by sub-item 2's fix, same branch | | 10. `test_fn_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float64` | COVERED | by sub-item 2's fix, same branch | - **FIXED:** 4 sub-items -- four independent patch artifacts, all against `pytorch/pytorch`. Each is a self-contained PR; they do not depend on each other and can land in any order. Patches 1 and 2 both touch `torch/testing/_internal/common_methods_invocations.py` but in regions ~10k lines apart, so they do not conflict. - **COVERED:** 6 sub-items -- re-run against the staged fix of their group and confirmed passing, so no separate branch. - **NEEDS_HUMAN / STALE_SKIP / INVALID_ENTRY / UNVERIFIED:** none. Two follow-ups that fall outside these ten and are deliberately *not* in any patch: - `torch/_meta_registrations.py` `check_grid_sampler_3d` still restricts 5-D bicubic to `cpu`/`cuda`, while XPU eager now supports it. That leaves `test_fake_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` and `test_fake_autocast_nn_functional_grid_sample_xpu_float32` failing (before and after this work, and with no disable issue of their own), and is why sub-item 2's patch keeps the two `TestFakeTensor::test_fake_crossref_backward_*` XPU xfails. - `test_histc_out_dtype_xpu_float64` fails exactly like its float32 sibling but has no disable issue. Sub-item 8's patch fixes it too. *Automated by issue-handler.*
Summary All ten disabled tests trace back to the same thing from opposite directions: torch-xpu-ops shipped four features -- complex `arange` (intel/torch-xpu-ops#5684), bicubic `grid_sampler_3d` (intel/torch-xpu-ops#5511), the `histc(out=)` dtype check (intel/torch-xpu-ops#5380), and a free-function rewrite of `multi_tensor_apply` (intel/torch-xpu-ops#5203) -- while pytorch still asserts XPU cannot do them. Nine tests are therefore `unittest.expectedFailure` entries that now report "Unexpected success", and the tenth is a profiler golden string naming a SYCL kernel that was renamed. The fix is four small pytorch patches: delete the three groups of stale expectations, and teach `ProfilerTree.fmt_name` to collapse a SYCL free-function kernel wrapper down to the kernel it wraps. Every one of the ten passes afterwards and no suite in the affected surface regressed, with two pre-existing `TestFakeTensor` grid_sample failures left untouched and recorded as a follow-up. - **Branches:** `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201987-test_python_ref__refs_arange`, `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201988-test_grad_nn_functional_grid_sample`, `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201991-test_profiler_experimental_tree`, `agent/fix-pytorch-issue-201994-test_histc_out_dtype` - **Base:** `d0b9d245f4f400496b3a41355330b4322ca267df` (pytorch `origin/main`) - **Changed files:** `torch/testing/_internal/common_methods_invocations.py`, `test/functorch/test_ops.py`, `test/profiler/test_profiler_tree.py`, `test/test_reductions.py` - **Four independent PRs, order does not matter.** Each branch closes its own upstream disable issues; none depends on another. - **Nothing was pushed.** The patches are exported as workflow artifacts for a human to review and apply.
_Generated by [fix job]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40215338955])._
Review Copy into a new comment, keep ONE verdict, add a note. Two verdicts in one comment are dropped as ambiguous. ``` **strong-accepted** **weak-accepted** **weak-rejected** **strong-rejected** **issue-drop** notes: ``` On a batch run add `item=` to say which sub-item the verdict is about, **in the bold text and in the marker** -- the marker is invisible, so the bold line is all a reader sees. One comment per sub-item, since a bare verdict on a batch does not say which test it means and is dropped. `run=` only when judging a run other than the newest, in both places too. A CI DISABLED sub-item, `item=` from the fan-out table: ``` **strong-accepted item=197334** notes: same TensorAssign overload as upstream CUDA, fp8 dispatch list matches ``` Another sub-item of the same batch, judged on an earlier run: ``` **weak-rejected run=35171979678 item=197335** notes: green only because the test is skipped, the kernel still lacks fp8 ``` An `[xpu-alignment]` issue that should not have been filed -- one issue per difference, so no `item=`: ``` **issue-drop** notes: accepted XPU/CUDA numerics difference, nothing to repair ```

Root Cause
Analyzed at pytorch origin/main@d0b9d245f4, torch-xpu-ops pin 4260c030d7 (the same pin the CI commit and the nightly wheel carry).
Nine of the ten sub-items are stale test expectations, not broken code: a feature XPU could not do was marked unittest.expectedFailure / xfail upstream, torch-xpu-ops then implemented it, and expectedFailure turns the resulting pass into a failure. Three distinct features, hence three groups:
Group 1 -- complex arange (sub-items 1, 6, 7). torch.arange gained complex dtypes in pytorch/pytorch#194890; XPU did not support them, so pytorch/pytorch#200510 added four DecorateInfo(unittest.expectedFailure, ..., device_type='xpu', dtypes=(torch.complex64, torch.complex128)) entries to arange's OpInfo (torch/testing/_internal/common_methods_invocations.py:12334-12342) and two more to its PythonRefInfo (:23715-23719). #5684 implements complex arange, so torch.arange(0, 5, 1, dtype=torch.complex128, device='xpu') returns correctly on the current pin and all six decorators are stale.
Group 2 -- 5-D bicubic grid_sample (sub-items 2, 3, 4, 9, 10). reference_inputs_grid_sample includes a 5-D bicubic sample. XPU used to raise on it, so the OpInfo carried eight XPU expectedFailure entries (common_methods_invocations.py:22172-22197) and test/functorch/test_ops.py:368 carried an op-wide xpu_unsupported = {xfail("nn.functional.grid_sample", device_type="xpu")} unioned into eleven skip lists. #5511 implements bicubic grid_sampler_3d, so F.grid_sample on a 5-D input with mode='bicubic' now succeeds on XPU and those expectations are stale.
Group 3 -- histc(out=) dtype check (sub-item 8). test/test_reductions.py:3406 carried @expectedFailureXPU on test_histc_out_dtype because XPU's _histc_out_xpu silently cast a mismatched out. #5380 added the check, so both instantiations now pass.
Sub-item 5 -- profiler tree golden string. The only genuine output mismatch. ProfilerTree.fmt_name collapses an XPU kernel's template arguments with ^(at::native::xpu::\w+)<.+>$ (test/profiler/test_profiler_tree.py:241), which only matches a SYCL functor name. #5203 rewrote multi_tensor_apply as a SYCL free function, so the profiler now reports a 762-character sycl::_V1::ext::oneapi::experimental::detail::NdRangeFreeFunctionKernelWrapper<&(void at::native::xpu::multi_tensor_apply_kernel<...>(...)), ...> that the pattern does not match. The unmunged name reaches assertExpectedInline, so the aten::_foreach_add_ subtree no longer matches the golden string, which still says at::native::xpu::MultiTensorApplyKernelFunctor<...>.
Every one of the four fixes is therefore in pytorch: the XPU side already works, only pytorch's statements about it are out of date.

Reproduce Run against the XPU nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261027+xpu`, which is built from exactly the failing CI commit's tree (`2026-10-27 nightly release (f6e5bb36...)`) and carries the **same** `third_party/xpu.txt` pin as that commit (`8c125b2e`). Device: this runner is BMG (8x Intel Arc Pro B60, device id `0xE211`); the CI job that failed ran on PVC (`dut7364_pvc_card_2`, `linux-noble-xpu-n-py3.11 / test (default, 12, 12)`). | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_correctness_NAdam_use_closure_False_xpu_float32` | CANNOT_VERIFY | PASSED on BMG in every configuration tried; CI signature is `Segmentation fault from GPU at 0xff00ffff00000000 ... NotPresent, level: 2 (PDP), access: 0 (Read)` on PVC | Attempts, all PASSED on BMG: | Attempt | Result | |---|---| | isolated test, nightly wheel | PASSED (47.8s) | | full `test_compiled_optimizers.py` in one process (the shape of the failing CI shard) | 749 passed, 61 skipped, 0 failures, no GPU fault (27m49s) | | `CompiledOptimizerParityTestsXPU` class in one process | 27 passed, 3 skipped (11m42s) | | `PYTORCH_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True` (unmaps freed pages, exposes use-after-free) | PASSED | | Level-Zero V1 adapter (`UR_LOADER_USE_LEVEL_ZERO_V2=0`) | PASSED | | `use_deterministic_algorithms(warn_only=True)` + `fill_uninitialized_memory` (NaN-fills every uninitialized ATen buffer, exposes read-before-write) | PASSED | **What the CI evidence adds beyond the disable issue.** The GPU page fault is raised at the first host synchronisation after the optimizer steps (`check_optim` -> `assertEqual` -> `_compare_regular_values_close`), so the faulting kernel is one of the preceding optimizer kernels, not the comparison. The fault is **not NAdam-specific**: in the neighbouring run on the same day ([run 40477121341]([运行记录：pytorch/pytorch@run:40477121341]), shard 12), `test_correctness_AdamW_use_closure_False_xpu_float32` hit the identical address, and its JUnit report captured the first-order failure before the crash: ``` AssertionError: Tensor-likes are not close! Mismatched elements: 100 / 100 (100.0%) Greatest absolute difference: nan at index (0, 0) (up to 1e-05 allowed) ``` So the primary symptom is **NaN parameters** after the compiled-vs-eager optimizer steps, with the unmapped-address GPU fault as the harder manifestation of the same corruption. In that run both tests passed when re-run alone; in the cited run NAdam failed on all three attempts. Separately, on PVC the day before, a different inductor test hit its own GPU page fault at a different address (`inductor/test_torchinductor_dynamic_shapes.py::DynamicShapesGPUTests::test_custom_scan_op_compiled_dynamic_shapes_xpu`, `0xff000000f4e82000`, write, level 1 PDE, [run 40363524522]([运行记录：pytorch/pytorch@run:40363524522])), which also passes on BMG here. Integer inputs in `[-2, 2]` keep a 1024-long dot product inside fp32's exact integer range (`|sum| <= 4096`), so every backend's accumulation order gives the same bits, while a wrong ordering of the foreach in-place adds still changes the result by O(magnitude) and is still caught. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- test-side numerics fix, fully within `test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py` - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** inductor *Automated by fix-root-cause.*

Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@88e0a917`. The `foreach_reads_sibling_target` case of `test_mutate_realized_buffer_in_make_fx_graph` (`test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py:11916`) builds its reference by running the traced function in eager with `torch._foreach_add_` patched to apply the adds one at a time, then compares it to `compile_fx_inner`'s result with `assertEqual`. Both sides compute `a = x @ w1` and `b = x @ w2` for `shape = (1024, 1024)` float32 -- eager through `aten::matmul`, the compiled graph through `extern_kernels.mm` (confirmed in the generated code; inductor emits only one fused pointwise kernel for the two adds, so the adds themselves are bit-exact). The two GEMM calls are therefore the only source of divergence, and on XPU they diverge: oneDNN's float32 GEMM on PVC is not bitwise reproducible, so two *identical* `x @ w` calls differ. ``` randn fp32 mm: 20/20 repeated calls differ bitwise (maxdiff 1.5e-05) max abs error vs the float64 result: 1.29e-04, mean |result| 25.5 ``` With K=1024 the accumulation magnitude is ~25 while the compared element is near zero (greatest relative difference 1.9e-05 on a value of ~0.8), so cancellation turns ordinary float32 GEMM noise into an absolute error of 1.5e-05 -- above `assertEqual`'s float32 `atol=1e-05`. It passes on CUDA because cuBLAS SGEMM is bitwise reproducible for a fixed shape, which makes both sides of the comparison identical there. Nothing about the behaviour under test -- that inductor applies a foreach in-place mutation of a realized buffer in list order -- depends on GEMM accuracy; the matmuls are only there to realize the buffers. The fix is to make the GEMM exact, which is the idiom the neighbouring tests in this file already use ("Keep the mm exact and bounded away from zero in low precision", "Integer values keep the mm exact in low precision"): draw the inputs from small integers so every partial sum is integral and below 2**24, and the result is identical in any accumulation order. Analyzed at pytorch origin/main@88e0a917.
The foreach_reads_sibling_target case of
test_mutate_realized_buffer_in_make_fx_graph
(test/inductor/test_torchinductor.py:11916) builds its reference by running
the traced function in eager with torch._foreach_add_ patched to apply the
adds one at a time, then compares it to compile_fx_inner's result with
assertEqual. Both sides compute a = x @ w1 and b = x @ w2 for
shape = (1024, 1024) float32 -- eager through aten::matmul, the compiled
graph through extern_kernels.mm (confirmed in the generated code; inductor
emits only one fused pointwise kernel for the two adds, so the adds themselves
are bit-exact). The two GEMM calls are therefore the only source of
divergence, and on XPU they diverge: oneDNN's float32 GEMM on PVC is not
bitwise reproducible, so two identical x @ w calls differ.
randn fp32 mm: 20/20 repeated calls differ bitwise   (maxdiff 1.5e-05)

in-place mutation of a realized buffer in list order -- depends on GEMM
accuracy; the matmuls are only there to realize the buffers. The fix is to
make the GEMM exact, which is the idiom the neighbouring tests in this file
already use ("Keep the mm exact and bounded away from zero in low precision",
"Integer values keep the mm exact in low precision"): draw the inputs from
small integers so every partial sum is integral and below 2**24, and the
result is identical in any accumulation order. Verified: 0/20 repeated
integer-valued x @ w calls differ, and the result equals the float64 result
exactly.

issues.title: FA4 backend is not supported on XPU
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

test/nn/attention/test_fa4.py currently only instantiates CUDA device tests. We want to enable XPU test collection for this file so that the coverage matrix reflects XPU. However, FA4 itself is currently CUDA-specific and is not supported by the XPU backend.

The FA4 tests depend on CUDA-only capability checks and the `flash_attn.cute.interface` package:

```
def _fa4_dependencies_available() -> bool:
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        return False
    major, _ = torch.cuda.get_device_capability(torch.cuda.current_device())
    if major not in (9, 10):
        return False

importlib.import_module("flash_attn.cute.interface")

```




### Versions

Pytorch 2.14

Automated fix session for this issue. Stages are appended below as they complete.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | pytorch | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Reproducer: `export/test_export_opinfo.py::TestExportOpInfoCPU::test_fake_export_xpu_nn_functional_scaled_dot_product_attention_cpu_float32` *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Reproduced against the **CPU-only** nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261028+cpu` (installed into an isolated venv, matching the issue's "CPU-only build - without CUDA or XPU support" environment). The failure is build-configuration specific: it needs a PyTorch built *without* XPU support, so the XPU nightly on this runner cannot show it. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_fake_export_xpu_nn_functional_scaled_dot_product_attention_cpu_float32` | REPRODUCED | `RuntimeError: false INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED at ".../DispatchStub.cpp":224 ... An unexpected device type was provided xpu` | The test currently reports `XFAIL` because upstream `test/export/test_export_opinfo.py` already carries `xfail("nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention")` in `fake_export_failures_xpu`, guarded by `if not torch.xpu._is_compiled()` and annotated with this issue. A minimal script shows the underlying failure and, side by side, that CUDA does not have it: ```text xpu compiled: False cuda built: False cuda:0: OK -> torch.Size([4, 3, 8]) cuda:0 xpu:0: FAIL -> RuntimeError: false INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED at DispatchStub.cpp:224 ... ``` *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@9e964d90d7d`. `DispatchStubImpl::try_get_call_ptr` (`aten/src/ATen/native/DispatchStub.cpp:147-224`) first checks the requested device against an **unconditional** `supported_devices` list that includes `c10::DeviceType::XPU`, then switches on it. But the `case DeviceType::XPU:` arm is wrapped in `#if defined(USE_XPU)` (`DispatchStub.cpp:208-211`), together with the `xpu_dispatch_ptr` member and `set_xpu_dispatch_ptr()` in the header (`DispatchStub.h:202-204`, `213-215`, `277-281`). In a build without XPU support the arm does not exist, so an XPU device type falls through to `default:` and trips `TORCH_INTERNAL_ASSERT(false, "An unexpected device type was provided ", device_type)` at `DispatchStub.cpp:224` instead of returning `ErrorType::MissingDeviceKernel`. That makes `DispatchStub::is_device_supported()` (`DispatchStub.h:305-332`) - documented as "Returns true if the dispatcher has a kernel registered for this device type" - **throw** for XPU rather than return `false`. The composite `scaled_dot_product_attention` uses exactly that predicate to decide whether it may ask for a fused backend (`aten/src/ATen/native/transformers/attention.cpp:837-839`), so fake-exporting SDPA onto `xpu:0` from a CPU-only build raises the internal assert. Every other device arm (`CUDA`, `HIP`, `MTIA`, `HPU`, `PrivateUse1`) is unguarded and returns `MissingDeviceKernel` when its pointer is null, which is why the same code path falls back to the math backend for `cuda:0` and only XPU fails: ```text xpu compiled: False cuda built: False cuda:0: OK -> torch.Size([4, 3, 8]) cuda:0 xpu:0: FAIL -> RuntimeError: ... An unexpected device type was provided xpu ``` The failure surfaced when `test/export/test_export_opinfo.py` was made device-generic and XPU-enabled (`#195440`, landed as `3bf5e7cb826`, 2026-10-08). That commit silenced it with `xfail("nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention")` in `fake_export_failures_xpu`, annotated with this issue - a silence, not a fix, so the bug is still live. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING - drop the `USE_XPU` guards so XPU behaves like every other non-CPU device arm, then remove the now-stale xfail. - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Analyzed at:** pytorch@9e964d90d7d - **What I changed:** `aten/src/ATen/native/DispatchStub.cpp` (-2: drop the `#if defined(USE_XPU)` around the `case DeviceType::XPU:` arm), `aten/src/ATen/native/DispatchStub.h` (-6: drop the same guard around both `xpu_dispatch_ptr` members and `set_xpu_dispatch_ptr()`), `test/export/test_export_opinfo.py` (-2: drop the now-stale `xfail("nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention")`). 10 deletions, 0 insertions. - **Why:** With the guard gone, an XPU device type reaches its own switch arm and returns `ErrorType::MissingDeviceKernel` when no kernel is registered, so `is_device_supported()` returns `false` instead of throwing -- the same behaviour the unguarded `CUDA`, `HIP`, `MTIA`, `HPU` and `PrivateUse1` arms already have at `aten/src/ATen/native/DispatchStub.cpp:199-221`, and what lets `attention.cpp:837-839` fall through to the math backend. In a build where `USE_XPU` *is* defined the preprocessed output is unchanged, so XPU builds are unaffected by construction. - **Skip added:** no (a stale xfail was removed) - **Ready for verify:** yes ```diff --- a/aten/src/ATen/native/DispatchStub.cpp +++ b/aten/src/ATen/native/DispatchStub.cpp @@ -209,10 +209,8 @@ DispatchResult DispatchStubImpl::try_get_call_ptr( case DeviceType::MTIA: return mtia_dispatch_ptr != nullptr ? DispatchResult(mtia_dispatch_ptr) : ErrorType::MissingDeviceKernel; -#if defined(USE_XPU) case DeviceType::XPU: return xpu_dispatch_ptr != nullptr ? DispatchResult(xpu_dispatch_ptr) : ErrorType::MissingDeviceKernel; -#endif case DeviceType::HPU: return hpu_dispatch_ptr != nullptr ? DispatchResult(hpu_dispatch_ptr) : ErrorType::MissingDeviceKernel; --- a/aten/src/ATen/native/DispatchStub.h +++ b/aten/src/ATen/native/DispatchStub.h @@ -199,9 +199,7 @@ struct TORCH_API DispatchStubImpl { void* mtia_dispatch_ptr; - #if defined(USE_XPU) void* xpu_dispatch_ptr; - #endif void* hpu_dispatch_ptr; @@ -210,9 +208,7 @@ struct TORCH_API DispatchStubImpl { void* mtia_dispatch_ptr = nullptr; - #if defined(USE_XPU) void* xpu_dispatch_ptr = nullptr; - #endif void* hpu_dispatch_ptr = nullptr; @@ -274,11 +270,9 @@ public: - #if defined(USE_XPU) void set_xpu_dispatch_ptr(FnPtr fn_ptr){ impl.xpu_dispatch_ptr = reinterpret_cast(fn_ptr); } - #endif --- a/test/export/test_export_opinfo.py +++ b/test/export/test_export_opinfo.py @@ -84,8 +84,6 @@ if not torch.xpu._is_compiled(): xfail("nn.functional.max_unpool2d", "grad"), - # [地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#5277] - xfail("nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention"), } ``` *Automated by fix-implement.*

An unexpected device type was provided xpu`. **Causality was established directly rather than assumed.** On this same build tree, re-adding *only* the two `#if defined(USE_XPU)` / `#endif` lines around the XPU switch arm and rebuilding incrementally reproduces the exact assert; removing them again and rebuilding passes. So the "before" is not merely a stale nightly: | Build (identical tree otherwise) | Result | |---|---| | fix branch, `USE_XPU` guard re-added to the XPU arm | FAIL - `INTERNAL ASSERT ... unexpected device type xpu` | | fix branch as committed | PASS | Regression checks on the fixed build: | Suite | Result | |---|---| | `test/export/test_export_opinfo.py` (whole file) | 1278 passed, 16 skipped, 62 xfailed | No failures and no unexpected XPASS, so dropping the one xfail entry did not leave any other entry in that set stale. XPU-enabled builds are unaffected by construction: when `USE_XPU` is defined, the preprocessed output of the changed lines is identical before and after, so no XPU build was needed to clear the change. - **Verdict:** PASSED - the reported test passes, and the A/B shows the fix is what makes it pass. - **Lint:** clean (`spin fixlint` reported no lint issues and modified no files) *Automated by fix-verify.*
Summary `DispatchStubImpl::try_get_call_ptr` screens the requested device against an unconditional `supported_devices` array that contains `DeviceType::XPU`, but its `case DeviceType::XPU:` arm - and the `xpu_dispatch_ptr` member and setter behind it - were wrapped in `#if defined(USE_XPU)`, so in a PyTorch build without XPU support an XPU device fell through to `default:` and tripped an internal assert instead of reporting a missing kernel; that made `is_device_supported()` throw where it is contractually supposed to return `false`, and the composite `scaled_dot_product_attention` uses exactly that predicate to decide whether it may ask for a fused backend, which is why fake-exporting SDPA onto `xpu:0` from a CPU-only build blew up while `cuda:0` quietly fell back to the math backend. The fix drops those three guards so XPU behaves like every other non-CPU arm, and removes the now-stale `xfail("nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention")` the test carried for this issue. On a CPU-only source build the reported test goes FAIL to PASS, the whole `test_export_opinfo.py` file is green (1278 passed, 0 failed, no unexpected XPASS), and an A/B that re-adds only the two guard lines and rebuilds brings the exact assert back - so the change, not a newer trunk, is what fixes it. XPU-enabled builds are untouched by construction, since with `USE_XPU` defined the preprocessed output is identical before and after. - **Branch:** `agent/fix-issue-5277` (in the **pytorch** checkout - the root cause is in `aten/`, not in torch-xpu-ops) - **Base:** `9e964d90d7d4fb61b6dcef79de105702bb1d771a` - **Changed files:** `aten/src/ATen/native/DispatchStub.cpp`, `aten/src/ATen/native/DispatchStub.h`, `test/export/test_export_opinfo.py` (10 deletions, 0 insertions) - **Note for the reviewer:** `MPS` still has the identical shape (`#if defined(USE_MPS)` around its arm while `mps_dispatch_ptr` is unguarded) and so stays latently affected. It was left alone because nothing in this report exercises it; worth a follow-up. - **Nothing was pushed.** The patch is exported as a workflow artifact for a human to review and apply.
