Two verdicts in one comment are dropped as ambiguous. ``` **strong-accepted** **weak-accepted** **weak-rejected** **strong-rejected** **issue-drop** notes: ``` On a batch run add `item=` to say which sub-item the verdict is about, **in the bold text and in the marker** -- the marker is invisible, so the bold line is all a reader sees. One comment per sub-item, since a bare verdict on a batch does not say which test it means and is dropped. `run=` only when judging a run other than the newest, in both places too. A CI DISABLED sub-item, `item=` from the fan-out table: ``` **strong-accepted item=197334** notes: same TensorAssign overload as upstream CUDA, fp8 dispatch list matches ``` Another sub-item of the same batch, judged on an earlier run: ``` **weak-rejected run=35171979678 item=197335** notes: green only because the test is skipped, the kernel still lacks fp8 ``` An `[xpu-alignment]` issue that should not have been filed -- one issue per difference, so no `item=`: ``` **issue-drop** notes: accepted XPU/CUDA numerics difference, nothing to repair ```

tree, re-adding only the two #if defined(USE_XPU) / #endif lines around the
XPU switch arm and rebuilding incrementally reproduces the exact assert; removing
them again and rebuilding passes. So the "before" is not merely a stale nightly:



Build (identical tree otherwise)
Result




fix branch, USE_XPU guard re-added to the XPU arm
FAIL - INTERNAL ASSERT ... unexpected device type xpu


fix branch as committed
PASS



Regression checks on the fixed build:



Suite
Result




test/export/test_export_opinfo.py (whole file)
1278 passed, 16 skipped, 62 xfailed

leave any other entry in that set stale. XPU-enabled builds are unaffected by
construction: when USE_XPU is defined, the preprocessed output of the changed
lines is identical before and after, so no XPU build was needed to clear the
change.

Summary
DispatchStubImpl::try_get_call_ptr screens the requested device against an
unconditional supported_devices array that contains DeviceType::XPU, but its
case DeviceType::XPU: arm - and the xpu_dispatch_ptr member and setter behind
it - were wrapped in #if defined(USE_XPU), so in a PyTorch build without XPU
support an XPU device fell through to default: and tripped an internal assert
instead of reporting a missing kernel; that made is_device_supported() throw
where it is contractually supposed to return false, and the composite
scaled_dot_product_attention uses exactly that predicate to decide whether it
may ask for a fused backend, which is why fake-exporting SDPA onto xpu:0 from a

fix drops those three guards so XPU behaves like every other non-CPU arm, and
removes the now-stale xfail("nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention") the
test carried for this issue. On a CPU-only source build the reported test goes
FAIL to PASS, the whole test_export_opinfo.py file is green (1278 passed, 0
failed, no unexpected XPASS), and an A/B that re-adds only the two guard lines and
rebuilds brings the exact assert back - so the change, not a newer trunk, is what
fixes it. XPU-enabled builds are untouched by construction, since with USE_XPU
defined the preprocessed output is identical before and after.

**Outcome:** IMPLEMENTING(fix_verified) Automated fix session for this issue. Follow progress in the [workflow run]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659770725]). Stage reports are collapsed below.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | pytorch | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Reproduced on the nightly XPU wheel `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu` with the pytorch test tree at `origin/main@349c819e3fb`, on a BMG runner (`Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics`, `torch.xpu.is_available() == True`). | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_fake_export_xpu_histogram_cpu_float32` | REPRODUCED | `Failed: Unexpected success` | The test is listed as an expected failure, but fake export of `torch.histogram` onto `xpu:0` actually succeeds on a machine with an XPU device, so `xfail` turns into an unexpected-success failure. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@349c819e3fb`. `torch.histogram` has no meta/`CompositeExplicitAutograd` kernel (`aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml:9818-9834` registers only `CPU, MPS, XPU`), so under `FakeTensorMode` it has to take the fallback path that runs the operator on a real device. `test/export/test_export_opinfo.py:46` puts `xfail("histogram")` in `fake_export_failures`, the set shared by `test_fake_export_cuda` and `test_fake_export_xpu` (`test/export/test_export_opinfo.py:75` and `:80`). That is correct for CUDA, which has no `histogram` kernel at all, but wrong for XPU: torch-xpu-ops does implement it (`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/HistogramddKernels.cpp`), so the fallback succeeds and the `xfail` fires as an unexpected success. Verified directly: `torch.histogram` under `FakeTensorMode` returns `FakeTensor(device=xpu:0)` when a device is present, and raises `RuntimeError: No XPU devices are available.` when the device is hidden (`ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=*:cpu ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=`) - which is why the case still xfails correctly on a CPU-only build and on an XPU build with no device, exactly as the report describes. The case appeared when `test/export/test_export_opinfo.py` was made device-generic and XPU was enabled (`pytorch/pytorch#195440` merged, `3bf5e7cb826`): the XPU expected-failure set was seeded from the CUDA one, inheriting `xfail("histogram")` without re-checking XPU operator coverage. Fix: pull `xfail("histogram")` out of the device-shared `fake_export_failures` bucket into its own bucket, unconditionally for CUDA, and for XPU only when `torch.xpu.is_available()` is false (the fallback needs a real device). CUDA behaviour is unchanged. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING - stale expected-failure entry in an upstream test file - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Analyzed at:** pytorch@349c819e3fb - **What I changed:** `test/export/test_export_opinfo.py` (+8 / -2) - moved `xfail("histogram")` out of the device-shared `fake_export_failures` set into its own `fake_export_histogram_failure` set, applied unconditionally to the CUDA expected-failure set and to the XPU one only when `torch.xpu.is_available()` is false. - **Why:** `torch.histogram` is registered for `CPU, MPS, XPU` only (`aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml:9818-9834`) and has no meta kernel, so `FakeTensorMode` runs it through the real-device fallback; XPU has a kernel (`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/HistogramddKernels.cpp`) so the fallback succeeds whenever a device is present, which is what turned the `xfail` into an unexpected success. Subtracting the entry from the shared set for XPU would have worked too (`xfail()` returns a hashable `SkipSpec` namedtuple, `torch/testing/_internal/common_device_type.py:1404-1417`), but it leaves the shared set's "failing fake export on gpu device" contract wrong for XPU; hoisting the entry states the per-backend condition where it is defined. - **Skip added:** no (an existing expected failure was narrowed, not added; skip-guard reviewer returned APPROVE) - **Ready for verify:** yes ```diff --- a/test/export/test_export_opinfo.py +++ b/test/export/test_export_opinfo.py @@ -44,7 +44,6 @@ export_failures = { # following are failing fake export on gpu device fake_export_failures = { - xfail("histogram"), xfail("masked.amax"), xfail("masked.amin"), xfail("masked.argmax"), @@ -71,13 +70,20 @@ fake_export_no_gpu_failures = { xfail("nonzero"), } +# histogram has no meta kernel, so fake export falls back to running it on the +# real device. CUDA has no histogram kernel at all, while XPU does, so on XPU +# this only fails when no device is available for the fallback. +fake_export_histogram_failure = {xfail("histogram")} + # CUDA-specific skip set generation -fake_export_failures_cuda = fake_export_failures.copy() +fake_export_failures_cuda = fake_export_failures | fake_export_histogram_failure if not torch.backends.cuda.is_built(): fake_export_failures_cuda |= fake_export_no_gpu_failures # XPU-specific skip set generation fake_export_failures_xpu = fake_export_failures.copy() +if not torch.xpu.is_available(): + fake_export_failures_xpu |= fake_export_histogram_failure if not torch.xpu._is_compiled(): fake_export_failures_xpu |= fake_export_no_gpu_failures fake_export_failures_xpu |= { ``` *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verify The fix is python-only (one test file), so no rebuild was needed: both runs use the same nightly XPU wheel `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu` and differ only by `test/export/test_export_opinfo.py`, with `before` taken from a worktree at the base commit `349c819e3fb` and `after` from `agent/fix-issue-5283`. BMG runner, `Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics`, 8 devices visible. | Test case | Before | After | |-----------|--------|-------| | `TestExportOpInfoCPU::test_fake_export_xpu_histogram_cpu_float32` | FAIL | PASS | `Before` was `Failed: Unexpected success`. Regression checks, each run on both trees so the delta is the fix and nothing else: | Suite | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `test_export_opinfo.py::TestExportOpInfoCPU -k test_fake_export_xpu` | 1 failed, 649 passed, 8 skipped, 20 xfailed | 650 passed, 8 skipped, 20 xfailed | | `test_export_opinfo.py::TestExportOpInfoCPU -k test_fake_export_cuda` | 438 failed, 202 passed, 8 skipped, 30 xfailed | 438 failed, 202 passed, 8 skipped, 30 xfailed | The whole XPU sweep goes from one failure to none, with the xfail count unchanged - no other case flipped in either direction. The CUDA sweep is byte-identical before and after, confirming CUDA keeps its unconditional `histogram` expected failure; its 438 failures are pre-existing on this CUDA-less build (fake export to `cuda:0` has no device to fall back to) and are not affected by this change. - **Verdict:** PASSED - the reported case passes and nothing else moved - **Lint:** clean (`lintrunner -a` on the changed file: "ok No lint issues") *Automated by fix-verify.*
Summary `torch.histogram` has no meta kernel, so fake export runs it through the real-device fallback, and `test/export/test_export_opinfo.py` kept `xfail("histogram")` in the expected-failure set shared by the CUDA and XPU variants of the test - correct for CUDA, which has no `histogram` kernel, but wrong for XPU, which has one, so the case passes on any machine with a device and the `xfail` reports an unexpected success. The fix hoists that entry into its own set, applied unconditionally for CUDA and for XPU only when `torch.xpu.is_available()` is false, since the fallback genuinely does fail with no device - which is why the case still xfails correctly on a CPU-only build. The reported case goes from `Failed: Unexpected success` to PASS, and running the full `test_fake_export_xpu` and `test_fake_export_cuda` sweeps on both the base and the fixed tree shows the XPU sweep losing its only failure with the xfail count unchanged and the CUDA sweep identical. - **Branch:** `agent/fix-issue-5283` (in the pytorch checkout - the fix is upstream, in `pytorch/pytorch`) - **Base:** `349c819e3fbec2522a51df12d2d6f7961a1aebcc` - **Changed files:** `test/export/test_export_opinfo.py` - **Nothing was pushed.** The patch is exported as a workflow artifact for a human to review and apply.
_Generated by [fix job]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659770725])._
Review Copy into a new comment, keep ONE verdict, add a note. Two verdicts in one comment are dropped as ambiguous. ``` **strong-accepted** **weak-accepted** **weak-rejected** **strong-rejected** **issue-drop** notes: ``` On a batch run add `item=` to say which sub-item the verdict is about, **in the bold text and in the marker** -- the marker is invisible, so the bold line is all a reader sees. One comment per sub-item, since a bare verdict on a batch does not say which test it means and is dropped. `run=` only when judging a run other than the newest, in both places too. A CI DISABLED sub-item, `item=` from the fan-out table: ``` **strong-accepted item=197334** notes: same TensorAssign overload as upstream CUDA, fp8 dispatch list matches ``` Another sub-item of the same batch, judged on an earlier run: ``` **weak-rejected run=35171979678 item=197335** notes: green only because the test is skipped, the kernel still lacks fp8 ``` An `[xpu-alignment]` issue that should not have been filed -- one issue per difference, so no `item=`: ``` **issue-drop** notes: accepted XPU/CUDA numerics difference, nothing to repair ```

issues.title: [profiler] XPU kernel activities lack stream/grid/block metadata expected by upstream Kineto trace tests
issues.body:
## Summary

XPU kernel activities in a Kineto chrome trace do not carry the `stream`, `grid` and `block` metadata keys that CUDA and ROCm emit. `device` and `correlation` are fine. This makes `test/profiler/test_profiler.py::TestProfilerDevice::test_kineto_kernel_metadata_in_trace` fail on XPU. It is a latent gap, not a regression: the class is instantiated without `allow_xpu=True`, so the test had never run on XPU until we enabled it.

| Key asserted by the test | CUDA | ROCm | XPU |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `device`, `correlation` | yes | yes | yes |
| `stream` | yes | yes | no (`sycl queue` / `l0 queue` instead) |
| `grid`, `block` | yes | yes | no |

```
AssertionError: 'stream' not found in {..., 'correlation': 1023, 'device': 0, 'l0 queue': '0x...', 'sycl queue': 64}
kernel 'gemm_kernel' missing 'stream'
```

`stream` fails first, but `grid`/`block` are a second independent gap: the trailing `has_kernel_launch_metadata` assertion would fail too.

## Where

- `libkineto/src/plugin/xpupti/XpuptiActivityHandlers.cpp`, `XpuptiActivityProfilerSession::handleRuntimeKernelMemcpyMemsetActivities()` never emits the three keys. `libkineto/include/MetadataFieldCatalog.h` confirms it: `XpuMetadataFields` has no `kStream`, `kGrid` or `kBlock`, while `CudaMetadataFields` and `RocmMetadataFields` define all three.
- Costs differ a lot between the two halves. `stream` is nearly free: `_sycl_queue_id` is already collected and emitted, just named `sycl queue`. `grid`/`block` look blocked in PTI 1.1.0 (oneAPI 2026.1): neither `pti_view_record_kernel` nor `_v2` in `pti/pti_view.h` carries any work-group count or size.

## Repro

Add `allow_xpu=True` to the `instantiate_device_type_tests(TestProfilerDevice, globals())` call in `test/profiler/test_profiler.py`, then:

```
python -m pytest test/profiler/test_profiler.py -k test_kineto_kernel_metadata_in_trace_xpu -v
```

Or without the harness:

```python
import json, torch
from torch.profiler import profile, ProfilerActivity

x = torch.randn(128, 128, device="xpu")
with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.XPU]) as prof:
    torch.mm(x, x)
    torch.xpu.synchronize()
prof.export_chrome_trace("t.json")
for e in json.load(open("t.json"))["traceEvents"]:
    if e.get("cat") == "kernel":
        print(e["name"], sorted(e.get("args", {})))
```

## Impact

About 5 upstream test IDs: this one, plus the 4 in `TestMetadataJsonFormat`, which asserts `common_keys = ["device", "stream", "correlation", "grid", "block"]` for every backend and so can never be enabled on XPU as written. We are skipping the failing test on XPU pointing at this issue so the rest of the newly enabled `TestProfilerDevice` XPU coverage can land.

## Question

Should xpupti emit `stream` (and eventually `grid`/`block`), or should an XPU-specific key set be agreed and the upstream test branch on backend the way it already does for ROCm (`expected = common_keys if TEST_WITH_ROCM else common_keys + cuda_only_keys`)? Given `grid`/`block` appear unavailable from PTI, is exposing work-group count and size in the kernel view records planned?

## Environment

PyTorch `2.15.0a0+gita56a3a1`, `torch.version.xpu = 20260101`, kineto `8b682ab`, Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550 (driver `1.6.33578+77`), oneAPI 2026.1.1 / PTI 1.1.0, kernel `6.17.0-35-generic`.

issues.body:
## Description
`test/test_torch.py::TestTorchDeviceTypeXPU::test_masked_scatter_xpu_complex128` aborts the entire Python process instead of failing/passing cleanly.

The test intentionally calls `masked_scatter_` with an undersized `src` and, for non-CUDA devices, expects a catchable `RuntimeError`:

```python
if self.device_type != 'cuda':
    # make src smaller. this should fail
    src = torch.zeros(num_copy - 1, dtype=dt, device=device)
    with self.assertRaises(RuntimeError):
        dest.masked_scatter_(mask, src)
```

On XPU the bounds check is a device-side assert in `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/Indexing.cpp:446` (`Assertion totalElements <= srcSize_ failed`). It aborts the process (`Fatal Python error: Aborted`) rather than raising a Python-catchable `RuntimeError`, so `assertRaises(RuntimeError)` cannot catch it. This matches the CUDA behavior the test explicitly excludes.

issues.title: [profiler] os.fork() deadlocks after Kineto XPU profiler initialization
issues.body:
## Summary

`os.fork()` deadlocks if the parent process has already initialized Kineto's XPU profiler. The child hangs before completing its own profiling session and the parent blocks forever in `os.waitpid()`. This breaks `test/profiler/test_profiler.py::TestProfilerDevice::test_forked_process` on any XPU build, and it is order-dependent today: the test passes in isolation (~2s) and only hangs once some earlier test in the same process has brought up the XPU profiler. That ordering is not guaranteed under test sharding.

## Repro

Deadlocks (killed by `timeout`, never prints "reaped"):

```python
import os, torch
from torch.profiler import profile, ProfilerActivity

# Initialize Kineto's XPU profiler in the parent.
x = torch.ones(1, device="xpu")
with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU, ProfilerActivity.XPU]):
    x + x
    torch.xpu.synchronize()

pid = os.fork()
if pid == 0:
    with profile(activities=[ProfilerActivity.CPU]):
        torch.ones(1) + torch.ones(1)
    os._exit(0)
print("parent: waiting on child", pid, flush=True)
print("parent: reaped", os.waitpid(pid, 0), flush=True)
```

Control: drop the XPU-primed block and make the parent's first session CPU-only, and the same fork reaps cleanly (`parent: reaped (192423, 0)`). So the trigger is specifically XPU profiler initialization in the parent, not fork-plus-profiler in general.

Stacks when hung: the child sits in `futex_do_wait`, the parent in `do_wait` under `os.waitpid`. Note the parent never observes the child's assertions, so a dead child would still report PASS if the wait ever returned.

## Impact

- `test_forked_process` cannot run on XPU builds. We are skipping it at process level (gated on the build, not on `device_type`, because the test is `@onlyOn("cpu")` so a device-scoped skip would never fire) while enabling XPU on the rest of `TestProfilerDevice` upstream.
- This costs the CPU coverage of that test on XPU machines specifically; CPU-only and CUDA builds keep it.
- The torch-xpu-ops test fork already works around it: `test/xpu/profiler/test_profiler_xpu.py` carries `@unittest.skipIf(torch.xpu.is_available(), "XPU complains about forking after init")`.

## Possibly related

- #2261 (closed) covers PTI `sycl_collector` *warnings* after fork ("Another subscriber already subscribed to Sycl runtime events"), not a deadlock.
- #2089 (closed) on `torch.xpu.is_available()` initializing a GPU context is adjacent root-cause context.

## Environment

PyTorch `2.15.0a0+gita56a3a1`, `torch.version.xpu = 20260101`, kineto `8b682ab`, Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550 (driver `1.6.33578+77`), oneAPI 2026.1.1 / PTI 1.1.0, kernel `6.17.0-35-generic`.

issues.title: [skip-added] test_effn_attn_uniform_zero_bias on XPU: SDPA never selects the efficient-attention backend
issues.body:
Auto-added by `fix-implement` (allow_skip=true), from the batch fan-out on intel/torch-xpu-ops#5272.

**Test:** `test/inductor/test_cuda_repro.py::CudaReproTests::test_effn_attn_uniform_zero_bias`
(upstream DISABLED test: pytorch/pytorch#196552)

**Original failure:** `AssertionError: 0 != 1` at `test_cuda_repro.py:298` (`self.assertEqual(len(biases), 1)`),
reached from `test_cuda_repro.py:328` -- the phase that traces
`F.scaled_dot_product_attention(..., attn_mask=padding_mask)` under
`sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION)` and expects exactly one
`aten._scaled_dot_product_efficient_attention` node in the joint graph.

**Root cause:** `select_sdp_backend_xpu` returns the *math* backend from its
`efficient_attention` case (`aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/Attention.cpp:224-231`):

```cpp
      case sdp::SDPBackend::efficient_attention:
        if (ctx.userEnabledMemEfficientSDP() &&
            can_use_mem_efficient_attention(kernel_params, print_debug)) {
          TORCH_WARN_ONCE(
              "SDPA Memory Efficient Attention backend is not supported on XPU, falling back to math backend.");
          return sdp::SDPBackend::math;
        }
```

So on XPU, `F.scaled_dot_product_attention` under
`sdpa_kernel(SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION)` traces to the math decomposition and
never emits an `_scaled_dot_product_efficient_attention` call for the test's
`joint_custom_post_pass` to capture. The earlier phases of the same test pass
because they invoke `aten._scaled_dot_product_efficient_attention.default`
directly, bypassing backend selection.

**Reason for skip:** making the XPU SDPA dispatcher actually select
`efficient_attention` is a capability change, not a test fix: `_fused_sdp_choice_xpu`
would have to stop routing to math, and XPU's
`_scaled_dot_product_efficient_attention_backward` currently re-runs the whole math
forward under autograd, so flipping the selection would be a behavioral and
performance change well beyond this failure. That decision belongs to the XPU SDPA
owners.

**Base analyzed:** pytorch@31527a43

Follow-up: either implement/enable efficient-attention backend selection on XPU and
remove the `@skipIfXpu`, or confirm the math fallback is intentional and upstream a
permanent test-side exclusion.

issues.title: [XPU] Integer matmul tests fail due to unsupported int types in dot_xpu_mkl and oneDNN
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Several matmul tests that check integer type support (int16, int32, int64) are skipped on XPU due to backend limitations. The dot_xpu_mkl and oneDNN kernels currently dispatch only for floating-point and complex types.

**Affected Tests (4 total):**
- `test_matmul_small_brute_force_1d_Nd[int16]`
- `test_matmul_small_brute_force_2d_Nd[int16]`
- `test_matmul_small_brute_force_3d_Nd[int16]`
- `test_corner_cases_of_cublasltmatmul[int16]`

**Root Cause:**
The XPU dispatch path for matmul operations (via dot_xpu_mkl and oneDNN kernels) does not support integer types (int16, int32, int64). When these types are used, the operation falls back to CPU execution or fails entirely on XPU devices.

python -m pytest test/test_linalg.py::TestLinalgDeviceXPU::test_matmul_small_brute_force_1d_Nd -xvs

issues.title: [XPU] aten::_dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight not implemented, causing dyn_quant tests to skip
issues.body:
Dynamic quantization tests that use 4-bit weight packing are skipped on XPU due to missing kernel implementation. The aten::_dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight operator is not registered for the XPU device, causing all dependent tests to skip.

Affected Tests (3 total):

test__dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight[xpu]
test__dyn_quant_matmul_4bit[xpu]
test_compile_dyn_quant_matmul_4bit[xpu]
Root Cause:
The aten::_dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight operator used for dynamic quantization in PyTorch does not have a kernel implementation for XPU devices. This is a PyTorch quantization utility operator, not a standard matrix operation.

nodes.body:
Automated fix session for intel/torch-xpu-ops#5332 (`aten::_dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight` not implemented on XPU).
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | unclear | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Three affected tests share one root cause (the missing `_dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight` / `_dyn_quant_matmul_4bit` XPU path), so this runs as a single bug rather than a batch fan-out. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Nightly XPU wheel `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu` (pytorch `a183c26ba18a214a0bf1d340ebda15a423be7a67`) on BMG (Intel Arc Pro B60). | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test__dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight[xpu]` | REPRODUCED | `NotImplementedError: The operator 'aten::_dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight' is not currently implemented for the XPU device.` | | `test__dyn_quant_matmul_4bit[xpu]` | REPRODUCED | `NotImplementedError: The operator 'aten::_dyn_quant_matmul_4bit' is not currently implemented for the XPU device.` | | `test_compile_dyn_quant_matmul_4bit[xpu]` | REPRODUCED | same, via the eager fallback of the compiled region | In CI these three never surface as failures because all 24 parametrizations are listed in `test/xpu/skip_list_common.py` under `test_linalg_xpu.py` (citing intel/torch-xpu-ops#2309), which is what the issue reports as "causing all dependent tests to skip". The underlying dispatch gap was confirmed directly by calling both operators on an XPU tensor. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at `torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c`, pytorch `origin/main@349c819e`. `aten::_dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight` and `aten::_dyn_quant_matmul_4bit` are registered for CPU only -- `aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml:4210-4216` lists a single `CPU:` dispatch entry for each, with the implementations in `aten/src/ATen/native/LinearAlgebra.cpp:3677` and `:3708`. There is no XPU kernel and no XPU dispatch key, so any call on an XPU tensor hits the unimplemented-operator path and raises `NotImplementedError`. The three `TestLinalgDevice` tests that exercise these ops are decorated `@onlyNativeDeviceTypes` and `xpu` is in `NATIVE_DEVICES` (`torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py:502`), so they are collected for XPU; torch-xpu-ops silences all 24 parametrizations in `test/xpu/skip_list_common.py:157-177` instead. The CPU operator has two code paths (`aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/int4mm_kernel.cpp`). The KleidiAI path is Arm-only. The portable fallback is the one to mirror: packing is just `cat([weights.flatten().float(), scales.flatten().float(), bias?.float()])` (`int4mm_kernel.cpp:957-968`), and the matmul re-splits that blob by element counts (`:1318-1329`) and runs a reference kernel that (a) dynamically quantizes each input row to asymmetric int8 and (b) accumulates `(q + lhs_offset) * (nibble - 8)` per weight group, scaling by the group scale and then by the row's reciprocal scale (`:971-1137` channelwise, `:1138-1272` groupwise). The channelwise variant is just the groupwise one with `block_size == K`, so a single XPU kernel covers both. Fix: add `_dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight_xpu` / `_dyn_quant_matmul_4bit_xpu` in torch-xpu-ops (`src/ATen/native/xpu/DynQuantInt4.cpp` plus a SYCL kernel pair under `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/`), reusing the fallback's packed-blob layout so a blob is interchangeable between CPU and XPU, then add the `XPU:` dispatch rows upstream and drop the skip-list entries. This repo already carries the adjacent int4 ops (`src/ATen/native/xpu/LinearInt4.cpp`, `src/ATen/native/xpu/WeightInt4Pack.cpp`), so the file and kernel conventions are established. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- bounded missing-kernel gap with fully specified upstream reference semantics - **Target repo:** torch-xpu-ops (lands first) + pytorch (companion) - **Domain:** `xpu-kernel` *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** torch-xpu-ops (lands first) + pytorch (companion) - **Analyzed at:** `torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c`, pytorch `origin/main@349c819e` - **What I changed:** - `src/ATen/native/xpu/DynQuantInt4.cpp` (new, 115 lines) -- the two dispatch-layer wrappers. - `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/DynQuantInt4Kernels.cpp` (new, 205 lines) and `.h` (new, 24 lines) -- per-row int8 activation quantization kernel plus the int4 weight GEMM. - `test/xpu/skip_list_common.py` (-25 lines) -- drops the 24 now-passing `dyn_quant` entries and the stale `#2309` comment. - pytorch `aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml` (+2) -- the `XPU:` dispatch rows. - pytorch `torch/csrc/inductor/aoti_torch/generated/c_shim_xpu.h` (+2) -- regenerated; a stale copy fails the build with "The generated AOTInductor C shim header files have unexpectedly changed" (`torchgen/gen_aoti_c_shim.py:762-795`). - **Why:** packing reproduces the portable CPU fallback verbatim -- `cat([weights.flatten().float(), scales.flatten().float(), bias?.float()])` (`aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/int4mm_kernel.cpp:957-968`) -- so a blob is interchangeable between CPU and XPU and matches the shape `meta__dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight` already reports (`torch/_meta_registrations.py:4515-4518`). The matmul splits that blob by element count exactly as the CPU dispatcher does (`int4mm_kernel.cpp:1318-1329`) and the kernel reproduces the reference arithmetic: per-row asymmetric int8 activation quantization (`:1152-1209`) then `(q + lhs_offset) * (nibble - 8)` accumulated per weight group and scaled (`:1223-1262`). The CPU reference splits channelwise (`:971-1137`) from groupwise (`:1138-1272`) for vectorization only -- channelwise is `block_size == K`, i.e. one block -- so one kernel covers both. The input-dtype guard copies CPU's (`aten/src/ATen/native/LinearAlgebra.cpp:3714-3718`), keeping eager in step with the meta function, which rejects bf16 unless `block_size == in_features` (`torch/_meta_registrations.py:4530-4537`). One deliberate divergence: an added `in_features % 2 == 0` check. Two 4-bit weights share a byte, so the CPU reference's `rhs_stride = ceil(K/2)` disagrees with its own `N * K / 2` buffer size for odd `K`; on a GPU that is an out-of-bounds read rather than a wrong number. - **Skip added:** no (24 stale skip entries removed) - **Ready for verify:** yes Before building, the arithmetic and the packed-blob layout were cross-checked against the real CPU operator in Python over all 8 test shapes plus two channelwise cases: packing is bit-identical (`torch.equal(xpu_layout_blob, torch._dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight(...))`) and the matmul matches the CPU op to <= 1.5e-5 absolute. ```diff diff --git a/src/ATen/native/xpu/DynQuantInt4.cpp b/src/ATen/native/xpu/DynQuantInt4.cpp new file mode 100644 index 00000000..c233e5a6 --- /dev/null +++ b/src/ATen/native/xpu/DynQuantInt4.cpp @@ -0,0 +1,115 @@ +/* + * Copyright 2020-2026 Intel Corporation + * + * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"); + * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License. + * You may obtain a copy of the License at + * + * [地址已移除] + */ + +#include +#include + +namespace at::native { + +// The packed buffer is laid out exactly like the portable (non-KleidiAI) +// fallback in aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/int4mm_kernel.cpp: a 1-D float32 blob +// holding the uint8 weight nibbles, then the per-group scales, then the +// optional bias. Keeping the layout identical means a blob packed on one of +// the two devices can be consumed on the other, and it matches the shape +// meta__dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight already reports. +Tensor _dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight_xpu( + const Tensor& weights, + const Tensor& scales_zeros, + const std::optional& bias, + const int64_t block_size, + const int64_t in_features, + [[maybe_unused]] const int64_t out_features) { + TORCH_CHECK( + weights.dtype() == at::kByte, __func__, " : expect weight to be kByte."); + TORCH_CHECK( + block_size == in_features || + (!(block_size % 32) && !(in_features % block_size)), + __func__, + ": Group size should be multiple of 32, in_features [", + in_features, + "]. Provided ", + block_size); + + std::vector tensors_to_cat = { + weights.reshape({-1}).to(kFloat), scales_zeros.reshape({-1}).to(kFloat)}; + if (bias.has_value()) { + tensors_to_cat.push_back(bias.value().reshape({-1}).to(kFloat)); + } + return at::cat(tensors_to_cat, 0); +} + +Tensor _dyn_quant_matmul_4bit_xpu( + const Tensor& inp, + const Tensor& packed_weights, + const int64_t block_size, + const int64_t in_features, + const int64_t out_features) { + TORCH_CHECK(inp.dim() == 2, __func__, " : expect input to be 2D tensor."); + TORCH_CHECK( + inp.dtype() == kFloat || + (inp.dtype() == kBFloat16 && block_size == in_features), + __func__, + " : expect input to be float32 or bfloat16 tensor."); + TORCH_CHECK( + inp.size(1) == in_features, + __func__, + " : expect input to have ", + in_features, + " columns, got ", + inp.size(1)); + TORCH_CHECK( + block_size == in_features || + (!(block_size % 32) && !(in_features % block_size)), + __func__, + ": Group size should be multiple of 32, in_features [", + in_features, + "]. Provided ", + block_size); + // Two 4-bit weights share a byte, so an odd in_features has no valid + // packing and would make the kernel read past the weight rows. + TORCH_CHECK( + in_features % 2 == 0, + __func__, + " : expect in_features to be even, got ", + in_features); + + const int64_t weight_elements = out_features * in_features / 2; + const int64_t scale_elements = out_features * (in_features / block_size); + auto packed = packed_weights.reshape({-1}); + TORCH_CHECK( + packed.numel() >= weight_elements + scale_elements, + __func__, + " : invalid packed weight tensor size."); + + auto weights = packed.narrow(0, 0, weight_elements).to(kByte); + auto scales_and_bias = + packed.narrow(0, weight_elements, packed.numel() - weight_elements) + .to(kFloat); + auto scales = scales_and_bias.narrow(0, 0, scale_elements); + + const int64_t bias_elements = + packed.numel() - weight_elements - scale_elements; + std::optional bias; + if (bias_elements) { + TORCH_CHECK( + bias_elements == out_features, + __func__, + " : expected bias length to match output dimension."); + bias = scales_and_bias.narrow(0, scale_elements, bias_elements); + } + + auto input = inp.contiguous(); + auto output = at::empty({input.size(0), out_features}, input.options()); + xpu::dyn_quant_matmul_4bit_kernel( + output, input, weights, scales, bias, block_size); + return output; +} + +} // namespace at::native diff --git a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/DynQuantInt4Kernels.cpp b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/DynQuantInt4Kernels.cpp new file mode 100644 index 00000000..e19ebc61 --- /dev/null +++ b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/DynQuantInt4Kernels.cpp @@ -0,0 +1,205 @@ +/* + * Copyright 2020-2026 Intel Corporation + * + * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"); + * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License. + * You may obtain a copy of the License at + * + * [地址已移除] + */ + +#include +#include +#include +#include + +#include + +namespace at::native::xpu { + +constexpr float kI8Min = -128.f; +constexpr float kI8Max = 127.f; + +// Asymmetric per-row int8 quantization of the activations, mirroring the +// portable CPU reference in aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/int4mm_kernel.cpp. One +// work-group per row; `scale` reduces identically on every work-item so the +// quantization loop needs no broadcast. +template +SYCL_EXT_ONEAPI_FUNCTION_PROPERTY((syclexp::nd_range_kernel<1>)) +void dyn_quant_lhs_kernel( + const scalar_t* inp, + int8_t* lhs_q, + float* lhs_scale, + int32_t* lhs_offset, + int64_t K) { + auto item = syclext::this_work_item::get_nd_item<1>(); + auto group = item.get_group(); + const int64_t row = item.get_group(0); + const int64_t lid = item.get_local_id(0); + const int64_t lrange = item.get_local_range(0); + const scalar_t* src = inp + row * K; It does mean the skip-list edit itself is not exercised end-to-end here. - Per the usual caveat: `Before` is the nightly wheel and `After` is a source build carrying the fix, so this does not by itself prove the fix is what made the tests pass. It cannot be green until step 2 is on pytorch `main`, so split > that one contiguous hunk out into a follow-up torch-xpu-ops PR. > > **No closing keyword in any of them** (`Fixes` / `Closes` / `Resolves`): > merging one would close the issue with the rest still out. In CI these three never surface as failures because all 24 parametrizations
are listed in test/xpu/skip_list_common.py under test_linalg_xpu.py
(citing #2309), which is what the issue reports as
"causing all dependent tests to skip". The underlying dispatch gap was
confirmed directly by calling both operators on an XPU tensor.
Automated by fix-reproduce.



Root Cause
Analyzed at torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c, pytorch origin/main@349c819e.
aten::_dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight and aten::_dyn_quant_matmul_4bit are
registered for CPU only -- aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml:4210-4216
lists a single CPU: dispatch entry for each, with the implementations in
aten/src/ATen/native/LinearAlgebra.cpp:3677 and :3708. There is no XPU
kernel and no XPU dispatch key, so any call on an XPU tensor hits the
unimplemented-operator path and raises NotImplementedError. The three
TestLinalgDevice tests that exercise these ops are decorated
@onlyNativeDeviceTypes and xpu is in NATIVE_DEVICES
(torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py:502), so they are collected for
XPU; torch-xpu-ops silences all 24 parametrizations in
test/xpu/skip_list_common.py:157-177 instead.
The CPU operator has two code paths
(aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/int4mm_kernel.cpp). The KleidiAI path is Arm-only.
The portable fallback is the one to mirror: packing is just
cat([weights.flatten().float(), scales.flatten().float(), bias?.float()])
(int4mm_kernel.cpp:957-968), and the matmul re-splits that blob by element
counts (:1318-1329) and runs a reference kernel that (a) dynamically
quantizes each input row to asymmetric int8 and (b) accumulates
(q + lhs_offset) * (nibble - 8) per weight group, scaling by the group
scale and then by the row's reciprocal scale (:971-1137 channelwise,
:1138-1272 groupwise). The channelwise variant is just the groupwise one
with block_size == K, so a single XPU kernel covers both.
Fix: add _dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight_xpu / _dyn_quant_matmul_4bit_xpu in
torch-xpu-ops (src/ATen/native/xpu/DynQuantInt4.cpp plus a SYCL kernel pair
under src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/), reusing the fallback's packed-blob layout
so a blob is interchangeable between CPU and XPU, then add the XPU: dispatch
rows upstream and drop the skip-list entries. This repo already carries the
adjacent int4 ops (src/ATen/native/xpu/LinearInt4.cpp,
src/ATen/native/xpu/WeightInt4Pack.cpp), so the file and kernel conventions
are established.

upstream reference semantics

Domain: xpu-kernel

+ * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+ * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.

+#include <ATen/native/xpu/sycl/DynQuantInt4Kernels.h>
+#include <comm/xpu_aten.h>
+
+namespace at::native {
+
+// The packed buffer is laid out exactly like the portable (non-KleidiAI)
+// fallback in aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/int4mm_kernel.cpp: a 1-D float32 blob
+// holding the uint8 weight nibbles, then the per-group scales, then the
+// optional bias. Keeping the layout identical means a blob packed on one of
+// the two devices can be consumed on the other, and it matches the shape
+// meta__dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight already reports.
+Tensor _dyn_quant_pack_4bit_weight_xpu(
+    const Tensor& weights,
+    const Tensor& scales_zeros,
+    const std::optional<Tensor>& bias,
+    const int64_t block_size,
+    const int64_t in_features,
+    [[maybe_unused]] const int64_t out_features) {
+  TORCH_CHECK(
+      weights.dtype() == at::kByte, __func__, " : expect weight to be kByte.");
+  TORCH_CHECK(
+      block_size == in_features ||
+          (!(block_size % 32) && !(in_features % block_size)),
+      __func__,
+      ": Group size should be multiple of 32, in_features [",
+      in_features,
+      "]. Provided ",
+      block_size);
+
+  std::vector<Tensor> tensors_to_cat = {
+      weights.reshape({-1}).to(kFloat), scales_zeros.reshape({-1}).to(kFloat)};
+  if (bias.has_value()) {
+    tensors_to_cat.push_back(bias.value().reshape({-1}).to(kFloat));
+  }
+  return at::cat(tensors_to_cat, 0);
+}
+
+Tensor _dyn_quant_matmul_4bit_xpu(
+    const Tensor& inp,
+    const Tensor& packed_weights,
+    const int64_t block_size,
+    const int64_t in_features,
+    const int64_t out_features) {
+  TORCH_CHECK(inp.dim() == 2, __func__, " : expect input to be 2D tensor.");
+  TORCH_CHECK(
+      inp.dtype() == kFloat ||
+          (inp.dtype() == kBFloat16 && block_size == in_features),
+      __func__,
+      " : expect input to be float32 or bfloat16 tensor.");
+  TORCH_CHECK(
+      inp.size(1) == in_features,
+      __func__,
+      " : expect input to have ",
+      in_features,
+      " columns, got ",
+      inp.size(1));
+  TORCH_CHECK(
+      block_size == in_features ||
+          (!(block_size % 32) && !(in_features % block_size)),
+      __func__,
+      ": Group size should be multiple of 32, in_features [",
+      in_features,
+      "]. Provided ",
+      block_size);
+  // Two 4-bit weights share a byte, so an odd in_features has no valid
+  // packing and would make the kernel read past the weight rows.
+  TORCH_CHECK(
+      in_features % 2 == 0,
+      __func__,
+      " : expect in_features to be even, got ",
+      in_features);
+
+  const int64_t weight_elements = out_features * in_features / 2;
+  const int64_t scale_elements = out_features * (in_features / block_size);
+  auto packed = packed_weights.reshape({-1});
+  TORCH_CHECK(
+      packed.numel() >= weight_elements + scale_elements,
+      __func__,
+      " : invalid packed weight tensor size.");
+
+  auto weights = packed.narrow(0, 0, weight_elements).to(kByte);
+  auto scales_and_bias =
+      packed.narrow(0, weight_elements, packed.numel() - weight_elements)
+          .to(kFloat);
+  auto scales = scales_and_bias.narrow(0, 0, scale_elements);
+
+  const int64_t bias_elements =
+      packed.numel() - weight_elements - scale_elements;
+  std::optional<Tensor> bias;
+  if (bias_elements) {
+    TORCH_CHECK(
+        bias_elements == out_features,
+        __func__,
+        " : expected bias length to match output dimension.");
+    bias = scales_and_bias.narrow(0, scale_elements, bias_elements);
+  }
+
+  auto input = inp.contiguous();
+  auto output = at::empty({input.size(0), out_features}, input.options());
+  xpu::dyn_quant_matmul_4bit_kernel(
+      output, input, weights, scales, bias, block_size);
+  return output;
+}
+
+} // namespace at::native

+/*
+ * Copyright 2020-2026 Intel Corporation
+ *
+ * Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License");
+ * you may not use this file except in compliance with the License.
+ * You may obtain a copy of the License at

+ */
+
+#include <ATen/ATen.h>
+#include <ATen/Dispatch.h>
+#include <ATen/xpu/XPUContext.h>
+#include <comm/SYCLContext.h>
+
+#include <ATen/native/xpu/sycl/DynQuantInt4Kernels.h>
+
+namespace at::native::xpu {
+
+constexpr float kI8Min = -128.f;
+constexpr float kI8Max = 127.f;
+
+// Asymmetric per-row int8 quantization of the activations, mirroring the
+// portable CPU reference in aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/int4mm_kernel.cpp. One
+// work-group per row; `scale` reduces identically on every work-item so the
+// quantization loop needs no broadcast.
+template <typename scalar_t>
+SYCL_EXT_ONEAPI_FUNCTION_PROPERTY((syclexp::nd_range_kernel<1>))
+void dyn_quant_lhs_kernel(
+    const scalar_t* inp,
+    int8_t* lhs_q,
+    float* lhs_scale,
+    int32_t* lhs_offset,
+    int64_t K) {
+  auto item = syclext::this_work_item::get_nd_item<1>();
+  auto group = item.get_group();
+  const int64_t row = item.get_group(0);
+  const int64_t lid = item.get_local_id(0);
+  const int64_t lrange = item.get_local_range(0);
+  const scalar_t* src = inp + row * K;
+
+  float local_min = std::numeric_limits<float>::max();
+  float local_max = std::numeric_limits<float>::lowest();
+  for (int64_t k = lid; k < K; k += lrange) {
+    const float v = static_cast<float>(src[k]);
+    local_min = sycl::fmin(local_min, v);
+    local_max = sycl::fmax(local_max, v);
+  }
+  const float rmin = sycl::fmin(
+      0.f, sycl::reduce_over_group(group, local_min, sycl::minimum<float>()));
+  const float rmax = sycl::fmax(
+      0.f, sycl::reduce_over_group(group, local_max, sycl::maximum<float>()));
+
+  const float scale = rmin == rmax ? 1.f : (kI8Max - kI8Min) / (rmax - rmin);
+  const float descaled_min = rmin * scale;
+  const float descaled_max = rmax * scale;
+  float zero_point = (kI8Min + descaled_min + kI8Max + descaled_max > 0)
+      ? kI8Min - descaled_min
+      : kI8Max - descaled_max;
+  zero_point = sycl::fmin(sycl::fmax(zero_point, kI8Min), kI8Max);
+  const int32_t nudged_zero_point =
+      static_cast<int32_t>(sycl::rint(zero_point));
+
+  if (lid == 0) {
+    lhs_scale[row] = scale ? 1.f / scale : 0.f;
+    lhs_offset[row] = -nudged_zero_point;
+  }
+
+  int8_t* dst = lhs_q + row * K;
+  for (int64_t k = lid; k < K; k += lrange) {
+    const int32_t v =
+        static_cast<int32_t>(sycl::round(static_cast<float>(src[k]) * scale)) +
+        nudged_zero_point;
+    dst[k] = static_cast<int8_t>(sycl::min(
+        sycl::max(v, static_cast<int32_t>(kI8Min)),
+        static_cast<int32_t>(kI8Max)));
+  }
+}
+
+// One work-item per output element. `block_size == K` degenerates to the
+// channelwise case of the CPU reference (a single block with one scale per
+// output channel).
+template <typename scalar_t>
+SYCL_EXT_ONEAPI_FUNCTION_PROPERTY((syclexp::nd_range_kernel<1>))
+void dyn_quant_matmul_4bit_sub_kernel(
+    scalar_t* out,
+    const int8_t* lhs_q,
+    const float* lhs_scale,
+    const int32_t* lhs_offset,
+    const uint8_t* weights,
+    const float* scales,
+    const float* bias,
+    int64_t N,
+    int64_t K,
+    int64_t block_size,
+    int64_t total) {
+  auto item = syclext::this_work_item::get_nd_item<1>();
+  const int64_t idx = item.get_global_linear_id();
+  if (idx >= total)
+    return;
+
+  const int64_t m = idx / N;
+  const int64_t n = idx % N;
+  const int64_t num_blocks = K / block_size;
+  const int8_t* lhs = lhs_q + m * K;
+  const uint8_t* rhs = weights + n * ((K + 1) / 2);
+  const int32_t offset = lhs_offset[m];
+
+  float acc = 0.f;
+  for (int64_t b = 0; b < num_blocks; ++b) {
+    int32_t iacc = 0;
+    for (int64_t i = 0; i < block_size; ++i) {
+      const int64_t k = b * block_size + i;
+      const uint8_t byte = rhs[k / 2];
+      const int32_t w =
+          static_cast<int32_t>((k & 1) ? (byte >> 4) : (byte & 0x0F)) - 8;
+      iacc += (static_cast<int32_t>(lhs[k]) + offset) * w;
+    }
+    acc += static_cast<float>(iacc) * scales[n * num_blocks + b];
+  }
+  acc *= lhs_scale[m];
+  if (bias)
+    acc += bias[n];
+  out[idx] = static_cast<scalar_t>(acc);
+}
+
+template <typename scalar_t>
+static void dyn_quant_matmul_4bit_impl(
+    const Tensor& output,
+    const Tensor& inp,
+    const Tensor& weights,
+    const Tensor& scales,
+    const std::optional<Tensor>& bias,
+    int64_t block_size) {
+  const int64_t M = inp.size(0);
+  const int64_t K = inp.size(1);
+  const int64_t N = output.size(1);
+  auto queue = getCurrentSYCLQueue();
+
+  auto lhs_q = at::empty({M, K}, inp.options().dtype(at::kChar));
+  auto lhs_scale = at::empty({M}, inp.options().dtype(at::kFloat));
+  auto lhs_offset = at::empty({M}, inp.options().dtype(at::kInt));
+
+  {
+    constexpr auto kptr = dyn_quant_lhs_kernel<scalar_t>;
+    const int64_t local_range = std::min<int64_t>(
+        at::xpu::getKernelMaxWorkGroupSize<kptr>(), std::max<int64_t>(K, 1));
+    sycl_kernel_submit<kptr>(
+        M * local_range,
+        local_range,
+        queue,
+        0,
+        inp.const_data_ptr<scalar_t>(),
+        lhs_q.mutable_data_ptr<int8_t>(),
+        lhs_scale.mutable_data_ptr<float>(),
+        lhs_offset.mutable_data_ptr<int32_t>(),
+        K);
+  }
+
+  {
+    constexpr auto kptr = dyn_quant_matmul_4bit_sub_kernel<scalar_t>;
+    const int64_t total = M * N;
+    const int64_t local_range = at::xpu::getKernelMaxWorkGroupSize<kptr>();
+    const int64_t num_groups = (total + local_range - 1) / local_range;
+    sycl_kernel_submit<kptr>(
+        num_groups * local_range,
+        local_range,
+        queue,
+        0,
+        output.mutable_data_ptr<scalar_t>(),
+        lhs_q.const_data_ptr<int8_t>(),
+        lhs_scale.const_data_ptr<float>(),
+        lhs_offset.const_data_ptr<int32_t>(),
+        weights.const_data_ptr<uint8_t>(),
+        scales.const_data_ptr<float>(),
+        bias.has_value() ? bias->const_data_ptr<float>() : nullptr,
+        N,
+        K,
+        block_size,
+        total);
+  }
+}
+
+void dyn_quant_matmul_4bit_kernel(
+    const Tensor& output,
+    const Tensor& inp,
+    const Tensor& weights,
+    const Tensor& scales,
+    const std::optional<Tensor>& bias,
+    int64_t block_size) {
+  if (output.numel() == 0)
+    return;
+  AT_DISPATCH_SWITCH(
+      inp.scalar_type(),
+      "dyn_quant_matmul_4bit_xpu",
+      AT_DISPATCH_CASE(at::kFloat, [&] {
+        dyn_quant_matmul_4bit_impl<scalar_t>(
+            output, inp, weights, scales, bias, block_size);
+      }) AT_DISPATCH_CASE(at::kBFloat16, [&] {
+        dyn_quant_matmul_4bit_impl<scalar_t>(
+            output, inp, weights, scales, bias, block_size);
+      }));
+}
+
+} // namespace at::native::xpu

issues.title: [inductor][distributed] Inductor cudagraphs silently no-op on XPU: cudagraph_trees needs XPU allocator checkpoint bindings (`_xpu_getCheckpointState` et al.)
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`torch.compile` with `torch._inductor.config.triton.cudagraphs = True` silently does
nothing on XPU. The flag *is* read and inductor reaches its device check, which only
clears CUDA, so cudagraphs are skipped — and a test that asserts "graphs work" passes
without ever capturing one.

```bash
python - <<'EOF'
import torch
with torch._inductor.config.patch({"triton.cudagraphs": True}):
    f = torch.compile(lambda x: (x + 1).sum(), backend="inductor", fullgraph=True)
    inp = torch.randn(2, 8, device="xpu:1")
    for _ in range(3):
        out = f(inp)
print("out:", out.device)
EOF
```

```
W torch/_inductor/cudagraph_utils.py:401] [__cudagraphs] skipping cudagraphs due to skipping cudagraphs due to multiple devices: device(type='xpu', index=1)
out: xpu:1
```

The "multiple devices" wording is misleading — there is a single XPU device; the check
simply does not accept a non-CUDA device.

There are two blockers, in order:

**1. The gate.** `torch/_inductor/cudagraph_utils.py`,
`check_multiple_devices_or_any_cpu_nodes()` only clears a device whose `.type == "cuda"`:

```python
if (
    len(device_node_mapping) == 1
    and next(iter(device_node_mapping.keys())).type == "cuda"
):
    return None
```

**2. The runtime.** With that check relaxed to accept `xpu`, capture then dies:

```
File "torch/_inductor/cudagraph_trees.py", line 2377, in __init__
    with graph_capture_lock, torch.cuda.device(device_index):
File "torch/cuda/__init__.py", line 181, in _exchange_device
    raise RuntimeError("PyTorch was compiled without CUDA support")
```

`cudagraph_trees.py` has 64 CUDA call sites across 22 distinct APIs. Most already map
1:1 onto `torch.xpu` — `synchronize`, `device`, `current_stream`, `Stream`, `stream`,
`graph`, `graph_pool_handle`, `current_device`, `memory`, `memory_snapshot`,
`is_initialized` are all present, plus `XPUGraph` where CUDA has `CUDAGraph` — and the
three core pool hooks exist as `torch._C._xpu_beginAllocateCurrentThreadToPool`,
`_xpu_endAllocateToPool`, `_xpu_releasePool`.

What is missing on the XPU side:

| CUDA binding | XPU equivalent | Used at | Needed for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_cuda_getCheckpointState` | **missing** | `cudagraph_trees.py:1612`, in `_add_first_outputs` | **first recording of every graph** |
| `_cuda_setCheckpointPoolState` | **missing** | `:3257` | restoring allocator state when re-entering a recorded graph |
| `_cuda_cudaCachingAllocator_raw_delete` | **missing** | `:3267` | freeing outputs during that restore |
| `_cuda_checkPoolLiveAllocations` | **missing** | `:2215` | live-allocation asserts |
| `_cuda_isHistoryEnabled` | **missing** (XPU has `_xpu_recordMemoryHistory`) | `:203` | memory-history debug |

Because `_cuda_getCheckpointState` sits on the *first recording* path, this cannot be
worked around in Python: XPU cannot capture even a single graph through
`cudagraph_trees` today.

### Suggested fix

1. **XPU allocator (this repo):** add the missing bindings above — at minimum
   `_xpu_getCheckpointState`, `_xpu_setCheckpointPoolState` and an XPU `raw_delete`,
   since those three gate capture and replay.
2. **PyTorch inductor (separate PR):** make `cudagraph_utils` accept the current
   accelerator and route `cudagraph_trees` through
   `torch.get_device_module(device_type)`, aliasing `CUDAGraph`/`XPUGraph`. A
   `torch._inductor.config.triton.xpugraphs` switch would let tests select the XPU path
   explicitly while `triton.cudagraphs` remains the CUDA one. No such option exists
   today — `hasattr(config.triton, "xpugraphs")` is `False`, and patching it raises
   `AttributeError: torch._inductor.config.triton.xpugraphs does not exist`.

### Test impact

While porting `test/distributed/tensor/test_compile_on_one_rank.py` to be
device-agnostic (pytorch/pytorch#114850), 29 of its 30 tests were enabled on XPU. The
one exception is
`TestCompileOnOneRankDeviceAsParameter::test_cudagraphs_under_coor_runs_on_nonzero_device`,
which had to be marked `@skipIfXpu(msg="inductor cudagraphs is CUDA-only")`: with the
skip removed it *passes in 2.7s without recording a graph* — green but vacuous, which
is worse than an explicit skip.

A second case is in `test/distributed/test_inductor_collectives.py`:
`TestCollectivesMultiProc::test_allreduce_inductor_cudagraph_trees` compiles a function
containing `dist.all_reduce` with `{"triton.cudagraphs": True, "triton.cudagraph_trees": True}`
and only asserts that compiled output matches eager output. On XPU it passes without
recording a graph; with `TORCH_LOGS=perf_hints` each rank logs
`skipping cudagraphs due to multiple devices: device(type='xpu', index=N)`. The gate has
since been refactored into `_CUDAGRAPH_SUPPORTED_DEVICE_TYPES = frozenset(OrderedSet(["cuda"]))`
in `cudagraph_utils.py`, but still only admits `cuda`. It is marked
`@skipIfXpu(msg="inductor cudagraphs is CUDA-only: [地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#5338]")`.

Closing this issue should include removing both skips and confirming the tests record and
replay a graph on XPU.

Note that `torch.xpu.XPUGraph`, `torch.xpu.graph` and `torch.xpu.make_graphed_callables`
all work in eager mode. The gap is only that inductor never routes to them.

Related: #3570 skips the xccl collective graph-replay UTs (`test_allreduce_graph_replay`
et al.), which is c10d-level graph capture; this issue is about inductor's graph path.

### Versions

```
torch              2.15.0a0+git28789c4  (source build, commit 28789c4f989)
torch.version.xpu  20260100
triton-xpu         3.8.0+git1e2d42a0
device             4x Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100
backend            xccl
```

Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | torch-xpu-ops | | Dependencies | (none named in the issue) | | Handling | agent-fixable | *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Reproduced on the nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu`, BMG (Intel Arc Pro B60), torch-xpu-ops at `73a6552c`. `rn50.log.json` was regenerated first via `test_rn50_profiling.py`; the overlapping-kernels case only reads that artifact. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_for_overlapping_kernels.py::TestOverlappingKernels::test_overlapping_kernels` | REPRODUCED | `AssertionError: Scalars are not equal! Expected 0 but got 56` | Reproduce command: ``` python -m pytest -s -v test/profiling/test_rn50_profiling.py python -m pytest -s test/profiling/test_for_overlapping_kernels.py ``` Identical signature and identical count to the 2026-10-14 nightly reported above ([job log]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:38571105611])): 56 overlapping pairs, all between consecutive oneDNN kernels (`gen_conv` / `gen_reorder`). The 951 overlaps in the issue's original (2026-09-14) log were dominated by a different problem — `gpu_user_annotation` events being counted as kernels — which #5363 fixed; the 56 that remain are the ones analysed below. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at `torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c`, nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu`. Every one of the 971 device events in `rn50.log.json` sits on a **single** queue — same trace `pid`/`tid` (`0`/`64`), one `l0 queue` handle, one `engine_index`/`engine_ordinal` — and PyTorch creates XPU streams with `sycl::property::queue::in_order()` (`c10/xpu/XPUStream.cpp:139-142`). Two kernels on such a queue cannot run concurrently, so an overlap in the trace is an inconsistency in the *reported* device timestamps, not real concurrency. Sorted by submission order (`kernel_id`) rather than by `ts`, the trace has exactly 56 adjacent pairs whose spans overlap, every one by **5.0–6.5 us**, and every one inside an `aten::convolution_overrideable` (53 forward convs in the profiled iteration). The ~467 SYCL kernels in the same trace never overlap and the median inter-kernel gap is **+1.7 us**, so the error is a small offset on specific events rather than noise that scales with kernel length. It is not oneDNN-specific. A short standalone reproducer (torchvision resnet50 train step, batch 256, plain `torch.profiler.profile`, no schedule) intermittently shows the same violation between a *SYCL* kernel (`BatchNormBackwardKernelFunctor`) and `gen_conv`, with overlaps of **10.7 us** in one run and **14.2–14.6 us** in another. It is not a proven cause, and the timestamp path is below PyTorch either way. **Why not simply loosen the test:** `OVERLAP_TOLERANCE = 1` us (`test/profiling/test_for_overlapping_kernels.py:17`) would have to absorb an artifact measured at 5–6.5 us here but at 14.6 us in a synthetic run, so no threshold is both safe and still catches the gross trace corruption the test was written to guard (intel/torch-xpu-ops#2741). That trade-off is the profiler owner's call; `allow_skip=false` for this issue, so the agent also did not silence the test. - **Verdict:** NEEDS_HUMAN — the timestamps come from Intel PTI, a component the agent cannot change or rebuild; suggest the `dependency component: PTI` label and an upstream PTI/Level-Zero report with the evidence above. - **Target repo:** N/A - **Domain:** none of the registered domains (`xpu-kernel`, `inductor`, `upstream-pytorch`) covers the profiler trace path. *Automated by fix-root-cause.*

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-09-13] torch.add(dense, dense, out=sparse_csr) aborts the process on XPU instead of raising
issues.body:
<!-- alignment-published-unit: issue-196906 -->
## Summary

On XPU, `torch.add(a, b, out=out)` with strided `a` and `b` and a valid sparse CSR `out` terminates the process with SIGSEGV and no Python-level exception. Upstream CPU raises a catchable (if unpolished) `RuntimeError: ... INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED`, so an XPU user gets strictly less than upstream: no diagnosable error at all, and no chance to handle it.

The layout combination itself need not be supported. The defect is that `add_out_sparse_compressed_xpu` re-dispatches instead of rejecting it, so the call never terminates.

## Upstream source

- pytorch/pytorch#196906, "torch.add with dense inputs and valid sparse CSR out triggers INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED", created 2026-09-13T15:45:32Z, reported on CPU/CUDA build 2.13.0+cu126. Still OPEN with no linked fix PR or cross-referenced commit as of 2026-09-14.
- Found by an xpu-alignment scan of the half-open window `[2026-09-13T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-14T00:00:00Z)` against the `pytorch/pytorch` default-branch snapshot `ad9448bc18658ff31d7512c2e5368f0718cf1ea0`.

## Observed XPU behavior

Runner result: `returncode -11` (SIGSEGV), `timed_out: false`, 8.049 s, no `RESULT` token, no traceback.

```text
torch_version: 2.15.0.dev20260912+xpu
xpu_available: True
xpu_device_name: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
control_layout: torch.sparse_csr
control_device: xpu:0
control_dense: [[3.0, 0.0], [0.0, 3.0]]
a_layout_device: torch.strided xpu:0
b_layout_device: torch.strided xpu:0
out_layout_device: torch.sparse_csr xpu:0
marker: calling torch.add(dense, dense, out=sparse_csr)
```

## Target-path evidence

- `aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml` at the snapshot dispatches `add.out` for `SparseCsrXPU` to `add_out_sparse_compressed_xpu`, which this repository implements.
- The control call (sparse CSR + sparse CSR) ran first and returned `torch.sparse_csr` on `xpu:0` densifying to `[[3.0, 0.0], [0.0, 3.0]]`, so the `SparseCsrXPU` add path is reachable and functional on this device. No XPU-to-CPU fallback warning was emitted for `add` (the one fallback warning in the log comes from sparse CSR construction).
- The operand layouts and devices were printed immediately before the call, and the reproducer runs under `python -u`, so the pre-call marker being the last line places the abort inside the target call, not in setup and not after it.

## Root cause

`src/ATen/native/sparse/xpu/SparseCsrTensorMath.cpp:400`:

```cpp
Tensor& add_out_sparse_compressed_xpu(
    const Tensor& self,
    const SparseCsrTensor& other,
    const Scalar& alpha,
    SparseCsrTensor& out) {
  if (self.layout() == kStrided) {
    at::add_out(out, self, other.to_dense(), alpha);
    return out;
  } else if (other.layout() == kStrided) {
    at::add_out(out, other, self.to_dense(), alpha);
    return out;
  }
```

`Tensor::to_dense()` on a strided tensor returns that tensor unchanged, so when both inputs are strided and `out` is sparse CSR the re-dispatch of `at::add_out` selects `SparseCsrXPU` again (the key comes from `out`) with identical layouts. That recurses without bound and exhausts the native stack, which Python cannot convert into `RecursionError`; the reproducer catches `RecursionError` explicitly and it never fired.

The log contains no native backtrace, so the recursion mechanism is inferred from the source above; what the run directly establishes is an uncatchable process abort inside the target call.

The second branch has the same trap: `add(sparse_csr, dense, out=sparse_csr)` enters `else if (other.layout() == kStrided)`, re-dispatches with two strided inputs, and then takes the first branch. Both branches need the guard.

Suggested fix: `TORCH_CHECK` the supported `out` layout (strided when either input is strided) before re-dispatching, so the unsupported combination produces a user-facing error instead of unbounded re-entry.

## Ownership

Upstream CPU takes a different branch for the same inputs: `add_out_sparse_compressed_cpu` calls `add_out_dense_sparse_compressed_cpu(out, self, other, alpha)`, whose `TORCH_INTERNAL_ASSERT(src.layout() == kSparseCsr || src.layout() == kSparseCsc)` is the assertion pytorch/pytorch#196906 reports. Fixing that CPU entry point, or improving its error message, does not touch `add_out_sparse_compressed_xpu`, which is separate code in this repository. No `pytorch/pytorch` issue or PR owns the XPU function, and a search of `intel/torch-xpu-ops` (sparse csr add, add_out_sparse_compressed, SparseCsrTensorMath, xpu-alignment) found no existing tracker.

Summary
On XPU, torch.add(a, b, out=out) with strided a and b and a valid sparse CSR out terminates the process with SIGSEGV and no Python-level exception. Upstream CPU raises a catchable (if unpolished) RuntimeError: ... INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED, so an XPU user gets strictly less than upstream: no diagnosable error at all, and no chance to handle it.
The layout combination itself need not be supported. The defect is that add_out_sparse_compressed_xpu re-dispatches instead of rejecting it, so the call never terminates.
Upstream source

pytorch/pytorch#196906, "torch.add with dense inputs and valid sparse CSR out triggers INTERNAL ASSERT FAILED", created 2026-09-13T15:45:32Z, reported on CPU/CUDA build 2.13.0+cu126. Still OPEN with no linked fix PR or cross-referenced commit as of 2026-09-14.
Found by an xpu-alignment scan of the half-open window [2026-09-13T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-14T00:00:00Z) against the pytorch/pytorch default-branch snapshot ad9448bc18658ff31d7512c2e5368f0718cf1ea0.

Observed XPU behavior
Runner result: returncode -11 (SIGSEGV), timed_out: false, 8.049 s, no RESULT token, no traceback.

xpu_available: True
xpu_device_name: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
control_layout: torch.sparse_csr
control_device: xpu:0
control_dense: [[3.0, 0.0], [0.0, 3.0]]

b_layout_device: torch.strided xpu:0

    const Tensor& self,
    const SparseCsrTensor& other,
    const Scalar& alpha,
    SparseCsrTensor& out) {
  if (self.layout() == kStrided) {
    at::add_out(out, self, other.to_dense(), alpha);
    return out;
  } else if (other.layout() == kStrided) {
    at::add_out(out, other, self.to_dense(), alpha);
    return out;
  }

- **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING - guard the unsupported `out` layout in the XPU sparse-compressed add entry point.

- **Target repo:** torch-xpu-ops
- **Analyzed at:** torch-xpu-ops@b483fef6

@@ -402,6 +402,17 @@ Tensor& add_out_sparse_compressed_xpu(

## Summary

`torch.add` on XPU crashed the process with an uncatchable SIGSEGV whenever one
input was strided and `out` was a sparse compressed tensor.

`add_out_sparse_compressed_xpu` handles a strided operand by densifying the other
operand and re-dispatching `at::add_out`. `Tensor::to_dense()` returns a strided
tensor unchanged, and `add.out`'s dispatch key is computed from *every* tensor
argument including `out` — so a sparse compressed `out` re-selected the same
function with identical layouts and recursed until the native stack was
exhausted. The upstream CPU and CUDA paths never re-dispatch; they call local
non-dispatching helpers whose asserts turn the same call into a catchable
`RuntimeError`.

The fix rejects a non-strided `out` on the strided path with a `TORCH_CHECK`,
turning the crash into a clear error while leaving every combination that
previously produced correct results untouched (`csr+csr -> csr` and all
strided-`out` combinations). Porting CUDA's
`add_out_dense_sparse_compressed_cuda` so a sparse `out` could actually be
computed is the structurally cleaner change, but it is a new kernel's worth of
work and would still need this same rejection for the layouts it cannot serve;
it is left as separate work.

- `src/ATen/native/sparse/xpu/SparseCsrTensorMath.cpp` — the guard
- `test/regressions/test_sparse_csr_add.py` — new regression test (5 cases)

Nothing was pushed and no PR was opened; the patch is exported as a workflow
artifact for a human to apply.

issues.title: [nativert] Runtime has no XPU support: placement rejects XPU, no XPU AOTI runner, no SPIR-V Triton loader
issues.body:
`torch/nativert` cannot execute a PT2 archive placed on XPU. Three independent gaps, in the order an XPU model hits them (paths from pytorch/pytorch main @ 589c789f3a9):

1. `isSameDevice` (`torch/nativert/executor/PlacementUtils.cpp:5-25`) allowlists CPU/CUDA/meta/MTIA and does `TORCH_CHECK(false, "isSameDevice: Unsupported device type ...")` for anything else. It is reached for every weight from `torch/nativert/executor/Weights.cpp:176`, so loading a model with `xpu:0` tensor meta throws immediately. `Placement` itself is device-agnostic and `convertDevice` (`torch/nativert/graph/Graph.cpp:1167-1185`) parses `"xpu:0"` fine, so the rejection is purely this allowlist.

2. The AOTI delegate resolves its runner through `AOTIModelContainerRunnerRegistry()->Create(device.type(), ...)` (`torch/nativert/executor/AOTInductorDelegateExecutor.cpp:112-118`), and only two keys are ever registered: `at::kCPU` (`AOTInductorDelegateExecutor.cpp:72-74`) and `at::kCUDA` (`AOTInductorModelContainerCudaShim.cpp:20-22`, built from the CUDA-gated `libtorch_nativert_cuda_sources` list in `build_variables.bzl:675-678`). There is no XPU shim and no `libtorch_nativert_xpu_sources`, so `Create(kXPU, ...)` returns `nullptr` and the next line null-derefs without a `TORCH_CHECK`. An XPU AOTI runner already exists upstream (`torch/csrc/inductor/aoti_runner/model_container_runner_xpu.cpp`), so this is wiring rather than new functionality.

3. `TritonKernelManagerRegistry` dispatch (`torch/nativert/kernels/TritonKernel.cpp:215-241`) keys off the artifact extension: `.cubin` -> kCUDA, `.hsaco` -> kHIP, `.so` -> kCPU, `.bin` -> kMTIA. There is no `.spv`/SYCL branch, so an XPU Triton kernel falls through to `TORCH_CHECK(loader_ != nullptr, "couldn't find triton kernel loader ...")` at `TritonKernel.cpp:243-245`.

The Python side is already device-generic: `lower_exported_program` calls plain `torch._inductor.aot_compile` (`torch/nativert/backends/_lower_utils.py:56-58`). I confirmed on Intel GPU that export, AOTI lowering and `package_pt2` all succeed for an XPU module and the failure comes only from the runner. Note that in OSS builds nothing runs on any device yet: `PyModelRunner` is bound to an empty `StubModelRunner` behind `#ifdef FBCODE_CAFFE2` (`torch/nativert/python/Bindings.cpp:83-100`), which is why `test/export/test_nativert.py` is gated `FBcode only for now`.

Filed as the tracked reference for the `@skipXPUIf` on `TestNativeRTDevice.test_aoti` in `test/export/test_nativert.py`.

> Drafted with the assistance of an AI assistant and reviewed before filing.

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] TestTorchDeviceSpecific tests fail on XPU/CPU after enabling allow_xpu (PR #195303 zero_ memset + CUDA-only test assumptions)
issues.body:
> The content below was drafted by an AI assistant and reviewed by me before posting.

## Summary
In my pr [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#196420] if enable some onlyCUDA functions on XPU we got failed because CUDA has implemented #195303, please check whether XPU also need this optimization.

## Failing tests
XPU:
- `TestTorchDeviceSpecificXPU::test_zero_dense_emits_memset_xpu`
- `TestTorchDeviceSpecificXPU::test_zero_strided_emits_fill_kernel_xpu`
- `TestTorchDeviceSpecificXPU::test_reduced_type_float_copy_emits_vectorized_kernel_xpu_bfloat16`
- `TestTorchDeviceSpecificXPU::test_reduced_type_float_copy_emits_vectorized_kernel_xpu_float16`

CPU (same class, also newly instantiated):
- `test_zero_dense_emits_memset_cpu`, `test_zero_strided_emits_fill_kernel_cpu`, `test_reduced_type_float_copy_emits_vectorized_kernel_cpu_{bfloat16,float16}`, `test_serialization_cpu`, `test_storage_all_devices_non_blocking_True_cpu`

## Root cause
1. **Functional gap vs pytorch/pytorch#195303**: that PR makes CUDA `zero_` use `cudaMemsetAsync` instead of a fill kernel. `test_zero_dense_emits_memset` asserts a "Memset" profiler event. On XPU, `zero_` still launches a fill kernel (`urEnqueueKernelLaunchWithArgsExp` appears in the trace, no Memset), so XPU has not adopted the memset-based `zero_`.
2. **CUDA-only test assumptions**:
   - `test_reduced_type_float_copy_emits_vectorized_kernel` and `test_zero_strided_emits_fill_kernel` assert on CUDA kernel names (`vectorized_elementwise_kernel`, `elementwise_kernel`) that XPU does not emit.

## Proposed resolution
- Implement a memset-based `zero_` fast path for XPU (align with #195303) so `test_zero_dense_emits_memset` passes on XPU, OR gate the memset/kernel-name tests `@onlyCUDA`.
- For the kernel-name profiler tests, either add XPU-specific expected kernel names or restrict to CUDA.

## References
- pytorch/pytorch#195303
- Related: intel/torch-xpu-ops#5018, intel/torch-xpu-ops#5234

nodes.body:
Starting automated fix on this issue. Follow progress in the [workflow run]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659851858]).
Triage | Field | Value | |---|---| | issue_type | single-bug | | scope | test-only (skip list) | | reproduction_missing | no | | runtime_dependencies | none | | handling | agent-fixable | Existing work found during triage: intel/torch-xpu-ops#5888 (open, approved) proposes a fix for this issue, and a maintainer pointed that out in a comment above. Both were taken into account before doing any work, and the run was reduced to independently verifying that claim instead of re-deriving a patch.
Reproduce Environment: nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu`, BMG runner (`xpu-agent`). The issue body's reproducer names the upstream file `test/test_torch.py`; in this repo the equivalent is the vendored copy `test/xpu/test_torch_xpu.py`, which is what CI actually runs (upstream `test_torch.py` is not in the `PYTORCH_TEST_DIR` section of the skip dict). ``` cd test/xpu python test_torch_xpu.py \ TestTorchDeviceTypeXPU.test_broadcast_fn_map_xpu \ TestTorchDeviceTypeXPU.test_broadcast_fn_map2_xpu -v ``` ``` test_broadcast_fn_map_xpu ... ok (0.024s) test_broadcast_fn_map2_xpu ... ok (0.001s) Ran 2 tests in 0.026s OK ``` Verdict: **NOT_REPRODUCED** as a runtime failure. `TypeError: map_ is only implemented on CPU tensors` does not occur any more. The defect is a stale skip, not a failing test.
Root cause `Tensor.map_` / `Tensor.map2_` apply a Python callable element-wise and are CPU-only by design; CUDA does not implement them either. `test_broadcast` is meant to return early for `map`/`map2` on accelerator tensors, but the guard was originally `small.is_cuda`, so XPU fell through to the CPU-only call. That guard has since been widened on both sides: - this repo: intel/torch-xpu-ops#3112 changed the vendored `test/xpu/test_torch_xpu.py` to `small.device.type in ["cuda", "xpu"]` **and** deleted the two skip-list entries, because the guard made them unnecessary; - upstream: the same change landed in `test/test_torch.py` via `pytorch/pytorch#197120` (commit `282ec02f`, 2026-10-20), so the reproducer quoted in the issue body no longer fails there either. intel/torch-xpu-ops#3288 then re-added the two entries to `test/xpu/skip_list_common.py` as "won't fix" cases, after the guard fix had already made them redundant. That re-add is the regression this issue observed: the cases are not broken, they are merely excluded from CI by ```python # test/xpu/skip_list_common.py, under "test_torch_xpu.py" # TypeError: map2_ is only implemented on CPU tensors "test_broadcast_fn_map2_xpu", "test_broadcast_fn_map_xpu", ``` which `launch_test` turns into a pytest `-k "not ..."` deselection. No product (kernel/dispatch) change is involved; implementing `map_` on XPU is not the right fix, since the test treats these as CPU-only and CUDA is excluded the same way. Target repo: `torch-xpu-ops`. Fix: delete those three lines.
Verify The fix described above already exists as intel/torch-xpu-ops#5888 — a three-line deletion of exactly those entries, nothing else. It is **APPROVED**, **MERGEABLE**, and its `linux-ut (basic)` job passed (12m13s) with the skip removed, i.e. CI ran both cases unskipped and green. So this run produced **no patch of its own**: a bot branch would be a byte-for-byte duplicate of an approved human PR, and re-proposing it would only add review noise. What it adds instead is independent confirmation, on this BMG runner and today's nightly, that 1. both cases pass once the skip is gone, and 2. the upstream half is genuinely in place on `main`, so no companion upstream change is needed. | Case | Before (skip list as-is) | After (skips removed, per intel/torch-xpu-ops#5888) | |---|---|---| | `test_broadcast_fn_map_xpu` | deselected by CI | pass | | `test_broadcast_fn_map2_xpu` | deselected by CI | pass |
Summary `map_`/`map2_` are CPU-only by design and `test_broadcast` returns early for them on accelerators, so the two XPU cases are not actually broken: the guard in the vendored `test/xpu/test_torch_xpu.py` was widened to cover XPU by intel/torch-xpu-ops#3112 (and upstream by `pytorch/pytorch#197120`, commit `282ec02f`), but intel/torch-xpu-ops#3288 re-added skip-list entries that had just been made redundant, which is the regression reported here. Verified on this BMG runner against nightly `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu` that both cases pass, and that the stale entries in `test/xpu/skip_list_common.py` are all that remains. The correct fix is already open, approved and CI-green as intel/torch-xpu-ops#5888, so no competing patch was produced. - **Outcome:** SKIPPED — fix already proposed; merge intel/torch-xpu-ops#5888 and close this issue. - **Branch:** none. - **Base:** `73a6552c3c122614d2651de2a0c6feb8f81ae613` - **Changed files:** none. - **Nothing was pushed**, and no patch artifact is attached — deliberately, since the only change needed is already in an approved PR.
_Generated by [fix job]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659851858])._
Review Copy into a new comment, keep ONE verdict, add a note. Two verdicts in one comment are dropped as ambiguous. ``` **strong-accepted** **weak-accepted** **weak-rejected** **strong-rejected** **issue-drop** notes: ``` On a batch run add `item=` to say which sub-item the verdict is about, **in the bold text and in the marker** -- the marker is invisible, so the bold line is all a reader sees. One comment per sub-item, since a bare verdict on a batch does not say which test it means and is dropped. `run=` only when judging a run other than the newest, in both places too. A CI DISABLED sub-item, `item=` from the fan-out table: ``` **strong-accepted item=197334** notes: same TensorAssign overload as upstream CUDA, fp8 dispatch list matches ``` Another sub-item of the same batch, judged on an earlier run: ``` **weak-rejected run=35171979678 item=197335** notes: green only because the test is skipped, the kernel still lacks fp8 ``` An `[xpu-alignment]` issue that should not have been filed -- one issue per difference, so no `item=`: ``` **issue-drop** notes: accepted XPU/CUDA numerics difference, nothing to repair ```
