nodes.body:
Automated fix session for this issue. Stages are appended below as they complete.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | pytorch | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Nightly XPU wheel `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu` on BMG, pytorch source tree at `origin/main` (`41d0c916cdc`) for the test file. The test is currently hidden by `@skipIfXpu(msg=".../issues/5375")` in `test/test_torch.py`, so it reports `skipped` as-is; removing the decorator in place (reverted afterwards) exposes the real failure. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_grad_scaling_state_dict_xpu` | REPRODUCED | `AssertionError: False is not true` at `self.assertTrue(isinstance(s1._scale, torch.FloatTensor))` | *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@41d0c916cdc`. `test_grad_scaling_state_dict` asserts the lazily-created `GradScaler._scale` tensor through a *legacy tensor type* check: `isinstance(s1._scale, torch.cuda.FloatTensor)` when `device.type == "cuda"`, and `isinstance(s1._scale, torch.FloatTensor)` otherwise (`test/test_torch.py:6075-6078`). The `else` branch silently assumes "not CUDA means CPU". On XPU, `_scale` is created with `torch.full((), ..., dtype=torch.float32, device=dev)` on the scaler's device (`torch/amp/grad_scaler.py:181`), so it is an XPU tensor -- `t.type()` returns the string `"torch.xpu.FloatTensor"` while `torch.FloatTensor` is the CPU float type, and the `isinstance` is correctly `False`. The test, not the scaler, is wrong. It cannot be fixed by reaching for a `torch.xpu.FloatTensor` class: legacy tensor types are generated only for `CPU`, `CUDA`, `SparseCPU`, `SparseCUDA` in `all_declared_types()` (`torch/csrc/utils/tensor_types.cpp:130-131`), under an explicit `NOTE: Do not add more types here ... maintained for backwards-compatibility only`. XPU legacy types deliberately do not exist. The failure appeared when `pytorch/pytorch#197120` ("[Test][XPU] Refactor test_torch.py and enable XPU", `282ec02fd44`, 2026-10-20) enabled this `@onlyNativeDeviceTypes` test on XPU and silenced it with `@skipIfXpu(msg=".../issues/5375")` (`test/test_torch.py:6061`) -- a skip, not a fix. The fix is to drop the legacy-type branch for a device-generic assertion on what the test actually cares about (the lazily-initialized scale is float32 and sits on the scaler's device) and remove the skip. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- test-side device assumption in pytorch, fixable in place - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch *Automated by fix-root-cause.*

Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | unclear | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Reproduced on the latest XPU nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261019+xpu` on BMG (`Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics`). The test is currently masked by an `@unittest.skipIf(TEST_XPU, ...)` decorator plus a `skip_list_common.py` entry (both added by #3260); per fix-reproduce's "all skipped" rule the decorator was removed in place for one run and then reverted. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_tensor_storage_type_xpu` (all 12 dtypes) | REPRODUCED | `AttributeError: module 'torch.xpu' has no attribute 'FloatStorage'` (and the 11 other storage classes) | With the skip in place the run is `1 skipped`; with it removed, `12 failed`. The vendored copy of the test already selects `torch.xpu` as the expected module for XPU devices, so the failure surfaces as a missing attribute rather than the `None mismatch: None is not ` quoted in the issue; both have the same cause - XPU has no legacy typed storage classes and `Tensor.storage_type()` therefore returns `None`. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@9544ec5e23`, torch-xpu-ops `main@76cc8324`. `Tensor.storage_type()` is `torch/_tensor.py:1360`, which delegates to `TypedStorage._get_legacy_storage_class()` (`torch/storage.py:1499`). That method returns `None` for any device whose type is not in its hardcoded list `["cpu", "cuda", "hpu", privateuse1_backend_name]` (`torch/storage.py:1505-1511`); `xpu` is absent, so it short-circuits to `None` before even looking up a class. Adding `xpu` to that list alone is not enough: the lookup that follows, `getattr(torch.xpu, "FloatStorage")` (`torch/storage.py:1513-1520`), would raise `AttributeError` and be swallowed back into `None`, because `torch/xpu/__init__.py` defines no legacy typed storage classes at all - unlike `torch/cuda/__init__.py:1875-2036`, which defines `_CudaLegacyStorage` plus the 12 dtype subclasses and registers them in `torch._storage_classes`. The same hardcoded device list appears a second time in `_get_device_from_module()` (`torch/storage.py:677-682`), which is what `TypedStorage.__new__` uses to pick the allocation device (`torch/storage.py:765`) and what `_LegacyStorageMeta.__instancecheck__` uses (`torch/storage.py:1534`), so it needs `xpu` too or a `torch.xpu.FloatStorage` would allocate on CPU. Fix strategy: mirror the CUDA module - add `_XpuLegacyStorage` and the 12 dtype subclasses to `torch/xpu/__init__.py`, register them in `torch._storage_classes`, export them from `__all__`, and add `"xpu"` to both device lists in `torch/storage.py`. The torch-xpu-ops side is the companion half: the test is currently masked by an `@unittest.skipIf(TEST_XPU, ...)` decorator in `test/xpu/test_torch_xpu.py` and an entry in `test/xpu/skip_list_common.py` (both added by #3260, whose premise was exactly "XPU does not provide typed storage classes"); both come off once the pytorch half is in the nightly, so pytorch lands first. Collision note for the implement stage: `pytorch/pytorch#194591` is open and rewrites both device lists in `torch/storage.py` to resolve the module generically, and also makes `test/test_torch.py::test_tensor_storage_type` derive its expected module from the device. It does not add the XPU classes, so it does not fix this issue on its own, but if it lands first the `torch/storage.py` half of this patch becomes redundant. This patch therefore leaves `test/test_torch.py` untouched to avoid conflicting with it - note that upstream's own `instantiate_device_type_tests(TestTorchDeviceType, globals())` does not pass `allow_xpu`, so the XPU variant of that test only exists in torch-xpu-ops' vendored copy, which is where the verification runs. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING - framework-level gap with a clear CUDA precedent to mirror - **Target repo:** pytorch (lands first) + torch-xpu-ops (companion) - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch *Automated by fix-root-cause.*

Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | upstream-pytorch (legacy `TypedStorage` surface) | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | needs-human - prior maintainer `issue-drop` still stands | Re-run gate: this is a **human-feedback re-run**. Two human comments landed after the previous agent report: 1. 2026-10-23, review verdict `issue-drop`: "root cause clear and fix correct, but `storage_type()` / `Storage` is deprecated legacy API (upstream stopped extending it [...]); MPS/MTIA also return None. Upstream test_torch does not run this test on XPU, only our vendored copy expects `torch.xpu.FloatStorage`. Keep the skip (#3260), no fix needed." 2. 2026-10-28 08:51, `@torchxpubot fix`. This was a bulk re-trigger: the same account posted 61 identical comments across the issue tracker between 08:43:36 and 08:53:08, so it carries no direction specific to this issue and is not a reversal of (1). The governing input is therefore the `issue-drop` verdict, which rejected the previous run's patch on policy grounds, not on correctness. This run did not re-propose that patch. It re-measured the current state and checked the three premises the verdict rests on. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Measured on the latest XPU nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu` on BMG. | What | Observed | |---|---| | `torch.randn(10, device="xpu").storage_type()` | `None` (CPU returns `torch.FloatStorage`) | | `hasattr(torch.xpu, "FloatStorage")` | `False` | | device list in `TypedStorage._get_legacy_storage_class()` | still `["cpu", "cuda", "hpu", privateuse1]` | | `pytest test_torch_xpu.py -k test_tensor_storage_type` | `12 skipped` | The underlying behaviour is unchanged since the previous run, and this repo's CI is green because the skip from #3260 is in place - both the `@unittest.skipIf(TEST_XPU, ...)` decorator in `test/xpu/test_torch_xpu.py` and the `skip_list_common.py` entry. No change in this repo is needed to keep it that way. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Summary No fix was produced and no branch exists. The `issue-drop` review is the most recent technical direction on this issue, and the `@torchxpubot fix` that started this run was one of 61 bulk re-triggers posted in a ten-minute window rather than a reversal of it, so re-delivering the already-rejected patch would have spent a source build to arrive back at the same rejected proposal. The behaviour does still reproduce on nightly `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu` - `storage_type()` returns `None` on XPU - but the skip keeps this repo green and nothing needs to change to hold that state. Two of the three premises behind the verdict hold as written: `TypedStorage` is deprecated upstream ("it will be removed in the future and `UntypedStorage` will be the only storage class"), and `mps` / `mtia` are absent from the same hardcoded device list, so they return `None` exactly as XPU does. The third premise is now out of date, and it is the one thing worth weighing before closing: upstream **does** run this test on XPU. Commit `282ec02fd4` ("[Test][XPU] Refactor test_torch.py and enable XPU", `pytorch/pytorch#197120`, landed 2026-10-20) switched `test/test_torch.py` to `instantiate_device_type_tests(TestTorchDeviceType, globals(), allow_xpu=True)` and marked this case `@expectedFailureXPU` with a comment pointing at this issue. The xfail keeps upstream CI green either way, so it creates no pressure to fix - but it does leave an upstream xfail referencing an issue that is about to be dropped. - **Verdict:** SKIPPED - the `issue-drop` stands; nothing to change in either repo - **Branch:** none - **Changed files:** none - **Nothing was committed or pushed.** There is no patch artifact for this run. Follow-ups for a human, none of them done here: - This issue is still open. If the drop stands it can be closed as won't-fix. - Consider rewording the upstream `@expectedFailureXPU` comment in `test/test_torch.py` to state the intent ("XPU has no legacy typed storage classes, same as MPS/MTIA") instead of linking an issue that will be dropped. - The skip here is applied twice, decorator plus skip-list entry. Harmless, left untouched.
_Generated by [fix job]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659869909])._
Review Copy into a new comment, keep ONE verdict, add a note. Two verdicts in one comment are dropped as ambiguous. ``` **strong-accepted** **weak-accepted** **weak-rejected** **strong-rejected** **issue-drop** notes: ``` On a batch run add `item=` to say which sub-item the verdict is about, **in the bold text and in the marker** -- the marker is invisible, so the bold line is all a reader sees. One comment per sub-item, since a bare verdict on a batch does not say which test it means and is dropped. `run=` only when judging a run other than the newest, in both places too. A CI DISABLED sub-item, `item=` from the fan-out table: ``` **strong-accepted item=197334** notes: same TensorAssign overload as upstream CUDA, fp8 dispatch list matches ``` Another sub-item of the same batch, judged on an earlier run: ``` **weak-rejected run=35171979678 item=197335** notes: green only because the test is skipped, the kernel still lacks fp8 ``` An `[xpu-alignment]` issue that should not have been filed -- one issue per difference, so no `item=`: ``` **issue-drop** notes: accepted XPU/CUDA numerics difference, nothing to repair ```

issues.title: [upstream_ut] test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu: fill_xpu not implemented for Bits/Float4
issues.body:
## Description
test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_* fail for bits1x8, bits2x4, bits4x2,
bits8, bits16 and float4_e2m1fn_x2. zero_() on a view of these dtypes dispatches
to fill_xpu, which is not implemented for these types.

## Error log
```
  File "test/test_torch.py", line 171, in test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel
    raw.view(dtype).zero_()
NotImplementedError: "fill_xpu" not implemented for 'Bits16'/'Bits8'/'Bits1x8'/'Bits2x4'/'Bits4x2'/'Float4_e2m1fn_x2'
```

## Reproduce
```
python test/test_torch.py TestTorchDeviceTypeXPU.test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_bits16
```

Automated fix session for this issue. Stages below are appended as they complete.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | both | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Nightly XPU wheel `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu` (pytorch `a183c26b`) on BMG (`xpu-agent`), against the pytorch test tree at `origin/main` (`807c4660609`). All six dtypes still fail. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_bits1x8` | REPRODUCED | `NotImplementedError: "fill_xpu" not implemented for 'Bits1x8'` | | `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_bits2x4` | REPRODUCED | `NotImplementedError: "fill_xpu" not implemented for 'Bits2x4'` | | `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_bits4x2` | REPRODUCED | `NotImplementedError: "fill_xpu" not implemented for 'Bits4x2'` | | `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_bits8` | REPRODUCED | `NotImplementedError: "fill_xpu" not implemented for 'Bits8'` | | `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_bits16` | REPRODUCED | `NotImplementedError: "fill_xpu" not implemented for 'Bits16'` | | `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_float4_e2m1fn_x2` | REPRODUCED | `NotImplementedError: "fill_xpu" not implemented for 'Float4_e2m1fn_x2'` | Note on reading the pytest output: upstream already carries `@expectedFailureXPU` on this test, and `expectedFailure` in `torch/testing/_internal/common_device_type.py` *swallows* the exception and returns. So a green `PASSED` line for these node ids means "still failing as expected", not "fixed". The verdict above therefore comes from calling `raw.view(dtype).zero_()` directly, which raises for each of the six dtypes. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `807c4660`, torch-xpu-ops `main@73a6552c`. `aten::zero_` routes XPU to the composite `at::native::zero_` (`native_functions.yaml:6921`, `CPU, MPS, XPU: zero_`). That composite only takes a memset fast path when `self.device() == at::kCPU` (`aten/src/ATen/native/Fill.cpp:152-155`); every other device registered to it falls through to `self.fill_(0)` at `Fill.cpp:157`. The XPU fill kernel's `AT_DISPATCH_V2` list (`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/FillKernel.cpp:35-49`) covers all types plus complex, float8 and barebones-unsigned, but **not** the bitserial `Bits*` types nor `Float4_e2m1fn_x2` -- so `zero_()` on a view of those dtypes raises `NotImplementedError: "fill_xpu" not implemented for 'Bits16'`. Upstream added `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel` together with the CUDA memset path in `3c96a8e511f` (2026-08-31), which registers `CUDA: zero_cuda_` and memsets dense tensors in `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/TensorFactories.cu:37-61`. XPU got no equivalent, and the test was later silenced with `@expectedFailureXPU` (`test/test_torch.py:219`) -- a skip, not a fix. The XPU half of that mirror **already landed here**: `zero_xpu_` memsets dense tensors on the current XPU stream and falls back to `fill_(0)` otherwise (`src/ATen/native/xpu/TensorFactories.cpp:46-55`, merged `c8f531da`, 2026-10-27, intel/torch-xpu-ops#5659). What is missing is the upstream dispatch wiring -- nothing dispatches to it, which is precisely why that PR's regression test calls `at::native::zero_xpu_` directly rather than through `zero_()`. The remaining fix is therefore pytorch-only. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- wire `XPU: zero_xpu_` into `aten::zero_` and drop the now-unnecessary `@expectedFailureXPU`. - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch (also loaded: xpu-kernel) *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Analyzed at:** pytorch `807c4660` - **What I changed:** `aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml` (+2/-1) -- split XPU out of the composite `zero_` dispatch row into its own `XPU: zero_xpu_` entry. `test/test_torch.py` (-1) -- removed the `@expectedFailureXPU` on `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel`. - **Why:** XPU was registered to the composite `at::native::zero_`, whose memset fast path is gated on `self.device() == at::kCPU` (`aten/src/ATen/native/Fill.cpp:152`), so XPU fell through to `self.fill_(0)` (`Fill.cpp:157`), which has no kernel for the bitserial dtypes (`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/FillKernel.cpp:35-49` dispatches all types plus complex, float8 and barebones-unsigned, but not `Bits*`/`Float4_e2m1fn_x2`). Routing XPU to the already-merged `zero_xpu_` (`src/ATen/native/xpu/TensorFactories.cpp:46-55`) takes the device-memset path instead -- the same shape CUDA uses at `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/TensorFactories.cu:37-61`. Codegen emits `TORCH_XPU_API` for XPU dispatch kernels (cf. the generated `ATen/ops/eye_native.h:23` for `eye_out_xpu`), which matches the existing `TORCH_XPU_API` on the `zero_xpu_` definition, so no torch-xpu-ops-side change is needed. The decorator removal is the stale test expectation this fix invalidates. - **Rejected alternative:** adding the missing dtypes to the XPU fill kernel's dispatch list. A fill kernel for a bitserial type has no meaningful scalar value to broadcast, and CUDA solved the same problem with a memset rather than by widening `fill`. - **Skip added:** no (one stale `@expectedFailureXPU` removed) - **Ready for verify:** yes ```diff --- a/aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml +++ b/aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml @@ -6918,8 +6918,9 @@ device_check: NoCheck # TensorIterator variants: method, function dispatch: - CPU, MPS, XPU: zero_ + CPU, MPS: zero_ CUDA: zero_cuda_ + XPU: zero_xpu_ Meta: zero_meta_ --- a/test/test_torch.py +++ b/test/test_torch.py @@ -216,7 +216,6 @@ class TestTorchDeviceType(TestCase): self.assertEqual(base, torch.ones(4, device=device)) @onlyNativeDeviceTypes - @expectedFailureXPU # @dtypes(torch.bits1x8, torch.bits2x4, torch.bits4x2, torch.bits8, torch.bits16, torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2) def test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel(self, device, dtype): ``` *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verify Source build of `agent/fix-issue-5378` (`c4bfa2fe`) with `TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc` and `third_party/xpu.txt` locally pointed at torch-xpu-ops `73a6552c` (the first pin that contains `zero_xpu_`). `torch` resolves to the checkout (`2.16.0a0+gitc4bfa2f`) on an Intel Arc Pro B60 (BMG). The baseline and fixed trees differ only by the two changed files. | Test case | Before | After | |-----------|--------|-------| | `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_bits1x8` | FAIL | PASS | | `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_bits2x4` | FAIL | PASS | | `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_bits4x2` | FAIL | PASS | | `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_bits8` | FAIL | PASS | | `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_bits16` | FAIL | PASS | | `test_zero_dtypes_without_fill_kernel_xpu_float4_e2m1fn_x2` | FAIL | PASS | `Before` was `NotImplementedError: "fill_xpu" not implemented for ''`. The tests now pass with no `@expectedFailureXPU` shielding them, so a green result here is a real pass rather than a swallowed exception. Regression checks on the fixed build: | Suite | Result | |---|---| | `test_torch.py -k xpu` | 740 passed, 155 skipped, 6 xfailed | | `test_torch.py -k "zero and xpu"` | 18 passed | | `test_ops.py -k "zero_ and xpu"` | 143 passed, 28 skipped, 2 xfailed | | `test_tensor_creation_ops.py -k xpu` | 409 passed, 57 skipped | | `test_view_ops.py -k xpu` | 281 passed, 2 skipped | | `test/regressions/test_zero_xpu.py` (this repo) | 2 passed | The strided, transposed and empty-view `zero_` tests in `test_torch.py` matter most here: they must keep taking the `fill_(0)` fallback rather than the memset, and they pass. - **Verdict:** PASSED - **Lint:** clean (`lintrunner -a` on both changed files: no issues, no files rewritten) *Automated by fix-verify.*
Summary **Outcome:** IMPLEMENTING(fix_verified) The XPU half of this bug was already fixed and merged here as `zero_xpu_` (intel/torch-xpu-ops#5659) -- nothing upstream dispatched to it, so `aten::zero_` on XPU still went through the composite `zero_`, whose memset fast path is CPU-only, and fell back to `fill_(0)`, which has no kernel for the bitserial `Bits*` dtypes or `Float4_e2m1fn_x2`. The remaining fix is one line of upstream dispatch -- route `XPU: zero_xpu_` the way CUDA routes `zero_cuda_` -- plus removing the `@expectedFailureXPU` that was silencing the test. On a source build all six dtypes now zero correctly, and 1591 XPU tests across five suites (including the strided/transposed/empty-view `zero_` cases that must still take the `fill_(0)` fallback) show no regression. - **Branch:** `agent/fix-issue-5378` -- in the **pytorch** checkout, not this repo - **Base:** `807c4660609ba5ae290125608309e228659a4626` (pytorch `origin/main`) - **Changed files:** `aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml`, `test/test_torch.py` - **Landing order:** upstream `third_party/xpu.txt` pins `8c125b2e`, which predates the `zero_xpu_` commit `c8f531da`. The PR must land after (or stacked on) a pin bump that includes it, or the XPU build cannot resolve `at::native::zero_xpu_`. Verification used a local `xpu.txt` override, which is deliberately not part of the patch. - **Nothing was pushed.** The patch is exported as a workflow artifact for a human to review and apply.

issues.title: [xccl] Flight recorder does not mark completed works: state stays "scheduled"/"started" and last_completed_collective is -1
issues.body:
> Drafted with assistance from an AI coding agent (Claude Code) and reviewed/verified by me on 4x Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550.

### Summary

XCCL's flight recorder never transitions entries to the `completed` state, so
trace-verification assertions that pass on NCCL fail on XPU.

### Observed vs expected

Running the upstream flight-recorder tests against XCCL (ported in place to be
device-agnostic), three fields disagree with the NCCL behaviour:

| Field | XCCL | NCCL |
|---|---|---|
| `pg_status["0"]["last_completed_collective"]` | `-1` | `2` |
| `entries[-1]["state"]` | `scheduled` / `started` | `completed` |
| `entries[-1]["time_discovered_completed_ns"]` | `None` | not `None` |

Everything else in the trace is correct: `pg_config`, `ranks`, `record_id`,
`thread_id`/`thread_name`, entry counts, and `profiling_name` (modulo the
expected `xccl:` vs `nccl:` prefix).

### Reproduction

PyTorch `2.15.0a0+git4d3ac9e`, oneCCL 2022.1, 4x Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550,
`triton-xpu 3.8.0+git1e2d42a0`.

The equivalent check in torch-xpu-ops' own
`test/xpu/distributed/test_c10d_xccl.py` (branch `daisyden/distributed_2.13`) is
commented out with the note "Watchdog will fix marking works completed", which
suggests this is known:

    # self.assertEqual(str(pg_status["0"]["last_completed_collective"]), "2")
    # self.assertEqual(last["state"], "completed") # Watchdog will fix marking works completed

### Impact

8 test methods (18 parametrizations) in `test/distributed/test_c10d_nccl.py`
`NCCLTraceTest` cannot be enabled for XPU: `test_short_json`,
`test_short_pickle`, `test_long`, `test_trace_while_all_works_retired`,
`test_trace_while_active`, `test_batched_send_recv`,
`test_batched_send_recv_compiled`, `test_individual_send_recv`.

**Before closing this ticket, remove the corresponding `@skipIfXpu` lines from the upstream tests.**

issues.title: [xccl] ProcessGroupXCCL does not implement registerOnCompletionHook
issues.body:
> Drafted with assistance from an AI coding agent (Claude Code) and reviewed/verified by me on 4x Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550.

### Summary

`ProcessGroupXCCL` does not override `Backend::registerOnCompletionHook()`, so
registering an onCompletion hook on an XCCL process group raises instead of
working:

    RuntimeError: Only ProcessGrouppNCCL supports onCompletion hook, but got xccl backend.

The Python binding `_register_on_completion_hook` is visible on
`ProcessGroupXCCL` (inherited), which makes the capability look supported until
it is called.

### Root cause

`torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/Backend.hpp:672` provides the default:

    virtual void registerOnCompletionHook(
        std::function<void(std::shared_ptr<WorkInfo>)>&& hook) {
      TORCH_CHECK(
          false,
          "Only ProcessGrouppNCCL supports onCompletion hook, but got ",
          getBackendName(),
          " backend.");
    }

`ProcessGroupXCCL.hpp` has no override, so XCCL inherits the throwing default.
`waitForPendingWorks()` has the same shape immediately below it and may be
affected too.

### Reproduction

PyTorch `2.15.0a0+git4d3ac9e`, oneCCL 2022.1, 4x Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550.

### Impact

All 5 tests in `WorkHookTest` in `test/distributed/test_c10d_nccl.py` cannot be
enabled for XPU: `test_on_completion_hook_broadcast`,
`test_on_completion_hook_mixed_ops`, `test_on_completion_hook_with_ddp`,
`test_on_completion_hook_all_gather_object`, and `test_on_completion_hook_seq`.

**Before closing this ticket, remove the corresponding `@skipIfXpu` lines from the upstream tests.**

issues.title: [xccl] ProcessGroupXCCL does not implement collective time estimation
issues.body:
> Drafted with assistance from an AI coding agent (Claude Code) and reviewed/verified by me on 4x Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550.

### Summary

`ProcessGroupXCCL` does not override `Backend::supportsTimeEstimation()`, so
collective time estimation is unavailable on XPU:

    NotImplementedError: collective time estimator is not supported in the current
    version of backend

### Root cause

`torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/Backend.hpp:175` defaults to unsupported:

    virtual bool supportsTimeEstimation() const {
      return false;
    }

`ProcessGroupXCCL` has no override, so XCCL reports no support. Note the Python
bindings `_supports_time_estimate`, `_start_time_estimate` and
`_end_time_estimate` are all visible on `ProcessGroupXCCL` (inherited), which
makes the capability look available until it is used.

By contrast `ProcessGroupNCCL.hpp` overrides it and returns true when built with
`NCCL_SIM_INFO_INITIALIZER`.

### Reproduction

PyTorch `2.15.0a0+git4d3ac9e`, oneCCL 2022.1, 4x Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550.

### Impact

- `CommTest::test_time_estimate_nccl` in `test/distributed/test_c10d_nccl.py`
  cannot be enabled for XPU.
- `test/inductor/test_comm_analysis.py` is only partly portable for the same
  reason: its two NCCL tests assert `backend.supports_time_estimate` is true, and
  `_nccl_estimate()` in `torch/_inductor/comm_analysis.py` hardcodes
  `torch.device("cuda")`, so the Inductor collective-runtime estimator has no XPU
  path.

**Before closing this ticket, remove the corresponding `@skipIfXpu` lines from the upstream tests.**

nodes.body:
Created oneCCL (MLSL) feature request **MLSL-4970** for this.

oneCCL 2022.1 has only `onecclGroupStart()`/`onecclGroupEnd()`, with no equivalent of `ncclGroupSimulateEnd(ncclSimInfo_t*)`. The request is for an `onecclGroupSimulateEnd(onecclSimInfo_t*)` API that returns the estimated time of the grouped operations without launching them, plus a way to detect whether it is supported.

Once that is available, the torch-xpu-ops follow-up is to implement `supportsTimeEstimation()`, `startTimeEstimate()` and `endTimeEstimate()` in `ProcessGroupXCCL`, and to add an XPU path to `_nccl_estimate()` in `torch/_inductor/comm_analysis.py`.

issues.title: [xccl] Profiler kernel events lack collective metadata annotations
issues.body:
> Drafted with assistance from an AI coding agent (Claude Code) and reviewed/verified by me on 4x Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550.

### Summary

Kineto `kernel` events for XCCL collectives do not carry the collective metadata
that NCCL kernels get, so profiler traces cannot be correlated with collective
operations on XPU.

### Observed

Profiling a `dist.all_reduce` on XCCL with
`ProfilerActivity.CPU + ProfilerActivity.XPU`, the collective kernel is recorded:

    name: oneccl_reduce_base<float, 2, 16, 1, 1, 2>
    cat : kernel

but its `args` contain only SYCL/Level-Zero plumbing:

    ['External id', 'appended', 'appended_rel_to_start', 'context', 'correlation',
     'device', 'engine_index', 'engine_ordinal', 'kernel_id', 'l0 queue',
     'source_file_name', 'source_line_number', 'submitted',
     'submitted_rel_to_start', 'sycl queue', 'sycl_enqk_begin',
     'sycl_enqk_begin_rel_to_start', 'sycl_invocation_id', 'sycl_node_id',
     'sycl_task_begin', 'sycl_task_begin_rel_to_start']

### Expected

NCCL kernel events are annotated with, at minimum:

    Collective name, dtype, In msg nelems, Out msg nelems

### Reproduction

PyTorch `2.15.0a0+git4d3ac9e`, oneCCL 2022.1, 4x Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550.

### Impact

`CommTest::test_profiler_nccl_annotations_on_gpu_kernels` (both
`use_python_export` parametrizations) in `test/distributed/test_c10d_nccl.py`
cannot be enabled for XPU. It fails with
`AssertionError: 0 not greater than 0 : Expected at least one GPU kernel with NCCL annotations`.

**Before closing this ticket, remove the corresponding `@skipIfXpu` lines from the upstream tests.**

issues.title: [xccl] ProcessGroupXCCL inherits unimplemented Backend virtuals (splitting, shrinking, suspend/resume, memory stats, comm_split_count)
issues.body:
> Drafted with assistance from an AI coding agent (Claude Code) and reviewed/verified by me on 4x Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550.

### Summary

`ProcessGroupXCCL` does not override a family of `Backend` virtuals, so each one
silently inherits a `false` or throwing default. The Python bindings remain
visible on `ProcessGroupXCCL`, so the capabilities look supported until they are
used.

This is an umbrella for the pattern; #5382 and #5383 are two already-filed
instances of it.

### Unimplemented virtuals

| Virtual | Default in `torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/Backend.hpp` | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| `supportsSplitting` | `:157` returns `false` | `split_group` fails: "No backend for the parent process group or its backend does not support splitting" |
| `supportsTimeEstimation` | `:175` returns `false` | see #5383 |
| `supportsShrinking` | `:193` returns `false` | `shrink_group` raises `TypeError: Process group backend ... does not support shrinking operations` |
| `registerOnCompletionHook` | `:672` `TORCH_CHECK(false)` | see #5382 |
| `waitForPendingWorks` | `:681` `TORCH_CHECK(false)` | untested, same shape |
| `suspend` | `:795` `TORCH_CHECK(false)` | "Backend xccl does not support suspend" |
| `resume` | `:801` `TORCH_CHECK(false)` | as above |
| `getMemoryStats` | `:807` `TORCH_CHECK(false)` | "Backend xccl does not support getMemoryStats" |

Two adjacent gaps of a slightly different kind:

- **`comm_split_count`** is bound for `ProcessGroupNCCL` only
  (`torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/init.cpp:3937`), so
  `AttributeError: 'ProcessGroupXCCL' object has no attribute 'comm_split_count'`.
- **`Work::getTimeout`** (`torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/Work.cpp:197`) throws
  "This Backend doesn't support getTimeout." This is on `Work`, not `Backend`.

### Reproduction

PyTorch `2.15.0a0+git4d3ac9e`, oneCCL 2022.1, 4x Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550.

The `ProcessGroupXCCL.Options` row was verified separately on PyTorch
`2.15.0a0+gita2f26c4`, 4x Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100.

### Impact

24 tests in `ProcessGroupNCCLGroupTest` (`test/distributed/test_c10d_nccl.py`)
cannot be enabled for XPU:

- splitting (6): `test_comm_split_group`, `..._backend_filter`,
  `..._backend_validation`, `..._mixed_backend`, `..._out_of_order_ranks`,
  `test_comm_split_initialized_parent_with_lazy_default`
- shrinking (8): `test_shrink_group_basic`, `..._flags`, `..._backend_properties`,
  `..._multiple_comms`, `..._multiple_exclusions`, `..._multiple_iterations`,
  `..._performance`, `..._vs_abort_reinit_performance`
- `comm_split_count` (5): `test_comm_split_subgroup`, `test_non_blocking_init`,
  `test_non_blocking_with_eager_init`, `test_abort_in_destroy_multi_pgs`,
  `test_abort_in_destroy_mixed_empty_pgs`
- suspend/resume (2): `test_suspend`, `test_resume`
- memory stats (1): `test_get_memory_stats`
- `Work::getTimeout` (2): `test_extend_nccl_pg_timeout_backend0`,
  `test_extend_nccl_pg_timeout_backend_xccl`

### Missing TORCH_XCCL_* environment knobs

NCCL exposes several policy knobs that have no `TORCH_XCCL_*` counterpart, so the
corresponding behaviour cannot be exercised or configured on XPU:

| NCCL env var | XCCL equivalent | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `TORCH_NCCL_PROPAGATE_ERROR` | none | error-propagation policy |
| `TORCH_NCCL_HEARTBEAT_TIMEOUT_SEC` | none | watchdog heartbeat / dump-on-timeout |
| `TORCH_NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING` | none | async error handling mode |

(`TORCH_NCCL_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE` and `TORCH_NCCL_DEBUG_INFO_TEMP_FILE` do have
backend-neutral `TORCH_FR_*` spellings and are fine.)

Blocks 9 further tests, ported to be device-agnostic but gated with `@skipIfXpu`:

- `NcclErrorHandlingTest` (8): error-propagation and blocking-wait behaviour
- `NcclErrorDumpTest` (1): dump-on-timeout via the heartbeat monitor

Also NCCL-library-specific and not portable: `NcclUserBufferRegistrationTest` (2)
needs `NCCL_ALGO`/`NCCL_DEBUG`/`NCCL_DEBUG_SUBSYS` and scrapes NCCL debug logs;
`ProcessGroupNCCLLargerScaleTest` (3) needs `comm_split_count`; `CommTest::test_intra_node_comm_all_reduce` (2) uses NCCL-only intra-node comm (`_get_intra_node_comm_usage_counter`) and fails on XPU with `AttributeError: module 'torch.distributed' has no attribute 'ProcessGroupNCCL'`.

### Further gaps outside the Backend-virtual family

These are distinct root causes, each blocking tests that cannot be enabled for XPU.
The `ProcessGroupNCCLGroupTest` ones are left failing (not skipped) so the gap stays
visible in CI; the `test_c10d_torchcomms.py` one is gated with `@skipIfXpu`:

| Gap | Detail | Tests |
|---|---|---|
| `_get_process_group_uid` is NCCL-only | `torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:2224` returns `-1` unless `isinstance(backend, ProcessGroupNCCL)`, even though `ProcessGroupXCCL.uid` exists. Already noted by @guangyey on pytorch/pytorch#183625: "This function name is `_get_process_group_uid` but only return backend `ProcessGroupNCCL`'s uid. It doesn't make sense." | `test_get_uid` |
| no `_DEFAULT_PG_XCCL_TIMEOUT` | `torch.distributed.constants.default_pg_nccl_timeout` falls back to `None` when `_DEFAULT_PG_NCCL_TIMEOUT` is absent, so tests comparing against it see `None` while the actual default is `0:30:00` | `test_init_process_group_nccl_timeout` |
| `c10d::gather_into_tensor_` unregistered for XPU | `NotImplementedError: The operator 'c10d::gather_into_tensor_' is not currently implemented for the XPU device` | `test_gather_single` |
| XCCL does not raise `DistBackendError` | abort/error paths surface a different exception type than NCCL | `test_abort_in_destroy_pg`, `test_nccl_dist_backend_error` |
| extra-context check is NVML-specific | `_helper_test_extra_cuda_context_by_nvml` uses `pynvml`; the memory-based fallback also measures CUDA context. Likely not portable as written | `test_extra_cuda_context` |
| `ProcessGroupXCCL.Options` has no `config` | `ProcessGroupNCCL.Options` carries a `config` (`ncclConfig_t`), so tests set `opts.config.cga_cluster_size` / `opts.config.max_ctas` directly. `ProcessGroupXCCL.Options` exposes only `backend`, `enable_reconfigure`, `global_ranks_in_group`, `group_name`, `is_high_priority_stream` -- the sub-struct is absent, so those knobs cannot be written. `is_high_priority_stream` itself does exist. On an XPU-only build `dist.ProcessGroupNCCL` is absent entirely, so the tests fail with `AttributeError: module 'torch.distributed' has no attribute 'ProcessGroupNCCL'` before reaching the config | `test_c10d_torchcomms.py`: `test_new_group_with_pg_options`, `test_new_group_sequential_pg_options_produce_distinct_groups`,test_new_group_qualified_backend_passes_through |

Note `c10d::allreduce_` also has no `SparseXPU` registration, which blocks
`SparseCollective::test_ddp_set_sparse_metadata` and
`ProcessGroupNCCLOpTest::test_sparse_allreduce_ops` (both skipped with
`@skipIfXpu`).

**Before closing this ticket, remove the corresponding `@skipIfXpu` lines from the upstream tests.**

Suspend/Shrinking/Resume functionalities are not supported by oneCCL.
Split: was enabled for TorchComms, so it is possible that the support was not enabled for C10D backend. @Chao1Han Can you please confirm?
ProcessGroupXCCL.Options does not have config options (as ncclConfig_t) due to not having support from oneCCL: We can open a feature request.

Can investigate: c10d::gather_into_tensor/timeout/memstat support

nodes.body:
Created oneCCL (MLSL) feature requests for the two items above:

1. `ProcessGroupXCCL.Options` has no `config` (equivalent of `ncclConfig_t`): **MLSL-4968**. oneCCL 2022.1 already declares `onecclConfig_t` (with `cgaClusterSize`, `minCTAs`, `maxCTAs`, ...) and `onecclCommInitRankConfig`, but the legacy plugin currently ignores every field except `multiThreaded`. So the request is for these fields to take effect end-to-end, be inherited across split, and be queryable. It is linked to the CTA-policy work in MLSL-4044. Exposing `config` on `ProcessGroupXCCL.Options` is then a torch-xpu-ops follow-up.
2. `getMemoryStats` (equivalent of `ncclCommMemStats`): **MLSL-4969**. This needs a new per-communicator memory statistics API in oneCCL; `ProcessGroupXCCL::getMemoryStats()` would be built on top of it.

issues.title: test_nn.py cases fail under dynamo wrapper (PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_DYNAMO=1) on XPU
issues.body:
## Describe the bug

When running the following `test/test_nn.py` cases with the dynamo wrapper (`PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_DYNAMO=1`), they all fail. They pass in the normal (non-dynamo) test run.

Affected cases:
- `test_Hardshrink_no_batch_dim_xpu`
- `test_Softshrink_no_batch_dim_xpu`
- `test_Conv1d_zero_batch_xpu_fp32`
- `test_Conv2d_zero_batch_xpu_fp32`
- `test_Conv3d_zero_batch_xpu_fp32`
- `test_Conv1d_zero_batch_xpu_tf32`
- `test_Conv2d_zero_batch_xpu_tf32`
- `test_Conv3d_zero_batch_xpu_tf32`
- `test_Embedding_sparse_xpu`
- `test_EmbeddingBag_sparse_xpu`

## Repro

```
PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_DYNAMO=1 python test/test_nn.py TestNN.test_Hardshrink_no_batch_dim_xpu
PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_DYNAMO=1 python test/test_nn.py TestNN.test_EmbeddingBag_sparse_xpu
```

## Observed failures

There appear to be two distinct root causes, both in the dynamo / compiled-autograd path.

**1. Hardshrink / Softshrink** — compiled autograd fails running fake tensor meta for the backward op:

```
torch._dynamo.exc.TorchRuntimeError: RuntimeError when making fake tensor call
  Explanation: Dynamo failed to run FX node with fake tensors:
  call_function torch._dynamo.compiled_autograd.ops.HardshrinkBackward0(...)
  got RuntimeError('TensorIterator does not support symbolic shapes; please
  implement this operator in torch/_refs using the elementwise or reduction helpers ...')

E ... failed while attempting to run meta for aten.hardshrink_backward.default
E RuntimeError: TensorIterator does not support symbolic shapes; ...
```

**2. Embedding / EmbeddingBag / Conv zero-batch** — `IndexError` in dynamo PGO stride handling:

```
File ".../torch/_dynamo/pgo.py", line 340, in is_stride_dynamic
    return self.stride[dim] is auto_dynamic
IndexError: tuple index out of range

from user code:
   File "<eval_with_key>.6", line 5, in forward
    getitem = inputs[0]
```

## Environment
- Python 3.10.20, pytest 7.3.2
- torch 2.15.0.dev20260907+xpu (git f2ac3133587499ab2dfe33d5f4009bf89accebb0)
- Device: XPU (`torch.xpu.is_available()` = True)
- Reproduce with [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#189653]

## Notes
Both root causes look like they live in upstream PyTorch (compiled autograd / dynamo PGO / backward meta implementations) rather than in torch-xpu-ops kernels; the XPU dynamo test config surfaces them.

Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | batch-bug (heterogeneous) | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | pytorch | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | The 10 affected `test_nn.py` cases group into the two distinct root causes the issue describes, and the maintainer asked for them to be handled separately. First, the six `Conv*_zero_batch` cases no longer show the PGO `IndexError` reported in September -- they now fail earlier with a `NoneType` gradient in compiled autograd, so this run treats them as a **third** root cause rather than folding them in with the sparse-embedding group. Second, every corresponding CPU case (`test_Hardshrink_no_batch_dim`, `test_Conv1d_zero_batch`, `test_Embedding_sparse`, `test_EmbeddingBag_sparse`) passes under the same dynamo wrapper, so all three signatures are specific to the accelerator path in `common_nn.py::test_accelerator`. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@9544ec5e23`. All three root causes are in device-agnostic pytorch code; none is in a torch-xpu-ops kernel. Two of the three reproduce on CPU tensors alone once compiled autograd is enabled, which matches the issue's own reading: the XPU dynamo test config is what exposes them, because `test_nn.py`'s accelerator variants are the only `PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_DYNAMO=1` cases that ever run on a machine with an accelerator (the CUDA variants are dropped from collection on the CPU-only `dynamo_wrapped` shards). **A. Hardshrink / Softshrink (sub-items 1-2).** `hardshrink_backward` is a structured op whose only meta function is `TORCH_META_FUNC(hardshrink_backward)` in `aten/src/ATen/native/Activation.cpp:210`, which calls `build_borrowing_binary_op` -- TensorIterator, which refuses symbolic shapes. FakeTensor prefers a registered meta kernel over decomposing (`torch/_subclasses/fake_tensor.py:3341-3360`), so compiled autograd's symbolic trace of `HardshrinkBackward0` lands on the C++ meta and raises. `softshrink_backward` had the identical problem until `pytorch/pytorch#200802` (merged `b262babb27`, 2026-10-18) restored its decomposition and added it to the core ATen set -- which is why sub-item 2 is expected to be already fixed on current main while sub-item 1 still fails. `hardshrink_backward` and `softshrink_backward` share one kernel in eager (`shrink_backward_stub`, dispatched from `Activation.cpp:363` and `:375`, implemented once in `aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/Activation.cpp:683` and `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/ActivationSoftshrinkKernel.cu:36`) and have identical meta functions, so that same decomposition is bit-exact for `hardshrink_backward`. **B. Conv zero-batch (sub-items 3-8).** `_convolution_double_backward` (`aten/src/ATen/native/Convolution.cpp:1831`) wraps the `gW` and `gI` computations in `if (input_nonempty)` (`:1863`, `:1922`, `:1977`) and returns **undefined** tensors for them when the input has no elements, ignoring the gradients it was asked for -- confirmed directly: `_convolution_double_backward` with a `(0, 4, 10)` input and all three incoming grads defined returns `(ggO, None, None)`, where the non-empty call returns all three. Its single-backward sibling `convolution_backward` handles the same empty case explicitly and returns defined zeros (`ConvBackend::Empty`, `Convolution.cpp:2230-2239`). Eager tolerates the undefined grads because `InputBuffer::add` early-returns on them (`torch/csrc/autograd/input_buffer.cpp:358`), but compiled autograd decides graph structure at trace time from all-defined dummy outputs and emits an unconditional accumulation node (`torch/csrc/dynamo/python_compiled_autograd.cpp:1121-1128` -> `torch/_dynamo/compiled_autograd.py:874`), so the runtime `None` reaches `torch.add` and raises `TypeError`. **C. Its three preceding guards cover `auto_dynamic` / `auto_unset` / a non-static size but not a short tuple, so the sparse gradient that compiled autograd wraps as a graph input (`_automatic_dynamic`, `builder.py:5144`) raises `IndexError`. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- three independent, source-local fixes - **Target repo:** pytorch (all three sub-items) - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch (A, B), inductor (C) *Automated by fix-root-cause.*

### 🐛 Describe the bug

During upstream tests generalization a new failing test case has been discovered. It needs further investigation.

Test case:
`test_cuda_multigpu.py::TestMultiGPUDeviceXPU::test_stream_event_nogil_xpu`

The test hangs infinitely on BMG platform it was tested. When interrupted by `Ctrl + C` it shows the following error log:

<details>

<summary>Error log</summary>

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/usr/lib/python3.12/threading.py", line 1073, in _bootstrap_inner
    self.run()
```

nodes.body:
Starting automated fix on this issue. Follow progress in the [workflow run]([运行记录：intel/torch-xpu-ops@run:40659890425]). **Target:** `test_cuda_multigpu.py::TestMultiGPUDeviceXPU::test_stream_event_nogil_xpu` (hangs on BMG)
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | unclear | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Reproduced on the XPU nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu`, on an 8x BMG (Arc Pro B60) runner, against the pytorch source tree at `origin/main` (`807c4660609`). The test file was renamed upstream since the issue was filed (`test/test_cuda_multigpu.py` -> `test/test_multigpu.py`), and the case is currently skipped by a `skipXPUIf` decorator pointing at this issue, so the decorator was removed temporarily to get a real result. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_multigpu.py::TestMultiGPUDeviceXPU::test_stream_event_nogil_xpu` | REPRODUCED | `AssertionError: 1861.293125 not greater than 2437.1396556` | The failure signature differs from the one in the issue body. Here the case fails deterministically on its first iteration (`_stream_synchronize`) at the final relative-timing assertion, before it ever reaches `_event_wait`. The reported `assertTrue(s0.query())` failure inside `_event_wait` -- and the infinite hang it caused, because the child thread died before its `c2p.put()` and the parent then blocked forever on `c2p.get()` -- no longer reproduces: with the timing problem worked around, all three sync functions pass and every `query()` assertion in `_event_wait` holds. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@807c4660609`. `test_stream_event_nogil` checks that stream/event synchronization releases the GIL, by spinning a fixed `FIFTY_MIL_CYCLES` on two devices from two threads and asserting the measured times overlap: `assertGreater(parent_time + child_time, total_time * 1.3)` (`test/test_multigpu.py:572`). Both quantities come from `Event.elapsed_time()` spanning the whole `sync_func` call, so they also include any host-side stall between `e_tik.record()` and the spin kernel actually launching (`test/test_multigpu.py:460-473`). On XPU the first `_sleep()` in a process pays a one-time lazy initialization that lands inside that window: `at::xpu::sleep` compiles its spin kernel at runtime via `sycl_ext_oneapi_kernel_compiler` (torch-xpu-ops `src/ATen/xpu/Sleep.cpp:26-62`), a documented workaround for PVC's bundled IGC not exposing `ext_oneapi_clock_sub_group`. Measured on BMG: the first `_sleep()` costs 1212 ms (process-global bundle build) plus 517 ms for the first launch on a second device, against 0.1-0.3 ms once warm. That inflates the first iteration's `parent_time` to ~1700 ms around a ~21 ms spin, so `parent_time + child_time` degenerates to `total_time` (observed ratio 0.993 vs the required 1.3) and the case fails deterministically on its first `sync_func`. The behaviour the test actually targets is correct on XPU: `THXPStream_synchronize` and `THXPEvent_synchronize` both take `pybind11::gil_scoped_release` (`torch/csrc/xpu/Stream.cpp:99-107`, `torch/csrc/xpu/Event.cpp:122-130`), and with the lazy init outside the measured window the two threads do overlap - 45 instrumented samples across all three sync functions gave ratios 1.598-1.792, and every `query()` assertion inside `_event_wait` held. The case surfaced now because `pytorch/pytorch#197241` (merged, `06413cc8b6c`, 2026-10-28) generalized `test_cuda_multigpu.py` into `test/test_multigpu.py` and enabled it for XPU, landing the `@skipXPUIf(True, ...)` at `test/test_multigpu.py:524` that points at this issue. That skip confirms the failure; it is not a fix. Upstream already treats first-call initialization as a measurement hazard rather than a product defect: `get_cycles_per_ms` throws away the two highest and two lowest of ten samples precisely because "the very first cuda call likely does a bunch of init, which takes much longer than subsequent calls" (`torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py:6303-6345`). The fix applies the same treatment here - warm up the two devices the test uses with a throwaway `_sleep()` before the measurement loop, and drop the `@skipXPUIf`. Nothing in torch-xpu-ops needs to change: the online compilation in `Sleep.cpp` is a deliberate, already-TODO'd tradeoff, and `_sleep` is a test-only utility. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING - device-agnostic warmup removes the lazy-init cost from the timed window. - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** upstream-pytorch *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Analyzed at:** pytorch@807c4660609 - **What I changed:** `test/test_multigpu.py` (+7/-1) - dropped the stale `@skipXPUIf(True, ...)` decorator on `test_stream_event_nogil` and added a warmup that runs a throwaway `device_module._sleep(1)` + `synchronize()` on `devices[:2]` before the measurement loop. - **Why:** the measured windows span the whole `sync_func` call (`test/test_multigpu.py:460-473`), so the one-time XPU spin-kernel online compilation (1212 ms process-global plus 517 ms for the first launch on a second device) landed inside the first measurement and collapsed the `1.3` overlap ratio at `test/test_multigpu.py:572` to 0.993. Moving that cost into an unmeasured warmup is the same treatment `get_cycles_per_ms` applies by discarding its extreme samples because "the very first cuda call likely does a bunch of init" (`torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py:6303-6345`). The assertion and its `1.3` factor are untouched. - **Skip added:** no (an existing stale skip was removed) - **Ready for verify:** yes ```diff @@ -521,10 +521,16 @@ class TestMultiGPUDevice(TestCase): p2c.get() c2p.put(sync_func(device_module, FIFTY_MIL_CYCLES)) - @skipXPUIf(True, "[地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#5402]") @deviceCountAtLeast(2) def test_stream_event_nogil(self, devices): device_module = torch.get_device_module(devices[0]) + # The first _sleep() on a device pays one-time lazy initialization (on + # XPU, around a second of online spin-kernel compilation), which the + # measurements below would otherwise charge to the first sync_func. + for device in devices[:2]: + with device_module.device(device): + device_module._sleep(1) + device_module.synchronize() for sync_func in [ self._stream_synchronize, self._event_synchronize, ``` *Automated by fix-implement.*

Reproduce
Reproduced on the XPU nightly wheel 2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu, on an 8x BMG
(Arc Pro B60) runner, against the pytorch source tree at origin/main
(807c4660609). The test file was renamed upstream since the issue was
filed (test/test_cuda_multigpu.py -> test/test_multigpu.py), and the case
is currently skipped by a skipXPUIf decorator pointing at this issue, so the
decorator was removed temporarily to get a real result.



Test case
Verdict
Observed




test_multigpu.py::TestMultiGPUDeviceXPU::test_stream_event_nogil_xpu
REPRODUCED
AssertionError: 1861.293125 not greater than 2437.1396556



The failure signature differs from the one in the issue body. Here the case
fails deterministically on its first iteration (_stream_synchronize) at the
final relative-timing assertion, before it ever reaches _event_wait. The
reported assertTrue(s0.query()) failure inside _event_wait -- and the
infinite hang it caused, because the child thread died before its
c2p.put() and the parent then blocked forever on c2p.get() -- no longer
reproduces: with the timing problem worked around, all three sync functions
pass and every query() assertion in _event_wait holds.
Automated by fix-reproduce.



Root Cause
Analyzed at pytorch origin/main@807c4660609.
test_stream_event_nogil checks that stream/event synchronization releases the
GIL, by spinning a fixed FIFTY_MIL_CYCLES on two devices from two threads and
asserting the measured times overlap:
assertGreater(parent_time + child_time, total_time * 1.3)
(test/test_multigpu.py:572). Both quantities come from Event.elapsed_time()
spanning the whole sync_func call, so they also include any host-side stall
between e_tik.record() and the spin kernel actually launching
(test/test_multigpu.py:460-473). On XPU the first _sleep() in a process pays a
one-time lazy initialization that lands inside that window: at::xpu::sleep
compiles its spin kernel at runtime via sycl_ext_oneapi_kernel_compiler
(torch-xpu-ops src/ATen/xpu/Sleep.cpp:26-62), a documented workaround for PVC's
bundled IGC not exposing ext_oneapi_clock_sub_group. Measured on BMG: the first
_sleep() costs 1212 ms (process-global bundle build) plus 517 ms for the first
launch on a second device, against 0.1-0.3 ms once warm. That inflates the first
iteration's parent_time to ~1700 ms around a ~21 ms spin, so
parent_time + child_time degenerates to total_time (observed ratio 0.993 vs
the required 1.3) and the case fails deterministically on its first sync_func.
The behaviour the test actually targets is correct on XPU:
THXPStream_synchronize and THXPEvent_synchronize both take
pybind11::gil_scoped_release (torch/csrc/xpu/Stream.cpp:99-107,
torch/csrc/xpu/Event.cpp:122-130), and with the lazy init outside the measured
window the two threads do overlap - 45 instrumented samples across all three sync
functions gave ratios 1.598-1.792, and every query() assertion inside
_event_wait held. The case surfaced now because pytorch/pytorch#197241
(merged, 06413cc8b6c, 2026-10-28) generalized test_cuda_multigpu.py into
test/test_multigpu.py and enabled it for XPU, landing the @skipXPUIf(True, ...)
at test/test_multigpu.py:524 that points at this issue. That skip confirms the
failure; it is not a fix.
Upstream already treats first-call initialization as a measurement hazard rather
than a product defect: get_cycles_per_ms throws away the two highest and two
lowest of ten samples precisely because "the very first cuda call likely does a
bunch of init, which takes much longer than subsequent calls"
(torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py:6303-6345). The fix applies the same
treatment here - warm up the two devices the test uses with a throwaway _sleep()
before the measurement loop, and drop the @skipXPUIf. Nothing in torch-xpu-ops
needs to change: the online compilation in Sleep.cpp is a deliberate,
already-TODO'd tradeoff, and _sleep is a test-only utility.

Verdict: IMPLEMENTING - device-agnostic warmup removes the lazy-init cost from the timed window.
Target repo: pytorch
Domain: upstream-pytorch

Automated by fix-root-cause.



Implement Result

Target repo: pytorch
Analyzed at: pytorch@807c4660609
What I changed: test/test_multigpu.py (+7/-1) - dropped the stale
@skipXPUIf(True, ...) decorator on test_stream_event_nogil and added a
warmup that runs a throwaway device_module._sleep(1) + synchronize() on
devices[:2] before the measurement loop.
Why: the measured windows span the whole sync_func call
(test/test_multigpu.py:460-473), so the one-time XPU spin-kernel online
compilation (1212 ms process-global plus 517 ms for the first launch on a
second device) landed inside the first measurement and collapsed the 1.3
overlap ratio at test/test_multigpu.py:572 to 0.993. Moving that cost into
an unmeasured warmup is the same treatment get_cycles_per_ms applies by
discarding its extreme samples because "the very first cuda call likely does
a bunch of init" (torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py:6303-6345). The
assertion and its 1.3 factor are untouched.
Skip added: no (an existing stale skip was removed)
Ready for verify: yes

Automated fix session for intel/torch-xpu-ops#5403 — `TestMultiGPUDeviceXPU::test_caching_pinned_memory_multi_gpu`. Runner: `xpu-agent` (BMG), 8 XPU devices visible. **Outcome:** IMPLEMENTING(fix_verified)
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | unclear | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Reproducer: `test/test_cuda_multigpu.py::TestMultiGPUDeviceXPU::test_caching_pinned_memory_multi_gpu_xpu` (upstream pytorch test suite, generalized for XPU). Failure: `AssertionError not raised : allocation reused too soon` — the pinned-host allocation is handed back out before the in-flight async H2D copy on another device has completed. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Reproduced on the latest XPU nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu`, runner `xpu-agent` (BMG, Arc Pro B60, 8 devices visible). The upstream node id cannot be run as-is: `test/test_multigpu.py` carries `@skipXPUIf(True, ...)` naming this very issue, so the test is silenced on XPU. Per the reproduce contract the marker was treated as hiding the failure, and the test body was re-run through its own `TestCase` assertions in a standalone script (`agent_space_xpu/repro/repro_5403.py`). | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_multigpu.py::TestMultiGPUDeviceXPU::test_caching_pinned_memory_multi_gpu` | REPRODUCED | `AssertionError: AssertionError not raised : allocation reused too soon` | Note: this repo's own copy of the test, `test/xpu/test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py::TestCudaMultiGPU::test_caching_pinned_memory_multi_gpu`, reports SKIPPED rather than failing. Its guard is `@unittest.skipIf(not TEST_MULTIGPU, ...)` and `TEST_MULTIGPU` comes from `common_cuda`, so it is false on an XPU-only host. That is a separate gap worth a follow-up; it is not what this issue is about. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at `torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c`, pytorch `origin/main@807c4660`. The non-blocking host-to-device branch of `_copy_xpu` issues the transfer with `sycl::queue::memcpy` and then registers the pinned source with the caching host allocator (`src/ATen/native/xpu/Copy.cpp:277-282`). On this stack the Level Zero runtime serves a host/device `memcpy` of **64 KiB or less** with a host-side copy, and to preserve in-order semantics it first drains the queue. The call therefore does not return until every previously submitted command on the stream has finished - including the copy itself. By the time `copy_()` returns, the `XPUEvent` that `record_event` goes on to record (`aten/src/ATen/xpu/CachingHostAllocator.cpp`, `record_stream`) is already signalled, so the next `pin_memory()` gets the same block straight back and the test's `assertNotEqual(t.data_ptr(), ptr)` fails. Measured directly, both at the torch level and with a standalone SYCL program: on a queue holding ~400 ms of work, `queue.memcpy` of 4 KiB returns after ~400 ms, while a kernel submission on the same queue returns in 0.1 ms. The cut-off is sharp - 65536 bytes blocks, 131072 bytes does not. `urEnqueueUSMMemcpy` is called with `blocking = 0`, so the wait is inside the adapter, not something the caller asked for; wrapping the copy in an explicit command group, with or without `depends_on`, and `ext_oneapi_memcpy2d` all behave identically. This also means every small `non_blocking=True` H2D copy currently serialises the host with the GPU, independent of the pinned-memory question. Upstream CUDA performs the same step with a single `cudaMemcpyAsync` (`aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Copy.cu:820`) followed by `record_event` (`:838`), which is genuinely asynchronous - that is the behaviour the test encodes. The fix is to enqueue the sub-threshold copy as a device kernel instead: both operands on this path are device-accessible USM (pinned host memory, or the staging buffer the same branch takes from the XPU host allocator), and a kernel submission does not wait for the queue to drain. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING - the asynchronous path is implementable inside `src/ATen/native/xpu/` - **Target repo:** torch-xpu-ops - **Domain:** xpu-kernel *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** torch-xpu-ops - **Analyzed at:** `torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c` - **What I changed:** `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.{h,cpp}` (+25) adds `copy_bytes_kernel`, a raw-pointer byte copy between two device-accessible USM pointers; `src/ATen/native/xpu/Copy.cpp` (+24/-2) routes the two `non_blocking` H2D sub-branches through a new `memcpyHostToDeviceAsync` helper that picks the kernel at or below 64 KiB and keeps `queue::memcpy` above it; `test/regressions/test_pinned_memory_async_copy.py` (+66) is a new regression test covering one size on each side of the threshold. - **Why:** the sub-threshold `queue::memcpy` is what drains the queue and makes the copy synchronous, so the pinned block is free again when `copy_()` returns; a kernel submission is enqueued without that wait. Larger copies are left on `queue::memcpy` because the measured host stall does not occur there (131072 bytes submits in 0.1 ms) and the copy engine is the faster path. CUDA does the equivalent step with one `cudaMemcpyAsync` at `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Copy.cu:820`. - **Skip added:** no - **Ready for verify:** yes ```diff diff --git a/src/ATen/native/xpu/Copy.cpp b/src/ATen/native/xpu/Copy.cpp index 069e6a15..6e2c6128 100644 --- a/src/ATen/native/xpu/Copy.cpp +++ b/src/ATen/native/xpu/Copy.cpp @@ -71,6 +71,28 @@ static bool copy_requires_temporaries(TensorIterator& iter, bool p2p_enabled) { } } +// The Level Zero runtime serves host-to-device copies up to this size with a +// host-side memcpy, which first drains the in-order queue. A small +// `non_blocking` copy would therefore block the caller until the queue is +// idle, and the pinned source is no longer in flight once copy_() returns, so +// the caching host allocator recycles it right away. A device kernel is +// enqueued asynchronously whatever the size; above the threshold the queue's +// copy engine is asynchronous too and faster, so it stays in use there. +constexpr int64_t kHostCopyKernelMaxBytes = 64 * 1024; + +// `src` must be device-accessible USM: pinned host memory, or a buffer from +// the XPU host allocator. +static void memcpyHostToDeviceAsync( + void* dst, + const void* src, + int64_t nbytes) { + if (nbytes <= kHostCopyKernelMaxBytes) { + copy_bytes_kernel(dst, src, nbytes); + } else { + getCurrentSYCLQueue().memcpy(dst, src, nbytes); + } +} + static bool maybe_enable_p2p_access(Device dst_device, Device src_device) { if (dst_device.is_cpu() || src_device.is_cpu()) { return false; @@ -275,7 +297,7 @@ void _copy_xpu(TensorIterator& iter, bool non_blocking) { if (non_blocking) { if (copy_kind == _H2D_) { if (at::detail::getXPUHooks().isPinnedPtr(src)) { - q.memcpy(dst, src, nbytes); + memcpyHostToDeviceAsync(dst, src, nbytes); at::getHostAllocator(at::kXPU)->record_event( const_cast(src), iter.tensor(1).storage().data_ptr().get_context(), @@ -294,7 +316,7 @@ void _copy_xpu(TensorIterator& iter, bool non_blocking) { } std::memcpy(stage_mem, src, nbytes); - q.memcpy(dst, stage_mem, nbytes); + memcpyHostToDeviceAsync(dst, stage_mem, nbytes); at::getHostAllocator(at::kXPU)->record_event( const_cast(stage_mem), stage_mem_dptr.get_context(), diff --git a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.cpp b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.cpp index 09eebb1f..a14ff7eb 100644 --- a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.cpp +++ b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.cpp @@ -17,6 +17,7 @@ #include #include +#include #include @@ -236,4 +237,23 @@ void copy_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter) { } } +struct CopyBytesFunctor { + void operator()(sycl::item<1> item) const { + dst_[item.get_id(0)] = src_[item.get_id(0)]; + } + CopyBytesFunctor(char* dst, const char* src) : dst_(dst), src_(src) {} + + private: + char* dst_; + const char* src_; +}; + +void copy_bytes_kernel(void* dst, const void* src, size_t nbytes) { + sycl_kernel_submit( + sycl::range<1>(nbytes), + getCurrentSYCLQueue(), + CopyBytesFunctor( + reinterpret_cast(dst), reinterpret_cast(src))); +} + } // namespace at::native::xpu diff --git a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.h b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.h index ed48dda8..0ce8236f 100644 --- a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.h +++ b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.h @@ -16,4 +16,9 @@ namespace at::native::xpu { TORCH_XPU_API void copy_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter); +// Copies raw bytes between two device-accessible USM pointers. Both must be +// reachable from the current device, i.e. device memory or host memory +// allocated through SYCL (pinned memory). +TORCH_XPU_API void copy_bytes_kernel(void* dst, const void* src, size_t nbytes); + } // namespace at::native::xpu diff --git a/test/regressions/test_pinned_memory_async_copy.py b/test/regressions/test_pinned_memory_async_copy.py new file mode 100644 index 00000000..0eb22605 --- /dev/null +++ b/test/regressions/test_pinned_memory_async_copy.py @@ -0,0 +1,66 @@ +# Copyright 2026 Intel Corporation +# +# Licensed under the Apache License, Version 2.0 (the "License"); +# you may not use this file except in compliance with the License. +# You may obtain a copy of the License at +# +# [地址已移除] + +# Owner(s): ["module: intel"] +""" +Regression test for non_blocking host-to-device copies out of pinned memory. + +A sub-64-KiB `sycl::queue::memcpy` is served by the Level Zero runtime with a +host-side copy that first drains the in-order queue, so the transfer had +already completed by the time `copy_()` returned and the caching host +allocator handed the pinned block straight back to the next `pin_memory()`. +The sizes below sit on either side of that threshold. See +intel/torch-xpu-ops#5403. +""" + +import torch +from torch.testing._internal.common_utils import ( + get_cycles_per_ms, + instantiate_parametrized_tests, + parametrize, + run_tests, + TestCase, +) + + +class TestPinnedMemoryAsyncCopy(TestCase): + @parametrize("numel", [1, 64 * 1024]) + def test_pinned_block_held_until_copy_completes(self, numel): + cycles_per_ms = get_cycles_per_ms(device="xpu") + + # Two things have to happen before the timed section. Submitting a + # SYCL kernel for the first time in a process costs tens of + # milliseconds of kernel creation, and that perturbs the spin kernel + # torch.xpu._sleep builds its delay out of, ending the delay early. + # Dropping the cached pinned blocks afterwards then leaves the block + # under test as the only reuse candidate, so the assertion below + # cannot pass just because some other free block was handed out. + warmup = torch.ones(numel).pin_memory() + torch.zeros(numel, device="xpu").copy_(warmup, non_blocking=True) + torch.xpu.synchronize() + del warmup + torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache() + + src = torch.ones(numel).pin_memory() + ptr = src.data_ptr() + dst = torch.zeros(numel, device="xpu") + + torch.xpu._sleep(int(1000 * cycles_per_ms)) + dst.copy_(src, non_blocking=True) + + del src + other = torch.full((numel,), 2.0).pin_memory() + self.assertNotEqual(other.data_ptr(), ptr, msg="allocation reused too soon") + self.assertEqual(dst, torch.ones(numel, device="xpu")) + + +instantiate_parametrized_tests(TestPinnedMemoryAsyncCopy) + + +if __name__ == "__main__": + run_tests() ``` *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verify Built from source against pytorch `origin/main@807c4660` with `TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc` on runner `xpu-agent` (BMG, 8 devices). The baseline and fixed builds are the same tree and differ only in the two `Copy.cpp` call sites. | Test case | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `test_multigpu.py::TestMultiGPUDeviceXPU::test_caching_pinned_memory_multi_gpu` | FAIL | PASS (10/10 fresh processes) | | `test/regressions/test_pinned_memory_async_copy.py` (new, 2 params) | FAIL at `numel=1` | PASS (16/16 runs) | `Before` is `AssertionError: AssertionError not raised : allocation reused too soon`. A real A/B was run rather than relying on the nightly-vs-source comparison: reverting only the two call sites back to `q.memcpy` and rebuilding the same tree makes both tests fail 5/5 with that same message, and restoring them makes both pass 5/5 again. So the change is what makes them pass. Regression checks on the fixed build: | Suite | Result | |---|---| | `test/regressions/` (this repo, full) | 445 passed, 1 skipped, 44 subtests, 1 failed | | pytorch `test/test_multigpu.py` (full, with the `#5403` skip removed) | 30 passed, 32 skipped | | pytorch `test/test_xpu.py` | 195 passed, 6 skipped, 3 xfailed, 3 failed | The four failures are independent of this change: `test_xpu_ops_header` and `test_xpu_header_installed` check for headers under `torch/include/ATen/ops`, which an editable install never populates (the directory is empty); `test_sleep` passes a float into a `uint64_t` pybind argument; `test_cached_zes_device_infos` concerns device-info caching. One thing worth flagging, found while chasing a flaky first draft of the regression test: `at::xpu::sleep` spins on `syclex::clock()`, and when first-use SYCL kernel creation (tens of ms) happens while it spins, the spin ends early. The committed test warms the copy path and empties the host cache before its timed section for that reason. Any test whose timing rests on `torch.xpu._sleep` is exposed to this; it is pre-existing and not addressed here. - **Verdict:** PASSED - the reported assertion passes and the A/B attributes it to this change - **Lint:** clean (`lintrunner -a -m origin/main`) *Automated by fix-verify.*
Summary The pinned-memory event machinery was never the problem - the copy was. A `non_blocking` host-to-device transfer of 64 KiB or less is served by the Level Zero runtime with a host-side memcpy that drains the in-order queue first, so `copy_()` returned only once the copy had already run and the caching host allocator recycled the pinned source immediately; the same stall also serialises the host with the GPU on every small async H2D copy. Copies at or below that threshold now go through a SYCL byte-copy kernel, which is enqueued without waiting for the queue, while larger ones keep the copy engine. Reproducer: test/test_cuda_multigpu.py::TestMultiGPUDeviceXPU::test_caching_pinned_memory_multi_gpu_xpu (upstream pytorch test suite, generalized for XPU).
Failure: AssertionError not raised : allocation reused too soon — the pinned-host allocation is handed back out before the in-flight async H2D copy on another device has completed.
Automated by issue-triage.



Reproduce
Reproduced on the latest XPU nightly wheel 2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu, runner xpu-agent (BMG, Arc Pro B60, 8 devices visible).
The upstream node id cannot be run as-is: test/test_multigpu.py carries @skipXPUIf(True, ...) naming this very issue, so the test is silenced on XPU. Per the reproduce contract the marker was treated as hiding the failure, and the test body was re-run through its own TestCase assertions in a standalone script (agent_space_xpu/repro/repro_5403.py).



Test case
Verdict
Observed




test_multigpu.py::TestMultiGPUDeviceXPU::test_caching_pinned_memory_multi_gpu
REPRODUCED
AssertionError: AssertionError not raised : allocation reused too soon



Note: this repo's own copy of the test, test/xpu/test_cuda_multigpu_xpu.py::TestCudaMultiGPU::test_caching_pinned_memory_multi_gpu, reports SKIPPED rather than failing. Its guard is @unittest.skipIf(not TEST_MULTIGPU, ...) and TEST_MULTIGPU comes from common_cuda, so it is false on an XPU-only host. That is a separate gap worth a follow-up; it is not what this issue is about.
Automated by fix-reproduce.



Root Cause
Analyzed at torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c, pytorch origin/main@807c4660.
The non-blocking host-to-device branch of _copy_xpu issues the transfer with sycl::queue::memcpy and then registers the pinned source with the caching host allocator (src/ATen/native/xpu/Copy.cpp:277-282). On this stack the Level Zero runtime serves a host/device memcpy of 64 KiB or less with a host-side copy, and to preserve in-order semantics it first drains the queue. The call therefore does not return until every previously submitted command on the stream has finished - including the copy itself. By the time copy_() returns, the XPUEvent that record_event goes on to record (aten/src/ATen/xpu/CachingHostAllocator.cpp, record_stream) is already signalled, so the next pin_memory() gets the same block straight back and the test's assertNotEqual(t.data_ptr(), ptr) fails.
Measured directly, both at the torch level and with a standalone SYCL program: on a queue holding ~400 ms of work, queue.memcpy of 4 KiB returns after ~400 ms, while a kernel submission on the same queue returns in 0.1 ms. The cut-off is sharp - 65536 bytes blocks, 131072 bytes does not. urEnqueueUSMMemcpy is called with blocking = 0, so the wait is inside the adapter, not something the caller asked for; wrapping the copy in an explicit command group, with or without depends_on, and ext_oneapi_memcpy2d all behave identically. This also means every small non_blocking=True H2D copy currently serialises the host with the GPU, independent of the pinned-memory question.
Upstream CUDA performs the same step with a single cudaMemcpyAsync (aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Copy.cu:820) followed by record_event (:838), which is genuinely asynchronous - that is the behaviour the test encodes. The fix is to enqueue the sub-threshold copy as a device kernel instead: both operands on this path are device-accessible USM (pinned host memory, or the staging buffer the same branch takes from the XPU host allocator), and a kernel submission does not wait for the queue to drain.

Verdict: IMPLEMENTING - the asynchronous path is implementable inside src/ATen/native/xpu/
Target repo: torch-xpu-ops
Domain: xpu-kernel

Automated by fix-root-cause.



Implement Result

Target repo: torch-xpu-ops
Analyzed at: torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c
What I changed: src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.{h,cpp} (+25) adds copy_bytes_kernel, a raw-pointer byte copy between two device-accessible USM pointers; src/ATen/native/xpu/Copy.cpp (+24/-2) routes the two non_blocking H2D sub-branches through a new memcpyHostToDeviceAsync helper that picks the kernel at or below 64 KiB and keeps queue::memcpy above it; test/regressions/test_pinned_memory_async_copy.py (+66) is a new regression test covering one size on each side of the threshold.
Why: the sub-threshold queue::memcpy is what drains the queue and makes the copy synchronous, so the pinned block is free again when copy_() returns; a kernel submission is enqueued without that wait. Larger copies are left on queue::memcpy because the measured host stall does not occur there (131072 bytes submits in 0.1 ms) and the copy engine is the faster path. CUDA does the equivalent step with one cudaMemcpyAsync at aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Copy.cu:820.
Skip added: no
Ready for verify: yes

diff --git a/src/ATen/native/xpu/Copy.cpp b/src/ATen/native/xpu/Copy.cpp
index 069e6a15..6e2c6128 100644

+++ b/src/ATen/native/xpu/Copy.cpp
@@ -71,6 +71,28 @@ static bool copy_requires_temporaries(TensorIterator& iter, bool p2p_enabled) {

+// The Level Zero runtime serves host-to-device copies up to this size with a
+// host-side memcpy, which first drains the in-order queue. A small
+// `non_blocking` copy would therefore block the caller until the queue is
+// idle, and the pinned source is no longer in flight once copy_() returns, so

+// enqueued asynchronously whatever the size; above the threshold the queue's
+// copy engine is asynchronous too and faster, so it stays in use there.
+constexpr int64_t kHostCopyKernelMaxBytes = 64 * 1024;

diff --git a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.cpp b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.cpp
index 09eebb1f..a14ff7eb 100644
--- a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.cpp
+++ b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.cpp
@@ -17,6 +17,7 @@
 #include <ATen/native/xpu/sycl/Loops.h>
 
 #include <ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.h>
+#include <comm/SYCLContext.h>
 
 #include <type_traits>
 
@@ -236,4 +237,23 @@ void copy_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter) {
   }
 }
 
+struct CopyBytesFunctor {
+  void operator()(sycl::item<1> item) const {
+    dst_[item.get_id(0)] = src_[item.get_id(0)];
+  }
+  CopyBytesFunctor(char* dst, const char* src) : dst_(dst), src_(src) {}
+
+ private:
+  char* dst_;
+  const char* src_;
+};
+
+void copy_bytes_kernel(void* dst, const void* src, size_t nbytes) {
+  sycl_kernel_submit(
+      sycl::range<1>(nbytes),
+      getCurrentSYCLQueue(),
+      CopyBytesFunctor(
+          reinterpret_cast<char*>(dst), reinterpret_cast<const char*>(src)));
+}
+
 } // namespace at::native::xpu

+++ b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/CopyKernel.h
@@ -16,4 +16,9 @@ namespace at::native::xpu {

+// reachable from the current device, i.e. device memory or host memory

+TORCH_XPU_API void copy_bytes_kernel(void* dst, const void* src, size_t nbytes);
