+"""
+Regression test for non_blocking host-to-device copies out of pinned memory.
+
+A sub-64-KiB `sycl::queue::memcpy` is served by the Level Zero runtime with a
+host-side copy that first drains the in-order queue, so the transfer had
+already completed by the time `copy_()` returned and the caching host
+allocator handed the pinned block straight back to the next `pin_memory()`.
+The sizes below sit on either side of that threshold. See
+intel/torch-xpu-ops#5403.
+"""
+
+import torch
+from torch.testing._internal.common_utils import (
+    get_cycles_per_ms,
+    instantiate_parametrized_tests,
+    parametrize,
+    run_tests,
+    TestCase,
+)
+
+
+class TestPinnedMemoryAsyncCopy(TestCase):
+    @parametrize("numel", [1, 64 * 1024])
+    def test_pinned_block_held_until_copy_completes(self, numel):
+        cycles_per_ms = get_cycles_per_ms(device="xpu")
+
+        # Two things have to happen before the timed section. Submitting a
+        # SYCL kernel for the first time in a process costs tens of
+        # milliseconds of kernel creation, and that perturbs the spin kernel
+        # torch.xpu._sleep builds its delay out of, ending the delay early.
+        # Dropping the cached pinned blocks afterwards then leaves the block
+        # under test as the only reuse candidate, so the assertion below
+        # cannot pass just because some other free block was handed out.
+        warmup = torch.ones(numel).pin_memory()
+        torch.zeros(numel, device="xpu").copy_(warmup, non_blocking=True)
+        torch.xpu.synchronize()
+        del warmup
+        torch.accelerator.empty_host_cache()
+
+        src = torch.ones(numel).pin_memory()
+        ptr = src.data_ptr()
+        dst = torch.zeros(numel, device="xpu")
+
+        torch.xpu._sleep(int(1000 * cycles_per_ms))
+        dst.copy_(src, non_blocking=True)
+
+        del src
+        other = torch.full((numel,), 2.0).pin_memory()
+        self.assertNotEqual(other.data_ptr(), ptr, msg="allocation reused too soon")
+        self.assertEqual(dst, torch.ones(numel, device="xpu"))
+
+
+instantiate_parametrized_tests(TestPinnedMemoryAsyncCopy)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    run_tests()

issues.title: [xccl][symm_mem] Gap checklist for enabling upstream symmetric-memory tests on XPU
issues.body:
> Drafted with assistance from an AI coding agent (Claude Code). Static analysis is against
> torch-xpu-ops `main` (1a18a331) and pytorch `d232af7b2f8`. The "Measured on hardware"
> sections were verified by running the ported tests on 4x Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100
> with the `xccl` backend, 4 ranks.

### What already works

`XPUSymmetricMemory` implements the `SymmetricMemory` base interface and
`XPUSymmetricMemoryAllocator` is registered via
`register_allocator(c10::DeviceType::XPU, allocator)`: `alloc`, `free`,
`get_alloc_size`, `rendezvous`, `get_buffer_ptrs`, `get_signal_pad_ptrs`,
`get_buffer_ptrs_dev`, `get_signal_pad_ptrs_dev`, `get_buffer_size`,
`get_offset`, `barrier`, `put_signal`, `wait_signal`, `get_rank`,
`get_world_size`, `get_device`.

Five Python ops are registered for XPU: `get_remote_tensors`,
`fused_all_gather_matmul`, `fused_all_gather_scaled_matmul`,
`fused_matmul_reduce_scatter`, `fused_scaled_matmul_reduce_scatter`.

**Measured on hardware.** Basic alloc / rendezvous / barrier / signalling do work, and
`fused_all_gather_matmul` works. Two corrections to the expectation that all the fused
async-TP ops work:

- `fused_matmul_reduce_scatter` returns **NaN** on XPU -- see gap 7.5 below.
- `fused_all_gather_scaled_matmul` and `fused_scaled_matmul_reduce_scatter` are
  **unverified**: every test covering them skips behind a CUDA compute-capability gate
  (`Requires compute capability >= 8.9`, `only supports sm>=90`), so they were never
  exercised on XPU.

`has_allocation` is also missing from the allocator (gap 7.1).

### 1. Multicast

- [ ] `XPUSymmetricMemory::has_multicast_support()` returns `false` (`src/xccl/XPUSymmetricMemory.cpp:128`)
- [ ] `XPUSymmetricMemory::get_multicast_ptr()` returns `nullptr` (`:132`)
- [ ] `XPUSymmetricMemoryAllocator::has_multicast_support()` returns `false` (`:453`)

**Measured on hardware.** `_SymmetricMemory.has_multicast_support(DeviceType.XPU, 0)`
returns `False`. This single item accounts for **47** of the 118 skips in
`test_symmetric_memory.py` -- by far the largest blocker by test count.

### 2. Symmetric-memory collective kernels (no XPU registration)

Registered only under `TORCH_LIBRARY_IMPL(symm_mem, CUDA)` in
`CUDASymmetricMemoryOps.cu`; torch-xpu-ops has no `TORCH_LIBRARY_IMPL(symm_mem, XPU)` at all.

- [ ] `one_shot_all_reduce` / `_out` / `_copy` / `_copy_out`
- [ ] `two_shot_all_reduce_` / `_out`
- [ ] `multimem_one_shot_all_reduce`, `multimem_one_shot_reduce_out`
- [ ] `multimem_all_reduce_`, `multimem_all_gather_out`
- [ ] `reduce_scatter_out`
- [ ] `memset32_`, `stream_write_value32_`, `memcpy_to_multicast_`
- [ ] `_async_input_mm`

**Measured on hardware.** Each op below now has a failing test attached, all raising
`NotImplementedError: The operator '<op>' is not currently implemented for the XPU device`:

| Missing op | Failing test |
|---|---|
| `one_shot_all_reduce_copy` | `SymmMemCollectiveTest.test_one_shot_all_reduce` |
| `one_shot_all_reduce_out` | 6 x `LoweringTest`: `test_comm_buffer_reuse`, `test_comm_buffer_inplace_prevention`, `test_lowering_one_shot_all_reduce`, `test_output_buffer_reuse`, `test_external_allocation_fallback`, `test_symm_mem_alloc_id_no_collision_after_reseed` |
| `one_shot_all_reduce_copy_out` | `LoweringTest.test_output_buffer_reuse_copy_variant` |
| `two_shot_all_reduce_` | `SymmMemCollectiveTest.test_two_shot_all_reduce` |
| `reduce_scatter_out` | `SymmMemCollectiveTest.test_reduce_scatter`, `test_reduce_scatter_corner_cases` |
| `memset32_` | `SymmMemSingleProcTest.test_memset32` |
| `stream_write_value32_` | `SymmMemSingleProcTest.test_stream_write_value32` |

### 3. Python-level ops registered for CUDA only

- [ ] `_low_contention_all_gather`
- [ ] `_low_contention_all_gather_ce_multicast` / `_out`
- [ ] `_low_contention_reduce_scatter`

**Measured on hardware.** `_low_contention_all_gather` blocks
`SymmetricMemoryTest.test_low_contention_all_gather` (2 params);
`_low_contention_reduce_scatter` blocks
`SymmetricMemoryTest.test_low_contention_reduce_scatter` (4 params).

### 4. No XPU SHMEM backend

- [ ] `symm_mem.is_nvshmem_available()` has no XPU equivalent; the binding is
      `_is_nvshmem_available` -> `c10d::nvshmem_extension::is_nvshmem_available`
      (`init.cpp:1188`). torch-xpu-ops contains no `nvshmem`/`rocshmem`-style
      SHMEM layer (strict token search over `src/` returns nothing).
- [ ] `_shmem_triton.get_shmem_backend_module()` dispatches to
      `_rocshmem_triton` on ROCm else `_nvshmem_triton` - there is no XPU branch,
      so `@requires_shmem` Triton kernels cannot target XPU.
- [ ] NVSHMEM op family, all `TORCH_LIBRARY_IMPL(symm_mem, CUDA)` in
      `nvshmem_extension.cu`: `nvshmem_broadcast`, `nvshmem_all_to_all`,
      `nvshmem_get`, `nvshmem_put`, `nvshmem_put_with_signal`,
      `nvshmem_wait_for_signal`, `all_to_all_vdev`, `all_to_all_vdev_2d`,
      `all_to_all_vdev_2d_offset`, `tile_reduce`, `multi_root_tile_reduce`

### 5. Backend naming

- [ ] `symm_mem.set_backend()` accepts only `Literal["NVSHMEM", "CUDA", "NCCL"]`
      (`_symmetric_memory/__init__.py:2296`). No `"XCCL"` name, so tests pinning a
      backend explicitly have no XPU equivalent.

### 6. Token switch

- [ ] `torch.distributed._token_switch` provides only `TokenSwitchNCCL`, and
      `_import_nccl_ep()` requires the NCCL expert-parallel package. No XCCL
      equivalent class or EP backend.

### 7. Gaps found only by running the tests

These are not visible from op-registration analysis and were each reproduced on hardware.

- [ ] **7.1 `is_symm_mem_tensor()` is always `False` on XPU.**
      `XPUSymmetricMemoryAllocator` does not override `has_allocation`, whose base
      implementation returns `false`
      (`torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/symm_mem/SymmetricMemory.hpp:129`). A tensor
      allocated by `symm_mem.empty(128, device="xpu")` reports
      `is_symm_mem_tensor(t) == False`. Blocks
      `SymmetricMemoryTest.test_is_symm_mem_tensor` and
      `LoweringTest.test_custom_op_symm_mem_realization`. Same shape as the
      `ProcessGroupXCCL` Backend-virtuals gap: the binding is present, the virtual is
      not overridden, and a permissive default hides it.
- [ ] **7.2 No MemPool backend for XPU.** `symm_mem.get_mem_pool(device)` raises
      `RuntimeError: SymmetricMemory MemPool did not find backend for device type xpu`
      from `get_mempool_allocator` (`_symmetric_memory/__init__.py:2329`). Blocks 5 of
      6 `SymmMemPoolTest` tests.
- [ ] **7.3 Invalid arguments abort the process instead of raising.** Five
      `SymmMemNegativeTest` tests expect a catchable `RuntimeError` (e.g.
      `assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, r"must be in \[0")` for an out-of-bounds channel
      or rank); on XPU the child dies with SIGABRT (exit `-6`), so the negative paths
      cannot be tested at all.
- [ ] **7.4 `wait_signal` honours no timeout.**
      `SymmMemNegativeTest.test_wait_signal_timeout` and `SymmetricMemoryTest.test_get`
      hang until the harness kills them (300s / 420s) instead of timing out.
- [ ] **7.5 `fused_matmul_reduce_scatter` produces NaN.** 4 failing tests
      (`AsyncTPTest.test_fused_matmul_reduce_scatter` x3 params and
      `test_fused_matmul_reduce_scatter_bfloat16_custom_reduce`): 512/512 elements
      mismatched, `Greatest absolute difference: nan`. Note
      `fused_all_gather_matmul` passes, so this is specific to the reduce-scatter
      direction.
- [ ] **7.6 `ProcessGroupXCCL.Options` has no `use_pg_for_symm_mem_rendezvous`.** The
      options object exposes only `backend`, `enable_reconfigure`,
      `global_ranks_in_group`, `group_name`, `is_high_priority_stream`, so PG-based
      symmetric-memory rendezvous cannot be requested. Blocks
      `SymmetricMemoryTest.test_pg_rendezvous_abort_after`.

`SymmetricMemoryTest.test_rendezvous_via_pg_allgather` is blocked by the XCCL flight
recorder gap in #5381 rather than by anything here: rendezvous records zero
`xccl:_all_gather_base` entries.

### Test impact (measured)

The earlier estimate in this issue counted test *methods*; the numbers below count
parametrized test *cases*, which is what the runner reports, so the totals are larger.

`test_symmetric_memory.py`, after a device-agnostic port: **140 cases -- 22 pass,
118 skip, 0 fail**, with 39 cases gated `@skipIfXpu` referencing this issue.

| Class | Cases | Pass | Skip |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SymmetricMemoryTest` | 30 | 9 | 21 |
| `AsyncTPTest` | 25 | 6 | 19 |
| `SymmMemCollectiveTest` | 49 | 0 | 49 |
| `LoweringTest` | 10 | 1 | 9 |
| `SymmMemPoolTest` | 6 | 1 | 5 |
| `SymmMemEmptySetDeviceTest` | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| `SymmMemNegativeTest` | 6 | 0 | 6 |
| `SymmMemSingleProcTest` | 3 | 1 | 2 |
| `ExternalNcclCommRegistrationTest` | 4 | 0 | 4 |
| `TorchCommsCudaSymmMemTest` | 2 | 0 | 2 |
| `SymmetricMemoryTestCudaGraph` | 1 | 0 | 1 |

Of the 118 skips, only 39 are XPU gaps from this issue. The rest are multicast (47,
gap 1), CUDA compute-capability gates (14), NCCL-only facilities (10) and other
CUDA-specific paths.

A caveat on any earlier XPU results from this file: before the port it reported `OK`
for all 140 cases on XPU **while executing nothing**. `device_type` was hardcoded to
`"cuda"` at module scope, so `world_size` came from `torch.cuda.device_count()` == 0
and no subprocess was ever spawned -- the harness logs `Note: no subprocesses were
spawned, test was likely skipped` and still prints `ok`.

`test_nccl.py`: **37 cases, all gated**. Every one is NCCL-symmetric-memory specific
(`symm_mem.set_backend("NCCL")`, the torchcomms `nccl2` backend, NCCL CFT
logical-endpoint handles), so they are skipped rather than ported. This supersedes the
earlier "25 tests, 15 portable" estimate.

`test_nvshmem.py`, `test_shmem_triton.py` and `test_token_switch.py` are blocked
at module level and cannot be enabled at all until items 4 and 6 land.

`TestNCCL` in `test_nccl.py` (7 tests) is **out of scope**: it exercises the raw
`torch.cuda.nccl` binding (`unique_id`, `init_rank`, `broadcast`, `reduce`,
`all_reduce`, `all_gather`, `reduce_scatter`, `version`) and there is no
`torch.xpu.xccl` module, so it should stay NCCL-gated. It is already
`instantiate_device_type_tests(..., only_for="cuda")`, so it generates no XPU cases.

### Two PyTorch-side CUDA hardcodes surfaced by this port

Not torch-xpu-ops work, recorded here so they are not mistaken for XPU gaps:

- `torch/_inductor/fx_passes/low_contention_collectives.py` falls back to
  `torch.cuda.current_device()`, raising `AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA
  enabled` from inside an Inductor FX pass on any non-CUDA build.
- `torch/_inductor/codegen/wrapper.py` emits `torch.device("cuda:N")` into the
  generated `empty_strided_p2p` call regardless of the buffer's actual device.

**Before closing this ticket, remove the corresponding `@skipIfXpu` lines from the upstream tests.**

issues.title: [distributed] ProcessGroupXCCL does not implement supportsTimeEstimation(), so collective time estimation is unavailable on XPU
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`ProcessGroupXCCL` does not override the experimental collective time-estimation API,
so it inherits `return false` from `Backend.hpp`. As a result
`torch.distributed._time_estimator()` raises on XPU, and inductor's NCCL-based
collective estimator silently declines to run.

```bash
python - <<'EOF'
import os, torch, torch.distributed as dist
os.environ.update(MASTER_ADDR="localhost", MASTER_PORT="29711")
dist.init_process_group("xccl", rank=0, world_size=1, store=dist.HashStore())
b = dist.group.WORLD._get_backend(torch.device("xpu"))
print("backend:", type(b).__name__)
print("_supports_time_estimate:", b._supports_time_estimate)
dist.destroy_process_group()
EOF
```

```
backend: ProcessGroupXCCL
_supports_time_estimate: False
```

The capability is a virtual with a `false` default in
`torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/Backend.hpp:175`:

```cpp
  // Experimental collective time-estimation API. Backends that return true
  // must simulate collectives issued between startTimeEstimate() and
  // endTimeEstimate(), which returns the estimated duration in microseconds.
  virtual bool supportsTimeEstimation() const {
    return false;
  }

  virtual void startTimeEstimate() {
    TORCH_CHECK(false, c10::str("Backend ", getBackendName(),
                                " does not support time estimation"));
  }

  virtual float endTimeEstimate() {
    TORCH_CHECK(false, c10::str("Backend ", getBackendName(),
                                " does not support time estimation"));
  }
```

Only `ProcessGroupNCCL.hpp:839` overrides it. `grep -rn supportsTimeEstimation
src/xccl/` in this repo returns nothing.

### Impact

Two consumers in PyTorch:

1. `torch/distributed/distributed_c10d.py:3773` — `dist._time_estimator()` raises
   `NotImplementedError: collective time estimator is not supported in the current
   version of backend ...`, so the public estimator context manager is unusable on XPU.
2. `torch/_inductor/comm_analysis.py:868` — `if not backend._supports_time_estimate:
   return None`, so inductor falls back to its analytical formula instead of a measured
   estimate when scheduling/reordering collectives on XPU.

### What XCCL needs

`supportsTimeEstimation()` returning `true`, plus `startTimeEstimate()` /
`endTimeEstimate()` (the base class `TORCH_CHECK`s on both), simulating the collectives
issued between them and returning the estimated duration in microseconds.

### Note: a second, PyTorch-side blocker

Even once XCCL implements the above, inductor's estimator will not reach it —
`torch/_inductor/comm_analysis.py:863` hardcodes the device before looking up the
backend:

```python
        device = torch.device("cuda")
        try:
            backend = pg._get_backend(device)
        except RuntimeError:
            return None
```

On an XPU-only build `pg._get_backend(torch.device("cuda"))` raises `RuntimeError` and
the function returns `None`. That line needs to follow the current accelerator; it is a
PyTorch fix rather than a torch-xpu-ops one, and is mentioned here only so the two are
not fixed in isolation.

### Test impact

In `test/inductor/test_comm_analysis.py`, two tests assert this capability:

- `TestNcclEstimateDeviceResolution::test_multi_backend_pg_resolves_to_nccl`
- `TestNcclEstimateDeviceResolution::test_single_nccl_backend_resolves_correctly`

Both do `self.assertTrue(backend._supports_time_estimate)`, so they cannot pass on XPU
today; while porting that file for device-agnosticism (pytorch/pytorch#114850) they are
being marked `@skipIfXpu` referencing this issue. The file's third test,
`test_fake_backend_falls_back_to_analytical`, is backend-agnostic and now runs on XPU
(it was previously excluded by a module-level `if not dist.is_nccl_available():
sys.exit(0)` guard).

### Versions

```
torch     2.15.0a0+git3c3da2a  (source build, commit 3c3da2a5e8b)
device    4x Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100
backend   xccl
```

issues.title: [distributed] XPU storages cannot be IPC-shared: no `_share_xpu_`, so `reduce_tensor()` silently falls back to the non-IPC path
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`torch.multiprocessing.reductions.reduce_tensor()` implements cross-process IPC sharing
only for CUDA storages. XPU tensors fall through to the plain, non-IPC path **without
any error or warning**, so code that expects an IPC handle silently receives a
differently-shaped payload.

```bash
python -c "
import torch
from torch.multiprocessing.reductions import reduce_tensor
t = torch.randn(8, device='xpu')
fn, args = reduce_tensor(t)
print('reduce_tensor(xpu) ->', fn.__name__, '| nargs:', len(args))
print('has _share_xpu_ :', hasattr(t.untyped_storage(), '_share_xpu_'))
print('has _share_cuda_:', hasattr(t.untyped_storage(), '_share_cuda_'))
"
```

```
reduce_tensor(xpu) -> rebuild_tensor | nargs: 3
has _share_xpu_ : False
has _share_cuda_: True
```

For a CUDA tensor the same call returns `rebuild_cuda_tensor` with **15** arguments
(handle, ref-counter handle/offset, event handle, ...). For XPU it returns
`rebuild_tensor` with **3**. Any consumer indexing the IPC payload -- e.g. patching the
device index before rebuilding on the receiving rank -- gets an `IndexError` rather than
a clear "unsupported" error.

The gate is `torch/multiprocessing/reductions.py:346`:

```python
    storage = tensor._typed_storage()

    if storage._untyped_storage.device.type == "cuda":
        (
            device, handle, storage_size_bytes, storage_offset_bytes,
            ref_counter_handle, ref_counter_offset, event_handle, event_sync_required,
        ) = storage._share_cuda_()
```

There is no `_share_xpu_` on `UntypedStorage`, and no XPU IPC binding at all:
`[n for n in dir(torch._C) if n.startswith('_xpu_') and ('ipc' in n or 'share' in n)]`
is empty.

Note the asymmetry: XPU **event** IPC is already wired up at `reductions.py:629`, so only
storage/tensor sharing is missing.

```python
    ipc_event_classes = [torch.cuda.Event, torch.xpu.Event]
```

### What XPU needs

An `UntypedStorage._share_xpu_()` equivalent (returning the handle/offset/ref-counter/
event tuple, backed by level-zero IPC memory handles) plus a `rebuild_xpu_tensor()`
counterpart, and the `device.type == "cuda"` gate above generalised to dispatch on the
storage's device.

### Test impact

Two files under `test/distributed/` depend on this and cannot be ported for XPU
(pytorch/pytorch#114850) until it exists:

- **`test_p2p_ipc.py`** -- deliberately written device-agnostically (its own comment says
  "So that tests are written in device-agnostic way"; it uses `device_module.set_device`,
  `torch.device(device_type, self.rank)` etc. with a single `device_type = "cuda"` at the
  top). Its entire purpose is passing an IPC handle to a peer process so it can map the
  sender's allocation. Currently `Ran 2 tests ... OK (skipped=2)` on XPU via
  `requires_cuda_p2p_access()`.
- **`test_cupy_as_tensor.py`** -- same shape, body already generic
  (`torch._C._accelerator_setAllocatorSettings`, `torch.get_device_module(device_type)`),
  gated to CUDA only by `instantiate_device_type_tests(..., only_for="cuda")`. Currently
  `Ran 0 tests` on XPU.

`test_cupy_as_tensor.py` additionally needs a foreign-array-interface import path: it
builds a wrapper exposing `__cuda_array_interface__`, and `torch.as_tensor` on that
protocol initialises the CUDA backend regardless of the `device=` argument --

```
as_tensor(__cuda_array_interface__, device='xpu') ->
    RuntimeError: Cannot initialize CUDA without ATen_cuda library...
```

That part is arguably by design (the protocol is CUDA-specific; DLPack is the portable
route), so IPC storage sharing is the actionable ask here -- noted only so the two are
not conflated: fixing `_share_xpu_` alone unblocks `test_p2p_ipc.py` but not the cuPy one.

### What must pass to close this

`test/distributed/test_p2p_ipc.py` -- both tests must **run and pass** on XPU, not skip:

```bash
python test/distributed/test_p2p_ipc.py -v
```

- `P2PIpcTest::test_p2p_ipc`
- `P2PIpcTest::test_p2p_ipc_expandable_segments`

Today that file reports `Ran 2 tests ... OK (skipped=2)` on XPU; a green run with zero
skips is the acceptance criterion, once its single `device_type = "cuda"` and its
`requires_cuda_p2p_access()` class gate are made accelerator-generic on the PyTorch side.

`test/distributed/test_cupy_as_tensor.py::CupyAsTensorTestXPU::test_cupy_as_tensor_xpu`
(currently `Ran 0 tests`; the class is generated by
`instantiate_device_type_tests(CupyAsTensorTest, globals(), only_for="cuda")`, so XPU needs
`allow_xpu=True` there) is the second file this unblocks,
but it *additionally* needs the foreign-array-interface path described above, so it is a
follow-on rather than a gate on closing this issue.

### Versions

```
torch     2.15.0a0+git3c3da2a  (source build, commit 3c3da2a5e8b)
device    4x Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100
backend   xccl
```

issues.title: [distributed] ProcessGroupXCCL has no one-sided window API (new_window / mem_allocator), so test_c10d_window.py cannot run on XPU
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`test/distributed/test_c10d_window.py` is a backend-agnostic harness for the c10d
one-sided window API (`Backend.new_window` / `Window.put` / `signal` / `wait_signal` /
`map_remote_tensor`), parameterised over `(backend, device)` pairs:

```python
WINDOW_BACKENDS = [
    ("nccl2", "cuda"),
]
```

XCCL implements none of that surface: `grep -rniE "mem_allocator|new_window" src/xccl/`
in this repo returns nothing. On the PyTorch side the implementation lives only in
`torch/csrc/distributed/c10d/nccl2/WindowNCCL.cpp` (plus `ProcessGroupNCCL.cpp` /
`ProcessGroupNCCLUtils.cpp`).

The test already self-skips for backends without support:

```python
        if not dist._supports_window() or not self.backend.supports_window:
            self.skipTest(f"{self.backend_name} does not support windows")
```

so adding `("xccl", "xpu")` to `WINDOW_BACKENDS` today would only manufacture 11 more
skips rather than gain coverage. Current XPU state: `Ran 11 tests ... OK (skipped=11)`.

### What XPU needs

`ProcessGroupXCCL` needs to expose `mem_allocator` and implement the window surface
(`new_window`, `Window.put` / `signal` / `wait_signal` / `map_remote_tensor`) and report
`supports_window`.

Encouragingly the allocator half already exists -- `torch.xpu.MemPool` and
`torch.xpu.use_mem_pool` are both present, and the test builds its pool as
`torch.cuda.MemPool(self.backend.mem_allocator)`, so the missing piece is the
backend-side allocator/window API rather than XPU memory-pool support.

Once that lands, enabling the test is a one-line change to `WINDOW_BACKENDS` (the file
was explicitly written to be extended that way -- see its header comment "enabled by
extending WINDOW_BACKENDS").

Found while auditing `test/distributed/` for device-agnostic XPU support
(pytorch/pytorch#114850).

### What must pass to close this

`test/distributed/test_c10d_window.py` -- with `("xccl", "xpu")` added to
`WINDOW_BACKENDS`, the generated `XcclWindowTest` class (the file builds one class per
entry: `globals()[f"{backend_name.capitalize()}WindowTest"]`) must run all 11 tests
without hitting the `does not support windows` skip:

```bash
python test/distributed/test_c10d_window.py -v
```

- `XcclWindowTest::test_put_signal_wait_sync`
- `XcclWindowTest::test_put_signal_wait_async`
- `XcclWindowTest::test_signal_wait`
- `XcclWindowTest::test_put_dtypes_and_sizes`
- `XcclWindowTest::test_new_window_with_tensor`
- `XcclWindowTest::test_map_remote_tensor_local`
- `XcclWindowTest::test_window_attr`
- `XcclWindowTest::test_register_errors`
- `XcclWindowTest::test_put_out_of_bounds`
- `XcclWindowTest::test_put_argument_validation_is_rank_local`
- `XcclWindowTest::test_put_uses_destination_window_metadata`

Today the file reports `Ran 11 tests ... OK (skipped=11)` on XPU (the nccl2 class skipping
on a non-CUDA build). Acceptance criterion: 22 tests run, the 11 XCCL ones green and none
of them skipped. `test_window_attr` and `test_register_errors` in particular pin down the
`mem_allocator` / registration surface, so they are the ones to watch first.

### Versions

```
torch     2.15.0a0+git3c3da2a  (source build, commit 3c3da2a5e8b)
device    4x Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100
backend   xccl
```

issues.title: [distributed] No XPU equivalent of NCCL Copy Engine collectives, so test_ce_colls.py cannot run on XPU
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`test/distributed/test_ce_colls.py` exercises NCCL's *copy-engine* (CE) collectives. It
is unreachable on an XPU build: the module exits at import, before any test is collected.

```python
if not dist.is_available() or not dist.is_nccl_available():
    print("c10d NCCL not available, skipping tests", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(0)
```

Current XPU state: exits with `c10d NCCL not available, skipping tests` (0 tests
collected).

Beyond that guard the tests are NCCL-specific by construction:

- `@requires_nccl_version((2, 28), "Need NCCL 2.28+ for CE collectives")` on the class
- `@requires_cuda_p2p_access()` on the class
- `symm_mem.set_backend("NCCL")` in setup, i.e. they select the NCCL symmetric-memory
  backend explicitly rather than using the generic symmetric-memory API

So this is not a test-side port: it would need CE-equivalent functionality in XCCL (and a
way to select it through `symm_mem.set_backend`). Filing it to record the gap rather than
to claim the test is nearly portable.

For contrast, the generic symmetric-memory path *is* available on XPU --
`symm_mem.get_backend(torch.device("xpu"))` returns `"XPU"` (implemented in
`src/xccl/XPUSymmetricMemory.cpp`) -- so `test/distributed/test_symmetric_memory.py` can
be ported while this file cannot.

Found while auditing `test/distributed/` for device-agnostic XPU support
(pytorch/pytorch#114850).

### What must pass to close this

`test/distributed/test_ce_colls.py` -- the module must get past its import-time
`is_nccl_available()` exit and both tests must run and pass on XPU:

```bash
python test/distributed/test_ce_colls.py -v
```

- `NCCLCopyEngineCollectives::test_ce_allgather`
- `NCCLCopyEngineCollectives::test_ce_alltoall`

Today the file collects 0 tests on XPU. Note the class name itself encodes the NCCL
dependency, so closing this realistically means either an XCCL CE-equivalent selectable
through `symm_mem.set_backend`, or agreement that the file stays CUDA-only and the issue
is closed as won't-fix -- worth deciding before any work starts.

### Versions

```
torch     2.15.0a0+git3c3da2a  (source build, commit 3c3da2a5e8b)
device    4x Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100
backend   xccl
```

The oneCCL side of this is tracked in **MLSL-4946** (NCCL 2.28 CE Collective Support). I added the PyTorch context from this issue there: the two `test_ce_colls.py` tests to enable, the need for an XCCL CE path selectable through `symm_mem.set_backend`, and the oneCCL prerequisites.

As @githubsgi noted above, the prerequisites are symmetric-window buffer registration and a zero-CTA policy that routes allgather/alltoall to copy engines. On the oneCCL side those are MLSL-3938 (symmetric memory) and MLSL-4558 / MLSL-4562 under MLSL-4044 (CTA policy, including ZERO -> copy-engine routing). MLSL-4946 is now linked to MLSL-4044 and MLSL-4562.

issues.title: [distributed] ProcessGroupXCCL does not implement the c10d reconfigure API, so test_c10d_fault_tolerance.py has zero XPU coverage
issues.body:
### Describe the bug

`ProcessGroupXCCL` does not implement the c10d fault-tolerance / reconfigure API, so it
inherits `return false` from `Backend.hpp:232`:

```cpp
  // supportsReconfigure advertises support; get_reconfigure_handle returns an
  // opaque handle that peers exchange out-of-band; reconfigure (re)initializes
  // the communicator with a new set of peers.
  virtual bool supportsReconfigure() const {
    return false;
  }
```

Only `ProcessGroupGloo.hpp:278` and `nccl2/ProcessGroupNCCL.hpp:302` override it.
`grep -rniE "reconfigure" src/xccl/` in this repo returns nothing.

Worse, `enable_reconfigure=True` is **silently accepted** on XPU -- no error, no warning,
the capability simply reports false:

```bash
python - <<'EOF'
import torch, torch.distributed as dist, tempfile
f = tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile(delete=False)
dist.init_process_group("xccl", world_size=1, rank=0,
                        store=dist.FileStore(f.name, 1), enable_reconfigure=True)
pg = dist.distributed_c10d._get_default_group()
b = dist.get_backend_impl(pg, torch.device("xpu"))
print("backend:", type(b).__name__)
print("dist._supports_reconfigure():", dist._supports_reconfigure())
print("backend.supports_reconfigure:", b.supports_reconfigure)
EOF
```

```
backend: ProcessGroupXCCL
dist._supports_reconfigure(): False
backend.supports_reconfigure: False
```

Arguably a smaller bug in its own right: asking for `enable_reconfigure=True` on a backend
that cannot honour it should raise (or at least warn) rather than hand back a process group
that quietly lacks the capability.

### What XPU needs

1. `supportsReconfigure()` returning `true`, plus `getReconfigureHandle()` and
   `reconfigure()` -- the handle is an opaque blob peers exchange out-of-band, and
   `reconfigure()` must re-initialize the communicator against a new peer set (including
   shrinking, merging, and recovering after `abort()`).
2. `get_error()` reporting `ErrorType::COMM_ERROR` after an `abort()` and
   `ErrorType::TIMEOUT` after a collective times out (the tests assert both).
3. Work-result reporting (`Work::get_future_result()` -> `WorkResult::TIMEOUT` /
   `COMM_ERROR`), which is what `FaultToleranceBackend.supports_work_result` gates.

### Test impact

`test/distributed/test_c10d_fault_tolerance.py` builds one test class per entry in

```python
FAULT_TOLERANCE_BACKENDS = [
    FaultToleranceBackend("gloo", "cpu"),
    FaultToleranceBackend("nccl2", "cuda", supports_work_result=True),
]
```

so on XPU (`python test/distributed/test_c10d_fault_tolerance.py -v`) the picture is:

```
Ran 34 tests in 42.110s
OK (skipped=19)
```

| Class | Collected | Pass | Skip |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GlooFaultToleranceTest` (cpu) | 16 | 13 | 3 (2x "gloo does not report work results", 1x nonblocking-NCCL-init) |
| `Nccl2FaultToleranceTest` (cuda) | 16 | 0 | 16 -- "fault tolerance CUDA tests require at least 3 GPUs" (`not TEST_CUDA`, line 392) |
| `ReconfigureContractTest` / `BackendCapabilityContractTest` | 2 | 2 | 0 (device-free) |

So all 16 accelerator-path tests are dead on XPU, and the only thing exercising reconfigure
is the CPU/gloo class.

Note this file is *less* forgiving than `test_c10d_window.py` (see #5407): it has no
capability-based self-skip. Adding `FaultToleranceBackend("xccl", "xpu",
supports_work_result=True)` today would make all 16 tests **hard-fail**, not skip, at the
two assertions in `_init_reconfigurable_pg` (lines 81-82):

```python
        self.assertTrue(dist._supports_reconfigure())
        self.assertTrue(self.backend.supports_reconfigure)
```

### What must pass to close this

With `("xccl", "xpu")` added to `FAULT_TOLERANCE_BACKENDS`, the generated
`XcclFaultToleranceTest` class must run all 16 tests green with no skips:

```bash
python test/distributed/test_c10d_fault_tolerance.py -v
```

- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_reconfigure_basic`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_reconfigure_then_all_reduce`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_reconfigure_then_send_recv`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_reconfigure_identity`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_reconfigure_scale_down_up`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_reconfigure_single_to_all`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_reconfigure_late_join`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_reconfigure_merge_split`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_shrink_exclude_last_rank`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_shrink_exclude_middle_rank`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_reconfigure_after_abort`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_reconfigure_after_timeout`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_reconfigure_rejects_reused_uuid`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_reconfigure_timeout_is_retryable`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_work_explicit_timeout_includes_prelaunch_stall`
- `XcclFaultToleranceTest::test_work_reports_communicator_error`

The last two are the ones needing item 3 above; the class-level gate at lines 390-393
(`not TEST_CUDA or torch.cuda.device_count() < 3`) also has to become accelerator-generic,
and the suite needs 3 devices.

### Note: PyTorch-side prep work

Independently of XCCL, the test file itself has to be made device-generic before an XPU
entry can work. These are PyTorch changes (part of pytorch/pytorch#114850), listed so the
two halves are not fixed in isolation:

- `device` property hardcodes `f"cuda:{self.rank}"` (lines 50-51) and `_init_reconfigurable_pg`
  calls `torch.cuda.set_device` (lines 72-73)
- `test_work_explicit_timeout_includes_prelaunch_stall` uses `torch.cuda.synchronize()`,
  `torch.cuda._sleep()` and `torch.cuda.current_stream().query()` (lines 154-166)
- `test_work_reports_communicator_error` uses `torch.cuda.synchronize()` (line 173) and
  asserts the literal backend string `"NCCL operation failed"` (line 186)
- backend-name branches at lines 293, 336 and 358

### Versions

```
torch     2.15.0a0+git3c3da2a  (source build, commit 3c3da2a5e8b)
device    4x Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100
backend   xccl
```

issues.title: The test enters an unrecoverable "Level Zero DEVICE_LOST" or resource failure state and may hang, requiring a machine reboot
issues.body:
## Summary

`test/regressions/test_copy.py` now fails 9/9 XPU unit tests. All failures are Level Zero runtime failures during basic copy/clone paths, reported as one of:

- `UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`
- `UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`
- `UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY`

Once a machine enters this state, all following tests show the same class of failures and affected test runs can hang instead of exiting normally. Rebooting the machine can temporarily recover it, but if the issue is hit again later, subsequent tests fail or hang again until another reboot. This creates a reboot/fail-or-hang/reboot loop for UT execution.

The failures happen in simple tensor transfer/copy/assertion code paths, so this looks like a machine-level XPU runtime/device stability or memory/resource management regression rather than a test expectation mismatch.

## Environment

- OS: Ubuntu 26.04 LTS, Linux `7.0.0-30-generic`, x86_64
- CPU: Intel(R) Xeon(R) 6767P, 2 sockets, 256 logical CPUs
- Python: `3.12.14`
- XPU available: True
- Intel GPU driver packages:
  - `libze1: 1.32.0-1~26.04~ppa1`
  - `intel-opencl-icd: 26.31.39395.13-1~26.04~ppa1`
- XPU driver version reported by PyTorch: `1.17.39395+13`
- XPU hardware: 8x Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics, each reported with 24480 MB memory
- `xpu-smi discovery`: all 8 devices show `Device State: normal` at collection time

## Reproducer

From the PyTorch base repo / torch-xpu-ops regression test directory:

```bash
docker run -it --device=/dev/mem --device=/dev/dri \
--group-add video --privileged  --shm-size=8g \
intel/omix:latest-runtime-ubuntu26.04 bash --norc --noprofile

# in container
bash

# setup python
curl -LsSf [地址已移除] | sh
source $HOME/.local/bin/env
uv venv myvenv --python 3.12.14 --clear
source myvenv/bin/activate
uv pip install pip wheel "setuptools<81"

uv pip install torch torchaudio torchvision triton-xpu --index-url [地址已移除] --pre

# prepare pytorch
pytorch_commit="$(python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.git_version)')"
git clone [地址已移除]
cd pytorch
git checkout ${pytorch_commit}

uv pip install -r .ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt
uv pip install -U typing_extensions
uv pip install pytest pytest-timeout pytest-xdist pytest-rerunfailures

# pytest 
cd third_party/
git clone [地址已移除]
xpu_ops_commit="$(cat xpu.txt)"
cd torch-xpu-ops
git checkout $xpu_ops_commit

test/regressions
pytest -v test_copy.py
```

PyTorch's repro hints from the failing tests also point to commands like:

```bash
python test/regressions/test_copy.py TestSimpleCopyXPU.test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float32
python test/regressions/test_copy.py TestSimpleCopyXPU.test_copy_and_clone_float4_xpu
python test/regressions/test_copy.py TestSimpleCopyXPU.test_copy_kernel_bcomplex32_xpu
```

## Observed Result

All 9 collected tests failed:

```text
test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_bcomplex32_xpu FAILED
test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_float4_xpu FAILED
test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float32 FAILED
test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float8_e4m3fn FAILED
test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float8_e4m3fnuz FAILED
test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float8_e5m2 FAILED
test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float8_e5m2fnuz FAILED
test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float8_e8m0fnu FAILED
test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_kernel_bcomplex32_xpu FAILED
```

Failure summary:

```text
FAILED test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_bcomplex32_xpu - RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 40 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES)
FAILED test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_float4_xpu - RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 20 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST)
FAILED test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float32 - RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 39 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY)
FAILED test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float8_e4m3fn - RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 20 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST)
FAILED test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float8_e4m3fnuz - RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 39 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY)
FAILED test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float8_e5m2 - RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 20 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST)
FAILED test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float8_e5m2fnuz - RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 39 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY)
FAILED test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float8_e8m0fnu - RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 20 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST)
FAILED test_copy.py::TestSimpleCopyXPU::test_copy_kernel_bcomplex32_xpu - RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 40 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES)
```

Additional machine-level behavior:

- Once the machine hits this issue, later tests also fail with `UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`, `UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES`, or `UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY`.
- Some affected test runs hang and do not exit normally after the device/resource failure.
- Rebooting the machine temporarily clears the state.
- After reboot, the machine can hit the same issue again; once that happens, all following tests fail or hang again until another reboot.
- This makes UT runs unable to make forward progress without repeatedly rebooting the machine.

## Representative Failure Details

### `test_copy_and_clone_xpu_float32`

The regular `float32` copy path fails on `copy_` with device OOM:

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/root/pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/regressions/test_copy.py", line 31, in test_copy_and_clone
    b_xpu.copy_(a_xpu)
RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 39 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY)
```

### `test_copy_and_clone_float4_xpu`

The float4 transfer path fails while moving a CPU tensor to XPU:

```text
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/root/pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/regressions/test_copy.py", line 55, in test_copy_and_clone_float4
    a_xpu = a_cpu.to(xpu_device).view(torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2)
```

nodes.body:
This is because of two issues:
1. GSD-13281. This is a request that ports the memory overcommit flag to Linux 7.0. So the application will use device memory by default, and not fallback to the host memory. In this way, the host memory will never be overcommitted and leads to crash.
2. COMPLRLLVM-77770L We request the SYCL not maintain their own memory pool, and use L0 memory pool by default. This I think is more related to this issue. But this fix will only be available after 2026.3

For now, I still suggests that we use the monitor memory usage + explicit kill process workaround.

nodes.body:
All issues have the same origin: MKL and CPU implementation differs. For input sizes appropriate for canonical fft, namely equal to 2^N the results are identical. For other sizes, the result depends on grouping/padding strategy. It's worth mentioning, that neither XPU nor CPU results are accurate here, reference calculated in double precision using math-dedicated libraries is different. Moreover, the results in fft vs dft for double precision can differ up to 2 decimal places.

The solution is to correct accuracy, but also distinguish 2^n and non 2^n sizes. In the first case, the implementations on CPU and XPU are equivalent, and the results are much closer.
nodes.bodyText:
All issues have the same origin: MKL and CPU implementation differs. For input sizes appropriate for canonical fft, namely equal to 2^N the results are identical. For other sizes, the result depends on grouping/padding strategy. It's worth mentioning, that neither XPU nor CPU results are accurate here, reference calculated in double precision using math-dedicated libraries is different. Moreover, the results in fft vs dft for double precision can differ up to 2 decimal places.
The solution is to correct accuracy, but also distinguish 2^n and non 2^n sizes. In the first case, the implementations on CPU and XPU are equivalent, and the results are much closer.

issues.title: [Inductor][XPU] test_lookup_table.py TestLookupTable unit tests fail: lookup returns empty on XPU
issues.body:
## Description
All `TestLookupTable` unit tests in `test/inductor/test_lookup_table.py` fail on XPU because the Inductor lookup table only supports CUDA devices.

## Root cause
`torch/_inductor/lookup_table/choices.py::LookupTableChoices._get_device_key` returns `None` for any device whose `type != "cuda"`. `make_lookup_key` then returns `None` whenever the device key is `None`, so on XPU every lookup key is `None` and lookups return `{}`.

## Failing tests
- test_batch_lookup_mixed_entries
- test_device_key_lookup_scenarios (3 param variants)
- test_device_key_priority
- test_hash_checking_disabled_edge_cases (4 param variants)
- test_make_lookup_key_variants
- test_multiple_calls_work
- test_successful_lookup_with_template_filtering
- test_template_hash_checking (4 param variants)
- test_template_hash_checking_disabled
- test_template_hash_mixed_scenarios
- test_validation_error

## Sample error
```
AssertionError: 'triton' not found in {}
```
(test_make_lookup_key_variants: `AssertionError: None is not an instance of <class 'str'>`)

## Repro
```
python test/inductor/test_lookup_table.py TestLookupTable.test_make_lookup_key_variants
```

issues.title: [Inductor][XPU] test_lookup_table.py TestLookupTableE2E fails: choice filtering not applied on XPU
issues.body:
## Description
All `TestLookupTableE2E` tests in `test/inductor/test_lookup_table.py` fail on XPU with "Expected N choices, got M" because the lookup-table-based autotune choice filtering is never applied.

## Root cause
Same as #5442: `LookupTableChoices._get_device_key` only supports `"cuda"`, so `make_lookup_key` returns `None` on XPU. The lookup table entry set up by the test is never matched, so no choices are filtered and the full default choice set reaches `verify_choice_names`.

## Failing tests
- test_decompose_k_lookup_table_entry
- test_mixed_template_configs
- test_multiple_configs_same_template
- test_template_hash_filtering_e2e
- test_tma_lookup_table_entry (addmm, mm)
- test_valid_lookup_table_entry (addmm, bmm, mm, mm_plus_mm)

## Sample error
```
torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: LoweringException: ValueError: Expected 1 choices, got 8
  target: aten.mm.default (xpu:0, torch.float16)
```

## Repro
```
python test/inductor/test_lookup_table.py TestLookupTableE2E.test_valid_lookup_table_entry_operation_mm
```

Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | pytorch | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Checked on the latest XPU nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261019+xpu` (BMG, `xpu:0`) against `pytorch/pytorch` `origin/main` @ `9544ec5e23`. On current `main` the whole file is gated behind `@unittest.skipIf(not HAS_CUDA_AND_TRITON, "CUDA not available")` and `BaseE2ELookupTableTest.setUp` hardcodes `torch.device("cuda")`, so on XPU every case reports `skipped`, not `failed`. Per the reproduce contract the CUDA-only marker was lifted in place (gate -> `HAS_GPU`, device -> `GPU_TYPE`) and the case re-run; the file was reverted afterwards. Without the marker the reported failure appears, which confirms the skip was hiding it. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `TestLookupTableE2E.test_valid_lookup_table_entry_operation_mm` | REPRODUCED | `InductorError: LoweringException: ValueError: Expected 1 choices, got 5` (`target: aten.mm.default`, `xpu:0`, `torch.float16`) | The choice count differs from the 8 quoted in the issue only because the nightly's default `max_mm_configs` has moved; the signature and cause are the same. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at `pytorch@9544ec5e23` (`origin/main`), nightly `2.16.0.dev20261019+xpu`. `LookupTableChoices._get_device_key` (`torch/_inductor/lookup_table/choices.py:49-56`) returns `None` for every device whose `type != "cuda"`, and `_get_lookup_table` (`choices.py:37`) additionally hard-gates on `torch.cuda.is_available()`. On XPU both gates fire: `make_lookup_key` bails out at `choices.py:107-110` because `dev_key is None`, so `lookup_template_configs` finds no key variant and returns `{}` (`choices.py:234-263`). With no configs returned, Inductor never filters the autotune choice set, and the `verify_choice_names` preprocessing hook the test installs sees the full default set -- `ValueError: Expected 1 choices, got 5` on `aten.mm.default (xpu:0, torch.float16)`. The CUDA device key is not an architecture string at all: `gcnArchName` is bound to `cudaDeviceProp::gcnArchName` only on ROCm builds and aliases plain `cudaDeviceProp::name` on CUDA builds (`torch/csrc/cuda/Module.cpp:1229-1236`). The exact XPU analog is therefore `torch.xpu.get_device_properties(index).name`, which keeps key semantics identical across backends and needs no new API. The tests cannot observe the fix as written: the file hardcodes `torch.device("cuda")` in `BaseE2ELookupTableTest.setUp` (`test/inductor/test_lookup_table.py:719`) and in `create_mock_mm_kernel_inputs`' default (`:103`), and both test classes are gated by `@unittest.skipIf(not HAS_CUDA_AND_TRITON, "CUDA not available")` (`:164`, `:854`). The file's own `__main__` guard is already GPU-generic (`if HAS_GPU and HAS_CPU and is_big_gpu()`, `:1110`) and `is_big_gpu` already carries an XPU branch (`torch/_inductor/utils.py:2134`), so generalizing the gates to `HAS_GPU` / `GPU_TYPE` follows the direction the file already set. Prior art: `pytorch/pytorch#196414` proposed a new `DeviceInterface.get_lookup_architecture()` hook for exactly this; it was closed unmerged (2026-09-30) on process grounds -- a maintainer asked for the design to be discussed on `pytorch/pytorch#200253` first. A new public `DeviceInterface` method is therefore the wrong bet; the in-tree idiom for XPU enablement in Inductor is a direct per-device branch (`torch/_inductor/utils.py:2146-2149`). `pytorch/pytorch#192986` is open and refactors this same test file, so expect textual collision there. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- device-key generalization plus test device-genericization, both inside `torch/_inductor` and `test/inductor` - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Domain:** inductor *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** pytorch - **Analyzed at:** `pytorch@9544ec5e23` - **What I changed:** `torch/_inductor/lookup_table/choices.py` (+12/-9): `_get_device_key` gains an XPU branch and the CUDA branch is rewritten as an explicit per-device dispatch; `_get_lookup_table`'s availability gate moves from `torch.cuda.is_available()` to `torch.accelerator.is_available()`; one stale log string. `test/inductor/test_lookup_table.py` (+11/-9): both class gates go from `HAS_CUDA_AND_TRITON` to `HAS_GPU`, and every hardcoded `cuda` device becomes `GPU_TYPE`. - **Why:** `gcnArchName` is bound to `cudaDeviceProp::gcnArchName` only on ROCm builds and aliases plain `cudaDeviceProp::name` on CUDA builds (`torch/csrc/cuda/Module.cpp:1229-1236`), so `torch.xpu.get_device_properties(index).name` is the exact XPU analog and the key keeps the same meaning on every backend. `torch.accelerator.is_available()` is already the in-tree gate idiom (`torch/_inductor/codecache.py:1683`). `HAS_GPU` / `GPU_TYPE` is the direction the file already set: its `__main__` guard is `if HAS_GPU and HAS_CPU and is_big_gpu()` (`test/inductor/test_lookup_table.py:1110` pre-patch) and `is_big_gpu` already branches on XPU (`torch/_inductor/utils.py:2134`). No new public API, deliberately: `pytorch/pytorch#196414` added a `DeviceInterface.get_lookup_architecture()` hook for this and was closed unmerged pending design discussion on `pytorch/pytorch#200253`. - **Skip added:** no (two pre-existing CUDA-only gates were *loosened*, so strictly more tests run; a fresh-context skip-guard reviewer confirmed no skip-shaped workaround in the diff) - **Ready for verify:** yes ```diff --- a/torch/_inductor/lookup_table/choices.py +++ b/torch/_inductor/lookup_table/choices.py @@ -34,7 +34,7 @@ class LookupTableChoices(InductorChoices): Get the template lookup table from config. Override this method to use custom lookup table sources (database, API, etc.). """ - if not torch.cuda.is_available() or config.lookup_table.table is None: + if not torch.accelerator.is_available() or config.lookup_table.table is None: return {} return config.lookup_table.table @@ -45,15 +45,18 @@ class LookupTableChoices(InductorChoices): Generate a device key for lookup table indexing. For CPU devices, returns None. For CUDA devices, returns the props.gcnArchName string. + For XPU devices, returns the props.name string. """ - if device.type != "cuda": - # only cuda devices are supported, this indicates that the system is not in use - # for this device - return None + # gcnArchName is the gfx target on ROCm and an alias of props.name on + # CUDA, so props.name is the matching key for other accelerators. + if device.type == "cuda": + return torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device.index).gcnArchName + if device.type == "xpu": + return torch.xpu.get_device_properties(device.index).name - # Get CUDA device properties - props = torch.cuda.get_device_properties(device.index) - return props.gcnArchName + # only cuda and xpu devices are supported, this indicates that the system + # is not in use for this device + return None @@ -226,7 +229,7 @@ class LookupTableChoices(InductorChoices): lookup_table = self._get_lookup_table() if not lookup_table: - log.debug("Lookup table: no table configured or CUDA unavailable") + log.debug("Lookup table: no table configured or no accelerator available") return {} --- a/test/inductor/test_lookup_table.py +++ b/test/inductor/test_lookup_table.py @@ -24,7 +24,7 @@ -from torch.testing._internal.inductor_utils import HAS_CPU, HAS_CUDA_AND_TRITON, HAS_GPU +from torch.testing._internal.inductor_utils import GPU_TYPE, HAS_CPU, HAS_GPU @@ -100,11 +100,13 @@ class BaseLookupTableTest(TestCase): def create_mock_mm_kernel_inputs( self, shapes: list[tuple[int, ...]] | None = None, - device: torch.device = torch.device("cuda"), + device: torch.device | None = None, dtype: torch.dtype = torch.float32, scalars: dict[str, float | int] | None = None, ) -> MockMMKernelInputs: """Create MockMMKernelInputs with real tensors""" + if device is None: + device = torch.device(GPU_TYPE) if shapes is None: @@ -161,7 +163,7 @@ -@unittest.skipIf(not HAS_CUDA_AND_TRITON, "CUDA not available") +@unittest.skipIf(not HAS_GPU, "Triton + GPU not available") @instantiate_parametrized_tests class TestLookupTable(BaseLookupTableTest): @@ -553,7 +555,7 @@ (x3, in test_device_key_lookup_scenarios' stub overrides) class TableKeyChoices(LookupTableChoices): @staticmethod def _get_device_key(device): - if device.type != "cuda": + if device.type != GPU_TYPE: return None @@ -716,7 +718,7 @@ class BaseE2ELookupTableTest(BaseLookupTableTest): - self.device = torch.device("cuda") + self.device = torch.device(GPU_TYPE) @@ -851,7 +853,7 @@ -@unittest.skipIf(not HAS_CUDA_AND_TRITON, "CUDA not available") +@unittest.skipIf(not HAS_GPU, "Triton + GPU not available") @instantiate_parametrized_tests class TestLookupTableE2E(BaseE2ELookupTableTest): ``` *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verify Verified on a source build of the fix branch -- `torch 2.16.0a0+git6424a48`, `TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc`, BMG, `TORCHINDUCTOR_FORCE_DISABLE_CACHES=1`. A source build was needed only because the fix lives inside the installed `torch` package; nothing C++ changed. Baseline and fixed trees differ only by the two changed files. | Test case | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `TestLookupTableE2E::test_valid_lookup_table_entry_operation_mm` | FAIL | PASS | | `TestLookupTableE2E::test_valid_lookup_table_entry_operation_addmm` | FAIL | PASS | | `TestLookupTableE2E::test_valid_lookup_table_entry_operation_bmm` | FAIL | PASS | | `TestLookupTableE2E::test_valid_lookup_table_entry_operation_mm_plus_mm` | FAIL | PASS | | `TestLookupTableE2E::test_tma_lookup_table_entry_operation_mm` | FAIL | PASS | | `TestLookupTableE2E::test_tma_lookup_table_entry_operation_addmm` | FAIL | PASS | | `TestLookupTableE2E::test_decompose_k_lookup_table_entry` | FAIL | PASS | | `TestLookupTableE2E::test_mixed_template_configs` | FAIL | PASS | | `TestLookupTableE2E::test_multiple_configs_same_template` | FAIL | PASS | | `TestLookupTableE2E::test_template_hash_filtering_e2e` | FAIL | PASS | | rest of `test_lookup_table.py` (incl. all of `TestLookupTable`) | FAIL / skipped | PASS | `Before` was `InductorError: LoweringException: ValueError: Expected 1 choices, got 5`. **Causality was isolated on a single build**, so this is not just "passes on a newer tree": with the test file generalized but `torch/_inductor/lookup_table/choices.py` reverted to base `9544ec5e23`, the file reports `29 failed, 8 passed`; with `choices.py` fixed it reports `37 passed`. On the unmodified base the same build reports `37 skipped`, which is how this went unnoticed. Regression checks on the fixed build: | Suite | Result | |---|---| | `test/inductor/test_lookup_table.py` (whole file) | 37 passed | | `test/inductor/test_select_algorithm.py` | 54 passed, 1 skipped, 3 failed -- all 3 reproduce on base `9544ec5e23` and are unrelated (`test_benchmark_request_restores_serialized_cudagraph_policy`, `test_benchmark_request_uses_automatic_cudagraph_policy`, `test_bmm_xpu_ascending_k_loop`) | `LookupTableChoices` is opt-in -- `config.lookup_table.table` defaults to `None` and nothing in `torch/` installs the handler by default -- so the blast radius of the `choices.py` change is the lookup-table path, which `test_lookup_table.py` covers end to end. - **Verdict:** PASSED -- all 37 cases in the file pass, and the product fix is demonstrably what makes them pass - **Lint:** clean (`spin fixlint` changed no files; `spin lint` reports no issues) *Automated by fix-verify.*
Summary **Outcome:** IMPLEMENTING(fix_verified) One bug sits behind all eleven failing cases: Inductor's autotune lookup table was wired to CUDA only, so on XPU `LookupTableChoices` produced no lookup key, returned no configs, and never filtered the choice set -- the tests then saw the full default set and raised `Expected N choices, got M`. Verification isolated causality on a single source build: generalized test with the old `choices.py` gives 29 failures, with the fix 37/37 pass, and on the untouched base the same build silently reports 37 skipped. The patch deliberately avoids new public API: `pytorch/pytorch#196414` solved this with a new `DeviceInterface.get_lookup_architecture()` hook and was closed unmerged pending a design discussion on `pytorch/pytorch#200253`, so this takes the per-device-branch idiom already used elsewhere in `torch/_inductor` instead. The CUDA device key is not an architecture string at all: gcnArchName is bound to cudaDeviceProp::gcnArchName only on ROCm builds and aliases plain cudaDeviceProp::name on CUDA builds (torch/csrc/cuda/Module.cpp:1229-1236). The exact XPU analog is therefore torch.xpu.get_device_properties(index).name, which keeps key semantics identical across backends and needs no new API.

The file's own __main__ guard is already GPU-generic (if HAS_GPU and HAS_CPU and is_big_gpu(), :1110) and is_big_gpu already carries an XPU branch (torch/_inductor/utils.py:2134), so generalizing the gates to HAS_GPU / GPU_TYPE follows the direction the file already set.
Prior art: pytorch/pytorch#196414 proposed a new DeviceInterface.get_lookup_architecture() hook for exactly this; it was closed unmerged (2026-09-30) on process grounds -- a maintainer asked for the design to be discussed on pytorch/pytorch#200253 first. Domain: inductor

issues.title: test_snode_runtime.py ComputeBoundedTests return 0 estimated runtime on XPU (roofline flops fallback swallowed)
issues.body:
## Description

Inductor's per-node runtime estimator returns `0` for all compute-bound ops on
XPU, so `test/inductor/test_snode_runtime.py::ComputeBoundedTests` (e.g.
`test_conv3d`, `test_conv2d`, `test_mm`) fail with `assertNotZero`.

## Root cause

In `torch/_inductor/scheduler.py::BaseSchedulerNode._get_estimated_runtime`:

```python
gpu_flops = get_device_tflops(dtype) * 10**12
...
if gpu_flops <= 0:
    raise AssertionError(f"gpu_flops cannot be <= 0, but got {gpu_flops}")
...
except Exception:
    return 0
```

On XPU, `get_device_tflops` (`torch/_inductor/utils.py`) calls `datasheet_tops`,
which returns `None` because the current XPU device is not present in
`torch/_inductor/analysis/device_info.py`. With no CUDA available it returns
`0.0` and logs "roofline estimates will use memory bandwidth only".

However, the scheduler's `gpu_flops <= 0` guard raises `AssertionError`, which is
swallowed by `except Exception: return 0`. It therefore never reaches the
memory-bandwidth fallback (the `flops_est == 0` branch), even though
`gpu_memory_bandwidth` is valid. The estimated runtime becomes `0`.

## Repro

```
python test/inductor/test_snode_runtime.py ComputeBoundedTests.test_conv3d
```

## Expected

When device TFLOPS are unknown (`gpu_flops <= 0`), fall back to the
memory-bandwidth-only estimate instead of returning `0`. Additionally, adding the
XPU device spec to `device_info.py` would provide a real flops estimate.

## Environment
- Device: Intel XPU
- Affected tests: `ComputeBoundedTests.test_conv1d/conv2d/conv2d_transpose/conv3d/mm/addmm/bmm/...`

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-09-20] ctc_loss on XPU indexes with unvalidated target labels: out-of-bounds read in forward, out-of-bounds write in backward
issues.body:
<!-- alignment-published-unit: pr-197799 -->
## Summary

`torch.nn.functional.ctc_loss` on XPU accepts target label values outside `[0, num_classes)` and uses them directly as indices into device memory. The forward alpha kernel reads at the out-of-range label offset and the backward kernel writes the accumulated gradient at that offset. Both return normally, so an invalid label produces a finite loss and a silent out-of-bounds device write instead of an error.

## Upstream source

- pytorch/pytorch#197799 (open, unmerged) "Fix ctc_loss CPU OOB access on out-of-range target values", fixing pytorch/pytorch#193794. It adds a `check_target_values` helper to `aten/src/ATen/native/LossCTC.cpp`, gated on `targets.device().is_cpu()`, and states in its own notes: "Remaining scope: CUDA, XPU, and MPS kernels are untouched. The CUDA implementation documents the same gap at `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/LossCTC.cu:212-214`; validating there needs a device sync, so it is left for a separate change."
- Alignment scan window: `[2026-09-20T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-21T00:00:00Z)`, `pytorch/pytorch` frozen default-branch head `f3d603baf74daa6ac8fbf15feb37f0edb6ac9ad3`.

## Observed XPU behavior

With `num_classes = 20` and target values `100` and `-5` (batch rows 0 and 1), no exception is raised in either direction:

```text
TARGET: xpu device = Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
torch version: 2.15.0.dev20260920+xpu
TARGET: in-range control loss = 11.84984302520752 device = xpu:0
TARGET: out-of-range targets xpu:0 values 100 -5 num_classes 20
forward returned 11.999288558959961 without raising
backward also returned without raising
```

## Target-path evidence

`_ctc_loss` for XPU dispatches to `ctc_loss_xpu` (`src/ATen/native/xpu/LossCTC.cpp:18`), which calls `at::native::xpu::ctc_loss_kernel` in `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LossCTCKernels.cpp`. Only XPU tensors are used in the reproducer and both the control loss and the bad-target loss are produced on `xpu:0`, so no CPU kernel participates.

The XPU kernel validates `BLANK`, the tensor shapes, `target_lengths[i] >= 0`, and `targets.size(1) >= max_target_length` (`LossCTCKernels.cpp:292-390`), but never the target values themselves. `get_target_prime` carries the ported CUDA comment `- note that no bound-checking is done` (`LossCTCKernels.cpp:42`) and returns `target[offset + stride * (idx / 2)]`, which is then used as an index:

- forward alpha kernel: `log_probs_data_[... + lp_char_stride_ * target_prime]` (`LossCTCKernels.cpp:103-140`)
- backward gradient kernel: `gradient_data_[gr_batch_offset + t * gr_input_stride_ + gr_char_stride_ * current_target_prime]`, an unbounded **write** index (`LossCTCKernels.cpp:800-811`)

## Reproducer

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

T, N, C, L = 50, 2, 20, 10
torch.manual_seed(0)
log_probs = torch.randn(T, N, C, device="xpu").log_softmax(2).requires_grad_()
input_lengths = torch.full((N,), T, dtype=torch.long, device="xpu")
target_lengths = torch.full((N,), L, dtype=torch.long, device="xpu")

in_range = torch.randint(1, C, (N, L), dtype=torch.long, device="xpu")
control = F.ctc_loss(log_probs, in_range, input_lengths, target_lengths)
torch.xpu.synchronize()
print("in-range control loss =", float(control.detach()), "device =", control.device)

bad = in_range.clone()
bad[0, 0] = C + 80   # 100, out of range for num_classes = 20
bad[1, 0] = -5       # negative label

loss = F.ctc_loss(log_probs, bad, input_lengths, target_lengths)
torch.xpu.synchronize()
print("forward returned", float(loss.detach()), "without raising")
loss.backward()
torch.xpu.synchronize()
print("backward also returned without raising")
```

Expected: a `RuntimeError` naming the valid target range, as the upstream CPU fix raises (`Expected target values to be in the range [0, C), but got value 100 for batch 0`). Actual: both directions complete and the backward writes at the out-of-range label offset.

## Environment

```text
python:        /opt/conda/bin/python3.13 (3.13.13)
torch:         2.15.0.dev20260920+xpu
torch path:    /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/__init__.py
xpu available: true
xpu device:    Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
```

## Ownership rationale

The XPU `ctc_loss` forward and backward kernels, including all of their input validation, live in this repository (`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LossCTCKernels.cpp`); the upstream CPU allocator's new check is explicitly gated to CPU tensors, so no upstream change reaches the XPU path. A search of `pytorch/pytorch` found no issue or PR that owns target-value validation for the XPU kernel, and no existing `intel/torch-xpu-ops` tracker covers it (issue #1637 was a separate `test_ctc_loss_error_xpu` floating-point exception, closed as completed).

### Tradeoff for maintainers

CUDA has the identical gap and documents it deliberately (`aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/LossCTC.cu:211-214`, present at the frozen head: "we do not check that the labels are in the valid range. As we use them for indexing in the kernels, you'll see memory errors when you pass corrupt labels"). Upstream deferred the accelerator side of #197799 because host-side validation of device targets requires a device sync per call. So this is a memory-safety gap XPU shares with CUDA rather than an XPU-vs-CUDA divergence, and the fix approach is a maintainer decision: host-side validation with a sync, an in-kernel bounds assert, or waiting for the upstream accelerator decision. Filed so the gap is tracked with a runner-backed reproducer either way.

_Filed by the automated xpu-alignment scan; results were independently reviewed before filing._

- **Reproduced:** yes, on `2.15.0.dev20260920+xpu` (latest nightly). Forward and
  backward both complete normally for target values `100` and `-5` with
  `num_classes = 20`.

**Root cause.** The XPU `ctc_loss` kernels use target label values directly as the
label-axis index without any bounds check. `get_target_prime`
(`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LossCTCKernels.cpp:44`) returns
`target[offset + stride * (idx / 2)]` and carries the ported CUDA comment
`- note that no bound-checking is done`; the host-side argument validation in
`ctc_loss_kernel_template` (`LossCTCKernels.cpp:292-392`) checks `BLANK`, the
tensor shapes and the two length lists, but never the target values. The returned
label then indexes device memory in four places: the forward alpha kernel
(`:96-137`, `:183`), the backward beta kernel (`:489`, `:514-523`), the
non-blank gradient collector -- which reads `targets_data_` directly rather than
through `get_target_prime` (`:664`) and uses it as an atomic **write** index
(`:686`) -- and the naive gradient collector (`:800-811`). Upstream's CPU fix
(pytorch/pytorch#197799 open) gates its new `check_target_values` helper on
`targets.device().is_cpu()`, so no upstream change reaches the XPU path. CPU on
the tested nightly also still accepts the bad label, confirming the upstream fix
has not landed.

**Fix strategy.** Validate the label in-kernel with `SYCL_KERNEL_ASSERT`, which is
this repo's established pattern for exactly this situation -- see
`CHECK_INDEX_IN_CLASS` in `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LossNLLKernel.cpp:30-35`,
used for `nll_loss` target bounds, and the same idiom in `Indexing.cpp`,
`ScatterGatherKernels.cpp` and `EmbeddingBag.h`. Concretely: thread `num_labels`
into `get_target_prime` and assert `0 <= label < num_labels` there (one choke
point covering six of the seven read sites), add the same assert at the direct
read in `CTCLossBackwardCollectNonblankKernelFunctor`, and plumb a `num_labels_`
member into the three functors that lack one
(`CTCLossLogAlphaKernelFunctor`, `CTCLossBackwardLogBetaKernelFunctor`,
`CTCLossBackwardCollectNonblankKernelFunctor`;
`CTCLossBackwardCollectKernelFunctor` already has it). Every `get_target_prime`
call site is already guarded by `s < 2 * target_length + 1` / `s < target_length`,
so only entries the kernels actually read are checked -- padding beyond
`target_lengths[b]` stays legal, matching the upstream CPU patch's semantics.

**Tradeoff (the issue names three options; this picks the second).** A host-side
check would need a D2H copy plus a full device sync on every `ctc_loss` call,
which is why upstream deferred it for accelerators. The in-kernel assert costs
nothing for valid input and needs no sync, but its failure mode is a device
assert that aborts the process with a diagnostic naming the file, line and
failing condition -- not a catchable `RuntimeError` as the issue's "Expected"
line asks for. That is the same behaviour `nll_loss` already has on XPU today,
verified on this runner:
`LossNLLKernel.cpp:155: Assertion 't >= 0 && t < n_classes' failed.`, exit 134.
It diverges from CUDA in the safe direction; CUDA's `ctc_loss` still has the gap.
If maintainers prefer the catchable error and accept the per-call sync, the
host-side variant is a separate change.

- **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- root cause is in this repo's SYCL kernel and the
  fix follows an existing in-repo pattern.

issues.title: Enable Inductor collective autotuning on XPU (device-agnostic _run_collective_benchmark)
issues.body:
## Summary
Inductor's collective autotuning path is currently CUDA-only. On an XPU build, the collective autotuning tests (e.g. `test/inductor/test_collective_autotuning.py`) pass while actually autotuning nothing — every choice is skipped and the autotuner silently falls back to the default implementation.

## Root Cause
`SelectAlgorithm._run_collective_benchmark` uses `torch.cuda.synchronize()` and `torch.cuda.Event` unconditionally:
- `torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py:5291`
- `torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py:5296`
- `torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py:5298-5299`

On an XPU-only build these raise `AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled`, so every choice fails and the autotuner falls back.

## Reproduction
Running the collective autotuning tests on 8x PVC (`xccl` available, `get_default_backend_for_device("xpu:0") == "xccl"`):

```
Collective benchmark exception for choice test::equiv_ar_autotuned_sum_allreduce_0. Skipping this choice.
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py", line 5348, in benchmark_collective_choice
    cls._run_collective_benchmark(
  File "torch/_inductor/select_algorithm.py", line 5291, in _run_collective_benchmark
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
  File "torch/cuda/__init__.py", line 596, in _lazy_init
    raise AssertionError("Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled")
AssertionError: Torch not compiled with CUDA enabled

Autotune Choices Stats:
{"num_choices": 3, "num_triton_choices": 0, "best_kernel": "...sum_allreduce_0", "best_time": Infinity}
At least one choice failed or timed out during collective benchmarking. Falling back to default implementation.
```

## Proposed Fix
Make `_run_collective_benchmark` device-agnostic (use the appropriate accelerator's `synchronize()` / `Event`, e.g. via `torch.accelerator` or the device-appropriate module) so collective autotuning works on XPU.

Ref: [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#197533]

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-09-21] adaptive_max_pool3d_backward on XPU reads a non-contiguous indices tensor as if it were contiguous: silently wrong gradients under torch.compile with channels_last_3d inputs
issues.body:
<!-- alignment-published-unit: issue-197888 -->
## Summary

`adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel` in `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/AdaptiveMaxPooling3dKernels.cpp` makes `gradOutput` contiguous but reads `indices` through its raw data pointer. When `indices` arrives with `channels_last_3d` strides the kernel scatters the gradient to the wrong positions, with no error. Inductor lays the saved indices out in the input's memory format, so `F.adaptive_max_pool3d` under `torch.compile` on a `channels_last_3d` XPU input trains with silently wrong gradients through every adaptive max pool.

This is the XPU half of upstream `pytorch/pytorch#197888`, which reports the same class of defect for the CPU kernels of `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward`, `fractional_max_pool2d_backward` and `fractional_max_pool3d_backward`. Only `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward` reproduces on XPU; the two XPU `fractional_max_pool*_backward` kernels use `PackedTensorAccessor64`, honour the real strides, and are correct.

## Upstream source and scan window

- Upstream issue: [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#197888] (OPEN, no fix PR as of this scan)
- Scan window: `[2026-09-21T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-22T00:00:00Z)` on `pytorch/pytorch`
- Frozen `pytorch/pytorch` default-branch head: `6b5c7ad181277ba21aa48b1dc03786ab95f68ad4`
- Upstream oracle: the correct gradient is the one obtained when the same index values are read with their real strides (equivalently, from a contiguous copy of `indices`). Upstream reports that on CUDA the compiled gradient matches eager, so upstream's stated fix scope is the CPU kernels.

## Root cause in this repository

`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/AdaptiveMaxPooling3dKernels.cpp`, `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel`:

```cpp
void adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel(
    const Tensor& gradOutput,
    const Tensor& input,
    const Tensor& indices,
    const Tensor& gradInput) {
  const Tensor gradOutput_ = gradOutput.contiguous();   // indices is not normalized
  ...
          const int64_t* indices_data = indices.const_data_ptr<int64_t>();
```

`gradOutput` is normalized, `indices` is not, and both templates then index `indices_data` with contiguous arithmetic. The XPU kernel is reached through `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_out_xpu` in `src/ATen/native/xpu/AdaptiveMaxPooling3d.cpp`.

The upstream CUDA kernel (`aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/AdaptiveMaxPooling3d.cu` at the frozen head) carries the same raw-pointer pattern, but upstream reports its compiled path does not hit it; the XPU compiled path does.

## Reproducer

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

A = torch.ops.aten

# 1. Kernel level: identical index values, contiguous vs channels_last_3d strides.
torch.manual_seed(0)
x3 = torch.randperm(240).float().reshape(1, 4, 4, 3, 5).to("xpu")
v, i = F.adaptive_max_pool3d(x3, (2, 3, 5), return_indices=True)
go = torch.arange(1.0, v.numel() + 1, device="xpu").reshape(v.shape)
i_nc = i.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last_3d)  # same values, different strides
print("indices strides", tuple(i_nc.stride()))
print(
    "same gradient as with contiguous indices:",
    torch.equal(
        A.adaptive_max_pool3d_backward(go, x3, i),
        A.adaptive_max_pool3d_backward(go, x3, i_nc),
    ),
)

# 2. User level: eager vs aot_eager vs inductor on a channels_last_3d input.
torch.manual_seed(0)
f = lambda t: F.adaptive_max_pool3d(t, (2, 3, 5))
x = torch.randperm(1 * 4 * 4 * 6 * 5).float().reshape(1, 4, 4, 6, 5).to("xpu")
for name, xin in (
    ("contiguous", x),
    ("channels_last_3d", x.contiguous(memory_format=torch.channels_last_3d)),
):
    grads = []
    for backend in (None, "aot_eager", "inductor"):
        torch._dynamo.reset()
        t = xin.detach().clone(memory_format=torch.preserve_format).requires_grad_()
        out = (f if backend is None else torch.compile(f, backend=backend))(t)
        w = torch.arange(1.0, out.numel() + 1, device="xpu").reshape(out.shape)
        (out * w).sum().backward()
        grads.append(t.grad.clone())
    print(
        f"{name:17s} aot_eager==eager: {torch.equal(grads[0], grads[1])}"
        f"   inductor==eager: {torch.equal(grads[0], grads[2])}"
        f"   max diff {(grads[0] - grads[2]).abs().max().item():.0f}"
    )
```

## Observed XPU behavior

```
KERNEL: adaptive_max_pool3d_backward indices_stride=(120, 1, 60, 20, 4) same_gradient_as_contiguous_indices=False
KERNEL: adaptive_max_pool2d_backward indices_stride=(60, 1, 20, 4) same_gradient_as_contiguous_indices=True
KERNEL: max_pool3d_with_indices_backward indices_stride=(96, 1, 32, 16, 4) same_gradient_as_contiguous_indices=True
KERNEL: fractional_max_pool2d_backward indices_stride=(36, 1, 12, 4) same_gradient_as_contiguous_indices=True
KERNEL: fractional_max_pool3d_backward indices_stride=(32, 1, 16, 8, 4) same_gradient_as_contiguous_indices=True
COMPILE: contiguous aot_eager==eager=True inductor==eager=True max_diff=0.0
COMPILE: channels_last_3d aot_eager==eager=True inductor==eager=False max_diff=118.0
```

## Target-path evidence

All five pooling backward ops were invoked with `xpu` tensors and asserted to have produced `xpu` outputs, so the divergence comes from the XPU SYCL kernels rather than from a host fallback. At user level, `aot_eager==eager=True` while `inductor==eager=False` on the same `channels_last_3d` XPU input, and `t.grad.device.type` was asserted to be `xpu`; that isolates the wrong gradient to the XPU backward kernel reached through inductor's memory-format choice, not to the tracing layer.

## Environment

```
torch            2.15.0.dev20260920+xpu
torch path       /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/__init__.py
python           3.13.13 (/opt/conda/bin/python3.13)
xpu available    True
xpu device       Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
```

## Ownership rationale

The wrong code is `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel` in this repository, reached through `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_out_xpu`; the fix is to normalize `indices` next to the existing `gradOutput.contiguous()` (or to index it through its real strides). Upstream `pytorch/pytorch#197888` reports CUDA's compiled gradient as correct and scopes its suggested fix to the CPU kernels, so landing it would not change the XPU kernel. No `pytorch/pytorch` issue or PR was found that explicitly owns the XPU part, and no existing `intel/torch-xpu-ops` tracker covers it.

Scope note for whoever picks this up: only `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward` needs the change on XPU. `adaptive_max_pool2d_backward`, `max_pool3d_with_indices_backward` and both `fractional_max_pool*_backward` kernels already handle non-contiguous `indices` correctly, so the two `fractional_max_pool*` thirds of the upstream oracle do not apply here.

Filed by the XPU alignment automation; the finding was produced by a scan and independently reviewed before filing.
