Reproduce Reproduced against the latest XPU nightly wheel `2.15.0.dev20260920+xpu` on an Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics device, using the reproducer from the issue body plus one extra case that forces the `atomic` variant of the same kernel (`isizeH % osizeH != 0`). | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | kernel, non-atomic path (`1x4x4x3x5 -> 2x3x5`) | REPRODUCED | `same_gradient_as_contiguous_indices=False` for `indices.stride()==(120, 1, 60, 20, 4)` | | kernel, atomic path (`1x4x4x5x5 -> 2x3x5`) | REPRODUCED | `same_gradient_as_contiguous_indices=False`, so both kernel templates are affected | | `torch.compile` end-to-end, `channels_last_3d` input | REPRODUCED | `inductor==eager=False`, `max_diff=118`; `aot_eager==eager=True` | `torch.compile` on a contiguous input is unaffected (`inductor==eager=True`), which matches the issue's claim that the trigger is the memory format inductor picks for the saved `indices`. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at `torch-xpu-ops@6a2d048e`, pytorch `origin/main@00ec4ca3a9`. `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel` (`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/AdaptiveMaxPooling3dKernels.cpp:500`) normalizes only one of the three tensors its kernels address with contiguous index arithmetic. Line 505 takes `gradOutput.contiguous()`, but `indices` is passed straight through as a raw pointer (lines 553 and 577) and both kernel templates then walk it as if it were contiguous: `indices_ + o_plane * osizeH_ * osizeW_ + oh * osizeW_ + ow` (lines 285 and 360). With `channels_last_3d` `indices` those offsets land on unrelated elements, so `atomicAdd`/`+=` scatters each `gradOutput` element to whatever input position the misread index happens to name -- wrong gradients, no error. The same applies to the destination: lines 550/574 take `gradInput.mutable_data_ptr()` and lines 283/358 offset it as `gradInput_ + d * isizeT_ * isizeH_ * isizeW_`, so a non-contiguous `gradInput` is written through contiguous arithmetic too. Both instances are silent and both are reachable from Python on the current nightly (`2.15.0.dev20260920+xpu`): the `indices` one through `torch.compile`, which saves `indices` in the input's memory format, and the `gradInput` one through the `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward.grad_input` out= overload -- pytorch's meta function requests contiguous strides with `set_output_raw_strided(0, input.sizes(), {}, input.options())` (`aten/src/ATen/native/AdaptiveMaxPooling3d.cpp:81`), and an empty `strides` argument does not restride a caller-supplied `out`. The XPU kernel is a direct port of the CUDA one, which carries the same raw-`indices` pattern (`aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/AdaptiveMaxPooling3d.cu:403,449,472`), so upstream `pytorch/pytorch#197888` -- which scopes its fix to the CPU kernels because it observes CUDA's compiled gradient as correct -- would not change the XPU path. The sibling 2D kernel in this repository already carries the fix pattern: `adaptive_max_pool2d_backward_kernel` normalizes `grad_output` and `indices` and stages a contiguous `grad_input` with a copy-back (`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/AdaptiveMaxPooling2dKernels.cpp:341-345,391-393`), and `#3941` established that idiom for the non-contiguous-output case in the same family. Fix strategy: apply that same normalization inside `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel`. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- kernel-local fix, pattern already present in the sibling 2D kernel - **Target repo:** torch-xpu-ops - **Domain:** xpu-kernel *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implementation One file changed: `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/AdaptiveMaxPooling3dKernels.cpp`. `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel` now normalizes `indices` the same way it already normalized `gradOutput`, and stages a contiguous `gradInput` with a copy-back when the caller's `gradInput` is not contiguous. Both dispatch lambdas (atomic and non-atomic) take their pointers from the normalized tensors. This is the idiom `adaptive_max_pool2d_backward_kernel` already uses in this repository. ```diff void adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel( const Tensor& input, const Tensor& indices, const Tensor& gradInput) { + // Both kernel templates address gradOutput, indices and gradInput with + // contiguous index arithmetic, so all three have to be normalized here. const Tensor gradOutput_ = gradOutput.contiguous(); + const Tensor indices_ = indices.contiguous(); + const Tensor gradInput_ = gradInput.is_contiguous() + ? gradInput + : at::empty(gradInput.sizes(), gradInput.options()); - gradInput.zero_(); + gradInput_.zero_(); @@ (both AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND2 lambdas) - scalar_t* gradInput_data = gradInput.mutable_data_ptr(); + scalar_t* gradInput_data = gradInput_.mutable_data_ptr(); const scalar_t* gradOutput_data = gradOutput_.const_data_ptr(); - const int64_t* indices_data = indices.const_data_ptr(); + const int64_t* indices_data = indices_.const_data_ptr(); @@ (end of function) } + + if (!gradInput.is_contiguous()) { + gradInput.copy_(gradInput_); + } } ``` The alternative -- teaching the kernels to take strides, as the forward kernel does for its input -- was rejected: the forward kernel encodes `argmax` as a contiguous linear offset, so honoring arbitrary `gradInput` strides would mean changing an index encoding that the CPU and CUDA kernels share. Skip-guard review: APPROVE (no skip-shaped workaround; kernel-only change). *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verification Source build of pytorch `00ec4ca3a9` with this branch checked out at `third_party/torch-xpu-ops` (`USE_XPU=1`, `TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc`), on an Intel Arc Pro B60. `torch 2.15.0a0+git00ec4ca` imported from the source tree, worktree clean. | Case | Before (nightly `2.15.0.dev20260920+xpu`) | After | |---|---|---| | backward kernel, non-atomic template, `channels_last_3d` `indices` | wrong gradient | matches contiguous | | backward kernel, atomic template, `channels_last_3d` `indices` | wrong gradient | matches contiguous | | `torch.compile` (inductor) vs eager, `channels_last_3d` input | `max_diff=118` | `max_diff=0` | | `torch.compile` (inductor) vs eager, contiguous input | `max_diff=0` | `max_diff=0` | | `adaptive_max_pool3d_backward.grad_input` out= with `channels_last_3d` `gradInput` | wrong gradient | matches contiguous | `aot_eager` matched eager both before and after, which is consistent with the root cause being in the XPU kernel rather than in the decomposition. ``` pytest -q test/xpu/test_ops_xpu.py -k adaptive_max_pool3d # 19 passed pytest -q test/xpu/test_modules_xpu.py -k AdaptiveMaxPool3d # 24 passed, 2 skipped lintrunner -a -m HEAD~1 # no lint issues ``` - **Verdict:** PASSED *Automated by fix-verify.*

body plus one extra case that forces the atomic variant of the same kernel

REPRODUCED

Line 505 takes gradOutput.contiguous(), but indices is passed straight

One file changed: src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/AdaptiveMaxPooling3dKernels.cpp.
adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel now normalizes indices the same way it
already normalized gradOutput, and stages a contiguous gradInput with a
copy-back when the caller's gradInput is not contiguous. Both dispatch lambdas
(atomic and non-atomic) take their pointers from the normalized tensors. This is
the idiom adaptive_max_pool2d_backward_kernel already uses in this repository.
 void adaptive_max_pool3d_backward_kernel(
     const Tensor& input,
     const Tensor& indices,
     const Tensor& gradInput) {
+  // Both kernel templates address gradOutput, indices and gradInput with
+  // contiguous index arithmetic, so all three have to be normalized here.
   const Tensor gradOutput_ = gradOutput.contiguous();
+  const Tensor indices_ = indices.contiguous();
+  const Tensor gradInput_ = gradInput.is_contiguous()
+      ? gradInput
+      : at::empty(gradInput.sizes(), gradInput.options());

-  gradInput.zero_();
+  gradInput_.zero_();
@@ (both AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND2 lambdas)
-          scalar_t* gradInput_data = gradInput.mutable_data_ptr<scalar_t>();
+          scalar_t* gradInput_data = gradInput_.mutable_data_ptr<scalar_t>();

               gradOutput_.const_data_ptr<scalar_t>();
-          const int64_t* indices_data = indices.const_data_ptr<int64_t>();
+          const int64_t* indices_data = indices_.const_data_ptr<int64_t>();
@@ (end of function)
   }
+
+  if (!gradInput.is_contiguous()) {
+    gradInput.copy_(gradInput_);
+  }
 }

contiguous linear offset, so honoring arbitrary gradInput strides would mean

issues.title: [skip-added] test_regional_fallback_by_default_invoke_subgraph_xpu on XPU (dill 0.3.7 by-value pickling)
issues.body:
Auto-added by `fix-implement` (`allow_skip=true`) while handling the DISABLED test tracked by `pytorch/pytorch#195876`.

**Test:** `test/inductor/test_compile_subprocess.py::GPUTests::test_regional_fallback_by_default_invoke_subgraph_xpu`

**Original failure:** `torch._inductor.exc.InductorError: TypeError: cannot pickle '_thread._local' object`

**Root cause (device independent).** `test_compile_subprocess.py` re-runs `CommonTemplate` with `fx_compile_mode = SUBPROCESS`, so each graph goes through `GraphPickler` (`torch/fx/_graph_pickler.py`), which uses `dill` instead of the stdlib pickler when `dill` is importable. dill's `_locate_function` resolves a dotted module name by importing the parent package and doing `getattr(parent, last_component)`; for `torch._higher_order_ops.invoke_subgraph` that returns the `InvokeSubgraphHOP` instance re-exported by `torch/_higher_order_ops/__init__.py`, not the submodule. Every function and class defined in `invoke_subgraph.py` therefore looks unresolvable, dill pickles them by value, and walking their `__globals__` reaches a `_thread._local`.

This test is the only `CommonTemplate` case that calls `get_invoke_subgraph_compile_options()`, which hangs `functools.partial` compiler callables off `NestedCompileRegionOptions`, so it is the only one that trips the path.

**Reason for skip.** The same test is already declared `TestFailure(("cpu", "cuda"), is_skip=True)` in that file for exactly this reason; `xpu` was left out of the tuple, which is why XPU CI was the only configuration still running it. The patch just adds `"xpu"` to the existing tuple.

**Real fix is upstream and needs a maintainer decision.** The test passes unmodified under `dill==0.4.1` (newer dill honours `byref` for functions, not only classes); pytorch CI pins `dill==0.3.7` in `.ci/docker/requirements-ci.txt`. Either bumping that pin (rebuilds every CI image, and also changes the other four `is_skip` entries in the same dict) or teaching `GraphPickler` to force by-reference function saving (changes fx-graph serialization for every backend) would be a real fix. No XPU-side work is involved.

**Base analyzed:** pytorch@8224fee7

issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

```
import torch

DEVICE = "xpu"   # "cpu" -> OK, "xpu" -> ValueError
B, H, S, D = 2, 2, 7, 16
HID = H * D


class Attention(torch.nn.Module):
    def __init__(self):
        super().__init__()
        self.q_proj = torch.nn.Linear(HID, HID, bias=False)
        self.k_proj = torch.nn.Linear(HID, HID, bias=False)
        self.v_proj = torch.nn.Linear(HID, HID, bias=False)

    def forward(self, x, mask):
        q = self.q_proj(x).view(B, S, H, D).transpose(1, 2)
        k = self.k_proj(x).view(B, S, H, D).transpose(1, 2)
        v = self.v_proj(x).view(B, S, H, D).transpose(1, 2)
        attn = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, attn_mask=mask)
        attn = attn.transpose(1, 2).contiguous()
        return attn.reshape(B, S, -1)


model = Attention().eval().to(DEVICE)
inputs = {
    "x": torch.randn(B, S, HID, device=DEVICE),
    "mask": torch.zeros(B, 1, S, S, device=DEVICE).expand(B, H, S, S),
}
ep = torch.export.export(model, (), dict(inputs), strict=False)
torch.onnx.export(ep, args=(), kwargs=dict(inputs), dynamo=True, optimize=False)
```

nodes.body:
On XPU, SDPA backend selection depends on GradMode, and different backends produce different output memory layouts.

- requires_grad=False -> _fused_sdp_choice = 4 (overrideable aka oneDNN) -> alloc_with_matching_layout(query, ...) (Attention.cpp:336)	(224, 16, 32, 1) — follows query's layout
- requires_grad=True  -> _fused_sdp_choice = 0 (math) -> allocates its own buffer	(224, 112, 16, 1) — plain contiguous

The ONNX exporter evaluates the meta of the same SDPA node three times, and the grad context flips twice:
| # | Stage | Grad | Backend | SDPA output stride |
|---|-------|------|---------|--------------------|
| 1 | `torch.export.export` (pre-dispatch)          | on  | math         | `(224, 112, 16, 1)` |
| 2 | `run_decompositions()` (re-traced below autograd) | off | overrideable | `(224, 16, 32, 1)`  |
| 3 | `InsertTypePromotion` fake-tensor re-propagation   | on  | math         | `(224, 112, 16, 1)` |

Hence, the rootcause is that ONNX sometime run with grad mode and sometime run with no-grad mode.  PT XPU doesn't enable overrideable backward yet so that grad mode will choose math backend. Different backends have different layout and then throw error.

[地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#162454] will enable SDPA overrideable backend and this issue will be fixed.

issues.title: test_update_user_managed_buffer_xpu fails: constant-buffer allocation not reflected by XPU memory query
issues.body:
## Description
`test_update_user_managed_buffer` fails on XPU for both
`AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu` and `AOTInductorTestDualWrapper`. The test
allocates an owned constant buffer via `runner.update_constant_buffer(...)` and
asserts that memory usage increased (`mem_after > mem_before`). On XPU the two
measured values are identical, so the assertion fails.

## Failing tests
- `test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu::test_update_user_managed_buffer_xpu`
- `test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestDualWrapper::test_update_user_managed_buffer_xpu`

## Error
```
File "test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py", line 8622, in test_update_user_managed_buffer
    self.assertGreater(mem_after, mem_before)
AssertionError: -68702699520 not greater than -68702699520
```

## Analysis
The memory probe differs by device (test_aot_inductor.py:8601-8605):
```python
def constant_buffer_memory_used():
    if self.device == "cuda":
        return torch.cuda.memory_allocated(self.device)
    free_memory, _ = getattr(torch, GPU_TYPE).mem_get_info(self.device)
    return -free_memory
```
On XPU, `mem_get_info` free memory is unchanged across the constant-buffer
allocation (`update_constant_buffer(new_weights, True, False, False)`), so
`mem_after == mem_before`. Note the CUDA path also sets
`aot_inductor.weight_use_caching_allocator=True` (line 8590-8591), which is not
applied for XPU. The XPU memory query is likely too coarse to observe the
allocation, or the allocation path is not tracked by `mem_get_info`.

## Repro
```
python test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu.test_update_user_managed_buffer_xpu
```

## Environment
- pytorch: fc5530887482e83d171231ad1f7c1dd6498da99e
- torch-xpu-ops: 562950cc554685d4e7461d6277d71306d1e468eb
- Platform: Linux

@daisyden  I couldn't reproduce this on a bare-metal Max 1550 (same driver, 1.6.33578). I ran the full `test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py` the way CI does (`run_ut.sh` `PYTEST_ADDOPTS`, one tile per worker via `ZE_AFFINITY_MASK`, `numactl` pinning), without any test changes. Both `test_update_user_managed_buffer_xpu` variants passed. I logged `torch.xpu.mem_get_info()` after every test, and it never reported free == total.

`-68702699520` is exactly the total memory of one tile. On PVC-817255, `mem_get_info` returns free == total both before and after the 64 MB allocation, which means no real free-memory data comes back. The same numbers appear in every failing run I found (30987352138, 31362886717, 35871429007), so I suspect the CI environment rather than AOTI.

Automated fix session for intel/torch-xpu-ops#5484. Runner: `xpu-agent-pvc` (PVC, 8x Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100). Re-run requested with `--on pvc` after the previous BMG run. **Outcome:** IMPLEMENTING(fix_verified) -- fix committed on `agent/fix-issue-5484` in the `pytorch` checkout; patch exported as a workflow artifact.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | pytorch | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Human feedback since the last run (`fix --on pvc`) is treated as the primary input: the previous session ran on BMG and could not reproduce, so this run re-examines the failure on a PVC host. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Run on `xpu-agent-pvc` (PVC, Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100, 48 GB) against the latest XPU nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261020+xpu`, with the `pytorch` test tree at `origin/main` (`ed1fcb4b`). | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu::test_update_user_managed_buffer_xpu` | NOT_REPRODUCED as-is | `OK` (104s) | | same, with the driver free-memory query returning `free == total` | REPRODUCED | `AssertionError: -51522830336 not greater than -51522830336` | This host's `torch.xpu.mem_get_info` reports real free memory and tracks allocations (`delta == 67108864` for a 64 MB allocation), so the test passes here just as it did on BMG. Forcing the probe to see `free == total` -- what the maintainer comment above reports for the CI host PVC-817255 -- reproduces the reported assertion exactly, with this card's total (48 GB) in place of the Max 1550 tile's 64 GB. The run also pinned down why the XPU probe has to use that fragile query at all. Switching the test to the CUDA-style probe (`aot_inductor.weight_use_caching_allocator=True` plus `torch.xpu.memory_allocated`) on the unmodified nightly fails: ``` AssertionError: 268484608 not greater than 268484608 ``` The allocation is invisible to the XPU caching allocator because the config is silently ignored on XPU, which is the actual product bug behind this test failure. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Target repo | pytorch | | Domain | inductor / AOTInductor runtime, XPU memory | | Analyzed sha | `ed1fcb4b699c215ddb7b59184d4d9d578f96f12e` | | Verdict | IMPLEMENTING | **1. `aot_inductor.weight_use_caching_allocator` is silently ignored on XPU.** `RAII_gpuMalloc` in `torch/csrc/inductor/aoti_runtime/model_base.h` honours the `AOT_INDUCTOR_USE_CACHING_ALLOCATOR` macro only in its `USE_CUDA` branch. The `USE_XPU` branch unconditionally calls `sycl::malloc_device`, and there is no `aoti_torch_xpu_caching_allocator_raw_*` entry in the XPU shim to call. The inductor config itself is device-agnostic (`get_caching_allocator_macro` in `torch/_inductor/cpp_builder.py` always emits the macro), so on XPU the macro is defined and then has no effect: AOTI constant buffers always come from raw USM device memory, outside the PyTorch XPU caching allocator and therefore invisible to `torch.xpu.memory_allocated`. **2. That forces the test onto a host-dependent probe.** Because the allocator probe cannot work on XPU, `test_update_user_managed_buffer` falls back to `-torch.xpu.mem_get_info(...)[0]`, i.e. the driver free-memory query (`sycl::ext::intel::info::device::free_memory`, read by `XPUAllocator::getMemoryInfo` in `c10/xpu/XPUCachingAllocator.h`). Whether that query returns anything useful is a property of the host: on the CI host PVC-817255 it returns `free == total` regardless of what is allocated, so `mem_before == mem_after` and `assertGreater` fails; on BMG and on this Max 1100 runner it reports real free memory and the test passes. So the assertion failure is a true XPU gap in the AOTInductor runtime surfacing through a probe that happens to work on most hosts. Reproduce
Run on xpu-agent-pvc (PVC, Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100, 48 GB) against the
latest XPU nightly wheel 2.16.0.dev20261020+xpu, with the pytorch test tree
at origin/main (ed1fcb4b).



Test case
Verdict
Observed




AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu::test_update_user_managed_buffer_xpu
NOT_REPRODUCED as-is
OK (104s)


same, with the driver free-memory query returning free == total
REPRODUCED
AssertionError: -51522830336 not greater than -51522830336



This host's torch.xpu.mem_get_info reports real free memory and tracks
allocations (delta == 67108864 for a 64 MB allocation), so the test passes
here just as it did on BMG. Forcing the probe to see free == total -- what
the maintainer comment above reports for the CI host PVC-817255 -- reproduces
the reported assertion exactly, with this card's total (48 GB) in place of the
Max 1550 tile's 64 GB.
The run also pinned down why the XPU probe has to use that fragile query at
all. Switching the test to the CUDA-style probe
(aot_inductor.weight_use_caching_allocator=True plus
torch.xpu.memory_allocated) on the unmodified nightly fails:
AssertionError: 268484608 not greater than 268484608

The allocation is invisible to the XPU caching allocator because the config is
silently ignored on XPU, which is the actual product bug behind this test
failure.
Automated by fix-reproduce.



Root Cause



Field
Value




Target repo
pytorch


Domain
inductor / AOTInductor runtime, XPU memory


Analyzed sha
ed1fcb4b699c215ddb7b59184d4d9d578f96f12e


Verdict
IMPLEMENTING



1. aot_inductor.weight_use_caching_allocator is silently ignored on XPU.
RAII_gpuMalloc in torch/csrc/inductor/aoti_runtime/model_base.h honours the
AOT_INDUCTOR_USE_CACHING_ALLOCATOR macro only in its USE_CUDA branch. The
USE_XPU branch unconditionally calls sycl::malloc_device, and there is no
aoti_torch_xpu_caching_allocator_raw_* entry in the XPU shim to call. The
inductor config itself is device-agnostic (get_caching_allocator_macro in
torch/_inductor/cpp_builder.py always emits the macro), so on XPU the macro is
defined and then has no effect: AOTI constant buffers always come from raw USM
device memory, outside the PyTorch XPU caching allocator and therefore invisible
to torch.xpu.memory_allocated.
2. That forces the test onto a host-dependent probe. Because the allocator
probe cannot work on XPU, test_update_user_managed_buffer falls back to
-torch.xpu.mem_get_info(...)[0], i.e. the driver free-memory query
(sycl::ext::intel::info::device::free_memory, read by XPUAllocator::getMemoryInfo
in c10/xpu/XPUCachingAllocator.h). Whether that query returns anything useful
is a property of the host: on the CI host PVC-817255 it returns free == total
regardless of what is allocated, so mem_before == mem_after and
assertGreater fails; on BMG and on this Max 1100 runner it reports real
free memory and the test passes.
So the assertion failure is a true XPU gap in the AOTInductor runtime surfacing
through a probe that happens to work on most hosts. Fixing the gap also removes
the dependency on the unreliable query.
Fix strategy. Add aoti_torch_xpu_caching_allocator_raw_alloc /
_raw_delete to the XPU shim, honour AOT_INDUCTOR_USE_CACHING_ALLOCATOR in
the USE_XPU branch of RAII_gpuMalloc, and then let the test enable the
config and use memory_allocated for both CUDA and XPU.
Automated by fix-root-cause.

XPU caching allocator. That is the FAIL this run fixes.
Automated by fix-reproduce.



Root Cause



Field
Value




Target repo
pytorch


Domain
inductor / AOTInductor runtime, XPU memory


Analyzed sha
807c4660609ba5ae290125608309e228659a4626


Verdict
IMPLEMENTING



Re-confirmed against today's origin/main; unchanged from the previous
session's analysis, which the maintainer review accepted.
1. aot_inductor.weight_use_caching_allocator is silently ignored on XPU.
get_caching_allocator_macro in torch/_inductor/cpp_builder.py emits
AOT_INDUCTOR_USE_CACHING_ALLOCATOR for every device, but RAII_gpuMalloc in
torch/csrc/inductor/aoti_runtime/model_base.h only honours that macro in its
USE_CUDA branch (lines 1090-1118). The USE_XPU branch (lines 1120-1129)
unconditionally calls sycl::malloc_device, and the XPU shim has no
aoti_torch_xpu_caching_allocator_raw_* entry point to call in the first place
(CUDA's lives in shim_cuda.cpp:85). So on XPU the macro is defined and then
does nothing: AOTI constant buffers always come from raw USM device memory,
outside the PyTorch XPU caching allocator and therefore invisible to
torch.xpu.memory_allocated / torch.accelerator.memory_allocated.
2. That is what forces the test onto a host-dependent probe. Because the
allocator probe cannot work on XPU, test_update_user_managed_buffer falls back
to -torch.xpu.mem_get_info(...)[0], the driver free-memory query
(sycl::ext::intel::info::device::free_memory, read by
XPUAllocator::getMemoryInfo). Whether that query returns anything useful is a
property of the host: on the CI host PVC-817255 it returns free == total
regardless of what is allocated, so mem_before == mem_after and
assertGreater fails; on this BMG runner and on the previous session's Max 1100
it reports real free memory and the test passes.
So the assertion failure is a real XPU gap in the AOTInductor runtime, surfacing
through a probe that happens to work on most hosts. Closing the gap also removes
the dependency on the unreliable query.
Fix strategy. Add aoti_torch_xpu_caching_allocator_raw_alloc / _raw_delete
to the XPU shim backed by c10::xpu::XPUCachingAllocator, honour
AOT_INDUCTOR_USE_CACHING_ALLOCATOR in the USE_XPU branch of RAII_gpuMalloc,
and let the test enable the config on every GPU and measure with
torch.accelerator.memory_allocated. The config's doc comment stops naming CUDA
only. This is the shape pytorch/pytorch#201813 was approved in, including the
two review changes requested there (torch.accelerator.memory_allocated instead
of a per-device getattr, and the config.py comment).
Automated by fix-root-cause.

Summary
The AOTInductor runtime ignores aot_inductor.weight_use_caching_allocator on
XPU -- RAII_gpuMalloc honours AOT_INDUCTOR_USE_CACHING_ALLOCATOR only in its
CUDA branch and the XPU shim had no caching-allocator entry point -- so AOTI
constant buffers always come from raw sycl::malloc_device and never appear in
memory_allocated, which is why test_update_user_managed_buffer had to fall
back to the driver free-memory query and fails on a host where that query reports
free == total. This run re-derived the fix in the shape the upstream reviewers
settled on: the XPU shim gains
aoti_torch_xpu_caching_allocator_raw_alloc / _raw_delete backed by
c10::xpu::XPUCachingAllocator, the XPU branch of RAII_gpuMalloc uses them,
the test enables the config on every GPU and measures with
torch.accelerator.memory_allocated, and the config's doc comment stops naming
CUDA only. On a BMG source build both test variants pass, the probe sees exactly
the 67125248 bytes of the owned constant buffer with the config on and 0 with it
off, and 42 related AOTI constant/weight tests still pass on the unchanged
default path.
Two things for the reviewer. This work is already upstream and approved as
pytorch/pytorch#201813 (green CI, not yet merged); this patch is that same
change re-derived and re-verified on BMG, so the useful action is to land the
upstream PR rather than to apply this artifact. And the reported failure is
host-specific -- the Arc Pro B60 here, like the previous session's Max 1100,
reports real free memory -- so the FAIL -> PASS evidence is the allocator probe
plus the config-on/config-off delta on one build; the underlying mem_get_info
breakage on PVC-817255 is untouched by this change and stays tracked as
#5846.

This UT failure could not be reproduced even with  CI Docker image. The failure occurred because Inductor decided not to fuse the kernels, causing the generated kernel count to increase from the expected 6 to 9. According to `speedup_by_combo_kernel`, fusion is rejected only when both the fused and unfused execution times are ≥ 0.3 ms, and the fused execution time is greater than or equal to the unfused execution time. However, the measured execution times on PVC Max 1550 are well below 0.3 ms, so fusion should normally be selected. This UT failure may have been caused by occasional benchmark timing fluctuations.

issues.title: [upstream_ut] XPU backward kernels missing input-validation error checks (replication_pad2d, grid_sample)
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Running upstream `test/test_nn.py` on XPU, two "error-checking" cases fail because
the XPU backward kernels do not raise the validation error that CPU/CUDA raise.
Both PASS on CPU.

**test_Pad_backward_channel_mismatch_xpu** (test/test_nn.py:8791)
```
with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, "grad_output channel unexpected"):
AssertionError: RuntimeError not raised
```
The XPU `replication_pad2d_backward` kernel lacks the channel-dim bounds check that
CPU/CUDA got from pytorch/pytorch#189463; it silently returns a wrong-shaped result.
Related: #4565.

**test_grid_sample_backward_error_checking_xpu** (test/test_nn.py:7132)
```
with self.assertRaisesRegex(ValueError, "expected grad_output to have sizes"):
AssertionError: ValueError not raised
```
The XPU `grid_sampler` backward does not validate grad_output sizes.

Note: neither case is caught by torch-xpu-ops CI because the vendored
`test/xpu/test_nn_xpu.py` is a stale copy that does not contain these cases.

### Versions
main

Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | batch-bug (heterogeneous) | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | torch-xpu-ops | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Sub-items handled by this run: 1. `test_Pad_backward_channel_mismatch_xpu` (`test/test_nn.py`) -- XPU `replication_pad2d_backward` missing the channel-dim bounds check. 2. `test_grid_sample_backward_error_checking_xpu` (`test/test_nn.py`) -- XPU `grid_sampler` backward missing grad_output size validation. The two sub-items sit in unrelated kernels, so each takes its own fix branch; neither is expected to cover the other. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Checked against the latest nightly wheel `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu` on BMG (`Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics`), driving the two `aten` backward ops directly, exactly as the upstream tests do. | Sub-item | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | 1. `test_Pad_backward_channel_mismatch_xpu` | REPRODUCED | three of the six pad backward ops disagree with CPU/CUDA -- see breakdown below | | 2. `test_grid_sample_backward_error_checking_xpu` | NOT_REPRODUCED | both `grid_sampler_2d_backward` and `grid_sampler_3d_backward` already raise `ValueError: grid_sampler(): expected grad_output to have sizes ...` | Sub-item 1 breakdown. The test asserts every `{reflection,replication}_pad{1,2,3}d_backward` raises `RuntimeError, "grad_output channel unexpected"`: | Op | Result | |---|---| | `reflection_pad1d_backward` | ok -- `grad_output channel unexpected. Expected: 2, Got: 0` | | `reflection_pad2d_backward` | **no error raised at all** | | `reflection_pad3d_backward` | ok | | `replication_pad1d_backward` | ok | | `replication_pad2d_backward` | **wrong message** -- `gradOutput channel unexpected` (camelCase, regex does not match) | | `replication_pad3d_backward` | **wrong message** -- `grad_output width unexpected` (mislabeled; it is the channel check) | The missing `reflection_pad2d_backward` check is not merely cosmetic: running it leaves the device wedged, and the *next* XPU kernel launch in the same process fails with `UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES` -- i.e. the out-of-bounds read the check is meant to prevent. Sub-item 2 was fixed after this issue was filed, by intel/torch-xpu-ops#5584, which added `check_grid_sampler_{2d,3d}_backward` to the XPU kernels. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at `torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c`, pytorch `a183c26b` (the sha the `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu` wheel was built from). Upstream splits the pad backward ops into two groups. `reflection_pad{1,3}d_backward` and `replication_pad1d_backward` are **structured**, so their `TORCH_META_FUNC` runs `at::native::padding::pad_backward_shape_check` for every backend -- XPU included, for free. `reflection_pad2d_backward`, `replication_pad2d_backward` and `replication_pad3d_backward` are **not** structured: each backend's own function has to call that helper itself. CPU does so in `aten/src/ATen/native/ReflectionPad.cpp:84` and `aten/src/ATen/native/ReplicationPadding.cpp:68,84`; CUDA does so in `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/ReflectionPad.cu:601` and `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/ReplicationPadding.cu:241,296`. XPU is exactly the backend that never adopted the shared helper, and hand-rolls its own checks instead -- which is why all three of its non-structured backward ops disagree with CPU/CUDA, and the three structured ones agree: - `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ReflectionPadKernels.cpp:819-832` validates only `grad_output`'s width and height. With no channel check, a `grad_output` of `(2, 0, 6, 8)` against an input of `(2, 2, 4, 4)` passes, a non-empty `grad_input` is allocated from the *input* shape, and the kernel then indexes `grad_output` with the input's channel counter -- the out-of-bounds read that wedges the device (`UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES` on the next launch). This is the segfault `pytorch/pytorch#142834` described. - `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ReplicationPaddingKernels.cpp:555-560` does have a channel check (added by intel/torch-xpu-ops#4758) but spells the message `gradOutput channel unexpected`, while every other backend and the meta kernel say `grad_output channel unexpected`. - `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ReplicationPaddingKernels.cpp:694-699` checks the channel dim but labels the message `grad_output width unexpected` -- a copy-paste slip, so the text names the wrong dimension. So the fix is the one upstream already settled on: delete the hand-rolled, drift-prone copies in those three XPU functions and call `at::native::padding::pad_backward_shape_check(grad_output, input, padding, dim)`, the same single source of truth CPU, CUDA and `_meta_registrations.py` share. That closes the missing check, corrects both messages, and stops the messages from drifting again. Sub-item 2 needs no change: intel/torch-xpu-ops#5584 already wired `check_grid_sampler_{2d,3d}_backward` into `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/GridSampler.cpp:686,1831`. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- missing/incorrect use of a shared ATen validation helper in three XPU kernels. - **Target repo:** torch-xpu-ops - **Domain:** xpu-kernel *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result ```diff --- a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ReflectionPadKernels.cpp +++ b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ReflectionPadKernels.cpp @@ -813,23 +813,8 @@ void reflection_pad2d_backward_kernel( int64_t input_h = input.size(dim_h); int64_t input_w = input.size(dim_w); - int64_t output_h = input_h + pad_t + pad_b; - int64_t output_w = input_w + pad_l + pad_r; - - TORCH_CHECK( - output_w == grad_output_.size(dim_w), - "grad_output width " - "unexpected. Expected: ", - output_w, - ", Got: ", - grad_output_.size(dim_w)); - TORCH_CHECK( - output_h == grad_output_.size(dim_h), - "grad_output height " - "unexpected. Expected: ", - output_h, - ", Got: ", - grad_output_.size(dim_h)); + at::native::padding::pad_backward_shape_check( + grad_output_, input, padding, /*dim=*/2); Tensor grad_output = grad_output_.contiguous(); --- a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ReplicationPaddingKernels.cpp +++ b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ReplicationPaddingKernels.cpp @@ -19,6 +19,7 @@ DISABLE_RETURN_TYPE_WARNING_BEGIN #include +#include #include @@ -526,51 +527,12 @@ void replication_pad2d_backward_kernel( TORCH_CHECK(padding.size() == 4, "padding Size is expected to be 4"); + at::native::padding::pad_backward_shape_check( + grad_output, input, padding, /*dim=*/2); + const auto padL = padding[0]; - const auto padR = padding[1]; const auto padT = padding[2]; - const auto padB = padding[3]; - ... 40 lines of hand-rolled channel/width/height checks removed ... - TORCH_CHECK( - ichannel == grad_output.size(dimc), - "gradOutput channel unexpected. Expected: ", + const int numInputDims = input.dim(); @@ -632,12 +594,7 @@ static inline void shapeAndGradOutputCheck3d( - int64_t pad_left, - int64_t pad_right, - int64_t pad_top, - int64_t pad_bottom, - int64_t pad_front, - int64_t pad_back) { + IntArrayRef padding) { @@ -689,30 +643,8 @@ static inline void shapeAndGradOutputCheck3d( - TORCH_CHECK( - num_planes == grad_output.size(plane_dim), - "grad_output width unexpected. Expected: ", - ... width / height / depth checks removed ... + at::native::padding::pad_backward_shape_check( + grad_output, input, padding, /*dim=*/3); } ``` `test/regressions/test_replication_pad_channel_mismatch.py` asserted the old `gradOutput channel unexpected` text, so it moves to the shared message and is widened from replication 2d only to all six `{reflection,replication}_pad{1,2,3}d_backward` ops, mirroring the upstream test. Three files changed, 56 insertions, 124 deletions. `lintrunner` reports no issues. *Automated by fix-implement.*
Verify Source build: pytorch `a183c26b` (the sha the `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu` nightly was built from) with `third_party/xpu.txt` pinned to the fix branch, `TORCH_XPU_ARCH_LIST=bmg,pvc`, on Intel Arc Pro B60 (BMG). Upstream `test/test_nn.py` calls `instantiate_device_type_tests(TestNNDeviceType, globals(), allow_mps=True)` -- no `allow_xpu=True` -- so the `_xpu` variants of these two cases do not exist in the upstream file as checked out. The XPU variants were generated with a wrapper that imports `TestNNDeviceType` under `XPUPatchForImport` and re-instantiates it `only_for="xpu"`, i.e. exactly what the vendored `test/xpu/test_nn_xpu.py` does, so the node ids match the ones the issue reports. Per-op before/after on the one failing sub-item (each row run in its own process, since the pre-fix out-of-bounds read wedges the device for the rest of the process): | Op | Before | After | |---|---|---| | `reflection_pad1d_backward` | pass | pass | | `reflection_pad2d_backward` | **fail** -- no error raised | pass | | `reflection_pad3d_backward` | pass | pass | | `replication_pad1d_backward` | pass | pass | | `replication_pad2d_backward` | **fail** -- `gradOutput channel unexpected` | pass | | `replication_pad3d_backward` | **fail** -- `grad_output width unexpected` | pass | | Test | Result | |---|---| | `TestNNDeviceTypeXPU::test_Pad_backward_channel_mismatch_xpu` | PASSED | | `TestNNDeviceTypeXPU::test_grid_sample_backward_error_checking_xpu` | PASSED | | `test/regressions/test_replication_pad_channel_mismatch.py` | 8 passed | Regression sweep over everything that goes through the touched validation paths -- no failures: | Suite | Result | |---|---| | upstream `test_nn.py -k "Pad or pad"` (XPU) | 80 passed, 5 skipped | | `test/xpu/test_nn_xpu.py -k "Pad or pad"` | 174 passed, 10 skipped | | `test/xpu/test_ops_xpu.py` (replication/reflection/functional pad) | 122 passed | | `test/xpu/test_ops_gradients_xpu.py` (same ops) | 20 passed, 30 skipped | `lintrunner -m 73a6552c` reports no issues, so there was nothing for a lint pass to amend. - **Verdict:** PASSED *Automated by fix-verify.*

Both sub-items trace to one thing: XPU is the only backend that never adopted ATen's shared `padding::pad_backward_shape_check`. Sub-item 2 was fixed after this issue was filed, by #5584, which added check_grid_sampler_{2d,3d}_backward to the XPU kernels.
Automated by fix-reproduce.



Root Cause
Analyzed at torch-xpu-ops@73a6552c, pytorch a183c26b (the sha the 2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu wheel was built from).
Upstream splits the pad backward ops into two groups. reflection_pad{1,3}d_backward and replication_pad1d_backward are structured, so their TORCH_META_FUNC runs at::native::padding::pad_backward_shape_check for every backend -- XPU included, for free. reflection_pad2d_backward, replication_pad2d_backward and replication_pad3d_backward are not structured: each backend's own function has to call that helper itself. CPU does so in aten/src/ATen/native/ReflectionPad.cpp:84 and aten/src/ATen/native/ReplicationPadding.cpp:68,84; CUDA does so in aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/ReflectionPad.cu:601 and aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/ReplicationPadding.cu:241,296. XPU is exactly the backend that never adopted the shared helper, and hand-rolls its own checks instead -- which is why all three of its non-structured backward ops disagree with CPU/CUDA, and the three structured ones agree:

src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ReflectionPadKernels.cpp:819-832 validates only grad_output's width and height. With no channel check, a grad_output of (2, 0, 6, 8) against an input of (2, 2, 4, 4) passes, a non-empty grad_input is allocated from the input shape, and the kernel then indexes grad_output with the input's channel counter -- the out-of-bounds read that wedges the device (UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES on the next launch). This is the segfault pytorch/pytorch#142834 described.
src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ReplicationPaddingKernels.cpp:555-560 does have a channel check (added by #4758) but spells the message gradOutput channel unexpected, while every other backend and the meta kernel say grad_output channel unexpected.
src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ReplicationPaddingKernels.cpp:694-699 checks the channel dim but labels the message grad_output width unexpected -- a copy-paste slip, so the text names the wrong dimension.

So the fix is the one upstream already settled on: delete the hand-rolled, drift-prone copies in those three XPU functions and call at::native::padding::pad_backward_shape_check(grad_output, input, padding, dim), the same single source of truth CPU, CUDA and _meta_registrations.py share. That closes the missing check, corrects both messages, and stops the messages from drifting again.
Sub-item 2 needs no change: #5584 already wired check_grid_sampler_{2d,3d}_backward into src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/GridSampler.cpp:686,1831.

Verdict: IMPLEMENTING -- missing/incorrect use of a shared ATen validation helper in three XPU kernels.
Target repo: torch-xpu-ops
Domain: xpu-kernel

Automated by fix-root-cause.

issues.title: FlopCounterMode reports 0 FLOPs for SDPA on XPU (`_scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable` has no flop formula)
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Bug Description

`torch.utils.flop_counter.FlopCounterMode` reports **0 FLOPs** for every `scaled_dot_product_attention` call on XPU. The same call on CPU is counted correctly. This affects any XPU user of the flop counter, not just tests.

This blocks enabling `test_flop_counter.py::TestFlopCounterDeviceXPU::test_sdpa_gqa_xpu` on XPU (see pytorch/pytorch#197249), which asserts `gqa_flops > 0` and fails with `AssertionError: False is not true`.

## Affected Tests

```
op_ut,test/test_flop_counter.py,TestFlopCounterDeviceXPU.test_sdpa_gqa_xpu
```
Note: Test will be enabled in [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#197249]

## Reproducer

```python
import torch, torch.nn.functional as F
from torch.utils.flop_counter import FlopCounterMode

q = torch.randn(2, 32, 128, 64, device="xpu", dtype=torch.float16)
k = torch.randn(2, 8, 128, 64, device="xpu", dtype=torch.float16)
v = torch.randn(2, 8, 128, 64, device="xpu", dtype=torch.float16)

with FlopCounterMode(display=False) as mode:
    F.scaled_dot_product_attention(q, k, v, is_causal=True, enable_gqa=True)
print(sum(v for _, v in mode.flop_counts["Global"].items()))
```

## Error Message

```
XPU SDPA flops : 0
CPU SDPA flops : 268435456
```

Expected the XPU count to be non-zero

## Root Cause Analysis

XPU SDPA dispatches to `aten::_scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable` (confirmed with a `TorchDispatchMode` trace). That op is **not registered** in `torch/utils/flop_counter.py`:

```python
>>> torch.ops.aten._scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable in flop_registry
False
```

`register_flop_formula` for `sdpa_flop` covers only the CUDA/CPU variants (`_scaled_dot_product_efficient_attention`, `_scaled_dot_product_flash_attention`, `_scaled_dot_product_flash_attention_for_cpu`, `_scaled_dot_product_cudnn_attention`), and `sdpa_backward_flop` likewise omits the overrideable backward op. Unregistered ops contribute 0, so the total is 0.

## Suggested Fix

Add the overrideable ops to the existing formulas in `torch/utils/flop_counter.py` — the math is backend-independent, so no new formula is needed:

- `aten._scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable` → `sdpa_flop`
- `aten._scaled_dot_product_fused_attention_overrideable_backward` → `sdpa_backward_flop`

Both overloads exist in this build. The fix is upstream in pytorch/pytorch.

## Related Intel/torch-xpu-ops Issues

- #4853 — `Inductor flop counter reports 0 FLOPs on XPU (get_device_tflops has no non-CUDA fallback)`. **Different layer**: #4853 is Inductor's peak-TFLOPS/roofline path; this issue is the dispatch-level `flop_registry`. Fixing one does not fix the other.
- #5444, #5124 — roofline runtime estimates returning 0 on XPU (same layer as #4853)

### Versions

torch 2.15.0a0+gita95d76a
commit 08bdc2a8e0d
Platform: linux, Python 3.12.3
Device: Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1550 (PVC)

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-09-24] XPU linspace/logspace compute the half and bfloat16 step in the output dtype, so results diverge from CPU
issues.body:
## Upstream source - Origin: `pytorch/pytorch@1614f7f277b640ca057b20aa452178eb1f31e898` (PR #198415), "[BE] Compute linspace/logspace step in the opmath type for half and bfloat16", committed `2026-09-24T03:52:29Z`. It changes `aten/src/ATen/native/cpu/RangeFactoriesKernel.cpp` and `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/RangeFactories.cu` only. - Scan window: `[2026-09-24T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-25T00:00:00Z)` on `pytorch/pytorch`, frozen default-branch head `cae30b13eb94e8a7faa09cd832f9cc84f9935e44`. The commit is an ancestor of that head (`compare` reports `behind_by: 0`), so the CPU/CUDA fix has landed. Upstream summary of the defect: for half and bfloat16 the step was rounded to the output dtype before being multiplied by the index, so the rounding compounds across the range. Upstream switched the step (and, for `logspace`, the base and hence the `pow`) to `at::opmath_type`, which promotes exactly half and bfloat16 and leaves float, double and complex bit-identical. ## Observed XPU behavior Running `linspace`/`logspace` in half and bfloat16 on XPU and comparing against the CPU result and against a float64 reference rounded to the output dtype: ```text TARGET-PATH-PROOF float16 logspace: out=xpu:0 dtype=torch.float16 numel=38 OBSERVED float16 logspace: vs float64-rounded reference xpu 26/38 cpu 0/38 | xpu vs cpu 26 | max|err| xpu 1.6958520834906494 cpu 0.19585208349064942 TARGET-PATH-PROOF bfloat16 logspace: out=xpu:0 dtype=torch.bfloat16 numel=38 OBSERVED bfloat16 logspace: vs float64-rounded reference xpu 21/38 cpu 0/38 | xpu vs cpu 21 | max|err| xpu 7.6047930354503706 cpu 1.6958520834906494 OBSERVED commit example linspace(0, 10, 38) half element 3: xpu 0.810546875 cpu 0.810546875 correctly-rounded 0.811035156 unwidened-step 0.810546875 ``` Two distinct observations: 1. **`logspace` is already wrong relative to CPU in the tested build.** CPU `logspace` computed its step and `pow` in double before this commit, so it is exact against the float64 reference (`0/38`). XPU disagrees with CPU on 26 of 38 half elements and 21 of 38 bfloat16 elements, and its maximum absolute error is an order of magnitude larger (`1.696` vs `0.196` in half; `7.605` vs `1.696` in bfloat16). This divergence does not depend on the upstream commit at all. 2. **`linspace` produces the unwidened-step value.** For the commit's own worked example, `linspace(0, 10, 38)` in half, element 3, XPU returns `0.810546875`, which is the unwidened-step value rather than the correctly rounded `0.811035156`. CPU in the tested build returns the same wrong value because the build predates the commit; at the frozen upstream head CPU returns the correctly rounded value, so XPU will diverge from CPU once the fix reaches an XPU build. `linspace(-3, 7, 129)` and bfloat16 `linspace(0, 10, 38)` were bit-identical to CPU, as expected: those ranges have steps that are exactly representable in the output dtype. Raw evidence: `runner/logs/commit-1614f7f277b640ca057b20aa452178eb1f31e898.log` (sha256 `f21a7d72489ec2ca21500fde3db72ec763eaf89bdf2210e161b386b7e3077a80`) from `scripts/repro_commit-1614f7f2.py` (sha256 `c224fe97212035e50f55f077e1be82b95b7e1f88488af37fccc1bb7d40ba9674`), returncode 0, 3.736 s, no timeout. ## Target-path evidence Every compared XPU tensor is reported on `xpu:0` with the expected dtype and `numel`, and the CPU and float64 references are computed separately on CPU, so the comparison is not XPU against itself. The XPU implementation is this repository's own kernel. In `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/RangeFactoriesKernel.cpp`, the non-integral dispatch of both kernels still declares the step in `scalar_t`: ```cpp // linspace_kernel, AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_AND_COMPLEX_TYPES_AND2(kHalf, kBFloat16, ...) scalar_t step = (scalar_end - scalar_start) / static_cast(steps - 1); // logspace_kernel, same dispatch scalar_t scalar_base = static_cast(base); scalar_t step = (scalar_end - scalar_start) / static_cast(steps - 1); ``` This is the pre-commit CUDA code, line for line. `LogspaceFunctor` does cast to `at::opmath_type` for the `sycl::pow` call, but its exponent `scalar_start_ + step_ * ind` is already accumulated in `scalar_t` before that cast, which is why `logspace` is the worse of the two. For contrast, `arange_kernel` and `range_kernel` in the same file already widen via `at::acc_type_device`, so the gap is specific to `linspace_kernel` and `logspace_kernel`. ## Why this is XPU-owned The upstream commit touches only the CPU and CUDA kernels. XPU has its own SYCL kernels in this repository, so nothing upstream can fix them. The change needed here is the direct analogue of the CUDA patch: introduce `using step_t = at::opmath_type` in the half/bfloat16 dispatch of `linspace_kernel` and `logspace_kernel`, compute the step (and `logspace`'s base) in `step_t`, and let `LinspaceFunctor`/`LogspaceFunctor` carry it through their existing `step_type` template parameter. The integral dispatches already use `float`/`double` and should not change; `opmath_type` leaves float, double and complex bit-identical, so only half and bfloat16 outputs move. Searched for prior art and found none: `intel/torch-xpu-ops` has no open or closed issue or PR covering the `linspace`/`logspace` step type (the merged #4331 "Align range factories with shared PyTorch helpers" did not change it, and the current `main` source above is unwidened), and `pytorch/pytorch` has no issue or PR claiming the XPU side of #198415. ## Reproducer

DTYPES = (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16)

print(f"ENV device={torch.xpu.get_device_name(0)}")

    ("linspace", lambda dt, dev: torch.linspace(0, 10, 38, dtype=dt, device=dev),
     lambda dev: torch.linspace(0, 10, 38, dtype=torch.float64, device=dev)),
    ("linspace(-3,7,129)", lambda dt, dev: torch.linspace(-3, 7, 129, dtype=dt, device=dev),
     lambda dev: torch.linspace(-3, 7, 129, dtype=torch.float64, device=dev)),
    ("logspace", lambda dt, dev: torch.logspace(0, 3, 38, dtype=dt, device=dev),
     lambda dev: torch.logspace(0, 3, 38, dtype=torch.float64, device=dev)),
)

for dtype in DTYPES:
    dname = str(dtype).replace("torch.", "")
    for label, make, make_ref in CASES:

        cpu = make(dtype, "cpu")
        ref = make_ref("cpu")

        print(
            f"{dname} {label}: out={xpu.device} "
            f"vs float64-rounded reference xpu {int((xpu_c != want).sum())}/{want.numel()} "
            f"cpu {int((cpu != want).sum())}/{want.numel()} | "
            f"xpu vs cpu {int((xpu_c != cpu).sum())} | "
            f"max|err| xpu {(xpu_c.double() - ref).abs().max().item()!r} "
            f"cpu {(cpu.double() - ref).abs().max().item()!r}"
        )

x = torch.linspace(0, 10, 38, dtype=torch.float16, device="xpu")
cpu_x = torch.linspace(0, 10, 38, dtype=torch.float16)
print(
    f"commit example linspace(0, 10, 38) half element 3: xpu {float(x[3])!r} "
    f"cpu {float(cpu_x[3])!r} correctly-rounded 0.811035156 unwidened-step 0.810546875"
)

1614f7f277b640ca057b20aa452178eb1f31e898 by introducing

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-09-25] XPU layer_norm returns non-zero on a constant input: vectorized WelfordCombine averages partial means instead of using Welford's increment
issues.body:
<!-- alignment-published-unit: issue-198581 -->
## Summary

`F.layer_norm` on an exactly constant input returns a non-zero result on XPU. A constant input has exactly zero variance, so every output element must be exactly zero, and CPU eager does return exactly zero on the same values.

Observed on `Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics`, torch `2.15.0.dev20260925+xpu`, with `eps=1e-5` on `torch.ones(4, width)`:

| dtype | width | XPU max abs | saved mean exactly 1 | CPU max abs |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| float32 | 220 | 5.654593e-05 | no | 0.000000e+00 |
| float32 | 244 | 3.769729e-05 | no | 0.000000e+00 |
| float16 | 220 | 5.656481e-05 | no | 0.000000e+00 |
| float16 | 244 | 3.767014e-05 | no | 0.000000e+00 |
| bfloat16 | 220 | 5.650520e-05 | no | 0.000000e+00 |
| bfloat16 | 244 | 3.767014e-05 | no | 0.000000e+00 |

21 of the 27 (dtype, width) pairs tested were exactly zero; widths 48, 96, 164, 188, 192, 384 and 768 were clean on this device. The saved mean is the culprit: `rstd` behaviour is not implicated, and with `eps=1e-5` the factor `rsqrt(1e-5) = 316.23` amplifies a one-ulp mean error into the values above.

## Upstream source

- `pytorch/pytorch#198581` (OPEN, labels `module: correctness (silent)` and `module: norms and normalization`) reports the same defect for `cuWelfordCombine` in `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/layer_norm_kernel.cu`, measured on gfx950 and gfx942.
- `pytorch/pytorch#198587` proposed the CUDA-side fix but is CLOSED and UNMERGED (no merge timestamp, no merge commit). It was closed by its own author on 2026-09-26T01:42:13Z alongside an unsigned-CLA notice, with green CI and no maintainer review, so the close is not an upstream rejection of the premise.
- That PR touches only `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/layer_norm_kernel.cu` and `test/test_nn.py`, and its own text states that XPU inherits the new bitwise-exactness expectation which the patch neither changes nor verifies. No issue or PR in `pytorch/pytorch` owns the XPU half of the work, and no `intel/torch-xpu-ops` tracker covers it.
- Alignment scan window: `[2026-09-25T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-26T00:00:00Z)`.

## Root cause on XPU

`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LayerNormKernels.cpp:370-393`, `WelfordCombine`:

```cpp
U delta = dataB.mean - dataA.mean;             // line 376
U count = dataA.count + dataB.count;
if (count > decltype(dataB.count){0}) {
  auto coef = sycl::native::recip(count);       // line 380
  auto nA = dataA.count * coef;
  auto nB = dataB.count * coef;
  mean = nA * dataA.mean + nB * dataB.mean;     // line 383
  sigma2 = dataA.sigma2 + dataB.sigma2 + delta * delta * dataA.count * nB;
}
```

Line 383 combines two partial means as a weighted average rather than as Welford's increment. It is exact only when `nA + nB == 1` exactly, which no reciprocal guarantees, correctly rounded or not. The canonical in-tree combine, `WelfordOps::combine` in `aten/src/ATen/native/SharedReduceOps.h`, instead uses `a.mean + delta * nb_over_n`, which cannot move the mean when both partials agree.

The observed failure set points at the formula rather than at `sycl::native::recip` accuracy: widths 220 and 244 are both in the set upstream measured as failing even with a correctly rounded reciprocal (smallest 164, 188, 220, 244), while the `3 * 2^k` widths that dominate the ROCm reports (48, 96, 192, 384, 768) are clean on this device.

## Target-path evidence

- `layer_norm_kernel_impl` (`LayerNormKernels.cpp:686-690`) selects `launch_vectorized_layer_norm_kernel` for float / half / bfloat16 when `N % 4 == 0`, `N <= 2^24`, and the buffers are 16-byte aligned. Every width in the table is a multiple of 4, so the vectorized kernel ran; its `compute_stats` calls `WelfordCombine` at lines 425 (intra-subgroup shuffle) and 450 (inter-subgroup merge).
- The `N % 4 != 0` fallback, `launch_rowwise_moments_kernel`, builds its reduction from `WelfordOps<...>` (`LayerNormKernels.cpp:207`), i.e. the mean-preserving combine. The divergence is therefore confined to the vectorized arm, matching upstream's account of why non-multiple-of-4 widths are clean.
- The reproducer asserts that the output device type is xpu and reads the saved mean through `torch.native_layer_norm`, whose mean is `T_ACC` (float32) for all three input dtypes. It is inexact in all six failing rows.

## Reproducer

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

for dtype in (torch.float32, torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
    for width in (220, 244, 384):
        x = torch.ones(4, width, dtype=dtype, device='xpu')
        out = F.layer_norm(x, (width,), eps=1e-5)
        _, mean, _ = torch.native_layer_norm(x, (width,), None, None, 1e-5)
        cpu = F.layer_norm(x.cpu(), (width,), eps=1e-5)
        print(
            dtype,
            width,
            'xpu_max_abs=%.6e' % out.abs().max().item(),
            'saved_mean_exact=%s' % bool((mean == 1).all().item()),
            'cpu_max_abs=%.6e' % cpu.abs().max().item(),
        )
```

Expected at every width: `xpu_max_abs=0.000000e+00` and `saved_mean_exact=True`. Observed: widths 220 and 244 are non-zero with an inexact saved mean in all three dtypes, while CPU is exactly zero; width 384 is a control that passes on this device.

## Suggested direction

Bring `WelfordCombine` into agreement with `WelfordOps::combine`, keeping `sigma2` as is since it already uses `nB` and is Chan's `M2` term, independent of how the mean is formed:

```cpp
auto nB = dataB.count * coef;
mean = (dataA.count == U(0)) ? dataB.mean : dataA.mean + delta * nB;
sigma2 = dataA.sigma2 + dataB.sigma2 + delta * delta * dataA.count * nB;
```

`delta` is already `dataB.mean - dataA.mean` at line 376, so the increment is based on `dataA`. The select covers the idle-lane merge where `dataA.count == 0` and the weighted form would otherwise rescale `dataB.mean`; the mirrored case needs no guard because `nB` is then exactly zero. On a constant input `delta` is exactly zero, so the mean cannot move however accurate `coef` is. This does change bitwise forward output for non-constant input, as the equivalent upstream change does.

`WelfordOnlineSum` (line 360) also uses `sycl::native::recip`, but it is not implicated for a constant input: `delta` is exactly zero from the second element onward, and the first element divides by a count of exactly 1.

## Evidence limitations

Stated so they are not mistaken for oversights:

- The reproducer's control, a plain `x.mean(dim=-1)` on the same tensor, was itself inexact for float32 at widths 220 and 244, so it does not isolate `layer_norm` for that dtype. For float16 and bfloat16 the control passed, but its result is rounded to the low-precision output dtype while the saved mean is float32, so it is a weak control either way. The CPU-versus-XPU `layer_norm` oracle is unaffected - CPU returned exactly zero in all six failing rows - and neither is the source divergence above. Whether XPU's generic mean reduction is also inexact at these widths is a separate question this scan does not settle.
- Only multiples of 4 were exercised, so the `N % 4 != 0` fallback is clean by source reading rather than by measurement.
- Backward was not exercised on XPU. Upstream reports that `native_layer_norm_backward` consumes the saved `mean` and `rstd` and contains no Welford reduction, so it should inherit the forward fix, but that was not verified here.

## Environment

```
python : /opt/conda/bin/python3.13 (3.13.13)
torch  : 2.15.0.dev20260925+xpu (/opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/__init__.py)
device : Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
```

## Ownership

The affected kernel is `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LayerNormKernels.cpp` in this repository, so the change belongs to `intel/torch-xpu-ops`. It does not depend on `pytorch/pytorch#198587` landing: the weighted-average combine is present in the XPU source independently of that PR, and the defect reproduces in the tested build.

Root Cause
Analyzed at torch-xpu-ops@692ddf7e, pytorch origin/main@1efe96b0.
WelfordCombine (src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LayerNormKernels.cpp:383) merges two partial means as a weighted average, mean = nA * dataA.mean + nB * dataB.mean, where nA/nB come from sycl::native::recip(count) at line 380. That is exact only when nA + nB == 1 exactly, which no reciprocal guarantees. The canonical in-tree combine, WelfordOps::combine in aten/src/ATen/native/SharedReduceOps.h:106-124, instead uses a.mean + delta * nb_over_n, which cannot move the mean when the two partials agree. On a constant input the saved mean therefore comes back one ulp off, and rsqrt(eps) (line 527) scales that into the observed 5.65e-05.
The divergence is confined to the vectorized arm. layer_norm_kernel_impl (lines 724-744) picks launch_vectorized_layer_norm_kernel for float / half / bfloat16 when N % 4 == 0 and the buffers are 16-byte aligned, and compute_stats calls WelfordCombine at lines 425, 453 and 485; the N % 4 != 0 fallback builds its reduction from WelfordOps (line 207), i.e. the mean-preserving form, which is why non-multiple-of-4 widths are clean. The width pattern follows: at N=220 the row is 55 vectors over one 32-lane subgroup, so lanes merge unequal counts (8 and 4) and the weights 2/3/1/3 are inexact, whereas N=384 gives every lane 3 vectors, making both weights exactly 0.5.
Upstream has since taken, and then lost, the identical change on the CUDA side, which matters for review: pytorch/pytorch#198737 (superseding the closed pytorch/pytorch#198587) applied exactly mean = (dataA.count == U(0)) ? dataB.mean : dataA.mean + delta * nB to cuWelfordCombine, was approved and merged on 2026-10-06 (dca0b4b6), and was reverted on 2026-10-08 (5cbf855e) as ghfirst "Diff reverted internally" -- a Meta-internal revert with no public failure cited, and no re-land so far. pytorch/pytorch#198581 is closed as completed by the now-reverted merge, so the upstream bug is in fact still live. The XPU fix is self-contained in this repo and does not depend on that PR, but it does make XPU exact where CUDA currently is not, and -- as the upstream PR stated for its own change -- it alters bitwise forward output for non-constant input. Flagging it so the reviewer can weigh that divergence; the defect itself is unambiguous and reproduces here.

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-09-27] XPU addcmul/addcdiv dispatch on the out= dtype, so a wider out= widens the computation and diverges from CPU and CUDA
issues.body:
## Upstream source - Origin: `pytorch/pytorch@ebc5cc437ec936657e95f35de3084d65a764ac6e` (PR #196924), `[MPS] Migrate addc[mul|div] to Metal`, a default-branch commit inside the scan window. ghstack chain #196924 -> #198743 -> #198753 (the last landed as `4b0647ed`). - Scan window: `[2026-09-27T00:00:00Z, 2026-09-28T00:00:00Z)` on `pytorch/pytorch`, frozen default-branch head `2e9b4aff8d49b22bbebf288ccbf63983c51e45f0`. The commit is reachable from that head. - Upstream defect, quoted from the commit message: the Metal `_cast_` ternary kernels `were instantiated for the output dtype, so an out= wider than the common dtype widened the computation as well. They now compute at the iterator's common dtype and cast on store, like CPU.` The commit notes this is the same cast error that was already fixed for `lerp` and `clamp`. CPU and CUDA were already correct; the commit fixed MPS. XPU has its own ternary kernels in this repository and still has the defect. ## Observed XPU behavior `torch.addcmul` and `torch.addcdiv` with `float16` inputs and a `float32` `out=`, on inputs whose intermediate overflows in half but not in float32: ```text TARGET: addcmul.out inputs=torch.float16 out=torch.float32 in_device=xpu:0 out_device=xpu:0 CHECK addcmul-wide-out: cpu=['inf', '17.0'] xpu=['240001.0', '17.0'] CHECK addcmul-wide-out: FAIL (xpu widened the computation) TARGET: addcdiv.out inputs=torch.float16 out=torch.float32 in_device=xpu:0 out_device=xpu:0 CHECK addcdiv-wide-out: cpu=['inf', '2.75'] xpu=['120001.0', '2.75'] CHECK addcdiv-wide-out: FAIL (xpu widened the computation) TARGET: addcmul value=0 in_device=xpu:0 out_device=xpu:0 dtype=torch.float32 CHECK addcmul-value-zero: cpu=['nan', 'nan', 'nan'] xpu=['nan', 'nan', 'nan'] CHECK addcmul-value-zero: PASS TARGET: addcdiv value=0 in_device=xpu:0 out_device=xpu:0 dtype=torch.float32 CHECK addcdiv-value-zero: cpu=['nan', 'nan', 'nan'] xpu=['nan', 'nan', 'nan'] CHECK addcdiv-value-zero: PASS RESULT: CONFIRMED failed=addcmul-wide-out,addcdiv-wide-out ``` `1 + 60000 * 4` and `1 + 60000 / 0.5` overflow `float16`, so the reference result is `inf`: the TensorIterator common dtype for this call is `float16`, because `compute_common_dtype` skips output operands, and the established semantics are to compute at the common dtype and cast on store. CPU returns `inf`; XPU returns the `float32` values `240001.0` and `120001.0`. XPU therefore returns a silently different number than CPU and CUDA for the same supported call, in both directions of the family (`addcmul.out` and `addcdiv.out`). The second oracle carried by the same chain (#198753: with `value=0`, NaN/Inf in `tensor1` must still propagate) passed on XPU for both ops, so this report is scoped to the `out=` dtype only. Raw evidence: `runner/logs/commit-ebc5cc437ec936657e95f35de3084d65a764ac6e.log` (sha256 `0a4c4502cb14520ce4971caed4c85553a628767c4f56fbf1ba5a7ac29b7cdbac`) produced from `scripts/repro_commit-ebc5cc437ec936657e95f35de3084d65a764ac6e.py` (sha256 `5d40eb5cec83fa4831d5b4c14ec412dbac29c917b6a3186b191c3e3ed7ee34b0`); returncode 0, 3.736 s, no timeout. ## Target-path evidence Every compared XPU tensor is reported on `xpu:0` with its dtype, and the CPU reference is built separately on CPU from the same initialized values, so the comparison is not XPU against itself. The printed `inputs=torch.float16 out=torch.float32` pair is exactly the mixed-dtype `aten::addcmul.out` / `aten::addcdiv.out` call that reaches `at::native::xpu::addcmul_kernel` / `addcdiv_kernel`. `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/PointwiseOpsKernels.cpp` computes the common dtype but then dispatches the real branches on the output dtype: ```cpp void addcmul_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter, const Scalar& value) { // ... auto dtype = iter.common_dtype(); if (iter.is_cpu_scalar(3)) { if (at::isComplexType(dtype)) { // dtype: correct AT_DISPATCH_COMPLEX_TYPES(dtype, "addcmul_xpu", ... } else { AT_DISPATCH_ALL_TYPES_AND2( at::ScalarType::Half, at::ScalarType::BFloat16, iter.dtype(), // output dtype "addcmul_xpu", ... } } else if (at::isComplexType(dtype)) { // dtype: correct // ... } else { AT_DISPATCH_ALL_TYPES_AND_COMPLEX_AND2( at::ScalarType::Half, at::ScalarType::BFloat16, iter.dtype(), // output dtype "addcmul_xpu", ... } } void addcdiv_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter, const Scalar& value) { auto dtype = iter.common_dtype(); if (at::isComplexType(dtype)) { /* dtype: correct */ } else { AT_DISPATCH_ALL_TYPES_AND2( at::ScalarType::Half, at::ScalarType::BFloat16, iter.dtype(), // output dtype "addcdiv_xpu", ... } } ``` `iter.dtype()` is `iter.dtype(0)`, the output operand's current dtype. In `aten/src/ATen/TensorIterator.cpp` at the frozen head, `compute_types` only replaces a mismatched output with a common-dtype temporary when `common_device == kCPU`; on a device iterator the output operand keeps `float32`. So on this call `iter.dtype()` is `float32` while `iter.common_dtype()` is `float16`: `scalar_t` and therefore `at::acc_type_device` are instantiated at `float32`, the functor argument types no longer match the half inputs, and `gpu_kernel_impl` takes its dynamic-casting path (`src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/Loops.h:559`) which converts each half input up on load. The arithmetic runs in `float32` instead of at the iterator's common dtype, which is exactly the observed output. CUDA at the same frozen head dispatches both kernels on the common dtype: ```cpp // aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/PointwiseOpsKernel.cu void addcdiv_cuda_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter, const Scalar& value) { auto dtype = iter.common_dtype(); if (at::isComplexType(dtype)) { /* ... */ } else { AT_DISPATCH_ALL_TYPES_AND2(kHalf, kBFloat16, dtype, "addcdiv_cuda", [&]() { ``` `addcmul_cuda_kernel` is the same, including its CPU-scalar `tensor2` branch. ## Why this is XPU-owned The kernels are in this repository. The upstream commit changed only the MPS Metal kernels, and CPU and CUDA already dispatch on the common dtype, so nothing upstream can correct the XPU dispatch. The fix is to pass the already-computed `dtype` (that is, `iter.common_dtype()`) instead of `iter.dtype()` in the three non-complex `AT_DISPATCH` calls above: both branches of `addcmul_kernel` and the non-complex branch of `addcdiv_kernel`. The complex branches already use `dtype`. Note that no OpInfo sample can cover this, because a `SampleInput` cannot express an `out=` dtype that differs from the inputs (observed upstream in #198795), so a targeted test is needed rather than a new sample. Prior art was searched and none covers this work. In `intel/torch-xpu-ops`: #3275 changed `addcmul` to `sycl::fma` for FMA parity, #3608 fixed the CPU-scalar `tensor2` error, and #5523 is the same class of defect (computing in the output dtype) but in `linspace_kernel`/`logspace_kernel`; no open or closed issue or PR covers the addc{mul,div} `out=` dtype. In `pytorch/pytorch` there is no issue or PR claiming an XPU side of #196924. ## Reproducer
