issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-10-15] [26-10-15] XPU nll_loss2d accumulates fp16 in global atomics: mean cross_entropy returns inf/NaN and all-zero gradients
issues.body:
<!-- alignment-published-unit: issue-201120 -->
## Summary

`F.cross_entropy` with `reduction="mean"` on a spatial (4-D) fp16 input returns `inf`, then `NaN` with an all-zero gradient, once the per-work-group partial sums exceed the fp16 range, even though the true loss is ~3.5. The XPU `nll_loss2d` forward reduces each work group in `acc_type_device<scalar_t, kXPU>` (fp32) but casts the result back to `scalar_t` and accumulates it into fp16 global accumulators, and `output`/`total_weight` are allocated in the input dtype.

Found by an upstream alignment scan of the window `[2026-10-15T00:00:00Z, 2026-10-16T00:00:00Z)`. Upstream source: [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#201120] (reported for CUDA, `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/NLLLoss2d.cu`, open, no fix landed). XPU has its own kernels, so the CUDA fix will not cover XPU.

## Observed XPU behavior

`Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics`, torch `2.16.0.dev20261015+xpu`:

| pixels (HxW) | XPU fp16 loss | fp64 CPU reference | all-zero grad |
|---|---|---|---|
| 128x128 = 16384 | 3.513671875 | 3.5134 | no |
| 181x181 = 32761 | `inf` | 3.5003 | no |
| 256x256 = 65536 | `nan` | 3.5044 | **yes** |

The signature matches the upstream CUDA report exactly: the loss sum overflows to `inf` first, then `total_weight` overflows and `inf/inf` gives `NaN`; the backward divides by the overflowed `total_weight`, so the input gradient is silently all zero. Autocast is unaffected because autocast runs nll_loss in fp32.

## Target-path evidence

The reproducer keeps the tensors on XPU for the whole measured op (`input.device=xpu:0`, `dtype=torch.float16`, `loss.device=xpu:0`, `grad.device=xpu:0`) and compares against an fp64 CPU reference computed from the identical initialized inputs, so only the XPU kernels are measured. The code path is:

- `src/ATen/native/xpu/LossNLL2d.cpp:58-59` - `output` and `total_weight` are allocated with `self.options()`, i.e. fp16.
- `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LossNLL2dKernels.cpp:123-128` - each work group reduces in `accscalar_t` (fp32) and then does `atomicAdd(sycl_global_ptr<scalar_t>(total_weight), static_cast<scalar_t>(acc_weight_reduce))` and the same for `output`, so the cross-work-group accumulation is fp16.
- `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LossNLL2dKernels.cpp:137` - `*output /= *total_weight` in fp16.
- `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LossNLL2dKernels.cpp:324` - backward computes `-(size_average ? *grad_output / *total_weight : *grad_output)`, which is 0 once `total_weight` is `inf`.

## Reproducer

```python
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

torch.manual_seed(0)
C = 21
for H in (128, 181, 256):
    x_cpu = torch.randn(1, C, H, H, dtype=torch.half)
    y_cpu = torch.randint(0, C, (1, H, H))

    x = x_cpu.detach().to("xpu").requires_grad_(True)
    y = y_cpu.to("xpu")

    loss = F.cross_entropy(x, y)
    loss.backward()

    ref = F.cross_entropy(x_cpu.double(), y_cpu).item()
    print(
        f"{H * H} px: loss {loss.item()} (fp64 {ref:.4f}), "
        f"all-zero grad: {bool((x.grad == 0).all())}"
    )
```

Output:

```
16384 px: loss 3.513671875 (fp64 3.5134), all-zero grad: False
32761 px: loss inf (fp64 3.5003), all-zero grad: False
65536 px: loss nan (fp64 3.5044), all-zero grad: True
```

## Environment

```
torch 2.16.0.dev20261015+xpu
python 3.13.13 (/opt/conda/bin/python3.13)
torch path /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/__init__.py
xpu device Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
```

## Ownership

The accumulation and the output allocation are XPU code in this repository (`LossNLL2d.cpp`, `LossNLL2dKernels.cpp`), so the fix is independent XPU work: allocate `output`/`total_weight` in the accumulate type (or accumulate into fp32 scratch) and cast only the final mean back to the input dtype, matching what the upstream issue proposes for `NLLLoss2d.cu`. Summary
F.cross_entropy with reduction="mean" on a spatial (4-D) fp16 input returns inf, then NaN with an all-zero gradient, once the per-work-group partial sums exceed the fp16 range, even though the true loss is ~3.5. The XPU nll_loss2d forward reduces each work group in acc_type_device<scalar_t, kXPU> (fp32) but casts the result back to scalar_t and accumulates it into fp16 global accumulators, and output/total_weight are allocated in the input dtype.
Found by an upstream alignment scan of the window [2026-10-15T00:00:00Z, 2026-10-16T00:00:00Z). Upstream source: pytorch/pytorch#201120 (reported for CUDA, aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/NLLLoss2d.cu, open, no fix landed). XPU has its own kernels, so the CUDA fix will not cover XPU.
Observed XPU behavior
Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics, torch 2.16.0.dev20261015+xpu:



pixels (HxW)
XPU fp16 loss
fp64 CPU reference
all-zero grad




128x128 = 16384
3.513671875
3.5134
no


181x181 = 32761
inf
3.5003
no


256x256 = 65536
nan
3.5044
yes



The signature matches the upstream CUDA report exactly: the loss sum overflows to inf first, then total_weight overflows and inf/inf gives NaN; the backward divides by the overflowed total_weight, so the input gradient is silently all zero. Autocast is unaffected because autocast runs nll_loss in fp32.

The reproducer keeps the tensors on XPU for the whole measured op (input.device=xpu:0, dtype=torch.float16, loss.device=xpu:0, grad.device=xpu:0) and compares against an fp64 CPU reference computed from the identical initialized inputs, so only the XPU kernels are measured. The code path is:

src/ATen/native/xpu/LossNLL2d.cpp:58-59 - output and total_weight are allocated with self.options(), i.e. fp16.
src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/LossNLL2dKernels.cpp:123-128 - each work group reduces in accscalar_t (fp32) and then does atomicAdd(sycl_global_ptr<scalar_t>(total_weight), static_cast<scalar_t>(acc_weight_reduce)) and the same for output, so the cross-work-group accumulation is fp16.

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-10-15] [26-10-15] XPU complex log1p loses the real part near the unit circle: 2.6e-3 relative error where CPU complex64 reaches 4e-8
issues.body:
<!-- alignment-published-unit: pr-201093 -->
## Summary

Complex `torch.log1p` on XPU computes `log(hypot(1 + x, y))` for `|z| >= 0.5`, so the real part `log|1 + z|` cancels catastrophically whenever `1 + z` is close to the unit circle. On `-0.5+0.866j`-style inputs XPU complex64 is off by up to 2.6e-3 relative while CPU complex64 reaches 3.8e-8 on the same input and dtype, i.e. the loss is algorithmic rather than a float32 limit.

Found by an upstream alignment scan of the window `[2026-10-15T00:00:00Z, 2026-10-16T00:00:00Z)`. Upstream source: [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#201093] ([MPS] Fix complex log1p precision, open), which fixes the same signature for MPS only (`UnaryKernel.metal`, `c10/metal/utils.h`).

## Observed XPU behavior

`Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics`, torch `2.16.0.dev20261015+xpu`, complex64, reference in complex128 computed from the same float32-rounded inputs so only kernel error is measured:

| input | XPU real part | reference real part | XPU rel. err | CPU complex64 rel. err |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `-0.5+0.8660311772678856j` | 5.006777e-06 | 4.993587e-06 | **2.6e-3** | 3.8e-08 |
| `-0.5+0.866083136886985j` | 5.006665e-05 | 5.000465e-05 | **1.2e-3** | 1.1e-08 |
| `-0.5+0.8666025617317318j` | 4.997197e-04 | 4.997314e-04 | 2.3e-05 | 5.9e-08 |
| `1e-19+1e-18j` | 9.999999683e-20 | 9.999999683e-20 | 0 | 0 |
| `0.25+0.1j` | 0.226333350 | 0.226333355 | 2.2e-08 | 2.2e-08 |

Small-`|z|` inputs are accurate (they take the `log1p(r)/2` branch), so this is specifically the `|z| >= 0.5` fallback. For scale, upstream's own device-generic `test_log1p_complex` asserts the real part with `atol=0.0, rtol=1e-6`; the inputs above miss that by three orders of magnitude but are not among the values the test currently uses, which is why XPU CI is green today.

## Target-path evidence

The reproducer builds the inputs on CPU and moves them to XPU, and the log shows `input.device=xpu:0`, `out.device=xpu:0`, `dtype=torch.complex64`, so the measured op is the XPU kernel. The path is:

- `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/UnaryLogKernels.cpp:90` - the complex branch of `log1p_kernel` calls `std::log1p` on `c10::complex`, resolving to `c10_complex_math::log1p`.
- `c10/util/complex_math.h` (pytorch/pytorch) - `log1p` is `#if defined(__APPLE__) || defined(__MACOSX) || defined(__CUDACC__) || defined(__HIPCC__) || defined(__SYCL_DEVICE_ONLY__)`; that branch uses the accurate `0.5 * log1p(x * (x + 2) + y * y)` form only when `std::abs(z) < 0.5` and otherwise returns `{log(hypot(x + 1, y)), atan2(y, x + 1)}`.
- The non-device branch of the same header (the numpy-based `log_u * (z / (u - 1))` form) is what CPU uses and what reaches 3.8e-08 above.

`__SYCL_DEVICE_ONLY__` was added to that `#if` by pytorch/pytorch@eb4ea2668 (pytorch/pytorch#174492, "[XPU] Fix numerical instability in logcumsumexp with complex inputs", fixing intel/torch-xpu-ops#2816), which deliberately moved XPU off the CPU formula because that formula produced NaNs for complex64 in `logcumsumexp`. A fix therefore must not simply revert to the CPU branch.

## Reproducer

```python
import torch

near_unit = []
for d in (1e-5, 1e-4, 1e-3):
    near_unit.append(complex(-0.5, (0.75 + d) ** 0.5))

VALUES = [1e-19 + 1e-18j, 1e-10 + 1e-9j, 0.25 + 0.1j] + near_unit
z_cpu = torch.tensor(VALUES, dtype=torch.complex64)
z = z_cpu.to("xpu")

got = torch.log1p(z)
cpu_c64 = torch.log1p(z_cpu)
# reference from the float32-rounded inputs, so only kernel error is measured
ref = torch.log1p(z_cpu.to(torch.complex128))

for i, value in enumerate(VALUES):
    g, c, r = complex(got.cpu()[i]), complex(cpu_c64[i]), complex(ref[i])
    denom = max(abs(r.real), 1e-300)
    print(
        f"log1p({value}) xpu={g} ref={r} "
        f"xpu_real_rel_err={abs(g.real - r.real) / denom:.3g} "
        f"cpu_real_rel_err={abs(c.real - r.real) / denom:.3g}"
    )
```

Relevant output:

```
log1p((-0.5+0.8660311772678856j)) xpu=(5.006777428206988e-06+1.0472004413604736j) ref=(4.993586760599212e-06+1.0472004342356604j) xpu_real_rel_err=0.00264 cpu_real_rel_err=3.78e-08
log1p((-0.5+0.866083136886985j)) xpu=(5.006664650863968e-05+1.0472264289855957j) ref=(5.000464863599523e-05+1.0472264204315511j) xpu_real_rel_err=0.00124 cpu_real_rel_err=1.12e-08
log1p((0.25+0.1j)) xpu=(0.226333349943161+0.07982999086380005j) ref=(0.2263333548909902+0.07982998689674933j) xpu_real_rel_err=2.19e-08 cpu_real_rel_err=2.19e-08
```

## Environment

```
torch 2.16.0.dev20261015+xpu
python 3.13.13 (/opt/conda/bin/python3.13)
torch path /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/__init__.py
xpu device Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
```

## Ownership

The defective code is the `__SYCL_DEVICE_ONLY__`-gated branch of `c10::complex` `log1p` in `c10/util/complex_math.h`, so the change belongs in **pytorch/pytorch**; the remedy used by the MPS PR applies directly, namely select the `log1p(r)/2` branch on `|r| < 0.5` with `r = |1 + z|^2 - 1` evaluated with compensated arithmetic (fma plus a two-sum) instead of selecting on `|z| < 0.5`, keeping the `hypot` form only as the overflow fallback. A local functor in `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/UnaryLogKernels.cpp` would be the alternative if the shared header is not the preferred place. This issue tracks the XPU parity work; pytorch/pytorch#201093 is MPS-only and its only generic change is removing an MPS xfail, so it will not fix XPU when it lands, and no `intel/torch-xpu-ops` issue covers this signature (#2257's log1p entries and #2816 are resolved and concern different inputs).

This issue was produced by an automated upstream-alignment scan with an AI assistant; the evidence above was gathered on an XPU host and independently reviewed.

nodes.body:
I have reproduction for following tests:
```
test/dynamo/test_repros.py::ReproTests::test_dynamo_set_recursion_limit
test/dynamo/test_dynamic_shapes.py::DynamicShapesReproTests::test_dynamo_set_recursion_limit_dynamic_shapes
```

#### Why there is no reproduction on pytorch windows CI?
The test ```test_repros.py``` is decorated with ```@unittest.skipIf(sys.version_info < (3, 12) or sys.version_info >= (3, 14), "only 3.12, 3.13 affected by c recursion limit")```. PyTorch's Windows CI runs Python 3.10, so the test is skipped there. XPU Windows CI runs Python 3.12, which is inside the affected range, so the test runs and crashes. DynamicShapesReproTests is generated from ReproTests. ```test_dynamic_shapes.py``` calls make_dynamic_cls, which goes through make_test_cls_with_patches (it wraps every test_* method of ```ReproTests``` with ```@functools.wraps```.) in ```torch/_dynamo/testing.py``` and as a result ```test_dynamo_set_recursion_limit_dynamic_shapes``` carries the same skip condition.


#### Recursion limit per python version
- ```< 3.12 ``` - there is no separate C recursion limit. C-level recursion is governed by ```sys.setrecursionlimit```, so ```torch._dynamo.set_recursion_limit``` has nothing extra to raise;
- ``` 3.12 – 3.13 ``` - CPython has a separate, hard-coded C recursion limit that Python code can't change. ```torch._dynamo.set_recursion_limit``` works around it by raising that limit. **This is the range the test targets**;
- ``` >= 3.14 ``` - CPython replaced the counter with stack-pointer-based overflow protection. The fixed constant no longer exists;


#### What is the root cause of crashing on XPU windows CI?
As mentioned XPU CI runs this test on python 3.12. The test raises the dynamo C recursion limit to 20000 and traces a 500-deep recursion on the main thread. That needs far more native stack than the Windows main thread has (1 MB venv python.exe / 2 MB base python.exe, versus 8 MB on Linux). With limits of 8000-20000 the main thread overflows; the same test passes at 20000 on a 128 MB thread. The failure is device-agnostic (CPU, eager) and not an XPU defect.

issues.title: [OOB Performance] dynamo models regression with transformers 5.18.0
issues.bodyText:
🐛 Describe the bug
During OOB regular test(inductor mode), found 3 dynamo model cases regression. Details as below:
Top suspect:

transformers 5.18 masking_utils change: under torch.compile, when there is no padding mask (the benchmark case), the attention mask is no longer created and None is passed instead. Results are still correct; causal masking is still applied.
Without the mask, Inductor's fused softmax+dropout kernel loses one input load: 1 load + 3 stores = 4, down from 5.
PyTorch XPUReductionHeuristic._persistent_inner_config (from 91ae1ab, #169257, still on main) uses XBLOCK=1 only if loads + stores ≥ 5, otherwise XBLOCK=8. At 4 it switches to XBLOCK=8, so each program processes 8 rows × 1024 elements plus dropout RNG.
As a result, these softmax kernels are 5.5–8.7× slower per call: PLBart 1.17 → 6.52 ms, hf_T5 ~0.78 → 4.3–6.8 ms. The two generated Triton kernels are nearly identical except for XBLOCK. GEMM and other kernels are unchanged.

### Summary

All 16 cases are the test_fsdp_core parity tests that inject a device-side delay, and every one dies in torch.testing._internal.common_utils.measure -> torch.get_device_module(device)._sleep(test_cycles) -> torch._C._xpu_sleep, which raises NotImplementedError: Requires the ext_oneapi_clock_sub_group extension, which is not supported on this device. The failing set is exactly the delayed_optim_step / delayed_reduce_scatter / mixture_of_experts_with_delay_before_free parametrizations, i.e. the ones that call _sleep, so the single cause is that the XPU _sleep implementation needs a SYCL extension the PVC runner's driver does not expose.

All 16 cases are the test_fsdp_core parity tests that inject a device-side delay, and every one dies in torch.testing._internal.common_utils.measure -> torch.get_device_module(device)._sleep(test_cycles) -> torch._C._xpu_sleep, which raises NotImplementedError: Requires the ext_oneapi_clock_sub_group extension, which is not supported on this device. issues.title: [Bug Skip]: [New Case] test_sac_ilp: the selective-activation-checkpointing ILP picks different decisions on XPU
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug with skip template

<!-- cases:begin -->
Cases:
upstream_distributed,test.distributed._tools.test_sac_ilp.TestSACILP,test_sac_ilp_case1
upstream_distributed,test.distributed._tools.test_sac_ilp.TestSACILP,test_sac_ilp_case2

<!-- cases:end -->

### Summary

Both TestSACILP cases disagree with the expected solver outcome: case1 gets peak_mem == -1, i.e. sac_milp found no feasible solution, and case2 gets a non-empty ac_decisions dict ({'Transformer.layers.0': 0.8954, ...}) where the test expects {}. Both read the same ILP output from the same runtime/memory estimates, so they are one cause: the estimates that feed sac_milp on XPU differ from the ones the test's budget assertions were written against.

### ErrorLog

#### AssertionError: {'Transformer.layers.0': 0.8954, 'Transfor[90 chars]7789} != {}

```

    self.assertDictEqual(ac_decisions, {})
  File "/home/jenkins/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.12.15-linux-x86_64-gnu/lib/python3.12/unittest/case.py", line 1184, in assertDictEqual
    self.fail(self._formatMessage(msg, standardMsg))

    raise self.failureException(msg)
AssertionError: {'Transformer.layers.0': 0.8954, 'Transfor[90 chars]7789} != {}
+ {}
- {'Transformer.layers.0': 0.8954,
-  'Transformer.layers.1': 0.925,
-  'Transformer.layers.2': 0.8954,
-  'Transformer.layers.3.attention': 0.7789}

To execute this test, run the following from the base repo dir:
    PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 python test/distributed/_tools/test_sac_ilp.py TestSACILP.test_sac_ilp_case2

This message can be suppressed by setting PYTORCH_PRINT_REPRO_ON_FAILURE=0
```

issues.title: [Bug Skip]: [New Case] test_zero_model_parallel hardcodes the nccl-legacy backend, which does not exist in an XPU build
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug with skip template

<!-- cases:begin -->
Cases:
upstream_distributed,test.distributed.optim.test_zero_redundancy_optimizer.TestZeroRedundancyOptimizerDistributedFreshPG,test_zero_model_parallel_parameters_as_bucket_view_False
upstream_distributed,test.distributed.optim.test_zero_redundancy_optimizer.TestZeroRedundancyOptimizerDistributedFreshPG,test_zero_model_parallel_parameters_as_bucket_view_True

<!-- cases:end -->

### Summary

Both parameters_as_bucket_view variants call create_pg(self.device, world_size=2, backend="nccl-legacy"), and init_process_group reaches _create_nccl_process_group, which raises RuntimeError: Distributed package doesn't have NCCL built in. One cause: the test asks for a NCCL backend by name instead of the accelerator's backend, so it can never run on XPU as written.

### 🐛 Describe the bug with skip template

Cases:
upstream_distributed,test.distributed.pipelining.test_schedule_multiproc.PerEdgeScheduleTest,test_grad_with_per_edge_ScheduleClass0_use_tracer_False

### Summary

issues.title: [Bug Skip]: [New Case] test_coor_compiles_on_gpu_build_with_no_visible_device: XPU devices are still visible when the test hides them
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug with skip template

<!-- cases:begin -->
Cases:
upstream_distributed,test.distributed.tensor.test_compile_on_one_rank.TestCompileOnOneRankDeviceAsParameter,test_coor_compiles_on_gpu_build_with_no_visible_device

<!-- cases:end -->

### Summary

The spawned child exits 1 with 'AssertionError: expected no visible devices', so the test's assertEqual on the exit code gets 1 instead of 0. The mechanism the test uses to hide accelerators from the child does not hide XPU devices.

### ErrorLog

#### AssertionError: Scalars are not equal! ; AssertionError: expected no visible devices

```

    self.assertEqual(
  File "/home/jenkins/actions-runner/_work/torch-xpu-ops/torch-xpu-ops/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py", line 5097, in assertEqual
    raise error_metas.pop()[0].to_error(  # type: ignore[index]
AssertionError: Scalars are not equal!

Expected 0 but got 1.
Absolute difference: 1
Relative difference: inf
CooR compile failed with no visible device:
Traceback (most recent call last):

AssertionError: expected no visible devices


To execute this test, run the following from the base repo dir:
```

### 🐛 Describe the bug with skip template

### Summary

All four negative tests that exercise the error paths of the symmetric-memory signal ops fail together: test_barrier_timeout, test_put_signal_timeout and test_wait_signal_timeout each hang until the harness kills the worker at 300 s instead of the op timing out, and test_put_wait_signal_rank_out_of_bounds gets exit -6 instead of 0. upstream_distributed,test.distributed.test_symmetric_memory.SymmMemNegativeTest,test_wait_signal_timeout

Summary
All four negative tests that exercise the error paths of the symmetric-memory signal ops fail together: test_barrier_timeout, test_put_signal_timeout and test_wait_signal_timeout each hang until the harness kills the worker at 300 s instead of the op timing out, and test_put_wait_signal_rank_out_of_bounds gets exit -6 instead of 0. The coincidence is the feature, not the machine: these are precisely the cases that assert the timeout and bounds-checking behaviour of put_signal / wait_signal / barrier, and the rest of the file passed.

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-10-17] XPU div by a Python scalar returns inf (fp16: NaN) where CPU is finite: the is_cpu_scalar reciprocal branch has no overflow/subnormal guard
issues.body:
<!-- alignment-published-unit: pr-201302 -->
## Summary

On XPU, `tensor / python_scalar` does not divide: the `is_cpu_scalar(2)` branch of the XPU
division kernels computes `inv_b = 1 / s` on the host in opmath and runs a multiply kernel.
When `1 / s` overflows or becomes subnormal in opmath, every element is lost: `x / 1e-39`
returns `inf` for all finite `x` (fp16: `NaN` for `x == 0`) where correctly rounded CPU
division returns a finite value. All three rounding modes (`None`, `"trunc"`, `"floor"`) are
affected, for fp32, bf16 and fp16.

This is silent numerical corruption, not the documented 1-ulp cost: the kernels' own comment
sanctions losing "one bit of precision compared to computing the division", and `inf`/`NaN`
for a finite quotient is far outside that.

## Upstream source

- `pytorch/pytorch#201302` — "[CUDA] Divide by CPU scalars whose reciprocal overflows, and use
  true division for trunc", [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#201302] (open at review time).
- Background: `pytorch/pytorch#191495` (closed), `pytorch/pytorch#8919` (original reciprocal
  optimization).
- Scan window: `2026-10-17T00:00:00Z` to `2026-10-18T00:00:00Z` (half-open UTC),
  `pytorch/pytorch` default branch.

The upstream PR adds a host-side `is_usable_reciprocal(inv_b)` helper
(`inv_b == 0 || std::isnormal(inv_b)`) in `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/BinaryInternal.h` and uses
it to fall back to real division in `BinaryDivTrueKernel.cu` and `BinaryDivFloorKernel.cu`;
`BinaryDivTruncKernel.cu` switches to `trunc(a / b)` unconditionally. All of those files are
CUDA-private, so nothing in that PR reaches XPU.

## Observed XPU behavior

27 of 27 tested (dtype, scalar, rounding_mode) combinations show the signature — CPU finite,
XPU `inf`/`NaN`:

```
  MISMATCH[signature] dtype=torch.float32 s=1e-39 mode=None
    xpu=[inf, inf, inf, inf, -inf]
    cpu=[9.999997314334689e+33, 9.999998261528069e+28, 9.999997781483192e+18, inf, -3.499999245708147e+32]
  MISMATCH[signature] dtype=torch.float32 s=1e-39 mode=floor
    xpu=[inf, inf, inf, inf, -inf]
    cpu=[9.999997314334689e+33, 9.999998261528069e+28, 9.999997781483192e+18, inf, -3.499999245708147e+32]
  MISMATCH[signature] dtype=torch.bfloat16 s=5e-40 mode=trunc
    xpu=[inf, inf, inf, inf, -inf]
    cpu=[2.003902068840785e+34, 2.005462863642316e+29, 2.0032011142543966e+19, inf, -6.997431313259826e+32]
  MISMATCH[signature] dtype=torch.float16 s=1e-39 mode=None
    xpu=[inf, nan, nan, inf, -inf]
    cpu=[inf, 0.0, 0.0, inf, -inf]
summary: signature=27 other=0
```

Every non-signature case matched CPU exactly (`other=0`), so the oracle is not picking up
ordinary rounding noise. The fp16 rows are the `0 * inf = NaN` case: `0 / 1e-39` must be `0`.

## Root cause in torch-xpu-ops

All three XPU division kernels hold the reciprocal trick with no guard:

- `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivTrueKernel.cpp:36-47`
  — `auto inv_b = opmath_t(1.0) / iter.scalar_value<opmath_t>(2);` then a `MulFunctor` kernel.
- `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivTruncKernel.cpp:50-59`
  — `auto inv_b = accscalar_t(1.0) / iter.scalar_value<accscalar_t>(2);` then
  `DivTruncScalarFunctor`, i.e. `sycl::trunc(a * inv_b_)`.
- `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivFloorKernel.cpp:85-100`
  — `auto inv_b = accscalar_t(1.0) / b;` then `DivFloorWithScalarFunctor`, whose
  `div = (a_ - mod) * inv_b_` becomes `inf`.

For fp32/bf16/fp16 the accumulate type is `float`, and `1 / 9.99e-40f` overflows `float`, so
`inv_b` is `inf` and the multiply loses every element. `float64` is unaffected because
`1 / 1e-39` is representable in `double`.

Adjacent, from the same lines: XPU computes the reciprocal directly in `opmath_t`, whereas the
current CUDA `div_true_kernel_cuda` computes it in `high_prec_t` (`double`) before narrowing.
That is a separate 1-ulp-class difference, not part of this report's oracle.

## Target-path evidence

The divisor is a Python float, which is what selects the `is_cpu_scalar(2)` branch under test;
the reproducer asserts `xpu_out.device.type == "xpu"` for every case and reads the compared
values back from the XPU result. A CPU fallback is ruled out behaviorally: it would have
returned the CPU values. The observed pattern — every element `inf`, and `NaN` exactly where
the input is `0` — is precisely what multiplying by an overflowed host-computed reciprocal
produces.

## Reproducer

```python
import torch

for dtype in (torch.float32, torch.bfloat16, torch.float16):
    cpu = torch.tensor([1e-5, 1e-10, 1e-20, 1.0, -3.5e-7], dtype=dtype)
    xpu = cpu.to("xpu")
    for s in (1e-39, 5e-40, 1e-45):          # 1/s overflows or is subnormal in fp32
        for mode in (None, "trunc", "floor"):
            got = torch.div(xpu, s, rounding_mode=mode)
            ref = torch.div(cpu, s, rounding_mode=mode)
            assert got.device.type == "xpu"
            print(dtype, s, mode, got.float().cpu().tolist(), ref.float().tolist())
```

The exact script executed for this scan is `scripts/repro_pr-201302.py`, SHA-256
`4d10c2c59aa5bb6be92b2b1a5fc6a9f79bac4ec0037fcdacf24c0ffe3940a349`, with the raw log at
`runner/logs/pr-201302.log`, SHA-256
`9591765d21d3406da00157acc890678af6840c9aa2ab5ada07422f9cd2269bde`.

## Environment

- torch `2.16.0.dev20261017+xpu` (`/opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/__init__.py`)
- Python 3.13.13 (`/opt/conda/bin/python3.13`)
- `Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics`, `torch.xpu.is_available()` true, no environment warnings

## Why this belongs in intel/torch-xpu-ops

The oracle is correctly rounded CPU division, which is current established behavior and not
something `pytorch/pytorch#201302` introduces, so the defect in the XPU kernels exists today
and its fix does not depend on that PR landing. The code holding the defect is XPU-owned:
`BinaryDivTrueKernel.cpp`, `BinaryDivTruncKernel.cpp` and `BinaryDivFloorKernel.cpp` in this
repository are independent reimplementations, and the upstream fix touches only
`aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/`.

Note for test planning: the two new upstream regression tests
(`test_division_by_scalar_without_finite_normal_reciprocal` and
`test_div_trunc_by_scalar_matches_cpu` in `test/test_binary_ufuncs.py`) are decorated
`@onlyCUDA`, so XPU CI will not pick this up even after the PR lands.

No `intel/torch-xpu-ops` issue and no `pytorch/pytorch` issue or PR covering the XPU side of
this was found at review time.

Example rows: ``` MISMATCH[signature] dtype=torch.bfloat16 s=5e-40 mode=trunc xpu=[inf, inf, inf, inf, -inf] cpu=[2.003902068840785e+34, 2.005462863642316e+29, 2.0032011142543966e+19, inf, -6.997431313259826e+32] MISMATCH[signature] dtype=torch.float16 s=1e-39 mode=None xpu=[inf, nan, nan, inf, -inf] cpu=[inf, 0.0, 0.0, inf, -inf] ``` *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at `torch-xpu-ops@36aa2394` (origin/main), pytorch `origin/main`. All three XPU division kernels apply the "multiply by the host-computed reciprocal" optimization to a CPU scalar divisor with no guard on the reciprocal itself. `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivTrueKernel.cpp:42` computes `inv_b = opmath_t(1.0) / iter.scalar_value(2)` and then runs a `MulFunctor` kernel; `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivTruncKernel.cpp:57` does the same into `DivTruncScalarFunctor` (`sycl::trunc(a * inv_b_)`); `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivFloorKernel.cpp:97` into `DivFloorWithScalarFunctor`, whose `div = (a_ - mod) * inv_b_` at line 51 is the multiply. For fp32, bf16 and fp16 the accumulate type is `float`, so a divisor around `1e-39` makes `1 / b` overflow to `inf` (and a divisor near `float` max makes it subnormal). Multiplying by `inf` maps every finite element to `+-inf`, and `0 * inf` to `NaN`, which is the exact pattern observed. `float64` is unaffected because `1 / 1e-39` is representable in `double`. The in-code comments on those branches sanction losing "one bit of precision"; total loss of the value is outside that. The bug is not new -- the reciprocal branch is original XPU code and these files have not been touched since #4099. What is new is only the report: `pytorch/pytorch#201302` ("[CUDA] Divide by CPU scalars whose reciprocal overflows, and use true division for trunc") proposed the equivalent CUDA fix and was **closed unmerged by its author within hours, with no review** (`pytorch/pytorch#201302` closed 2026-10-18, CI green, zero reviews). Its design is still the right reference: a host-side `is_usable_reciprocal(inv_b)` helper (`inv_b == 0 || std::isnormal(inv_b)`) in `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/BinaryInternal.h`, used to fall back to real division. Note also `pytorch/pytorch#191495`, closed `not planned`, where a maintainer ruled that the reciprocal path's **one-bit** divergence from CPU is within expected accuracy -- that rationale is explicitly about one bit and does not cover `inf`/`NaN` for a finite quotient, which is what this issue reports. Fix strategy: add `is_usable_reciprocal` to `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryInternal.h` and, in each of the three kernels, fall back to real division in the accumulate type when the guard rejects `inv_b`. Measured CPU reference semantics are "divide in opmath with the divisor held at opmath precision, then narrow", so the fallbacks keep `opmath_t` / `accscalar_t` rather than adopting upstream's `high_prec_t` (`double`) -- for fp32 a `double` divide then narrow does **not** reproduce CPU bit-for-bit, while an `opmath_t` divide does. The guard is host-side and the fast path is untouched, so there is no cost in the common case. Out of scope deliberately: the separate trunc issue that PR also addressed (a one-ulp error in `a * (1/b)` can move `trunc` by a whole integer), which this issue's oracle does not flag. - **Verdict:** IMPLEMENTING -- defect is in XPU-owned kernels in this repo, mechanism and fix are both local and small. - **Target repo:** torch-xpu-ops - **Domain:** xpu-kernel > [!NOTE] > Reviewer judgement call: CUDA has the same unguarded reciprocal today and the upstream fix attempt was closed, so this patch makes XPU match CPU and diverge from CUDA. That direction is defensible -- `inf` for a finite quotient is not the one-bit tradeoff upstream signed off on, and XPU `tensor / tensor` is already finite here -- but it is a policy call that belongs to a human, which is why it is flagged rather than buried. *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Implement Result - **Target repo:** torch-xpu-ops - **Analyzed at:** `torch-xpu-ops@36aa2394` - **What I changed:** `BinaryInternal.h` (+17) adds the host-side `is_usable_reciprocal` guard and its complex overload; `BinaryDivTrueKernel.cpp` (+16/-1) keeps `b` and falls back to a `DivFunctor` kernel; `BinaryDivTruncKernel.cpp` (+21/-2) adds `DivTruncByScalarFunctor` (`trunc(acc(a) / b)`) and the guard; `BinaryDivFloorKernel.cpp` (+23/-1) adds `DivFloorByScalarFunctor` (`c10::div_floor_floating(acc(a), b)`), the guard, and the `BinaryInternal.h` include. - **Why:** each of the three kernels multiplied by a host-computed `1/b` with nothing checking that the reciprocal survived; the guard sends the overflowed/subnormal case down a real division in the accumulate type instead. The fallbacks hold the divisor at `opmath_t`/`accscalar_t` rather than at `double` because that is what reproduces CPU: for a float32 tensor, dividing in float32 matches `torch.div` on CPU bit-for-bit over all 27 probed cases, while dividing in float64 and narrowing does not. The fast path and the tensor-tensor path are untouched. - **Skip added:** no - **Ready for verify:** yes ```diff diff --git a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivFloorKernel.cpp b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivFloorKernel.cpp index 84886b7e..f22d0426 100644 --- a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivFloorKernel.cpp +++ b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivFloorKernel.cpp @@ -14,6 +14,7 @@ #include #include +#include #include #include @@ -39,6 +40,21 @@ struct DivFloorIntergerFunctor { } }; +template +struct DivFloorByScalarFunctor { + DivFloorByScalarFunctor(accscalar_t b) : b_(b) {} + + scalar_t operator()(scalar_t a) const { + // suppress compiler optimization on data type promotion + volatile accscalar_t res = + c10::div_floor_floating(static_cast(a), b_); + return res; + } + + private: + accscalar_t b_; +}; + template struct DivFloorWithScalarFunctor { DivFloorWithScalarFunctor(accscalar_t b, accscalar_t inv_b) @@ -85,7 +101,9 @@ void div_floor_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter) { } else if (iter.is_cpu_scalar(2)) { // optimization for floating-point types: if the second operand is a CPU // scalar, compute a * reciprocal(b). Note that this may lose one bit of - // precision compared to computing the division. + // precision compared to computing the division. If 1/b overflowed or went + // subnormal in the accumulate type, divide by b instead so the value is + // not lost. AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND2( kHalf, kBFloat16, dtype, "div_floor_xpu", [&]() { using accscalar_t = at::acc_type_device; @@ -96,6 +114,10 @@ void div_floor_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter) { auto inv_b = accscalar_t(1.0) / b; iter.remove_operand(2); + if (C10_UNLIKELY(!is_usable_reciprocal(inv_b))) { + gpu_kernel(iter, DivFloorByScalarFunctor(b)); + return; + } gpu_kernel( iter, DivFloorWithScalarFunctor(b, inv_b)); }); diff --git a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivTrueKernel.cpp b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivTrueKernel.cpp index cedebe77..e8441718 100644 --- a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivTrueKernel.cpp +++ b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryDivTrueKernel.cpp @@ -34,13 +34,28 @@ void div_true_kernel(TensorIteratorBase& iter) { return; } if (iter.is_cpu_scalar(2)) { + // optimization for floating-point types: if the second operand is a CPU + // scalar, compute a * reciprocal(b). Note that this may lose one bit of - // precision compared to computing the division. + // precision compared to computing the division. If 1/b overflowed or went + // subnormal in the accumulate type, divide by b instead so the value is + // not lost. AT_DISPATCH_FLOATING_TYPES_AND2( kHalf, kBFloat16, dtype, "div_trunc_xpu", [&]() { using accscalar_t = at::acc_type_device; - auto inv_b = accscalar_t(1.0) / iter.scalar_value(2); + auto b = iter.scalar_value(2); + auto inv_b = accscalar_t(1.0) / b; iter.remove_operand(2); + if (C10_UNLIKELY(!is_usable_reciprocal(inv_b))) { + gpu_kernel(iter, DivTruncByScalarFunctor(b)); + return; + } gpu_kernel(iter, DivTruncScalarFunctor(inv_b)); }); } else { diff --git a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryInternal.h b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryInternal.h index ae748177..59623288 100644 --- a/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryInternal.h +++ b/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/BinaryInternal.h @@ -10,8 +10,11 @@ #pragma once +#include #include +#include + namespace at::native::xpu { template @@ -37,4 +40,18 @@ struct MulFunctor { } }; +// Whether a host-computed reciprocal 1/b of a CPU scalar divisor can replace +// division by b: it must not have overflowed or become subnormal, otherwise +// multiplying by it loses the value entirely rather than one bit of precision. +template +bool is_usable_reciprocal(T inv_b) { + return inv_b == T(0) || std::isnormal(inv_b); +} + +template +bool is_usable_reciprocal(c10::complex inv_b) { + return is_usable_reciprocal(inv_b.real()) && + is_usable_reciprocal(inv_b.imag()); +} + } // namespace at::native::xpu ``` *Automated by fix-implement.*

The before/after was taken on the **same** source build (fix reverted vs fix applied), not nightly-wheel vs source build, so the usual "maybe something else upstream fixed it" confound does not apply here -- reverting just these four files brings the failure straight back. Regression checks on the fixed build: | Suite | Result | |---|---| | `test_binary_ufuncs.py -k "(div or division or floor_divide or true_divide or remainder or fmod) and xpu"` | 1555 passed, 42 skipped, 5 xfailed | | `test_ops.py -k "(div or floor_divide or true_divide) and xpu"` | 397 passed, 91 skipped, 2 xfailed | The fast path is unchanged bit-for-bit: upstream `test_division_by_scalar`, which asserts `tensor / s` equals `tensor * (1 / s)` with `atol=0, rtol=0` over `logspace(-4, 4)` divisors, still passes -- those reciprocals are all normal, so the new guard never fires there. The fix adds a host-side `is_usable_reciprocal` guard in `BinaryInternal.h` and, when it rejects the reciprocal, dispatches a fallback that really divides in the accumulate type; the fast path is untouched and bit-identical. issues.title: timm_models amp_bf16 training accuracy regressions vs oneAPI (botnet26t_256, eca_halonext26ts, rexnet_100)
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

E2E accuracy regressions with the **dpclang** build compared to the **oneAPI** build. All 3 cases pass with oneAPI and fail with dpclang (`fail_accuracy`); all are `timm_models` / `amp_bf16` / `training`.

| Suite | Dtype | Mode | Model | oneAPI | dpclang | Detail (dpclang) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| timm_models | amp_bf16 | training | botnet26t_256 | pass | fail_accuracy | RMSE (res-fp64): 0.01796, (ref-fp64): 0.00811, shape=torch.Size([2048]), multiplier 2.0, tol 0.01 |
| timm_models | amp_bf16 | training | eca_halonext26ts | pass | fail_accuracy | RMSE (res-fp64): 0.00383, (ref-fp64): 0.00124, shape=torch.Size([2048]), multiplier 2.0, tol 0.01 |
| timm_models | amp_bf16 | training | rexnet_100 | pass | fail_accuracy | RMSE (res-fp64): 0.00302, (ref-fp64): 0.00043, shape=torch.Size([1044]), multiplier 2.0, tol 0.01 |

No other accuracy regressions: huggingface and torchbench are clean, and the official model list (650 cases) has 0 regressions.

### Reproducer

```bash

# in container
docker run -it -e TZ=Aisa/Shanghai -e http_proxy -e https_proxy -v ${HOME}:${HOME} --device=/dev/mem --device=/dev/dri --group-add video --privileged --shm-size=8g intelgpu/ubuntu-24.04-lts2:2523.40 bash

# setup python
curl -LsSf [地址已移除] | sh
source $HOME/.local/bin/env
uv venv myvenv --clear --python 3.12.15
source myvenv/bin/activate
uv pip install pip wheel "setuptools<81"

gh --repo intel/torch-xpu-ops run download 38882733178 -p "Torch-XPU-Wheel-*"
uv pip install Torch-XPU-Wheel-*/*.whl

gh --repo intel/torch-xpu-ops run download 38882733178 -n dpclang
rm -rf install-dpclang && mkdir install-dpclang
tar xzvf install-dpclang.tgz -C install-dpclang
export CMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=$(pwd)/install-dpclang
export PKG_CONFIG_PATH=$(pwd)/install-dpclang/lib/pkgconfig:$PKG_CONFIG_PATH
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$(pwd)/install-dpclang/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH
export PATH=$(pwd)/install-dpclang/bin:$PATH

# prepare pytorch
pytorch_commit="$(python -c 'import torch; print(torch.version.git_version)')"
git clone [地址已移除]
cd pytorch
git checkout ${pytorch_commit}

# install deps
uv pip install pip pandas psutil scipy requests
uv pip install -r .ci/docker/ci_commit_pins/huggingface-requirements.txt
uv pip install timm

# sync model list
rm -rf torch torch-xpu-ops
git clone [地址已移除]
rsync -avz ./torch-xpu-ops/.ci/benchmarks/ ./benchmarks/dynamo/

python benchmarks/dynamo/timm_models.py -d xpu --accuracy --amp --amp-dtype bfloat16 --training \
    --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs \
    --only botnet26t_256   # also: eca_halonext26ts, rexnet_100
```

### Versions

- Target (dpclang): Inductor-dpclang-ondemand-LTS2 run `38882733178`, commit `cde6c073db9ea641f76eb91bd93533cf969a62ba`
- Baseline (oneAPI): Inductor-build-ondemand-LTS2 run `39186464115`

issues.title: [Inductor][OOB/gpt-oss]Inductor cpp_wrapper masks NameError for user-defined autotuned Triton kernel (_finalize_matmul MXFP4 MoE) on XPU
issues.body:
## Summary

Running the MXFP4 MoE path of **gpt-oss-20b** through Inductor on XPU fails inside the user-defined Triton kernel `_finalize_matmul` (from `kernels-community/gpt-oss-triton-kernels`, `build/torch-xpu/matmul_ogs.py:265`), which Inductor captures into the compiled graph.

When Inductor's C++ wrapper (`cpp_wrapper`) is enabled, running the kernel from the generated C++ wrapper raises the opaque:

```
RuntimeError: Failed to run kernel with autotuning
```
(from `torch/csrc/inductor/cpp_wrapper/lazy_triton_compile.h`, via `runTritonKernelWithAutotune`)

## Root cause

The real underlying error is a `NameError` that is **masked** by the cpp_wrapper path.

When Inductor precompiles a user-defined, autotuned `@triton.jit` kernel in its **subprocess compile worker**, the kernel's module-level global helper (a `@triton.constexpr_function` evaluated at compile time) is **NOT** present in the namespace used by Triton's `ast_to_ttir` in that worker. The kernel body therefore raises:

```
NameError('<helper> is not defined')
```

The same kernel compiles and runs fine in **eager Triton**, because eager uses `fn.__globals__` (where the helper is defined).

This mirrors `_finalize_matmul` in gpt-oss-triton-kernels, whose body does:

```python
USE_FUSED_MIXED_PREC_ACC: tl.constexpr = cuda_capability_geq(10, 0)
```

where `cuda_capability_geq` is a module-global `constexpr_function`.

With Inductor `cpp_wrapper` ON (the `transformers` `run_llm.py` default), the real `NameError` is masked as the opaque `RuntimeError: Failed to run kernel with autotuning`.

## Minimal reproducer

```python
"""
Mini reproducer for the gpt-oss-20b MXFP4 MoE Inductor/XPU failure.

Root cause (component): PyTorch Inductor user-defined-Triton-kernel path.
When Inductor precompiles a user-defined, autotuned @triton.jit kernel in its
subprocess compile worker, the kernel's module-level global helper (a
@triton.constexpr_function that is evaluated at compile time) is NOT present in
the namespace used by Triton's ast_to_ttir in that worker -> the kernel body
raises NameError('<helper> is not defined').

The SAME kernel compiles and runs fine in eager Triton, because eager uses
fn.__globals__ (where the helper is defined).

This mirrors kernels-community/gpt-oss-triton-kernels `_finalize_matmul`, whose
body does:  USE_FUSED_MIXED_PREC_ACC: tl.constexpr = cuda_capability_geq(10, 0)
where cuda_capability_geq is a module-global constexpr_function.

With Inductor cpp_wrapper ON (transformers run_llm.py default), the real
NameError is masked as the opaque:
    RuntimeError: Failed to run kernel with autotuning
    (torch/csrc/inductor/cpp_wrapper/lazy_triton_compile.h)

Run:
    python minirepro_triton_global.py                 # python wrapper -> NameError
    TORCHINDUCTOR_CPP_WRAPPER=1 python minirepro...    # cpp wrapper  -> masked error
"""

import os
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


# --- module-level global helpers referenced INSIDE the jit kernel body ---
# Evaluated at Triton compile time (constexpr). Lives only in module globals,
# exactly like target_info.cuda_capability_geq in gpt-oss-triton-kernels.
# IMPORTANT: it must query the live driver (not a foldable constant) so the
# call survives Dynamo tracing into the captured kernel, and is only evaluated
# in Inductor's compile worker -- where the module global is missing.
from triton.runtime import driver


def current_target():
    try:
        active_driver = driver.active
    except RuntimeError:
        return None
    return active_driver.get_current_target()


current_target.__triton_builtin__ = True


@triton.constexpr_function
def my_cap_geq(major, minor=0):
    target = current_target()
    if target is None or target.backend != "cuda":
        return False
    return target.arch >= major * 10 + minor


# Autotune with several configs -> pushes Inductor onto its async/subprocess
# compile path, which is where the module global gets dropped.
@triton.autotune(
    configs=[
        triton.Config({"BLOCK": b}, num_warps=w)
        for b in (256, 512, 1024, 2048)
        for w in (2, 4, 8)
    ],
    key=["N"],
)
@triton.jit
def add_kernel(X, Y, Out, N, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    USE_ALT: tl.constexpr = my_cap_geq(10, 0)  # <-- global constexpr call
    pid = tl.program_id(0)
    offs = pid * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    mask = offs < N
    x = tl.load(X + offs, mask=mask)
    y = tl.load(Y + offs, mask=mask)
    out = (x - y) if USE_ALT else (x + y)
    tl.store(Out + offs, out, mask=mask)


def run(x, y):
    out = torch.empty_like(x)
    n = x.numel()
    grid = lambda meta: (triton.cdiv(n, meta["BLOCK"]),)
    add_kernel[grid](x, y, out, n)
    return out


def main():
    if os.environ.get("TORCHINDUCTOR_CPP_WRAPPER") == "1":
        import torch._inductor.config as ic

        ic.cpp_wrapper = True
        print(">>> cpp_wrapper = True")

    dev = "xpu"
    x = torch.randn(8192, device=dev)
    y = torch.randn(8192, device=dev)

    try:
        o = run(x, y)
        torch.xpu.synchronize()
        print("[eager]   OK   max_err =", (o - (x + y)).abs().max().item())
    except Exception as e:
        print("[eager]   FAILED:", type(e).__name__, repr(e)[:200])

    try:
        o = torch.compile(run)(x, y)
        torch.xpu.synchronize()
        print("[compile] OK   max_err =", (o - (x + y)).abs().max().item())
    except Exception as e:
        print("[compile] FAILED:", type(e).__name__, repr(e)[:400])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

### How to run

```bash
# python wrapper -> surfaces the real NameError
python minirepro_triton_global.py

# cpp wrapper -> real error masked as "Failed to run kernel with autotuning"
TORCHINDUCTOR_CPP_WRAPPER=1 python minirepro_triton_global.py
```

## Expected behavior

- The user-defined autotuned Triton kernel should compile and run under `torch.compile` on XPU, with module-level global helpers (e.g. a `@triton.constexpr_function`) available in the compile-worker namespace, matching eager Triton behavior.
- At minimum, the cpp_wrapper path should not mask the underlying `NameError` behind the opaque `RuntimeError: Failed to run kernel with autotuning`.

## Actual behavior

- `[eager]` path: OK.
- `[compile]` path (python wrapper): fails with `NameError('<helper> is not defined')` raised from Triton `ast_to_ttir` in the subprocess compile worker.
- `[compile]` path (cpp_wrapper): fails with the opaque `RuntimeError: Failed to run kernel with autotuning`.

## Environment

- Model: gpt-oss-20b, MXFP4 MoE path
- Kernel: `_finalize_matmul` from `kernels-community/gpt-oss-triton-kernels` (`build/torch-xpu/matmul_ogs.py:265`)
- Device: Intel XPU
- Please let me know any additional version info (torch / triton / torch-xpu-ops build) you need and I'll attach it.

issues.title: [PTL][WSL] test_gradgrad_nn_Transformer_xpu_float64 takes ~800 s on PTL-H and exceeds the 600 s UT timeout
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`test_modules.py::TestModuleXPU::test_gradgrad_nn_Transformer_xpu_float64` passes on PTL-H, but takes about 800 s (797 s measured). The UT run uses `--timeout 600 --timeout_method=thread`, so pytest-timeout aborts the case and the run reports a failure. On earlier nightlies this case also took down the xdist worker (one of the 32 cases in #4877).

This issue tracks a PR that skips the case on PTL.

**Repro** (from `third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu`):
```
PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 PYTORCH_ENABLE_XPU_FALLBACK=1 \
python -m pytest -v --timeout 600 --timeout_method=thread \
  ../../../../test/test_modules.py::TestModuleXPU::test_gradgrad_nn_Transformer_xpu_float64
```
- `--timeout 600`: `Timeout` at 600 s. Pytest-timeout dumps the stack at `torch/autograd/gradcheck.py` `_test_batched_grad`, called from `gradgradcheck`.
- `--timeout 3000`: `1 passed in 797.49s (0:13:17)`.

**Proposed fix:** skip the case on PTL (Windows/WSL), or mark it slow, so it doesn't hit the 600 s cap.

Split from #4877.

issues.title: [XPU] Support scale_result in torch._scaled_mm (aten::_scaled_mm)
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`torch._scaled_mm` accepts an optional `scale_result` tensor to scale the GEMM output before downcasting to float8 dtypes. On XPU, `scale_result` is accepted by the operator interface in `aten/src/ATen/native/mkldnn/xpu/ScaledBlas.cpp`, but it is not applied during execution.

### Reproduction
```python
import torch

a = torch.randint(-1, 2, (32, 16), device="xpu").float().to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
b = torch.randint(-1, 2, (16, 32), device="xpu").float().to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
scale = torch.ones((), device="xpu")
scale_result = torch.full((), 0.5, device="xpu")

out = torch._scaled_mm(a, b, scale_a=scale, scale_b=scale, scale_result=scale_result, out_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
expected = (a.float() @ b.float()).mul(scale_result).to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
assert torch.equal(out, expected)  # Fails: out is not scaled by scale_result
```

pytest test/test_scaled_matmul_cuda.py -k test_float8_scale_result

issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`test_linalg_xpu.py::TestLinalgXPU::test_inverse_errors_large_xpu_{complex128,complex64,float32,float64}` fails on PTL-H with `UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`, for all four dtypes, also when each case runs alone. The test expects `torch.linalg.LinAlgError: (Batch element 0): The diagonal element 11 is zero`

In a whole-file run (`run_test_with_skip.py` style, xdist `-n 1`) the device stays lost afterwards: about 539 later cases in `test_linalg_xpu.py` fail with DEVICE_LOST.

**Minimal repro:**
```python
import torch
x = torch.empty((8, 10, 616, 616), dtype=torch.complex128, device="xpu")
x[:] = torch.eye(616, dtype=torch.complex128, device="xpu")
x[..., 10, 10] = 0
torch.inverse(x)   # expected LinAlgError; got:
# RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 20 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST)
```
**Test repro** (from `third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu`):
```
PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 PYTORCH_ENABLE_XPU_FALLBACK=1 python -m pytest -v \
  "test_linalg_xpu.py::TestLinalgXPU::test_inverse_errors_large_xpu_complex128"
```

issues.title: [PTL][WSL] test_cond_xpu_complex128: torch.linalg.cond(x, 'fro') is ~20% off for complex128
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`test_linalg_xpu.py::TestLinalgXPU::test_cond_xpu_complex128` fails on PTL-H, both alone and in the whole-file run:
```
AssertionError: Scalars are not close!
Expected (180.26537343957503+0j) but got 145.27934540799103.
Absolute difference: 34.986028031584 (up to 0 allowed)
Relative difference: 0.19408068984092122 (up to 0.01 allowed)
```
(`test/test_linalg.py:1697` `test_cond` -> `run_test_case`, line 1683.)

Checking each norm type separately, only `p='fro'` on the 32x32 input is wrong. Every other `p` (1, -1, 2, -2, inf, -inf, 'nuc', None) and the batched (2,3,3,3) input match NumPy:
```python
import torch, numpy as np
torch.manual_seed(0)
x = torch.randn(32, 32, dtype=torch.complex128, device="xpu")
print(torch.linalg.cond(x, 'fro').item(), np.linalg.cond(x.cpu().numpy(), 'fro'))
# xpu 127.14  numpy 162.95  (rel 0.22)
```
The run prints `UserWarning: Aten Op fallback from XPU to CPU happends`, so some op on this path falls back to CPU. `cond(x, 'fro')` = ‖x‖_F · ‖x⁻¹‖_F. The likely suspect is the complex128 inverse path, or a fallback/copy between XPU and CPU (not confirmed).

**Test repro** (from `third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu`):

issues.title: [XPU] Implement aten::_scaled_addmm and aten::_scaled_addmm.out for XPU
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

The scaled matrix multiply-add operators `torch.nn.functional.scaled_addmm`, `torch._scaled_addmm`, and in-place `scaled_addmm_` delegate to `aten::_scaled_addmm.out`, which currently only registers a `CUDA` dispatch in `aten/src/ATen/native/native_functions.yaml`. Calling `scaled_addmm` on XPU fails with `NotImplementedError`

Affected Tests
In `test/test_scaled_matmul_cuda.py`:
- `test_scaled_addmm_tensorwise`
- `test_scaled_addmm_wgrad_accumulation`
- `test_scaled_addmm_scalar_semantics`
- `test_scaled_addmm_empty`
- `test_scaled_addmm_validation`
- `test_scaled_addmm_mxfp8`
- `test_scaled_addmm_nvfp4`
- `test_scaled_addmm_fullgraph`
- `test_scaled_addmm_inplace_tunableop`

Reproduction
```python
import torch
from torch.nn.functional import scaled_addmm

m, n, k = 32, 32, 32
inp = torch.randn(m, n, device="xpu", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
mat1 = torch.randn(m, k, device="xpu").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn)
mat2 = torch.randn(n, k, device="xpu").to(torch.float8_e4m3fn).t()
scale_a = torch.ones(1, device="xpu")
scale_b = torch.ones(1, device="xpu")

scaled_addmm(inp, mat1, mat2, scale_a, scale_b)
```

issues.title: [PTL][WSL] test_indexing.py: index_reduce cases hit UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES after earlier TestIndexingDeviceXPU cases (then DEVICE_LOST)
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

In a whole-file run of upstream `test/test_indexing.py` on PTL-H (`run_test_with_skip.py` style, xdist `-n 1`), the run is clean up to `test_index_reduce_reduce_mean_xpu_int64`. Then `TestIndexingDeviceXPU::test_index_reduce_reduce_mean_xpu_int8` fails with:
```
RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 40 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_RESOURCES)
  File ".../test/test_indexing.py", line 1923, in test_index_reduce
```
After that, the rest of the `index_reduce` mean/prod cases fail (OUT_OF_RESOURCES, then `UR_RESULT_ERROR_DEVICE_LOST`). In total: 75 failed / 305 passed / 17 skipped.

It depends on test order and state:
- `test_index_reduce_reduce_mean_xpu_int8` alone: **passed**
- `-k index_reduce` (72 cases, one process): **72 passed**
- the whole `TestIndexingDeviceXPU` class in one process: **fails** (OUT_OF_RESOURCES, then DEVICE_LOST)

So an earlier case in `TestIndexingDeviceXPU` leaks or exhausts a device resource, and `index_reduce` is the first to run out. Which case does it is not identified yet.

issues.title: [distributed][xccl] ProcessGroupXCCL::reduce does not handle ReduceOp.PREMUL_SUM ("PreMulSum requires oneCCL>=2022.0" with oneCCL 2022.1)
issues.body:
Found while addressing review on pytorch/pytorch#198063 (porting `test/distributed/test_c10d_ops_nccl.py` to XPU), where the reviewer asked to enable `PREMUL_SUM` for XCCL. `all_reduce` and `reduce_scatter` work, but `reduce` does not, so the affected cases are skipped on XPU with a link to this issue. The details below were drafted with an AI assistant (Claude Code) and reproduced on our 4x Max 1100 machine.

> ### 🐛 Describe the bug
>
> `ReduceOp.PREMUL_SUM` works with XCCL for `all_reduce` and `reduce_scatter`, but `reduce` raises `ValueError: PreMulSum requires oneCCL>=2022.0`, even though the runtime oneCCL is 2022.1.
>
> ```python
> import torch
> import torch.distributed as dist
>
> dist.init_process_group("xccl")
> rank = dist.get_rank()
> torch.xpu.set_device(rank)
> op = dist.ReduceOp.PREMUL_SUM(2.0)
>
> t = torch.ones(4, device="xpu")
> dist.all_reduce(t, op=op)
> print(f"rank {rank}: all_reduce PREMUL_SUM ok -> {t[0].item()}")
>
> t = torch.ones(4, device="xpu")
> try:
>     dist.reduce(t, dst=0, op=op)
>     print(f"rank {rank}: reduce PREMUL_SUM ok -> {t[0].item()}")
> except Exception as e:
>     print(f"rank {rank}: reduce PREMUL_SUM failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
> dist.destroy_process_group()
> ```
>
> ```
> $ torchrun --nproc-per-node=2 premul_reduce_repro.py
> rank 0: all_reduce PREMUL_SUM ok -> 4.0
> rank 0: reduce PREMUL_SUM failed: ValueError: PreMulSum requires oneCCL>=2022.0
> rank 1: all_reduce PREMUL_SUM ok -> 4.0
> rank 1: reduce PREMUL_SUM failed: ValueError: PreMulSum requires oneCCL>=2022.0
> ```
>
> **Cause.** In `src/xccl/ProcessGroupXCCL.cpp`, `allreduce_impl`, `allreduce_coalesced` and `reduce_scatter` call `applyPreMulSumIfNeeded(input, opts.reduceOp)`, which scales the input by the factor and turns the op into `SUM` (the comment explains that native oneCCL premul is scale-up only, so it is always emulated). `reduce` (both the `reduce` and `_reduce_oop` paths, `xccl::onecclReduce(input, output, comm, opts.reduceOp, root, stream)`) passes `opts.reduceOp` straight through, so it reaches `getXcclReduceOp` in `src/xccl/xccl.h`, which throws when `ENABLE_XCCL_PREMUL_SUM_SUPPORT` is not defined at build time. The `oneCCL>=2022.0` wording is misleading here because the runtime oneCCL is 2022.1.
>
> **Suggested fix.** Apply `applyPreMulSumIfNeeded` in the `reduce` paths too, as for `allreduce` / `reduce_scatter`. #1571 ("Cannot use ReduceOp.PREMUL_SUM with XCCL") covered the other collectives but not `reduce`.
>
> **Test impact.** In `test/distributed/test_c10d_ops_nccl.py`, `ProcessGroupNCCLOpTest::test_reduce_op_premul_sum` and the premul sub-case of `ProcessGroupNCCLOpTest::test_reduce_ops` fail on XPU with this error and are skipped there. This issue should only be closed once those skips are removed and both pass on XPU.
>
> ### Versions
>
> ```
> torch              2.15.0a0+git1285517 (source build)
> torch-xpu-ops      5934d4f5
> oneCCL             2022.1 (DLE 2026.1.2.25)
> device             4x Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100
> backend            xccl
> ```
issues.bodyText:
Found while addressing review on pytorch/pytorch#198063 (porting test/distributed/test_c10d_ops_nccl.py to XPU), where the reviewer asked to enable PREMUL_SUM for XCCL. all_reduce and reduce_scatter work, but reduce does not, so the affected cases are skipped on XPU with a link to this issue. The details below were drafted with an AI assistant (Claude Code) and reproduced on our 4x Max 1100 machine.

🐛 Describe the bug
ReduceOp.PREMUL_SUM works with XCCL for all_reduce and reduce_scatter, but reduce raises ValueError: PreMulSum requires oneCCL>=2022.0, even though the runtime oneCCL is 2022.1.
import torch
import torch.distributed as dist

dist.init_process_group("xccl")
rank = dist.get_rank()
torch.xpu.set_device(rank)
op = dist.ReduceOp.PREMUL_SUM(2.0)

t = torch.ones(4, device="xpu")
dist.all_reduce(t, op=op)
print(f"rank {rank}: all_reduce PREMUL_SUM ok -> {t[0].item()}")

t = torch.ones(4, device="xpu")
try:
    dist.reduce(t, dst=0, op=op)
    print(f"rank {rank}: reduce PREMUL_SUM ok -> {t[0].item()}")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"rank {rank}: reduce PREMUL_SUM failed: {type(e).__name__}: {e}")
dist.destroy_process_group()
$ torchrun --nproc-per-node=2 premul_reduce_repro.py
rank 0: all_reduce PREMUL_SUM ok -> 4.0
rank 0: reduce PREMUL_SUM failed: ValueError: PreMulSum requires oneCCL>=2022.0
rank 1: all_reduce PREMUL_SUM ok -> 4.0
rank 1: reduce PREMUL_SUM failed: ValueError: PreMulSum requires oneCCL>=2022.0

Cause. In src/xccl/ProcessGroupXCCL.cpp, allreduce_impl, allreduce_coalesced and reduce_scatter call applyPreMulSumIfNeeded(input, opts.reduceOp), which scales the input by the factor and turns the op into SUM (the comment explains that native oneCCL premul is scale-up only, so it is always emulated). reduce (both the reduce and _reduce_oop paths, xccl::onecclReduce(input, output, comm, opts.reduceOp, root, stream)) passes opts.reduceOp straight through, so it reaches getXcclReduceOp in src/xccl/xccl.h, which throws when ENABLE_XCCL_PREMUL_SUM_SUPPORT is not defined at build time. The oneCCL>=2022.0 wording is misleading here because the runtime oneCCL is 2022.1.
Suggested fix. Apply applyPreMulSumIfNeeded in the reduce paths too, as for allreduce / reduce_scatter. #1571 ("Cannot use ReduceOp.PREMUL_SUM with XCCL") covered the other collectives but not reduce.
Test impact. In test/distributed/test_c10d_ops_nccl.py, ProcessGroupNCCLOpTest::test_reduce_op_premul_sum and the premul sub-case of ProcessGroupNCCLOpTest::test_reduce_ops fail on XPU with this error and are skipped there. This issue should only be closed once those skips are removed and both pass on XPU.
Versions
torch              2.15.0a0+git1285517 (source build)
torch-xpu-ops      5934d4f5
oneCCL             2022.1 (DLE 2026.1.2.25)
device             4x Intel(R) Data Center GPU Max 1100
backend            xccl

issues.title: ci/dpclang: GoogleFnet E2E performance drops 3-4.7x vs oneAPI (all dtypes, inference & training)
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

E2E performance of **GoogleFnet** (huggingface) drops sharply with the **dpclang** build compared to the **oneAPI** build: in every dtype/mode both inductor and eager are ~3–4.7x slower. Batch size is the same (16) on both sides.

Ratio = baseline latency / target latency (< 1 means dpclang is slower; drop threshold 0.90).

| Dtype | Mode | Inductor oneAPI (ms) | Inductor dpclang (ms) | Inductor ratio | Eager ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| amp_bf16 | inference | 68.45 | 303.90 | 0.274 | 0.225 |
| amp_bf16 | training | 203.40 | 829.55 | 0.302 | 0.245 |
| amp_fp16 | inference | 68.54 | 322.91 | 0.254 | 0.212 |
| amp_fp16 | training | 201.46 | 690.00 | 0.340 | 0.292 |
| bfloat16 | inference | 69.01 | 308.95 | 0.266 | 0.223 |
| bfloat16 | training | 201.98 | 721.45 | 0.337 | 0.280 |
| float16 | inference | 70.03 | 317.65 | 0.268 | 0.220 |
| float16 | training | 202.03 | 734.78 | 0.320 | 0.275 |
| float32 | inference | 68.60 | 294.74 | 0.276 | 0.233 |
| float32 | training | 202.80 | 719.29 | 0.343 | 0.282 |

GoogleFnet replaces attention with FFT. In the same dpclang run, most new UT failures are FFT related (`MKL FFT doesn't support tensors of type: Half`), so this may share the root cause of #5068 (dpclang build without MKL).

### Reproducer

```bash
python benchmarks/dynamo/huggingface.py -d xpu --performance --bfloat16 --inference \
    --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only GoogleFnet
```

### Versions

- Target (dpclang): Inductor-dpclang-ondemand-LTS2 run `38882733178`, commit `cde6c073db9ea641f76eb91bd93533cf969a62ba`
- Baseline (oneAPI): Inductor-build-ondemand-LTS2 run `39186464115`

issues.title: [upstream_ut] test_dynamic_shapes_2d_blocking_round_robin: combo-kernel count expectation is device dependent on XPU
issues.body:
Auto-added by fix-implement (allow_skip=true) while handling intel/torch-xpu-ops#5272.

Test: `test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py::ComboKernelDynamicShapesTests::test_dynamic_shapes_2d_blocking_round_robin`
Upstream disable issue: `pytorch/pytorch#201543` (Platforms: xpu, PVC CI job `linux-noble-xpu-n-py3.11`)

Original failure: `AssertionError: False is not true` from
`self.assertTrue(5 <= torch._inductor.metrics.generated_kernel_count <= 6)`.

Root cause: `generated_kernel_count` counts every `Kernel` object inductor
builds, including the throwaway ones built only to benchmark a combo kernel.
With `benchmark_combo_kernel=True` the expected 5 is "3 standalone subkernel
modules + 1 combo kernel benchmarked + 1 combo kernel emitted", so the range
`5..6` only holds while `Scheduler.speedup_by_combo_kernel` *accepts* the
fusion. On the PVC CI device it rejects (the combo is not measured as
profitable for these tiny tensors, and any register spill scores the combo as
`inf`), the three adds are emitted standalone, and the count becomes 7.
Forcing that verdict on BMG reproduces 7 exactly. Numerics pass in all cases.
The sibling XPU failure `pytorch/pytorch#194896`
(`ComboKernelBenchmarkTests::test_round_robin_dispatch`, "Expected 6 but got
9", 4 subkernels) is the same arithmetic.

Reason for skip: the test hard-codes the CUDA benchmark outcome, so there is no
XPU-side product bug to fix. Two follow-ups need a human:

1. Decide whether these combo-kernel tests should assert emitted kernels (e.g.
   `len(code)` from `run_and_get_kernels`, which `ComboKernelTests` already
   uses) instead of `generated_kernel_count`, which is inflated by probe
   codegen -- that would make the expectation device-independent and let XPU
   run the test again.
2. Check whether the combo-kernel benchmark gate is unfairly strict on XPU:
   the combo path rejects on `n_spills > 0`
   (`torch/_inductor/codegen/triton.py:9447`) while the standalone path
   tolerates `n_spills > 8` (`triton.py:9240`, commented "n_spills ...
   sometimes it can be inaccurate"). Needs a PVC runner to evaluate; the combo
   kernel does not spill on BMG.

Base analyzed: pytorch@f54c229e83

nodes.body:
Automated fix session for this issue, triggered by `@torchxpubot fix --on pvc`. Runner: `xpu-agent-pvc` (PVC, Intel Data Center GPU Max). This comment is updated in place as each stage completes.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | pytorch | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | Reproducer named in the body: `test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py::ComboKernelDynamicShapesTests::test_dynamic_shapes_2d_blocking_round_robin`. The issue points at pytorch code (`test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py`, `torch/_inductor/codegen/triton.py`), so scope is `pytorch`. The two follow-ups it records both need a PVC machine, which this run has. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce Runner `xpu-agent-pvc`, Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100 (PVC), compute-runtime `26.31.39395.16`, IGC `2.40.16`. Nightly wheels `2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu` and `2.16.0.dev20261020+xpu` (the nightly closest to the CI failure on 2026-10-20); both ship `triton-xpu 3.9.0+gitb6f7ac74`, the same commit pytorch CI pins in `.ci/docker/ci_commit_pins/triton-xpu.txt`, so triton codegen here is identical to CI's. | Test case | Verdict | Observed | |---|---|---| | `test_dynamic_shapes_2d_blocking_round_robin` | NOT_REPRODUCED | passes; `generated_kernel_count` = 5 (assertion allows 5..6), 1 kernel emitted | | `test_round_robin_dispatch` (sibling, `pytorch/pytorch#194896`) | NOT_REPRODUCED | passes | The test passed under every variation that could plausibly differ from CI: the single node id, the whole `ComboKernelDynamicShapesTests` class, and the whole `test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py` file as the CI shard runs it (179 passed, 25 skipped, 0 failed); with a cold per-run inductor cache and with one cache shared across the whole file; on two different cards; on an idle GPU and on a GPU saturated by three concurrent 8192x8192 matmul loops. `generated_kernel_count` was 5 in all 10 measurements, never 6 and never 7. What is *not* aligned, and cannot be from this runner: the GPU driver / IGC stack. pytorch's CI image installs the rolling `repositories.intel.com/gpu` unified driver at image-build time, while this container carries the `kobuk-team/intel-graphics` PPA build above. Register allocation (and therefore `n_spills`) is decided by IGC, so that is the one deciding variable left unmatched. Neither a pytorch source build nor installing the CI torch wheel would change it, so neither was run. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause Analyzed at pytorch `origin/main@3afdbd3b95`. `generated_kernel_count` for this test is fully determined by one boolean: whether `Scheduler.speedup_by_combo_kernel` (`torch/_inductor/scheduler.py:12850`) accepts the fusion. Accounting: 3 standalone subkernel probes (`compile_kernel`) + 1 combo probe (`benchmark_combo_kernel`) + 1 emitted combo kernel = 5 when accepted. The assertion `5 <= count <= 6` therefore encodes "the combo kernel was formed", via a counter that also counts throwaway probe codegen. There are two rejection paths, and they do not produce the same count. Both were exercised directly on PVC by forcing each one: - A **subkernel** scoring `inf` in `benchmark_codegened_module` (`triton.py:9240`, `n_spills > 8`, or a swallowed probe compile/launch exception) returns `False` early, before the combo probe: 3 probes + 3 standalone kernels = **6**, which still satisfies the assertion. Forced on PVC: count 6, 3 kernels emitted, test still passes. - The **final timing comparison** `ms2 - ms2_clone < ms1 or small_kernel` runs after the combo probe, so rejecting there gives 3 + 1 + 3 = **7** -- the failing count recorded on this issue. So the CI failure can only have come from the timing comparison, with `small_kernel` false -- i.e. the three 20x30..40x32 adds measuring >= 0.3 ms in total *and* the combo kernel measuring no faster than their sum. That is a pure wall-clock verdict on the CI machine, not a codegen difference. On PVC the combo is accepted with a measured 2.8-6.5x speedup and zero register spills anywhere, including under heavy GPU contention. This also settles the two follow-ups the issue recorded, both in the negative: 1. Asserting emitted kernels instead of `generated_kernel_count` would **not** make the expectation device-independent. Emitted kernels are 1 when the combo is accepted and 3 when it is rejected, so that assertion encodes exactly the same device-dependent verdict; it only renumbers it. 2. The `n_spills > 0` gate in `benchmark_combo_kernel` (`triton.py:9447`) is **inert for this test** and is not unfairly strict. It sets `ms = ms_clone = inf`, after which `small_kernel = (inf - inf < 0.3) or (ms1 < 0.3)` is true via its second term for tensors this small, so the fusion is accepted anyway. Forced on PVC: count 5, combo still formed. The only spill threshold that can actually reject is the subkernel one, which is `> 8` -- the same value the regular fusion path uses. No gate change is warranted. No change is proposed. A test whose expectation is a benchmark outcome cannot be made device-independent without changing what it asserts (dropping the perf gate for this test, or widening the range to 7, which makes the assertion vacuous since 7 *is* "nothing was combined"). That is a test-design decision for the inductor owners, and on current evidence the test passes on PVC, so the more useful next step is to re-enable it upstream and see whether it still fails. - **Verdict:** NEEDS_HUMAN -- does not reproduce on PVC; both recorded follow-ups resolve to "no change", leaving a judgement call on the upstream disable - **Target repo:** N/A - **Domain:** inductor / torch.compile (pytorch) *Automated by fix-root-cause.*
Summary **Outcome:** NEEDS_HUMAN(no_longer_reproduces_on_pvc) -- no patch produced. On a PVC runner the test passes in every configuration tried (10 measurements, `generated_kernel_count` = 5 every time, zero register spills, combo kernel accepted at a measured 2.8-6.5x speedup), including under heavy GPU contention and on the nightly closest to the original CI failure, with the exact triton commit pytorch CI pins. Working out the kernel-count arithmetic on hardware shows the count is 5 when the combo kernel is accepted, 6 when a subkernel probe scores `inf` (which still satisfies the asserted 5..6), and 7 only when `speedup_by_combo_kernel` rejects at its final wall-clock comparison -- so the CI failure was a timing verdict on that machine, not a codegen or register-spill difference. That also answers both follow-ups this issue recorded, in the negative: the `n_spills > 0` gate is inert for a kernel this small (the `small_kernel` escape accepts it anyway), and asserting emitted kernels instead of `generated_kernel_count` would carry the same device dependence (1 kernel when accepted, 3 when rejected). The only variable this runner cannot match is the CI image's GPU driver / IGC build, and neither a pytorch source build nor the CI torch wheel would change it. Two decisions are left for a human: whether to lift the upstream disable `pytorch/pytorch#201543` (and its sibling `pytorch/pytorch#194896`) now that both tests pass on PVC, and whether inductor owners want these combo-kernel tests to stop asserting a benchmark outcome at all -- there is no test-side change that keeps the assertion meaningful *and* device-independent, since widening the range to 7 would accept "nothing was combined". - **Branch:** none -- no code change was made, so nothing was committed and no patch artifact is produced for this run. - **Base:** `3afdbd3b95ecc89f9113968991569dd7412a2a79` (pytorch `origin/main`) - **Changed files:** none - **Nothing was pushed.**

Reproducer named in the body:
test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py::ComboKernelDynamicShapesTests::test_dynamic_shapes_2d_blocking_round_robin.
The issue points at pytorch code (test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py,
torch/_inductor/codegen/triton.py), so scope is pytorch. The two follow-ups
it records both need a PVC machine, which this run has.
Automated by issue-triage.



Reproduce
Runner xpu-agent-pvc, Intel Data Center GPU Max 1100 (PVC), compute-runtime
26.31.39395.16, IGC 2.40.16. Nightly wheels 2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu and
2.16.0.dev20261020+xpu (the nightly closest to the CI failure on 2026-10-20);
both ship triton-xpu 3.9.0+gitb6f7ac74, the same commit pytorch CI pins in
.ci/docker/ci_commit_pins/triton-xpu.txt, so triton codegen here is identical
to CI's.



Test case
Verdict
Observed




test_dynamic_shapes_2d_blocking_round_robin
NOT_REPRODUCED
passes; generated_kernel_count = 5 (assertion allows 5..6), 1 kernel emitted


test_round_robin_dispatch (sibling, pytorch/pytorch#194896)
NOT_REPRODUCED
passes



The test passed under every variation that could plausibly differ from CI: the
single node id, the whole ComboKernelDynamicShapesTests class, and the whole
test/inductor/test_combo_kernels.py file as the CI shard runs it (179 passed,
25 skipped, 0 failed); with a cold per-run inductor cache and with one cache
shared across the whole file; on two different cards; on an idle GPU and on a
GPU saturated by three concurrent 8192x8192 matmul loops. generated_kernel_count
was 5 in all 10 measurements, never 6 and never 7.
What is not aligned, and cannot be from this runner: the GPU driver / IGC
stack. pytorch's CI image installs the rolling repositories.intel.com/gpu
unified driver at image-build time, while this container carries the
kobuk-team/intel-graphics PPA build above. Register allocation (and therefore
n_spills) is decided by IGC, so that is the one deciding variable left
unmatched. Neither a pytorch source build nor installing the CI torch wheel
would change it, so neither was run.
Automated by fix-reproduce.



Root Cause
Analyzed at pytorch origin/main@3afdbd3b95.
generated_kernel_count for this test is fully determined by one boolean:
whether Scheduler.speedup_by_combo_kernel (torch/_inductor/scheduler.py:12850)
accepts the fusion. Accounting: 3 standalone subkernel probes (compile_kernel)

1 combo probe (benchmark_combo_kernel) + 1 emitted combo kernel = 5 when
accepted. The assertion 5 <= count <= 6 therefore encodes "the combo kernel was
formed", via a counter that also counts throwaway probe codegen.

There are two rejection paths, and they do not produce the same count. Both were
exercised directly on PVC by forcing each one:

A subkernel scoring inf in benchmark_codegened_module (triton.py:9240,
n_spills > 8, or a swallowed probe compile/launch exception) returns False
early, before the combo probe: 3 probes + 3 standalone kernels = 6, which
still satisfies the assertion. Forced on PVC: count 6, 3 kernels emitted, test
still passes.
The final timing comparison ms2 - ms2_clone < ms1 or small_kernel runs
after the combo probe, so rejecting there gives 3 + 1 + 3 = 7 -- the
failing count recorded on this issue.

So the CI failure can only have come from the timing comparison, with
small_kernel false -- i.e. the three 20x30..40x32 adds measuring >= 0.3 ms in
total and the combo kernel measuring no faster than their sum. That is a pure
wall-clock verdict on the CI machine, not a codegen difference. On PVC the combo
is accepted with a measured 2.8-6.5x speedup and zero register spills anywhere,
including under heavy GPU contention.
This also settles the two follow-ups the issue recorded, both in the negative:

Asserting emitted kernels instead of generated_kernel_count would not
make the expectation device-independent. Emitted kernels are 1 when the combo
is accepted and 3 when it is rejected, so that assertion encodes exactly the
same device-dependent verdict; it only renumbers it.
The n_spills > 0 gate in benchmark_combo_kernel (triton.py:9447) is
inert for this test and is not unfairly strict. It sets
ms = ms_clone = inf, after which small_kernel = (inf - inf < 0.3) or (ms1 < 0.3) is true via its second term for tensors this small, so the
fusion is accepted anyway. Forced on PVC: count 5, combo still formed. The
only spill threshold that can actually reject is the subkernel one, which is
> 8 -- the same value the regular fusion path uses. No gate change is
warranted.

No change is proposed. A test whose expectation is a benchmark outcome cannot be
made device-independent without changing what it asserts (dropping the perf gate
for this test, or widening the range to 7, which makes the assertion vacuous
since 7 is "nothing was combined"). That is a test-design decision for the
inductor owners, and on current evidence the test passes on PVC, so the more
useful next step is to re-enable it upstream and see whether it still fails.

Verdict: NEEDS_HUMAN -- does not reproduce on PVC; both recorded follow-ups
resolve to "no change", leaving a judgement call on the upstream disable
Target repo: N/A
Domain: inductor / torch.compile (pytorch)

Outcome: NEEDS_HUMAN(no_longer_reproduces_on_pvc) -- no patch produced.
On a PVC runner the test passes in every configuration tried (10 measurements,

accepted at a measured 2.8-6.5x speedup), including under heavy GPU contention
and on the nightly closest to the original CI failure, with the exact triton

the count is 5 when the combo kernel is accepted, 6 when a subkernel probe scores

failure was a timing verdict on that machine, not a codegen or register-spill
difference. That also answers both follow-ups this issue recorded, in the
negative: the n_spills > 0 gate is inert for a kernel this small (the

accepted, 3 when rejected). The only variable this runner cannot match is the CI

### 🐛 Describe the bug with skip template

### Summary

Backward of nn.functional.conv3d with padding='same' produces float32 gradients that miss the test tolerance: greatest absolute difference 9.1552734375e-05 against 1e-05 allowed, on one element of ten, for sample input 8. test_grad, test_vjp and test_jvpvjp of the same OpInfo fail on the same sample with the same mismatch, so a single change in conv3d backward numerics accounts for all three. The chunked path of nn.functional.linear_cross_entropy (_linear_cross_entropy_batch_chunked_no_reduction) calls an autograd.Function that does not override the setup_context staticmethod, so any functorch transform over it raises before a single XPU kernel runs. Summary

The OpInfo is absent from the baseline, so these are first-run failures.

### 🐛 Describe the bug with skip template
