<!-- cases:end -->

### Summary

Under vmap, the backward of chunked nn.functional.linear_cross_entropy accumulates gradients with inplace arithmetic whose `other` operand is batched while `self` is not, so vmap refuses the operation. Both dtypes of test_vmap_autograd_grad over the new nn_functional_linear_cross_entropy_chunked OpInfo fail this way at sample input 0. Same new op as the related issue but a distinct failure path: this one gets past the setup_context check and dies in the chunk loop, so the two are listed apart.

### ErrorLog

#### RuntimeError: vmap: inplace arithmetic(self, *extra_args) is not possible because there exists a Tensor `other` in extra_args that has more elements than `self`. This happened due to `other` being vmapped over but `self` not being vmapped over in a vmap. Please try to use out-of-place operators instead of inplace arithmetic. If said operator is being called inside the PyTorch framework, please file a bug report instead. ; Exception: vmap: inplace arithmetic(self, *extra_args) is not possible because there exists a Tensor `other` in extra_args that has more elements than `self`. Summary
Under vmap, the backward of chunked nn.functional.linear_cross_entropy accumulates gradients with inplace arithmetic whose other operand is batched while self is not, so vmap refuses the operation. Both dtypes of test_vmap_autograd_grad over the new nn_functional_linear_cross_entropy_chunked OpInfo fail this way at sample input 0. Same new op as the related issue but a distinct failure path: this one gets past the setup_context check and dies in the chunk loop, so the two are listed apart.

issues.title: [Bug Skip]: [New Case] aten::_upsample_nearest_exact1d has no vmap batching rule, failing the interpolate nearest-exact has_batch_rule tests
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug with skip template

<!-- cases:begin -->
Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_ops_xpu.TestOperatorsXPU,test_vmapjvpall_has_batch_rule_nn_functional_interpolate_nearest-exact_xpu_float32
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.functorch.test_ops_xpu.TestOperatorsXPU,test_vmapvjp_has_batch_rule_nn_functional_interpolate_nearest-exact_xpu_float32

<!-- cases:end -->

### Summary

nn.functional.interpolate with mode='nearest-exact' on a 3D input dispatches to aten::_upsample_nearest_exact1d, for which no batching rule is registered, so the two has_batch_rule tests - which run with the vmap fallback disabled - fail at sample input 0 with the same error. Both are first-run failures for this OpInfo variant, which the baseline does not contain.

### ErrorLog

issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug with skip template

<!-- cases:begin -->
Cases:
~~op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.test_fx_xpu.TestFX,test_wrapped_trace_while_already_patched~~

<!-- cases:end -->

### Summary

TestFX.setUp calls find_library_location('libtorchbind_test.so'), which the XPU test environment does not ship, so the case errors before any test body runs. This is an unmet test prerequisite rather than an XPU kernel problem, and the case is absent from the baseline, so this is its first run here. It needs the library made available or the case excluded.

### ErrorLog

#### FileNotFoundError: Could not find library 'libtorchbind_test.so' in installed or build paths

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/__w/torch-xpu-ops/torch-xpu-ops/pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/../../../../test/test_fx.py", line 288, in setUp
    lib_file_path = find_library_location("libtorchbind_test.so")
                    ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
  File "/__w/torch-xpu-ops/torch-xpu-ops/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py", line 6134, in find_library_location
    raise FileNotFoundError(f"Could not find library '{lib_name}' in installed or build paths")
FileNotFoundError: Could not find library 'libtorchbind_test.so' in installed or build paths
```

### Reproduce

```bash
cd pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu
pytest -sv test_fx_xpu.py::TestFX::test_wrapped_trace_while_already_patched
```

Summary

issues.title: [Bug Skip]: [Regression] Quantized threshold returns a wrong element for threshold=0.0 on XPU
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug with skip template

<!-- cases:begin -->
Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.quantization.core.test_quantized_op_xpu.TestQuantizedOpsXPU,test_qthreshold_xpu

<!-- cases:end -->

### Summary

test_qthreshold_xpu fails on the hypothesis example X=[0., -1.] (quint8, scale 1/255, zero_point 255) with threshold=0.0 and value=-1.0: one of the two elements differs from the reference by a full 1.0, so the XPU quantized threshold takes the wrong branch for one of those inputs rather than merely rounding differently. The case passed in the baseline. The example is hypothesis-generated, so the exact falsifying input may differ between runs.

### ErrorLog

#### AssertionError: Quantized tensor-likes are not close!

```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/__w/torch-xpu-ops/torch-xpu-ops/pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/../../../../test/quantization/core/test_quantized_op.py", line 897, in test_qthreshold
    elements=hu.floats(-1e3, 1e3, allow_nan=False, allow_infinity=False),
    ^^^^^^^
  File "/__w/torch-xpu-ops/torch-xpu-ops/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/hypothesis/core.py", line 1267, in wrapped_test
    raise the_error_hypothesis_found
  File "/__w/torch-xpu-ops/torch-xpu-ops/pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/../../../../test/quantization/core/test_quantized_op.py", line 922, in test_qthreshold
    self.assertEqual(qY, qY_hat, msg=lambda msg: f"{msg}\n{name} qthreshold failed")
  File "/__w/torch-xpu-ops/torch-xpu-ops/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py", line 5097, in assertEqual
    raise error_metas.pop()[0].to_error(  # type: ignore[index]
AssertionError: Quantized tensor-likes are not close!

Mismatched elements: 1 / 2 (50.0%)
Greatest absolute difference: 1.0 at index (0,) (up to 1e-05 allowed)
Greatest relative difference: 1.0 at index (0,) (up to 1.3e-06 allowed)
native qthreshold failed

To execute this test, run the following from the base repo dir:
    PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 python ../../test/quantization/core/test_quantized_op.py TestQuantizedOpsXPU.test_qthreshold_xpu

This message can be suppressed by setting PYTORCH_PRINT_REPRO_ON_FAILURE=0
Falsifying example: test_qthreshold(
    X=(array([ 0., -1.], dtype=float32),
     (0.00392156862745098, 255, torch.quint8)),
    threshold=0.0,
    value=-1.0,
    self=<test_quantized_op.TestQuantizedOpsXPU testMethod=test_qthreshold_xpu>,
)

You can reproduce this example by temporarily adding @reproduce_failure('6.56.4', b'AXicY2RkQAGMaHwGRjQaTRQAAV4ACQ==') as a decorator on your test case
```

cd pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu

🐛 Describe the bug with skip template

Cases:
op_ut,third_party.torch-xpu-ops.test.xpu.quantization.core.test_quantized_op_xpu.TestQuantizedOpsXPU,test_qthreshold_xpu

Summary
test_qthreshold_xpu fails on the hypothesis example X=[0., -1.] (quint8, scale 1/255, zero_point 255) with threshold=0.0 and value=-1.0: one of the two elements differs from the reference by a full 1.0, so the XPU quantized threshold takes the wrong branch for one of those inputs rather than merely rounding differently. The case passed in the baseline. The example is hypothesis-generated, so the exact falsifying input may differ between runs.
ErrorLog
AssertionError: Quantized tensor-likes are not close!
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/__w/torch-xpu-ops/torch-xpu-ops/pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/../../../../test/quantization/core/test_quantized_op.py", line 897, in test_qthreshold
    elements=hu.floats(-1e3, 1e3, allow_nan=False, allow_infinity=False),
    ^^^^^^^
  File "/__w/torch-xpu-ops/torch-xpu-ops/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/hypothesis/core.py", line 1267, in wrapped_test
    raise the_error_hypothesis_found
  File "/__w/torch-xpu-ops/torch-xpu-ops/pytorch/third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/../../../../test/quantization/core/test_quantized_op.py", line 922, in test_qthreshold
    self.assertEqual(qY, qY_hat, msg=lambda msg: f"{msg}\n{name} qthreshold failed")
  File "/__w/torch-xpu-ops/torch-xpu-ops/.venv/lib/python3.12/site-packages/torch/testing/_internal/common_utils.py", line 5097, in assertEqual
    raise error_metas.pop()[0].to_error(  # type: ignore[index]
AssertionError: Quantized tensor-likes are not close!

Mismatched elements: 1 / 2 (50.0%)
Greatest absolute difference: 1.0 at index (0,) (up to 1e-05 allowed)
Greatest relative difference: 1.0 at index (0,) (up to 1.3e-06 allowed)
native qthreshold failed

To execute this test, run the following from the base repo dir:
    PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 python ../../test/quantization/core/test_quantized_op.py TestQuantizedOpsXPU.test_qthreshold_xpu

This message can be suppressed by setting PYTORCH_PRINT_REPRO_ON_FAILURE=0
Falsifying example: test_qthreshold(
    X=(array([ 0., -1.], dtype=float32),
     (0.00392156862745098, 255, torch.quint8)),
    threshold=0.0,
    value=-1.0,
    self=<test_quantized_op.TestQuantizedOpsXPU testMethod=test_qthreshold_xpu>,
)

You can reproduce this example by temporarily adding @reproduce_failure('6.56.4', b'AXicY2RkQAGMaHwGRjQaTRQAAV4ACQ==') as a decorator on your test case

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-10-21] XPU segment_reduce max/min backward gives a negative tied gradient to every tied element instead of splitting it
issues.body:
<!-- alignment-published-unit: issue-201633 -->
## Summary

The backward of `torch.segment_reduce` / `torch._segment_reduce` with `reduce="max"` or `reduce="min"` on XPU splits the incoming gradient between the elements tied at the segment extremum only when that gradient is positive. For a negative gradient every tied element receives the full gradient, so the segment's input gradients sum to `k * grad_output` instead of `grad_output`. XPU `amax` / `amin` backward splits evenly for both signs.

The error is silent, sign-dependent and therefore biased (it does not average out over training steps). `gradcheck` does not see it, because random inputs have no ties, and the existing tests only call `.sum().backward()`, i.e. use a positive incoming gradient.

## Upstream source

- pytorch/pytorch#201633 (open, filed 2026-10-21) reports the same defect for the CPU and CUDA kernels.
- Found by an XPU alignment scan of the window `[2026-10-21T00:00:00Z, 2026-10-22T00:00:00Z)` over `pytorch/pytorch`, frozen default-branch head `37f56e48ce431907080585a595c437f9edb23411`.

## Observed XPU behavior

Validated on XPU with `torch 2.16.0.dev20261021+xpu`:

```
case reduce=max grad_out=+1.0 tied=2 grad=[0.5, 0.5, 0.0] grad_sum=+1.000000 amax_amin_grad=[0.5, 0.5, 0.0] amax_amin_sum=+1.000000 matches_reference=True
case reduce=max grad_out=-1.0 tied=2 grad=[-1.0, -1.0, 0.0] grad_sum=-2.000000 amax_amin_grad=[-0.5, -0.5, -0.0] amax_amin_sum=-1.000000 matches_reference=False
case reduce=min grad_out=+1.0 tied=2 grad=[0.5, 0.5, 0.0] grad_sum=+1.000000 amax_amin_grad=[0.5, 0.5, 0.0] amax_amin_sum=+1.000000 matches_reference=True
case reduce=min grad_out=-1.0 tied=2 grad=[-1.0, -1.0, 0.0] grad_sum=-2.000000 amax_amin_grad=[-0.5, -0.5, -0.0] amax_amin_sum=-1.000000 matches_reference=False
```

Expected for `grad_out=-1`: `[-0.5, -0.5, 0.0]`, as for `amax` / `amin`. The positive-gradient rows already split evenly in the same kernel, so the kernel is inconsistent with itself as well as with `amax` / `amin`.

## Target path and root cause

`segment_reduce_backward_kernel` in `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/SegmentReduceKernels.cpp` (line 290). In the `MAX`/`MIN` branch (line 338) the first loop selects the tied elements with `isnan(values_data[data_index]) || values_data[data_index] == output_data[output_index]` and counts them, and the second loop then divides by that count:

```cpp
// src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/SegmentReduceKernels.cpp:359
if (grad_input_data[data_index] > 0) {
  grad_input_data[data_index] = grad_input_data[data_index] / counter;
}
```

The division loop gates on the sign of the value it just wrote instead of re-using the tie predicate, so only positive gradients are divided. The fix is to select the tied elements in the division loop with the same predicate used in the assignment loop.

This kernel backs both `_segment_reduce_lengths_backward_kernel` (line 554) and `_segment_reduce_offsets_backward_kernel` (line 573), so lengths- and offsets-based calls are both affected.

Target-path evidence: `aten::_segment_reduce_backward` has an XPU kernel registered (`dispatch_segment_reduce_backward_xpu True`), and both the forward output and the accumulated `.grad` are `xpu` tensors. The `amax` / `amin` reference was computed from the same XPU inputs on the same device, so the discrepancy is between two XPU paths and is not a host/device comparison artifact.

## Reproducer

```python
import torch

for reduce, vals in (("max", [2.0, 2.0, 1.0]), ("min", [1.0, 1.0, 2.0])):
    for g in (1.0, -1.0):
        data = torch.tensor(vals, device="xpu", requires_grad=True)
        out = torch.segment_reduce(data, reduce, lengths=torch.tensor([3], device="xpu"))
        out.backward(torch.tensor([g], device="xpu"))

        ref = torch.tensor(vals, device="xpu", requires_grad=True)
        (ref.amax() if reduce == "max" else ref.amin()).backward(torch.tensor(g, device="xpu"))

        print(f"{reduce} grad_out={g:+.0f}  segment_reduce: {data.grad.tolist()} "
              f"(sum {data.grad.sum().item():+.1f})   "
              f"{'amax' if reduce == 'max' else 'amin'}: {ref.grad.tolist()}")
```

## Environment

```
torch 2.16.0.dev20261021+xpu
python 3.13.13
device Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
```

## Ownership

The XPU kernel carries its own copy of the gate. The same `grad_input_data[data_index] > 0` gate is present upstream in `aten/src/ATen/native/SegmentReduce.cpp:271` and `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/SegmentReduce.cu:222` at the scanned head, so an upstream fix to the CPU and CUDA kernels will not change `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/SegmentReduceKernels.cpp`; the XPU change is independent work in this repository.

Current stage of the related upstream fix: pytorch/pytorch#201633 is open and the reporter states they have a fix and will open a PR; no fix PR is linked to the issue as of this scan, so the upstream change is **proposed, not landed**. The XPU fix should adopt the same tie predicate so XPU matches the CPU/CUDA convention once that PR lands.

Summary
The backward of torch.segment_reduce / torch._segment_reduce with reduce="max" or reduce="min" on XPU splits the incoming gradient between the elements tied at the segment extremum only when that gradient is positive. For a negative gradient every tied element receives the full gradient, so the segment's input gradients sum to k * grad_output instead of grad_output. XPU amax / amin backward splits evenly for both signs.
The error is silent, sign-dependent and therefore biased (it does not average out over training steps). gradcheck does not see it, because random inputs have no ties, and the existing tests only call .sum().backward(), i.e. use a positive incoming gradient.
Upstream source

pytorch/pytorch#201633 (open, filed 2026-10-21) reports the same defect for the CPU and CUDA kernels.
Found by an XPU alignment scan of the window [2026-10-21T00:00:00Z, 2026-10-22T00:00:00Z) over pytorch/pytorch, frozen default-branch head 37f56e48ce431907080585a595c437f9edb23411.

Observed XPU behavior
Validated on XPU with torch 2.16.0.dev20261021+xpu:
case reduce=max grad_out=+1.0 tied=2 grad=[0.5, 0.5, 0.0] grad_sum=+1.000000 amax_amin_grad=[0.5, 0.5, 0.0] amax_amin_sum=+1.000000 matches_reference=True
case reduce=max grad_out=-1.0 tied=2 grad=[-1.0, -1.0, 0.0] grad_sum=-2.000000 amax_amin_grad=[-0.5, -0.5, -0.0] amax_amin_sum=-1.000000 matches_reference=False
case reduce=min grad_out=+1.0 tied=2 grad=[0.5, 0.5, 0.0] grad_sum=+1.000000 amax_amin_grad=[0.5, 0.5, 0.0] amax_amin_sum=+1.000000 matches_reference=True
case reduce=min grad_out=-1.0 tied=2 grad=[-1.0, -1.0, 0.0] grad_sum=-2.000000 amax_amin_grad=[-0.5, -0.5, -0.0] amax_amin_sum=-1.000000 matches_reference=False

Expected for grad_out=-1: [-0.5, -0.5, 0.0], as for amax / amin. The positive-gradient rows already split evenly in the same kernel, so the kernel is inconsistent with itself as well as with amax / amin.
Target path and root cause
segment_reduce_backward_kernel in src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/SegmentReduceKernels.cpp (line 290). In the MAX/MIN branch (line 338) the first loop selects the tied elements with isnan(values_data[data_index]) || values_data[data_index] == output_data[output_index] and counts them, and the second loop then divides by that count:
// src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/SegmentReduceKernels.cpp:359
if (grad_input_data[data_index] > 0) {
  grad_input_data[data_index] = grad_input_data[data_index] / counter;
}
The division loop gates on the sign of the value it just wrote instead of re-using the tie predicate, so only positive gradients are divided. The fix is to select the tied elements in the division loop with the same predicate used in the assignment loop.
This kernel backs both _segment_reduce_lengths_backward_kernel (line 554) and _segment_reduce_offsets_backward_kernel (line 573), so lengths- and offsets-based calls are both affected.
Target-path evidence: aten::_segment_reduce_backward has an XPU kernel registered (dispatch_segment_reduce_backward_xpu True), and both the forward output and the accumulated .grad are xpu tensors. The amax / amin reference was computed from the same XPU inputs on the same device, so the discrepancy is between two XPU paths and is not a host/device comparison artifact.
Reproducer
import torch

for reduce, vals in (("max", [2.0, 2.0, 1.0]), ("min", [1.0, 1.0, 2.0])):
    for g in (1.0, -1.0):
        data = torch.tensor(vals, device="xpu", requires_grad=True)
        out = torch.segment_reduce(data, reduce, lengths=torch.tensor([3], device="xpu"))
        out.backward(torch.tensor([g], device="xpu"))

        ref = torch.tensor(vals, device="xpu", requires_grad=True)
        (ref.amax() if reduce == "max" else ref.amin()).backward(torch.tensor(g, device="xpu"))

        print(f"{reduce} grad_out={g:+.0f}  segment_reduce: {data.grad.tolist()} "
              f"(sum {data.grad.sum().item():+.1f})   "
              f"{'amax' if reduce == 'max' else 'amin'}: {ref.grad.tolist()}")
Environment
torch 2.16.0.dev20261021+xpu
python 3.13.13
device Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics

Ownership
The XPU kernel carries its own copy of the gate. The same grad_input_data[data_index] > 0 gate is present upstream in aten/src/ATen/native/SegmentReduce.cpp:271 and aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/SegmentReduce.cu:222 at the scanned head, so an upstream fix to the CPU and CUDA kernels will not change src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/SegmentReduceKernels.cpp; the XPU change is independent work in this repository.

+"""
+Regression test for segment_reduce max/min backward on tied segments (XPU).
+
+The backward kernel assigns the incoming gradient to every element tied at the
+segment extremum and then divides by the tie count. The division used to be
+gated on the written value being positive, so a negative gradient was handed in
+full to each of the k tied elements and the segment's input gradients summed to
+k * grad_output instead of grad_output (intel/torch-xpu-ops#5808).
+
+amax/amin backward splits evenly for both signs and is the reference here. The
+test stays XPU-only: the same gate is still present in the upstream CPU and
+CUDA kernels (pytorch/pytorch#201633), so a device-generic version would fail
+on CPU.
+"""
+
+import torch
+from torch.testing._internal.common_utils import (
+    instantiate_parametrized_tests,
+    parametrize,
+    run_tests,
+    TestCase,
+)
+
+# Segment 0 has three tied elements, segment 1 none, segment 2 two.
+_VALUES = [3.0, 3.0, 3.0, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 5.0]
+_LENGTHS = [3, 2, 2]
+
+
+def _amax_amin_reference_grad(reduce, grad_output):
+    """Per-segment amax/amin backward over the same XPU inputs."""
+    data = torch.tensor(_VALUES, device="xpu", requires_grad=True)
+    outputs = []
+    start = 0
+    for length in _LENGTHS:
+        segment = data[start : start + length]
+        outputs.append(segment.amax() if reduce == "max" else segment.amin())
+        start += length
+    torch.stack(outputs).backward(grad_output)
+    return data.grad
+
+
+@instantiate_parametrized_tests
+class TestSegmentReduceBackwardTies(TestCase):
+    @parametrize("reduce", ["max", "min"])
+    @parametrize("mode", ["lengths", "offsets"])
+    @parametrize("grad_sign", [1.0, -1.0])
+    def test_tied_gradient_is_split_for_both_signs(self, reduce, mode, grad_sign):
+        grad_output = grad_sign * torch.tensor([1.0, 2.0, 3.0], device="xpu")
+
+        data = torch.tensor(_VALUES, device="xpu", requires_grad=True)
+        if mode == "lengths":
+            segments = {"lengths": torch.tensor(_LENGTHS, device="xpu")}
+        else:
+            offsets = torch.tensor(_LENGTHS, device="xpu").cumsum(0)
+            segments = {"offsets": torch.cat([offsets.new_zeros(1), offsets])}
+        torch.segment_reduce(data, reduce, **segments).backward(grad_output)
+
+        self.assertEqual(data.grad, _amax_amin_reference_grad(reduce, grad_output))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    run_tests()

## 🐛 Describe the bug

The memory-efficient attention backend ops `aten::_efficient_attention_forward` and `aten::_efficient_attention_backward` are not implemented for the XPU backend. Automated fix session for this issue. Stages are appended below as they complete.
Issue Triage | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Issue type | single-bug | | Reproduction missing | no | | Scope | both | | Dependencies | (none) | | Handling | agent-fixable | All 30 listed tests trace to one gap: `aten::_efficient_attention_forward` / `aten::_efficient_attention_backward` have no XPU dispatch entry, and the upstream OpInfo carries `skipXPU`. *Automated by issue-triage.*
Reproduce | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Verdict | REPRODUCED | | Stage | nightly | | Base | `torch 2.16.0.dev20261028+xpu` (PVC) | **The reproducer in the issue body does not fail.** `select_sdp_backend_xpu` already maps `SDPBackend.EFFICIENT_ATTENTION` to the math backend on XPU, so the snippet only warns: ``` UserWarning: SDPA Memory Efficient Attention backend is not supported on XPU, falling back to math backend. ``` The gap is reachable only through the low-level op, which is what the 30 listed tests call. Refined reproducer: ```bash python -c " import torch q = torch.randn(1, 128, 8, 64, device='xpu', dtype=torch.float16) torch.ops.aten._efficient_attention_forward(q, q, q, None, None, None, None, None, 0.0, 0, False) " ``` ``` NotImplementedError: Could not run 'aten::_efficient_attention_forward' with arguments from the 'CPU' backend. ... 'aten::_efficient_attention_forward' is only available for these backends: [XPU, Meta, BackendSelect, ...] ``` Note the error names the *CPU* backend: `_efficient_attention_forward` is listed in `XPUFallback.cpp`'s CPU fallback table, but the op has no CPU kernel, so the fallback copies the tensors host-ward and then fails there. Two of the 30 test ids in the issue body do not exist: `test_schema_check.py` instantiates only `TestSchemaCheckModeOpInfoCPU` (no `allow_xpu=True`), so there is no `TestSchemaCheckModeOpInfoXPU`. The other 28 collect and are skipped. *Automated by fix-reproduce.*
Root Cause | Field | Value | |-------|-------| | Verdict | IMPLEMENTING | | Target repo | torch-xpu-ops + pytorch (two patches) | | Domain | transformers / SDPA | | Analyzed sha | `ee500dcf` (torch-xpu-ops), `421855c5` (pytorch main) | `aten::_efficient_attention_forward` / `_efficient_attention_backward` are registered for CUDA only in `native_functions.yaml`; there is no XPU entry and no XPU implementation. Three separate gates then keep the tests off XPU: 1. the missing dispatch entries (the functional gap), 2. `skipXPU` on the `torch.ops.aten._efficient_attention_forward` OpInfo, which is what skips the `test_ops` / `test_meta` / `test_decomp` / `test_testing` cases, 3. five `@skipIfXpu` decorators in `test/test_transformers.py`. A fourth, smaller one: the stale `"_efficient_attention_forward"` entry in `XPUFallback.cpp` and in `test/xpu/skip_list_common.py`. **Fix strategy.** The sibling op `_scaled_dot_product_efficient_attention` is already satisfied on XPU by a math fallback in the same file (`src/ATen/native/transformers/Attention.cpp`), so the low-level op gets the same treatment rather than a new fused kernel: evaluate the attention with ATen math ops in float32 while honouring the full op contract (BSHD layout, grouped query attention, custom causal masks, local windows, packed `cu_seqlens` sequences, per-batch `seqlen_k`, padded logsumexp, zeroed fully-masked rows, philox-replayable dropout). The backward re-runs that forward under autograd with the dropout mask replayed from the saved philox state, which is how the existing sibling backward works too. This is a correctness/coverage fallback, not a performance path; it does not change SDPA backend selection, so intel/torch-xpu-ops#4813 is untouched. *Automated by fix-root-cause.*

listed in XPUFallback.cpp's CPU fallback table, but the op has no CPU
kernel, so the fallback copies the tensors host-ward and then fails there.

aten::_efficient_attention_forward / _efficient_attention_backward are

issues.title: ci/dpclang: USE_SYCL_SPECTRAL E2E performance drops vs oneAPI after re-verification (10 configs, mostly eager)
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

E2E performance drops of the **dpclang** build with `USE_SYCL_SPECTRAL` compared to the **oneAPI** build. All 10 cases are **re-verified**: target and baseline were re-run back to back (47 configurations re-run; these 10 still drop).

- 9 cases are **eager-only** drops (inductor ratio 0.99–1.03, eager ratio 0.83–0.90), the same pattern as #5783 (dpclang without `USE_SYCL_SPECTRAL`).
- `basic_gnn_sage` float32 training drops on **both** inductor (0.691) and eager (0.681).

`USE_SYCL_SPECTRAL` fixes the GoogleFnet drop from #5782; those cases are not in this list.

Ratio = baseline latency / target latency (< 1 means dpclang is slower; drop threshold 0.90).

| Suite | Dtype | Mode | Model | Inductor ratio | Eager ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| torchbench | float32 | training | basic_gnn_sage | 0.691 | 0.681 |
| torchbench | amp_fp16 | inference | basic_gnn_gcn | 1.019 | 0.829 |
| torchbench | amp_bf16 | inference | basic_gnn_gcn | 0.996 | 0.833 |
| torchbench | bfloat16 | inference | pyhpc_isoneutral_mixing | 1.027 | 0.861 |
| torchbench | amp_bf16 | inference | timm_nfnet | 0.995 | 0.864 |
| torchbench | amp_bf16 | inference | hf_T5 | 1.006 | 0.869 |
| huggingface | amp_fp16 | inference | MobileBertForMaskedLM | 0.990 | 0.879 |
| torchbench | amp_fp16 | inference | hf_T5 | 1.000 | 0.887 |
| torchbench | amp_fp16 | inference | timm_nfnet | 1.002 | 0.889 |
| huggingface | amp_bf16 | inference | LayoutLMForMaskedLM | 1.030 | 0.896 |

### Reproducer

```bash
python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py -d xpu --performance --float32 --training --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only basic_gnn_sage
python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py -d xpu --performance --amp --amp-dtype float16 --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only basic_gnn_gcn
python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py -d xpu --performance --amp --amp-dtype bfloat16 --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only basic_gnn_gcn
python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py -d xpu --performance --bfloat16 --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only pyhpc_isoneutral_mixing
python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py -d xpu --performance --amp --amp-dtype bfloat16 --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only timm_nfnet
python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py -d xpu --performance --amp --amp-dtype bfloat16 --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only hf_T5
python benchmarks/dynamo/huggingface.py -d xpu --performance --amp --amp-dtype float16 --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only MobileBertForMaskedLM
python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py -d xpu --performance --amp --amp-dtype float16 --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only hf_T5
python benchmarks/dynamo/torchbench.py -d xpu --performance --amp --amp-dtype float16 --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only timm_nfnet
python benchmarks/dynamo/huggingface.py -d xpu --performance --amp --amp-dtype bfloat16 --inference --backend=inductor --cold-start-latency -n10 --disable-cudagraphs --only LayoutLMForMaskedLM
```

Environment setup: same as the CI E2E job (PyTorch + torch-xpu-ops wheel from the run below, `benchmarks/dynamo` synced from `torch-xpu-ops/.ci/benchmarks`; torchbench models need the `benchmark` repo installed).

### Versions

- Target (dpclang, USE_SYCL_SPECTRAL): run `39577406274`
- Baseline (oneAPI): Inductor-build-ondemand-LTS2 run `39186464115`

issues.body:
# [BMG] AOTInductor BMM tests crash pytest worker on setup (pass on PVC)

## Summary

On BMG (Battlemage), several `inductor/test_aot_inductor.py` BMM tests crash the
pytest worker during test setup. The same tests pass on PVC (Data Center GPU Max 1550).

Error signature (identical across cases, only the worker id and test name vary):

```
failed on setup with "worker 'gwNN' crashed while running
'test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::<Class>::<test>'"
```

## Affected tests (10 unique, AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu + AOTInductorTestDualWrapper)

- `inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu::test_bmm_large_batch_dynamic_xpu`
- `inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu::test_bmm_shared_a_not_offered_when_disabled_xpu`
- `inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu::test_bmm_shared_a_not_offered_without_broadcast_xpu`
- `inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu::test_bmm_shared_a_numerics_xpu`
- `inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu::test_bmm_shared_a_offered_when_eligible_xpu`
- `inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestDualWrapper::test_bmm_large_batch_dynamic_xpu`
- `inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestDualWrapper::test_bmm_shared_a_not_offered_when_disabled_xpu`
- `inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestDualWrapper::test_bmm_shared_a_not_offered_without_broadcast_xpu`
- `inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestDualWrapper::test_bmm_shared_a_numerics_xpu`
- `inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::AOTInductorTestDualWrapper::test_bmm_shared_a_offered_when_eligible_xpu`

## Platform

- Fails: BMG
- Passes: PVC (Intel Data Center GPU Max 1550)
- Source: 2026WW42 BMG-vs-PVC UT gap report

issues.title: _weight_int4pack_mm_xpu : expect A to be contiguous — fails at batch_size=1, works at batch_size=2
issues.body:
Reproducer (pure PyTorch, Intel XPU):


```python
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
from torchao.quantization import quantize_, Int4WeightOnlyConfig

assert torch.xpu.is_available()
dev = "xpu"
torch.manual_seed(0)

S, K, N = 4, 2048, 2048

lin = nn.Linear(K, N, bias=False).to(dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16).eval()
quantize_(lin, Int4WeightOnlyConfig(int4_packing_format="plain_int32"))

def make_activation(bs):
    return torch.randn(bs, K, S, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16).transpose(1, 2)

for bs in (1, 2):
    x = make_activation(bs)
    print(f"bs={bs}: x{tuple(x.shape)} contig={x.is_contiguous()}", end="  ->  ")
    try:
        with torch.no_grad():
            y = lin(x)
        torch.xpu.synchronize()
        print(f"OK  y{tuple(y.shape)}")
    except RuntimeError as e:
        print(f"ERROR: {e}")
```

Output (torch 2.15.0.dev20260920+xpu, Intel(R) Arc(TM) B390 GPU):

```
bs=1: x(1, 4, 2048) contig=False  ->  ERROR: _weight_int4pack_mm_xpu : expect A to be contiguous.
bs=2: x(2, 4, 2048) contig=False  ->  OK  y(2, 4, 2048)
```

issues.title: [PTL][WSL] float64 argmax/argmin (and max(dim).indices) return a wrong index on PTL-H; the max value is correct
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

On the PTL-H iGPU (`Intel(R) Graphics [0xb082]`), `torch.argmax` / `torch.argmin` and `torch.max(x, dim).indices` on a 1-D **float64** tensor can return the index of an element that is *not* the maximum (minimum). `x.max()` returns the correct value, so only the index half of the arg-reduction is wrong. float32 is correct for the same data, and the same build-equivalent run on B580 (`0xe20b`) is correct for every size.

Seen first in #4881 (cases 96-102) and still failing on pytorch main `e149fba4` + torch-xpu-ops `bbede152`.

**Minimal repro:**
```python
import torch
torch.manual_seed(0)
for n in (1024, 4096, 1048576):
    x = torch.randn(n, dtype=torch.float64)
    c, g = x.argmax().item(), x.to("xpu").argmax().item()
    print(n, "cpu", c, x[c].item(), "xpu", g, x[g].item())
# PTL-H:
# 1024    -> same index (OK)

On the PTL-H iGPU (Intel(R) Graphics [0xb082]), torch.argmax / torch.argmin and torch.max(x, dim).indices on a 1-D float64 tensor can return the index of an element that is not the maximum (minimum). x.max() returns the correct value, so only the index half of the arg-reduction is wrong. float32 is correct for the same data, and the same build-equivalent run on B580 (0xe20b) is correct for every size.
Seen first in #4881 (cases 96-102) and still failing on pytorch main e149fba4 + torch-xpu-ops bbede152.
Minimal repro:
import torch
torch.manual_seed(0)
for n in (1024, 4096, 1048576):
    x = torch.randn(n, dtype=torch.float64)
    c, g = x.argmax().item(), x.to("xpu").argmax().item()
    print(n, "cpu", c, x[c].item(), "xpu", g, x[g].item())

### 🐛 Describe the bug

`test_scaled_matmul_cuda_xpu.py::TestFP8MatmulXPU::test_passed_swizzle_arrays_xpu` (#4881 case 104) fails with `AssertionError: ValueError not raised`. The test passes MXFP8 inputs (`float8_e4m3fn` + `float8_e8m0fnu` block scales, K/32) without the required `swizzle_a` / `swizzle_b` and expects `ValueError: swizzle_a and swizzle_b must each have 1 value`. On XPU the call does not raise.

Upstream marks the test `@skipXPU` (`test/test_scaled_matmul_cuda.py:3038`), but torch-xpu-ops replaces `common_device_type.skipXPU` with its own `_skipXPU` (`test/xpu/xpu_test_utils.py:856` / `:1200`), so the case runs in the XPU suite. Needs a decision: either add the swizzle-argument check on the XPU `_scaled_mm` path, or skip the case in `skip_list_common.py` with a reason.

Fails the same way on PTL-H (pytorch main `e149fba4` + txo `bbede152`) and on B580 (pytorch `ff30875` + txo `4c5017a7`), so it is not PTL-specific.

Repro:
```
cd third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu
PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_SLOW=1 PYTORCH_ENABLE_XPU_FALLBACK=1 python -m pytest -v "test_scaled_matmul_cuda_xpu.py::TestFP8MatmulXPU::test_passed_swizzle_arrays_xpu"
```

Found while re-checking #4881. The other FP8 case from #4881, `test_float8_scale_result_xpu` (case 103), is already tracked in #4760 / #5771.

issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

`test_torch_xpu.py::TestTorchDeviceTypeXPU::test_cpp_warnings_have_python_context_xpu` (#4881 case 199) fails with `AssertionError: False is not true` at `test/xpu/test_torch_xpu.py:1170`, in the jitted part of the test.

`torch.jit.script` now emits a `FutureWarning` ("`torch.jit.script` is deprecated. Please switch to `torch.compile` or `torch.export`."). That warning becomes `w[0]` instead of the RangeFactories C++ warning, so the "Triggered internally at ...RangeFactories" regex does not match. Upstream `test/test_torch.py` (around line 933) already filters it:
```python
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=DeprecationWarning)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=FutureWarning)
```
The torch-xpu-ops copy of the test does not. The eager half of the test passes. The fix is test-only: sync the txo copy with upstream.

Verified:
```python
import torch, warnings
def f():
    out = torch.empty((5,)); torch.arange(0, 3, out=out); return out
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    torch.jit.script(f)()
print([x.category.__name__ for x in w])   # ['FutureWarning', 'UserWarning']
```

🐛 Describe the bug
test_torch_xpu.py::TestTorchDeviceTypeXPU::test_cpp_warnings_have_python_context_xpu (#4881 case 199) fails with AssertionError: False is not true at test/xpu/test_torch_xpu.py:1170, in the jitted part of the test.
torch.jit.script now emits a FutureWarning ("torch.jit.script is deprecated. Please switch to torch.compile or torch.export."). That warning becomes w[0] instead of the RangeFactories C++ warning, so the "Triggered internally at ...RangeFactories" regex does not match. Upstream test/test_torch.py (around line 933) already filters it:
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=DeprecationWarning)
warnings.filterwarnings("ignore", category=FutureWarning)
The torch-xpu-ops copy of the test does not. The eager half of the test passes. The fix is test-only: sync the txo copy with upstream.
Verified:
import torch, warnings
def f():
    out = torch.empty((5,)); torch.arange(0, 3, out=out); return out
with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
    torch.jit.script(f)()
print([x.category.__name__ for x in w])   # ['FutureWarning', 'UserWarning']
Same failure on PTL-H (main e149fba4 + txo bbede152) and B580 (ff30875 + 4c5017a7), so it is not PTL-specific.

cd third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu

issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

Found while re-checking #4881 on pytorch main
Collecting the torch-xpu-ops wrapper fails before any test runs:
```
ImportError while importing test module '.../third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/test_schema_check.py'.
E   ImportError: cannot import name 'TestSchemaCheck' from partially initialized module 'test_schema_check'
    (most likely due to a circular import) (.../test/xpu/test_schema_check.py)
no tests collected, 1 error
```
The wrapper does `from test_schema_check import TestSchemaCheck, TestSchemaCheckModeOpInfo` inside `XPUImportCtx` (line 21). Its own module name is also `test_schema_check`, so the import resolves to the half-initialized wrapper instead of upstream `test/test_schema_check.py`. The wrapper was last changed in c40ac307 (#4210, "Use upstream version of test_hub and test_schema_check"). It collected in the #4881 reporter run (nightly 2.14.0.dev20260803), so something on the pytorch side changed the import order since then. Not root-caused yet.

Two neighbouring wrappers fail to collect on the same main for a different reason. They already have issues:
- `test_dataloader_xpu.py`: `ImportError: cannot import name 'TestDataLoaderDeviceType'` (upstream #189250 renamed it to `TestDataLoaderDevice`). See #5120 (closed) and open PR #5514.
- `test_prims_xpu.py`: `ImportError: cannot import name 'TestPrims'` (upstream #194182). See #5146.

All three files are listed in `skip_list_common.py` with `None` (run without skips), so `run_test_with_skip.py` loses the whole file.

Repro (pytorch main `e149fba4`, txo main `bbede152`):
```
cd third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu
python -m pytest --collect-only -q test_schema_check.py

🐛 Describe the bug
Found while re-checking #4881 on pytorch main
Collecting the torch-xpu-ops wrapper fails before any test runs:
ImportError while importing test module '.../third_party/torch-xpu-ops/test/xpu/test_schema_check.py'.
E   ImportError: cannot import name 'TestSchemaCheck' from partially initialized module 'test_schema_check'
    (most likely due to a circular import) (.../test/xpu/test_schema_check.py)
no tests collected, 1 error

The wrapper does from test_schema_check import TestSchemaCheck, TestSchemaCheckModeOpInfo inside XPUImportCtx (line 21). Its own module name is also test_schema_check, so the import resolves to the half-initialized wrapper instead of upstream test/test_schema_check.py. The wrapper was last changed in c40ac30 (#4210, "Use upstream version of test_hub and test_schema_check"). It collected in the #4881 reporter run (nightly 2.14.0.dev20260803), so something on the pytorch side changed the import order since then. Not root-caused yet.
Two neighbouring wrappers fail to collect on the same main for a different reason. They already have issues:

test_dataloader_xpu.py: ImportError: cannot import name 'TestDataLoaderDeviceType' (upstream #189250 renamed it to TestDataLoaderDevice). See #5120 (closed) and open PR #5514.
test_prims_xpu.py: ImportError: cannot import name 'TestPrims' (upstream #194182). See #5146.

### Summary

The only new failure of the run: profiling with a scope (hardware-metrics) XPU activity list raises at profiler start, from XpuptiScopeProfilerApi::enableScopeProfiler with PTI error code 50 (PTI_ERROR_DRIVER), so no trace is collected. The test asserts only that the scope config is accepted, and its own docstring records that per-kernel metric values need ZET_ENABLE_METRICS=1 and sysctl dev.xe.observation_paranoid=0; neither is set anywhere in CI, so the driver has no permission to arm metrics collection. Fixing it means either accepting the config without a hard error when the driver cannot provide metrics, or guarding the test on metrics availability instead of TEST_XPU alone. The failure is confined to this one case in one file and the traceback ends inside the scope-profiler enable path, not in driver teardown, so it is not runner noise.

Summary
The only new failure of the run: profiling with a scope (hardware-metrics) XPU activity list raises at profiler start, from XpuptiScopeProfilerApi::enableScopeProfiler with PTI error code 50 (PTI_ERROR_DRIVER), so no trace is collected. The test asserts only that the scope config is accepted, and its own docstring records that per-kernel metric values need ZET_ENABLE_METRICS=1 and sysctl dev.xe.observation_paranoid=0; neither is set anywhere in CI, so the driver has no permission to arm metrics collection. Fixing it means either accepting the config without a hard error when the driver cannot provide metrics, or guarding the test on metrics availability instead of TEST_XPU alone. The failure is confined to this one case in one file and the traceback ends inside the scope-profiler enable path, not in driver teardown, so it is not runner noise.

issues.title: [Inductor][XPU] Feature gap: no Triton fallback for get_device_tflops on XPU, devices missing from device_info datasheet get 0 runtime estimate
issues.body:
### Feature gap

On XPU, Inductor's peak-FLOPS lookup has **no fallback** when the device is missing from the static datasheet `torch/_inductor/analysis/device_info.py`. CUDA computes it at runtime via Triton; XPU just returns `0.0`.

`torch/_inductor/utils.py` `_get_device_tflops`:

```python
ds_tops = datasheet_tops(dtype, is_tf32=is_tf32, device_name=device_info_key)  # 1) static table
if ds_tops is not None:
    return ds_tops

if device.type != "cuda" or not torch.cuda.is_available():
    log.warning("get_device_tflops: no Triton fallback available for %s. Returning 0.0 ...", device)
    return 0.0                                                                   # XPU ends here

from triton.testing import get_max_simd_tflops, get_max_tensorcore_tflops       # 2) CUDA-only fallback
```

DRAM bandwidth (`_get_device_dram_gbps`) already falls back to `triton.testing.get_dram_gbps` for both `cuda` and `xpu`, so only TFLOPS is missing.

### Impact

`BaseSchedulerNode._get_estimated_runtime` (`torch/_inductor/scheduler.py`) asserts `gpu_flops > 0` inside a `try/except Exception: return 0`, **before** the compute-bound / memory-bound split. So on any Intel GPU not in the table, every node's runtime estimate is `0` — memory-bound nodes too, even though bandwidth is known.

- Not a correctness issue: results are fine. It degrades Inductor's runtime-estimate-driven heuristics (fusion / comm reordering / overlap), i.e. a potential perf issue.
- Each new Intel SKU needs a hand-written datasheet entry, otherwise UT like `test/inductor/test_snode_runtime.py` fails. Example: #5124 (Arc Pro B60), fixed by adding a table entry (pytorch PR: pytorch/pytorch#201789). B50 / B65 are still missing.

### Proposal

Add an XPU TFLOPS fallback, so the table stays the preferred (exact) source and the fallback only covers unknown devices:

```
peak_tflops ≈ num_xe_cores × ops_per_clock_per_core(arch, dtype) × clock
```

- core count / clock: from `torch.xpu.get_device_properties()` (need to confirm which fields are exposed, e.g. max clock frequency).
- `ops_per_clock_per_core`: not reported by the driver — needs a small **per-architecture** table (Xe-HPC/PVC, Xe2/BMG/LNL, Xe3/PTL, ...) for vector (fp32/fp64) and XMX (fp16/bf16/tf32/int8) paths. Per-arch instead of per-SKU, so much less maintenance.
- Clock choice (base vs boost) should match how existing table entries were derived, so table vs fallback give consistent numbers.

Where to implement (to discuss):
- **A.** XPU implementation of `triton.testing.get_max_tensorcore_tflops` / `get_max_simd_tflops` in intel-xpu-backend-for-triton, and relax the `device.type != "cuda"` guard in PyTorch. Symmetric with CUDA, two repos.
- **B.** An `xpu` branch directly in `_get_device_tflops` (or register via `register_device_info` at XPU init). One repo, faster.

Related small fix worth doing independently: in `_get_estimated_runtime`, only require `gpu_flops > 0` when `estimate_flops()` is non-zero, so memory-bound nodes fall back to bandwidth instead of 0 on any backend.

The vector number is +# 8 XVE per Xe core * SIMD16 * 2 (FMA); the XMX number is specific to the +# architecture. Keying on the architecture rather than the SKU is what makes +# this a fallback worth having: a new SKU of a known architecture needs no +# entry. +# +# Cross-checked against the datasheet entries above, which this reproduces: +# Data Center GPU Max 1100 (56 Xe cores at 1.55GHz) -> 22.2 / 355.5 / 711.1, +# Arc Pro B70 (32 Xe cores at 2.8GHz) -> 22.94 / 183.5 / 367. +_XPU_FLOPS_PER_CLOCK_PER_XE_CORE: dict[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int]] = { + (12, 60): (256, 4096), # Xe-HPC, Ponte Vecchio + (12, 61): (256, 4096), # Xe-HPC, Ponte Vecchio VG + (20, 1): (256, 2048), # Xe2, Battlemage G21 + (20, 2): (256, 2048), # Xe2, Battlemage G31 + (20, 4): (256, 2048), # Xe2, Lunar Lake +} + +def xpu_runtime_tops( + dtype: torch.dtype, is_tf32: bool = False, device: torch.device | None = None +) -> float | None: + index = 0 if device is None or device.index is None else device.index + props = torch.xpu.get_device_properties(index) + version = props.version.split(".") + try: + rates = _XPU_FLOPS_PER_CLOCK_PER_XE_CORE[(int(version[0]), int(version[1]))] + except (IndexError, KeyError, ValueError): + return None + vector, xmx = rates + + if dtype == torch.float64: + per_clock = vector // 2 + elif dtype == torch.float32: + per_clock = xmx if is_tf32 else vector + elif dtype == torch.int8: + per_clock = xmx * 2 + elif dtype in _XPU_XMX_DTYPES: + per_clock = xmx + else: + return None + + try: + from triton.runtime import driver + # --- a/torch/_inductor/analysis/device_info.py
+++ b/torch/_inductor/analysis/device_info.py
+# Peak FLOPs per clock per Xe core on Intel GPUs, as (vector engines, XMX
+# engines), keyed by the (major, minor) IP version that
+# `torch.xpu.get_device_properties().version` reports. The vector number is
+# 8 XVE per Xe core * SIMD16 * 2 (FMA); the XMX number is specific to the
+# architecture. Keying on the architecture rather than the SKU is what makes
+# this a fallback worth having: a new SKU of a known architecture needs no
+# entry.
+#
+# Cross-checked against the datasheet entries above, which this reproduces:
+# Data Center GPU Max 1100 (56 Xe cores at 1.55GHz) -> 22.2 / 355.5 / 711.1,
+# Arc Pro B70 (32 Xe cores at 2.8GHz) -> 22.94 / 183.5 / 367.
+_XPU_FLOPS_PER_CLOCK_PER_XE_CORE: dict[tuple[int, int], tuple[int, int]] = {
+    (12, 60): (256, 4096),  # Xe-HPC, Ponte Vecchio
+    (12, 61): (256, 4096),  # Xe-HPC, Ponte Vecchio VG
+    (20, 1): (256, 2048),  # Xe2, Battlemage G21
+    (20, 2): (256, 2048),  # Xe2, Battlemage G31
+    (20, 4): (256, 2048),  # Xe2, Lunar Lake
+}
+
+def xpu_runtime_tops(
+    dtype: torch.dtype, is_tf32: bool = False, device: torch.device | None = None
+) -> float | None:
+    index = 0 if device is None or device.index is None else device.index
+    props = torch.xpu.get_device_properties(index)
+    version = props.version.split(".")
+    try:
+        rates = _XPU_FLOPS_PER_CLOCK_PER_XE_CORE[(int(version[0]), int(version[1]))]
+    except (IndexError, KeyError, ValueError):
+        return None
+    vector, xmx = rates
+
+    if dtype == torch.float64:
+        per_clock = vector // 2
+    elif dtype == torch.float32:
+        per_clock = xmx if is_tf32 else vector
+    elif dtype == torch.int8:
+        per_clock = xmx * 2
+    elif dtype in _XPU_XMX_DTYPES:
+        per_clock = xmx
+    else:
+        return None
+
+    try:
+        from triton.runtime import driver
+        # torch.xpu exposes the memory clock but not the GPU core clock, so
+        # Triton's XPU driver is the only source for it.
+        clock_khz = driver.active.utils.get_device_properties(index)["sm_clock_rate"]
+    except Exception:
+        return None
+
+    return props.gpu_subslice_count * per_clock * clock_khz * 1e3 / 1e12

Outcome: IMPLEMENTING(fix_verified), with the caveat below.
Filed as a feature gap, this turned out to have a hard reproducer: 11 cases in
test/inductor/test_snode_runtime.py fail on the Arc Pro B60 this job ran on,
because _get_device_tflops returns 0.0 for any XPU missing from the static
datasheet and the scheduler required gpu_flops > 0 before it split
compute-bound from memory-bound work. The fix adds xpu_runtime_tops, which
derives the theoretical peak from the Xe core count torch.xpu reports and the
core clock the Triton XPU driver reports times a per-architecture
FLOPs-per-clock constant, and defers the scheduler's FLOPS requirement to the
compute-bound branch so memory-bound nodes fall back to bandwidth on any
backend. All 27 cases pass, test_analysis.py is unchanged at 62 passed, and
the derived B60 figures (12.288 fp32 TFLOPS, 196.6 INT8 TOPS) match Intel's
published numbers.
The issue asked for a design decision, and this run made it rather than
waiting - worth a reviewer's attention. Option A (XPU implementations of
triton.testing.get_max_*_tflops plus relaxing the device.type != "cuda"
guard) is not reachable from this repository pair: the installed helpers are
hardcoded to torch.cuda.get_device_capability(), so it needs a change in
intel-xpu-backend-for-triton. Option B was taken for that reason. Two things to
check specifically: the per-architecture FLOPs-per-clock constants are hardware
facts, derived to reproduce the existing Max 1100 / B70 / B580 entries but not
independently sourced; and the PVC entry assumes the driver reports 1.55 GHz,
which could not be checked on this BMG runner. Pulling the clock out of
Triton's driver dict is also a private-API read - exposing SYCL's
max_clock_frequency (already in c10's DeviceProp) on _XpuDeviceProperties
would be the cleaner source, at the cost of a C++ change.

issues.title: [CI][infra] PVC-817255: torch.xpu.mem_get_info() always reports free == total
issues.body:
### Problem

On CI host **PVC-817255**, `torch.xpu.mem_get_info()` returns `free == total` regardless of how much memory is allocated, i.e. no real free-memory data comes back from the driver.

Observed in `test/inductor/test_aot_inductor.py::{AOTInductorTestABICompatibleGpu,AOTInductorTestDualWrapper}::test_update_user_managed_buffer_xpu` (#5484):

```
self.assertGreater(mem_after, mem_before)
AssertionError: -68702699520 not greater than -68702699520
```

`-68702699520` is exactly the total memory of one tile, before and after a 64 MB allocation. Same values in every failing run found: 30987352138, 31362886717, 35871429007.

### Host-specific

| Host | `mem_get_info` | Test |
|---|---|---|
| PVC-817255 (CI) | free == total | FAIL |
| PVC Max 1550 bare metal, same driver 1.6.33578 | real data | PASS |
| PVC Max 1100 (`xpu-agent-pvc`) | real data | PASS |
| BMG B60 (`xpu-agent`) | real data | PASS |

Not a PyTorch / AOTI bug: the test passes everywhere else, and forcing `free == total` reproduces the exact failure.

### Ask

Please check PVC-817255 (driver / container / virtualization setup, e.g. Level Zero free-memory reporting, `ZES_ENABLE_SYSMAN`), or take the host out of the UT pool. Any other test relying on `torch.xpu.mem_get_info` is affected on this host too.

Ref: #5484

### 🐛 Describe the bug with skip template

Four `test_ops_xpu.py` python-reference executor cases for `nn.functional.nll_loss` fail on XPU across all dtypes. The `_refs` decomposition under the aten executor hits a data-dependent `aten._local_scalar_dense.default` during tracing and errors out. This is dtype-independent (fails on bfloat16/float16/float32/float64), suggesting an upstream `_refs.nn.functional.nll_loss` decomposition issue rather than an XPU numerics gap. issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-10-23] XPU index_fill_ stores through an unvalidated index: the generic XPU IndexKernel backbone has no bounds assertion
issues.body:
<!-- alignment-published-unit: issue-201807 -->
## Summary

`torch.ops.aten.index_fill_` on XPU accepts an out-of-range index, computes a
destination offset from it, and stores unconditionally. There is no device-side
bounds assertion anywhere on this path, so the store leaves the target tensor's
storage and the call returns normally with no error. CUDA validates the same index
on the device before the address is formed and traps the kernel.

## Upstream source

- Upstream report: [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#201807]
- Scan window: `2026-10-23T00:00:00Z` .. `2026-10-24T00:00:00Z` (half-open UTC)
- `pytorch/pytorch` default-branch snapshot: `18d8d0974472b71069c8a6d50f1262915e63cd20`

The upstream report was closed on 2026-10-23 as expected behavior, and that closure
is exactly what makes this an XPU-only defect. The maintainer's rationale: on CUDA,
index validation for `index_fill_` happens on the device on purpose, because a
host-side check would need a device-to-host sync on every call; the
`CUDA_KERNEL_ASSERT` in `aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/Indexing.cu` runs *before* the
index is used to compute an address, so it traps the kernel and the out-of-bounds
access never happens. The comment ends: out-of-bounds accesses that happen with **no**
check firing are tracked in [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#195547]

On XPU there is no check to fire.

## Reproducer

```python
import torch

self_t = torch.randn(7, 2, 9, 9, dtype=torch.float32, device='xpu')
before = self_t.clone()
index = torch.tensor(-860848056773112400, dtype=torch.int64, device='xpu')

torch.ops.aten.index_fill_(self_t, 0, index, 2.71828)
torch.xpu.synchronize()

print('elements modified:', int((self_t != before).sum().cpu()), 'of', self_t.numel())
```

## Observed XPU behavior

```text
torch: 2.16.0.dev20261023+xpu
xpu device: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
target inputs: self=(7, 2, 9, 9) self.device=xpu:0 index=-860848056773112400
TARGET_CALL aten.index_fill_(self, 0, huge_negative_index, 2.71828)
elements modified in self: 0 of 1134
```

No exception, no `AssertHandler::printMessage`, exit code 0. `self` is unmodified, so
the store did not land inside `self`.

Expected: a clean index-out-of-range error, or at minimum the device-side bounds
assertion that CUDA and the other XPU indexing kernels already have.

## Target-path evidence

1. `REGISTER_XPU_DISPATCH(index_fill_stub, &xpu::index_fill_kernel)` --
   `src/ATen/native/xpu/TensorAdvancedIndexing.cpp:60`
2. `index_fill_kernel` -- `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/Indexing.cpp:127`, which calls
   `launch_index_kernel` with the generic `IndexKernel` backbone.
3. `IndexKernel::init_global_batch_info` -- `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/Indexing.h:229`
   reads the index value and applies only the negative wrap, with no range check:

```cpp
glb_batch_group_loc_off = cfg_.iinfo_.data[idx_off];
glb_batch_group_loc_off = glb_batch_group_loc_off >= 0
    ? glb_batch_group_loc_off
    : cfg_.indexing_dimension_size_ + glb_batch_group_loc_off;
```

   With `index = -860848056773112400` and `indexing_dimension_size_ = 7` the result is
   still about -8.6e18.

4. `IndexKernel::operator()` (`Indexing.h:294`) feeds that through
   `indexing_logical_off` and then
   `IndexToOffset<ValType, int64_t, -1>::get` (`src/comm/TensorInfo.h:174`), which
   decomposes the linear offset with truncating `%` and `/` and does not clamp.
5. `IndexFillScalarFunctor` (`Indexing.cpp:115-123`) stores unconditionally:

```cpp
dst[dst_off] = alpha;
```

The missing assertion is specific to this backbone, not an XPU-wide convention -- the
sibling XPU indexing kernels do carry it:

- `take`: `SYCL_KERNEL_ASSERT(idx < numel_ && idx >= -numel_ && "take_put_kernel_template() index out of bounds")` -- `Indexing.cpp:726`
- `index_select`: `SYCL_KERNEL_ASSERT(idx >= -size_ && idx < size_ && "index_select(): index out of bounds")` -- `Indexing.cpp:2296`
- advanced indexing: `SYCL_KERNEL_ASSERT(index >= -sizes_[i] && index < sizes_[i] && "index out of bounds")` -- `Indexing.h:614`

## Remaining XPU work

Add a device-side bounds assertion on the index value in the shared `IndexKernel`
backbone, before the destination offset is formed, matching the CUDA formulation and
the assertions the other XPU indexing kernels already use. The comment at
`Indexing.h:333` records that this backbone also serves `index_copy` and `index_add`,
so placing the check in the backbone rather than in `index_fill_kernel` covers those
paths too.

## Ownership

No upstream change covers this, now or when it lands.

- `pytorch/pytorch#201807` is closed as expected behavior *for CUDA*, on the grounds
  that the CUDA device-side check exists and fires. Stage: closed, no fix PR.
- `pytorch/pytorch#195547` (open umbrella, "Missing shape checks result in
  out-of-bounds access of Tensor data") asks for validation that is device-agnostic
  and runs before dispatch, derived from the operator's schema or meta function. A
  data-dependent index *value* cannot be validated there without a device-to-host
  synchronization, which is precisely why CUDA does this check on the device. So the
  umbrella's fix, when it lands, will not close this gap. Stage: proposed, no
  implementation.

The kernel is in `intel/torch-xpu-ops`, so the fix belongs here.

## Related trackers

- [地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#4284] -- open. XPU `index_add` with an
  out-of-range index aborts the process via `SYCL_KERNEL_ASSERT` instead of raising a
  catchable Python error. That is the complementary half of the problem (a check that
  exists but aborts); it does not add a missing check, so it does not cover this
  issue.
- [地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#4391] -- closed unmerged on 2026-07-26.
  Attempted catchable errors for `index_add`/`index_reduce` in `Indexing.cpp`; it did
  not touch the `IndexKernel` backbone's missing assertion.
- [地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#5460] -- open. `ctc_loss` on XPU
  indexes with unvalidated target labels; same defect class, different kernel.
- [地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#3445] -- open. `index_select` with an
  empty source diverges from CPU; adjacent gap in the same file, different condition.

## Environment

```text
torch           2.16.0.dev20261023+xpu
python          3.13.13 (/opt/conda/bin/python3.13)
torch path      /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/__init__.py
xpu_available   true
device          Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
```

Source lines cited above were read in `intel/torch-xpu-ops` `main` at 8413340.

## Scope note

The run established that no check fired and that `self` was not modified. It did not
determine which memory the store reached. The defect supported by the evidence is the
absent bounds check on a store whose address is derived from an unvalidated index, not
a specific corrupted allocation.

## Provenance

Found by an automated XPU alignment scan and independently reviewed before filing.

glb_batch_group_loc_off = cfg_.iinfo_.data[idx_off];

issues.title: [xpu-alignment] [26-10-23] XPU scatter_.value stores past the end of self: ScatterFillInternalKernel drops the index bounds assertion its tensor-source sibling has
issues.body:
<!-- alignment-published-unit: issue-201808 -->
## Summary

`torch.ops.aten.scatter_` with a `Scalar` value on XPU accepts an out-of-range index
and stores at `self_data + idx_dim * index_stride_` without validating `idx_dim`. The
call returns normally with no error. The tensor-source `scatter_` path in the same
file does assert the index, and CUDA asserts it on the device before forming the
address.

## Upstream source

- Upstream report: [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#201808]
- Scan window: `2026-10-23T00:00:00Z` .. `2026-10-24T00:00:00Z` (half-open UTC)
- `pytorch/pytorch` default-branch snapshot: `18d8d0974472b71069c8a6d50f1262915e63cd20`

The upstream report was closed on 2026-10-23 as expected behavior, and that closure is
exactly what makes this an XPU-only defect. The maintainer's rationale: on CUDA, index
validation for `scatter_` happens on the device on purpose, because a host-side check
would need a device-to-host sync on every call; the `CUDA_KERNEL_ASSERT` in
`aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/ScatterGatherKernel.cu` runs *before* the index is used to
compute an address, so it traps the kernel and the out-of-bounds access never happens.
The comment ends: out-of-bounds accesses that happen with **no** check firing are
tracked in [地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#195547]

On the XPU `scatter_.value` path there is no check to fire.

## Reproducer

```python
import torch

self_t = torch.tensor(3, dtype=torch.int64, device='xpu')   # 0-dim
index = torch.tensor(3, dtype=torch.int64, device='xpu')    # 0-dim, out of range

torch.ops.aten.scatter_(self_t, -1, index, 1.0)
torch.xpu.synchronize()

print('self after scatter_:', self_t.cpu().flatten().tolist())
```

## Observed XPU behavior

```text
torch: 2.16.0.dev20261023+xpu
xpu device: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
target inputs: self.dim=0 self.dtype=torch.int64 self.device=xpu:0 index.dim=0 index=3
TARGET_CALL aten.scatter_(self_0dim, -1, index_0dim, 1.0)
self after scatter_: [3]
```

No exception, no `AssertHandler::printMessage`, exit code 0. `self` still holds its
initial value, so the store did not land inside `self`.

For comparison, the same scan's `aten.gather` and `aten.take` reproducers on XPU did
trip their device-side assertions (`ScatterGatherKernels.cpp:230` and
`Indexing.cpp:726`), which is the behavior upstream calls correct. `scatter_.value`
has no equivalent.

Expected: a clean validation error, or at minimum the device-side bounds assertion
that CUDA and the tensor-source XPU `scatter_` path already have.

## Target-path evidence

1. `REGISTER_XPU_DISPATCH(scatter_fill_stub, &xpu::scatter_fill_kernel)` --
   `src/ATen/native/xpu/TensorAdvancedIndexing.cpp:52`
2. `scatter_fill_kernel` -- `src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ScatterGatherKernels.cpp:808`,
   which calls `ScatterFillBaseKernel<>()` with `tensor_assign`.
3. `ScatterFillBaseKernel` (`:686` overload) computes
   `auto index_size = ensure_nonempty_size(self, dim);` at `:710` and passes it to
   `ScatterFillInternalKernel` at `:727`.
4. `ScatterFillInternalKernel` (`:601`) accepts `index_size` and never forwards it to
   the loop functor (`:624-628`).
5. `ScatterFillInternalKernelLoopFunctor::operator()` (`:572-577`) stores
   unconditionally:

```cpp
void operator()(int i) const {
  auto offsets = offset_calc_.get(i);
  int64_t idx_dim = *(index_t*)(index_ptr_ + offsets[1]);
  char* self_data = self_ptr_ + offsets[0];
  f_((scalar_t*)self_data + idx_dim * index_stride_, (scalar_t*)&src_val_);
}
```

The functor does not even take an `index_size` parameter, so the bound is computed,
threaded one level down, and then discarded.

The tensor-source sibling on the same path does have the check --
`ScatterGatherInternalKernelLoopFunctor` at `:235-238`:

```cpp
int64_t idx_dim = *(index_t*)(index_ptr_ + offsets[2]);
SYCL_KERNEL_ASSERT(
    idx_dim >= 0 && idx_dim < index_size_ &&
    "scatter gather kernel index out of bounds");
```

For the reproducer's inputs `index_stride_` is 1 and `idx_dim` is 3, so the store is
24 bytes past an 8-byte 0-dim int64 tensor, which matches the unchanged `self` in the
log.

`ScatterFillBaseKernel` also backs `scatter_fill_kernel_add` (`:894`) and
`scatter_fill_kernel_multiply` (`:902`), so the gap is not limited to `tensor_assign`.

## Remaining XPU work

Add `SYCL_KERNEL_ASSERT(idx_dim >= 0 && idx_dim < index_size)` in
`ScatterFillInternalKernelLoopFunctor`, before the address is formed, using the
`index_size` that `ScatterFillInternalKernel` already receives -- mirroring
`ScatterGatherInternalKernelLoopFunctor` at `ScatterGatherKernels.cpp:235-238`. That
also covers the `scatter_fill_kernel_add` and `scatter_fill_kernel_multiply` reduce
variants, which share the same loop functor.

## Ownership

No upstream change covers this, now or when it lands.

- `pytorch/pytorch#201808` is closed as expected behavior *for CUDA*, on the grounds
  that the CUDA device-side check exists and fires. Stage: closed, no fix PR.
- `pytorch/pytorch#195547` (open umbrella, "Missing shape checks result in
  out-of-bounds access of Tensor data") asks for validation that is device-agnostic
  and runs before dispatch, derived from the operator's schema or meta function. A
  data-dependent index *value* cannot be validated there without a device-to-host
  synchronization, which is precisely why CUDA does this check on the device. So the
  umbrella's fix, when it lands, will not close this gap. Stage: proposed, no
  implementation.

The kernel is in `intel/torch-xpu-ops`, so the fix belongs here.

## Related trackers

- [地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#4284] -- open. XPU `index_add` with an
  out-of-range index aborts the process via `SYCL_KERNEL_ASSERT` instead of raising a
  catchable Python error. That is the complementary half of the problem (a check that
  exists but aborts); it does not add a missing check, so it does not cover this
  issue. Note that adding the assertion asked for here will produce that abort
  behavior until #4284 is resolved, which is still strictly better than an unchecked
  store.
- [地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#4391] -- closed unmerged on 2026-07-26.
  Attempted catchable errors for `index_add`/`index_reduce`; it did not touch
  `ScatterGatherKernels.cpp`.
- [地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#5460] -- open. `ctc_loss` on XPU
  indexes with unvalidated target labels; same defect class, different kernel.
- Companion finding from the same scan: XPU `index_fill_` has no bounds assertion in
  the generic `IndexKernel` backbone (`Indexing.h:229`), filed separately because it
  is a different kernel needing a different change.

## Environment

```text
torch           2.16.0.dev20261023+xpu
python          3.13.13 (/opt/conda/bin/python3.13)
torch path      /opt/conda/lib/python3.13/site-packages/torch/__init__.py
xpu_available   true
device          Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
```

Source lines cited above were read in `intel/torch-xpu-ops` `main` at 8413340. The
runner's own assertion messages in this scan carry
`third_party/torch-xpu-ops/src/ATen/native/xpu/sycl/ScatterGatherKernels.cpp:230`,
which agrees with this checkout.

## Scope note

The run established that no check fired and that `self` was not modified. It did not
determine which memory the store reached. The defect supported by the evidence is the
absent bounds check on a store whose address is derived from an unvalidated index, not
a specific corrupted allocation.

## Provenance

Found by an automated XPU alignment scan and independently reviewed before filing.

issues.title: [XPU][Windows][Alder Lake UHD] float32-to-float16/bfloat16 tensor conversion fails with Level Zero error 45
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

## Description

A direct PyTorch XPU tensor conversion fails on an Intel Alder Lake-P UHD
Graphics device with:

```text
RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 45
(UR_RESULT_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT)

The conversion fails in isolated tests without ACE-Step or a model loaded.
The same failure was reproduced with both PyTorch 2.14.1+xpu and
2.9.0+xpu in separate environments.

## Minimal reproducer
import torch

print("PyTorch:", torch.__version__)
print("XPU available:", torch.xpu.is_available())
print("Device:", torch.xpu.get_device_name(0))

x = torch.zeros((2, 1_440_000), device="xpu", dtype=torch.float32)
torch.xpu.synchronize()
print("float32 allocation: PASS")

for dtype in (torch.float16, torch.bfloat16):
    print(f"Converting to {dtype}...")
    y = x.to(dtype)
    torch.xpu.synchronize()
    print("PASS:", y.dtype)

Both low-precision conversions fail with Level Zero error 45 on this system.


## Controls
The following operations passed:

XPU device detection and small tensor allocation
Large float32 CPU-to-XPU transfer
Large float32 XPU tensor allocation and arithmetic
Boolean attention-mask conversion on XPU
Small XPU matrix multiplication
Converting the large tensor to float16 or bfloat16 on CPU allowed the
transfer to XPU, but a subsequent arithmetic operation on that low-precision
XPU tensor failed.


## Environment
OS: Windows
GPU: Intel UHD Graphics, Alder Lake-P GT1
PCI device ID: 8086:46A3
Intel graphics driver: 32.0.101.7092
This is the newest driver available for this system.
PyTorch builds tested, separately:
2.14.1+xpu
2.9.0+xpu
Level Zero driver reported by PyTorch: 1.6.34728
PyTorch reports XPU as available, but warns that this GPU is not officially
supported.
ACE-Step context
In ACE-Step, audio generation with the LM disabled also fails on XPU while
preparing reference audio. The traceback reaches
conditioning_batch.py when moving the reference-audio tensor to XPU and
converting it to the VAE dtype (bfloat16 on XPU).

Enhance Caption separately fails during the Qwen3 LM forward pass. The
application-level failures may have a different immediate cause, but the
standalone low-precision conversion failure seems relevant to investigating
the audio-generation path.


## Related reports
[intel/torch-xpu-ops#2657]([地址已移除：intel/torch-xpu-ops#2657]):
Level Zero error 45 during a low-precision model cast on Arc/Linux;
that report says PyTorch 2.9 passed on its different setup.
[pytorch/pytorch#201826]([地址已移除：pytorch/pytorch#201826]):
low-precision SDPA instability on Arc 140V; a different operation and GPU.
[oneDNN#5758]([地址已移除：uxlfoundation/oneDNN#5758]):
investigation of intermittent low-precision SDPA results on Arc B580;
related XPU context, but not the same tensor-conversion failure.
Does this look like a known hardware limitation or a backend/runtime bug?
Is there a recommended diagnostic or a minimal supported operation set for
this GPU generation?

### Versions

## Versions

**Primary environment (ACE-Step / original XPU environment)**

- PyTorch: `2.14.1+xpu`
- Python: `3.11` (patch version not recorded)
- Transformers: `4.57.6`
- TorchAO: `0.15.0+xpu`
- OS: Windows (exact edition/build not recorded)
- Intel graphics driver: `32.0.101.7092`
- Level Zero driver reported by PyTorch: `1.6.34728`

**Separate isolated PyTorch test environment**

- PyTorch: `2.9.0+xpu`
- torchvision: `0.24.0+xpu`
- torchaudio: `2.9.0+xpu`

**Hardware**

- GPU: Intel UHD Graphics, Alder Lake-P GT1
- PCI device ID: `8086:46A3`

Large float32 XPU tensor allocation and arithmetic
Boolean attention-mask conversion on XPU
Small XPU matrix multiplication

transfer to XPU, but a subsequent arithmetic operation on that low-precision
XPU tensor failed.


## Environment
OS: Windows
GPU: Intel UHD Graphics, Alder Lake-P GT1
PCI device ID: 8086:46A3
Intel graphics driver: 32.0.101.7092
This is the newest driver available for this system.
PyTorch builds tested, separately:
2.14.1+xpu
2.9.0+xpu
Level Zero driver reported by PyTorch: 1.6.34728
PyTorch reports XPU as available, but warns that this GPU is not officially
supported.
ACE-Step context
In ACE-Step, audio generation with the LM disabled also fails on XPU while
preparing reference audio. The traceback reaches
conditioning_batch.py when moving the reference-audio tensor to XPU and
converting it to the VAE dtype (bfloat16 on XPU).

Enhance Caption separately fails during the Qwen3 LM forward pass. The
application-level failures may have a different immediate cause, but the
standalone low-precision conversion failure seems relevant to investigating
the audio-generation path.

low-precision SDPA instability on Arc 140V; a different operation and GPU.
[oneDNN#5758]([地址已移除：uxlfoundation/oneDNN#5758]):
investigation of intermittent low-precision SDPA results on Arc B580;
related XPU context, but not the same tensor-conversion failure.

Is there a recommended diagnostic or a minimal supported operation set for
this GPU generation?

issues.title: [oneAPI DLE 2026.2] PyTorch build fails: sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::ipc_memory is deprecated (-Werror) in c10/xpu/XPUCachingAllocator.cpp
issues.body:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

PyTorch build fails with oneAPI DLE 2026.2 (compiler `/opt/intel/oneapi/compiler/2026.2`, `SYCL_COMPILER_VERSION=20260200`) because `sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::ipc_memory` is now deprecated in favor of `ipc::memory`. `c10/xpu` is built with `-Werror`, so the deprecation warning becomes a hard error.

Failing target: `c10/xpu/CMakeFiles/c10_xpu.dir/XPUCachingAllocator.cpp.o`

```
c10/xpu/XPUCachingAllocator.cpp:2187:57: error: 'sycl::_V1::ext::oneapi::experimental::ipc_memory' is deprecated: The ipc_memory namespace is deprecated. Use the ipc::memory namespace instead. [-Werror=deprecated-declarations]
 2187 |     sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::ipc_memory::handle handle =
/opt/intel/oneapi/compiler/2026.2/include/sycl/ext/oneapi/experimental/ipc_memory.hpp:102:63: note: declared here
  102 |                             "ipc::memory namespace instead.") ipc_memory {
c10/xpu/XPUCachingAllocator.cpp:2188:54: error: ... ipc_memory::get(
c10/xpu/XPUCachingAllocator.cpp:2190:64: error: ... ipc_memory::handle_data_t handle_data =
c10/xpu/XPUCachingAllocator.cpp:2320:22: error: ... (ipc_memory::handle_data_t in MemHandleCacheEntry ctor)
c10/xpu/XPUCachingAllocator.cpp:2325:66: error: ... ipc_memory::open(
c10/xpu/XPUCachingAllocator.cpp:2336:54: error: ... ipc_memory::close(
cc1plus: all warnings being treated as errors
```

Affected usages in `c10/xpu/XPUCachingAllocator.cpp`:
- `DeviceCachingAllocator::shareIpcHandle` (L2187-2190)
- `NativeCachingAllocator::MemHandleCacheEntry::MemHandleCacheEntry` (L2319-2325)
- `NativeCachingAllocator::MemHandleCacheEntry::clear` (L2336)

### Suggested fix

Migrate to the new `sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::ipc::memory` namespace, guarded by compiler version to keep older oneAPI working, e.g.:

```cpp
#if SYCL_COMPILER_VERSION >= 20260200
namespace sycl_ipc_memory = sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::ipc::memory;
#else
namespace sycl_ipc_memory = sycl::ext::oneapi::experimental::ipc_memory;
#endif
```

### Versions

- PyTorch: main @ d2f3a9d2e41e2fb201224ec61f74aa000a37e513
- oneAPI: Deep Learning Essentials 2026.2 (`SYCL_COMPILER_VERSION=20260200`)
- Compiler: GCC 13 (gcc-toolset-13)
- OS: Linux
